verses.original: וְהָיָה כִי יְבִיאֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֶל אֶרֶץ הַכְּנַעֲנִי וְהַחִתִּי וְהָאֱמֹרִי וְהַחִוִּי וְהַיְבוּסִי אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע לַאֲבֹתֶיךָ לָתֶת לָךְ אֶרֶץ זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ וְעָבַדְתָּ אֶת הָעֲבֹדָה הַזֹּאת בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: And it will be, when YHWH will bring you to the land of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, which He swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you will perform this service in this month.

tex.original: \hE{וְהָיָה כִי יְבִיאֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֶל אֶרֶץ הַכְּנַעֲנִי וְהַחִתִּי וְהָאֱמֹרִי וְהַחִוִּי וְהַיְבוּסִי אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע לַאֲבֹתֶיךָ לָתֶת לָךְ אֶרֶץ זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ וְעָבַדְתָּ אֶת הָעֲבֹדָה הַזֹּאת בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה׃}
tex.english:
\eE{
		And it will be, when YHWH will bring you to the land of
		the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the
		Hivite and the Jebusite, which He swore to your fathers to
		give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you
		will perform this service in this month.
	}

verses.original: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצֹּת וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי חַג לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: You shall eat unleavened bread seven days, and on the seventh day is a festival to YHWH.

tex.original: \hE{שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצֹּת וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי חַג לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: מַצּוֹת יֵאָכֵל אֵת שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים וְלֹא יֵרָאֶה לְךָ חָמֵץ וְלֹא יֵרָאֶה לְךָ שְׂאֹר בְּכל גְּבֻלֶךָ׃
verses.english: Unleavened bread will be eaten for the seven days, and leavened bread shall not be seen for you, and leaven shall not be seen for you within all your borders.

tex.original: \hE{מַצּוֹת יֵאָכֵל אֵת שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים וְלֹא יֵרָאֶה לְךָ חָמֵץ וְלֹא יֵרָאֶה לְךָ שְׂאֹר בְּכל גְּבֻלֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וְהִגַּדְתָּ לְבִנְךָ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא לֵאמֹר בַּעֲבוּר זֶה עָשָׂה יְהֹוָה לִי בְּצֵאתִי מִמִּצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: And you shall tell your child in that day, saying, ‘Because of that which YHWH did for me when I went out from Egypt.’

tex.original: \hE{וְהִגַּדְתָּ לְבִנְךָ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא לֵאמֹר בַּעֲבוּר זֶה עָשָׂה יְהֹוָה לִי בְּצֵאתִי מִמִּצְרָיִם׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה לְךָ לְאוֹת עַל יָדְךָ וּלְזִכָּרוֹן בֵּין עֵינֶיךָ לְמַעַן תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת יְהֹוָה בְּפִיךָ כִּי בְּיָד חֲזָקָה הוֹצִאֲךָ יְהֹוָה מִמִּצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: And it will become a sign on your hand and a reminder between your eyes for you so that YHWH’s instruction will be in your mouth, because YHWH brought you out from Egypt with a strong hand.

tex.original: \hE{וְהָיָה לְךָ לְאוֹת עַל יָדְךָ וּלְזִכָּרוֹן בֵּין עֵינֶיךָ לְמַעַן תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת יְהֹוָה בְּפִיךָ כִּי בְּיָד חֲזָקָה הוֹצִאֲךָ יְהֹוָה מִמִּצְרָיִם׃}

verses.original: וְשָׁמַרְתָּ אֶת הַחֻקָּה הַזֹּאת לְמוֹעֲדָהּ מִיָּמִים יָמִימָה׃
verses.english: And you shall observe this law at its appointed time, regularly.

tex.original: \hE{וְשָׁמַרְתָּ אֶת הַחֻקָּה הַזֹּאת לְמוֹעֲדָהּ מִיָּמִים יָמִימָה׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה כִּי יְבִאֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֶל אֶרֶץ הַכְּנַעֲנִי כַּאֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע לְךָ וְלַאֲבֹתֶיךָ וּנְתָנָהּ לָךְ׃
verses.english: And it will be, when YHWH will bring you to the land of the Canaanite as He swore to you and to your fathers and will give it to you,

tex.original: \hE{וְהָיָה כִּי יְבִאֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֶל אֶרֶץ הַכְּנַעֲנִי כַּאֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע לְךָ וְלַאֲבֹתֶיךָ וּנְתָנָהּ לָךְ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		He swore to you. But God did not swear it to them. Could
%		it mean for
%		you? Probably not. Rashi, citing the Mechilta, says He
%		swore when He
%		said, “And I’ll bring you to the land that I raised my
%		hand …” (Exod
%		6:8). But there is no swearing of an oath to the people
%		there. Ramban
%		suggests that the word of God itself may constitute an
%		oath, but that is
%		not correct. The Tanak definitely distinguishes the
%		cases in which a
%		divine oath is sworn. Ramban also takes the earlier
%		words “He swore to
%		your fathers to give to you” (13:5) to constitute an
%		oath to the people.
%		If an oath to the ancestors is in fact the explanation
%		of this, then I
%		believe we should focus on the words that God says to
%		Abraham in the
%		middle of their covenant ceremony. There the fire that
%		expresses the
%		presence of God passes between the parts of animals,
%		which constitutes
%		an oath ceremony; and the stated purpose of this
%		ceremony is to confirm
%		that Abraham will possess the land. God states that
%		after a period of
%		slavery “a fourth generation will come back here” (Gen
%		15:7–16). Or,
%		more generally, we may say that the promise to Abraham
%		is repeated to
%		his descendants, the later patriarchs, showing that the
%		oath carries
%		through the lineage to the descendants. Since the whole
%		people of Israel
%		is a descendant of Abraham, the oath may be regarded as
%		made to them as
%		well. I am not certain of the answer to this problem. I
%		point it out in
%		order to make it known and in the hope that someone else
%		may solve it.
%	}

verses.original: וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ כל פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם לַיהֹוָה וְכל פֶּטֶר שֶׁגֶר בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לְךָ הַזְּכָרִים לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: that you will pass every first birth of a womb to YHWH; and every first birth, offspring of an animal, that you will have—the males—is YHWH’s.

tex.original: \hE{וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ כל פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם לַיהֹוָה וְכל פֶּטֶר שֶׁגֶר בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לְךָ הַזְּכָרִים לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְכל פֶּטֶר חֲמֹר תִּפְדֶּה בְשֶׂה וְאִם לֹא תִפְדֶּה וַעֲרַפְתּוֹ וְכֹל בְּכוֹר אָדָם בְּבָנֶיךָ תִּפְדֶּה׃
verses.english: And you shall redeem every first birth of an ass with a lamb, and if you will not redeem, then you shall break its neck. And you shall redeem every human firstborn among your sons.

tex.original: \hE{וְכל פֶּטֶר חֲמֹר תִּפְדֶּה בְשֶׂה וְאִם לֹא תִפְדֶּה וַעֲרַפְתּוֹ וְכֹל בְּכוֹר אָדָם בְּבָנֶיךָ תִּפְדֶּה׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה כִּי יִשְׁאָלְךָ בִנְךָ מָחָר לֵאמֹר מַה זֹּאת וְאָמַרְתָּ אֵלָיו בְּחֹזֶק יָד הוֹצִיאָנוּ יְהֹוָה מִמִּצְרַיִם מִבֵּית עֲבָדִים׃
verses.english: And it will be, when your child will ask you tomorrow, saying, ‘What is this?’ that you’ll say to him, ‘With strength of hand YHWH brought us out from Egypt, from a house of slaves.

tex.original: \hE{וְהָיָה כִּי יִשְׁאָלְךָ בִנְךָ מָחָר לֵאמֹר מַה זֹּאת וְאָמַרְתָּ אֵלָיו בְּחֹזֶק יָד הוֹצִיאָנוּ יְהֹוָה מִמִּצְרַיִם מִבֵּית עֲבָדִים׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי כִּי הִקְשָׁה פַרְעֹה לְשַׁלְּחֵנוּ וַיַּהֲרֹג יְהֹוָה כּל בְּכוֹר בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם מִבְּכֹר אָדָם וְעַד בְּכוֹר בְּהֵמָה עַל כֵּן אֲנִי זֹבֵחַ לַיהֹוָה כּל פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם הַזְּכָרִים וְכל בְּכוֹר בָּנַי אֶפְדֶּה׃
verses.english: And it was when Pharaoh hardened against letting us go, and YHWH killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from firstborn of a human to firstborn of an animal. On account of this I am sacrificing to YHWH every first birth of a womb—the males—and I shall redeem every firstborn of my sons.’

tex.original: \hE{וַיְהִי כִּי הִקְשָׁה פַרְעֹה לְשַׁלְּחֵנוּ וַיַּהֲרֹג יְהֹוָה כּל בְּכוֹר בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם מִבְּכֹר אָדָם וְעַד בְּכוֹר בְּהֵמָה עַל כֵּן אֲנִי זֹבֵחַ לַיהֹוָה כּל פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם הַזְּכָרִים וְכל בְּכוֹר בָּנַי אֶפְדֶּה׃}
tex.english:
\eE{
		And it was when Pharaoh hardened against letting us go,
		and YHWH killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from
		firstborn of a human to firstborn of an animal. On account
		of this I am sacrificing to YHWH every first birth of a
		womb—the males—and I shall redeem every firstborn of my
		sons.’
	}

verses.original: וְהָיָה לְאוֹת עַל יָדְכָה וּלְטוֹטָפֹת בֵּין עֵינֶיךָ כִּי בְּחֹזֶק יָד הוֹצִיאָנוּ יְהֹוָה מִמִּצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: And it will become a sign on your hand and bands between your eyes, because with strength of hand YHWH brought us out from Egypt.”

tex.original: \hE{וְהָיָה לְאוֹת עַל יָדְכָה וּלְטוֹטָפֹת בֵּין עֵינֶיךָ כִּי בְּחֹזֶק יָד הוֹצִיאָנוּ יְהֹוָה מִמִּצְרָיִם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		a sign on your hand and bands between your eyes. The
%		context of this and
%		the similar expression in v. 9 indicates clearly that
%		this is a
%		metaphor, meaning that the Passover observance is to
%		become a vivid,
%		conscious concern of the people of Israel. The
%		occurrence of the similar
%		expression in Deut 6:8 came to be taken literally,
%		referring to the
%		practice of wrapping one’s hand and forehead in
%		phylacteries
%		(tephillin).
%	}

verses.original: וַיְהִי בְּשַׁלַּח פַּרְעֹה אֶת הָעָם וְלֹא נָחָם אֱלֹהִים דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּים כִּי קָרוֹב הוּא כִּי אָמַר אֱלֹהִים פֶּן יִנָּחֵם הָעָם בִּרְאֹתָם מִלְחָמָה וְשָׁבוּ מִצְרָיְמָה׃
verses.english: And it was, when Pharaoh let the people go, that God did not lead them by way of the Philistines’ land—because it was close—because God said, “In case the people will be dissuaded when they see war, and they’ll go back to Egypt.”

tex.original: \hE{וַיְהִי בְּשַׁלַּח פַּרְעֹה אֶת הָעָם וְלֹא נָחָם אֱלֹהִים דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּים כִּי קָרוֹב הוּא כִּי אָמַר אֱלֹהִים פֶּן יִנָּחֵם הָעָם בִּרְאֹתָם מִלְחָמָה וְשָׁבוּ מִצְרָיְמָה׃}
tex.english:
\eE{
		And it was, when Pharaoh let the people go,
		that God did not lead them by way of the Philistines’
		land—because it was close—because God said, “In case the
		people will be dissuaded when they see war, and they’ll go
		back to Egypt.”
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Philistines. Philistines are present along the coast by
%		the time of
%		Ramesses III, who mentions them in “The War against the
%		Sea Peoples” (c.
%		1188 B.C.E.).
%	}

verses.original: וַיַּסֵּב אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָעָם דֶּרֶךְ הַמִּדְבָּר יַם סוּף וַחֲמֻשִׁים עָלוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: And God turned the people by way of the wilderness of the Red Sea. And the children of Israel went up armed from the land of Egypt.

tex.original: \hE{וַיַּסֵּב אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָעָם דֶּרֶךְ הַמִּדְבָּר יַם סוּף וַחֲמֻשִׁים עָלוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		by way of the wilderness of the Red Sea. They are not
%		sent through
%		Philistine territory because they might be afraid and
%		turn back. But
%		then they are sent to the Red Sea! Is that better? And,
%		in fact, at the
%		Red Sea they will be afraid and wish they were back in
%		Egypt!
%		(14:10–12). The difference is psychological. They have
%		been slaves for
%		generations. Decision making, willpower, and
%		responsibility have not
%		been part of their lives. One does not acquire
%		responsibility instantly
%		when one becomes free. Facing opponents and having to
%		take arms and
%		fight would terrify them, and their natural reaction
%		would be to turn
%		and flee. But the Red Sea situation is different. With
%		the Egyptian army
%		behind them and an opened sea in front of them, they do
%		not need to make
%		a decision, exert willpower, or take responsibility.
%		They have no choice
%		but to go forward. Footnote 13:18. Red Sea. Recent
%		commentators and
%		translators have called this the “Sea of Reeds,” a
%		different body of
%		water from the Red Sea; but there is no such body of
%		water. They say
%		this because (1) the sea is called yam sûp in the
%		Hebrew, and sûp
%		elsewhere means a reed (Exod 2:3); (2) reeds do not grow
%		by the Red Sea;
%		and (3) they conceive of a smaller body of water than
%		the Red Sea being
%		subject to some sort of drying or splitting, as opposed
%		to the larger,
%		deeper Red Sea. But none of these considerations
%		outweighs the simple
%		fact that the Tanak refers to the eastern arm of the
%		sea—the body of
%		water now known as the Gulf of Eilat or the Gulf of
%		Aqaba—as yam sûp as
%		well (Num 14:25; 21:4; Deut 1:40; 2:1; Judg 11:16; 1
%		Kings 9:26; Jer
%		49:21). There is therefore no doubt that the body of
%		water that is
%		pictured in the story of the splitting of the sea in the
%		Torah is the
%		body of water that is known in English as the Red Sea. I
%		have returned
%		to this traditional English translation so it will be
%		clear what body of
%		water is meant. I have no objection to translations that
%		use “Reed Sea”
%		or “Sea of Suph” as long as it is clear that it is this
%		body of water.
%		(As for its Hebrew name, yam sûp, we just do not know
%		how that came to
%		be its name.) Footnote 13:18. armed. Or prepared to
%		fight, or resolute
%		(Propp). But the text has just said that God does not
%		want them to have
%		to face a fight with the Philistines. So why note that
%		they are armed at
%		this point? Answer: (1) because they will fight the
%		Amalekites a short
%		time later (see the comment on 17:9); and (2) in
%		recognition of the fact
%		that one day they will have to fight for the promised
%		land.
%	}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף עִמּוֹ כִּי הַשְׁבֵּעַ הִשְׁבִּיעַ אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר פָּקֹד יִפְקֹד אֱלֹהִים אֶתְכֶם וְהַעֲלִיתֶם אֶת עַצְמֹתַי מִזֶּה אִתְּכֶם׃
verses.english: And Moses took Joseph’s bones with him, because he had had the children of Israel swear, saying, “God will take account of you, and you’ll bring up my bones from here with you.”

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף עִמּוֹ כִּי הַשְׁבֵּעַ הִשְׁבִּיעַ אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר פָּקֹד יִפְקֹד אֱלֹהִים אֶתְכֶם וְהַעֲלִיתֶם אֶת עַצְמֹתַי מִזֶּה אִתְּכֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיִּסְעוּ מִסֻּכֹּת וַיַּחֲנוּ בְאֵתָם בִּקְצֵה הַמִּדְבָּר׃
verses.english: And they traveled from Succoth and camped in Etham at the edge of the wilderness.

tex.original: \hR{וַיִּסְעוּ מִסֻּכֹּת וַיַּחֲנוּ בְאֵתָם בִּקְצֵה הַמִּדְבָּר׃}

verses.original: וַיהֹוָה הֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵיהֶם יוֹמָם בְּעַמּוּד עָנָן לַנְחֹתָם הַדֶּרֶךְ וְלַיְלָה בְּעַמּוּד אֵשׁ לְהָאִיר לָהֶם לָלֶכֶת יוֹמָם וָלָיְלָה׃
verses.english: And YHWH was going in front of them by day in a column of cloud to show them the way, and by night in a column of fire to shed light for them, so as to go by day and by night.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיהֹוָה הֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵיהֶם יוֹמָם בְּעַמּוּד עָנָן לַנְחֹתָם הַדֶּרֶךְ וְלַיְלָה בְּעַמּוּד אֵשׁ לְהָאִיר לָהֶם לָלֶכֶת יוֹמָם וָלָיְלָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		a column of cloud and a column of fire. The cloud and
%		fire have a
%		two-sided function, both conveying God’s presence and
%		reflecting God’s
%		mysteriousness. The narrative reports that YHWH Himself
%		goes in front of
%		the Israelites in the wilderness, but they do not see
%		the deity because
%		He travels in the daytime in the column of cloud and by
%		night in the
%		column of fire. Exodus must be read with a consciousness
%		that the cloud
%		or the fire is present at all times, a constant miracle,
%		an introduction
%		of the cosmic in history. One must have a sense of the
%		awe involved in
%		this phenomenon, particularly expressed in fire. It is a
%		miraculously
%		burning bush that first draws Moses. Now the people
%		experience a similar
%		phenomenon: a continuous, miraculous fire.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא יָמִישׁ עַמּוּד הֶעָנָן יוֹמָם וְעַמּוּד הָאֵשׁ לָיְלָה לִפְנֵי הָעָם׃
verses.english: The column of cloud by day and the column of fire by night did not depart in front of the people.

tex.original: \hJ{לֹא יָמִישׁ עַמּוּד הֶעָנָן יוֹמָם וְעַמּוּד הָאֵשׁ לָיְלָה לִפְנֵי הָעָם׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיָשֻׁבוּ וְיַחֲנוּ לִפְנֵי פִּי הַחִירֹת בֵּין מִגְדֹּל וּבֵין הַיָּם לִפְנֵי בַּעַל צְפֹן נִכְחוֹ תַחֲנוּ עַל הַיָּם׃
verses.english: “Speak to the children of Israel that they should go back and camp in front of Pi-Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, in front of Baal-Zephon. You shall camp facing it, by the sea.

tex.original: \hP{דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיָשֻׁבוּ וְיַחֲנוּ לִפְנֵי פִּי הַחִירֹת בֵּין מִגְדֹּל וּבֵין הַיָּם לִפְנֵי בַּעַל צְפֹן נִכְחוֹ תַחֲנוּ עַל הַיָּם׃}

verses.original: וְאָמַר פַּרְעֹה לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נְבֻכִים הֵם בָּאָרֶץ סָגַר עֲלֵיהֶם הַמִּדְבָּר׃
verses.english: And Pharaoh will say about the children of Israel: ‘They’re muddled in the land! The wilderness has closed them in.’

tex.original: \hP{וְאָמַר פַּרְעֹה לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נְבֻכִים הֵם בָּאָרֶץ סָגַר עֲלֵיהֶם הַמִּדְבָּר׃}

verses.original: וְחִזַּקְתִּי אֶת לֵב פַּרְעֹה וְרָדַף אַחֲרֵיהֶם וְאִכָּבְדָה בְּפַרְעֹה וּבְכל חֵילוֹ וְיָדְעוּ מִצְרַיִם כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵן׃
verses.english: And I’ll strengthen Pharaoh’s heart, and he’ll pursue them, and I’ll be glorified against Pharaoh and against all of his army, and Egypt will know that I am YHWH.” And they did so.

tex.original: \hP{וְחִזַּקְתִּי אֶת לֵב פַּרְעֹה וְרָדַף אַחֲרֵיהֶם וְאִכָּבְדָה בְּפַרְעֹה וּבְכל חֵילוֹ וְיָדְעוּ מִצְרַיִם כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵן׃}

verses.original: וַיֻּגַּד לְמֶלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם כִּי בָרַח הָעָם וַיֵּהָפֵךְ לְבַב פַּרְעֹה וַעֲבָדָיו אֶל הָעָם וַיֹּאמְרוּ מַה זֹּאת עָשִׂינוּ כִּי שִׁלַּחְנוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעבְדֵנוּ׃
verses.english: And it was told to the king of Egypt that the people had fled, and the heart of Pharaoh and his servants was changed toward the people. And they said, “What is this that we’ve done, that we let Israel go from serving us?!”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֻּגַּד לְמֶלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם כִּי בָרַח הָעָם וַיֵּהָפֵךְ לְבַב פַּרְעֹה וַעֲבָדָיו אֶל הָעָם וַיֹּאמְרוּ מַה זֹּאת עָשִׂינוּ כִּי שִׁלַּחְנוּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעבְדֵנוּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		and the heart of Pharaoh … was changed. The word that
%		was used for the
%		stick’s changing into a snake and the water’s changing
%		into blood and
%		the changing of the wind that carried away the locusts
%		is now used to
%		describe Pharaoh’s change of heart. Those past cases,
%		plus the passive
%		(Niphal) form of the verb here, indicate that it is not
%		Pharaoh himself
%		but God who causes the change.
%	}

verses.original: וַיֶּאְסֹר אֶת רִכְבּוֹ וְאֶת עַמּוֹ לָקַח עִמּוֹ׃
verses.english: And he hitched his chariot and took his people with him.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֶּאְסֹר אֶת רִכְבּוֹ וְאֶת עַמּוֹ לָקַח עִמּוֹ׃}
tex.english: \eJ{And he hitched his chariot and took his people with him.}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת רֶכֶב בָּחוּר וְכֹל רֶכֶב מִצְרָיִם וְשָׁלִשִׁם עַל כֻּלּוֹ׃
verses.english: And he took six hundred chosen chariots—and all the chariotry of Egypt—and officers over all of it.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּקַּח שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת רֶכֶב בָּחוּר וְכֹל רֶכֶב מִצְרָיִם וְשָׁלִשִׁם עַל כֻּלּוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיְחַזֵּק יְהֹוָה אֶת לֵב פַּרְעֹה מֶלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם וַיִּרְדֹּף אַחֲרֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יֹצְאִים בְּיָד רָמָה׃
verses.english: And YHWH strengthened the heart of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and he pursued the children of Israel. And the children of Israel were going out with a high hand.

tex.original: \hP{וַיְחַזֵּק יְהֹוָה אֶת לֵב פַּרְעֹה מֶלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם וַיִּרְדֹּף אַחֲרֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל יֹצְאִים בְּיָד רָמָה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּרְדְּפוּ מִצְרַיִם אַחֲרֵיהֶם וַיַּשִּׂיגוּ אוֹתָם חֹנִים עַל הַיָּם כּל סוּס רֶכֶב פַּרְעֹה וּפָרָשָׁיו וְחֵילוֹ עַל פִּי הַחִירֹת לִפְנֵי בַּעַל צְפֹן׃
verses.english: And Egypt pursued them, and they caught up to them, camping by the sea—every chariot horse of Pharaoh and his horsemen and his army—at Pi-Hahiroth, in front of Baal-Zephon.

tex.original:
\hJ{וַיִּרְדְּפוּ מִצְרַיִם אַחֲרֵיהֶם}
	\hP{וַיַּשִּׂיגוּ אוֹתָם חֹנִים עַל הַיָּם כּל סוּס רֶכֶב פַּרְעֹה וּפָרָשָׁיו וְחֵילוֹ עַל פִּי הַחִירֹת לִפְנֵי בַּעַל צְפֹן׃}

verses.original: וּפַרְעֹה הִקְרִיב וַיִּשְׂאוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת עֵינֵיהֶם וְהִנֵּה מִצְרַיִם נֹסֵעַ אַחֲרֵיהֶם וַיִּירְאוּ מְאֹד וַיִּצְעֲקוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: And Pharaoh came close! And the children of Israel raised their eyes, and here was Egypt coming after them, and they were very afraid. And the children of Israel cried out to YHWH.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֶל מֹשֶׁה הֲמִבְּלִי אֵין קְבָרִים בְּמִצְרַיִם לְקַחְתָּנוּ לָמוּת בַּמִּדְבָּר מַה זֹּאת עָשִׂיתָ לָּנוּ לְהוֹצִיאָנוּ מִמִּצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: And they said to Moses, “Was it because of an absence—none!—of graves in Egypt that you took us to die in the wilderness?! What is this that you’ve done to us to bring us out of Egypt?

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֶל מֹשֶׁה הֲמִבְּלִי אֵין קְבָרִים בְּמִצְרַיִם לְקַחְתָּנוּ לָמוּת בַּמִּדְבָּר מַה זֹּאת עָשִׂיתָ לָּנוּ לְהוֹצִיאָנוּ מִמִּצְרָיִם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		an absence—none!—of graves. Their words are redundant.
%		The prophet
%		Elijah uses the same expression: “Is it because of an
%		absence—none!—of a
%		God in Israel that you go to inquire of Baal?!” (2 Kings
%		1:3,6,16). The
%		redundancy dramatizes the question in each case, as if
%		to say, “Was it
%		because of a complete and utter lack …”—the way people
%		speak when
%		accusing someone of doing something completely
%		senseless. Footnote
%		14:11. you’ve done to us. As with Joseph, people focus
%		on the human,
%		Moses, as if he and not God were the one who brought
%		this about.

verses.original: הֲלֹא זֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְנוּ אֵלֶיךָ בְמִצְרַיִם לֵאמֹר חֲדַל מִמֶּנּוּ וְנַעַבְדָה אֶת מִצְרָיִם כִּי טוֹב לָנוּ עֲבֹד אֶת מִצְרַיִם מִמֻּתֵנוּ בַּמִּדְבָּר׃
verses.english: Isn’t this the thing that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying: Stop from us! And let’s serve Egypt. Because serving Egypt is better for us than our dying in the wilderness!”

tex.original: \hE{הֲלֹא זֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְנוּ אֵלֶיךָ בְמִצְרַיִם לֵאמֹר חֲדַל מִמֶּנּוּ וְנַעַבְדָה אֶת מִצְרָיִם כִּי טוֹב לָנוּ עֲבֹד אֶת מִצְרַיִם מִמֻּתֵנוּ בַּמִּדְבָּר׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל הָעָם אַל תִּירָאוּ הִתְיַצְּבוּ וּרְאוּ אֶת יְשׁוּעַת יְהֹוָה אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה לָכֶם הַיּוֹם כִּי אֲשֶׁר רְאִיתֶם אֶת מִצְרַיִם הַיּוֹם לֹא תֹסִפוּ לִרְאֹתָם עוֹד עַד עוֹלָם׃
verses.english: And Moses said to the people, “Don’t be afraid. Stand still and see YHWH’s salvation that He’ll do for you today. For, as you’ve seen Egypt today, you’ll never see them again, ever.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל הָעָם אַל תִּירָאוּ הִתְיַצְּבוּ וּרְאוּ אֶת יְשׁוּעַת יְהֹוָה אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה לָכֶם הַיּוֹם כִּי אֲשֶׁר רְאִיתֶם אֶת מִצְרַיִם הַיּוֹם לֹא תֹסִפוּ לִרְאֹתָם עוֹד עַד עוֹלָם׃}

verses.original: יְהֹוָה יִלָּחֵם לָכֶם וְאַתֶּם תַּחֲרִשׁוּן׃
verses.english: YHWH will fight for you, and you’ll keep quiet!”

tex.original: \hJ{יְהֹוָה יִלָּחֵם לָכֶם וְאַתֶּם תַּחֲרִשׁוּן׃}
tex.english: \eJ{YHWH will fight for you, and you’ll keep quiet!”}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה מַה תִּצְעַק אֵלָי דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיִסָּעוּ׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “Why do you cry out to me? Speak to the children of Israel that they should move!

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה מַה תִּצְעַק אֵלָי דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיִסָּעוּ׃}

verses.original: וְאַתָּה הָרֵם אֶת מַטְּךָ וּנְטֵה אֶת יָדְךָ עַל הַיָּם וּבְקָעֵהוּ וְיָבֹאוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם בַּיַּבָּשָׁה׃
verses.english: And you, lift your staff and reach your hand out over the sea—and split it! And the children of Israel will come through the sea on the dry ground.

tex.original: \hP{וְאַתָּה הָרֵם אֶת מַטְּךָ וּנְטֵה אֶת יָדְךָ עַל הַיָּם וּבְקָעֵהוּ וְיָבֹאוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם בַּיַּבָּשָׁה׃}

verses.original: וַאֲנִי הִנְנִי מְחַזֵּק אֶת לֵב מִצְרַיִם וְיָבֹאוּ אַחֲרֵיהֶם וְאִכָּבְדָה בְּפַרְעֹה וּבְכל חֵילוֹ בְּרִכְבּוֹ וּבְפָרָשָׁיו׃
verses.english: And I, here, I’m strengthening Egypt’s heart, and they’ll come after them, and I’ll be glorified against Pharaoh and against all of his army, against his chariots and against his horsemen.

tex.original: \hP{וַאֲנִי הִנְנִי מְחַזֵּק אֶת לֵב מִצְרַיִם וְיָבֹאוּ אַחֲרֵיהֶם וְאִכָּבְדָה בְּפַרְעֹה וּבְכל חֵילוֹ בְּרִכְבּוֹ וּבְפָרָשָׁיו׃}

verses.original: וְיָדְעוּ מִצְרַיִם כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה בְּהִכָּבְדִי בְּפַרְעֹה בְּרִכְבּוֹ וּבְפָרָשָׁיו׃
verses.english: And Egypt will know that I am YHWH when I’m glorified against Pharaoh, against his chariots and against his horsemen.”

tex.original: \hP{וְיָדְעוּ מִצְרַיִם כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה בְּהִכָּבְדִי בְּפַרְעֹה בְּרִכְבּוֹ וּבְפָרָשָׁיו׃}

verses.original: וַיִּסַּע מַלְאַךְ הָאֱלֹהִים הַהֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵי מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֵּלֶךְ מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶם וַיִּסַּע עַמּוּד הֶעָנָן מִפְּנֵיהֶם וַיַּעֲמֹד מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: And the angel of God who was going in front of the camp of Israel moved and went behind them, and the column of cloud went from in front of them and stood behind them.

tex.original:
\hE{וַיִּסַּע מַלְאַךְ הָאֱלֹהִים הַהֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵי מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֵּלֶךְ מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶם}
	\hJ{וַיִּסַּע עַמּוּד הֶעָנָן מִפְּנֵיהֶם וַיַּעֲמֹד מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא בֵּין מַחֲנֵה מִצְרַיִם וּבֵין מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיְהִי הֶעָנָן וְהַחֹשֶׁךְ וַיָּאֶר אֶת הַלָּיְלָה וְלֹא קָרַב זֶה אֶל זֶה כּל הַלָּיְלָה׃
verses.english: And it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. And there was the cloud and darkness [for the Egyptians], while it [the column of fire] lit the night [for the Israelites], and one did not come near the other all night.

tex.original:
\hE{וַיָּבֹא בֵּין מַחֲנֵה מִצְרַיִם וּבֵין מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל}
	\hJ{וַיְהִי הֶעָנָן וְהַחֹשֶׁךְ וַיָּאֶר אֶת הַלָּיְלָה וְלֹא קָרַב זֶה אֶל זֶה כּל הַלָּיְלָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּט מֹשֶׁה אֶת יָדוֹ עַל הַיָּם וַיּוֹלֶךְ יְהֹוָה אֶת הַיָּם בְּרוּחַ קָדִים עַזָּה כּל הַלַּיְלָה וַיָּשֶׂם אֶת הַיָּם לֶחָרָבָה וַיִּבָּקְעוּ הַמָּיִם׃
verses.english: And Moses reached his hand out over the sea, and YHWH drove back the sea with a strong east wind all night and turned the sea into dry ground, and the water was split.
verses.commentary: Each source repeats its own word for dry ground across the sea and flood stories: J uses ḥārābâ (Gen 7:22), while P uses yabbāšâ, also found in its creation account (Gen 1:9–10; 8:14).

verses.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם בַּיַּבָּשָׁה וְהַמַּיִם לָהֶם חוֹמָה מִימִינָם וּמִשְּׂמֹאלָם׃
verses.english: And the children of Israel came through the sea on the dry ground. And the water was a wall to them at their right and at their left.

tex.original: \hP{וַיָּבֹאוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם בַּיַּבָּשָׁה וְהַמַּיִם לָהֶם חוֹמָה מִימִינָם וּמִשְּׂמֹאלָם׃}

verses.original: וַיִּרְדְּפוּ מִצְרַיִם וַיָּבֹאוּ אַחֲרֵיהֶם כֹּל סוּס פַּרְעֹה רִכְבּוֹ וּפָרָשָׁיו אֶל תּוֹךְ הַיָּם׃
verses.english: And Egypt pursued and came after them, every horse of Pharaoh, his chariots and his horsemen, through the sea.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּרְדְּפוּ מִצְרַיִם וַיָּבֹאוּ אַחֲרֵיהֶם כֹּל סוּס פַּרְעֹה רִכְבּוֹ וּפָרָשָׁיו אֶל תּוֹךְ הַיָּם׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי בְּאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַבֹּקֶר וַיַּשְׁקֵף יְהֹוָה אֶל מַחֲנֵה מִצְרַיִם בְּעַמּוּד אֵשׁ וְעָנָן וַיָּהם אֵת מַחֲנֵה מִצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: And it was in the morning watch, and YHWH gazed at Egypt’s camp through a column of fire and cloud and threw Egypt’s camp into tumult,

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְהִי בְּאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַבֹּקֶר וַיַּשְׁקֵף יְהֹוָה אֶל מַחֲנֵה מִצְרַיִם בְּעַמּוּד אֵשׁ וְעָנָן וַיָּהם אֵת מַחֲנֵה מִצְרָיִם׃}

verses.original: וַיָּסַר אֵת אֹפַן מַרְכְּבֹתָיו וַיְנַהֲגֵהוּ בִּכְבֵדֻת וַיֹּאמֶר מִצְרַיִם אָנוּסָה מִפְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי יְהֹוָה נִלְחָם לָהֶם בְּמִצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: and He turned its chariots’ wheel so that it drove it with heaviness. And Egypt said, “Let me flee from Israel, because YHWH is fighting for them against Egypt!”

	\hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר מִצְרַיִם אָנוּסָה מִפְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי יְהֹוָה נִלְחָם לָהֶם בְּמִצְרָיִם׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה נְטֵה אֶת יָדְךָ עַל הַיָּם וְיָשֻׁבוּ הַמַּיִם עַל מִצְרַיִם עַל רִכְבּוֹ וְעַל פָּרָשָׁיו׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “Reach your hand out over the sea, and the water will go back over Egypt, over his chariots and over his horsemen.”

verses.original: וַיֵּט מֹשֶׁה אֶת יָדוֹ עַל הַיָּם וַיָּשׁב הַיָּם לִפְנוֹת בֹּקֶר לְאֵיתָנוֹ וּמִצְרַיִם נָסִים לִקְרָאתוֹ וַיְנַעֵר יְהֹוָה אֶת מִצְרַיִם בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם׃
verses.english: And Moses reached his hand out over the sea, and the sea went back to its strong flow toward morning, and Egypt was fleeing toward it. And YHWH tossed the Egyptians into the sea.

verses.original: וַיָּשֻׁבוּ הַמַּיִם וַיְכַסּוּ אֶת הָרֶכֶב וְאֶת הַפָּרָשִׁים לְכֹל חֵיל פַּרְעֹה הַבָּאִים אַחֲרֵיהֶם בַּיָּם לֹא נִשְׁאַר בָּהֶם עַד אֶחָד׃
verses.english: And the waters went back and covered the chariots and the horsemen—all of Pharaoh’s army who were coming after them in the sea. Not even one of them was left.

tex.original: \hP{וַיָּשֻׁבוּ הַמַּיִם וַיְכַסּוּ אֶת הָרֶכֶב וְאֶת הַפָּרָשִׁים לְכֹל חֵיל פַּרְעֹה הַבָּאִים אַחֲרֵיהֶם בַּיָּם לֹא נִשְׁאַר בָּהֶם עַד אֶחָד׃}

verses.original: וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָלְכוּ בַיַּבָּשָׁה בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם וְהַמַּיִם לָהֶם חֹמָה מִימִינָם וּמִשְּׂמֹאלָם׃
verses.english: And the children of Israel had gone on the dry ground through the sea, and the water had been a wall to them at their right and at their left.

tex.original: \hP{וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָלְכוּ בַיַּבָּשָׁה בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם וְהַמַּיִם לָהֶם חֹמָה מִימִינָם וּמִשְּׂמֹאלָם׃}

verses.original: וַיּוֹשַׁע יְהֹוָה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִיַּד מִצְרָיִם וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת מִצְרַיִם מֵת עַל שְׂפַת הַיָּם׃
verses.english: And YHWH saved Israel from Egypt’s hand that day. And Israel saw Egypt dead on the seashore,

tex.original: \hJ{וַיּוֹשַׁע יְהֹוָה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִיַּד מִצְרָיִם וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת מִצְרַיִם מֵת עַל שְׂפַת הַיָּם׃}

verses.original: וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַיָּד הַגְּדֹלָה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה יְהֹוָה בְּמִצְרַיִם וַיִּירְאוּ הָעָם אֶת יְהֹוָה וַיַּאֲמִינוּ בַּיהֹוָה וּבְמֹשֶׁה עַבְדּוֹ׃
verses.english: and Israel saw the big hand that YHWH had used against Egypt, and the people feared YHWH, and they trusted in YHWH and in Moses His servant.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַיָּד הַגְּדֹלָה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה יְהֹוָה בְּמִצְרַיִם וַיִּירְאוּ הָעָם אֶת יְהֹוָה וַיַּאֲמִינוּ בַּיהֹוָה וּבְמֹשֶׁה עַבְדּוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		they trusted. This word is also translated often as
%		“believed” (Hebrew
%		wayya’mînû). It does not have the meaning here that it
%		has in later
%		religious concepts. That is, it does not function in the
%		sense of
%		believing that a God exists. This notion of belief in
%		does not occur in
%		Biblical Hebrew (nor in other ancient Near Eastern
%		languages). In pagan
%		religion the gods, being observable forces in nature
%		(e.g., the sun, the
%		sky, the storm wind), are not a matter of belief but of
%		knowledge. So in
%		the conception of YHWH in Exodus, God becomes known;
%		God’s existence and
%		power are a matter of knowledge, not belief. When one
%		has seen ten
%		plagues and a sea split and has a column of cloud and
%		fire visible at
%		all times, one does not ask, “Do you believe in God?” As
%		the term is
%		used in the Hebrew Bible, it means not belief in, but
%		belief that; that
%		is, it means that if YHWH says He will do something one
%		can trust that
%		He will do it.
%	}

verses.original: אָז יָשִׁיר מֹשֶׁה וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת לַיהֹוָה וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֵאמֹר אָשִׁירָה לַיהֹוָה כִּי גָאֹה גָּאָה סוּס וְרֹכְבוֹ רָמָה בַיָּם׃
verses.english: Then Moses and the children of Israel sang this song to YHWH. And they said, saying: Let me sing to YHWH, for He triumphed! Horse and its rider He cast in the sea.

verses.original: עזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ וַיְהִי לִי לִישׁוּעָה זֶה אֵלִי וְאַנְוֵהוּ אֱלֹהֵי אָבִי וַאֲרֹמְמֶנְהוּ׃
verses.english: My strength and song are Yah, and He became a salvation for me. This is my God, and I’ll praise Him, my father’s God, and I’ll hail Him.

tex.original: \hProtoA{עזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ וַיְהִי לִי לִישׁוּעָה זֶה אֵלִי וְאַנְוֵהוּ אֱלֹהֵי אָבִי וַאֲרֹמְמֶנְהוּ׃}

verses.original: יְהֹוָה אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה יְהֹוָה שְׁמוֹ׃
verses.english: YHWH is a warrior. YHWH is His name.

tex.original: \hProtoA{יְהֹוָה אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה יְהֹוָה שְׁמוֹ׃}
tex.english: \eProtoA{YHWH is a warrior. YHWH is His name.}

verses.original: מַרְכְּבֹת פַּרְעֹה וְחֵילוֹ יָרָה בַיָּם וּמִבְחַר שָׁלִשָׁיו טֻבְּעוּ בְיַם סוּף׃
verses.english: Pharaoh’s chariots and his army He plunged in the sea and the choice of his troops drowned in the Red Sea.

tex.original: \hProtoA{מַרְכְּבֹת פַּרְעֹה וְחֵילוֹ יָרָה בַיָּם וּמִבְחַר שָׁלִשָׁיו טֻבְּעוּ בְיַם סוּף׃}

verses.original: תְּהֹמֹת יְכַסְיֻמוּ יָרְדוּ בִמְצוֹלֹת כְּמוֹ אָבֶן׃
verses.english: The deeps covered them. They sank in the depths like a stone.

tex.original: \hProtoA{תְּהֹמֹת יְכַסְיֻמוּ יָרְדוּ בִמְצוֹלֹת כְּמוֹ אָבֶן׃}

verses.original: יְמִינְךָ יְהֹוָה נֶאְדָּרִי בַּכֹּחַ יְמִינְךָ יְהֹוָה תִּרְעַץ אוֹיֵב׃
verses.english: Your right hand, YHWH, awesome in power, your right hand, YHWH, crushed the foe.

tex.original: \hProtoA{יְמִינְךָ יְהֹוָה נֶאְדָּרִי בַּכֹּחַ יְמִינְךָ יְהֹוָה תִּרְעַץ אוֹיֵב׃}

verses.original: וּבְרֹב גְּאוֹנְךָ תַּהֲרֹס קָמֶיךָ תְּשַׁלַּח חֲרֹנְךָ יֹאכְלֵמוֹ כַּקַּשׁ׃
verses.english: And in your triumph’s greatness you threw down your adversaries. You let go your fury: it consumed them like straw.

tex.original: \hProtoA{וּבְרֹב גְּאוֹנְךָ תַּהֲרֹס קָמֶיךָ תְּשַׁלַּח חֲרֹנְךָ יֹאכְלֵמוֹ כַּקַּשׁ׃}

verses.original: וּבְרוּחַ אַפֶּיךָ נֶעֶרְמוּ מַיִם נִצְּבוּ כְמוֹ נֵד נֹזְלִים קָפְאוּ תְהֹמֹת בְּלֶב יָם׃
verses.english: And by wind from your nostrils water was massed, surf piled up like a heap, the deeps congealed in the heart of the sea.

tex.original: \hProtoA{וּבְרוּחַ אַפֶּיךָ נֶעֶרְמוּ מַיִם נִצְּבוּ כְמוֹ נֵד נֹזְלִים קָפְאוּ תְהֹמֹת בְּלֶב יָם׃}

verses.original: אָמַר אוֹיֵב אֶרְדֹּף אַשִּׂיג אֲחַלֵּק שָׁלָל תִּמְלָאֵמוֹ נַפְשִׁי אָרִיק חַרְבִּי תּוֹרִישֵׁמוֹ יָדִי׃
verses.english: The enemy said, “I’ll pursue! I’ll catch up! I’ll divide spoil! My soul will be sated! I’ll unsheathe my sword! My hand will deprive them!”

tex.original: \hProtoA{אָמַר אוֹיֵב אֶרְדֹּף אַשִּׂיג אֲחַלֵּק שָׁלָל תִּמְלָאֵמוֹ נַפְשִׁי אָרִיק חַרְבִּי תּוֹרִישֵׁמוֹ יָדִי׃}

verses.original: נָשַׁפְתָּ בְרוּחֲךָ כִּסָּמוֹ יָם צָלְלוּ כַּעוֹפֶרֶת בְּמַיִם אַדִּירִים׃
verses.english: You blew with your wind. Sea covered them. They sank like lead in the awesome water.

tex.original: \hProtoA{נָשַׁפְתָּ בְרוּחֲךָ כִּסָּמוֹ יָם צָלְלוּ כַּעוֹפֶרֶת בְּמַיִם אַדִּירִים׃}

verses.original: מִי כָמֹכָה בָּאֵלִם יְהֹוָה מִי כָּמֹכָה נֶאְדָּר בַּקֹּדֶשׁ נוֹרָא תְהִלֹּת עֹשֵׂה פֶלֶא׃
verses.english: Who is like you among the gods, YHWH! Who is like you: awesome in holiness! fearsome with splendors! making miracles!

tex.original: \hProtoA{מִי כָמֹכָה בָּאֵלִם יְהֹוָה מִי כָּמֹכָה נֶאְדָּר בַּקֹּדֶשׁ נוֹרָא תְהִלֹּת עֹשֵׂה פֶלֶא׃}

verses.original: נָטִיתָ יְמִינְךָ תִּבְלָעֵמוֹ אָרֶץ׃
verses.english: You reached your right hand: earth swallowed them.

tex.original: \hProtoA{נָטִיתָ יְמִינְךָ תִּבְלָעֵמוֹ אָרֶץ׃}
tex.english: \eProtoA{You reached your right hand: earth swallowed them.}

verses.original: נָחִיתָ בְחַסְדְּךָ עַם זוּ גָּאָלְתָּ נֵהַלְתָּ בְעזְּךָ אֶל נְוֵה קדְשֶׁךָ׃
verses.english: You led, in your kindness, the people you redeemed; you ushered, in your strength, to your holy abode.

tex.original: \hProtoA{נָחִיתָ בְחַסְדְּךָ עַם זוּ גָּאָלְתָּ נֵהַלְתָּ בְעזְּךָ אֶל נְוֵה קדְשֶׁךָ׃}

verses.original: שָׁמְעוּ עַמִּים יִרְגָּזוּן חִיל אָחַז יֹשְׁבֵי פְּלָשֶׁת׃
verses.english: Peoples heard—they shuddered. Shaking seized Philistia’s residents.

tex.original: \hProtoA{שָׁמְעוּ עַמִּים יִרְגָּזוּן חִיל אָחַז יֹשְׁבֵי פְּלָשֶׁת׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Peoples heard. This is not just about Egypt. As in the
%		matter of the
%		plagues, the object is not only to defeat or punish the
%		Egyptians. It is
%		to make YHWH known in the world. So the Song of the Sea
%		declares that
%		others hear of this event: Philistia, Edom, Moab, all of
%		Canaan’s
%		residents.
%	}

verses.original: אָז נִבְהֲלוּ אַלּוּפֵי אֱדוֹם אֵילֵי מוֹאָב יֹאחֲזֵמוֹ רָעַד נָמֹגוּ כֹּל יֹשְׁבֵי כְנָעַן׃
verses.english: Then Edom’s chiefs were terrified. Moab’s chieftains: trembling seized them. All Canaan’s residents melted.

tex.original: \hProtoA{אָז נִבְהֲלוּ אַלּוּפֵי אֱדוֹם אֵילֵי מוֹאָב יֹאחֲזֵמוֹ רָעַד נָמֹגוּ כֹּל יֹשְׁבֵי כְנָעַן׃}

verses.original: תִּפֹּל עֲלֵיהֶם אֵימָתָה וָפַחַד בִּגְדֹל זְרוֹעֲךָ יִדְּמוּ כָּאָבֶן עַד יַעֲבֹר עַמְּךָ יְהֹוָה עַד יַעֲבֹר עַם זוּ קָנִיתָ׃
verses.english: Terror and fear came over them. At the power of your arm they’re silent like stone. ’Til your people passed, YHWH, ’til the people you created passed.

tex.original: \hProtoA{תִּפֹּל עֲלֵיהֶם אֵימָתָה וָפַחַד בִּגְדֹל זְרוֹעֲךָ יִדְּמוּ כָּאָבֶן עַד יַעֲבֹר עַמְּךָ יְהֹוָה עַד יַעֲבֹר עַם זוּ קָנִיתָ׃}

verses.original: תְּבִאֵמוֹ וְתִטָּעֵמוֹ בְּהַר נַחֲלָתְךָ מָכוֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ פָּעַלְתָּ יְהֹוָה מִקְּדָשׁ אֲדֹנָי כּוֹנְנוּ יָדֶיךָ׃
verses.english: You’ll bring them and plant them in your legacy’s mountain, your throne’s platform, that you made, YHWH; a holy place, Lord, that your hands reared.

tex.original: \hProtoA{תְּבִאֵמוֹ וְתִטָּעֵמוֹ בְּהַר נַחֲלָתְךָ מָכוֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ פָּעַלְתָּ יְהֹוָה מִקְּדָשׁ אֲדֹנָי כּוֹנְנוּ יָדֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: יְהֹוָה יִמְלֹךְ לְעֹלָם וָעֶד׃
verses.english: YHWH will reign forever and ever!

tex.original: \hProtoA{יְהֹוָה יִמְלֹךְ לְעֹלָם וָעֶד׃}
tex.english: \eProtoA{YHWH will reign forever and ever!}

verses.original: כִּי בָא סוּס פַּרְעֹה בְּרִכְבּוֹ וּבְפָרָשָׁיו בַּיָּם וַיָּשֶׁב יְהֹוָה עֲלֵהֶם אֶת מֵי הַיָּם וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָלְכוּ בַיַּבָּשָׁה בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם׃
verses.english: Because Pharaoh’s horses with his chariots and with his horsemen came in the sea, and YHWH brought back the water of the sea over them, and the children of Israel had gone on the dry ground through the sea.

tex.original: \hR{כִּי בָא סוּס פַּרְעֹה בְּרִכְבּוֹ וּבְפָרָשָׁיו בַּיָּם וַיָּשֶׁב יְהֹוָה עֲלֵהֶם אֶת מֵי הַיָּם וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הָלְכוּ בַיַּבָּשָׁה בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם׃}

verses.original: וַתִּקַּח מִרְיָם הַנְּבִיאָה אֲחוֹת אַהֲרֹן אֶת הַתֹּף בְּיָדָהּ וַתֵּצֶאןָ כל הַנָּשִׁים אַחֲרֶיהָ בְּתֻפִּים וּבִמְחֹלֹת׃
verses.english: And Miriam, the prophetess, Aaron’s sister, took a drum in her hand, and all the women went out behind her with drums and with dances.

tex.original: \hE{וַתִּקַּח מִרְיָם הַנְּבִיאָה אֲחוֹת אַהֲרֹן אֶת הַתֹּף בְּיָדָהּ וַתֵּצֶאןָ כל הַנָּשִׁים אַחֲרֶיהָ בְּתֻפִּים וּבִמְחֹלֹת׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Miriam, the prophetess. Here we are informed that she is
%		a prophetess.
%		This will be crucial later, when she and Aaron will
%		speak against Moses,
%		saying, “Has YHWH only just spoken through Moses? Hasn’t
%		He also spoken
%		through us?” (Num 12:2).
%	}

verses.original:
וַתַּעַן לָהֶם מִרְיָם
שִׁירוּ לַיהֹוָה כִּי גָאֹה גָּאָה סוּס וְרֹכְבוֹ רָמָה בַיָּם׃
verses.english:
And Miriam sang to them
Sing to YHWH for he triumphed! Horse and its rider he cast in the sea.

tex.original:
\hE{וַתַּעַן לָהֶם מִרְיָם}\\
	\hProto{שִׁירוּ לַיהֹוָה כִּי גָאֹה גָּאָה סוּס וְרֹכְבוֹ רָמָה בַיָּם׃}%
tex.english:
\eE{And Miriam sang to them}\\
	\eProto{Sing to YHWH for he triumphed! Horse and its rider he cast in the sea.}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Miriam sang. This song is therefore known both as the
%		Song of the Sea
%		and as the Song of Miriam. My teacher Frank Moore Cross
%		and my senior
%		colleague David Noel Freedman demonstrated together that
%		this is one of
%		the oldest—if not the oldest—passages in the Bible. The
%		Red Sea episode
%		was thus an early and decisive element of Israel’s
%		story.
%	}

verses.original: וַיַּסַּע מֹשֶׁה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִיַּם סוּף וַיֵּצְאוּ אֶל מִדְבַּר שׁוּר וַיֵּלְכוּ שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים בַּמִּדְבָּר וְלֹא מָצְאוּ מָיִם׃
verses.english: And Moses had Israel travel from the Red Sea, and they went out to the wilderness of Shur. And they went three days in the wilderness. And they did not find water.

tex.original:
\hR{וַיַּסַּע מֹשֶׁה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִיַּם סוּף וַיֵּצְאוּ אֶל מִדְבַּר שׁוּר}
	\hJ{וַיֵּלְכוּ שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים בַּמִּדְבָּר וְלֹא מָצְאוּ מָיִם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		they went three days in the wilderness. The original
%		request they made
%		of Pharaoh—a three-day trip in the wilderness—is now
%		fulfilled. And they
%		are not returning!
%	}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ מָרָתָה וְלֹא יָכְלוּ לִשְׁתֹּת מַיִם מִמָּרָה כִּי מָרִים הֵם עַל כֵּן קָרָא שְׁמָהּ מָרָה׃
verses.english: And they came to Marah, and they were not able to drink water from Marah because it was bitter. On account of this he called its name Marah.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּבֹאוּ מָרָתָה וְלֹא יָכְלוּ לִשְׁתֹּת מַיִם מִמָּרָה כִּי מָרִים הֵם עַל כֵּן קָרָא שְׁמָהּ מָרָה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּלֹּנוּ הָעָם עַל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר מַה נִּשְׁתֶּה׃
verses.english: And the people complained at Moses, saying, “What shall we drink?”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּלֹּנוּ הָעָם עַל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר מַה נִּשְׁתֶּה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the people complained at Moses. The narrative has
%		proceeded from the
%		confrontation between Moses and the deity to that
%		between Moses and the
%		Pharaoh, and now to the ongoing confrontation between
%		Moses and the
%		people. And, as I indicated earlier, each new stage of
%		confrontation
%		carries with it the background of what has come before,
%		so that Moses’
%		experiences with the people—involving sometimes wisdom,
%		sometimes rage,
%		and sometimes affection—must be read with some
%		appreciation of the
%		growth that has taken place in his personality through
%		his earlier
%		encounters with divinity and royalty. Having defeated
%		the leader of
%		Egypt, Moses now finds himself to be the leader of a
%		people, a people
%		who never chose him to lead them. Through a series of
%		crises, the people
%		doubt his competence and rebel against his authority.
%	}

verses.original: וַיִּצְעַק אֶל יְהֹוָה וַיּוֹרֵהוּ יְהֹוָה עֵץ וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ אֶל הַמַּיִם וַיִּמְתְּקוּ הַמָּיִם שָׁם שָׂם לוֹ חֹק וּמִשְׁפָּט וְשָׁם נִסָּהוּ׃
verses.english: And he cried to YHWH, and YHWH showed him a tree, and he threw it into the water, and the water sweetened. He set law and judgment for them there, and He tested them there.

tex.original:
\hJ{וַיִּצְעַק אֶל יְהֹוָה וַיּוֹרֵהוּ יְהֹוָה עֵץ וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ אֶל הַמַּיִם וַיִּמְתְּקוּ הַמָּיִם}
	\hE{שָׁם שָׂם לוֹ חֹק וּמִשְׁפָּט וְשָׁם נִסָּהוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע לְקוֹל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְהַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו תַּעֲשֶׂה וְהַאֲזַנְתָּ לְמִצְוֺתָיו וְשָׁמַרְתָּ כּל חֻקָּיו כּל הַמַּחֲלָה אֲשֶׁר שַׂמְתִּי בְמִצְרַיִם לֹא אָשִׂים עָלֶיךָ כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה רֹפְאֶךָ׃
verses.english: And He said, “If you’ll listen to the voice of YHWH, your God, and you’ll do what is right in His eyes and turn your ear to His commandments and observe all His laws, I won’t set on you any of the sickness that I set on Egypt, because I, YHWH, am your healer.”
verses.commentary: Exodus 15:26 has an unusually strong concentration of Deuteronomistic phrasing for Genesis–Numbers. Its source remains uncertain: E also shares such language and may be responsible here (see the note on Exod 12:24).

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמֶר אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע לְקוֹל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְהַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו תַּעֲשֶׂה וְהַאֲזַנְתָּ לְמִצְוֺתָיו וְשָׁמַרְתָּ כּל חֻקָּיו כּל הַמַּחֲלָה אֲשֶׁר שַׂמְתִּי בְמִצְרַיִם לֹא אָשִׂים עָלֶיךָ כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה רֹפְאֶךָ׃}
tex.english:
\eE{
		And He said, “If you’ll listen to the voice of YHWH, your
		God, and you’ll do what is right in His eyes and turn your
		ear to His commandments and observe all His laws, I won’t
		set on you any of the sickness that I set on Egypt,
		because I, YHWH, am your healer.”
	}
tex.commentary:
%\fC{
	%	REF: Exod 15:26 has more phrases that sound
	%	Deuteronomistic than any other passage in Genesis
	%	through Numbers. Still, it is uncertain and may be E,
	%	which has other similarities to Deuteronomistic
	%	language. (See the note on Exod 12:24.)
	%}
	\fC{%
		Exodus 15:26 has an unusually strong concentration of
		Deuteronomistic phrasing for
		Genesis–Numbers. Its source remains uncertain: E also
		shares such language and may be
		responsible here (see the note on Exod 12:24).%
	}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ אֵילִמָה וְשָׁם שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה עֵינֹת מַיִם וְשִׁבְעִים תְּמָרִים וַיַּחֲנוּ שָׁם עַל הַמָּיִם׃
verses.english: And they came to Elim. And twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees were there. And they camped there by the water.

tex.original: \hR{וַיָּבֹאוּ אֵילִמָה וְשָׁם שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה עֵינֹת מַיִם וְשִׁבְעִים תְּמָרִים וַיַּחֲנוּ שָׁם עַל הַמָּיִם׃}

verses.original: וַיִּסְעוּ מֵאֵילִם וַיָּבֹאוּ כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל מִדְבַּר סִין אֲשֶׁר בֵּין אֵילִם וּבֵין סִינָי בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי לְצֵאתָם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: And they traveled from Elim, and all of the congregation of the children of Israel came to the wilderness of Sîn, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their exodus from the land of Egypt.

tex.original: \hR{וַיִּסְעוּ מֵאֵילִם וַיָּבֹאוּ כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל מִדְבַּר סִין אֲשֶׁר בֵּין אֵילִם וּבֵין סִינָי בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי לְצֵאתָם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃}
tex.english:
\eR{
		And they traveled from Elim, and all of the
		congregation of the children of Israel came to the
		wilderness of Sîn, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the
		fifteenth day of the second month after their exodus from
		the land of Egypt.%
	}

verses.original: (וילינו) [וַיִּלּוֹנוּ] כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעַל אַהֲרֹן בַּמִּדְבָּר׃
verses.english: And all of the congregation of the children of Israel complained at Moses and at Aaron in the wilderness.
verses.commentary: Qere Ketiv.

tex.original: \hP{(וילינו) [וַיִּלּוֹנוּ] כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעַל אַהֲרֹן בַּמִּדְבָּר׃}
tex.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

%	\footnote{
%		at Moses and at Aaron. This is one of the most explicit
%		cases in the
%		Bible of the way humans focus on the visible human
%		figure rather than on
%		God. They complain at Moses and Aaron. They say, “You
%		brought us out”
%		(16:3). Moses answers that they will soon see that “YHWH
%		brought you
%		out” (16:6). And he tells them that their complaints are
%		“at YHWH,” and
%		he adds, “What are we, that you complain at us?!”
%		(16:8). The miracle of
%		manna follows, confirming the message that Moses has
%		just told them in
%		three different ways. But by the very next chapter: “the
%		people
%		complained at Moses and said, ‘Why did you bring us
%		up?’” (17:3). They
%		continue to resist the fact that they are experiencing
%		divine power,
%		that they are actually encountering God.
%	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֲלֵהֶם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִי יִתֵּן מוּתֵנוּ בְיַד יְהֹוָה בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם בְּשִׁבְתֵּנוּ עַל סִיר הַבָּשָׂר בְּאכְלֵנוּ לֶחֶם לָשֹׂבַע כִּי הוֹצֵאתֶם אֹתָנוּ אֶל הַמִּדְבָּר הַזֶּה לְהָמִית אֶת כּל הַקָּהָל הַזֶּה בָּרָעָב׃
verses.english: And the children of Israel said to them, “Who would make it so that we had died by YHWH’s hand in the land of Egypt, when we sat by a pot of meat, when we ate bread to the full! Because you brought us out to this wilderness to kill this whole community with starvation!”

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֲלֵהֶם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִי יִתֵּן מוּתֵנוּ בְיַד יְהֹוָה בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם בְּשִׁבְתֵּנוּ עַל סִיר הַבָּשָׂר בְּאכְלֵנוּ לֶחֶם לָשֹׂבַע כִּי הוֹצֵאתֶם אֹתָנוּ אֶל הַמִּדְבָּר הַזֶּה לְהָמִית אֶת כּל הַקָּהָל הַזֶּה בָּרָעָב׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And the children of Israel said to them, “Who would make
		it so that we had died by YHWH’s hand in the land of
		Egypt, when we sat by a pot of meat, when we ate bread to
		the full! Because you brought us out to this wilderness to
		kill this whole community with starvation!”
	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה הִנְנִי מַמְטִיר לָכֶם לֶחֶם מִן הַשָּׁמָיִם וְיָצָא הָעָם וְלָקְטוּ דְּבַר יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ לְמַעַן אֲנַסֶּנּוּ הֲיֵלֵךְ בְּתוֹרָתִי אִם לֹא׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “Here, I’m raining bread from the skies for you, and let the people go out and gather the daily ration in its day in order that I can test them: will they go by my instruction or not.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה הִנְנִי מַמְטִיר לָכֶם לֶחֶם מִן הַשָּׁמָיִם וְיָצָא הָעָם וְלָקְטוּ דְּבַר יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ לְמַעַן אֲנַסֶּנּוּ הֲיֵלֵךְ בְּתוֹרָתִי אִם לֹא׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי וְהֵכִינוּ אֵת אֲשֶׁר יָבִיאוּ וְהָיָה מִשְׁנֶה עַל אֲשֶׁר יִלְקְטוּ יוֹם יוֹם׃
verses.english: And it will be that on the sixth day they’ll prepare what they bring in, and it will be twice as much as they’ll gather on regular days.”

tex.original: \hJ{וְהָיָה בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי וְהֵכִינוּ אֵת אֲשֶׁר יָבִיאוּ וְהָיָה מִשְׁנֶה עַל אֲשֶׁר יִלְקְטוּ יוֹם יוֹם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		on regular days. Hebrew yôm yôm; meaning that the sixth
%		day’s yield will
%		be double what is gathered on an ordinary day of the
%		week (Sunday
%		through Thursday).
%	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן אֶל כּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עֶרֶב וִידַעְתֶּם כִּי יְהֹוָה הוֹצִיא אֶתְכֶם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: And Moses and Aaron said to all the children of Israel, “At evening you’ll know that YHWH brought you out from the land of Egypt,

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן אֶל כּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עֶרֶב וִידַעְתֶּם כִּי יְהֹוָה הוֹצִיא אֶתְכֶם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃}

verses.original: וּבֹקֶר וּרְאִיתֶם אֶת כְּבוֹד יְהֹוָה בְּשׁמְעוֹ אֶת תְּלֻנֹּתֵיכֶם עַל יְהֹוָה וְנַחְנוּ מָה כִּי (תלונו) [תַלִּינוּ] עָלֵינוּ׃
verses.english: and in the morning you’ll see YHWH’s glory, because He has heard your complaints about YHWH. And what are we, that you complain at us?!”
verses.commentary: Qere Ketiv.

tex.original: \hP{וּבֹקֶר וּרְאִיתֶם אֶת כְּבוֹד יְהֹוָה בְּשׁמְעוֹ אֶת תְּלֻנֹּתֵיכֶם עַל יְהֹוָה וְנַחְנוּ מָה כִּי (תלונו) [תַלִּינוּ] עָלֵינוּ׃}
tex.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

%	\footnote{
%		YHWH’s glory. The glory surrounds God when in the
%		presence of humans. It
%		is some sort of indescribable substance that veils or
%		masks the deity,
%		who cannot be seen. “A human will not see me and live.”
%		Even the glory
%		itself is seen through a cloud. This is the first
%		mention of the divine
%		glory, and a few verses later it is seen for the first
%		time. It then
%		does not occur again until the revelation at Sinai. It
%		is impressive,
%		but also sad, that its first appearance comes in
%		response to the
%		people’s complaints over food rather than as the
%		surrounding of the
%		Sinai event. It suggests the extreme seriousness of what
%		is taking place
%		in this first period following the exodus. The people
%		are unprepared,
%		vulnerable, and frightened; and they are apparently in
%		need of manifest
%		evidence that the power that brought them out of Egypt
%		is still present,
%		that the exodus was just the beginning, that what comes
%		next is the
%		acquaintance and continuing relationship with God.
%	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה בְּתֵת יְהֹוָה לָכֶם בָּעֶרֶב בָּשָׂר לֶאֱכֹל וְלֶחֶם בַּבֹּקֶר לִשְׂבֹּעַ בִּשְׁמֹעַ יְהֹוָה אֶת תְּלֻנֹּתֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם מַלִּינִם עָלָיו וְנַחְנוּ מָה לֹא עָלֵינוּ תְלֻנֹּתֵיכֶם כִּי עַל יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: And Moses said, “When YHWH gives you meat to eat in the evening and bread to the full in the morning, because YHWH has heard your complaints that you’re making at Him! And what are we? Your complaints are not at us but at YHWH!”

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה בְּתֵת יְהֹוָה לָכֶם בָּעֶרֶב בָּשָׂר לֶאֱכֹל וְלֶחֶם בַּבֹּקֶר לִשְׂבֹּעַ בִּשְׁמֹעַ יְהֹוָה אֶת תְּלֻנֹּתֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם מַלִּינִם עָלָיו וְנַחְנוּ מָה לֹא עָלֵינוּ תְלֻנֹּתֵיכֶם כִּי עַל יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל אַהֲרֹן אֱמֹר אֶל כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל קִרְבוּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה כִּי שָׁמַע אֵת תְּלֻנֹּתֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: And Moses said to Aaron, “Say to all of the congregation of the children of Israel, ‘Come close in front of YHWH, because He has heard your complaints.’”

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל אַהֲרֹן אֱמֹר אֶל כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל קִרְבוּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה כִּי שָׁמַע אֵת תְּלֻנֹּתֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי כְּדַבֵּר אַהֲרֹן אֶל כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּפְנוּ אֶל הַמִּדְבָּר וְהִנֵּה כְּבוֹד יְהֹוָה נִרְאָה בֶּעָנָן׃
verses.english: And it was as Aaron was speaking to all of the congregation of the children of Israel: and they turned to the wilderness, and here was YHWH’s glory appearing in a cloud.

tex.original: \hP{וַיְהִי כְּדַבֵּר אַהֲרֹן אֶל כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּפְנוּ אֶל הַמִּדְבָּר וְהִנֵּה כְּבוֹד יְהֹוָה נִרְאָה בֶּעָנָן׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: שָׁמַעְתִּי אֶת תְּלוּנֹּת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דַּבֵּר אֲלֵהֶם לֵאמֹר בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם תֹּאכְלוּ בָשָׂר וּבַבֹּקֶר תִּשְׂבְּעוּ לָחֶם וִידַעְתֶּם כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: “I’ve heard the complaints of the children of Israel. Speak to them, saying, ‘Between the two evenings you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread, and you will know that I am YHWH, your God.’”

tex.original: \hP{שָׁמַעְתִּי אֶת תְּלוּנֹּת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל דַּבֵּר אֲלֵהֶם לֵאמֹר בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם תֹּאכְלוּ בָשָׂר וּבַבֹּקֶר תִּשְׂבְּעוּ לָחֶם וִידַעְתֶּם כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי בָעֶרֶב וַתַּעַל הַשְּׂלָו וַתְּכַס אֶת הַמַּחֲנֶה וּבַבֹּקֶר הָיְתָה שִׁכְבַת הַטַּל סָבִיב לַמַּחֲנֶה׃
verses.english: And it was in the evening, and quail went up and covered the camp. And in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.

tex.original: \hP{וַיְהִי בָעֶרֶב וַתַּעַל הַשְּׂלָו וַתְּכַס אֶת הַמַּחֲנֶה וּבַבֹּקֶר הָיְתָה שִׁכְבַת הַטַּל סָבִיב לַמַּחֲנֶה׃}

verses.original: וַתַּעַל שִׁכְבַת הַטָּל וְהִנֵּה עַל פְּנֵי הַמִּדְבָּר דַּק מְחֻסְפָּס דַּק כַּכְּפֹר עַל הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.english: And the layer of dew went up, and here, on the face of the wilderness: scaly thin, thin as frost on the ground.

tex.original: \hP{וַתַּעַל שִׁכְבַת הַטָּל וְהִנֵּה עַל פְּנֵי הַמִּדְבָּר דַּק מְחֻסְפָּס דַּק כַּכְּפֹר עַל הָאָרֶץ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּרְאוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֹּאמְרוּ אִישׁ אֶל אָחִיו מָן הוּא כִּי לֹא יָדְעוּ מַה הוּא וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֲלֵהֶם הוּא הַלֶּחֶם אֲשֶׁר נָתַן יְהֹוָה לָכֶם לְאכְלָה׃
verses.english: And the children of Israel saw, and each said to his brother, “What is it?”—because they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them, “That is the bread that YHWH has given you for food.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּרְאוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֹּאמְרוּ אִישׁ אֶל אָחִיו מָן הוּא כִּי לֹא יָדְעוּ מַה הוּא וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֲלֵהֶם הוּא הַלֶּחֶם אֲשֶׁר נָתַן יְהֹוָה לָכֶם לְאכְלָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		What is it? Hebrew mn hû!. This is a play on words,
%		because these words
%		can also mean “It is manna.” It thus explains the origin
%		of the word
%		“manna” as coming from their not having a name for
%		something new. The
%		famous comedy routine of “Who’s on first” in English is
%		actually an
%		equivalent that conveys what is happening here. They
%		say, “It’s what?”
%		And people then take this not as a question but as a
%		statement: “It’s
%		‘What’!” And it is known thereafter as “What.”
%	}

verses.original: זֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה לִקְטוּ מִמֶּנּוּ אִישׁ לְפִי אכְלוֹ עֹמֶר לַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת מִסְפַּר נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם אִישׁ לַאֲשֶׁר בְּאהֳלוֹ תִּקָּחוּ׃
verses.english: This is the thing that YHWH has commanded: Collect some of it, each according to what he eats; you shall take an omer per head, the number of your persons, each for whoever is in his tent.”

tex.original: \hP{זֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה לִקְטוּ מִמֶּנּוּ אִישׁ לְפִי אכְלוֹ עֹמֶר לַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת מִסְפַּר נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם אִישׁ לַאֲשֶׁר בְּאהֳלוֹ תִּקָּחוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּלְקְטוּ הַמַּרְבֶּה וְהַמַּמְעִיט׃
verses.english: And the children of Israel did so. And they collected—the one who took the most and the one who took the least.

tex.original: \hP{וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּלְקְטוּ הַמַּרְבֶּה וְהַמַּמְעִיט׃}

verses.original: וַיָּמֹדּוּ בָעֹמֶר וְלֹא הֶעְדִּיף הַמַּרְבֶּה וְהַמַּמְעִיט לֹא הֶחְסִיר אִישׁ לְפִי אכְלוֹ לָקָטוּ׃
verses.english: And they measured by the omer, and the one who took the most had not exceeded, and the one who took the least had not fallen short. Each had collected according to what he eats.

tex.original: \hP{וַיָּמֹדּוּ בָעֹמֶר וְלֹא הֶעְדִּיף הַמַּרְבֶּה וְהַמַּמְעִיט לֹא הֶחְסִיר אִישׁ לְפִי אכְלוֹ לָקָטוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ אַל יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר׃
verses.english: And Moses said to them, “Let no one leave any of it over until morning.”

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ אַל יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ אֶל מֹשֶׁה וַיּוֹתִרוּ אֲנָשִׁים מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר וַיָּרֻם תּוֹלָעִים וַיִּבְאַשׁ וַיִּקְצֹף עֲלֵהֶם מֹשֶׁה׃
verses.english: And they did not listen to Moses, and people left some of it over until morning, and it yielded worms and stank. And Moses was angry at them.

tex.original: \hP{וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ אֶל מֹשֶׁה וַיּוֹתִרוּ אֲנָשִׁים מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר וַיָּרֻם תּוֹלָעִים וַיִּבְאַשׁ וַיִּקְצֹף עֲלֵהֶם מֹשֶׁה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּלְקְטוּ אֹתוֹ בַּבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר אִישׁ כְּפִי אכְלוֹ וְחַם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְנָמָס׃
verses.english: And they collected it morning by morning, each by what he eats, and when the sun was hot it melted.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּלְקְטוּ אֹתוֹ בַּבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר אִישׁ כְּפִי אכְלוֹ וְחַם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְנָמָס׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי לָקְטוּ לֶחֶם מִשְׁנֶה שְׁנֵי הָעֹמֶר לָאֶחָד וַיָּבֹאוּ כּל נְשִׂיאֵי הָעֵדָה וַיַּגִּידוּ לְמֹשֶׁה׃
verses.english: And it was: on the sixth day they collected double bread, two times the omer for each one, and all the chiefs of the congregation came and told Moses.

tex.original: \hP{וַיְהִי בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי לָקְטוּ לֶחֶם מִשְׁנֶה שְׁנֵי הָעֹמֶר לָאֶחָד וַיָּבֹאוּ כּל נְשִׂיאֵי הָעֵדָה וַיַּגִּידוּ לְמֹשֶׁה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵהֶם הוּא אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה שַׁבָּתוֹן שַׁבַּת קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה מָחָר אֵת אֲשֶׁר תֹּאפוּ אֵפוּ וְאֵת אֲשֶׁר תְּבַשְּׁלוּ בַּשֵּׁלוּ וְאֵת כּל הָעֹדֵף הַנִּיחוּ לָכֶם לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת עַד הַבֹּקֶר׃
verses.english: And he said to them, “That is what YHWH spoke. Tomorrow is a ceasing, a holy Sabbath to YHWH. Bake what you’ll bake, and cook what you’ll cook, and leave what is left over for keeping until the morning.”

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵהֶם הוּא אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה שַׁבָּתוֹן שַׁבַּת קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה מָחָר אֵת אֲשֶׁר תֹּאפוּ אֵפוּ וְאֵת אֲשֶׁר תְּבַשְּׁלוּ בַּשֵּׁלוּ וְאֵת כּל הָעֹדֵף הַנִּיחוּ לָכֶם לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת עַד הַבֹּקֶר׃}

verses.original: וַיַּנִּיחוּ אֹתוֹ עַד הַבֹּקֶר כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה מֹשֶׁה וְלֹא הִבְאִישׁ וְרִמָּה לֹא הָיְתָה בּוֹ׃
verses.english: And they left it until the morning, as Moses had commanded, and it did not stink, and there was not a worm in it.

tex.original: \hP{וַיַּנִּיחוּ אֹתוֹ עַד הַבֹּקֶר כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה מֹשֶׁה וְלֹא הִבְאִישׁ וְרִמָּה לֹא הָיְתָה בּוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		as Moses had commanded. Until now, the text has always
%		said “as YHWH had
%		commanded” or “as God had commanded.” Here, for the
%		first time, it
%		attributes the commanding to Moses—even though Moses has
%		said explicitly
%		in the preceding verse that this is what YHWH has
%		spoken. Moses still
%		acts only by God’s direction, but the wording
%		participates in the
%		gradual impression through the Tanak that humans’ share
%		in the
%		responsibility for their fate is growing.
%	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אִכְלֻהוּ הַיּוֹם כִּי שַׁבָּת הַיּוֹם לַיהֹוָה הַיּוֹם לֹא תִמְצָאֻהוּ בַּשָּׂדֶה׃
verses.english: And Moses said, “Eat it today, because today is a Sabbath to YHWH. Today you won’t find it in the field.

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אִכְלֻהוּ הַיּוֹם כִּי שַׁבָּת הַיּוֹם לַיהֹוָה הַיּוֹם לֹא תִמְצָאֻהוּ בַּשָּׂדֶה׃}

verses.original: שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תִּלְקְטֻהוּ וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי שַׁבָּת לֹא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ׃
verses.english: Six days you shall collect it. And on the seventh day is a Sabbath; there will not be any in it.”

tex.original: \hP{שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תִּלְקְטֻהוּ וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי שַׁבָּת לֹא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי יָצְאוּ מִן הָעָם לִלְקֹט וְלֹא מָצָאוּ׃
verses.english: And it was: on the seventh day some of the people went out to collect, and they did not find any.

tex.original: \hP{וַיְהִי בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי יָצְאוּ מִן הָעָם לִלְקֹט וְלֹא מָצָאוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה עַד אָנָה מֵאַנְתֶּם לִשְׁמֹר מִצְוֺתַי וְתוֹרֹתָי׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “How long do you refuse to observe my commandments and my instructions?

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה עַד אָנָה מֵאַנְתֶּם לִשְׁמֹר מִצְוֺתַי וְתוֹרֹתָי׃}

verses.original: רְאוּ כִּי יְהֹוָה נָתַן לָכֶם הַשַּׁבָּת עַל כֵּן הוּא נֹתֵן לָכֶם בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי לֶחֶם יוֹמָיִם שְׁבוּ אִישׁ תַּחְתָּיו אַל יֵצֵא אִישׁ מִמְּקֹמוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי׃
verses.english: See that YHWH has given you the Sabbath. On account of this He is giving you two days’ bread on the sixth day. Stay, each in his place. Let no man go out from his place in the seventh day.”

tex.original: \hP{רְאוּ כִּי יְהֹוָה נָתַן לָכֶם הַשַּׁבָּת עַל כֵּן הוּא נֹתֵן לָכֶם בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי לֶחֶם יוֹמָיִם שְׁבוּ אִישׁ תַּחְתָּיו אַל יֵצֵא אִישׁ מִמְּקֹמוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁבְּתוּ הָעָם בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִעִי׃
verses.english: And the people ceased in the seventh day.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּשְׁבְּתוּ הָעָם בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִעִי׃}
tex.english: \eP{And the people ceased in the seventh day.}

verses.original: וַיִּקְרְאוּ בֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת שְׁמוֹ מָן וְהוּא כְּזֶרַע גַּד לָבָן וְטַעְמוֹ כְּצַפִּיחִת בִּדְבָשׁ׃
verses.english: And the house of Israel called its name “manna.” And it was like a coriander seed, white, and its taste was like a wafer in honey.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּקְרְאוּ בֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת שְׁמוֹ מָן וְהוּא כְּזֶרַע גַּד לָבָן וְטַעְמוֹ כְּצַפִּיחִת בִּדְבָשׁ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה זֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה מְלֹא הָעֹמֶר מִמֶּנּוּ לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם לְמַעַן יִרְאוּ אֶת הַלֶּחֶם אֲשֶׁר הֶאֱכַלְתִּי אֶתְכֶם בַּמִּדְבָּר בְּהוֹצִיאִי אֶתְכֶם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: And Moses said, “This is the thing that YHWH has commanded: ‘an omer-ful of it is for watching over through your generations so that they will see the bread that I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out from the land of Egypt.’”

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה זֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה מְלֹא הָעֹמֶר מִמֶּנּוּ לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם לְמַעַן יִרְאוּ אֶת הַלֶּחֶם אֲשֶׁר הֶאֱכַלְתִּי אֶתְכֶם בַּמִּדְבָּר בְּהוֹצִיאִי אֶתְכֶם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And Moses said, “This is the thing that YHWH has
		commanded: ‘an omer-ful of it is for watching over through
		your generations so that they will see the bread that I
		fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out from the
		land of Egypt.’”
	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל אַהֲרֹן קַח צִנְצֶנֶת אַחַת וְתֶן שָׁמָּה מְלֹא הָעֹמֶר מָן וְהַנַּח אֹתוֹ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: And Moses said to Aaron, “Take one jar and place an omer-ful of manna there and lay it in front of YHWH for watching over through your generations,”

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל אַהֲרֹן קַח צִנְצֶנֶת אַחַת וְתֶן שָׁמָּה מְלֹא הָעֹמֶר מָן וְהַנַּח אֹתוֹ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וַיַּנִּיחֵהוּ אַהֲרֹן לִפְנֵי הָעֵדֻת לְמִשְׁמָרֶת׃
verses.english: as YHWH had commanded Moses. And Aaron laid it in front of the Testimony for watching over.

tex.original: \hP{כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וַיַּנִּיחֵהוּ אַהֲרֹן לִפְנֵי הָעֵדֻת לְמִשְׁמָרֶת׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the Testimony. This term is introduced later as
%		referring to the words
%		of the Ten Commandments on the “tablets of the
%		Testimony” (Exod 31:18),
%		which are kept in the “Ark of the Testimony” (25:22),
%		which is in turn
%		housed in the “Tabernacle of the Testimony” (38:21). It
%		seems
%		chronologically out of place to report here that Aaron
%		placed the manna
%		there, when the tablets, ark, and Tabernacle have not
%		yet been made.
%		This problem has nothing to do with questions of
%		authorship in critical
%		biblical scholarship. Nor is it to be explained by the
%		traditional
%		rabbinic principle of “There is no early or late in the
%		Torah.” Rather,
%		there is a series of items that are reported to have
%		been placed by the
%		Testimony in the Tabernacle: the manna, the incense,
%		Aaron’s staff. The
%		placement of each is reported in the context of the
%		story or law that
%		relates to it. Since the story of the manna is told
%		here, the report
%		that Aaron placed it at the Testimony is included here
%		as well. To have
%		saved this report for a later, more chronologically
%		appropriate, point
%		in the Torah would have meant cutting it off from the
%		rest of the manna
%		story. The report in the next verse that they ate the
%		manna for forty
%		years likewise goes chronologically past the present
%		moment in the
%		story. It thus further confirms that the purpose of the
%		present context
%		is to cover the entire matter of the manna in one place.
%	}

verses.original: וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָכְלוּ אֶת הַמָּן אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה עַד בֹּאָם אֶל אֶרֶץ נוֹשָׁבֶת אֶת הַמָּן אָכְלוּ עַד בֹּאָם אֶל קְצֵה אֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן׃
verses.english: And the children of Israel ate the manna forty years until they came to settled land. They ate the manna until they came to the edge of the land of Canaan.

tex.original:
\hP{וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָכְלוּ אֶת הַמָּן אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה עַד בֹּאָם אֶל אֶרֶץ נוֹשָׁבֶת}
	\hJ{אֶת הַמָּן אָכְלוּ עַד בֹּאָם אֶל קְצֵה אֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן׃}

verses.original: וְהָעֹמֶר עֲשִׂרִית הָאֵיפָה הוּא׃
verses.english: (And an omer is a tenth of an ephah.)

tex.original: \hP{וְהָעֹמֶר עֲשִׂרִית הָאֵיפָה הוּא׃}
tex.english: \eP{(And an omer is a tenth of an ephah.)}

verses.original: וַיִּסְעוּ כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּדְבַּר סִין לְמַסְעֵיהֶם עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה וַיַּחֲנוּ בִּרְפִידִים וְאֵין מַיִם לִשְׁתֹּת הָעָם׃
verses.english: And all of the congregation of the children of Israel traveled from the wilderness of Sîn on their travels by YHWH’s word, and they camped in Rephidim. And there was no water for the people to drink.

tex.original: \hR{וַיִּסְעוּ כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּדְבַּר סִין לְמַסְעֵיהֶם עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה וַיַּחֲנוּ בִּרְפִידִים וְאֵין מַיִם לִשְׁתֹּת הָעָם׃}

verses.original: וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם מֹשֶׁה וַיֹּאמְרוּ תְּנוּ לָנוּ מַיִם וְנִשְׁתֶּה וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם מֹשֶׁה מַה תְּרִיבוּן עִמָּדִי מַה תְּנַסּוּן אֶת יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: And the people quarreled with Moses. And they said, “Give us water, and let us drink.” And Moses said to them, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test YHWH?!”

tex.original: \hE{וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם מֹשֶׁה וַיֹּאמְרוּ תְּנוּ לָנוּ מַיִם וְנִשְׁתֶּה וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם מֹשֶׁה מַה תְּרִיבוּן עִמָּדִי מַה תְּנַסּוּן אֶת יְהֹוָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		test. In each of the two chapters that precede this, God
%		is described as
%		testing the people (15:25; 16:4). (It is the same word
%		that is used for
%		God’s testing Abraham in ordering him to sacrifice
%		Isaac—Gen Footnote
%		22:1.) Now the people dare to test God, and Moses asks
%		them why they do
%		that. It is a rhetorical question: the point is that
%		there is no reason
%		to test God. It is presumptuous, because God can be
%		counted upon. This
%		is significant enough that at the end of the episode the
%		place is named
%		Massah, meaning “Test,” because of what the people dared
%		to do there.
%	}

verses.original: וַיִּצְמָא שָׁם הָעָם לַמַּיִם וַיָּלֶן הָעָם עַל מֹשֶׁה וַיֹּאמֶר לָמָּה זֶּה הֶעֱלִיתָנוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם לְהָמִית אֹתִי וְאֶת בָּנַי וְאֶת מִקְנַי בַּצָּמָא׃
verses.english: And the people thirsted for water there, and the people complained at Moses and said, “Why is this that you brought us up from Egypt: to kill me and my children and my cattle with thirst?!”

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּצְמָא שָׁם הָעָם לַמַּיִם וַיָּלֶן הָעָם עַל מֹשֶׁה וַיֹּאמֶר לָמָּה זֶּה הֶעֱלִיתָנוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם לְהָמִית אֹתִי וְאֶת בָּנַי וְאֶת מִקְנַי בַּצָּמָא׃}

verses.original: וַיִּצְעַק מֹשֶׁה אֶל יְהֹוָה לֵאמֹר מָה אֶעֱשֶׂה לָעָם הַזֶּה עוֹד מְעַט וּסְקָלֻנִי׃
verses.english: And Moses cried to YHWH, saying, “What shall I do to this people? A little more and they’ll stone me!”

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּצְעַק מֹשֶׁה אֶל יְהֹוָה לֵאמֹר מָה אֶעֱשֶׂה לָעָם הַזֶּה עוֹד מְעַט וּסְקָלֻנִי׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה עֲבֹר לִפְנֵי הָעָם וְקַח אִתְּךָ מִזִּקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמַטְּךָ אֲשֶׁר הִכִּיתָ בּוֹ אֶת הַיְאֹר קַח בְּיָדְךָ וְהָלָכְתָּ׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “Pass in front of the people and take some of Israel’s elders with you, and take your staff with which you struck the Nile in your hand, and you’ll go.

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה עֲבֹר לִפְנֵי הָעָם וְקַח אִתְּךָ מִזִּקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמַטְּךָ אֲשֶׁר הִכִּיתָ בּוֹ אֶת הַיְאֹר קַח בְּיָדְךָ וְהָלָכְתָּ׃}

verses.original: הִנְנִי עֹמֵד לְפָנֶיךָ שָּׁם עַל הַצּוּר בְּחֹרֵב וְהִכִּיתָ בַצּוּר וְיָצְאוּ מִמֶּנּוּ מַיִם וְשָׁתָה הָעָם וַיַּעַשׂ כֵּן מֹשֶׁה לְעֵינֵי זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: Here, I’ll be standing in front of you there on a rock at Horeb. And you’ll strike the rock, and water will come out of it, and the people will drink.” And Moses did so before the eyes of Israel’s elders.

tex.original: \hE{הִנְנִי עֹמֵד לְפָנֶיךָ שָּׁם עַל הַצּוּר בְּחֹרֵב וְהִכִּיתָ בַצּוּר וְיָצְאוּ מִמֶּנּוּ מַיִם וְשָׁתָה הָעָם וַיַּעַשׂ כֵּן מֹשֶׁה לְעֵינֵי זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		on a rock at Horeb. The word “rock” refers not to a
%		small stone but to a
%		crag of the mountain. God stands at a crag of Mount
%		Horeb/Sinai.
%		Footnote 17:6. at Horeb. Here is the story’s geography:
%		Moses and the
%		elders are to go on ahead of the people to Mount Horeb
%		(Sinai). The
%		miracle of the water will occur there, not at the site
%		of the quarrel
%		and testing. Only the elders see it, not the people
%		(17:6). The people
%		receive the water somewhere near Horeb, and then they
%		return to the camp
%		in the region of Rephidim (or perhaps the water flows
%		all the way to
%		where the people are). The site of their quarrel there
%		is named Massah
%		and Meribah. Amalek attacks and fights them there
%		(17:8). Then Jethro
%		goes to meet Moses at Horeb, where Moses is now encamped
%		(18:5). Moses
%		comes out to meet him and Moses’ wife and children there
%		(18:7). Then
%		Aaron and the elders join them for a sacred meal there.
%		The people come
%		there later from Rephidim (19:2). The important thing,
%		often overlooked,
%		is that the miracle of the water from the rock takes
%		place at Mount
%		Sinai. I learned this from William Propp. Footnote 17:6.
%		you’ll strike
%		the rock, and water will come out of it. Moses, who was
%		drawn from
%		water, and whose name stands for drawing from water, now
%		draws water
%		from the rock. He also met his wife by defending her
%		right to draw
%		water; the first plague he introduced involved turning
%		the waters (from
%		which he had once been drawn) to blood; he initiated the
%		splitting of
%		the sea; and he acted to sweeten the bitter water at
%		Marah. There will
%		be several more incidents involving water in Moses’
%		life. It seems to be
%		a key element in his destiny, which will culminate in
%		his tragic act
%		when he strikes a rock to get water again at a second
%		Meribah (Numbers
%		20). For this act he will be forbidden to enter the
%		promised land. His
%		life will end, as it began, at a river, the Jordan,
%		which he will not be
%		permitted to cross.
%	}

verses.original: וַיִּקְרָא שֵׁם הַמָּקוֹם מַסָּה וּמְרִיבָה עַל רִיב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל נַסֹּתָם אֶת יְהֹוָה לֵאמֹר הֲיֵשׁ יְהֹוָה בְּקִרְבֵּנוּ אִם אָיִן׃
verses.english: And he called the place’s name Massah and Meribah because of the quarrel of the children of Israel and because of their testing YHWH, saying, “Is YHWH among us or not?”

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּקְרָא שֵׁם הַמָּקוֹם מַסָּה וּמְרִיבָה עַל רִיב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל נַסֹּתָם אֶת יְהֹוָה לֵאמֹר הֲיֵשׁ יְהֹוָה בְּקִרְבֵּנוּ אִם אָיִן׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא עֲמָלֵק וַיִּלָּחֶם עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּרְפִידִם׃
verses.english: And Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.

tex.original: \hE{וַיָּבֹא עֲמָלֵק וַיִּלָּחֶם עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּרְפִידִם׃}
tex.english: \eE{And Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּחַר לָנוּ אֲנָשִׁים וְצֵא הִלָּחֵם בַּעֲמָלֵק מָחָר אָנֹכִי נִצָּב עַל רֹאשׁ הַגִּבְעָה וּמַטֵּה הָאֱלֹהִים בְּיָדִי׃
verses.english: And Moses said to Joshua, “Choose men for us and go, fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I’ll be standing up on the hilltop, and the staff of God in my hand.”

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּחַר לָנוּ אֲנָשִׁים וְצֵא הִלָּחֵם בַּעֲמָלֵק מָחָר אָנֹכִי נִצָּב עַל רֹאשׁ הַגִּבְעָה וּמַטֵּה הָאֱלֹהִים בְּיָדִי׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		fight against Amalek. Israel was not sent by way of the
%		Philistines’
%		land because they would be afraid of war (13:17), but
%		now, just a few
%		chapters later, they are sent to war against the Amalek!
%		And Israel
%		prevails! How do we explain this? Apparently the
%		intervening events have
%		made a change in the Israelites so that now they have
%		the confidence and
%		fortitude to fight. What are the intervening events: Red
%		Sea, Marah,
%		manna, Meribah. They have received four miraculous signs
%		that their God
%		is still with them even after they have left Egypt.
%	}

verses.original: וַיַּעַשׂ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כַּאֲשֶׁר אָמַר לוֹ מֹשֶׁה לְהִלָּחֵם בַּעֲמָלֵק וּמֹשֶׁה אַהֲרֹן וְחוּר עָלוּ רֹאשׁ הַגִּבְעָה׃
verses.english: And Joshua did as Moses said to him, to fight against Amalek; and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the hilltop.

tex.original: \hE{וַיַּעַשׂ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כַּאֲשֶׁר אָמַר לוֹ מֹשֶׁה לְהִלָּחֵם בַּעֲמָלֵק וּמֹשֶׁה אַהֲרֹן וְחוּר עָלוּ רֹאשׁ הַגִּבְעָה׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה כַּאֲשֶׁר יָרִים מֹשֶׁה יָדוֹ וְגָבַר יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכַאֲשֶׁר יָנִיחַ יָדוֹ וְגָבַר עֲמָלֵק׃
verses.english: And it was: when Moses would lift his hand, then Israel would predominate; and when he would rest his hand, then Amalek would predominate.

tex.original: \hE{וְהָיָה כַּאֲשֶׁר יָרִים מֹשֶׁה יָדוֹ וְגָבַר יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכַאֲשֶׁר יָנִיחַ יָדוֹ וְגָבַר עֲמָלֵק׃}

verses.original: וִידֵי מֹשֶׁה כְּבֵדִים וַיִּקְחוּ אֶבֶן וַיָּשִׂימוּ תַחְתָּיו וַיֵּשֶׁב עָלֶיהָ וְאַהֲרֹן וְחוּר תָּמְכוּ בְיָדָיו מִזֶּה אֶחָד וּמִזֶּה אֶחָד וַיְהִי יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה עַד בֹּא הַשָּׁמֶשׁ׃
verses.english: And Moses’ hands were heavy. And they took a stone and set it under him, and he sat on it, and Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one from this side and one from this side, and his hands were supported until the sunset.

tex.original: \hE{וִידֵי מֹשֶׁה כְּבֵדִים וַיִּקְחוּ אֶבֶן וַיָּשִׂימוּ תַחְתָּיו וַיֵּשֶׁב עָלֶיהָ וְאַהֲרֹן וְחוּר תָּמְכוּ בְיָדָיו מִזֶּה אֶחָד וּמִזֶּה אֶחָד וַיְהִי יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה עַד בֹּא הַשָּׁמֶשׁ׃}

verses.original: וַיַּחֲלֹשׁ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶת עֲמָלֵק וְאֶת עַמּוֹ לְפִי חָרֶב׃
verses.english: And Joshua defeated Amalek and his people by the sword.

tex.original: \hE{וַיַּחֲלֹשׁ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶת עֲמָלֵק וְאֶת עַמּוֹ לְפִי חָרֶב׃}
tex.english: \eE{And Joshua defeated Amalek and his people by the sword.}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה כְּתֹב זֹאת זִכָּרוֹן בַּסֵּפֶר וְשִׂים בְּאזְנֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כִּי מָחֹה אֶמְחֶה אֶת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמָיִם׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “Write this—a memorial—in a scroll and set it in Joshua’s ears, because I shall wipe out the memory of Amalek from under the skies!”

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה כְּתֹב זֹאת זִכָּרוֹן בַּסֵּפֶר וְשִׂים בְּאזְנֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כִּי מָחֹה אֶמְחֶה אֶת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמָיִם׃}

verses.original: וַיִּבֶן מֹשֶׁה מִזְבֵּחַ וַיִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ יְהֹוָה נִסִּי׃
verses.english: And Moses built an altar and called its name “YHWH is my standard.”

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּבֶן מֹשֶׁה מִזְבֵּחַ וַיִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ יְהֹוָה נִסִּי׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר כִּי יָד עַל כֵּס יָהּ מִלְחָמָה לַיהֹוָה בַּעֲמָלֵק מִדֹּר דֹּר׃
verses.english: And he said, “Because—hand on YH’s throne—YHWH has war against Amalek from generation to generation.”

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמֶר כִּי יָד עַל כֵּס יָהּ מִלְחָמָה לַיהֹוָה בַּעֲמָלֵק מִדֹּר דֹּר׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		hand on YH’s throne. No one is sure what this means. It
%		may be an oath
%		formula. The word for “throne,” Hebrew ks, may be a form
%		of kiss’, as
%		some versions have understood it.
%	}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁמַע יִתְרוֹ כֹהֵן מִדְיָן חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה אֵת כּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה אֱלֹהִים לְמֹשֶׁה וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַמּוֹ כִּי הוֹצִיא יְהֹוָה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: And Jethro, priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law, heard everything that God had done for Moses and for Israel, His people, that YHWH had brought Israel out from Egypt.

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּשְׁמַע יִתְרוֹ כֹהֵן מִדְיָן חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה אֵת כּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה אֱלֹהִים לְמֹשֶׁה וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַמּוֹ כִּי הוֹצִיא יְהֹוָה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרָיִם׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח יִתְרוֹ חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה אֶת צִפֹּרָה אֵשֶׁת מֹשֶׁה אַחַר שִׁלּוּחֶיהָ׃
verses.english: And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses’ wife, after her being sent off,

tex.original:
\hE{וַיִּקַּח יִתְרוֹ חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה אֶת צִפֹּרָה אֵשֶׁת מֹשֶׁה}
	\hRJE{אַחַר שִׁלּוּחֶיהָ׃}
tex.english:
\eE{And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses’ wife,}
	\eRJE{after her being sent off,}

verses.original: וְאֵת שְׁנֵי בָנֶיהָ אֲשֶׁר שֵׁם הָאֶחָד גֵּרְשֹׁם כִּי אָמַר גֵּר הָיִיתִי בְּאֶרֶץ נכְרִיָּה׃
verses.english: and her two sons, of whom one’s name was Gershom, because he said, “I was an alien in a foreign land,”

tex.original: \hE{וְאֵת שְׁנֵי בָנֶיהָ אֲשֶׁר שֵׁם הָאֶחָד גֵּרְשֹׁם כִּי אָמַר גֵּר הָיִיתִי בְּאֶרֶץ נכְרִיָּה׃}

verses.original: וְשֵׁם הָאֶחָד אֱלִיעֶזֶר כִּי אֱלֹהֵי אָבִי בְּעֶזְרִי וַיַּצִּלֵנִי מֵחֶרֶב פַּרְעֹה׃
verses.english: and one’s name was Eliezer, “because my father’s God was my help and rescued me from Pharaoh’s sword.”

tex.original: \hE{וְשֵׁם הָאֶחָד אֱלִיעֶזֶר כִּי אֱלֹהֵי אָבִי בְּעֶזְרִי וַיַּצִּלֵנִי מֵחֶרֶב פַּרְעֹה׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא יִתְרוֹ חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה וּבָנָיו וְאִשְׁתּוֹ אֶל מֹשֶׁה אֶל הַמִּדְבָּר אֲשֶׁר הוּא חֹנֶה שָׁם הַר הָאֱלֹהִים׃
verses.english: And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, and his sons and his wife came to Moses, to the wilderness in which he was camping, at the Mountain of God.

tex.original: \hE{וַיָּבֹא יִתְרוֹ חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה וּבָנָיו וְאִשְׁתּוֹ אֶל מֹשֶׁה אֶל הַמִּדְבָּר אֲשֶׁר הוּא חֹנֶה שָׁם הַר הָאֱלֹהִים׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל מֹשֶׁה אֲנִי חֹתֶנְךָ יִתְרוֹ בָּא אֵלֶיךָ וְאִשְׁתְּךָ וּשְׁנֵי בָנֶיהָ עִמָּהּ׃
verses.english: And he said to Moses, “I, your father-in-law, Jethro, have come to you, and your wife and her two sons with her.”

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל מֹשֶׁה אֲנִי חֹתֶנְךָ יִתְרוֹ בָּא אֵלֶיךָ וְאִשְׁתְּךָ וּשְׁנֵי בָנֶיהָ עִמָּהּ׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּצֵא מֹשֶׁה לִקְרַאת חֹתְנוֹ וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ וַיִּשַּׁק לוֹ וַיִּשְׁאֲלוּ אִישׁ לְרֵעֵהוּ לְשָׁלוֹם וַיָּבֹאוּ הָאֹהֱלָה׃
verses.english: And Moses went out to his father-in-law, and he bowed, and he kissed him, and they asked each other how they were, and they came to the tent.

tex.original: \hE{וַיֵּצֵא מֹשֶׁה לִקְרַאת חֹתְנוֹ וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ וַיִּשַּׁק לוֹ וַיִּשְׁאֲלוּ אִישׁ לְרֵעֵהוּ לְשָׁלוֹם וַיָּבֹאוּ הָאֹהֱלָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Moses went out to his father-in-law. Jethro arrives with
