%		witness. Rashi understands this to mean that he brings
%		witnesses. Ibn
%		Ezra suggests that it means that he brings a portion of
%		the torn animal
%		as evidence. The latter is the understanding of most
%		contemporary
%		translators.
%	}

verses.original: וְכִי יִשְׁאַל אִישׁ מֵעִם רֵעֵהוּ וְנִשְׁבַּר אוֹ מֵת בְּעָלָיו אֵין עִמּוֹ שַׁלֵּם יְשַׁלֵּם׃
verses.english: And if a man will ask it of his neighbor, and it is injured or dies, its owner not being with it, he shall pay.

tex.original: \hE{וְכִי יִשְׁאַל אִישׁ מֵעִם רֵעֵהוּ וְנִשְׁבַּר אוֹ מֵת בְּעָלָיו אֵין עִמּוֹ שַׁלֵּם יְשַׁלֵּם׃}

verses.original: אִם בְּעָלָיו עִמּוֹ לֹא יְשַׁלֵּם אִם שָׂכִיר הוּא בָּא בִּשְׂכָרוֹ׃
verses.english: If its owner is with it, he shall not pay. If it was hired, he has its hire coming to him.

tex.original: \hE{אִם בְּעָלָיו עִמּוֹ לֹא יְשַׁלֵּם אִם שָׂכִיר הוּא בָּא בִּשְׂכָרוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְכִי יְפַתֶּה אִישׁ בְּתוּלָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא אֹרָשָׂה וְשָׁכַב עִמָּהּ מָהֹר יִמְהָרֶנָּה לּוֹ לְאִשָּׁה׃
verses.english: “And if a man will deceive a virgin who is not betrothed, and he lies with her, he shall espouse her by a bride-price to him as a wife.

tex.original: \hE{וְכִי יְפַתֶּה אִישׁ בְּתוּלָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא אֹרָשָׂה וְשָׁכַב עִמָּהּ מָהֹר יִמְהָרֶנָּה לּוֹ לְאִשָּׁה׃}

verses.original: אִם מָאֵן יְמָאֵן אָבִיהָ לְתִתָּהּ לוֹ כֶּסֶף יִשְׁקֹל כְּמֹהַר הַבְּתוּלֹת׃
verses.english: If her father will refuse to give her to him, he shall weigh out money corresponding to the bride-price of virgins.

tex.original: \hE{אִם מָאֵן יְמָאֵן אָבִיהָ לְתִתָּהּ לוֹ כֶּסֶף יִשְׁקֹל כְּמֹהַר הַבְּתוּלֹת׃}

verses.original: מְכַשֵּׁפָה לֹא תְחַיֶּה׃
verses.english: “You shall not let a witch live.

tex.original: \hE{מְכַשֵּׁפָה לֹא תְחַיֶּה׃}
tex.english: \eE{“You shall not let a witch live.}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		a witch. Why does the text condemn only women and not
%		male sorcerers?
%		Males are identified as practicing magic as well, as in
%		the case of the
%		Egyptian magicians (Exod 7:11). The feminine form of
%		this word occurs
%		only here out of the entire Tanak. And the Septuagint
%		has the masculine
%		plural (which is used to include both men and women)
%		here instead of the
%		Masoretic Text’s feminine singular. This suggests that
%		the original text
%		forbids the practice of magic by either men or women
%		(sorcerers or
%		witches). Note also: the text does not deny that magic
%		works. (On the
%		contrary, the Egyptian magicians can turn staffs into
%		snakes.) It
%		forbids the practice of magic.
%	}

verses.original: כּל שֹׁכֵב עִם בְּהֵמָה מוֹת יוּמָת׃
verses.english: “Anyone who lies with an animal shall be put to death.

tex.original: \hE{כּל שֹׁכֵב עִם בְּהֵמָה מוֹת יוּמָת׃}
tex.english: \eE{“Anyone who lies with an animal shall be put to death.}

verses.original: זֹבֵחַ לָאֱלֹהִים יחֳרָם בִּלְתִּי לַיהֹוָה לְבַדּוֹ׃
verses.english: “One who sacrifices to gods shall be completely destroyed—except to YHWH alone.

tex.original: \hE{זֹבֵחַ לָאֱלֹהִים יחֳרָם בִּלְתִּי לַיהֹוָה לְבַדּוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		completely destroyed. Hebrew erem refers to the rule of
%		destroying an
%		individual or community along with all his family,
%		animals, and
%		possessions and thus dedicating them to the deity rather
%		than profiting
%		in any way from them.
%	}

verses.original: וְגֵר לֹא תוֹנֶה וְלֹא תִלְחָצֶנּוּ כִּי גֵרִים הֱיִיתֶם בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: “And you shall not persecute an alien, and you shall not oppress him, because you were aliens in the land of Egypt.

tex.original: \hE{וְגֵר לֹא תוֹנֶה וְלֹא תִלְחָצֶנּוּ כִּי גֵרִים הֱיִיתֶם בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃}

verses.original: כּל אַלְמָנָה וְיָתוֹם לֹא תְעַנּוּן׃
verses.english: “You shall not degrade any widow or orphan.

tex.original: \hE{כּל אַלְמָנָה וְיָתוֹם לֹא תְעַנּוּן׃}
tex.english: \eE{“You shall not degrade any widow or orphan.}

verses.original: אִם עַנֵּה תְעַנֶּה אֹתוֹ כִּי אִם צָעֹק יִצְעַק אֵלַי שָׁמֹעַ אֶשְׁמַע צַעֲקָתוֹ׃
verses.english: If you will degrade them, when they will cry out to me I’ll hear their cry,

tex.original: \hE{אִם עַנֵּה תְעַנֶּה אֹתוֹ כִּי אִם צָעֹק יִצְעַק אֵלַי שָׁמֹעַ אֶשְׁמַע צַעֲקָתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְחָרָה אַפִּי וְהָרַגְתִּי אֶתְכֶם בֶּחָרֶב וְהָיוּ נְשֵׁיכֶם אַלְמָנוֹת וּבְנֵיכֶם יְתֹמִים׃
verses.english: and my anger will flare, and I’ll kill you with a sword, and your wives will be widows and your children orphans!

tex.original: \hE{וְחָרָה אַפִּי וְהָרַגְתִּי אֶתְכֶם בֶּחָרֶב וְהָיוּ נְשֵׁיכֶם אַלְמָנוֹת וּבְנֵיכֶם יְתֹמִים׃}

verses.original: אִם כֶּסֶף תַּלְוֶה אֶת עַמִּי אֶת הֶעָנִי עִמָּךְ לֹא תִהְיֶה לוֹ כְּנֹשֶׁה לֹא תְשִׂימוּן עָלָיו נֶשֶׁךְ׃
verses.english: “If you will lend money to my people, to the poor who is with you, you shall not be like a creditor to him; you shall not impose interest on him.

tex.original: \hE{אִם כֶּסֶף תַּלְוֶה אֶת עַמִּי אֶת הֶעָנִי עִמָּךְ לֹא תִהְיֶה לוֹ כְּנֹשֶׁה לֹא תְשִׂימוּן עָלָיו נֶשֶׁךְ׃}

verses.original: אִם חָבֹל תַּחְבֹּל שַׂלְמַת רֵעֶךָ עַד בֹּא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ תְּשִׁיבֶנּוּ לוֹ׃
verses.english: If you take your neighbor’s clothing as security, you shall give it back to him by the sunset,

tex.original: \hE{אִם חָבֹל תַּחְבֹּל שַׂלְמַת רֵעֶךָ עַד בֹּא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ תְּשִׁיבֶנּוּ לוֹ׃}

verses.original: כִּי הִוא כְסוּתֹה לְבַדָּהּ הִוא שִׂמְלָתוֹ לְעֹרוֹ בַּמֶּה יִשְׁכָּב וְהָיָה כִּי יִצְעַק אֵלַי וְשָׁמַעְתִּי כִּי חַנּוּן אָנִי׃
verses.english: because it is his only apparel; it is his clothing for his skin. In what will he sleep? And it will be, when he will cry out to me, that I shall listen, because I am gracious.

tex.original: \hE{כִּי הִוא כְסוּתֹה לְבַדָּהּ הִוא שִׂמְלָתוֹ לְעֹרוֹ בַּמֶּה יִשְׁכָּב וְהָיָה כִּי יִצְעַק אֵלַי וְשָׁמַעְתִּי כִּי חַנּוּן אָנִי׃}

verses.original: אֱלֹהִים לֹא תְקַלֵּל וְנָשִׂיא בְעַמְּךָ לֹא תָאֹר׃
verses.english: “You shall not blaspheme God, and you shall not curse a chieftain among your people.

tex.original: \hE{אֱלֹהִים לֹא תְקַלֵּל וְנָשִׂיא בְעַמְּךָ לֹא תָאֹר׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		chieftain. Hebrew nî’. Elsewhere in the Torah the text
%		refers to the
%		chieftain of a tribe (Num 2:3–29) or of a priestly
%		family (Num 3:24–35)
%		or of a city (Gen 34:2). Here it may allude to a king of
%		Israel, “a
%		chieftain among your people” (as in 1 Kings 11:34; Ezek
%		34:24), or it
%		may mean any of these leaders.
%	}

verses.original: מְלֵאָתְךָ וְדִמְעֲךָ לֹא תְאַחֵר בְּכוֹר בָּנֶיךָ תִּתֶּן לִי׃
verses.english: “You shall not delay your fulfillment and your flowing. “You shall give me the firstborn of your sons.

tex.original: \hE{מְלֵאָתְךָ וְדִמְעֲךָ לֹא תְאַחֵר בְּכוֹר בָּנֶיךָ תִּתֶּן לִי׃}

verses.original: כֵּן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְשֹׁרְךָ לְצֹאנֶךָ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים יִהְיֶה עִם אִמּוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי תִּתְּנוֹ לִי׃
verses.english: “You shall do this to your ox and to your sheep: Seven days it will be with its mother. On the eighth day you shall give it to me.

tex.original: \hE{כֵּן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְשֹׁרְךָ לְצֹאנֶךָ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים יִהְיֶה עִם אִמּוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי תִּתְּנוֹ לִי׃}

verses.original: וְאַנְשֵׁי קֹדֶשׁ תִּהְיוּן לִי וּבָשָׂר בַּשָּׂדֶה טְרֵפָה לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ לַכֶּלֶב תַּשְׁלִכוּן אֹתוֹ׃
verses.english: “And you shall be holy people to me. “And you shall not eat meat in the field that is torn. You shall throw it to the dog.

tex.original: \hE{וְאַנְשֵׁי קֹדֶשׁ תִּהְיוּן לִי וּבָשָׂר בַּשָּׂדֶה טְרֵפָה לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ לַכֶּלֶב תַּשְׁלִכוּן אֹתוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		meat that is torn. This refers to the meat of an animal
%		that was killed
%		by another animal rather than having been killed in the
%		sacred manner
%		prescribed by the law. The word for “torn” (Hebrew trph)
%		later came to
%		be used for any prohibited foods.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא תִשָּׂא שֵׁמַע שָׁוְא אַל תָּשֶׁת יָדְךָ עִם רָשָׁע לִהְיֹת עֵד חָמָס׃
verses.english: “You shall not bring up a false report. Do not join your hand with a wicked person to be a malevolent witness.

tex.original: \hE{לֹא תִשָּׂא שֵׁמַע שָׁוְא אַל תָּשֶׁת יָדְךָ עִם רָשָׁע לִהְיֹת עֵד חָמָס׃}

verses.original: לֹא תִהְיֶה אַחֲרֵי רַבִּים לְרָעֹת וְלֹא תַעֲנֶה עַל רִב לִנְטֹת אַחֲרֵי רַבִּים לְהַטֹּת׃
verses.english: You shall not be following many to do bad. And you shall not testify about a dispute to bend following many, to bend it.

tex.original: \hE{לֹא תִהְיֶה אַחֲרֵי רַבִּים לְרָעֹת וְלֹא תַעֲנֶה עַל רִב לִנְטֹת אַחֲרֵי רַבִּים לְהַטֹּת׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		not be following many to do bad. Do not follow a group,
%		a crowd, a
%		majority if what they are doing is wrong. Do not do it
%		for acceptance,
%		for the secure feeling of being in a group, or for the
%		sadistic pleasure
%		of being able to exclude someone. It is easy to be
%		hurtful in a group.
%		And it is easy to keep silent when one’s group does
%		harm—or when its
%		leaders do harm from their position, which derives its
%		power from the
%		group. All of this is forbidden. It is utterly
%		inconsistent with the
%		Torah’s conceptions of what a human should be and how
%		one should behave
%		toward other human beings. This comment should be
%		unnecessary. Footnote
%		23:2. to bend following many, to bend it. When giving
%		testimony or when
%		sitting in judgment, do not incline toward the majority
%		of those
%		involved in the case or toward the majority of the
%		public. To “bend”
%		toward them is to “bend” justice.
%	}

verses.original: וְדָל לֹא תֶהְדַּר בְּרִיבוֹ׃
verses.english: And you shall not favor a weak person in his dispute.

tex.original: \hE{וְדָל לֹא תֶהְדַּר בְּרִיבוֹ׃}
tex.english: \eE{And you shall not favor a weak person in his dispute.}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		you shall not favor a weak person. Of course one should
%		not favor the
%		majority, or the rich, or the famous, or the powerful.
%		Of course we
%		should not bend the law for bad motives. We are reminded
%		that we also
%		must not bend the law or the truth even for good
%		motives, such as
%		feelings of compassion for the poor. Compare Lev 19:15.
%	}

verses.original: כִּי תִפְגַּע שׁוֹר אֹיִבְךָ אוֹ חֲמֹרוֹ תֹּעֶה הָשֵׁב תְּשִׁיבֶנּוּ לוֹ׃
verses.english: “If you will happen upon your enemy’s ox or his ass straying, you shall bring it back to him.

tex.original: \hE{כִּי תִפְגַּע שׁוֹר אֹיִבְךָ אוֹ חֲמֹרוֹ תֹּעֶה הָשֵׁב תְּשִׁיבֶנּוּ לוֹ׃}

verses.original: כִּי תִרְאֶה חֲמוֹר שֹׂנַאֲךָ רֹבֵץ תַּחַת מַשָּׂאוֹ וְחָדַלְתָּ מֵעֲזֹב לוֹ עָזֹב תַּעֲזֹב עִמּוֹ׃
verses.english: If you will see the ass of someone who hates you sagging under its burden, and you would hold back from helping him: you shall help with him.

tex.original: \hE{כִּי תִרְאֶה חֲמוֹר שֹׂנַאֲךָ רֹבֵץ תַּחַת מַשָּׂאוֹ וְחָדַלְתָּ מֵעֲזֹב לוֹ עָזֹב תַּעֲזֹב עִמּוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		you would hold back from helping him. That is, you would
%		hold back from
%		helping your adversary. Footnote 23:5. help. The Hebrew
%		‘zb (to leave)
%		is difficult. One possibility, suggested here, is to
%		read the word as
%		‘zr (to help). Alternatively, it may mean: “If you will
%		see the ass of
%		someone who hates you sagging under its burden, then you
%		shall hold back
%		from leaving it for him; you shall leave it with him.”
%		That is, do not
%		leave it for him to handle himself; do what is necessary
%		to assist and
%		leave it back with him. By any reading, though, the main
%		point is that
%		one must be of help, even to someone who bears one ill
%		will—perhaps
%		especially to someone who bears ill will.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא תַטֶּה מִשְׁפַּט אֶבְיֹנְךָ בְּרִיבוֹ׃
verses.english: “You shall not bend the judgment of your poor in his dispute.

tex.original: \hE{לֹא תַטֶּה מִשְׁפַּט אֶבְיֹנְךָ בְּרִיבוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		your poor. It is natural to use the phrase “your enemy,”
%		as in the
%		preceding verses, but we would not readily expect “your
%		poor”
%		linguistically. But the issue is not linguistic. It is
%		moral. The poor
%		are not neutral as a group. They are your poor, your
%		responsibility.
%	}

verses.original: מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק וְנָקִי וְצַדִּיק אַל תַּהֲרֹג כִּי לֹא אַצְדִּיק רָשָׁע׃
verses.english: “You shall keep far from a word of a lie, and do not kill an innocent and a virtuous person, because I shall not vindicate a wicked person.

tex.original: \hE{מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק וְנָקִי וְצַדִּיק אַל תַּהֲרֹג כִּי לֹא אַצְדִּיק רָשָׁע׃}

verses.original: וְשֹׁחַד לֹא תִקָּח כִּי הַשֹּׁחַד יְעַוֵּר פִּקְחִים וִיסַלֵּף דִּבְרֵי צַדִּיקִים׃
verses.english: “And you shall not take a bribe, because bribery will blind those who can see and will undermine the words of the virtuous.

tex.original: \hE{וְשֹׁחַד לֹא תִקָּח כִּי הַשֹּׁחַד יְעַוֵּר פִּקְחִים וִיסַלֵּף דִּבְרֵי צַדִּיקִים׃}

verses.original: וְגֵר לֹא תִלְחָץ וְאַתֶּם יְדַעְתֶּם אֶת נֶפֶשׁ הַגֵּר כִּי גֵרִים הֱיִיתֶם בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: “And you shall not oppress an alien—since you know the alien’s soul, because you were aliens in the land of Egypt.

tex.original: \hE{וְגֵר לֹא תִלְחָץ וְאַתֶּם יְדַעְתֶּם אֶת נֶפֶשׁ הַגֵּר כִּי גֵרִים הֱיִיתֶם בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		you know the alien’s soul. This verse, commanding not to
%		oppress an
%		alien residing among Israel, repeats a commandment that
%		has already been
%		given just a little earlier, in 22:20. But it says it
%		even more
%		eloquently. You have been aliens, so you know the alien.
%		You know how he
%		or she feels oppression inside. Few of the laws in this
%		code have an
%		extra line of explanation like this. Notably, another
%		law protecting
%		aliens in the preceding chapter also adds a line of
%		explanation (22:20).
%		Again, the treatment of a non-Israelite who is within
%		Israel’s power is
%		singled out in a special way.
%	}

verses.original: וְשֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים תִּזְרַע אֶת אַרְצֶךָ וְאָסַפְתָּ אֶת תְּבוּאָתָהּ׃
verses.english: “And six years you shall sow your land and gather its produce;

tex.original: \hE{וְשֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים תִּזְרַע אֶת אַרְצֶךָ וְאָסַפְתָּ אֶת תְּבוּאָתָהּ׃}

verses.original: וְהַשְּׁבִיעִת תִּשְׁמְטֶנָּה וּנְטַשְׁתָּהּ וְאָכְלוּ אֶבְיֹנֵי עַמֶּךָ וְיִתְרָם תֹּאכַל חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה כֵּן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְכַרְמְךָ לְזֵיתֶךָ׃
verses.english: and the seventh: you shall let it lie fallow and leave it, and your people’s indigent will eat, and what they leave the animal of the field will eat. You shall do this to your vineyard, to your olives.

tex.original: \hE{וְהַשְּׁבִיעִת תִּשְׁמְטֶנָּה וּנְטַשְׁתָּהּ וְאָכְלוּ אֶבְיֹנֵי עַמֶּךָ וְיִתְרָם תֹּאכַל חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה כֵּן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְכַרְמְךָ לְזֵיתֶךָ׃}

verses.original: שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תַּעֲשֶׂה מַעֲשֶׂיךָ וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי תִּשְׁבֹּת לְמַעַן יָנוּחַ שׁוֹרְךָ וַחֲמֹרֶךָ וְיִנָּפֵשׁ בֶּן אֲמָתְךָ וְהַגֵּר׃
verses.english: “Six days you shall do the things you do, and on the seventh day you shall cease, so that your ox and your ass will rest, and your maid’s son and the alien will be refreshed.

tex.original: \hE{שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תַּעֲשֶׂה מַעֲשֶׂיךָ וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי תִּשְׁבֹּת לְמַעַן יָנוּחַ שׁוֹרְךָ וַחֲמֹרֶךָ וְיִנָּפֵשׁ בֶּן אֲמָתְךָ וְהַגֵּר׃}

verses.original: וּבְכֹל אֲשֶׁר אָמַרְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶם תִּשָּׁמֵרוּ וְשֵׁם אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים לֹא תַזְכִּירוּ לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל פִּיךָ׃
verses.english: “And you shall be watchful in everything that I have said to you. And you shall not commemorate the name of other gods. Let it not be heard on your mouth.

tex.original: \hE{וּבְכֹל אֲשֶׁר אָמַרְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶם תִּשָּׁמֵרוּ וְשֵׁם אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים לֹא תַזְכִּירוּ לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל פִּיךָ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		commemorate. Other translations take this to mean
%		“mention,” i.e., that
%		one cannot even say the name of another god—but compare
%		Exod 20:21,
%		where this same word appears to refer to mentioning
%		YHWH’s name
%		institutionally. I therefore understand this verse to
%		mean that one is
%		commanded not to say another god’s name in a setting of
%		worship.
%	}

verses.original: שָׁלֹשׁ רְגָלִים תָּחֹג לִי בַּשָּׁנָה׃
verses.english: “You shall celebrate three pilgrimages for me in the year:

tex.original: \hE{שָׁלֹשׁ רְגָלִים תָּחֹג לִי בַּשָּׁנָה׃}
tex.english: \eE{“You shall celebrate three pilgrimages for me in the year:}

verses.original: אֶת חַג הַמַּצּוֹת תִּשְׁמֹר שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצּוֹת כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִךָ לְמוֹעֵד חֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב כִּי בוֹ יָצָאתָ מִמִּצְרָיִם וְלֹא יֵרָאוּ פָנַי רֵיקָם׃
verses.english: “You shall observe the Festival of Unleavened Bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time of the month of Abib, because you went out of Egypt in it. And none shall appear before me empty.

tex.original: \hE{אֶת חַג הַמַּצּוֹת תִּשְׁמֹר שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצּוֹת כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִךָ לְמוֹעֵד חֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב כִּי בוֹ יָצָאתָ מִמִּצְרָיִם וְלֹא יֵרָאוּ פָנַי רֵיקָם׃}
tex.english:
\eE{
		“You shall observe the Festival of Unleavened Bread. Seven
		days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you,
		at the appointed time of the month of Abib, because you
		went out of Egypt in it. And none shall appear before me
		empty.
	}

verses.original: וְחַג הַקָּצִיר בִּכּוּרֵי מַעֲשֶׂיךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּזְרַע בַּשָּׂדֶה וְחַג הָאָסִף בְּצֵאת הַשָּׁנָה בְּאסְפְּךָ אֶת מַעֲשֶׂיךָ מִן הַשָּׂדֶה׃
verses.english: “And the Festival of Harvest, the first fruits of what you do, of what you will sow in the field. “And the Festival of Gathering, at the end of the year, when you gather what you have done from the field.

tex.original: \hE{וְחַג הַקָּצִיר בִּכּוּרֵי מַעֲשֶׂיךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּזְרַע בַּשָּׂדֶה וְחַג הָאָסִף בְּצֵאת הַשָּׁנָה בְּאסְפְּךָ אֶת מַעֲשֶׂיךָ מִן הַשָּׂדֶה׃}

verses.original: שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים בַּשָּׁנָה יֵרָאֶה כּל זְכוּרְךָ אֶל פְּנֵי הָאָדֹן יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: “Three times in the year every male of yours shall appear in front of the Lord YHWH.

tex.original: \hE{שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים בַּשָּׁנָה יֵרָאֶה כּל זְכוּרְךָ אֶל פְּנֵי הָאָדֹן יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: לֹא תִזְבַּח עַל חָמֵץ דַּם זִבְחִי וְלֹא יָלִין חֵלֶב חַגִּי עַד בֹּקֶר׃
verses.english: “You shall not offer the blood of my sacrifice on leavened bread. And the fat of my festival shall not remain until morning.

tex.original: \hE{לֹא תִזְבַּח עַל חָמֵץ דַּם זִבְחִי וְלֹא יָלִין חֵלֶב חַגִּי עַד בֹּקֶר׃}

verses.original: רֵאשִׁית בִּכּוּרֵי אַדְמָתְךָ תָּבִיא בֵּית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תְבַשֵּׁל גְּדִי בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ׃
verses.english: “You shall bring the first of the firstfruits of your land to the house of YHWH, your God. “You shall not cook a kid in its mother’s milk.

tex.original: \hE{רֵאשִׁית בִּכּוּרֵי אַדְמָתְךָ תָּבִיא בֵּית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תְבַשֵּׁל גְּדִי בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the house of YHWH. This is a reference to the Temple,
%		the building that
%		will one day be the only sanctioned place of sacrifice
%		and the central
%		place of worship. The first house of YHWH will be
%		located at Shiloh. The
%		second and third will be located at Jerusalem. Footnote
%		23:19. a kid in
%		its mother’s milk. A Canaanite (Ugaritic) text may
%		picture the chief
%		god, El, having kid cooked in milk. This biblical law
%		may thus be a
%		prohibition against eating something that was regarded
%		as a food for a
%		deity. This explanation is uncertain because the
%		Canaanite text does not
%		specify mother’s milk, and the word there that is read
%		as “kid” is
%		partly effaced. Alternatively, the biblical law may be a
%		moral one,
%		consistent with other biblical law, which prohibits
%		sacrificing an ox or
%		sheep on the same day as its offspring (Lev 22:28) or
%		taking a mother
%		bird along with her eggs in the wild (Deut 22:6–7). This
%		law came to be
%		taken in later Jewish practice to amount to a complete
%		separation of
%		meat and dairy consumption. This practice is not
%		commanded in the Torah
%		but is rather based on postbiblical rabbinic rulings.
%	}

verses.original: הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי שֹׁלֵחַ מַלְאָךְ לְפָנֶיךָ לִשְׁמרְךָ בַּדָּרֶךְ וְלַהֲבִיאֲךָ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר הֲכִנֹתִי׃
verses.english: “Here, I’m sending an angel ahead of you to watch over you on the way and to bring you to the place that I’ve prepared.

tex.original: \hE{הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי שֹׁלֵחַ מַלְאָךְ לְפָנֶיךָ לִשְׁמרְךָ בַּדָּרֶךְ וְלַהֲבִיאֲךָ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר הֲכִנֹתִי׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		I’m sending an angel ahead of you. This will be repeated
%		twice (32:34;
%		33:2). It is another recurrence of language from the
%		accounts of the
%		patriarchs: Abraham told his servant that God will send
%		“His angel ahead
%		of you,” which would lead to the success of his mission
%		to get a wife
%		for Isaac (Gen 24:7; see also 32:4). That is now a
%		reminder that the
%		preceding angel on a journey is an assurance and
%		protection.
%	}

verses.original: הִשָּׁמֶר מִפָּנָיו וּשְׁמַע בְּקֹלוֹ אַל תַּמֵּר בּוֹ כִּי לֹא יִשָּׂא לְפִשְׁעֲכֶם כִּי שְׁמִי בְּקִרְבּוֹ׃
verses.english: Be watchful in front of him and listen to his voice. Don’t rebel against him, because he will not bear your offense, because my name is within him.

tex.original: \hE{הִשָּׁמֶר מִפָּנָיו וּשְׁמַע בְּקֹלוֹ אַל תַּמֵּר בּוֹ כִּי לֹא יִשָּׂא לְפִשְׁעֲכֶם כִּי שְׁמִי בְּקִרְבּוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		rebel. The Hebrew, tammr, here in the Masoretic Text has
%		the form of a
%		Hiphil of the root mrr, meaning “to make bitter.” But
%		these vowel points
%		are generally understood to be incorrect. The word
%		should rather be read
%		as temer, a form of the root mrh, meaning “to rebel,”
%		which is how the
%		Greek reads. The theme of rebellion will figure strongly
%		in the events
%		to come. Alternatively, one might argue that it is an
%		allusion to the
%		story of the bitter waters at Marah, which was the
%		people’s first
%		rebellion after crossing the Red Sea.
%	}

verses.original: כִּי אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע בְּקֹלוֹ וְעָשִׂיתָ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר אֲדַבֵּר וְאָיַבְתִּי אֶת אֹיְבֶיךָ וְצַרְתִּי אֶת צֹרְרֶיךָ׃
verses.english: But if you will listen to his voice and do everything that I speak, then I’ll be an enemy to your enemies and an opponent to your opponents.

tex.original: \hE{כִּי אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע בְּקֹלוֹ וְעָשִׂיתָ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר אֲדַבֵּר וְאָיַבְתִּי אֶת אֹיְבֶיךָ וְצַרְתִּי אֶת צֹרְרֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: כִּי יֵלֵךְ מַלְאָכִי לְפָנֶיךָ וֶהֱבִיאֲךָ אֶל הָאֱמֹרִי וְהַחִתִּי וְהַפְּרִזִּי וְהַכְּנַעֲנִי הַחִוִּי וְהַיְבוּסִי וְהִכְחַדְתִּיו׃
verses.english: When my angel will go ahead of you and will bring you to the Amorite and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Canaanite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, and I obliterate them,

tex.original: \hE{כִּי יֵלֵךְ מַלְאָכִי לְפָנֶיךָ וֶהֱבִיאֲךָ אֶל הָאֱמֹרִי וְהַחִתִּי וְהַפְּרִזִּי וְהַכְּנַעֲנִי הַחִוִּי וְהַיְבוּסִי וְהִכְחַדְתִּיו׃}

verses.original: לֹא תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה לֵאלֹהֵיהֶם וְלֹא תעבְדֵם וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם כִּי הָרֵס תְּהָרְסֵם וְשַׁבֵּר תְּשַׁבֵּר מַצֵּבֹתֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: you shall not bow to their gods, and you shall not serve them, and you shall not do like the things they do; but you shall tear them down and shatter their pillars.

tex.original: \hE{לֹא תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה לֵאלֹהֵיהֶם וְלֹא תעבְדֵם וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כְּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם כִּי הָרֵס תְּהָרְסֵם וְשַׁבֵּר תְּשַׁבֵּר מַצֵּבֹתֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַעֲבַדְתֶּם אֵת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וּבֵרַךְ אֶת לַחְמְךָ וְאֶת מֵימֶיךָ וַהֲסִרֹתִי מַחֲלָה מִקִּרְבֶּךָ׃
verses.english: And you will serve YHWH, your God, and He will bless your bread and your water, and I shall turn sickness away from within you.

tex.original: \hE{וַעֲבַדְתֶּם אֵת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וּבֵרַךְ אֶת לַחְמְךָ וְאֶת מֵימֶיךָ וַהֲסִרֹתִי מַחֲלָה מִקִּרְבֶּךָ׃}

verses.original: לֹא תִהְיֶה מְשַׁכֵּלָה וַעֲקָרָה בְּאַרְצֶךָ אֶת מִסְפַּר יָמֶיךָ אֲמַלֵּא׃
verses.english: There won’t be a bereaved woman and an infertile woman in your land. I shall fulfill the number of your days.

tex.original: \hE{לֹא תִהְיֶה מְשַׁכֵּלָה וַעֲקָרָה בְּאַרְצֶךָ אֶת מִסְפַּר יָמֶיךָ אֲמַלֵּא׃}

verses.original: אֶת אֵימָתִי אֲשַׁלַּח לְפָנֶיךָ וְהַמֹּתִי אֶת כּל הָעָם אֲשֶׁר תָּבֹא בָּהֶם וְנָתַתִּי אֶת כּל אֹיְבֶיךָ אֵלֶיךָ עֹרֶף׃
verses.english: I shall have my terror go ahead of you, and I shall throw all the people against whom you come into tumult, and I shall give all your enemies to you by the back.

tex.original: \hE{אֶת אֵימָתִי אֲשַׁלַּח לְפָנֶיךָ וְהַמֹּתִי אֶת כּל הָעָם אֲשֶׁר תָּבֹא בָּהֶם וְנָתַתִּי אֶת כּל אֹיְבֶיךָ אֵלֶיךָ עֹרֶף׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		by the back. The enemies will turn their backs and flee.
%		This image of
%		Israel’s enemies occurs in 2 Sam 22:41 and Ps 18:41. As
%		a terrifying
%		lesson, it is reversed in a case of a serious violation
%		by an Israelite
%		of a divine command, and then it is Israel that turns
%		its back to its
%		enemies (Josh 7:8,12).
%	}

verses.original: וְשָׁלַחְתִּי אֶת הַצִּרְעָה לְפָנֶיךָ וְגֵרְשָׁה אֶת הַחִוִּי אֶת הַכְּנַעֲנִי וְאֶת הַחִתִּי מִלְּפָנֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And I shall send the hornet ahead of you, and it will drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite from in front of you.

tex.original: \hE{וְשָׁלַחְתִּי אֶת הַצִּרְעָה לְפָנֶיךָ וְגֵרְשָׁה אֶת הַחִוִּי אֶת הַכְּנַעֲנִי וְאֶת הַחִתִּי מִלְּפָנֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: לֹא אֲגָרְשֶׁנּוּ מִפָּנֶיךָ בְּשָׁנָה אֶחָת פֶּן תִּהְיֶה הָאָרֶץ שְׁמָמָה וְרַבָּה עָלֶיךָ חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה׃
verses.english: I won’t drive them out from in front of you in one year, or else the land will be a devastation, and the animal of the field will be many at you.

tex.original: \hE{לֹא אֲגָרְשֶׁנּוּ מִפָּנֶיךָ בְּשָׁנָה אֶחָת פֶּן תִּהְיֶה הָאָרֶץ שְׁמָמָה וְרַבָּה עָלֶיךָ חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה׃}

verses.original: מְעַט מְעַט אֲגָרְשֶׁנּוּ מִפָּנֶיךָ עַד אֲשֶׁר תִּפְרֶה וְנָחַלְתָּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.english: Little by little I shall drive them out from in front of you, until you will be fruitful, and you will have a legacy of the land.

tex.original: \hE{מְעַט מְעַט אֲגָרְשֶׁנּוּ מִפָּנֶיךָ עַד אֲשֶׁר תִּפְרֶה וְנָחַלְתָּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ׃}

verses.original: וְשַׁתִּי אֶת גְּבֻלְךָ מִיַּם סוּף וְעַד יָם פְּלִשְׁתִּים וּמִמִּדְבָּר עַד הַנָּהָר כִּי אֶתֵּן בְּיֶדְכֶם אֵת יֹשְׁבֵי הָאָרֶץ וְגֵרַשְׁתָּמוֹ מִפָּנֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And I shall set your border from the Red Sea to the sea of the Philistines and from the wilderness to the river, because I shall put the residents of the land in your hand, and you’ll drive them out from in front of you.

tex.original: \hE{וְשַׁתִּי אֶת גְּבֻלְךָ מִיַּם סוּף וְעַד יָם פְּלִשְׁתִּים וּמִמִּדְבָּר עַד הַנָּהָר כִּי אֶתֵּן בְּיֶדְכֶם אֵת יֹשְׁבֵי הָאָרֶץ וְגֵרַשְׁתָּמוֹ מִפָּנֶיךָ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the Red Sea. This refers to the eastern arm of the Red
%		Sea, presently
%		the site of Eilat. The promised territory of Israel is
%		never conceived
%		of in the Torah as extending all the way across the
%		Sinai Peninsula to
%		the western arm of the Red Sea. It stops at the “river
%		of Egypt,” the
%		Wadi el-‘Arîsh, which is north of the eastern arm of the
%		Red Sea.
%		Footnote 23:31. the sea of the Philistines. The
%		Mediterranean Sea. The
%		Philistines came across the Mediterranean from the Greek
%		islands. They
%		lived in cities near the Mediterranean coast (Ashdod,
%		Ashkelon, Ekron,
%		Gath, and Gaza). Footnote 23:31. the river. This is
%		commonly understood
%		to refer to the Euphrates.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא תִכְרֹת לָהֶם וְלֵאלֹהֵיהֶם בְּרִית׃
verses.english: You shall not make a covenant with them and with their gods.

tex.original: \hE{לֹא תִכְרֹת לָהֶם וְלֵאלֹהֵיהֶם בְּרִית׃}

verses.original: לֹא יֵשְׁבוּ בְּאַרְצְךָ פֶּן יַחֲטִיאוּ אֹתְךָ לִי כִּי תַעֲבֹד אֶת אֱלֹהֵיהֶם כִּי יִהְיֶה לְךָ לְמוֹקֵשׁ׃
verses.english: They shall not live in your land, in case they will make you sin against me when you’ll serve their gods, because it will be a trap for you.”

tex.original: \hE{לֹא יֵשְׁבוּ בְּאַרְצְךָ פֶּן יַחֲטִיאוּ אֹתְךָ לִי כִּי תַעֲבֹד אֶת אֱלֹהֵיהֶם כִּי יִהְיֶה לְךָ לְמוֹקֵשׁ׃}

verses.original: וְאֶל מֹשֶׁה אָמַר עֲלֵה אֶל יְהֹוָה אַתָּה וְאַהֲרֹן נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא וְשִׁבְעִים מִזִּקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶם מֵרָחֹק׃
verses.english: And He said to Moses, “Come up to YHWH: you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s elders, and bow from a distance.

tex.original: \hE{וְאֶל מֹשֶׁה אָמַר עֲלֵה אֶל יְהֹוָה אַתָּה וְאַהֲרֹן נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא וְשִׁבְעִים מִזִּקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶם מֵרָחֹק׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		from a distance. This account has a multitude of
%		parallels to the
%		account of the binding of Isaac (Genesis 22): Moses says
%		the same words
%		to the elders that Abraham says to the servant boys:
%		“Sit here … we’ll
%		come back to you.” The Exodus account has servant boys
%		(n‘rîm) as well.
%		Both accounts use the term “from a distance” (mrq). Both
%		use the term
%		“to bow” (hištawôt). Both Moses and Abraham come up a
%		mountain. Both
%		have a burnt offering (ha‘lôt ‘ôlh). The two accounts
%		share a chain of
%		ten verbs: “and he said,” “and he took … and he set,”
%		“and he got up
%		early,” “and he built an altar,” “and he put out his
%		hand,” “and he/it
%		was,” “and he/they got up,” “and he/they came,” “and
%		he/they saw.” All
%		these parallels alert us to the fact that some important
%		connection
%		exists here. The culminating parallels indicate what
%		that connection is:
%		Abraham is rewarded at the end “because you did this
%		thing”; and the
%		people in Exodus promise that “We’ll do all the things.”
%		Abraham is
%		rewarded because “you listened to my voice”; and Exodus
%		reports that
%		“they said with one voice,” and they say, “we’ll
%		listen.” So (1) this is
%		a reminder that the merit of Abraham remains the basis
%		on which all of
%		this now happens. (2) This is a fulfillment of promises
%		made following
%		Abraham’s acts of extraordinary obedience. And (3)
%		Abraham’s obedience
%		is an example for the people to emulate. The contrast is
%		striking as
%		well. Abraham’s obedience is the centerpiece of the
%		first story. In this
%		second story, the people will soon commit their worst
%		act of
%		disobedience, the golden calf event. Note also: The
%		first story is at
%		“the mountain of YHWH.” The second is at “the mountain
%		of God.” And both
%		state that they are about divine appearances. The divine
%		appearances
%		mark the sacredness of the two mountain locations. The
%		“mountain of God”
%		is Horeb/Sinai. The identity of the “mountain of YHWH”
%		is uncertain,
%		although elsewhere it refers to the location of the
%		Temple in Jerusalem.
%		The parallels of these two stories connect the mountain
%		where the
%		greatest revelation takes place to the mountain where
%		the divine promise
%		was confirmed in the past—and where the Temple will
%		stand in the future.
%		(The location of the Temple is identified with the place
%		of the binding
%		of Isaac—Moriah—in 2 Chr Footnote 3:1.) The two sacred
%		mountains are
%		connected; the patriarch and his descendants are
%		connected; past,
%		present, and future are connected—all in the embroidery
%		of the Torah’s
%		wording.
%	}

verses.original: וְנִגַּשׁ מֹשֶׁה לְבַדּוֹ אֶל יְהֹוָה וְהֵם לֹא יִגָּשׁוּ וְהָעָם לֹא יַעֲלוּ עִמּוֹ׃
verses.english: And Moses will come over alone to YHWH, and they shall not come over, and the people shall not come up with him.”

tex.original: \hE{וְנִגַּשׁ מֹשֶׁה לְבַדּוֹ אֶל יְהֹוָה וְהֵם לֹא יִגָּשׁוּ וְהָעָם לֹא יַעֲלוּ עִמּוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה וַיְסַפֵּר לָעָם אֵת כּל דִּבְרֵי יְהֹוָה וְאֵת כּל הַמִּשְׁפָּטִים וַיַּעַן כּל הָעָם קוֹל אֶחָד וַיֹּאמְרוּ כּל הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה נַעֲשֶׂה׃
verses.english: And Moses came and told the people all of YHWH’s words and all the judgments. And all the people answered, one voice, and they said, “We’ll do all the things that YHWH has spoken.”

tex.original: \hE{וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה וַיְסַפֵּר לָעָם אֵת כּל דִּבְרֵי יְהֹוָה וְאֵת כּל הַמִּשְׁפָּטִים וַיַּעַן כּל הָעָם קוֹל אֶחָד וַיֹּאמְרוּ כּל הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה נַעֲשֶׂה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּכְתֹּב מֹשֶׁה אֵת כּל דִּבְרֵי יְהֹוָה וַיַּשְׁכֵּם בַּבֹּקֶר וַיִּבֶן מִזְבֵּחַ תַּחַת הָהָר וּשְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה מַצֵּבָה לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And Moses wrote all of YHWH’s words. And he got up early in the morning and built an altar below the mountain and twelve pillars for twelve tribes of Israel.

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּכְתֹּב מֹשֶׁה אֵת כּל דִּבְרֵי יְהֹוָה וַיַּשְׁכֵּם בַּבֹּקֶר וַיִּבֶן מִזְבֵּחַ תַּחַת הָהָר וּשְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה מַצֵּבָה לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח אֶת נַעֲרֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיַּעֲלוּ עֹלֹת וַיִּזְבְּחוּ זְבָחִים שְׁלָמִים לַיהֹוָה פָּרִים׃
verses.english: And he sent young men of the children of Israel, and they made burnt offerings, and they made peace-offering sacrifices to YHWH: bulls.

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּשְׁלַח אֶת נַעֲרֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיַּעֲלוּ עֹלֹת וַיִּזְבְּחוּ זְבָחִים שְׁלָמִים לַיהֹוָה פָּרִים׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה חֲצִי הַדָּם וַיָּשֶׂם בָּאַגָּנֹת וַחֲצִי הַדָּם זָרַק עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ׃
verses.english: And Moses took half of the blood and set it in basins and threw half of the blood on the altar.

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה חֲצִי הַדָּם וַיָּשֶׂם בָּאַגָּנֹת וַחֲצִי הַדָּם זָרַק עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח סֵפֶר הַבְּרִית וַיִּקְרָא בְּאזְנֵי הָעָם וַיֹּאמְרוּ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע׃
verses.english: And he took the scroll of the covenant and read in the people’s ears. And they said, “We’ll do everything that YHWH has spoken, and we’ll listen.”

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּקַּח סֵפֶר הַבְּרִית וַיִּקְרָא בְּאזְנֵי הָעָם וַיֹּאמְרוּ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמָע׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		We’ll do … and we’ll listen. It has been noted that the
%		word order here
%		seems backward: doesn’t one have to listen to the
%		command before one can
%		do it?! The promises to do and to listen come together
%		in the order of
%		this sentence in the Hebrew, so it may be that they were
%		a known
%		formula, constituting an oath of absolute obedience. But
%		I understand
%		them to be separate: The people’s promise to do the
%		commandments is a
%		repetition of what they had said before in v. 3. They
%		repeat it formally
%		now because Moses has just read them the written
%		document. The people’s
%		promise to listen is, as Rashbam wrote, a further
%		promise, a commitment
%		to follow the things that their God will say to them in
%		the future. In
%		Hebrew as in English, words for “listening” also imply
%		obeying, as in:
%		“Listen to your mother!” “Do you hear me?!” (As an
%		alternative and more
%		banal explanation of the seemingly backward order: the
%		Septuagint has
%		the two words in reverse order.)
%	}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַדָּם וַיִּזְרֹק עַל הָעָם וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֵּה דַם הַבְּרִית אֲשֶׁר כָּרַת יְהֹוָה עִמָּכֶם עַל כּל הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה׃
verses.english: And Moses took the blood and threw it on the people, and he said, “Here is the blood of the covenant that YHWH has made with you regarding all these things.”

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַדָּם וַיִּזְרֹק עַל הָעָם וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֵּה דַם הַבְּרִית אֲשֶׁר כָּרַת יְהֹוָה עִמָּכֶם עַל כּל הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעַל מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא וְשִׁבְעִים מִזִּקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s elders went up.

tex.original: \hE{וַיַּעַל מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא וְשִׁבְעִים מִזִּקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיִּרְאוּ אֵת אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְתַחַת רַגְלָיו כְּמַעֲשֵׂה לִבְנַת הַסַּפִּיר וּכְעֶצֶם הַשָּׁמַיִם לָטֹהַר׃
verses.english: And they saw the God of Israel. And below His feet it was like a structure of sapphire brick and like the essence of the skies for clarity.

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּרְאוּ אֵת אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְתַחַת רַגְלָיו כְּמַעֲשֵׂה לִבְנַת הַסַּפִּיר וּכְעֶצֶם הַשָּׁמַיִם לָטֹהַר׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		24:10–11. And they saw God. … And they envisioned God.
%		Some
%		have taken this to mean that they literally, physically
%		see God.
%		But, as Ibn Ezra properly observed, the verb for “they
%		saw” (Hebrew
%		r’h) is also used to refer to seeing in a vision, as
%		when Isaiah
%		says, “I saw the Lord sitting on a throne” (Isa 6:1).
%		This meaning
%		of “they saw” here is confirmed by the parallel use in
%		v. 11 of the
%		word “envisioned” (Hebrew zh), which regularly means to
%		have a
%		vision (as, for example in Isa 1:1). Also, this is
%		consistent with
%		the idea that no one ever sees the actual form of God
%		except
%		Moses on a single occasion. This idea is understood
%		throughout the
%		Tanak, without exception. (On the distinction between
%		vision and
%		regular experience, see The Hidden Face of God, pp.
%		17–18,
%		62–63.)
%	}

verses.original: וְאֶל אֲצִילֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא שָׁלַח יָדוֹ וַיֶּחֱזוּ אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים וַיֹּאכְלוּ וַיִּשְׁתּוּ׃
verses.english: And He did not put out His hand to the chiefs of the children of Israel. And they envisioned God. And they ate and drank.

tex.original: \hE{וְאֶל אֲצִילֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא שָׁלַח יָדוֹ וַיֶּחֱזוּ אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים וַיֹּאכְלוּ וַיִּשְׁתּוּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		He did not put out His hand. Those who take the passage
%		to mean that
%		this group actually sees God understand “He did not put
%		out His hand” to
%		mean that God does not kill them for seeing God. But the
%		text says “He
%		did not put out His hand to the chiefs …” The phrase “to
%		put out one’s
%		hand” followed by the preposition “to” (Hebrew ’el)
%		never refers to
%		killing in the Tanak. (When referring to killing, the
%		phrase occurs with
%		the preposition b.) And, in any case, there are other
%		cases of the
%		expression of God putting out a hand to humans that are
%		meant
%		positively. In Ps 144:7, this refers to God saving
%		someone. And there is
%		an even closer parallel in Jer 1:9, where it takes place
%		in a vision and
%		refers to God reaching out to touch Jeremiah’s mouth to
%		enable him to
%		speak. Here in Exodus, perhaps it means that in their
%		vision they see
%		but are not touched by God.
%	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה עֲלֵה אֵלַי הָהָרָה וֶהְיֵה שָׁם וְאֶתְּנָה לְךָ אֶת לֻחֹת הָאֶבֶן וְהַתּוֹרָה וְהַמִּצְוָה אֲשֶׁר כָּתַבְתִּי לְהוֹרֹתָם׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “Come up to me, to the mountain, and be there, and I’ll give you stone tablets and the instruction and the commandment that I’ve written to instruct them.”

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה עֲלֵה אֵלַי הָהָרָה וֶהְיֵה שָׁם וְאֶתְּנָה לְךָ אֶת לֻחֹת הָאֶבֶן וְהַתּוֹרָה וְהַמִּצְוָה אֲשֶׁר כָּתַבְתִּי לְהוֹרֹתָם׃}

verses.original: וַיָּקם מֹשֶׁה וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ מְשָׁרְתוֹ וַיַּעַל מֹשֶׁה אֶל הַר הָאֱלֹהִים׃
verses.english: And Moses and Joshua, his attendant, got up, and Moses went up to the Mountain of God.

tex.original: \hE{וַיָּקם מֹשֶׁה וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ מְשָׁרְתוֹ וַיַּעַל מֹשֶׁה אֶל הַר הָאֱלֹהִים׃}

verses.original: וְאֶל הַזְּקֵנִים אָמַר שְׁבוּ לָנוּ בָזֶה עַד אֲשֶׁר נָשׁוּב אֲלֵיכֶם וְהִנֵּה אַהֲרֹן וְחוּר עִמָּכֶם מִי בַעַל דְּבָרִים יִגַּשׁ אֲלֵהֶם׃
verses.english: And he said to the elders, “Sit for us here until we’ll come back to you. And here, Aaron and Hur are with you. Let whoever has any matters go over to them.”

tex.original: \hE{וְאֶל הַזְּקֵנִים אָמַר שְׁבוּ לָנוּ בָזֶה עַד אֲשֶׁר נָשׁוּב אֲלֵיכֶם וְהִנֵּה אַהֲרֹן וְחוּר עִמָּכֶם מִי בַעַל דְּבָרִים יִגַּשׁ אֲלֵהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעַל מֹשֶׁה אֶל הָהָר וַיְכַס הֶעָנָן אֶת הָהָר׃
verses.english: And Moses went up to the mountain. And the cloud covered the mountain.

tex.original:
\hE{וַיַּעַל מֹשֶׁה אֶל הָהָר}
	\hP{וַיְכַס הֶעָנָן אֶת הָהָר׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁכֹּן כְּבוֹד יְהֹוָה עַל הַר סִינַי וַיְכַסֵּהוּ הֶעָנָן שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים וַיִּקְרָא אֶל מֹשֶׁה בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מִתּוֹךְ הֶעָנָן׃
verses.english: And YHWH’s glory settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days. And He called to Moses on the seventh day from inside the cloud.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּשְׁכֹּן כְּבוֹד יְהֹוָה עַל הַר סִינַי וַיְכַסֵּהוּ הֶעָנָן שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים וַיִּקְרָא אֶל מֹשֶׁה בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מִתּוֹךְ הֶעָנָן׃}

verses.original: וּמַרְאֵה כְּבוֹד יְהֹוָה כְּאֵשׁ אֹכֶלֶת בְּרֹאשׁ הָהָר לְעֵינֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And the appearance of YHWH’s glory was like a consuming fire in the mountaintop before the eyes of the children of Israel.

tex.original: \hP{וּמַרְאֵה כְּבוֹד יְהֹוָה כְּאֵשׁ אֹכֶלֶת בְּרֹאשׁ הָהָר לְעֵינֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה בְּתוֹךְ הֶעָנָן וַיַּעַל אֶל הָהָר וַיְהִי מֹשֶׁה בָּהָר אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לָיְלָה׃
verses.english: And Moses came inside the cloud and went up into the mountain. And Moses was in the mountain forty days and forty nights.

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיִקְחוּ לִי תְּרוּמָה מֵאֵת כּל אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִדְּבֶנּוּ לִבּוֹ תִּקְחוּ אֶת תְּרוּמָתִי׃
verses.english: “Speak to the children of Israel that they shall take a donation for me. You shall take my donation from every man whose heart will move him.

tex.original: \hP{דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיִקְחוּ לִי תְּרוּמָה מֵאֵת כּל אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִדְּבֶנּוּ לִבּוֹ תִּקְחוּ אֶת תְּרוּמָתִי׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Speak to the children of Israel that they shall take a
%		donation for me.
%		You shall take my donation from every man whose heart
%		will move him. The
%		command is to all the people—to take from individuals,
%		who are
%		themselves part of the people. It is strange
%		linguistically. The whole
%		people is not commanded to give. People only have to
%		give if they are
%		individually moved to do so. But the whole people is
%		commanded to
%		collect it. It is like when someone says that he gave a
%		gift to his
%		congregation when he himself is a member of the
%		congregation.
%	}

verses.original: וְזֹאת הַתְּרוּמָה אֲשֶׁר תִּקְחוּ מֵאִתָּם זָהָב וָכֶסֶף וּנְחֹשֶׁת׃
verses.english: And this is the donation that you shall take from them: gold and silver and bronze

tex.original: \hP{וְזֹאת הַתְּרוּמָה אֲשֶׁר תִּקְחוּ מֵאִתָּם זָהָב וָכֶסֶף וּנְחֹשֶׁת׃}

verses.original: וּתְכֵלֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן וְתוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי וְשֵׁשׁ וְעִזִּים׃
verses.english: and blue and purple and scarlet and linen and goats’ hair

tex.original: \hP{וּתְכֵלֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן וְתוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי וְשֵׁשׁ וְעִזִּים׃}
tex.english: \eP{and blue and purple and scarlet and linen and goats’ hair}

verses.original: וְעֹרֹת אֵילִם מְאדָּמִים וְעֹרֹת תְּחָשִׁים וַעֲצֵי שִׁטִּים׃
verses.english: and rams’ skins dyed red and leather skins and acacia wood,

tex.original: \hP{וְעֹרֹת אֵילִם מְאדָּמִים וְעֹרֹת תְּחָשִׁים וַעֲצֵי שִׁטִּים׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		leather. Hebrew: skins that are tšîm. No one knows what
%		this means. It
%		has been understood to be dolphin skins, badger skins,
%		goatskins, and
%		skins of a particular color. It is cognate to an Arabic
%		word meaning
%		dolphin; but, since this word does not occur in the list
%		of sea or land
%		animals that are forbidden or permitted for food in
%		Leviticus 11, it may
%		not refer to a particular species of animal at all. It
%		may just mean
%		skins that have been tanned; that is: leather.
%	}

verses.original: שֶׁמֶן לַמָּאֹר בְּשָׂמִים לְשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה וְלִקְטֹרֶת הַסַּמִּים׃
verses.english: oil for lighting, spices for the anointing oil and for the incense fragrances,

tex.original: \hP{שֶׁמֶן לַמָּאֹר בְּשָׂמִים לְשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה וְלִקְטֹרֶת הַסַּמִּים׃}

verses.original: אַבְנֵי שֹׁהַם וְאַבְנֵי מִלֻּאִים לָאֵפֹד וְלַחֹשֶׁן׃
verses.english: onyx stones and stones to be set for the ephod and for the breastplate.

tex.original: \hP{אַבְנֵי שֹׁהַם וְאַבְנֵי מִלֻּאִים לָאֵפֹד וְלַחֹשֶׁן׃}

verses.original: וְעָשׂוּ לִי מִקְדָּשׁ וְשָׁכַנְתִּי בְּתוֹכָם׃
verses.english: And they shall make me a holy place, and I shall tent among them.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשׂוּ לִי מִקְדָּשׁ וְשָׁכַנְתִּי בְּתוֹכָם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		I shall tent among them. Forms of this Hebrew verb
%		(škantî) are
%		frequently taken to mean “to dwell”; but when it refers
%		to God, this
%		verb is a denominative from the noun miškn: Tabernacle.
%		As God explains
%		to David, “I haven’t lived in a house from the day I
%		brought the
%		children of Israel up from Egypt to this day, but I’ve
%		been going about
%		in a tent and in a Tabernacle” (2 Sam 7:6). The creator
%		cannot be
%		pictured as residing on the earth but rather is
%		understood to tent among
%		humans, that is, to be present in association with a non
%		permanent,
%		movable structure. Even after the Temple is built, God
%		is associated
%		with the Tabernacle, which is housed there (1 Kings 8:4;
%		Babylonian
%		Talmud Tractate Soa 9a) and represented by the space
%		under the wings of
%		the cherubs in the Holy of Holies (Ps 61:5).
%	}

verses.original: כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי מַרְאֶה אוֹתְךָ אֵת תַּבְנִית הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְאֵת תַּבְנִית כּל כֵּלָיו וְכֵן תַּעֲשׂוּ׃
verses.english: According to everything that I show you: the design of the Tabernacle and the design of all its equipment. And you shall do so.

tex.original: \hP{כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי מַרְאֶה אוֹתְךָ אֵת תַּבְנִית הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְאֵת תַּבְנִית כּל כֵּלָיו וְכֵן תַּעֲשׂוּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Tabernacle. There is more about the Tabernacle and its
%		contents than any
%		other subject in the Torah. There are long chapters
%		dealing with the
%		building of the Tabernacle, filled with details of
%		materials and
%		measurements in cubits. Tedious reading though it may be
%		for most
%		readers, it conveys the significance of the Tabernacle
%		as the channel to
%		YHWH. Exodus notes explicitly that the function of the
%		Tabernacle is: “I
%		shall meet there with the children of Israel … ” (29:43;
%		25:22). The
%		book of Exodus culminates in the Tabernacle’s
%		consecration (Exodus 40).
%	}

verses.original: וְעָשׂוּ אֲרוֹן עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים אַמָּתַיִם וָחֵצִי ארְכּוֹ וְאַמָּה וָחֵצִי רחְבּוֹ וְאַמָּה וָחֵצִי קֹמָתוֹ׃
verses.english: “And they shall make an ark of acacia wood, its length two and a half cubits and its width a cubit and a half and its height a cubit and a half.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשׂוּ אֲרוֹן עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים אַמָּתַיִם וָחֵצִי ארְכּוֹ וְאַמָּה וָחֵצִי רחְבּוֹ וְאַמָּה וָחֵצִי קֹמָתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְצִפִּיתָ אֹתוֹ זָהָב טָהוֹר מִבַּיִת וּמִחוּץ תְּצַפֶּנּוּ וְעָשִׂיתָ עָלָיו זֵר זָהָב סָבִיב׃
verses.english: And you shall plate it with pure gold. You shall plate it inside and outside. And you shall make a border of gold all around on it.

tex.original: \hP{וְצִפִּיתָ אֹתוֹ זָהָב טָהוֹר מִבַּיִת וּמִחוּץ תְּצַפֶּנּוּ וְעָשִׂיתָ עָלָיו זֵר זָהָב סָבִיב׃}

verses.original: וְיָצַקְתָּ לּוֹ אַרְבַּע טַבְּעֹת זָהָב וְנָתַתָּה עַל אַרְבַּע פַּעֲמֹתָיו וּשְׁתֵּי טַבָּעֹת עַל צַלְעוֹ הָאֶחָת וּשְׁתֵּי טַבָּעֹת עַל צַלְעוֹ הַשֵּׁנִית׃
verses.english: And you shall cast four rings of gold for it and place them on its four bases: and two rings on its one side and two rings on its second side.

tex.original: \hP{וְיָצַקְתָּ לּוֹ אַרְבַּע טַבְּעֹת זָהָב וְנָתַתָּה עַל אַרְבַּע פַּעֲמֹתָיו וּשְׁתֵּי טַבָּעֹת עַל צַלְעוֹ הָאֶחָת וּשְׁתֵּי טַבָּעֹת עַל צַלְעוֹ הַשֵּׁנִית׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ בַדֵּי עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים וְצִפִּיתָ אֹתָם זָהָב׃
verses.english: And you shall make poles of acacia wood and plate them with gold,

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ בַדֵּי עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים וְצִפִּיתָ אֹתָם זָהָב׃}

verses.original: וְהֵבֵאתָ אֶת הַבַּדִּים בַּטַּבָּעֹת עַל צַלְעֹת הָאָרֹן לָשֵׂאת אֶת הָאָרֹן בָּהֶם׃
verses.english: and bring the poles through the rings on the ark’s sides, in order to carry the ark with them.

tex.original: \hP{וְהֵבֵאתָ אֶת הַבַּדִּים בַּטַּבָּעֹת עַל צַלְעֹת הָאָרֹן לָשֵׂאת אֶת הָאָרֹן בָּהֶם׃}

verses.original: בְּטַבְּעֹת הָאָרֹן יִהְיוּ הַבַּדִּים לֹא יָסֻרוּ מִמֶּנּוּ׃
verses.english: The poles shall be in the ark’s rings; they shall not depart from it.

tex.original: \hP{בְּטַבְּעֹת הָאָרֹן יִהְיוּ הַבַּדִּים לֹא יָסֻרוּ מִמֶּנּוּ׃}

verses.original: וְנָתַתָּ אֶל הָאָרֹן אֵת הָעֵדֻת אֲשֶׁר אֶתֵּן אֵלֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And you shall place in the ark the Testimony that I shall give you.

tex.original: \hP{וְנָתַתָּ אֶל הָאָרֹן אֵת הָעֵדֻת אֲשֶׁר אֶתֵּן אֵלֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ כַפֹּרֶת זָהָב טָהוֹר אַמָּתַיִם וָחֵצִי ארְכָּהּ וְאַמָּה וָחֵצִי רחְבָּהּ׃
verses.english: And you shall make an atonement dais of pure gold, its length two and a half cubits and its width a cubit and a half.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ כַפֹּרֶת זָהָב טָהוֹר אַמָּתַיִם וָחֵצִי ארְכָּהּ וְאַמָּה וָחֵצִי רחְבָּהּ׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ שְׁנַיִם כְּרֻבִים זָהָב מִקְשָׁה תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם מִשְּׁנֵי קְצוֹת הַכַּפֹּרֶת׃
verses.english: And you shall make two cherubs of gold—you shall make them of hammered work—at the two ends of the atonement dais.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ שְׁנַיִם כְּרֻבִים זָהָב מִקְשָׁה תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם מִשְּׁנֵי קְצוֹת הַכַּפֹּרֶת׃}

verses.original: וַעֲשֵׂה כְּרוּב אֶחָד מִקָּצָה מִזֶּה וּכְרוּב אֶחָד מִקָּצָה מִזֶּה מִן הַכַּפֹּרֶת תַּעֲשׂוּ אֶת הַכְּרֻבִים עַל שְׁנֵי קְצוֹתָיו׃
verses.english: And make one cherub at this end and one cherub at that end. You shall make the cherubs from the atonement dais on its two sides.

tex.original: \hP{וַעֲשֵׂה כְּרוּב אֶחָד מִקָּצָה מִזֶּה וּכְרוּב אֶחָד מִקָּצָה מִזֶּה מִן הַכַּפֹּרֶת תַּעֲשׂוּ אֶת הַכְּרֻבִים עַל שְׁנֵי קְצוֹתָיו׃}

verses.original: וְהָיוּ הַכְּרֻבִים פֹּרְשֵׂי כְנָפַיִם לְמַעְלָה סֹכְכִים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם עַל הַכַּפֹּרֶת וּפְנֵיהֶם אִישׁ אֶל אָחִיו אֶל הַכַּפֹּרֶת יִהְיוּ פְּנֵי הַכְּרֻבִים׃
verses.english: And the two cherubs will be spreading wings above, covering over the atonement dais with their wings, and their faces each toward its brother: the cherubs’ faces shall be toward the atonement dais.

tex.original: \hP{וְהָיוּ הַכְּרֻבִים פֹּרְשֵׂי כְנָפַיִם לְמַעְלָה סֹכְכִים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם עַל הַכַּפֹּרֶת וּפְנֵיהֶם אִישׁ אֶל אָחִיו אֶל הַכַּפֹּרֶת יִהְיוּ פְּנֵי הַכְּרֻבִים׃}

verses.original: וְנָתַתָּ אֶת הַכַּפֹּרֶת עַל הָאָרֹן מִלְמָעְלָה וְאֶל הָאָרֹן תִּתֵּן אֶת הָעֵדֻת אֲשֶׁר אֶתֵּן אֵלֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And you shall place the atonement dais on the ark, from above, and you shall place in the ark the Testimony that I shall give you.

tex.original: \hP{וְנָתַתָּ אֶת הַכַּפֹּרֶת עַל הָאָרֹן מִלְמָעְלָה וְאֶל הָאָרֹן תִּתֵּן אֶת הָעֵדֻת אֲשֶׁר אֶתֵּן אֵלֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: וְנוֹעַדְתִּי לְךָ שָׁם וְדִבַּרְתִּי אִתְּךָ מֵעַל הַכַּפֹּרֶת מִבֵּין שְׁנֵי הַכְּרֻבִים אֲשֶׁר עַל אֲרוֹן הָעֵדֻת אֵת כּל אֲשֶׁר אֲצַוֶּה אוֹתְךָ אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And I shall meet with you there and speak with you from above the atonement dais, from between the two cherubs that are on the Ark of the Testimony, everything that I shall command you to the children of Israel.

tex.original: \hP{וְנוֹעַדְתִּי לְךָ שָׁם וְדִבַּרְתִּי אִתְּךָ מֵעַל הַכַּפֹּרֶת מִבֵּין שְׁנֵי הַכְּרֻבִים אֲשֶׁר עַל אֲרוֹן הָעֵדֻת אֵת כּל אֲשֶׁר אֲצַוֶּה אוֹתְךָ אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ שֻׁלְחָן עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים אַמָּתַיִם ארְכּוֹ וְאַמָּה רחְבּוֹ וְאַמָּה וָחֵצִי קֹמָתוֹ׃
verses.english: “And you shall make a table of acacia wood, its length two cubits and its width a cubit and its height a cubit and a half.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ שֻׁלְחָן עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים אַמָּתַיִם ארְכּוֹ וְאַמָּה רחְבּוֹ וְאַמָּה וָחֵצִי קֹמָתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְצִפִּיתָ אֹתוֹ זָהָב טָהוֹר וְעָשִׂיתָ לּוֹ זֵר זָהָב סָבִיב׃
verses.english: And you shall plate it with pure gold and make a border of gold all around for it

tex.original: \hP{וְצִפִּיתָ אֹתוֹ זָהָב טָהוֹר וְעָשִׂיתָ לּוֹ זֵר זָהָב סָבִיב׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ לּוֹ מִסְגֶּרֶת טֹפַח סָבִיב וְעָשִׂיתָ זֵר זָהָב לְמִסְגַּרְתּוֹ סָבִיב׃
verses.english: and make a rim of a handbreadth for it all around and make a border of gold for its rim all around.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ לּוֹ מִסְגֶּרֶת טֹפַח סָבִיב וְעָשִׂיתָ זֵר זָהָב לְמִסְגַּרְתּוֹ סָבִיב׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ לּוֹ אַרְבַּע טַבְּעֹת זָהָב וְנָתַתָּ אֶת הַטַּבָּעֹת עַל אַרְבַּע הַפֵּאֹת אֲשֶׁר לְאַרְבַּע רַגְלָיו׃
verses.english: And you shall make four rings of gold for it and put the rings on the four corners that its four legs have.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ לּוֹ אַרְבַּע טַבְּעֹת זָהָב וְנָתַתָּ אֶת הַטַּבָּעֹת עַל אַרְבַּע הַפֵּאֹת אֲשֶׁר לְאַרְבַּע רַגְלָיו׃}

verses.original: לְעֻמַּת הַמִּסְגֶּרֶת תִּהְיֶיןָ הַטַּבָּעֹת לְבָתִּים לְבַדִּים לָשֵׂאת אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָן׃
verses.english: The rings shall be in juxtaposition to the rim as housings for the poles in order to carry the table.

tex.original: \hP{לְעֻמַּת הַמִּסְגֶּרֶת תִּהְיֶיןָ הַטַּבָּעֹת לְבָתִּים לְבַדִּים לָשֵׂאת אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָן׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ אֶת הַבַּדִּים עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים וְצִפִּיתָ אֹתָם זָהָב וְנִשָּׂא בָם אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָן׃
verses.english: And you shall make the poles of acacia wood and plate them with gold, and the table will be carried with them.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ אֶת הַבַּדִּים עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים וְצִפִּיתָ אֹתָם זָהָב וְנִשָּׂא בָם אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָן׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ קְּעָרֹתָיו וְכַפֹּתָיו וּקְשׂוֹתָיו וּמְנַקִּיֹּתָיו אֲשֶׁר יֻסַּךְ בָּהֵן זָהָב טָהוֹר תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם׃
verses.english: And you shall make its dishes and its pans and its jars and its bowls with which libations will be poured. You shall make them of pure gold.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ קְּעָרֹתָיו וְכַפֹּתָיו וּקְשׂוֹתָיו וּמְנַקִּיֹּתָיו אֲשֶׁר יֻסַּךְ בָּהֵן זָהָב טָהוֹר תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם׃}

verses.original: וְנָתַתָּ עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן לֶחֶם פָּנִים לְפָנַי תָּמִיד׃
verses.english: And you shall place show bread on the table in front of me always.

tex.original: \hP{וְנָתַתָּ עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן לֶחֶם פָּנִים לְפָנַי תָּמִיד׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ מְנֹרַת זָהָב טָהוֹר מִקְשָׁה תֵּעָשֶׂה הַמְּנוֹרָה יְרֵכָהּ וְקָנָהּ גְּבִיעֶיהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶיהָ וּפְרָחֶיהָ מִמֶּנָּה יִהְיוּ׃
verses.english: “And you shall make a menorah of pure gold. The menorah shall be made of hammered work—its shaft and its branch, its cups, its ornaments, and its flowers shall be part of it—

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ מְנֹרַת זָהָב טָהוֹר מִקְשָׁה תֵּעָשֶׂה הַמְּנוֹרָה יְרֵכָהּ וְקָנָהּ גְּבִיעֶיהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶיהָ וּפְרָחֶיהָ מִמֶּנָּה יִהְיוּ׃}

verses.original: וְשִׁשָּׁה קָנִים יֹצְאִים מִצִּדֶּיהָ שְׁלֹשָׁה קְנֵי מְנֹרָה מִצִּדָּהּ הָאֶחָד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה קְנֵי מְנֹרָה מִצִּדָּהּ הַשֵּׁנִי׃
verses.english: and six branches coming out from its sides, three of the menorah’s branches from its one side and three of the menorah’s branches from its second side,

tex.original: \hP{וְשִׁשָּׁה קָנִים יֹצְאִים מִצִּדֶּיהָ שְׁלֹשָׁה קְנֵי מְנֹרָה מִצִּדָּהּ הָאֶחָד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה קְנֵי מְנֹרָה מִצִּדָּהּ הַשֵּׁנִי׃}

verses.original: שְׁלֹשָׁה גְבִעִים מְשֻׁקָּדִים בַּקָּנֶה הָאֶחָד כַּפְתֹּר וָפֶרַח וּשְׁלֹשָׁה גְבִעִים מְשֻׁקָּדִים בַּקָּנֶה הָאֶחָד כַּפְתֹּר וָפָרַח כֵּן לְשֵׁשֶׁת הַקָּנִים הַיֹּצְאִים מִן הַמְּנֹרָה׃
verses.english: three almond-shaped cups in the one branch, with ornament and flower, and three almond-shaped cups in the other branch, with ornament and flower. So it is for the six branches that come out from the menorah,

tex.original: \hP{שְׁלֹשָׁה גְבִעִים מְשֻׁקָּדִים בַּקָּנֶה הָאֶחָד כַּפְתֹּר וָפֶרַח וּשְׁלֹשָׁה גְבִעִים מְשֻׁקָּדִים בַּקָּנֶה הָאֶחָד כַּפְתֹּר וָפָרַח כֵּן לְשֵׁשֶׁת הַקָּנִים הַיֹּצְאִים מִן הַמְּנֹרָה׃}

verses.original: וּבַמְּנֹרָה אַרְבָּעָה גְבִעִים מְשֻׁקָּדִים כַּפְתֹּרֶיהָ וּפְרָחֶיהָ׃
verses.english: and four almond-shaped cups within the menorah, with its ornaments and its flowers,

tex.original: \hP{וּבַמְּנֹרָה אַרְבָּעָה גְבִעִים מְשֻׁקָּדִים כַּפְתֹּרֶיהָ וּפְרָחֶיהָ׃}

verses.original: וְכַפְתֹּר תַּחַת שְׁנֵי הַקָּנִים מִמֶּנָּה וְכַפְתֹּר תַּחַת שְׁנֵי הַקָּנִים מִמֶּנָּה וְכַפְתֹּר תַּחַת שְׁנֵי הַקָּנִים מִמֶּנָּה לְשֵׁשֶׁת הַקָּנִים הַיֹּצְאִים מִן הַמְּנֹרָה׃
verses.english: and an ornament under the two branches from it, and an ornament under the two branches from it, and an ornament under the two branches from it, for the six branches that come out from the menorah.

tex.original: \hP{וְכַפְתֹּר תַּחַת שְׁנֵי הַקָּנִים מִמֶּנָּה וְכַפְתֹּר תַּחַת שְׁנֵי הַקָּנִים מִמֶּנָּה וְכַפְתֹּר תַּחַת שְׁנֵי הַקָּנִים מִמֶּנָּה לְשֵׁשֶׁת הַקָּנִים הַיֹּצְאִים מִן הַמְּנֹרָה׃}

verses.original: כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶם וּקְנֹתָם מִמֶּנָּה יִהְיוּ כֻּלָּהּ מִקְשָׁה אַחַת זָהָב טָהוֹר׃
verses.english: Their ornaments and their branches shall be part of it, all of it one hammered work of pure gold.

tex.original: \hP{כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶם וּקְנֹתָם מִמֶּנָּה יִהְיוּ כֻּלָּהּ מִקְשָׁה אַחַת זָהָב טָהוֹר׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ אֶת נֵרֹתֶיהָ שִׁבְעָה וְהֶעֱלָה אֶת נֵרֹתֶיהָ וְהֵאִיר עַל עֵבֶר פָּנֶיהָ׃
verses.english: And you shall make its lamps seven, and it will hold up its lamps and light the area in front of it.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ אֶת נֵרֹתֶיהָ שִׁבְעָה וְהֶעֱלָה אֶת נֵרֹתֶיהָ וְהֵאִיר עַל עֵבֶר פָּנֶיהָ׃}

verses.original: וּמַלְקָחֶיהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶיהָ זָהָב טָהוֹר׃
verses.english: And its tongs and its fire-holders of pure gold.

tex.original: \hP{וּמַלְקָחֶיהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶיהָ זָהָב טָהוֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And its tongs and its fire-holders of pure gold.}

verses.original: כִּכָּר זָהָב טָהוֹר יַעֲשֶׂה אֹתָהּ אֵת כּל הַכֵּלִים הָאֵלֶּה׃
verses.english: He shall make it—all of these items—of a talent of pure gold.

tex.original: \hP{כִּכָּר זָהָב טָהוֹר יַעֲשֶׂה אֹתָהּ אֵת כּל הַכֵּלִים הָאֵלֶּה׃}

verses.original: וּרְאֵה וַעֲשֵׂה בְּתַבְנִיתָם אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה מרְאֶה בָּהָר׃
verses.english: And see and make them by their design that you are shown in the mountain.

tex.original: \hP{וּרְאֵה וַעֲשֵׂה בְּתַבְנִיתָם אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה מרְאֶה בָּהָר׃}

verses.original: וְאֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן תַּעֲשֶׂה עֶשֶׂר יְרִיעֹת שֵׁשׁ משְׁזָר וּתְכֵלֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן וְתֹלַעַת שָׁנִי כְּרֻבִים מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם׃
verses.english: “And you shall make the Tabernacle with ten curtains of woven linen and blue and purple and scarlet, with cherubs—you shall make them designer’s work.

tex.original: \hP{וְאֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן תַּעֲשֶׂה עֶשֶׂר יְרִיעֹת שֵׁשׁ משְׁזָר וּתְכֵלֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן וְתֹלַעַת שָׁנִי כְּרֻבִים מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		make the Tabernacle. No one has ever figured out how the
%		Tabernacle is
%		put together. The components are given here, but the
%		text does not say
%		how they are put together. Twenty frames are used for
%		each side wall and
%		six for the rear wall (plus two more for supporting the
%		rear corners).
%		The frames are ten cubits tall and “a cubit and a half
%		cubit” wide.
%		People have therefore assumed that the Tabernacle is
%		thirty cubits long
%		by ten cubits wide, and ten cubits high. Curtains fit
%		over these frames,
%		and the curtains are made of two giant fabrics. Each
%		fabric is made of
%		five pieces sewn together; the pieces are four cubits by
%		twenty-eight
%		cubits wide. So the two fabrics are each twenty by
%		twenty-eight. They
%		are attached together with gold clasps, making a double
%		fabric that is
%		forty by twenty-eight. When this forty-cubit piece is
%		placed over the
%		thirty-cubit-long structure of frames, it covers the top
%		and has ten
%		cubits left over to cover the ten-cubit-high rear wall.
%		In support of
%		this, people have noted that Solomon’s Temple is sixty
%		cubits long by
%		twenty wide, so the Temple and Tabernacle are in
%		two-to-one proportion.
%		But there are many things wrong with this. (1) The
%		Temple is thirty
%		cubits high, so the proportion there is three-to-one,
%		not two-to-one.
%		(2) The ten-cubit width is wrong, because six frames of
%		a cubit and a
%		half each make only a nine-cubit width. (3) The
%		twenty-eight-cubits-wide
%		curtains do not fit this structure. Its two sidewalls
%		are each ten
%		cubits high, and its ceiling is ten cubits across, which
%		requires a
%		cover that is thirty cubits wide. The
%		twenty-eight-cubits-wide curtain
%		leaves a whole cubit (eighteen inches) uncovered on each
%		side. (4) A
%		second set of curtains is made into two large fabrics
%		like the first
%		set, but this second set (made of goats’ hair) is made
%		of curtains that
%		are four cubits by thirty, instead of four by
%		twenty-eight, and there is
%		an extra, eleventh curtain at one end. The extra curtain
%		has no purpose,
%		and the thirty-cubits-length hangs down past the bottom
%		of the inner
%		fabric. (5) The gold clasps cannot be seen in this
%		arrangement. Also,
%		this arrangement leaves questions: (6) Why would the
%		frames be a cubit
%		and a half wide instead of just one cubit or two cubits?
%		And why does it
%		say “a cubit and a half cubit” instead of the normal
%		wording, “a cubit
%		and a half”? (7) Why are the curtains in groups of five,
%		which are each
%		four cubits wide? What is significant about four cubits?
%		All of these
%		problems and questions point to a different way that the
%		Tabernacle is
%		put together. I propose that the reason that the frames
%		are “a cubit and
%		a half cubit” is because they overlap each other by the
%		extra
%		half-cubit. This is more stable and better for
%		ventilation than if they
%		stood side by side (Figures 1 and 2). The twenty-frame
%		length by
%		six-frame width means a structure that is twenty cubits
%		by six cubits on
%		the inside. If the frames are a half-cubit wide, then it
%		is twenty by
%		eight on the outside (Figure 3). Now, if we take the two
%		large fabrics
%		that are twenty by twenty-eight cubits, and we connect
%		them with the
%		clasps, and then we fold it in half along the clasps, it
%		fits this
%		structure. The gold clasps now are visible: they
%		surround the entrance
%		to the Tabernacle. The twenty-cubit width of the fabric
%		matches the
%		twenty-cubit length of the Tabernacle. And the
%		twenty-eight-cubit length
%		of the fabric goes up one side of the Tabernacle (ten
%		cubits high),
%		across the ceiling (eight cubits), and down the other
%		side (ten cubits).
%		A temple has been excavated in Israel at Arad. Its
%		measurements are
%		twenty cubits by six cubits, the same as the (inside
%		dimensions of the)
%		Tabernacle. On the significance of these dimensions, see
%		the comment on
%		26:30.
%	}

verses.original: אֹרֶךְ הַיְרִיעָה הָאַחַת שְׁמֹנֶה וְעֶשְׂרִים בָּאַמָּה וְרֹחַב אַרְבַּע בָּאַמָּה הַיְרִיעָה הָאֶחָת מִדָּה אַחַת לְכל הַיְרִיעֹת׃
verses.english: The length of one curtain shall be twenty-eight in cubits, and the width of one curtain four in cubits: one size to all the curtains.

tex.original: \hP{אֹרֶךְ הַיְרִיעָה הָאַחַת שְׁמֹנֶה וְעֶשְׂרִים בָּאַמָּה וְרֹחַב אַרְבַּע בָּאַמָּה הַיְרִיעָה הָאֶחָת מִדָּה אַחַת לְכל הַיְרִיעֹת׃}

verses.original: חֲמֵשׁ הַיְרִיעֹת תִּהְיֶיןָ חֹבְרֹת אִשָּׁה אֶל אֲחֹתָהּ וְחָמֵשׁ יְרִיעֹת חֹבְרֹת אִשָּׁה אֶל אֲחֹתָהּ׃
verses.english: Five curtains will be connected, each to its sister-piece, and five curtains connected, each to its sister-piece.

tex.original: \hP{חֲמֵשׁ הַיְרִיעֹת תִּהְיֶיןָ חֹבְרֹת אִשָּׁה אֶל אֲחֹתָהּ וְחָמֵשׁ יְרִיעֹת חֹבְרֹת אִשָּׁה אֶל אֲחֹתָהּ׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ לֻלְאֹת תְּכֵלֶת עַל שְׂפַת הַיְרִיעָה הָאֶחָת מִקָּצָה בַּחֹבָרֶת וְכֵן תַּעֲשֶׂה בִּשְׂפַת הַיְרִיעָה הַקִּיצוֹנָה בַּמַּחְבֶּרֶת הַשֵּׁנִית׃
verses.english: And you shall make loops of blue on the side of the one curtain at the end of the connected group, and you shall do so in the side of the end curtain in the second connected group.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ לֻלְאֹת תְּכֵלֶת עַל שְׂפַת הַיְרִיעָה הָאֶחָת מִקָּצָה בַּחֹבָרֶת וְכֵן תַּעֲשֶׂה בִּשְׂפַת הַיְרִיעָה הַקִּיצוֹנָה בַּמַּחְבֶּרֶת הַשֵּׁנִית׃}

verses.original: חֲמִשִּׁים לֻלָאֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה בַּיְרִיעָה הָאֶחָת וַחֲמִשִּׁים לֻלָאֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה בִּקְצֵה הַיְרִיעָה אֲשֶׁר בַּמַּחְבֶּרֶת הַשֵּׁנִית מַקְבִּילֹת הַלֻּלָאֹת אִשָּׁה אֶל אֲחֹתָהּ׃
verses.english: You shall make fifty loops in the end of the curtain that is in the second connected group, with the loops parallel: each to its sister-piece.

tex.original: \hP{חֲמִשִּׁים לֻלָאֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה בַּיְרִיעָה הָאֶחָת וַחֲמִשִּׁים לֻלָאֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה בִּקְצֵה הַיְרִיעָה אֲשֶׁר בַּמַּחְבֶּרֶת הַשֵּׁנִית מַקְבִּילֹת הַלֻּלָאֹת אִשָּׁה אֶל אֲחֹתָהּ׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ חֲמִשִּׁים קַרְסֵי זָהָב וְחִבַּרְתָּ אֶת הַיְרִיעֹת אִשָּׁה אֶל אֲחֹתָהּ בַּקְּרָסִים וְהָיָה הַמִּשְׁכָּן אֶחָד׃
verses.english: And you shall make fifty clasps of gold and connect the curtains, each to its sister-piece, with the clasps. And the Tabernacle will be one.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ חֲמִשִּׁים קַרְסֵי זָהָב וְחִבַּרְתָּ אֶת הַיְרִיעֹת אִשָּׁה אֶל אֲחֹתָהּ בַּקְּרָסִים וְהָיָה הַמִּשְׁכָּן אֶחָד׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the Tabernacle will be one. In the simplest sense, this
%		means that once
%		they sew all the curtains together and connect all the
%		loops and clasps,
%		the Tabernacle will be one whole piece. But the
%		wording—“the Tabernacle
%		will be one”—also fits with the centrality of the
%		Tabernacle to Israel’s
%		monotheism. One God, one Tabernacle, one altar, only one
%		place of
%		worship. Later it will be confirmed by divine
%		commandment that Israel
%		may have only one place of sacrifice, and that this one
%		place is in
%		front of the Tabernacle (Leviticus 17). There cannot be
%		more than one
%		place to worship God, because that might suggest that
%		there is more than
%		one God. Or, to put it more essentially: it is
%		inconceivable in the
%		first place in this new religion of a single deity that
%		there could
%		possibly be more than a single sanctuary. Those who
%		claim that Israel’s
%		religion was not a real monotheism until a very late
%		stage (Second
%		Temple) have not appreciated the significance of the
%		commandment of
%		centralization of worship at a single location.
%	}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ יְרִיעֹת עִזִּים לְאֹהֶל עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּן עַשְׁתֵּי עֶשְׂרֵה יְרִיעֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם׃
verses.english: “And you shall make curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the Tabernacle. You shall make them eleven curtains.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ יְרִיעֹת עִזִּים לְאֹהֶל עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּן עַשְׁתֵּי עֶשְׂרֵה יְרִיעֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם׃}

verses.original: אֹרֶךְ הַיְרִיעָה הָאַחַת שְׁלֹשִׁים בָּאַמָּה וְרֹחַב אַרְבַּע בָּאַמָּה הַיְרִיעָה הָאֶחָת מִדָּה אַחַת לְעַשְׁתֵּי עֶשְׂרֵה יְרִיעֹת׃
verses.english: The length of one curtain shall be thirty in cubits, and the width of one curtain four in cubits: one size for eleven curtains.

tex.original: \hP{אֹרֶךְ הַיְרִיעָה הָאַחַת שְׁלֹשִׁים בָּאַמָּה וְרֹחַב אַרְבַּע בָּאַמָּה הַיְרִיעָה הָאֶחָת מִדָּה אַחַת לְעַשְׁתֵּי עֶשְׂרֵה יְרִיעֹת׃}

verses.original: וְחִבַּרְתָּ אֶת חֲמֵשׁ הַיְרִיעֹת לְבָד וְאֶת שֵׁשׁ הַיְרִיעֹת לְבָד וְכָפַלְתָּ אֶת הַיְרִיעָה הַשִּׁשִּׁית אֶל מוּל פְּנֵי הָאֹהֶל׃
verses.english: And you shall connect five of the curtains by themselves and six of the curtains by themselves. And you shall double-fold the sixth curtain opposite the front of the tent.

tex.original: \hP{וְחִבַּרְתָּ אֶת חֲמֵשׁ הַיְרִיעֹת לְבָד וְאֶת שֵׁשׁ הַיְרִיעֹת לְבָד וְכָפַלְתָּ אֶת הַיְרִיעָה הַשִּׁשִּׁית אֶל מוּל פְּנֵי הָאֹהֶל׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		double-fold the sixth curtain. The extra, eleventh
%		curtain of the tent
%		is four cubits wide. When folded, each half of it covers
%		half of the
%		eight-cubits-wide back of the Tabernacle (Figure 4).
%		This also answers
%		the question of why the curtains are four cubits wide.
%		And it further
%		confirms that the Tabernacle is eight cubits wide.
%		Footnote 26:9.
%		opposite the front of the tent. Meaning: it falls along
%		the back wall,
%		facing the front. Thus v. 12 refers to “the hanging one
%		that is left
%		over among the tent’s curtains” and instructs that “you
%		shall hang half
%		of the leftover curtain on the back parts of the
%		Tabernacle.”
%	}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ חֲמִשִּׁים לֻלָאֹת עַל שְׂפַת הַיְרִיעָה הָאֶחָת הַקִּיצֹנָה בַּחֹבָרֶת וַחֲמִשִּׁים לֻלָאֹת עַל שְׂפַת הַיְרִיעָה הַחֹבֶרֶת הַשֵּׁנִית׃
verses.english: And you shall make fifty loops on the side of the one end curtain in the connected group and fifty loops on the side of the curtain of the second connected group.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ חֲמִשִּׁים לֻלָאֹת עַל שְׂפַת הַיְרִיעָה הָאֶחָת הַקִּיצֹנָה בַּחֹבָרֶת וַחֲמִשִּׁים לֻלָאֹת עַל שְׂפַת הַיְרִיעָה הַחֹבֶרֶת הַשֵּׁנִית׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ קַרְסֵי נְחֹשֶׁת חֲמִשִּׁים וְהֵבֵאתָ אֶת הַקְּרָסִים בַּלֻּלָאֹת וְחִבַּרְתָּ אֶת הָאֹהֶל וְהָיָה אֶחָד׃
verses.english: And you shall make fifty clasps of bronze and bring the clasps into the loops and connect the tent. And it will be one.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ קַרְסֵי נְחֹשֶׁת חֲמִשִּׁים וְהֵבֵאתָ אֶת הַקְּרָסִים בַּלֻּלָאֹת וְחִבַּרְתָּ אֶת הָאֹהֶל וְהָיָה אֶחָד׃}

verses.original: וְסֶרַח הָעֹדֵף בִּירִיעֹת הָאֹהֶל חֲצִי הַיְרִיעָה הָעֹדֶפֶת תִּסְרַח עַל אֲחֹרֵי הַמִּשְׁכָּן׃
verses.english: And the hanging one that is left over among the tent’s curtains: you shall hang half of the leftover curtain on the back parts of the Tabernacle.

tex.original: \hP{וְסֶרַח הָעֹדֵף בִּירִיעֹת הָאֹהֶל חֲצִי הַיְרִיעָה הָעֹדֶפֶת תִּסְרַח עַל אֲחֹרֵי הַמִּשְׁכָּן׃}

verses.original: וְהָאַמָּה מִזֶּה וְהָאַמָּה מִזֶּה בָּעֹדֵף בְּאֹרֶךְ יְרִיעֹת הָאֹהֶל יִהְיֶה סָרוּחַ עַל צִדֵּי הַמִּשְׁכָּן מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה לְכַסֹּתוֹ׃
verses.english: And the cubit on this side and the cubit on that side in the leftover in the length of the tent’s curtains shall be hung on the sides of the Tabernacle, on this side and on that side, to cover it.

tex.original: \hP{וְהָאַמָּה מִזֶּה וְהָאַמָּה מִזֶּה בָּעֹדֵף בְּאֹרֶךְ יְרִיעֹת הָאֹהֶל יִהְיֶה סָרוּחַ עַל צִדֵּי הַמִּשְׁכָּן מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה לְכַסֹּתוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the cubit on this side and the cubit on that side in the
%		leftover in the
%		length. This second set of curtains is thirty cubits
%		long. When it is
%		spread over the inside set of curtains, which is only
%		twenty-eight
%		cubits, there is thus a cubit left over on each side. It
%		“shall be hung
%		on the sides of the Tabernacle, on this side and on that
%		side, to cover
%		it.” That is, it is folded under the inside linen fabric
%		so as to
%		protect it from touching the ground.
%	}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ מִכְסֶה לָאֹהֶל עֹרֹת אֵילִם מְאדָּמִים וּמִכְסֵה עֹרֹת תְּחָשִׁים מִלְמָעְלָה׃
verses.english: And you shall make a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red and a covering of leather skins above.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ מִכְסֶה לָאֹהֶל עֹרֹת אֵילִם מְאדָּמִים וּמִכְסֵה עֹרֹת תְּחָשִׁים מִלְמָעְלָה׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁים לַמִּשְׁכָּן עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים עֹמְדִים׃
verses.english: “And you shall make the frames for the Tabernacle of acacia wood, standing.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁים לַמִּשְׁכָּן עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים עֹמְדִים׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		frames. Trellises—not solid boards or planks. If they
%		were solid, then
%		the linen curtains would be sandwiched between the
%		boards on the inside
%		and the goats’ hair and leather coverings on the outside
%		and could never
%		be seen.
%	}

verses.original: עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת אֹרֶךְ הַקָּרֶשׁ וְאַמָּה וַחֲצִי הָאַמָּה רֹחַב הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד׃
verses.english: The frame’s length shall be ten cubits, and the width of one frame a cubit and a half cubit.

tex.original: \hP{עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת אֹרֶךְ הַקָּרֶשׁ וְאַמָּה וַחֲצִי הָאַמָּה רֹחַב הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד׃}

verses.original: שְׁתֵּי יָדוֹת לַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד מְשֻׁלָּבֹת אִשָּׁה אֶל אֲחֹתָהּ כֵּן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְכֹל קַרְשֵׁי הַמִּשְׁכָּן׃
verses.english: One frame has two projections, each aligned with its sister-piece: so you shall make for all the Tabernacle’s frames.

tex.original: \hP{שְׁתֵּי יָדוֹת לַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד מְשֻׁלָּבֹת אִשָּׁה אֶל אֲחֹתָהּ כֵּן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְכֹל קַרְשֵׁי הַמִּשְׁכָּן׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁים לַמִּשְׁכָּן עֶשְׂרִים קֶרֶשׁ לִפְאַת נֶגְבָּה תֵימָנָה׃
verses.english: And you shall make the frames for the Tabernacle: twenty frames for the south side—to the south.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁים לַמִּשְׁכָּן עֶשְׂרִים קֶרֶשׁ לִפְאַת נֶגְבָּה תֵימָנָה׃}

verses.original: וְאַרְבָּעִים אַדְנֵי כֶסֶף תַּעֲשֶׂה תַּחַת עֶשְׂרִים הַקָּרֶשׁ שְׁנֵי אֲדָנִים תַּחַת הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד לִשְׁתֵּי יְדֹתָיו וּשְׁנֵי אֲדָנִים תַּחַת הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד לִשְׁתֵּי יְדֹתָיו׃
verses.english: And you shall make forty bases of silver under the twenty frames: two bases under one frame for its two projections and two bases under each other frame for its two projections.

tex.original: \hP{וְאַרְבָּעִים אַדְנֵי כֶסֶף תַּעֲשֶׂה תַּחַת עֶשְׂרִים הַקָּרֶשׁ שְׁנֵי אֲדָנִים תַּחַת הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד לִשְׁתֵּי יְדֹתָיו וּשְׁנֵי אֲדָנִים תַּחַת הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד לִשְׁתֵּי יְדֹתָיו׃}

verses.original: וּלְצֶלַע הַמִּשְׁכָּן הַשֵּׁנִית לִפְאַת צָפוֹן עֶשְׂרִים קָרֶשׁ׃
verses.english: And for the Tabernacle’s second side, for the north side: twenty frames

tex.original: \hP{וּלְצֶלַע הַמִּשְׁכָּן הַשֵּׁנִית לִפְאַת צָפוֹן עֶשְׂרִים קָרֶשׁ׃}

verses.original: וְאַרְבָּעִים אַדְנֵיהֶם כָּסֶף שְׁנֵי אֲדָנִים תַּחַת הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד וּשְׁנֵי אֲדָנִים תַּחַת הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד׃
verses.english: and their forty bases of silver, two bases under one frame and two bases under each other frame.

tex.original: \hP{וְאַרְבָּעִים אַדְנֵיהֶם כָּסֶף שְׁנֵי אֲדָנִים תַּחַת הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד וּשְׁנֵי אֲדָנִים תַּחַת הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד׃}

verses.original: וּלְיַרְכְּתֵי הַמִּשְׁכָּן יָמָּה תַּעֲשֶׂה שִׁשָּׁה קְרָשִׁים׃
verses.english: And for the rear of the Tabernacle, to the west, you shall make six frames.

tex.original: \hP{וּלְיַרְכְּתֵי הַמִּשְׁכָּן יָמָּה תַּעֲשֶׂה שִׁשָּׁה קְרָשִׁים׃}

verses.original: וּשְׁנֵי קְרָשִׁים תַּעֲשֶׂה לִמְקֻצְעֹת הַמִּשְׁכָּן בַּיַּרְכָתָיִם׃
verses.english: And you shall make two frames for the Tabernacle’s corners in the rear,

tex.original: \hP{וּשְׁנֵי קְרָשִׁים תַּעֲשֶׂה לִמְקֻצְעֹת הַמִּשְׁכָּן בַּיַּרְכָתָיִם׃}

verses.original: וְיִהְיוּ תֹאֲמִם מִלְּמַטָּה וְיַחְדָּו יִהְיוּ תַמִּים עַל רֹאשׁוֹ אֶל הַטַּבַּעַת הָאֶחָת כֵּן יִהְיֶה לִשְׁנֵיהֶם לִשְׁנֵי הַמִּקְצֹעֹת יִהְיוּ׃
verses.english: and they shall be doubles from below, and together they shall be integrated on its top to one ring. It shall be so for the two of them; they will be for the two corners.

tex.original: \hP{וְיִהְיוּ תֹאֲמִם מִלְּמַטָּה וְיַחְדָּו יִהְיוּ תַמִּים עַל רֹאשׁוֹ אֶל הַטַּבַּעַת הָאֶחָת כֵּן יִהְיֶה לִשְׁנֵיהֶם לִשְׁנֵי הַמִּקְצֹעֹת יִהְיוּ׃}

verses.original: וְהָיוּ שְׁמֹנָה קְרָשִׁים וְאַדְנֵיהֶם כֶּסֶף שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר אֲדָנִים שְׁנֵי אֲדָנִים תַּחַת הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד וּשְׁנֵי אֲדָנִים תַּחַת הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד׃
verses.english: And they shall be eight frames and their bases of silver, sixteen bases, two bases under one frame and two bases under each other frame.

tex.original: \hP{וְהָיוּ שְׁמֹנָה קְרָשִׁים וְאַדְנֵיהֶם כֶּסֶף שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר אֲדָנִים שְׁנֵי אֲדָנִים תַּחַת הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד וּשְׁנֵי אֲדָנִים תַּחַת הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ בְרִיחִם עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים חֲמִשָּׁה לְקַרְשֵׁי צֶלַע הַמִּשְׁכָּן הָאֶחָד׃
verses.english: And you shall make bars of acacia wood: five for the frames of one side of the Tabernacle

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשִׂיתָ בְרִיחִם עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים חֲמִשָּׁה לְקַרְשֵׁי צֶלַע הַמִּשְׁכָּן הָאֶחָד׃}

verses.original: וַחֲמִשָּׁה בְרִיחִם לְקַרְשֵׁי צֶלַע הַמִּשְׁכָּן הַשֵּׁנִית וַחֲמִשָּׁה בְרִיחִם לְקַרְשֵׁי צֶלַע הַמִּשְׁכָּן לַיַּרְכָתַיִם יָמָּה׃
verses.english: and five bars for the frames of the second side of the Tabernacle and five bars for the frames of the side of the Tabernacle at the rear, to the west,

tex.original: \hP{וַחֲמִשָּׁה בְרִיחִם לְקַרְשֵׁי צֶלַע הַמִּשְׁכָּן הַשֵּׁנִית וַחֲמִשָּׁה בְרִיחִם לְקַרְשֵׁי צֶלַע הַמִּשְׁכָּן לַיַּרְכָתַיִם יָמָּה׃}

verses.original: וְהַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכֹן בְּתוֹךְ הַקְּרָשִׁים מַבְרִחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה׃
verses.english: and the middle bar through the frames extending from end to end.

tex.original: \hP{וְהַבְּרִיחַ הַתִּיכֹן בְּתוֹךְ הַקְּרָשִׁים מַבְרִחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה׃}

verses.original: וְאֶת הַקְּרָשִׁים תְּצַפֶּה זָהָב וְאֶת טַבְּעֹתֵיהֶם תַּעֲשֶׂה זָהָב בָּתִּים לַבְּרִיחִם וְצִפִּיתָ אֶת הַבְּרִיחִם זָהָב׃
verses.english: And you shall plate the frames with gold, and you shall make their rings gold, housings for the bars, and you shall plate the bars with gold.

tex.original: \hP{וְאֶת הַקְּרָשִׁים תְּצַפֶּה זָהָב וְאֶת טַבְּעֹתֵיהֶם תַּעֲשֶׂה זָהָב בָּתִּים לַבְּרִיחִם וְצִפִּיתָ אֶת הַבְּרִיחִם זָהָב׃}

verses.original: וַהֲקֵמֹתָ אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן כְּמִשְׁפָּטוֹ אֲשֶׁר הרְאֵיתָ בָּהָר׃
verses.english: And you shall set up the Tabernacle according to the model of it that you were shown in the mountain.

tex.original: \hP{וַהֲקֵמֹתָ אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן כְּמִשְׁפָּטוֹ אֲשֶׁר הרְאֵיתָ בָּהָר׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		set up the Tabernacle. What difference do these cubits
%		make? Why does it
%		matter whether the Tabernacle is eight by twenty cubits
%		or ten by
%		thirty? Because eight by twenty cubits, and ten cubits
%		high, is the size
%		of the space under the wings of the cherubs inside the
%		Holy of Holies in
%		the Temple in Jerusalem. Either the Tabernacle really
%		stood in that
%		space, or the space represented it symbolically while
%		the Tabernacle
%		itself was stored away somewhere inside the building.
%		The Tanak reports
%		that the Tabernacle is in fact brought to the Temple on
%		the day of its
%		dedication (1 Kings 8:4; 2 Chr 5:5). The Talmud reports
%		that it was in
%		fact thus stored beneath the Temple (Soa 9a). The
%		ancient historian
%		Josephus says that the effect of the cherubs’ wings in
%		the Temple was to
%		appear like a tent (Ant. 8.103). A psalm says: “I’ll
%		reside in your tent
%		forever, I’ll conceal myself in the hidden place of your
%		wings” (Ps
%		61:5). The book of 1 Chronicles (9:23) refers to the
%		Temple as “the
%		House of the Tent” (bêt h ’hel). It also speaks of the
%		“Tabernacle of
%		the House of God” (6:33; see also 1 Chr 23:22; 2 Chr
%		29:6–7; 24:6). What
%		this means is that the Temple was not just the successor
%		to the
%		Tabernacle. The Tabernacle, revered as the ancient
%		channel to God, was
%		actually located inside the Temple. So all the laws in
%		the Torah that
%		command that something be done at the Tabernacle applied
%		as long as the
%		first Temple stood in Jerusalem. By the time of the
%		Temple’s destruction
%		(587 B.C.E.), the Tabernacle and its contents—the ark,
%		the
%		tablets—disappear from the Bible. The rabbinic tradition
%		is that the
%		presence of God (Shechinah; which, by the way, has the
%		same root as the
%		word for the Tabernacle: miškn) was in the first Temple
%		but not in the
%		second (Yoma 21b; Rashi on Gen 9:27). This contributes
%		to an impression
%		of growing distance from the original feeling of a
%		direct connection
%		with God in the Hebrew Bible. This construction of the
%		Tabernacle also
%		goes against the dominant view of biblical scholars for
%		the past
%		century: that the Tabernacle was not real, that it was
%		simply a fiction,
%		invented to stand for the second Temple in Jerusalem.
%		That view was
%		based on the two-to-one correspondence of the
%		measurements of the
%		Tabernacle and the Temple. In the first place, we have
%		seen that the
%		correspondence is not correct. (See point number one in
%		the comment on
%		26:1 above.) Second, those measurements were based on
%		the first Temple,
%		not the second, in any case. And, third, this chapter is
%		part of a text
%		that is written in Classical Hebrew, which comes from a
%		period long
%		before the second Temple.
%	}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ פָרֹכֶת תְּכֵלֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן וְתוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי וְשֵׁשׁ משְׁזָר מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב יַעֲשֶׂה אֹתָהּ כְּרֻבִים׃
