%		East, from developing in Israel. That is, it functions to prevent the
%		establishment of a class of wealthy landowners at the top of the
%		economic scale and a mass of landless peasants at the bottom. Every
%		Israelite is to be apportioned some land (described in the books of
%		Numbers and Joshua), and the deity commands that in every fiftieth year
%		the system returns to where it started. If an Israelite has lost his
%		ancestral land as a result of debt or calamity, he regains ownership of
%		it in the jubilee year. Land is unalienable. Individuals can suffer
%		difficult times, but there is a divinely decreed limit to their loss,
%		and the nation as a whole can never degenerate into a two-tiered system
%		of the very rich and the very poor.
%	}

verses.original: יוֹבֵל הִוא שְׁנַת הַחֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה תִּהְיֶה לָכֶם לֹא תִזְרָעוּ וְלֹא תִקְצְרוּ אֶת סְפִיחֶיהָ וְלֹא תִבְצְרוּ אֶת נְזִרֶיהָ׃
verses.english: It, the year that makes fifty years, shall be a jubilee for you. You shall not seed, and you shall not harvest its free growths, and you shall not cut off its untrimmed fruits,

tex.original: \hP{יוֹבֵל הִוא שְׁנַת הַחֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה תִּהְיֶה לָכֶם לֹא תִזְרָעוּ וְלֹא תִקְצְרוּ אֶת סְפִיחֶיהָ וְלֹא תִבְצְרוּ אֶת נְזִרֶיהָ׃}

verses.original: כִּי יוֹבֵל הִוא קֹדֶשׁ תִּהְיֶה לָכֶם מִן הַשָּׂדֶה תֹּאכְלוּ אֶת תְּבוּאָתָהּ׃
verses.english: because it is a jubilee; it shall be a holy thing to you. You shall eat its produce from the field.

tex.original: \hP{כִּי יוֹבֵל הִוא קֹדֶשׁ תִּהְיֶה לָכֶם מִן הַשָּׂדֶה תֹּאכְלוּ אֶת תְּבוּאָתָהּ׃}

verses.original: בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל הַזֹּאת תָּשֻׁבוּ אִישׁ אֶל אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verses.english: In this jubilee year you shall go back, each to his possession.

tex.original: \hP{בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל הַזֹּאת תָּשֻׁבוּ אִישׁ אֶל אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְכִי תִמְכְּרוּ מִמְכָּר לַעֲמִיתֶךָ אוֹ קָנֹה מִיַּד עֲמִיתֶךָ אַל תּוֹנוּ אִישׁ אֶת אָחִיו׃
verses.english: And when you will make a sale to your fellow or buy from your fellow’s hand: each of you, do not persecute his brother.

tex.original: \hP{וְכִי תִמְכְּרוּ מִמְכָּר לַעֲמִיתֶךָ אוֹ קָנֹה מִיַּד עֲמִיתֶךָ אַל תּוֹנוּ אִישׁ אֶת אָחִיו׃}

verses.original: בְּמִסְפַּר שָׁנִים אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל תִּקְנֶה מֵאֵת עֲמִיתֶךָ בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי תְבוּאֹת יִמְכּר לָךְ׃
verses.english: You shall buy from your fellow by the number of years after the jubilee. He shall sell to you by the number of years of yields—

tex.original: \hP{בְּמִסְפַּר שָׁנִים אַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל תִּקְנֶה מֵאֵת עֲמִיתֶךָ בְּמִסְפַּר שְׁנֵי תְבוּאֹת יִמְכּר לָךְ׃}

verses.original: לְפִי רֹב הַשָּׁנִים תַּרְבֶּה מִקְנָתוֹ וּלְפִי מְעֹט הַשָּׁנִים תַּמְעִיט מִקְנָתוֹ כִּי מִסְפַּר תְּבוּאֹת הוּא מֹכֵר לָךְ׃
verses.english: corresponding to a greater amount of the years, you shall make its price greater; and corresponding to a smaller amount of the years, you shall make its price smaller—because it is a number of yields that he is selling to you.

tex.original: \hP{לְפִי רֹב הַשָּׁנִים תַּרְבֶּה מִקְנָתוֹ וּלְפִי מְעֹט הַשָּׁנִים תַּמְעִיט מִקְנָתוֹ כִּי מִסְפַּר תְּבוּאֹת הוּא מֹכֵר לָךְ׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		corresponding to a greater amount of the years, you shall
		make its price greater; and corresponding to a smaller
		amount of the years, you shall make its price
		smaller—because it is a number of yields that he is
		selling to you.
	}

verses.original: וְלֹא תוֹנוּ אִישׁ אֶת עֲמִיתוֹ וְיָרֵאתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶיךָ כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: And you shall not persecute—each of you—his brother, but you shall fear your God, because I am YHWH, your God.

tex.original: \hP{וְלֹא תוֹנוּ אִישׁ אֶת עֲמִיתוֹ וְיָרֵאתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶיךָ כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֶת חֻקֹּתַי וְאֶת מִשְׁפָּטַי תִּשְׁמְרוּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֹתָם וִישַׁבְתֶּם עַל הָאָרֶץ לָבֶטַח׃
verses.english: “And you shall do my laws and observe my judgments and do them, so you will live on the land in security.

tex.original: \hP{וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֶת חֻקֹּתַי וְאֶת מִשְׁפָּטַי תִּשְׁמְרוּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֹתָם וִישַׁבְתֶּם עַל הָאָרֶץ לָבֶטַח׃}

verses.original: וְנָתְנָה הָאָרֶץ פִּרְיָהּ וַאֲכַלְתֶּם לָשֹׂבַע וִישַׁבְתֶּם לָבֶטַח עָלֶיהָ׃
verses.english: And the land will give its fruit, and you will eat to the full, and you will live in security on it.

tex.original: \hP{וְנָתְנָה הָאָרֶץ פִּרְיָהּ וַאֲכַלְתֶּם לָשֹׂבַע וִישַׁבְתֶּם לָבֶטַח עָלֶיהָ׃}

verses.original: וְכִי תֹאמְרוּ מַה נֹּאכַל בַּשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁבִיעִת הֵן לֹא נִזְרָע וְלֹא נֶאֱסֹף אֶת תְּבוּאָתֵנוּ׃
verses.english: And if you will say, ‘What shall we eat in the seventh year? Here, we won’t seed and won’t gather our produce,’

tex.original: \hP{וְכִי תֹאמְרוּ מַה נֹּאכַל בַּשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁבִיעִת הֵן לֹא נִזְרָע וְלֹא נֶאֱסֹף אֶת תְּבוּאָתֵנוּ׃}

verses.original: וְצִוִּיתִי אֶת בִּרְכָתִי לָכֶם בַּשָּׁנָה הַשִּׁשִּׁית וְעָשָׂת אֶת הַתְּבוּאָה לִשְׁלֹשׁ הַשָּׁנִים׃
verses.english: I shall command my blessing for you in the sixth year, and it will make the produce for the three years.

tex.original: \hP{וְצִוִּיתִי אֶת בִּרְכָתִי לָכֶם בַּשָּׁנָה הַשִּׁשִּׁית וְעָשָׂת אֶת הַתְּבוּאָה לִשְׁלֹשׁ הַשָּׁנִים׃}

verses.original: וּזְרַעְתֶּם אֵת הַשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁמִינִת וַאֲכַלְתֶּם מִן הַתְּבוּאָה יָשָׁן עַד הַשָּׁנָה הַתְּשִׁיעִת עַד בּוֹא תְּבוּאָתָהּ תֹּאכְלוּ יָשָׁן׃
verses.english: And you will seed the eighth year and eat from the old produce until the ninth year; you will eat the old until its produce comes.

tex.original: \hP{וּזְרַעְתֶּם אֵת הַשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁמִינִת וַאֲכַלְתֶּם מִן הַתְּבוּאָה יָשָׁן עַד הַשָּׁנָה הַתְּשִׁיעִת עַד בּוֹא תְּבוּאָתָהּ תֹּאכְלוּ יָשָׁן׃}

verses.original: וְהָאָרֶץ לֹא תִמָּכֵר לִצְמִתֻת כִּי לִי הָאָרֶץ כִּי גֵרִים וְתוֹשָׁבִים אַתֶּם עִמָּדִי׃
verses.english: But the land shall not be sold permanently, because the land is mine, because you are aliens and visitors with me!

tex.original: \hP{וְהָאָרֶץ לֹא תִמָּכֵר לִצְמִתֻת כִּי לִי הָאָרֶץ כִּי גֵרִים וְתוֹשָׁבִים אַתֶּם עִמָּדִי׃}

verses.original: וּבְכֹל אֶרֶץ אֲחֻזַּתְכֶם גְּאֻלָּה תִּתְּנוּ לָאָרֶץ׃
verses.english: So in all the land in your possession you shall give a redemption for the land.

tex.original: \hP{וּבְכֹל אֶרֶץ אֲחֻזַּתְכֶם גְּאֻלָּה תִּתְּנוּ לָאָרֶץ׃}

verses.original: כִּי יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ וּמָכַר מֵאֲחֻזָּתוֹ וּבָא גֹאֲלוֹ הַקָּרֹב אֵלָיו וְגָאַל אֵת מִמְכַּר אָחִיו׃
verses.english: When your brother will be low so that he will sell any of his possession, then his redeemer who is the closest relative to him shall come and redeem his brother’s sale.

tex.original: \hP{כִּי יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ וּמָכַר מֵאֲחֻזָּתוֹ וּבָא גֹאֲלוֹ הַקָּרֹב אֵלָיו וְגָאַל אֵת מִמְכַּר אָחִיו׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		25:25,35,39. when your brother will be low. Meaning: when your
%		fellow Israelite will be so poor that he has difficulty holding on
%		to his land. It has long been noted that the three times that this
%		phrase occurs in this chapter reflect three stages of increasing
%		hardship. In the first, the person has to sell his land. In the
%		second, he has both lost his land and is without money. And in the
%		third, he himself is sold (or sells himself) into servitude. And at
%		each stage, the man’s fellow Israelite is commanded to help him. If
%		he has to sell his land, one must redeem it for him and then give it
%		back to him in the jubilee year. If he is without money, one must
%		lend him money without any charge or interest. And if he is sold,
%		one must not treat him as a slave.
%
%		Here the units of law convey the specific requirements while the
%		arrangement conveys the basic principle, namely, that as one’s
%		brother’s need increases, so does one’s responsibility to help him.
%		Further, one must thus help one’s fellow as a matter of law. The
%		chapter never speaks of charity, nor does it appeal to one’s
%		feelings of compassion or generosity. An unfortunate Israelite need
%		not feel degraded to be poor nor ashamed to be pitied. Economic
%		suffering is rather treated as a reality of life, which one is
%		required by law to remedy. The poor man thus can know that his
%		brother is helping him because the system requires brothers to help
%		one another and that, if the shoe were on the other foot, he would
%		do the same for his brother. This is not to say that the text denies
%		or discourages feelings of compassion, but only that the fulfillment
%		of the law is not made dependent upon the presence or absence of
%		such feelings.
%	}

verses.original: וְאִישׁ כִּי לֹא יִהְיֶה לּוֹ גֹּאֵל וְהִשִּׂיגָה יָדוֹ וּמָצָא כְּדֵי גְאֻלָּתוֹ׃
verses.english: And when a man will not have a redeemer, but his hand has come to attain it and he has found enough for his redemption,

tex.original: \hP{וְאִישׁ כִּי לֹא יִהְיֶה לּוֹ גֹּאֵל וְהִשִּׂיגָה יָדוֹ וּמָצָא כְּדֵי גְאֻלָּתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְחִשַּׁב אֶת שְׁנֵי מִמְכָּרוֹ וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת הָעֹדֵף לָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר מָכַר לוֹ וְשָׁב לַאֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verses.english: then he shall figure the years of his sale and pay back what is left over to the man to whom he sold it, and he shall go back to his possession.

tex.original: \hP{וְחִשַּׁב אֶת שְׁנֵי מִמְכָּרוֹ וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת הָעֹדֵף לָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר מָכַר לוֹ וְשָׁב לַאֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם לֹא מָצְאָה יָדוֹ דֵּי הָשִׁיב לוֹ וְהָיָה מִמְכָּרוֹ בְּיַד הַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ עַד שְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל וְיָצָא בַּיֹּבֵל וְשָׁב לַאֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verses.english: And if his hand has not found enough to pay it back to him, then his sale shall be in the hand of the one who bought it until the jubilee year, and it shall come out in the jubilee, and he shall go back to his possession.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם לֹא מָצְאָה יָדוֹ דֵּי הָשִׁיב לוֹ וְהָיָה מִמְכָּרוֹ בְּיַד הַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ עַד שְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל וְיָצָא בַּיֹּבֵל וְשָׁב לַאֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְאִישׁ כִּי יִמְכֹּר בֵּית מוֹשַׁב עִיר חוֹמָה וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ עַד תֹּם שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ יָמִים תִּהְיֶה גְאֻלָּתוֹ׃
verses.english: “And when a man will sell a home in a walled city, then its redemption shall be until the end of the year of its sale. Its redemption shall be for days.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִישׁ כִּי יִמְכֹּר בֵּית מוֹשַׁב עִיר חוֹמָה וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ עַד תֹּם שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ יָמִים תִּהְיֶה גְאֻלָּתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם לֹא יִגָּאֵל עַד מְלֹאת לוֹ שָׁנָה תְמִימָה וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר בָּעִיר אֲשֶׁר [לוֹ] (לא) חֹמָה לַצְּמִיתֻת לַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ לְדֹרֹתָיו לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיֹּבֵל׃
verses.english: And if it will not be redeemed by the completion of a full year for it, then the house that is in a city that has a wall shall be established permanently for the one who bought it, through his generations. It shall not come out in the jubilee.
verses.commentary: Qere Ketiv.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם לֹא יִגָּאֵל עַד מְלֹאת לוֹ שָׁנָה תְמִימָה וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר בָּעִיר אֲשֶׁר [לוֹ] (לא) חֹמָה לַצְּמִיתֻת לַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ לְדֹרֹתָיו לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיֹּבֵל׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And if it will not be redeemed by the completion of a full
		year for it, then the house that is in a city that has a
		wall shall be established permanently for the one who
		bought it, through his generations. It shall not come out
		in the jubilee.
	}

verses.original: וּבָתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים אֲשֶׁר אֵין לָהֶם חֹמָה סָבִיב עַל שְׂדֵה הָאָרֶץ יֵחָשֵׁב גְּאֻלָּה תִּהְיֶה לּוֹ וּבַיֹּבֵל יֵצֵא׃
verses.english: “As for houses of the villages that do not have a wall around them: it shall be figured along with the land’s field. It shall have redemption, and it shall come out in the jubilee.

tex.original: \hP{וּבָתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים אֲשֶׁר אֵין לָהֶם חֹמָה סָבִיב עַל שְׂדֵה הָאָרֶץ יֵחָשֵׁב גְּאֻלָּה תִּהְיֶה לּוֹ וּבַיֹּבֵל יֵצֵא׃}

verses.original: וְעָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם בָּתֵּי עָרֵי אֲחֻזָּתָם גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם תִּהְיֶה לַלְוִיִּם׃
verses.english: “As for the Levites’ cities, the houses in the cities of their possession: the Levites shall have eternal redemption.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם בָּתֵּי עָרֵי אֲחֻזָּתָם גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם תִּהְיֶה לַלְוִיִּם׃}

verses.original: וַאֲשֶׁר יִגְאַל מִן הַלְוִיִּם וְיָצָא מִמְכַּר בַּיִת וְעִיר אֲחֻזָּתוֹ בַּיֹּבֵל כִּי בָתֵּי עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם הִוא אֲחֻזָּתָם בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And that which one from the Levites will redeem: it shall come out, a sale of a house and of a city of his possession, in the jubilee, because that—the houses of the Levites’ cities—is their possession among the children of Israel.

tex.original: \hP{וַאֲשֶׁר יִגְאַל מִן הַלְוִיִּם וְיָצָא מִמְכַּר בַּיִת וְעִיר אֲחֻזָּתוֹ בַּיֹּבֵל כִּי בָתֵּי עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם הִוא אֲחֻזָּתָם בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And that which one from the Levites will redeem: it shall
		come out, a sale of a house and of a city of his
		possession, in the jubilee, because that—the houses of the
		Levites’ cities—is their possession among the children of
		Israel.
	}

verses.original: וּשְׂדֵה מִגְרַשׁ עָרֵיהֶם לֹא יִמָּכֵר כִּי אֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם הוּא לָהֶם׃
verses.english: But a field of their cities’ surrounding land shall not be sold, because it is an eternal possession for them.

tex.original: \hP{וּשְׂדֵה מִגְרַשׁ עָרֵיהֶם לֹא יִמָּכֵר כִּי אֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם הוּא לָהֶם׃}

verses.original: וְכִי יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ וּמָטָה יָדוֹ עִמָּךְ וְהֶחֱזַקְתָּ בּוֹ גֵּר וְתוֹשָׁב וָחַי עִמָּךְ׃
verses.english: “And when your brother will be low so that his hand is slipping with you, then you shall take hold of him—an alien and a visitor—and he shall live with you.

tex.original: \hP{וְכִי יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ וּמָטָה יָדוֹ עִמָּךְ וְהֶחֱזַקְתָּ בּוֹ גֵּר וְתוֹשָׁב וָחַי עִמָּךְ׃}

verses.original: אַל תִּקַּח מֵאִתּוֹ נֶשֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּית וְיָרֵאתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶיךָ וְחֵי אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ׃
verses.english: Do not take interest or a charge from him; but you shall fear your God, and your brother will live with you.

tex.original: \hP{אַל תִּקַּח מֵאִתּוֹ נֶשֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּית וְיָרֵאתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶיךָ וְחֵי אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ׃}

verses.original: אֶת כַּסְפְּךָ לֹא תִתֵּן לוֹ בְּנֶשֶׁךְ וּבְמַרְבִּית לֹא תִתֵּן אכְלֶךָ׃
verses.english: You shall not give him your money for interest, and you shall not give him your food for a charge.

tex.original: \hP{אֶת כַּסְפְּךָ לֹא תִתֵּן לוֹ בְּנֶשֶׁךְ וּבְמַרְבִּית לֹא תִתֵּן אכְלֶךָ׃}

verses.original: אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי אֶתְכֶם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם לָתֵת לָכֶם אֶת אֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן לִהְיוֹת לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים׃
verses.english: I am YHWH, your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan, to be God to you.

tex.original: \hP{אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי אֶתְכֶם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם לָתֵת לָכֶם אֶת אֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן לִהְיוֹת לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים׃}

verses.original: וְכִי יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ וְנִמְכַּר לָךְ לֹא תַעֲבֹד בּוֹ עֲבֹדַת עָבֶד׃
verses.english: “And when your brother will be low with you so that he is sold to you, you shall not have him work a slave’s work.

tex.original: \hP{וְכִי יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ עִמָּךְ וְנִמְכַּר לָךְ לֹא תַעֲבֹד בּוֹ עֲבֹדַת עָבֶד׃}

verses.original: כְּשָׂכִיר כְּתוֹשָׁב יִהְיֶה עִמָּךְ עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל יַעֲבֹד עִמָּךְ׃
verses.english: He shall be like an employee, like a visitor, with you. He shall work with you until the jubilee year.

tex.original: \hP{כְּשָׂכִיר כְּתוֹשָׁב יִהְיֶה עִמָּךְ עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל יַעֲבֹד עִמָּךְ׃}

verses.original: וְיָצָא מֵעִמָּךְ הוּא וּבָנָיו עִמּוֹ וְשָׁב אֶל מִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ וְאֶל אֲחֻזַּת אֲבֹתָיו יָשׁוּב׃
verses.english: And he shall go out from you, he and his children with him, and go back to his family, and he shall go back to his fathers’ possession.

tex.original: \hP{וְיָצָא מֵעִמָּךְ הוּא וּבָנָיו עִמּוֹ וְשָׁב אֶל מִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ וְאֶל אֲחֻזַּת אֲבֹתָיו יָשׁוּב׃}

verses.original: כִּי עֲבָדַי הֵם אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי אֹתָם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם לֹא יִמָּכְרוּ מִמְכֶּרֶת עָבֶד׃
verses.english: Because they are my servants, whom I brought out from the land of Egypt; they shall not be sold like the sale of a slave.

tex.original: \hP{כִּי עֲבָדַי הֵם אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי אֹתָם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם לֹא יִמָּכְרוּ מִמְכֶּרֶת עָבֶד׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		servant, slave. The same Hebrew root (‘bd) is used for “servant” and
%		“slave.” It has a wider range of meaning in Hebrew than either word has
%		in English. Here it results in the use of its two different translations
%		in the very same sentence, but this still conveys the Torah’s meaning
%		more correctly than leveling the nuances of the Hebrew into a single
%		English word.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא תִרְדֶּה בוֹ בְּפָרֶךְ וְיָרֵאתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: You shall not dominate him with harshness, but you shall fear your God.

tex.original: \hP{לֹא תִרְדֶּה בוֹ בְּפָרֶךְ וְיָרֵאתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶיךָ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		dominate. “You shall not dominate him.” This is the term that is used
%		for human dominion over animals in Genesis 1. Israelites are explicitly
%		denied the kind of power over other human beings, even a slave, that
%		they might exert over animals. Footnote 25:43. with harshness. This is
%		the term that is used for the way the Egyptians made the Israelites work
%		(Exod 1:14). Eliminating slavery on earth has been a gradual process
%		rather than a revolution. The Israelites are permitted to have slaves
%		themselves, but not in the manner of the Egyptians. They cannot overwork
%		them. They cannot mistreat them (so an Israelite who knocks out his
%		slave’s tooth must set the slave free; Exod 21:2). The rules that are
%		imposed on treatment of slaves in the Torah involve a recognition of a
%		slave’s humanity and dignity, and they establish that a slave has
%		rights. This was a crucial first stage in the long process leading to
%		opposition to slavery altogether.
%	}

verses.original: וְעַבְדְּךָ וַאֲמָתְךָ אֲשֶׁר יִהְיוּ לָךְ מֵאֵת הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר סְבִיבֹתֵיכֶם מֵהֶם תִּקְנוּ עֶבֶד וְאָמָה׃
verses.english: “And your slave and your maid that you will have: from the nations that are around you, you shall buy a slave or a maid from them.

tex.original: \hP{וְעַבְדְּךָ וַאֲמָתְךָ אֲשֶׁר יִהְיוּ לָךְ מֵאֵת הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר סְבִיבֹתֵיכֶם מֵהֶם תִּקְנוּ עֶבֶד וְאָמָה׃}

verses.original: וְגַם מִבְּנֵי הַתּוֹשָׁבִים הַגָּרִים עִמָּכֶם מֵהֶם תִּקְנוּ וּמִמִּשְׁפַּחְתָּם אֲשֶׁר עִמָּכֶם אֲשֶׁר הוֹלִידוּ בְּאַרְצְכֶם וְהָיוּ לָכֶם לַאֲחֻזָּה׃
verses.english: And also from the children of the visitors who reside with you—you shall buy from them and from their families that are with you—to whom they gave birth in your land. And they shall become a possession for you.

tex.original: \hP{וְגַם מִבְּנֵי הַתּוֹשָׁבִים הַגָּרִים עִמָּכֶם מֵהֶם תִּקְנוּ וּמִמִּשְׁפַּחְתָּם אֲשֶׁר עִמָּכֶם אֲשֶׁר הוֹלִידוּ בְּאַרְצְכֶם וְהָיוּ לָכֶם לַאֲחֻזָּה׃}

verses.original: וְהִתְנַחַלְתֶּם אֹתָם לִבְנֵיכֶם אַחֲרֵיכֶם לָרֶשֶׁת אֲחֻזָּה לְעֹלָם בָּהֶם תַּעֲבֹדוּ וּבְאַחֵיכֶם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אִישׁ בְּאָחִיו לֹא תִרְדֶּה בוֹ בְּפָרֶךְ׃
verses.english: And you shall make them a legacy for your children after you to inherit as a possession. You may have them work forever, but as for your brothers, the children of Israel—a man toward his brother—you shall not dominate him with harshness.

tex.original: \hP{וְהִתְנַחַלְתֶּם אֹתָם לִבְנֵיכֶם אַחֲרֵיכֶם לָרֶשֶׁת אֲחֻזָּה לְעֹלָם בָּהֶם תַּעֲבֹדוּ וּבְאַחֵיכֶם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אִישׁ בְּאָחִיו לֹא תִרְדֶּה בוֹ בְּפָרֶךְ׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And you shall make them a legacy for your children after
		you to inherit as a possession. You may have them work
		forever, but as for your brothers, the children of
		Israel—a man toward his brother—you shall not dominate him
		with harshness.
	}

verses.original: וְכִי תַשִּׂיג יַד גֵּר וְתוֹשָׁב עִמָּךְ וּמָךְ אָחִיךָ עִמּוֹ וְנִמְכַּר לְגֵר תּוֹשָׁב עִמָּךְ אוֹ לְעֵקֶר מִשְׁפַּחַת גֵּר׃
verses.english: “And if the hand of an alien and visitor with you will attain it, and your brother is low with him and is sold to the alien and visitor with you or to an offshoot of an alien’s family,

tex.original: \hP{וְכִי תַשִּׂיג יַד גֵּר וְתוֹשָׁב עִמָּךְ וּמָךְ אָחִיךָ עִמּוֹ וְנִמְכַּר לְגֵר תּוֹשָׁב עִמָּךְ אוֹ לְעֵקֶר מִשְׁפַּחַת גֵּר׃}

verses.original: אַחֲרֵי נִמְכַּר גְּאֻלָּה תִּהְיֶה לּוֹ אֶחָד מֵאֶחָיו יִגְאָלֶנּוּ׃
verses.english: after he is sold he shall have redemption. One of his brothers shall redeem him,

tex.original: \hP{אַחֲרֵי נִמְכַּר גְּאֻלָּה תִּהְיֶה לּוֹ אֶחָד מֵאֶחָיו יִגְאָלֶנּוּ׃}

verses.original: אוֹ דֹדוֹ אוֹ בֶן דֹּדוֹ יִגְאָלֶנּוּ אוֹ מִשְּׁאֵר בְּשָׂרוֹ מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ יִגְאָלֶנּוּ אוֹ הִשִּׂיגָה יָדוֹ וְנִגְאָל׃
verses.english: or his uncle or his uncle’s son shall redeem him, or some close relative of his from his family shall redeem him; or if his hand can attain it then he can redeem himself.

tex.original: \hP{אוֹ דֹדוֹ אוֹ בֶן דֹּדוֹ יִגְאָלֶנּוּ אוֹ מִשְּׁאֵר בְּשָׂרוֹ מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ יִגְאָלֶנּוּ אוֹ הִשִּׂיגָה יָדוֹ וְנִגְאָל׃}

verses.original: וְחִשַּׁב עִם קֹנֵהוּ מִשְּׁנַת הִמָּכְרוֹ לוֹ עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְהָיָה כֶּסֶף מִמְכָּרוֹ בְּמִסְפַּר שָׁנִים כִּימֵי שָׂכִיר יִהְיֶה עִמּוֹ׃
verses.english: And he shall figure with the one who buys him: from the year he was sold to him to the jubilee year; and the price of his sale shall be by the number of years. It shall be with him like the days of an employee:

tex.original: \hP{וְחִשַּׁב עִם קֹנֵהוּ מִשְּׁנַת הִמָּכְרוֹ לוֹ עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְהָיָה כֶּסֶף מִמְכָּרוֹ בְּמִסְפַּר שָׁנִים כִּימֵי שָׂכִיר יִהְיֶה עִמּוֹ׃}

verses.original: אִם עוֹד רַבּוֹת בַּשָּׁנִים לְפִיהֶן יָשִׁיב גְּאֻלָּתוֹ מִכֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ׃
verses.english: If there are still a great number of years, he shall pay back his redemption according to them from his purchase price.

tex.original: \hP{אִם עוֹד רַבּוֹת בַּשָּׁנִים לְפִיהֶן יָשִׁיב גְּאֻלָּתוֹ מִכֶּסֶף מִקְנָתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם מְעַט נִשְׁאַר בַּשָּׁנִים עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְחִשַּׁב לוֹ כְּפִי שָׁנָיו יָשִׁיב אֶת גְּאֻלָּתוֹ׃
verses.english: And if a small amount of years remain until the jubilee year, then he shall figure it for him. He shall pay back his redemption according to his years.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם מְעַט נִשְׁאַר בַּשָּׁנִים עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְחִשַּׁב לוֹ כְּפִי שָׁנָיו יָשִׁיב אֶת גְּאֻלָּתוֹ׃}

verses.original: כִּשְׂכִיר שָׁנָה בְּשָׁנָה יִהְיֶה עִמּוֹ לֹא יִרְדֶּנּוּ בְּפֶרֶךְ לְעֵינֶיךָ׃
verses.english: He shall be with him like a year-by-year employee. He shall not dominate him with harshness before your eyes.

tex.original: \hP{כִּשְׂכִיר שָׁנָה בְּשָׁנָה יִהְיֶה עִמּוֹ לֹא יִרְדֶּנּוּ בְּפֶרֶךְ לְעֵינֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם לֹא יִגָּאֵל בְּאֵלֶּה וְיָצָא בִּשְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל הוּא וּבָנָיו עִמּוֹ׃
verses.english: And if he will not be redeemed by these, then he shall go out in the jubilee year, he and his children with him.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם לֹא יִגָּאֵל בְּאֵלֶּה וְיָצָא בִּשְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל הוּא וּבָנָיו עִמּוֹ׃}

verses.original: כִּי לִי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבָדִים עֲבָדַי הֵם אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי אוֹתָם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: Because the children of Israel are servants to me. They are my servants, whom I brought out from the land of Egypt. I am YHWH, your God.

tex.original: \hP{כִּי לִי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבָדִים עֲבָדַי הֵם אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי אוֹתָם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ לָכֶם אֱלִילִם וּפֶסֶל וּמַצֵּבָה לֹא תָקִימוּ לָכֶם וְאֶבֶן מַשְׂכִּית לֹא תִתְּנוּ בְּאַרְצְכֶם לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺת עָלֶיהָ כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: “You shall not make idols, and you shall not set up an image or a pillar, and you shall not put a carved stone in your land to bow at it, because I am YHWH, your God.

tex.original: \hP{לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ לָכֶם אֱלִילִם וּפֶסֶל וּמַצֵּבָה לֹא תָקִימוּ לָכֶם וְאֶבֶן מַשְׂכִּית לֹא תִתְּנוּ בְּאַרְצְכֶם לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺת עָלֶיהָ כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: אֶת שַׁבְּתֹתַי תִּשְׁמֹרוּ וּמִקְדָּשִׁי תִּירָאוּ אֲנִי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: “You shall observe my Sabbaths and fear my sanctuary. I am YHWH.

tex.original: \hP{אֶת שַׁבְּתֹתַי תִּשְׁמֹרוּ וּמִקְדָּשִׁי תִּירָאוּ אֲנִי יְהֹוָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		observe my Sabbaths and fear my sanctuary. What is the reason for
%		mentioning these two here together: Sabbaths and sanctuary? This
%		pronouncement brings together the sanctification of time and the
%		sanctification of space. The Sabbath is the most sacred time. The
%		sanctuary (meaning first the Tabernacle and later the Temple) is the
%		most sacred space. This dual command thus embraces everything.
%	}

verses.original: אִם בְּחֻקֹּתַי תֵּלֵכוּ וְאֶת מִצְוֺתַי תִּשְׁמְרוּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֹתָם׃
verses.english: BY MY LAWS “If you will go by my laws, and if you will observe my commandments, and you will do them:

tex.original: \hP{אִם בְּחֻקֹּתַי תֵּלֵכוּ וְאֶת מִצְוֺתַי תִּשְׁמְרוּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֹתָם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		If you will go by my laws. The key to the relationship between
%		Leviticus’s laws and the Bible’s story is the list of blessings and
%		curses here in Leviticus 26. The list comes at the conclusion and is
%		arguably the culmination of the book. It indicates that all of this law
%		has implications. Leviticus has definite connections to what has come
%		before it. The blessings-and-curses list is the connection to what will
%		follow. It says, plainly enough: the people’s fate will depend on
%		whether they follow these laws or not. The blessings include rain,
%		produce, satiety, security, peace, victory, population, divine presence,
%		and divine relationship. The curses include illness, defeat, wild
%		animals, pestilence, famine, divine rejection, destruction, dispersion,
%		and exile. The blessings and curses thus provide for the eventuality of
%		a variety of essential matters in the realms of nature, human relations
%		(especially political relations), and divine-human relationship. All
%		future stories of the fortunes of the people of Israel in these realms
%		are to be understood, according to this text, as being the results of
%		whether “you will go by my laws, and if you will observe my
%		commandments, and you will do them” (26:3) or “if you will reject my
%		laws, and if your souls will scorn my judgments so as not to do all my
%		commandments, so that you break my covenant” (26:15). Underscoring the
%		literary force of these promises and threats is not only their placement
%		at the conclusion of the book but the fact that the list of curses is
%		the most artfully written section in the book. I call it the most
%		artfully written on the basis of its wording as much as its content,
%		including words of irony (“you will flee though no one is pursuing you,”
%		26:17), words of horror (“you will eat your sons’ flesh, and your
%		daughters’ flesh you will eat,” 26:29), and words of pathos (“the sound
%		of a driven leaf will chase them,” 26:36). The commandments thus are not
%		presented as a loosely relevant list. They are woven into the fabric of
%		the narrative as essential to the life of the community.
%	}

verses.original: וְנָתַתִּי גִשְׁמֵיכֶם בְּעִתָּם וְנָתְנָה הָאָרֶץ יְבוּלָהּ וְעֵץ הַשָּׂדֶה יִתֵּן פִּרְיוֹ׃
verses.english: then I shall give your rains in their time, and the earth will give its crop, and the tree of the field will give its fruit,

tex.original: \hP{וְנָתַתִּי גִשְׁמֵיכֶם בְּעִתָּם וְנָתְנָה הָאָרֶץ יְבוּלָהּ וְעֵץ הַשָּׂדֶה יִתֵּן פִּרְיוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְהִשִּׂיג לָכֶם דַּיִשׁ אֶת בָּצִיר וּבָצִיר יַשִּׂיג אֶת זָרַע וַאֲכַלְתֶּם לַחְמְכֶם לָשֹׂבַע וִישַׁבְתֶּם לָבֶטַח בְּאַרְצְכֶם׃
verses.english: and threshing will extend to vintage for you, and vintage will extend to seeding, and you will eat your bread to the full, and you will live in security in your land,

tex.original: \hP{וְהִשִּׂיג לָכֶם דַּיִשׁ אֶת בָּצִיר וּבָצִיר יַשִּׂיג אֶת זָרַע וַאֲכַלְתֶּם לַחְמְכֶם לָשֹׂבַע וִישַׁבְתֶּם לָבֶטַח בְּאַרְצְכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְנָתַתִּי שָׁלוֹם בָּאָרֶץ וּשְׁכַבְתֶּם וְאֵין מַחֲרִיד וְהִשְׁבַּתִּי חַיָּה רָעָה מִן הָאָרֶץ וְחֶרֶב לֹא תַעֲבֹר בְּאַרְצְכֶם׃
verses.english: and I shall give peace in the land, and you will lie down with no one making you afraid, and I shall make wild animals cease from the land, and a sword will not pass through your land,

tex.original: \hP{וְנָתַתִּי שָׁלוֹם בָּאָרֶץ וּשְׁכַבְתֶּם וְאֵין מַחֲרִיד וְהִשְׁבַּתִּי חַיָּה רָעָה מִן הָאָרֶץ וְחֶרֶב לֹא תַעֲבֹר בְּאַרְצְכֶם׃}

verses.original: וּרְדַפְתֶּם אֶת אֹיְבֵיכֶם וְנָפְלוּ לִפְנֵיכֶם לֶחָרֶב׃
verses.english: and you will chase your enemies, and they will fall in front of you by the sword,

tex.original: \hP{וּרְדַפְתֶּם אֶת אֹיְבֵיכֶם וְנָפְלוּ לִפְנֵיכֶם לֶחָרֶב׃}

verses.original: וְרָדְפוּ מִכֶּם חֲמִשָּׁה מֵאָה וּמֵאָה מִכֶּם רְבָבָה יִרְדֹּפוּ וְנָפְלוּ אֹיְבֵיכֶם לִפְנֵיכֶם לֶחָרֶב׃
verses.english: and five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand, and your enemies will fall in front of you by the sword,

tex.original: \hP{וְרָדְפוּ מִכֶּם חֲמִשָּׁה מֵאָה וּמֵאָה מִכֶּם רְבָבָה יִרְדֹּפוּ וְנָפְלוּ אֹיְבֵיכֶם לִפְנֵיכֶם לֶחָרֶב׃}

verses.original: וּפָנִיתִי אֲלֵיכֶם וְהִפְרֵיתִי אֶתְכֶם וְהִרְבֵּיתִי אֶתְכֶם וַהֲקִימֹתִי אֶת בְּרִיתִי אִתְּכֶם׃
verses.english: and I shall turn to you, and I shall make you fruitful and make you multiply, and I shall establish my covenant with you,

tex.original: \hP{וּפָנִיתִי אֲלֵיכֶם וְהִפְרֵיתִי אֶתְכֶם וְהִרְבֵּיתִי אֶתְכֶם וַהֲקִימֹתִי אֶת בְּרִיתִי אִתְּכֶם׃}

verses.original: וַאֲכַלְתֶּם יָשָׁן נוֹשָׁן וְיָשָׁן מִפְּנֵי חָדָשׁ תּוֹצִיאוּ׃
verses.english: and you will eat the oldest of the old, and you will take out the old because of the new,

tex.original: \hP{וַאֲכַלְתֶּם יָשָׁן נוֹשָׁן וְיָשָׁן מִפְּנֵי חָדָשׁ תּוֹצִיאוּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the oldest of the old. Old, stored produce will still make good food.
%		Footnote 26:10. take out the old because of the new. One will never run
%		out of food. There will be good stored produce right up to the time that
%		the new crops come in, and the old will have to be taken out in order to
%		make room for the new.
%	}

verses.original: וְנָתַתִּי מִשְׁכָּנִי בְּתוֹכְכֶם וְלֹא תִגְעַל נַפְשִׁי אֶתְכֶם׃
verses.english: and I shall put my Tabernacle among you, and my soul will not scorn you,

tex.original: \hP{וְנָתַתִּי מִשְׁכָּנִי בְּתוֹכְכֶם וְלֹא תִגְעַל נַפְשִׁי אֶתְכֶם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		my soul. Does God have a soul? This is the only place in the Torah that
%		refers to the deity’s nepeš (although a related verbal form, wayyinnpaš,
%		occurs in Exod 31:17). Elsewhere, the word refers to the living quality
%		in humans and animals and is associated with breath. It is usually
%		understood to mean soul, person, being, and life. It might possibly help
%		us to understand what is meant by creation in the image of God, but that
%		seems unlikely since animals are said to have a nepeš there as well, but
%		they are not said to be in the divine image (Gen 1:24–27). We must be
%		cautious in using the word’s occurrences here to conclude anything about
%		the Torah’s conception of God, because both of these occurrences are in
%		the phrase “my soul will scorn.” This phrase may simply have been a
%		known expression. It also occurs here with humans as the subject
%		(26:15); and it occurs in Jeremiah as well (14:19). It may refer to the
%		personal aspect of God, or it may rather refer to God in no specific
%		way. Rashi (following Siphra) takes the phrase to refer to the departure
%		of the divine presence (Shechinah). Here, too, we must be cautious,
%		first, because that is also the understanding of other metaphorical
%		phrases in the Tanak. Thus the Targum takes the phrase “God hides His
%		face” to mean the departure of the Shechinah as well. And, second, the
%		word Shechinah never occurs in the Torah or anywhere in the Hebrew
%		Bible.
%	}

verses.original: וְהִתְהַלַּכְתִּי בְּתוֹכְכֶם וְהָיִיתִי לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים וְאַתֶּם תִּהְיוּ לִי לְעָם׃
verses.english: and I shall walk among you, and I shall be God to you, and you will be a people to me.

tex.original: \hP{וְהִתְהַלַּכְתִּי בְּתוֹכְכֶם וְהָיִיתִי לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים וְאַתֶּם תִּהְיוּ לִי לְעָם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		walk among you. This same term is used to describe God’s walking among
%		humans in the garden of Eden (the Hebrew root in the Hitpael; Gen 3:8).
%		This blessing thus hints at a return of the closeness to the divine
%		presence that existed prior to the initial divine-human conflict in
%		Eden. Footnote 26:12. I shall be God to you, and you will be a people to
%		me. The last blessing of the list echoes what is thought to be the
%		wording of the marriage ceremony in ancient Israel: “I shall be a
%		husband to you, and you will be a wife to me”—as well as the adoption
%		ceremony: “I shall be a parent to you, and you will be a son/daughter to
%		me” (see, e.g., 2 Sam 7:14).
%	}

verses.original: אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי אֶתְכֶם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם מִהְיֹת לָהֶם עֲבָדִים וָאֶשְׁבֹּר מֹטֹת עֻלְּכֶם וָאוֹלֵךְ אֶתְכֶם קוֹמְמִיּוּת׃
verses.english: I am YHWH, your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from being slaves to them, and I broke the beams of your yoke and had you go standing tall.

tex.original: \hP{אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי אֶתְכֶם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם מִהְיֹת לָהֶם עֲבָדִים וָאֶשְׁבֹּר מֹטֹת עֻלְּכֶם וָאוֹלֵךְ אֶתְכֶם קוֹמְמִיּוּת׃}

verses.original: וְאִם לֹא תִשְׁמְעוּ לִי וְלֹא תַעֲשׂוּ אֵת כּל הַמִּצְוֺת הָאֵלֶּה׃
verses.english: “But if you will not listen to me and not do all these commandments,

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם לֹא תִשְׁמְעוּ לִי וְלֹא תַעֲשׂוּ אֵת כּל הַמִּצְוֺת הָאֵלֶּה׃}

verses.original: וְאִם בְּחֻקֹּתַי תִּמְאָסוּ וְאִם אֶת מִשְׁפָּטַי תִּגְעַל נַפְשְׁכֶם לְבִלְתִּי עֲשׂוֹת אֶת כּל מִצְוֺתַי לְהַפְרְכֶם אֶת בְּרִיתִי׃
verses.english: and if you will reject my laws, and if your souls will scorn my judgments so as not to do all my commandments, so that you break my covenant,

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם בְּחֻקֹּתַי תִּמְאָסוּ וְאִם אֶת מִשְׁפָּטַי תִּגְעַל נַפְשְׁכֶם לְבִלְתִּי עֲשׂוֹת אֶת כּל מִצְוֺתַי לְהַפְרְכֶם אֶת בְּרִיתִי׃}

verses.original: אַף אֲנִי אֶעֱשֶׂה זֹּאת לָכֶם וְהִפְקַדְתִּי עֲלֵיכֶם בֶּהָלָה אֶת הַשַּׁחֶפֶת וְאֶת הַקַּדַּחַת מְכַלּוֹת עֵינַיִם וּמְדִיבֹת נָפֶשׁ וּזְרַעְתֶּם לָרִיק זַרְעֲכֶם וַאֲכָלֻהוּ אֹיְבֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: I, too, I shall do this to you: Then I shall appoint terror over you with consumption and with fever, exhausting eyes and grieving the soul, and you will sow your seed in vain, for your enemies will eat it,

tex.original: \hP{אַף אֲנִי אֶעֱשֶׂה זֹּאת לָכֶם וְהִפְקַדְתִּי עֲלֵיכֶם בֶּהָלָה אֶת הַשַּׁחֶפֶת וְאֶת הַקַּדַּחַת מְכַלּוֹת עֵינַיִם וּמְדִיבֹת נָפֶשׁ וּזְרַעְתֶּם לָרִיק זַרְעֲכֶם וַאֲכָלֻהוּ אֹיְבֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְנָתַתִּי פָנַי בָּכֶם וְנִגַּפְתֶּם לִפְנֵי אֹיְבֵיכֶם וְרָדוּ בָכֶם שֹׂנְאֵיכֶם וְנַסְתֶּם וְאֵין רֹדֵף אֶתְכֶם׃
verses.english: and I shall set my face against you, and you will be struck before your enemies, and ones who hate you will dominate you, and you will flee though no one is pursuing you.

tex.original: \hP{וְנָתַתִּי פָנַי בָּכֶם וְנִגַּפְתֶּם לִפְנֵי אֹיְבֵיכֶם וְרָדוּ בָכֶם שֹׂנְאֵיכֶם וְנַסְתֶּם וְאֵין רֹדֵף אֶתְכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְאִם עַד אֵלֶּה לֹא תִשְׁמְעוּ לִי וְיָסַפְתִּי לְיַסְּרָה אֶתְכֶם שֶׁבַע עַל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: And if, even after these, you will not listen to me, then I shall add seven times more to discipline you for your sins:

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם עַד אֵלֶּה לֹא תִשְׁמְעוּ לִי וְיָסַפְתִּי לְיַסְּרָה אֶתְכֶם שֶׁבַע עַל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְשָׁבַרְתִּי אֶת גְּאוֹן עֻזְּכֶם וְנָתַתִּי אֶת שְׁמֵיכֶם כַּבַּרְזֶל וְאֶת אַרְצְכֶם כַּנְּחֻשָׁה׃
verses.english: and I shall break your strong pride, and I shall make your skies like iron and your land like bronze,

tex.original: \hP{וְשָׁבַרְתִּי אֶת גְּאוֹן עֻזְּכֶם וְנָתַתִּי אֶת שְׁמֵיכֶם כַּבַּרְזֶל וְאֶת אַרְצְכֶם כַּנְּחֻשָׁה׃}

verses.original: וְתַם לָרִיק כֹּחֲכֶם וְלֹא תִתֵּן אַרְצְכֶם אֶת יְבוּלָהּ וְעֵץ הָאָרֶץ לֹא יִתֵּן פִּרְיוֹ׃
verses.english: and your power will be used up in vain, and your land will not give its crop, and the tree of the land will not give its fruit.

tex.original: \hP{וְתַם לָרִיק כֹּחֲכֶם וְלֹא תִתֵּן אַרְצְכֶם אֶת יְבוּלָהּ וְעֵץ הָאָרֶץ לֹא יִתֵּן פִּרְיוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם תֵּלְכוּ עִמִּי קֶרִי וְלֹא תֹאבוּ לִשְׁמֹעַ לִי וְיָסַפְתִּי עֲלֵיכֶם מַכָּה שֶׁבַע כְּחַטֹּאתֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: And if you will go on with me in defiance and will not be willing to listen to me, then I shall add seven times more striking on you, corresponding to your sins:

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם תֵּלְכוּ עִמִּי קֶרִי וְלֹא תֹאבוּ לִשְׁמֹעַ לִי וְיָסַפְתִּי עֲלֵיכֶם מַכָּה שֶׁבַע כְּחַטֹּאתֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְהִשְׁלַחְתִּי בָכֶם אֶת חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה וְשִׁכְּלָה אֶתְכֶם וְהִכְרִיתָה אֶת בְּהֶמְתְּכֶם וְהִמְעִיטָה אֶתְכֶם וְנָשַׁמּוּ דַּרְכֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: and I shall let loose the wild animal among you, and it will bereave you, and it will cut off your cattle, and it will diminish you, and your roads will be desolated.

tex.original: \hP{וְהִשְׁלַחְתִּי בָכֶם אֶת חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה וְשִׁכְּלָה אֶתְכֶם וְהִכְרִיתָה אֶת בְּהֶמְתְּכֶם וְהִמְעִיטָה אֶתְכֶם וְנָשַׁמּוּ דַּרְכֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְאִם בְּאֵלֶּה לֹא תִוָּסְרוּ לִי וַהֲלַכְתֶּם עִמִּי קֶרִי׃
verses.english: And if you will not be disciplined for me by these, and you will go on with me in defiance,

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם בְּאֵלֶּה לֹא תִוָּסְרוּ לִי וַהֲלַכְתֶּם עִמִּי קֶרִי׃}

verses.original: וְהָלַכְתִּי אַף אֲנִי עִמָּכֶם בְּקֶרִי וְהִכֵּיתִי אֶתְכֶם גַּם אָנִי שֶׁבַע עַל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: then I shall go on with you, I also, in defiance. And I shall strike you, I too, seven times more for your sins:

tex.original: \hP{וְהָלַכְתִּי אַף אֲנִי עִמָּכֶם בְּקֶרִי וְהִכֵּיתִי אֶתְכֶם גַּם אָנִי שֶׁבַע עַל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְהֵבֵאתִי עֲלֵיכֶם חֶרֶב נֹקֶמֶת נְקַם בְּרִית וְנֶאֱסַפְתֶּם אֶל עָרֵיכֶם וְשִׁלַּחְתִּי דֶבֶר בְּתוֹכְכֶם וְנִתַּתֶּם בְּיַד אוֹיֵב׃
verses.english: and I shall bring a sword over you, requiting covenant retribution, and you will be gathered to your cities, and I shall let an epidemic go among you, and you will be put in your enemy’s hand.

tex.original: \hP{וְהֵבֵאתִי עֲלֵיכֶם חֶרֶב נֹקֶמֶת נְקַם בְּרִית וְנֶאֱסַפְתֶּם אֶל עָרֵיכֶם וְשִׁלַּחְתִּי דֶבֶר בְּתוֹכְכֶם וְנִתַּתֶּם בְּיַד אוֹיֵב׃}

verses.original: בְּשִׁבְרִי לָכֶם מַטֵּה לֶחֶם וְאָפוּ עֶשֶׂר נָשִׁים לַחְמְכֶם בְּתַנּוּר אֶחָד וְהֵשִׁיבוּ לַחְמְכֶם בַּמִּשְׁקָל וַאֲכַלְתֶּם וְלֹא תִשְׂבָּעוּ׃
verses.english: When I break the staff of bread for you, then ten women will bake your bread in one oven, and they will give back your bread by weight, and you will eat and not be full.

tex.original: \hP{בְּשִׁבְרִי לָכֶם מַטֵּה לֶחֶם וְאָפוּ עֶשֶׂר נָשִׁים לַחְמְכֶם בְּתַנּוּר אֶחָד וְהֵשִׁיבוּ לַחְמְכֶם בַּמִּשְׁקָל וַאֲכַלְתֶּם וְלֹא תִשְׂבָּעוּ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם בְּזֹאת לֹא תִשְׁמְעוּ לִי וַהֲלַכְתֶּם עִמִּי בְּקֶרִי׃
verses.english: And if, through this, you will not listen to me, and you will go on with me in defiance,

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם בְּזֹאת לֹא תִשְׁמְעוּ לִי וַהֲלַכְתֶּם עִמִּי בְּקֶרִי׃}

verses.original: וְהָלַכְתִּי עִמָּכֶם בַּחֲמַת קֶרִי וְיִסַּרְתִּי אֶתְכֶם אַף אָנִי שֶׁבַע עַל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: then I shall go on with you in a fury of defiance, and I shall discipline you, I also, seven times more for your sins:

tex.original: \hP{וְהָלַכְתִּי עִמָּכֶם בַּחֲמַת קֶרִי וְיִסַּרְתִּי אֶתְכֶם אַף אָנִי שֶׁבַע עַל חַטֹּאתֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וַאֲכַלְתֶּם בְּשַׂר בְּנֵיכֶם וּבְשַׂר בְּנֹתֵיכֶם תֹּאכֵלוּ׃
verses.english: and you will eat your sons’ flesh, and your daughters’ flesh you will eat,

tex.original: \hP{וַאֲכַלְתֶּם בְּשַׂר בְּנֵיכֶם וּבְשַׂר בְּנֹתֵיכֶם תֹּאכֵלוּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		you will eat your sons’ flesh and your daughters’ flesh. The blessings
%		and curses are not rewards and punishments. They are a formal part of
%		the biblical covenants (Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28)—with exact
%		parallels in legal contracts of the ancient Near East. They express the
%		outcomes of fulfillment or nonfulfillment of the covenant’s terms. A
%		people who is faithful to its God and keeps the Sabbath and honors its
%		parents and does not steal will be prosperous and enduring in its land.
%		A people who loses sight of its commitments and values will suffer. (It
%		should not be hard to think of contemporary parallels.) The frightful
%		curse of eating one’s own children comes true centuries later in one of
%		the most horrifying stories in the Bible (2 Kings 6:24–30). It is not
%		presented there as a punishment. It rather conveys the terrible state of
%		things in Israel in the wake of the heretical reigns of Kings Ahab and
%		Jehoram. There is a big difference between a punishment and a curse,
%		between a threat and a warning. This explanation is still distressing,
%		but it does not so easily picture the deity as malicious, as people have
%		sometimes taken these curses to mean. The God of the Hebrew Bible is not
%		the “Old Testament God of Wrath,” but rather a deity who is torn between
%		mercy and justice, between affection for humankind and regret over the
%		continuous conflict with them. The curses are a sad outcome of a certain
%		kind of human behavior. But, then, the blessings are the outcome of the
%		other kind.
%	}

verses.original: וְהִשְׁמַדְתִּי אֶת בָּמֹתֵיכֶם וְהִכְרַתִּי אֶת חַמָּנֵיכֶם וְנָתַתִּי אֶת פִּגְרֵיכֶם עַל פִּגְרֵי גִּלּוּלֵיכֶם וְגָעֲלָה נַפְשִׁי אֶתְכֶם׃
verses.english: and I shall destroy your high places, and I shall cut off your incense altars, and I shall put your carcasses on your idols’ carcasses, and my soul will scorn you,

tex.original: \hP{וְהִשְׁמַדְתִּי אֶת בָּמֹתֵיכֶם וְהִכְרַתִּי אֶת חַמָּנֵיכֶם וְנָתַתִּי אֶת פִּגְרֵיכֶם עַל פִּגְרֵי גִּלּוּלֵיכֶם וְגָעֲלָה נַפְשִׁי אֶתְכֶם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		high places. These were large stone platforms where sacrifices were
%		performed. Some were used for worship of YHWH, and others were used for
%		worship of pagan gods; but both kinds are regularly forbidden in the
%		Tanak. High places to the God of Israel are regarded as violations of
%		the laws of centralization of worship at a single site (see comments on
%		Lev 1:3 and 17:4). Footnote 26:30. incense altars. These were stands,
%		usually designed, on which incense was burned. Both high places and
%		incense altars have been excavated in Israel.
%	}

verses.original: וְנָתַתִּי אֶת עָרֵיכֶם חרְבָּה וַהֲשִׁמּוֹתִי אֶת מִקְדְּשֵׁיכֶם וְלֹא אָרִיחַ בְּרֵיחַ נִיחֹחֲכֶם׃
verses.english: and I shall make your cities a ruin, and I shall devastate your holy places, and I shall not smell your pleasant smell,

tex.original: \hP{וְנָתַתִּי אֶת עָרֵיכֶם חרְבָּה וַהֲשִׁמּוֹתִי אֶת מִקְדְּשֵׁיכֶם וְלֹא אָרִיחַ בְּרֵיחַ נִיחֹחֲכֶם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		not smell your pleasant smell. The “pleasant smell” has been referred to
%		many times as the product of the burning incense that accompanies the
%		sacrifices. Starting with Noah’s sacrifice after the flood, the smell of
%		sacrifices is meant to be attractive to the deity, but the curse here is
%		that God will refuse to smell it.
%	}

verses.original: וַהֲשִׁמֹּתִי אֲנִי אֶת הָאָרֶץ וְשָׁמְמוּ עָלֶיהָ אֹיְבֵיכֶם הַיֹּשְׁבִים בָּהּ׃
verses.english: and I, I, shall devastate the land, so your enemies who live in it will be astonished,

tex.original: \hP{וַהֲשִׁמֹּתִי אֲנִי אֶת הָאָרֶץ וְשָׁמְמוּ עָלֶיהָ אֹיְבֵיכֶם הַיֹּשְׁבִים בָּהּ׃}

verses.original: וְאֶתְכֶם אֱזָרֶה בַגּוֹיִם וַהֲרִיקֹתִי אַחֲרֵיכֶם חָרֶב וְהָיְתָה אַרְצְכֶם שְׁמָמָה וְעָרֵיכֶם יִהְיוּ חרְבָּה׃
verses.english: and you: I shall scatter among the nations, and I shall unsheathe my sword after you, and your land will be a devastation, and your cities will be a ruin.

tex.original: \hP{וְאֶתְכֶם אֱזָרֶה בַגּוֹיִם וַהֲרִיקֹתִי אַחֲרֵיכֶם חָרֶב וְהָיְתָה אַרְצְכֶם שְׁמָמָה וְעָרֵיכֶם יִהְיוּ חרְבָּה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		scatter among the nations. Among the worst curses was the curse of
%		exile: for a people to be driven off their land and scattered around the
%		world. This possibility was a reality in the ancient Near East, where
%		exile was a horrifying fate. This curse would come to pass for Israel
%		later in the Tanak, when they would come to know exile at the hands of
%		the Assyrians; and it would come to pass for Judah still later at the
%		hands of the Babylonians. But they would also come to know the blessing
%		of return. Footnote 26:33. unsheathe my sword. To appreciate the horror
%		of the metaphor of God saying He will go after Israel unsheathing a
%		sword, one should recall that this is exactly what the Egyptians say
%		that they will do to Israel in the Song of the Sea (Exod 15:9). That is,
%		God, who is Israel’s protector, threatens a curse in which God would
%		become like Israel’s enemies. It is one’s worst nightmare: that one’s
%		loving, protecting parents become a horrible threat.
%	}

verses.original: אָז תִּרְצֶה הָאָרֶץ אֶת שַׁבְּתֹתֶיהָ כֹּל יְמֵי השַּׁמָּה וְאַתֶּם בְּאֶרֶץ אֹיְבֵיכֶם אָז תִּשְׁבַּת הָאָרֶץ וְהִרְצָת אֶת שַׁבְּתֹתֶיהָ׃
verses.english: Then the land will accept its Sabbaths: all the days of devastation, while you are in your enemies’ land. Then the land will cease and accept its Sabbaths.

tex.original: \hP{אָז תִּרְצֶה הָאָרֶץ אֶת שַׁבְּתֹתֶיהָ כֹּל יְמֵי השַּׁמָּה וְאַתֶּם בְּאֶרֶץ אֹיְבֵיכֶם אָז תִּשְׁבַּת הָאָרֶץ וְהִרְצָת אֶת שַׁבְּתֹתֶיהָ׃}

verses.original: כּל יְמֵי השַּׁמָּה תִּשְׁבֹּת אֵת אֲשֶׁר לֹא שָׁבְתָה בְּשַׁבְּתֹתֵיכֶם בְּשִׁבְתְּכֶם עָלֶיהָ׃
verses.english: All the days of the desolation it will cease, the amount that it did not cease on your Sabbaths when you lived on it.

tex.original: \hP{כּל יְמֵי השַּׁמָּה תִּשְׁבֹּת אֵת אֲשֶׁר לֹא שָׁבְתָה בְּשַׁבְּתֹתֵיכֶם בְּשִׁבְתְּכֶם עָלֶיהָ׃}

verses.original: וְהַנִּשְׁאָרִים בָּכֶם וְהֵבֵאתִי מֹרֶךְ בִּלְבָבָם בְּאַרְצֹת אֹיְבֵיהֶם וְרָדַף אֹתָם קוֹל עָלֶה נִדָּף וְנָסוּ מְנֻסַת חֶרֶב וְנָפְלוּ וְאֵין רֹדֵף׃
verses.english: And those of you who remain: I shall bring faintness in their hearts in their enemies’ lands, and the sound of a driven leaf will chase them, and they will flee like the flight from a sword, and they will fall when there is no one pursuing,

tex.original: \hP{וְהַנִּשְׁאָרִים בָּכֶם וְהֵבֵאתִי מֹרֶךְ בִּלְבָבָם בְּאַרְצֹת אֹיְבֵיהֶם וְרָדַף אֹתָם קוֹל עָלֶה נִדָּף וְנָסוּ מְנֻסַת חֶרֶב וְנָפְלוּ וְאֵין רֹדֵף׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And those of you who remain: I shall bring faintness in
		their hearts in their enemies’ lands, and the sound of a
		driven leaf will chase them, and they will flee like the
		flight from a sword, and they will fall when there is no
		one pursuing,
	}

verses.original: וְכָשְׁלוּ אִישׁ בְּאָחִיו כְּמִפְּנֵי חֶרֶב וְרֹדֵף אָיִן וְלֹא תִהְיֶה לָכֶם תְּקוּמָה לִפְנֵי אֹיְבֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: and they will stumble, each over his brother, as in front of a sword, when there is no one pursuing, and you will not have a footing in front of your enemies,

tex.original: \hP{וְכָשְׁלוּ אִישׁ בְּאָחִיו כְּמִפְּנֵי חֶרֶב וְרֹדֵף אָיִן וְלֹא תִהְיֶה לָכֶם תְּקוּמָה לִפְנֵי אֹיְבֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וַאֲבַדְתֶּם בַּגּוֹיִם וְאָכְלָה אֶתְכֶם אֶרֶץ אֹיְבֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: and you will perish among the nations, and your enemies’ land will eat you up,

tex.original: \hP{וַאֲבַדְתֶּם בַּגּוֹיִם וְאָכְלָה אֶתְכֶם אֶרֶץ אֹיְבֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְהַנִּשְׁאָרִים בָּכֶם יִמַּקּוּ בַּעֲוֺנָם בְּאַרְצֹת אֹיְבֵיכֶם וְאַף בַּעֲוֺנֹת אֲבֹתָם אִתָּם יִמָּקּוּ׃
verses.english: and those of you who remain will rot for their crime in your enemies’ lands, and also for their fathers’ crimes with them they will rot.

tex.original: \hR{וְהַנִּשְׁאָרִים בָּכֶם יִמַּקּוּ בַּעֲוֺנָם בְּאַרְצֹת אֹיְבֵיכֶם וְאַף בַּעֲוֺנֹת אֲבֹתָם אִתָּם יִמָּקּוּ׃}

verses.original: וְהִתְוַדּוּ אֶת עֲוֺנָם וְאֶת עֲוֺן אֲבֹתָם בְּמַעֲלָם אֲשֶׁר מָעֲלוּ בִי וְאַף אֲשֶׁר הָלְכוּ עִמִּי בְּקֶרִי׃
verses.english: “When they will confess their crime and their fathers’ crime for their breach that they made against me, and also that they went on with me in defiance,

tex.original: \hR{וְהִתְוַדּוּ אֶת עֲוֺנָם וְאֶת עֲוֺן אֲבֹתָם בְּמַעֲלָם אֲשֶׁר מָעֲלוּ בִי וְאַף אֲשֶׁר הָלְכוּ עִמִּי בְּקֶרִי׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		their crime and their fathers’ crime. On one hand, this is yet another
%		reminder that it takes generations before the God of Israel will take
%		such actions. On the other hand, it means that the Israelites must
%		recognize that it is not only their own offenses that have led to these
%		things. They must come to terms with their parents’ offenses as well.
%		The ultimate revelation of the divine at Sinai includes the fact that
%		the deity “reckons fathers’ crime on children and on children’s
%		children, on third generations and on fourth generations.” Now the
%		perspective is turned to those children, generations later; and we learn
%		from the Torah, no less than from Freud, that humans must look back not
%		only at the good that their parents and grandparents did but also at
%		their errors and faults. It is an essential part of understanding how we
%		came to be what we are.
%	}

verses.original: אַף אֲנִי אֵלֵךְ עִמָּם בְּקֶרִי וְהֵבֵאתִי אֹתָם בְּאֶרֶץ אֹיְבֵיהֶם אוֹ אָז יִכָּנַע לְבָבָם הֶעָרֵל וְאָז יִרְצוּ אֶת עֲוֺנָם׃
verses.english: so I, I also, would go on with them in defiance, and I brought them into their enemies’ land; or if then their uncircumcised heart will be humbled and then they will accept their crime,

tex.original: \hR{אַף אֲנִי אֵלֵךְ עִמָּם בְּקֶרִי וְהֵבֵאתִי אֹתָם בְּאֶרֶץ אֹיְבֵיהֶם אוֹ אָז יִכָּנַע לְבָבָם הֶעָרֵל וְאָז יִרְצוּ אֶת עֲוֺנָם׃}

verses.original: וְזָכַרְתִּי אֶת בְּרִיתִי יַעֲקוֹב וְאַף אֶת בְּרִיתִי יִצְחָק וְאַף אֶת בְּרִיתִי אַבְרָהָם אֶזְכֹּר וְהָאָרֶץ אֶזְכֹּר׃
verses.english: then I shall remember my covenant of Jacob, and I shall remember also my covenant of Isaac and also my covenant of Abraham, and I shall remember the land.

tex.original: \hR{וְזָכַרְתִּי אֶת בְּרִיתִי יַעֲקוֹב וְאַף אֶת בְּרִיתִי יִצְחָק וְאַף אֶת בְּרִיתִי אַבְרָהָם אֶזְכֹּר וְהָאָרֶץ אֶזְכֹּר׃}

verses.original: וְהָאָרֶץ תֵּעָזֵב מֵהֶם וְתִרֶץ אֶת שַׁבְּתֹתֶיהָ בּהְשַׁמָּה מֵהֶם וְהֵם יִרְצוּ אֶת עֲוֺנָם יַעַן וּבְיַעַן בְּמִשְׁפָּטַי מָאָסוּ וְאֶת חֻקֹּתַי גָּעֲלָה נַפְשָׁם׃
verses.english: And the land will be left from them, and it will accept its Sabbaths while it is devastated from them, and they will accept their crime, because and only because they rejected my judgments and their soul scorned my laws.

tex.original: \hR{וְהָאָרֶץ תֵּעָזֵב מֵהֶם וְתִרֶץ אֶת שַׁבְּתֹתֶיהָ בּהְשַׁמָּה מֵהֶם וְהֵם יִרְצוּ אֶת עֲוֺנָם יַעַן וּבְיַעַן בְּמִשְׁפָּטַי מָאָסוּ וְאֶת חֻקֹּתַי גָּעֲלָה נַפְשָׁם׃}

verses.original: וְאַף גַּם זֹאת בִּהְיוֹתָם בְּאֶרֶץ אֹיְבֵיהֶם לֹא מְאַסְתִּים וְלֹא גְעַלְתִּים לְכַלֹּתָם לְהָפֵר בְּרִיתִי אִתָּם כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: “And even despite this, when they were in their enemies’ land I did not reject them and did not scorn them, to finish them, to break my covenant with them, because I am YHWH, their God!

tex.original: \hR{וְאַף גַּם זֹאת בִּהְיוֹתָם בְּאֶרֶץ אֹיְבֵיהֶם לֹא מְאַסְתִּים וְלֹא גְעַלְתִּים לְכַלֹּתָם לְהָפֵר בְּרִיתִי אִתָּם כִּי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וְזָכַרְתִּי לָהֶם בְּרִית רִאשֹׁנִים אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי אֹתָם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם לְעֵינֵי הַגּוֹיִם לִהְיוֹת לָהֶם לֵאלֹהִים אֲנִי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: So I shall remember for them the covenant of the first ones, whom I brought out from the land of Egypt before the eyes of the nations to be God to them. I am YHWH.”

tex.original: \hR{וְזָכַרְתִּי לָהֶם בְּרִית רִאשֹׁנִים אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי אֹתָם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם לְעֵינֵי הַגּוֹיִם לִהְיוֹת לָהֶם לֵאלֹהִים אֲנִי יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: אֵלֶּה הַחֻקִּים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִים וְהַתּוֹרֹת אֲשֶׁר נָתַן יְהֹוָה בֵּינוֹ וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּהַר סִינַי בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה׃
verses.english: These are the laws and the judgments and the instructions that YHWH gave between Him and the children of Israel in Mount Sinai by Moses’ hand.

tex.original: \hP{אֵלֶּה הַחֻקִּים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִים וְהַתּוֹרֹת אֲשֶׁר נָתַן יְהֹוָה בֵּינוֹ וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּהַר סִינַי בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		These are the laws and the judgments and the instructions. The present
%		age plainly appears to value the ethical more than the ritual in
%		religion. Some even feel the need to justify ritual by attempting to
%		connect each ritual act to some ethical value: “We keep kosher to remind
%		us to care about animals; we wear fringes to remind us to be kind....”
%		This is misleading. Certainly ritual acts can have consequences in the
%		ethical realm, but that is not their reason for being. If we are to
%		understand Leviticus, we must have an appreciation of what ritual meant
%		in its society intrinsically. Ritual can have aesthetic, psychological,
%		and inspirational value. It has the potential of generating feelings of
%		closeness to the sacred as well as feelings of identity, stability, and
%		security. For some, it means, in a world of uncertainty, to be told what
%		the “right” things are, what acts one can perform to feel that one is
%		acting in accordance with nothing less than the will of the creator of
%		the universe. In the matter of purity, for example, one can believe
%		that, when one has had contact with any of a group of things that
%		intimidate us but that are physiological facts of life (blood and other
%		bodily fluids, bodily sores, death), one can do things that remove the
%		condition that this contact has produced—and thus remove the fear. In
%		the matter of sacrifice, as we have observed, the ritual has an impact
%		on one’s feeling of guilt. In the observance of the holidays, the ritual
%		contributes to feelings of festivity and communal celebration—and the
%		sanctification of time. And in the variety of elaborate ceremonies
%		performed at the Tent of Meeting, officiated by the specially garbed
%		priests, accompanied by the burning of incense, the ritual contributes
%		an aesthetic component to religion as well. All of this is
%		known—consciously or intuitively—to those who have found meaning and
%		even enjoyment in the practice of the rituals of their own religion. The
%		ritual and the ethical are two components of religion—and of
%		Leviticus—that do not justify each other, but rather unite and produce
%		mutual support. Indeed, it is instructive that Leviticus, a book that is
%		so fundamentally concerned with distinction, does not make any explicit
%		distinction between its ethical and its ritual laws. Sometimes they are
%		mixed together, but they are never identified as two distinct categories
%		of law. We do a disservice when we interpret ritual matters in terms of
%		ethical justifications. We move ourselves even farther from the
%		appreciation of ritual and the awe before the holy. Similarly, when we
%		say that the Hebrew word qdōš means a neutral kind of “separate” rather
%		than meaning “holy, sacred,” we further lose our feeling for holiness.
%		And perhaps we err similarly when we say that Hebrew t means “to miss
%		the mark” rather than “to sin,” to do something wrong that places us in
%		a state that needs to be remedied through atonement and/or sacrifice
%		and/or compensation.
%	}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ כִּי יַפְלִא נֶדֶר בְּעֶרְכְּךָ נְפָשֹׁת לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: “Speak to the children of Israel. And you shall say to them: When a man will express a vow by your appraisal of persons for YHWH,

tex.original: \hP{דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ כִּי יַפְלִא נֶדֶר בְּעֶרְכְּךָ נְפָשֹׁת לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וְעַד בֶּן שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ חֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃
verses.english: then your appraisal shall be: “A male from twenty years old up to sixty years old: then your appraisal shall be fifty shekels of silver by the shekel of the Holy.

tex.original: \hP{וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וְעַד בֶּן שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ חֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם נְקֵבָה הִוא וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁקֶל׃
verses.english: And if it is a female, then your appraisal shall be thirty shekels.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם נְקֵבָה הִוא וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁקֶל׃}

verses.original: וְאִם מִבֶּן חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְעַד בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר עֶשְׂרִים שְׁקָלִים וְלַנְּקֵבָה עֲשֶׂרֶת שְׁקָלִים׃
verses.english: And if one is from five years old up to twenty years old, then your appraisal for a male shall be twenty shekels and for a female ten shekels.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם מִבֶּן חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְעַד בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר עֶשְׂרִים שְׁקָלִים וְלַנְּקֵבָה עֲשֶׂרֶת שְׁקָלִים׃}

verses.original: וְאִם מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וְעַד בֶּן חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר חֲמִשָּׁה שְׁקָלִים כָּסֶף וְלַנְּקֵבָה עֶרְכְּךָ שְׁלֹשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים כָּסֶף׃
verses.english: And if one is from a month old up to five years old, then your appraisal for a male shall be five shekels of silver and your appraisal for a female three shekels.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וְעַד בֶּן חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר חֲמִשָּׁה שְׁקָלִים כָּסֶף וְלַנְּקֵבָה עֶרְכְּךָ שְׁלֹשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים כָּסֶף׃}

verses.original: וְאִם מִבֶּן שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה אִם זָכָר וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר שָׁקֶל וְלַנְּקֵבָה עֲשָׂרָה שְׁקָלִים׃
verses.english: And if one is from sixty years old and up, if a male then your appraisal shall be fifteen shekels, and for a female ten shekels.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם מִבֶּן שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה אִם זָכָר וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר שָׁקֶל וְלַנְּקֵבָה עֲשָׂרָה שְׁקָלִים׃}

verses.original: וְאִם מָךְ הוּא מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ וְהֶעֱמִידוֹ לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן וְהֶעֱרִיךְ אֹתוֹ הַכֹּהֵן עַל פִּי אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנֹּדֵר יַעֲרִיכֶנּוּ הַכֹּהֵן׃
verses.english: And if he is lower than your estimate, then one shall stand him in front of the priest, and the priest shall appraise him. The priest shall appraise him on the basis of what the hand of the one making the vow can attain.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם מָךְ הוּא מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ וְהֶעֱמִידוֹ לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן וְהֶעֱרִיךְ אֹתוֹ הַכֹּהֵן עַל פִּי אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנֹּדֵר יַעֲרִיכֶנּוּ הַכֹּהֵן׃}

verses.original: וְאִם בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ לַיהֹוָה יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verses.english: “And if it is an animal from which people would bring an offering to YHWH, everything that he will give of it to YHWH will be a holy thing.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ לַיהֹוָה יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ׃}

verses.original: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verses.english: And he shall not exchange it and shall not trade it, good for bad or bad for good; and if he does trade an animal for an animal, then both it and the one traded for it shall be a holy thing.

tex.original: \hP{לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם כּל בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱמִיד אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן׃
verses.english: And if it is any impure animal, from which people would not bring an offering to YHWH, then he shall stand the animal in front of the priest,

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם כּל בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱמִיד אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן׃}

verses.original: וְהֶעֱרִיךְ הַכֹּהֵן אֹתָהּ בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כְּעֶרְכְּךָ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יִהְיֶה׃
verses.english: and the priest shall appraise it. Whether good or bad: according to your appraisal by the priest, so it shall be.

tex.original: \hP{וְהֶעֱרִיךְ הַכֹּהֵן אֹתָהּ בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כְּעֶרְכְּךָ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יִהְיֶה׃}

verses.original: וְאִם גָּאֹל יִגְאָלֶנָּה וְיָסַף חֲמִישִׁתוֹ עַל עֶרְכֶּךָ׃
verses.english: And if he will redeem it, then he shall add a fifth of it to your appraisal.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם גָּאֹל יִגְאָלֶנָּה וְיָסַף חֲמִישִׁתוֹ עַל עֶרְכֶּךָ׃}

verses.original: וְאִישׁ כִּי יַקְדִּשׁ אֶת בֵּיתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱרִיכוֹ הַכֹּהֵן בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כַּאֲשֶׁר יַעֲרִיךְ אֹתוֹ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יָקוּם׃
verses.english: “And when a man will consecrate his house to be a holy thing to YHWH, then the priest shall appraise it. Whether good or bad: as the priest will appraise it, so it shall stand.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִישׁ כִּי יַקְדִּשׁ אֶת בֵּיתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱרִיכוֹ הַכֹּהֵן בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כַּאֲשֶׁר יַעֲרִיךְ אֹתוֹ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יָקוּם׃}

verses.original: וְאִם הַמַּקְדִּישׁ יִגְאַל אֶת בֵּיתוֹ וְיָסַף חֲמִישִׁית כֶּסֶף עֶרְכְּךָ עָלָיו וְהָיָה לוֹ׃
verses.english: And if the one who consecrates it will redeem his house, then he shall add a fifth of the money of your appraisal to it, and it shall be his.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם הַמַּקְדִּישׁ יִגְאַל אֶת בֵּיתוֹ וְיָסַף חֲמִישִׁית כֶּסֶף עֶרְכְּךָ עָלָיו וְהָיָה לוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ יַקְדִּישׁ אִישׁ לַיהֹוָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ לְפִי זַרְעוֹ זֶרַע חֹמֶר שְׂעֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף׃
verses.english: “And if a man will consecrate any of a field of his possession to YHWH, then your appraisal shall be on the basis of its seed: the seed of a homer of barley at fifty shekels of silver.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ יַקְדִּישׁ אִישׁ לַיהֹוָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ לְפִי זַרְעוֹ זֶרַע חֹמֶר שְׂעֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף׃}

verses.original: אִם מִשְּׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל יַקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ כְּעֶרְכְּךָ יָקוּם׃
verses.english: If he will consecrate his field from the jubilee year, it shall stand according to your appraisal;

tex.original: \hP{אִם מִשְּׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל יַקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ כְּעֶרְכְּךָ יָקוּם׃}

verses.original: וְאִם אַחַר הַיֹּבֵל יַקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ וְחִשַּׁב לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַכֶּסֶף עַל פִּי הַשָּׁנִים הַנּוֹתָרֹת עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְנִגְרַע מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ׃
verses.english: and if he will consecrate his field after the jubilee, then the priest shall figure the money for him on the basis of the years that are left until the jubilee year, and it shall be subtracted from your appraisal.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם אַחַר הַיֹּבֵל יַקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ וְחִשַּׁב לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַכֶּסֶף עַל פִּי הַשָּׁנִים הַנּוֹתָרֹת עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְנִגְרַע מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם גָּאֹל יִגְאַל אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֹתוֹ וְיָסַף חֲמִשִׁית כֶּסֶף עֶרְכְּךָ עָלָיו וְקָם לוֹ׃
verses.english: And if the one who consecrates it will redeem the field, then he shall add a fifth of the money of your appraisal to it, and it will stand as his.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם גָּאֹל יִגְאַל אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֹתוֹ וְיָסַף חֲמִשִׁית כֶּסֶף עֶרְכְּךָ עָלָיו וְקָם לוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם לֹא יִגְאַל אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה וְאִם מָכַר אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר לֹא יִגָּאֵל עוֹד׃
verses.english: And if he will not redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed anymore.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם לֹא יִגְאַל אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה וְאִם מָכַר אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר לֹא יִגָּאֵל עוֹד׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verses.english: And when it goes out in the jubilee, the field shall be a holy thing to YHWH, like a devoted field; his possession shall be the priest’s.

tex.original: \hP{וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם אֶת שְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ יַקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: “And if he will consecrate any of a field that he has bought, that is not from a field of his possession, to YHWH,

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם אֶת שְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ יַקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְחִשַּׁב לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֵת מִכְסַת הָעֶרְכְּךָ עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְנָתַן אֶת הָעֶרְכְּךָ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: then the priest shall figure for him the count of your appraisal up to the jubilee year, and he shall give your appraisal on that day, a holy thing to YHWH.

tex.original: \hP{וְחִשַּׁב לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן אֵת מִכְסַת הָעֶרְכְּךָ עַד שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל וְנָתַן אֶת הָעֶרְכְּךָ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל יָשׁוּב הַשָּׂדֶה לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ מֵאִתּוֹ לַאֲשֶׁר לוֹ אֲחֻזַּת הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.english: In the jubilee year the field shall go back to the one from whom it was bought, to the one to whom the possession of the land belongs.

tex.original: \hP{בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל יָשׁוּב הַשָּׂדֶה לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ מֵאִתּוֹ לַאֲשֶׁר לוֹ אֲחֻזַּת הָאָרֶץ׃}

verses.original: וְכל עֶרְכְּךָ יִהְיֶה בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה יִהְיֶה הַשָּׁקֶל׃
verses.english: And all of your appraisal shall be by the shekel of the Holy. (The shekel shall be twenty gerah.)

tex.original: \hP{וְכל עֶרְכְּךָ יִהְיֶה בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה יִהְיֶה הַשָּׁקֶל׃}

verses.original: אַךְ בְּכוֹר אֲשֶׁר יְבֻכַּר לַיהֹוָה בִּבְהֵמָה לֹא יַקְדִּישׁ אִישׁ אֹתוֹ אִם שׁוֹר אִם שֶׂה לַיהֹוָה הוּא׃
verses.english: “Except: a firstling of the animals—which as a firstling is committed to YHWH—no man shall consecrate it. Whether an ox or a sheep, it is YHWH’s.

tex.original: \hP{אַךְ בְּכוֹר אֲשֶׁר יְבֻכַּר לַיהֹוָה בִּבְהֵמָה לֹא יַקְדִּישׁ אִישׁ אֹתוֹ אִם שׁוֹר אִם שֶׂה לַיהֹוָה הוּא׃}

verses.original: וְאִם בַּבְּהֵמָה הַטְּמֵאָה וּפָדָה בְעֶרְכֶּךָ וְיָסַף חֲמִשִׁתוֹ עָלָיו וְאִם לֹא יִגָּאֵל וְנִמְכַּר בְּעֶרְכֶּךָ׃
verses.english: And if it is of the impure animals, then he shall redeem it at your appraisal, and he shall add to it a fifth of it. And if it will not be redeemed then it shall be sold at your appraisal.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם בַּבְּהֵמָה הַטְּמֵאָה וּפָדָה בְעֶרְכֶּךָ וְיָסַף חֲמִשִׁתוֹ עָלָיו וְאִם לֹא יִגָּאֵל וְנִמְכַּר בְּעֶרְכֶּךָ׃}

verses.original: אַךְ כּל חֵרֶם אֲשֶׁר יַחֲרִם אִישׁ לַיהֹוָה מִכּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ מֵאָדָם וּבְהֵמָה וּמִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ לֹא יִמָּכֵר וְלֹא יִגָּאֵל כּל חֵרֶם קֹדֶשׁ קדָשִׁים הוּא לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: “Except: any devoted thing that a man will devote to YHWH from anything that he has—from human or animal or from a field of his possession—shall not be sold and shall not be redeemed. Any devoted thing: it is a holy of holies to YHWH.

tex.original: \hP{אַךְ כּל חֵרֶם אֲשֶׁר יַחֲרִם אִישׁ לַיהֹוָה מִכּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ מֵאָדָם וּבְהֵמָה וּמִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ לֹא יִמָּכֵר וְלֹא יִגָּאֵל כּל חֵרֶם קֹדֶשׁ קדָשִׁים הוּא לַיהֹוָה׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		“Except: any devoted thing that a man will devote to YHWH
		from anything that he has—from human or animal or from a
		field of his possession—shall not be sold and shall not be
		redeemed. Any devoted thing: it is a holy of holies to
		YHWH.
	}

verses.original: כּל חֵרֶם אֲשֶׁר יחֳרַם מִן הָאָדָם לֹא יִפָּדֶה מוֹת יוּמָת׃
verses.english: Anyone who will be devoted from humans shall not be redeemed. He shall be put to death.

tex.original: \hP{כּל חֵרֶם אֲשֶׁר יחֳרַם מִן הָאָדָם לֹא יִפָּדֶה מוֹת יוּמָת׃}

verses.original: וְכל מַעְשַׂר הָאָרֶץ מִזֶּרַע הָאָרֶץ מִפְּרִי הָעֵץ לַיהֹוָה הוּא קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: “And all the tithe of the land, from the land’s seed, from the tree’s fruit: it is YHWH’s, a holy thing to YHWH.

tex.original: \hP{וְכל מַעְשַׂר הָאָרֶץ מִזֶּרַע הָאָרֶץ מִפְּרִי הָעֵץ לַיהֹוָה הוּא קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְאִם גָּאֹל יִגְאַל אִישׁ מִמַּעַשְׂרוֹ חֲמִשִׁיתוֹ יֹסֵף עָלָיו׃
verses.english: And if a man will redeem some of his tithe, he shall add to it a fifth of it.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם גָּאֹל יִגְאַל אִישׁ מִמַּעַשְׂרוֹ חֲמִשִׁיתוֹ יֹסֵף עָלָיו׃}

verses.original: וְכל מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: And all the tithe of a herd or a flock, everything that passes under the rod: the tenth shall be a holy thing to YHWH.

tex.original: \hP{וְכל מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ וְאִם הָמֵר יְמִירֶנּוּ וְהָיָה הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל׃
verses.english: He shall not inspect it either for good or for bad. And he shall not trade it. And if he will trade it, then both it and the one traded for it shall be a holy thing. It shall not be redeemed.”

tex.original: \hP{לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ וְאִם הָמֵר יְמִירֶנּוּ וְהָיָה הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל׃}

verses.original: אֵלֶּה הַמִּצְוֺת אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶת מֹשֶׁה אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּהַר סִינָי׃
verses.english: These are the commandments that YHWH commanded Moses for the children of Israel in Mount Sinai.

tex.original: \hP{אֵלֶּה הַמִּצְוֺת אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶת מֹשֶׁה אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּהַר סִינָי׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		These are the commandments that YHWH commanded Moses for the children of
%		Israel in Mount Sinai. Literary studies of Leviticus are likely to begin
%		by raising the question of whether this book that contains so much law
%		and so little narrative belongs in a literary study at all. But at
%		bottom we do not have to argue that Leviticus is great literature in
%		order to justify its inclusion in a literary analysis. It is not
%		literature, not in the way in which almost anyone ever means that term.
%		But the literary study of the Hebrew Bible has to come to terms with
%		Leviticus, for it is embedded in the biblical narrative. Indeed, the
%		fact that no law code from ancient Israel survived independently, that
%		law codes survived only in contexts of narrative, is notable in itself.
%		Leviticus’s laws are integral—and assumed thereafter. The book begins
%		with the notation that YHWH speaks these things to Moses from the
%		Tabernacle (1:1), and it ends here with the reminder that “These are the
%		commandments that YHWH commanded Moses for the children of Israel at
%		Mount Sinai.” Some of the laws presume the preceding narrative, e.g.,
%		“You shall not do like what is done in the land of Egypt, in which you
%		lived …” (18:3), which presumes the bondage in Egypt. Legal authority is
%		vested in the priests (the power to teach and enforce, 10:10–11), which
%		is an essential element in narratives in subsequent books. As new
%		political figures, especially kings, will rise, the compatibility or
%		conflict between them and the priests will be critical to the narrative,
%		as it was critical in history. Leviticus thus is a design for an
%		organized society of people who help one another, who do not
%		intentionally injure one another, who respect one another’s property and
%		relationships, who regularly assemble to celebrate together, who
%		acknowledge their errors and atone for them, who regard life—in humans
%		and in animals—as sacred, who pursue purity in various forms, who
%		respect law, and who are utterly loyal to one God. It is against the
%		background of this design that the book of Numbers must be understood.
%		COMMENTARY ON THE TORAH
%		The book of Numbers is the story of a journey.
%		Against the backdrop of the book of Leviticus, with its absence of
%		movement, Numbers is entirely about movement. The journey as a literary
%		theme has been a recurring component of world literature from the epic
%		of Gilgamesh, the oldest known book, and the Odyssey to Alice’s
%		Adventures in Wonderland and The Wonderful Wizard of Oz. It reflects
%		real experience, it is a ready metaphor for human lives, and it is a
%		connector between the world of literature and the world of dreams, in
%		which experiences of journeys are common. The journey in literature can
%		be the experience of an individual or a group. In the book of Numbers it
%		is both. It is the people of Israel’s journey from Sinai to the border
%		of Canaan, from the site of the establishment of the covenant to the
%		place where it is to be fulfilled. And it is Moses’ journey from Mount
%		Sinai to Mount Abarim, from the place where he has seen God to the place
%		of his death. One must read the story in Numbers with a sense of what is
%		pictured: a great mass of people (603,550 adult males, plus the junior
%		and elderly males and the females of all ages), an entire nation, in
%		movement—with a visible miracle (the column of cloud and fire) and
%		miraculous feeding (manna) happening in their presence at all times over
%		a span of nearly forty years. It is the only age in the Bible in which
%		miracle is a daily fact of life. There is an organization for travel, a
%		hierarchy for community life (Moses, judges, priests), and formal
%		rituals of time (Sabbath, holidays, and new moons) and of space
%		(sacrifice, incense, vestments, the Tabernacle, fringes on clothing).

YHWH says Aaron Aaron (אַהֲרֹן) — meaning uncertain; perhaps Egyptian or otherwise non-Hebrew. Traditionally connected with “high/exalted”; folk etymologies include “mountain of strength.” A speculative Egyptian reading connects it with ꜥꜣ rn, “great is the name,” essentially “Big Name” / “Name's Huge.” It has also been suggested to mean “light-bringer”, a name traditionally associated with Lucifer, the latter of which is Latin for “light-bringer.” In Christian theology, Lucifer is associated with the sin of pride, and believed to have attempted a usurpation of God. In certain Historical Nameless Sects, Lucifer is explicitly identified with Aaron and the Aaronid priesthood, as well as the later Zadokite priesthood and its subsequent development into the Sadducees. He's a shiny bastard. From the gold. Don't look directly at him. Looks like a goddamn flashlight, the fruity bitch.” should count alongside Drew.

verses.english: and the Levites shall camp all around the Tabernacle of the Testimony, so there will not be a rage on the congregation of the children of Israel, and the Levites shall keep the charge of the Tabernacle of the Testimony.”
verses.commentary:
Ok, this line is a bit weird, so let's check the Hebrew and some other English translations to make sure we understand what's going on here.

The first part is pretty clear:

The Levites camp all around the Tabernacle.

Why?

Good question.

Here are some ways people have translated the reason.

• so that my wrath will not fall on the Israelite community
• to protect the community of Israel from the LORD’s anger
• so that no one may come near and cause my anger to strike the community of Israel
• so there shall be no sin among the children of Israel

The word קצף (qetseph) denotes a burst of wrath, anger, or displeasure. In the bible, it may describe the righteous indignation of YHWH, the impulsive rage of political rulers, or the communal fury of a nation. It can also connote foam, froth, boiling, breaking, or snapping.

In summary:

The Levites form a sort of protective ring around the Tabernacle, to prevent YHWH from breaking out and murdering all the Israel people who aren't Levites.

There's something fishy going on with the Levites.

	\item so that my wrath will not fall on the Israelite community % -NIV
	\item to protect the community of Israel from the LORD’s anger % -NLT
	\item so that no one may come near and cause my anger to strike the community of Israel % -Good News Translation
	\item so there shall be no sin among the children of Israel % -Brenton Septuagint Translation
	\end{enumerate}

	\aC{

%	\footnote{
%		six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty. Add to this the underage
%		and elderly men, the women of all ages, and the Levites, and the total
%		number of Israelites must approach two million. It has been calculated
%		that by these numbers, marching eight across, when the first Israelites
%		reach Mount Sinai, half of them would still be in Egypt! The
%		extraordinary size of this population is a famous old problem in
%		traditional and critical biblical scholarship. The numbers appear far
%		too high; but they do not appear to be entirely invented either, because
%		what would be the motive for contriving them in all of this
%		tribe-by-tribe detail for the first four chapters of Numbers? Some
%		suggest that the word for “thousand” here means rather a “clan,” but
%		that is not correct (see the comment on Num 3:43). One possibility is
%		that these are the numbers from the census that is attributed to King
%		David (2 Samuel 24; see the comment on Exod 30:12). (There are just
%		three censuses in the Tanak, the two censuses of Moses and the census of
%		David.) Coming centuries later, in a period in which Israel is settled
%		in the land, the numbers are more understandable in the Davidic era
%		(though they are questionably high even for that period). In this
%		scenario, the records here would have come from old documents among the

verses.original: וַיִּפְקֹד אֹתָם מֹשֶׁה עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה כַּאֲשֶׁר צֻוָּה׃
verses.english: And Moses counted them by YHWH’s word as he was commanded.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּפְקֹד אֹתָם מֹשֶׁה עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה כַּאֲשֶׁר צֻוָּה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּהְיוּ אֵלֶּה בְנֵי לֵוִי בִּשְׁמֹתָם גֵּרְשׁוֹן וּקְהָת וּמְרָרִי׃
verses.english: And these were Levi’s sons by their names: Gershon and Kohath and Merari.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּהְיוּ אֵלֶּה בְנֵי לֵוִי בִּשְׁמֹתָם גֵּרְשׁוֹן וּקְהָת וּמְרָרִי׃}

verses.original: וְאֵלֶּה שְׁמוֹת בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם לִבְנִי וְשִׁמְעִי׃
verses.english: And these are the names of Gershon’s sons by their families: Libni and Shimei.

tex.original: \hP{וְאֵלֶּה שְׁמוֹת בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם לִבְנִי וְשִׁמְעִי׃}

verses.original: וּבְנֵי קְהָת לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם עַמְרָם וְיִצְהָר חֶבְרוֹן וְעֻזִּיאֵל׃
verses.english: And Kohath’s sons by their families: Amram and Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.

tex.original: \hP{וּבְנֵי קְהָת לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם עַמְרָם וְיִצְהָר חֶבְרוֹן וְעֻזִּיאֵל׃}

verses.original: וּבְנֵי מְרָרִי לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם מַחְלִי וּמוּשִׁי אֵלֶּה הֵם מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַלֵּוִי לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם׃
verses.english: And Merari’s sons by their families: Mahli and Mushi. These are the Levite families by their fathers’ house.

tex.original: \hP{וּבְנֵי מְרָרִי לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם מַחְלִי וּמוּשִׁי אֵלֶּה הֵם מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַלֵּוִי לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם׃}

verses.original: לְגֵרְשׁוֹן מִשְׁפַּחַת הַלִּבְנִי וּמִשְׁפַּחַת הַשִּׁמְעִי אֵלֶּה הֵם מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּי׃
verses.english: Gershon had the Libnite family and the Shimeite family. These are the Gershonite families.

tex.original: \hP{לְגֵרְשׁוֹן מִשְׁפַּחַת הַלִּבְנִי וּמִשְׁפַּחַת הַשִּׁמְעִי אֵלֶּה הֵם מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּי׃}

verses.original: פְּקֻדֵיהֶם בְּמִסְפַּר כּל זָכָר מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וָמָעְלָה פְּקֻדֵיהֶם שִׁבְעַת אֲלָפִים וַחֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת׃
verses.english: Their counts by the number of every male from a month old and up: their counts were seven thousand five hundred.

tex.original: \hP{פְּקֻדֵיהֶם בְּמִסְפַּר כּל זָכָר מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וָמָעְלָה פְּקֻדֵיהֶם שִׁבְעַת אֲלָפִים וַחֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת׃}

verses.original: מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּי אַחֲרֵי הַמִּשְׁכָּן יַחֲנוּ יָמָּה׃
verses.english: The Gershonite families were to camp behind the Tabernacle, to the west.

tex.original: \hP{מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּי אַחֲרֵי הַמִּשְׁכָּן יַחֲנוּ יָמָּה׃}

verses.original: וּנְשִׂיא בֵית אָב לַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּי אֶלְיָסָף בֶּן לָאֵל׃
verses.english: And the chieftain of the Gershonite father’s house was Eliasaph son of Lael.

tex.original: \hP{וּנְשִׂיא בֵית אָב לַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּי אֶלְיָסָף בֶּן לָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וּמִשְׁמֶרֶת בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְהָאֹהֶל מִכְסֵהוּ וּמָסַךְ פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
