verses.english: And the charge of the sons of Gershon in the Tent of Meeting was the Tabernacle and the tent, its covering and the cover of the entrance of the Tent of Meeting

tex.original: \hP{וּמִשְׁמֶרֶת בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְהָאֹהֶל מִכְסֵהוּ וּמָסַךְ פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וְקַלְעֵי הֶחָצֵר וְאֶת מָסַךְ פֶּתַח הֶחָצֵר אֲשֶׁר עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ סָבִיב וְאֵת מֵיתָרָיו לְכֹל עֲבֹדָתוֹ׃
verses.english: and the courtyard’s hangings and the cover for the entrance of the courtyard that is all around the Tabernacle and the altar, and its cords, for all of its service.

tex.original: \hP{וְקַלְעֵי הֶחָצֵר וְאֶת מָסַךְ פֶּתַח הֶחָצֵר אֲשֶׁר עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ סָבִיב וְאֵת מֵיתָרָיו לְכֹל עֲבֹדָתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְלִקְהָת מִשְׁפַּחַת הַעַמְרָמִי וּמִשְׁפַּחַת הַיִּצְהָרִי וּמִשְׁפַּחַת הַחֶבְרֹנִי וּמִשְׁפַּחַת הָעזִּיאֵלִי אֵלֶּה הֵם מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַקְּהָתִי׃
verses.english: And Kohath had the Amramite family and the Izharite family and the Hebronite family and the Uzzielite family. These are the Kohathite families.

tex.original: \hP{וְלִקְהָת מִשְׁפַּחַת הַעַמְרָמִי וּמִשְׁפַּחַת הַיִּצְהָרִי וּמִשְׁפַּחַת הַחֶבְרֹנִי וּמִשְׁפַּחַת הָעזִּיאֵלִי אֵלֶּה הֵם מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַקְּהָתִי׃}

verses.original: בְּמִסְפַּר כּל זָכָר מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וָמָעְלָה שְׁמֹנַת אֲלָפִים וְשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שֹׁמְרֵי מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃
verses.english: By the number of every male from a month old and up: eight thousand six hundred keeping the charge of the Holy.

tex.original: \hP{בְּמִסְפַּר כּל זָכָר מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וָמָעְלָה שְׁמֹנַת אֲלָפִים וְשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת שֹׁמְרֵי מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃}

verses.original: מִשְׁפְּחֹת בְּנֵי קְהָת יַחֲנוּ עַל יֶרֶךְ הַמִּשְׁכָּן תֵּימָנָה׃
verses.english: The families of the children of Kohath were to camp to the south.

tex.original: \hP{מִשְׁפְּחֹת בְּנֵי קְהָת יַחֲנוּ עַל יֶרֶךְ הַמִּשְׁכָּן תֵּימָנָה׃}

verses.original: וּנְשִׂיא בֵית אָב לְמִשְׁפְּחֹת הַקְּהָתִי אֱלִיצָפָן בֶּן עֻזִּיאֵל׃
verses.english: And the chieftain of the father’s house for the Kohathite families was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.

tex.original: \hP{וּנְשִׂיא בֵית אָב לְמִשְׁפְּחֹת הַקְּהָתִי אֱלִיצָפָן בֶּן עֻזִּיאֵל׃}

verses.original: וּמִשְׁמַרְתָּם הָאָרֹן וְהַשֻּׁלְחָן וְהַמְּנֹרָה וְהַמִּזְבְּחֹת וּכְלֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר יְשָׁרְתוּ בָּהֶם וְהַמָּסָךְ וְכֹל עֲבֹדָתוֹ׃
verses.english: And their charge was the ark and the table and the menorah and the altars and the equipment of the Holy with which they minister and the cover and all of its service.

tex.original: \hP{וּמִשְׁמַרְתָּם הָאָרֹן וְהַשֻּׁלְחָן וְהַמְּנֹרָה וְהַמִּזְבְּחֹת וּכְלֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר יְשָׁרְתוּ בָּהֶם וְהַמָּסָךְ וְכֹל עֲבֹדָתוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		menorah. The lampstand has been compared in appearance—and as a
%		symbol—to a tree, and especially to the tree of life. It is therefore
%		notable that it is mentioned here as being the responsibility of the
%		Kohathites. And then just a few verses later the Kohathites are
%		identified as the Levite group who must be careful that their closeness
%		to the holy not cause them to die (see the comment on 4:15). The
%		menorah, the sacred object, which became a symbol of Israel (more
%		properly so than the six-pointed star that became a symbol some two
%		thousand years after this text), is also a reminder of the essential
%		human relationship to life and death that begins the Torah.
%	}

verses.original: וּנְשִׂיא נְשִׂיאֵי הַלֵּוִי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן פְּקֻדַּת שֹׁמְרֵי מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃
verses.english: And the chieftain of chieftains of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest, with responsibility for those who keep the charge of the Holy.

tex.original: \hP{וּנְשִׂיא נְשִׂיאֵי הַלֵּוִי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן פְּקֻדַּת שֹׁמְרֵי מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃}

verses.original: לִמְרָרִי מִשְׁפַּחַת הַמַּחְלִי וּמִשְׁפַּחַת הַמּוּשִׁי אֵלֶּה הֵם מִשְׁפְּחֹת מְרָרִי׃
verses.english: And Merari had the Mahlite family and the Mushite family. These are the Merarite families.

tex.original: \hP{לִמְרָרִי מִשְׁפַּחַת הַמַּחְלִי וּמִשְׁפַּחַת הַמּוּשִׁי אֵלֶּה הֵם מִשְׁפְּחֹת מְרָרִי׃}

verses.original: וּפְקֻדֵיהֶם בְּמִסְפַּר כּל זָכָר מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וָמָעְלָה שֵׁשֶׁת אֲלָפִים וּמָאתָיִם׃
verses.english: And their counts by the number of every male from a month old and up: six thousand two hundred.

tex.original: \hP{וּפְקֻדֵיהֶם בְּמִסְפַּר כּל זָכָר מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וָמָעְלָה שֵׁשֶׁת אֲלָפִים וּמָאתָיִם׃}

verses.original: וּנְשִׂיא בֵית אָב לְמִשְׁפְּחֹת מְרָרִי צוּרִיאֵל בֶּן אֲבִיחָיִל עַל יֶרֶךְ הַמִּשְׁכָּן יַחֲנוּ צָפֹנָה׃
verses.english: And the chieftain of the father’s house for the Merarite families was Zuriel son of Abihail. They were to camp on the side of the Tabernacle to the north.

tex.original: \hP{וּנְשִׂיא בֵית אָב לְמִשְׁפְּחֹת מְרָרִי צוּרִיאֵל בֶּן אֲבִיחָיִל עַל יֶרֶךְ הַמִּשְׁכָּן יַחֲנוּ צָפֹנָה׃}

verses.original: וּפְקֻדַּת מִשְׁמֶרֶת בְּנֵי מְרָרִי קַרְשֵׁי הַמִּשְׁכָּן וּבְרִיחָיו וְעַמֻּדָיו וַאֲדָנָיו וְכל כֵּלָיו וְכֹל עֲבֹדָתוֹ׃
verses.english: And the responsibility of the charge of the children of Merari was the Tabernacle’s frames and its bars and its columns and its bases and all of its equipment and all of its service

tex.original: \hP{וּפְקֻדַּת מִשְׁמֶרֶת בְּנֵי מְרָרִי קַרְשֵׁי הַמִּשְׁכָּן וּבְרִיחָיו וְעַמֻּדָיו וַאֲדָנָיו וְכל כֵּלָיו וְכֹל עֲבֹדָתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְעַמֻּדֵי הֶחָצֵר סָבִיב וְאַדְנֵיהֶם וִיתֵדֹתָם וּמֵיתְרֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: and the courtyard’s columns all around and their bases and their pegs and their cords.

tex.original: \hP{וְעַמֻּדֵי הֶחָצֵר סָבִיב וְאַדְנֵיהֶם וִיתֵדֹתָם וּמֵיתְרֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וְהַחֹנִים לִפְנֵי הַמִּשְׁכָּן קֵדְמָה לִפְנֵי אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד מִזְרָחָה מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו שֹׁמְרִים מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַזָּר הַקָּרֵב יוּמָת׃
verses.english: And those who camped in front of the Tabernacle, on the east, in front of the Tent of Meeting, to the east, were Moses and Aaron and his sons, keeping the charge of the holy place, for the charge of the children of Israel. And the outsider who will come close shall be put to death.

tex.original: \hP{וְהַחֹנִים לִפְנֵי הַמִּשְׁכָּן קֵדְמָה לִפְנֵי אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד מִזְרָחָה מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו שֹׁמְרִים מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַזָּר הַקָּרֵב יוּמָת׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And those who camped in front of the Tabernacle, on the
		east, in front of the Tent of Meeting, to the east, were
		Moses and Aaron and his sons, keeping the charge of the
		holy place, for the charge of the children of Israel. And
		the outsider who will come close shall be put to death.
	}

verses.original: כּל פְּקוּדֵי הַלְוִיִּם אֲשֶׁר פָּקַד מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם כּל זָכָר מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וָמַעְלָה שְׁנַיִם וְעֶשְׂרִים אָלֶף׃
verses.english: All the counts of the Levites that Moses and Aaron made by YHWH’s word, by their families, every male from a month old and up were twenty-two thousand.

tex.original: \hP{כּל פְּקוּדֵי הַלְוִיִּם אֲשֶׁר פָּקַד מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם כּל זָכָר מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וָמַעְלָה שְׁנַיִם וְעֶשְׂרִים אָלֶף׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה פְּקֹד כּל בְּכֹר זָכָר לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וָמָעְלָה וְשָׂא אֵת מִסְפַּר שְׁמֹתָם׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “Count every male firstborn of the children of Israel from a month old and up, and add up the number of their names.

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה פְּקֹד כּל בְּכֹר זָכָר לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וָמָעְלָה וְשָׂא אֵת מִסְפַּר שְׁמֹתָם׃}

verses.original: וְלָקַחְתָּ אֶת הַלְוִיִּם לִי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה תַּחַת כּל בְּכֹר בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵת בֶּהֱמַת הַלְוִיִּם תַּחַת כּל בְּכוֹר בְּבֶהֱמַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And you shall take the Levites for me—I am YHWH—in place of every firstborn in the children of Israel, and the Levites’ animals in place of every firstborn in the animals of the children of Israel.”

tex.original: \hP{וְלָקַחְתָּ אֶת הַלְוִיִּם לִי אֲנִי יְהֹוָה תַּחַת כּל בְּכֹר בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֵת בֶּהֱמַת הַלְוִיִּם תַּחַת כּל בְּכוֹר בְּבֶהֱמַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיִּפְקֹד מֹשֶׁה כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֹתוֹ אֶת כּל בְּכוֹר בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And Moses counted, as YHWH commanded him, every firstborn in the children of Israel.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּפְקֹד מֹשֶׁה כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֹתוֹ אֶת כּל בְּכוֹר בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי כל בְּכוֹר זָכָר בְּמִסְפַּר שֵׁמֹת מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וָמַעְלָה לִפְקֻדֵיהֶם שְׁנַיִם וְעֶשְׂרִים אֶלֶף שְׁלֹשָׁה וְשִׁבְעִים וּמָאתָיִם׃
verses.english: And every male firstborn, by the number of names, from a month old and up, by their counts were twenty-two thousand two hundred seventy-three.

tex.original: \hP{וַיְהִי כל בְּכוֹר זָכָר בְּמִסְפַּר שֵׁמֹת מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ וָמַעְלָה לִפְקֻדֵיהֶם שְׁנַיִם וְעֶשְׂרִים אֶלֶף שְׁלֹשָׁה וְשִׁבְעִים וּמָאתָיִם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		twenty-two thousand. The number of firstborn Israelite males is given
%		here as 22,273. This indicates that those who take the word for
%		“thousand” (Hebrew ’elep) to mean “clan” are mistaken, since firstborn
%		sons as a group do not constitute clans. Those who try to understand
%		this term as “clan” do this because they are troubled by the high
%		numbers of Israelites in the census in Numbers. But we cannot escape the
%		problem by redefining a term. Whatever we believe to have been the
%		historical case, the fact is that the text depicts a vast population in
%		the wilderness. And my concern is not to debate the numbers but rather
%		to recognize the significance of the numbers to the Torah and to its
%		story. Historically, only a portion of the Israelites may have had the
%		experience of slavery in Egypt, but all of Israel came to see the
%		experience as their own. For the Torah, it is important that the entire
%		people of Israel be seen as present at Mount Sinai. The complication of
%		this number of 22,273 firstborn males of all ages is that it is utterly
%		out of proportion to the number of over 600,000 adult males. I have seen
%		no satisfactory solution to this problem.
%	}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: קַח אֶת הַלְוִיִּם תַּחַת כּל בְּכוֹר בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֶת בֶּהֱמַת הַלְוִיִּם תַּחַת בְּהֶמְתָּם וְהָיוּ לִי הַלְוִיִּם אֲנִי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: “Take the Levites in place of every firstborn in the children of Israel, and the Levites’ animals in place of their animals, and the Levites shall be mine. I am YHWH.

tex.original: \hP{קַח אֶת הַלְוִיִּם תַּחַת כּל בְּכוֹר בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֶת בֶּהֱמַת הַלְוִיִּם תַּחַת בְּהֶמְתָּם וְהָיוּ לִי הַלְוִיִּם אֲנִי יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְאֵת פְּדוּיֵי הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה וְהַשִּׁבְעִים וְהַמָּאתָיִם הָעֹדְפִים עַל הַלְוִיִּם מִבְּכוֹר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And for the redemption of the two hundred seventy-three who are left over above the Levites from the firstborn of the children of Israel,

tex.original: \hP{וְאֵת פְּדוּיֵי הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה וְהַשִּׁבְעִים וְהַמָּאתָיִם הָעֹדְפִים עַל הַלְוִיִּם מִבְּכוֹר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וְלָקַחְתָּ חֲמֵשֶׁת חֲמֵשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים לַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ תִּקָּח עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה הַשָּׁקֶל׃
verses.english: you shall take five shekels each per head; you shall take it by the shekel of the Holy. (The shekel is twenty gerah.)

tex.original: \hP{וְלָקַחְתָּ חֲמֵשֶׁת חֲמֵשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים לַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ תִּקָּח עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה הַשָּׁקֶל׃}

verses.original: וְנָתַתָּה הַכֶּסֶף לְאַהֲרֹן וּלְבָנָיו פְּדוּיֵי הָעֹדְפִים בָּהֶם׃
verses.english: And you shall give the money to Aaron and to his sons for the redemption of those left over among them.”

tex.original: \hP{וְנָתַתָּה הַכֶּסֶף לְאַהֲרֹן וּלְבָנָיו פְּדוּיֵי הָעֹדְפִים בָּהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֵת כֶּסֶף הַפִּדְיוֹם מֵאֵת הָעֹדְפִים עַל פְּדוּיֵי הַלְוִיִּם׃
verses.english: And Moses took the money of the redemption from those left over above those who were redeemed by the Levites.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֵת כֶּסֶף הַפִּדְיוֹם מֵאֵת הָעֹדְפִים עַל פְּדוּיֵי הַלְוִיִּם׃}

verses.original: מֵאֵת בְּכוֹר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לָקַח אֶת הַכָּסֶף חֲמִשָּׁה וְשִׁשִּׁים וּשְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת וָאֶלֶף בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃
verses.english: He took the money from the firstborn of the children of Israel: one thousand three hundred sixty-five by the shekel of the Holy.

tex.original: \hP{מֵאֵת בְּכוֹר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לָקַח אֶת הַכָּסֶף חֲמִשָּׁה וְשִׁשִּׁים וּשְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת וָאֶלֶף בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּתֵּן מֹשֶׁה אֶת כֶּסֶף הַפְּדֻיִם לְאַהֲרֹן וּלְבָנָיו עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶת מֹשֶׁה׃
verses.english: And Moses gave the money for those who were redeemed to Aaron and to his sons by YHWH’s word, as YHWH commanded Moses.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּתֵּן מֹשֶׁה אֶת כֶּסֶף הַפְּדֻיִם לְאַהֲרֹן וּלְבָנָיו עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶת מֹשֶׁה׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן לֵאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן לֵאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,}

verses.original: נָשֹׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ בְּנֵי קְהָת מִתּוֹךְ בְּנֵי לֵוִי לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם׃
verses.english: “Add up the heads of the children of Kohath from among the children of Levi by their families, by their fathers’ house,

tex.original: \hP{נָשֹׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ בְּנֵי קְהָת מִתּוֹךְ בְּנֵי לֵוִי לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם׃}

verses.original: מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה וְעַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה כּל בָּא לַצָּבָא לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: from thirty years old and up to fifty years old, everyone who would come to the army to do work in the Tent of Meeting.

tex.original: \hP{מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה וְעַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה כּל בָּא לַצָּבָא לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: זֹאת עֲבֹדַת בְּנֵי קְהָת בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים׃
verses.english: This is the work of the sons of Kohath in the Tent of Meeting: the Holy of Holies.

tex.original: \hP{זֹאת עֲבֹדַת בְּנֵי קְהָת בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים׃}

verses.original: וּבָא אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו בִּנְסֹעַ הַמַּחֲנֶה וְהוֹרִדוּ אֵת פָּרֹכֶת הַמָּסָךְ וְכִסּוּ בָהּ אֵת אֲרֹן הָעֵדֻת׃
verses.english: “And Aaron and his sons shall come when the camp is to travel, and they shall take down the covering pavilion and cover the ark of the testimony with it.

tex.original: \hP{וּבָא אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו בִּנְסֹעַ הַמַּחֲנֶה וְהוֹרִדוּ אֵת פָּרֹכֶת הַמָּסָךְ וְכִסּוּ בָהּ אֵת אֲרֹן הָעֵדֻת׃}

verses.original: וְנָתְנוּ עָלָיו כְּסוּי עוֹר תַּחַשׁ וּפָרְשׂוּ בֶגֶד כְּלִיל תְּכֵלֶת מִלְמָעְלָה וְשָׂמוּ בַּדָּיו׃
verses.english: And they shall put a cover of leather and shall spread a fabric all of blue above it and put in its poles.

tex.original: \hP{וְנָתְנוּ עָלָיו כְּסוּי עוֹר תַּחַשׁ וּפָרְשׂוּ בֶגֶד כְּלִיל תְּכֵלֶת מִלְמָעְלָה וְשָׂמוּ בַּדָּיו׃}

verses.original: וְעַל שֻׁלְחַן הַפָּנִים יִפְרְשׂוּ בֶּגֶד תְּכֵלֶת וְנָתְנוּ עָלָיו אֶת הַקְּעָרֹת וְאֶת הַכַּפֹּת וְאֶת הַמְּנַקִּיֹּת וְאֵת קְשׂוֹת הַנָּסֶךְ וְלֶחֶם הַתָּמִיד עָלָיו יִהְיֶה׃
verses.english: And on the table of show bread they shall spread a blue fabric, and they shall put on it the dishes and the pans and the bowls and the libation jars; and the continual bread shall be on it.

tex.original: \hP{וְעַל שֻׁלְחַן הַפָּנִים יִפְרְשׂוּ בֶּגֶד תְּכֵלֶת וְנָתְנוּ עָלָיו אֶת הַקְּעָרֹת וְאֶת הַכַּפֹּת וְאֶת הַמְּנַקִּיֹּת וְאֵת קְשׂוֹת הַנָּסֶךְ וְלֶחֶם הַתָּמִיד עָלָיו יִהְיֶה׃}

verses.original: וּפָרְשׂוּ עֲלֵיהֶם בֶּגֶד תּוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי וְכִסּוּ אֹתוֹ בְּמִכְסֵה עוֹר תָּחַשׁ וְשָׂמוּ אֶת בַּדָּיו׃
verses.english: And they shall spread a scarlet fabric over them and cover it with a leather covering and set its poles.

tex.original: \hP{וּפָרְשׂוּ עֲלֵיהֶם בֶּגֶד תּוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי וְכִסּוּ אֹתוֹ בְּמִכְסֵה עוֹר תָּחַשׁ וְשָׂמוּ אֶת בַּדָּיו׃}

verses.original: וְלָקְחוּ בֶּגֶד תְּכֵלֶת וְכִסּוּ אֶת מְנֹרַת הַמָּאוֹר וְאֶת נֵרֹתֶיהָ וְאֶת מַלְקָחֶיהָ וְאֶת מַחְתֹּתֶיהָ וְאֵת כּל כְּלֵי שַׁמְנָהּ אֲשֶׁר יְשָׁרְתוּ לָהּ בָּהֶם׃
verses.english: And they shall take a blue fabric and cover the menorah for lighting and its lamps and its tongs and its fire-holders and all its equipment for oil with which they will minister for it.

tex.original: \hP{וְלָקְחוּ בֶּגֶד תְּכֵלֶת וְכִסּוּ אֶת מְנֹרַת הַמָּאוֹר וְאֶת נֵרֹתֶיהָ וְאֶת מַלְקָחֶיהָ וְאֶת מַחְתֹּתֶיהָ וְאֵת כּל כְּלֵי שַׁמְנָהּ אֲשֶׁר יְשָׁרְתוּ לָהּ בָּהֶם׃}

verses.original: וְנָתְנוּ אֹתָהּ וְאֶת כּל כֵּלֶיהָ אֶל מִכְסֵה עוֹר תָּחַשׁ וְנָתְנוּ עַל הַמּוֹט׃
verses.english: And they shall put it and all its equipment into a leather covering and put it on a beam.

tex.original: \hP{וְנָתְנוּ אֹתָהּ וְאֶת כּל כֵּלֶיהָ אֶל מִכְסֵה עוֹר תָּחַשׁ וְנָתְנוּ עַל הַמּוֹט׃}

verses.original: וְעַל מִזְבַּח הַזָּהָב יִפְרְשׂוּ בֶּגֶד תְּכֵלֶת וְכִסּוּ אֹתוֹ בְּמִכְסֵה עוֹר תָּחַשׁ וְשָׂמוּ אֶת בַּדָּיו׃
verses.english: And on the gold altar they shall spread a blue fabric, and they shall cover it with a leather covering and set its poles.

tex.original: \hP{וְעַל מִזְבַּח הַזָּהָב יִפְרְשׂוּ בֶּגֶד תְּכֵלֶת וְכִסּוּ אֹתוֹ בְּמִכְסֵה עוֹר תָּחַשׁ וְשָׂמוּ אֶת בַּדָּיו׃}

verses.original: וְלָקְחוּ אֶת כּל כְּלֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אֲשֶׁר יְשָׁרְתוּ בָם בַּקֹּדֶשׁ וְנָתְנוּ אֶל בֶּגֶד תְּכֵלֶת וְכִסּוּ אוֹתָם בְּמִכְסֵה עוֹר תָּחַשׁ וְנָתְנוּ עַל הַמּוֹט׃
verses.english: And they shall take all the equipment for ministering with which they minister in the Holy and put them into a blue fabric and cover them with a leather covering and put them on a beam.

tex.original: \hP{וְלָקְחוּ אֶת כּל כְּלֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אֲשֶׁר יְשָׁרְתוּ בָם בַּקֹּדֶשׁ וְנָתְנוּ אֶל בֶּגֶד תְּכֵלֶת וְכִסּוּ אוֹתָם בְּמִכְסֵה עוֹר תָּחַשׁ וְנָתְנוּ עַל הַמּוֹט׃}

verses.original: וְדִשְּׁנוּ אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּפָרְשׂוּ עָלָיו בֶּגֶד אַרְגָּמָן׃
verses.english: And they shall clear the ashes from the altar and spread a purple fabric over it.

tex.original: \hP{וְדִשְּׁנוּ אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּפָרְשׂוּ עָלָיו בֶּגֶד אַרְגָּמָן׃}

verses.original: וְנָתְנוּ עָלָיו אֶת כּל כֵּלָיו אֲשֶׁר יְשָׁרְתוּ עָלָיו בָּהֶם אֶת הַמַּחְתֹּת אֶת הַמִּזְלָגֹת וְאֶת הַיָּעִים וְאֶת הַמִּזְרָקֹת כֹּל כְּלֵי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּפָרְשׂוּ עָלָיו כְּסוּי עוֹר תַּחַשׁ וְשָׂמוּ בַדָּיו׃
verses.english: And they shall put on it all its equipment with which they minister at it—the fire-holders, the forks and the shovels and the basins—all the altar’s equipment, and they shall spread a leather covering on it and set its poles.

tex.original: \hP{וְנָתְנוּ עָלָיו אֶת כּל כֵּלָיו אֲשֶׁר יְשָׁרְתוּ עָלָיו בָּהֶם אֶת הַמַּחְתֹּת אֶת הַמִּזְלָגֹת וְאֶת הַיָּעִים וְאֶת הַמִּזְרָקֹת כֹּל כְּלֵי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּפָרְשׂוּ עָלָיו כְּסוּי עוֹר תַּחַשׁ וְשָׂמוּ בַדָּיו׃}

verses.original: וְכִלָּה אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו לְכַסֹּת אֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְאֶת כּל כְּלֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ בִּנְסֹעַ הַמַּחֲנֶה וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יָבֹאוּ בְנֵי קְהָת לָשֵׂאת וְלֹא יִגְּעוּ אֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ וָמֵתוּ אֵלֶּה מַשָּׂא בְנֵי קְהָת בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: And Aaron and his sons will finish covering the Holy and all the equipment of the Holy when the camp is to travel, and after that the children of Kohath shall come to carry, so they shall not touch the holy and die. These are what the children of Kohath are to carry in the Tent of Meeting.

tex.original: \hP{וְכִלָּה אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו לְכַסֹּת אֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְאֶת כּל כְּלֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ בִּנְסֹעַ הַמַּחֲנֶה וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יָבֹאוּ בְנֵי קְהָת לָשֵׂאת וְלֹא יִגְּעוּ אֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ וָמֵתוּ אֵלֶּה מַשָּׂא בְנֵי קְהָת בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And Aaron and his sons will finish covering the Holy and
		all the equipment of the Holy when the camp is to travel,
		and after that the children of Kohath shall come to carry,
		so they shall not touch the holy and die. These are what
		the children of Kohath are to carry in the Tent of
		Meeting.
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		so they shall not touch the holy and die. This is followed by: “they
%		shall not come to see as the Holy is covered up and die” (4:20). Thus,
%		twice more the text reminds us that closeness to the divine is
%		dangerous. The death of Aaron’s sons stands in the background of these
%		warnings. (In fact, it is mentioned in the preceding chapter; 3:4.) And
%		these warnings also remind us of the distinction between the ritual and
%		moral realms. Whatever their intentions, whatever their moral condition,
%		if these Kohathites touch what they are not supposed to touch or see
%		what they are not supposed to see, they will die.
%	}

verses.original: וּפְקֻדַּת אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן שֶׁמֶן הַמָּאוֹר וּקְטֹרֶת הַסַּמִּים וּמִנְחַת הַתָּמִיד וְשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה פְּקֻדַּת כּל הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְכל אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ בְּקֹדֶשׁ וּבְכֵלָיו׃
verses.english: “And the responsibility of Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest, is the oil for lighting and the incense of fragrances and the continual grain offering and the anointing oil—the responsibility for all of the Tabernacle and everything that is in it, in the Holy and in its equipment.”

tex.original: \hP{וּפְקֻדַּת אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן שֶׁמֶן הַמָּאוֹר וּקְטֹרֶת הַסַּמִּים וּמִנְחַת הַתָּמִיד וְשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה פְּקֻדַּת כּל הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְכל אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ בְּקֹדֶשׁ וּבְכֵלָיו׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		“And the responsibility of Eleazar son of Aaron, the
		priest, is the oil for lighting and the incense of
		fragrances and the continual grain offering and the
		anointing oil—the responsibility for all of the Tabernacle
		and everything that is in it, in the Holy and in its
		equipment.”
	}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן לֵאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן לֵאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,}

verses.original: אַל תַּכְרִיתוּ אֶת שֵׁבֶט מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַקְּהָתִי מִתּוֹךְ הַלְוִיִּם׃
verses.english: “You shall not cut off the tribe of the Kohathite families from among the Levites,

tex.original: \hP{אַל תַּכְרִיתוּ אֶת שֵׁבֶט מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַקְּהָתִי מִתּוֹךְ הַלְוִיִּם׃}

verses.original: וְזֹאת עֲשׂוּ לָהֶם וְחָיוּ וְלֹא יָמֻתוּ בְּגִשְׁתָּם אֶת קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו יָבֹאוּ וְשָׂמוּ אוֹתָם אִישׁ אִישׁ עַל עֲבֹדָתוֹ וְאֶל מַשָּׂאוֹ׃
verses.english: but do this to them so they will live and not die when they come close to the Holy of Holies: Aaron and his sons shall come, and they shall set them each at his work and to what he is to carry,

tex.original: \hP{וְזֹאת עֲשׂוּ לָהֶם וְחָיוּ וְלֹא יָמֻתוּ בְּגִשְׁתָּם אֶת קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו יָבֹאוּ וְשָׂמוּ אוֹתָם אִישׁ אִישׁ עַל עֲבֹדָתוֹ וְאֶל מַשָּׂאוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא יָבֹאוּ לִרְאוֹת כְּבַלַּע אֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ וָמֵתוּ׃
verses.english: and they shall not come to see as the Holy is covered up and die.”

tex.original: \hP{וְלֹא יָבֹאוּ לִרְאוֹת כְּבַלַּע אֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ וָמֵתוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: נָשֹׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן גַּם הֵם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם׃
verses.english: “Add up the heads of the children of Gershon, them as well, by their fathers’ house, by their families.

tex.original: \hP{נָשֹׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן גַּם הֵם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם׃}

verses.original: מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה עַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה תִּפְקֹד אוֹתָם כּל הַבָּא לִצְבֹא צָבָא לַעֲבֹד עֲבֹדָה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: You shall count them from thirty years old and up to fifty years old, everyone who would come to do army service, to do work in the Tent of Meeting.

tex.original: \hP{מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה עַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה תִּפְקֹד אוֹתָם כּל הַבָּא לִצְבֹא צָבָא לַעֲבֹד עֲבֹדָה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: זֹאת עֲבֹדַת מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּי לַעֲבֹד וּלְמַשָּׂא׃
verses.english: This is the work of the Gershonite families, for work and for carrying:

tex.original: \hP{זֹאת עֲבֹדַת מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּי לַעֲבֹד וּלְמַשָּׂא׃}

verses.original: וְנָשְׂאוּ אֶת יְרִיעֹת הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְאֶת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד מִכְסֵהוּ וּמִכְסֵה הַתַּחַשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָלָיו מִלְמָעְלָה וְאֶת מָסַךְ פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: And they shall carry the curtains of the Tabernacle, and the Tent of Meeting, its covering, and the leather covering that is on it above, and the cover of the entrance of the Tent of Meeting

tex.original: \hP{וְנָשְׂאוּ אֶת יְרִיעֹת הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְאֶת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד מִכְסֵהוּ וּמִכְסֵה הַתַּחַשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָלָיו מִלְמָעְלָה וְאֶת מָסַךְ פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וְאֵת קַלְעֵי הֶחָצֵר וְאֶת מָסַךְ פֶּתַח שַׁעַר הֶחָצֵר אֲשֶׁר עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ סָבִיב וְאֵת מֵיתְרֵיהֶם וְאֶת כּל כְּלֵי עֲבֹדָתָם וְאֵת כּל אֲשֶׁר יֵעָשֶׂה לָהֶם וְעָבָדוּ׃
verses.english: and the courtyard’s hangings and the cover for the entrance of the gate of the courtyard that is all around the Tabernacle and the altar, and their cords and all the equipment for their service. And everything that will be done for them: they shall do the work.

tex.original: \hP{וְאֵת קַלְעֵי הֶחָצֵר וְאֶת מָסַךְ פֶּתַח שַׁעַר הֶחָצֵר אֲשֶׁר עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ סָבִיב וְאֵת מֵיתְרֵיהֶם וְאֶת כּל כְּלֵי עֲבֹדָתָם וְאֵת כּל אֲשֶׁר יֵעָשֶׂה לָהֶם וְעָבָדוּ׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		and the courtyard’s hangings and the cover for the
		entrance of the gate of the courtyard that is all around
		the Tabernacle and the altar, and their cords and all the
		equipment for their service. And everything that will be
		done for them: they shall do the work.
	}

verses.original: עַל פִּי אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו תִּהְיֶה כּל עֲבֹדַת בְּנֵי הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּי לְכל מַשָּׂאָם וּלְכֹל עֲבֹדָתָם וּפְקַדְתֶּם עֲלֵהֶם בְּמִשְׁמֶרֶת אֵת כּל מַשָּׂאָם׃
verses.english: All the work of the children of the Gershonites shall be by the word of Aaron and his sons, for all their carrying and all their work. And you shall supervise them in the task: all their carrying.

tex.original: \hP{עַל פִּי אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו תִּהְיֶה כּל עֲבֹדַת בְּנֵי הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּי לְכל מַשָּׂאָם וּלְכֹל עֲבֹדָתָם וּפְקַדְתֶּם עֲלֵהֶם בְּמִשְׁמֶרֶת אֵת כּל מַשָּׂאָם׃}

verses.original: זֹאת עֲבֹדַת מִשְׁפְּחֹת בְּנֵי הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּי בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וּמִשְׁמַרְתָּם בְּיַד אִיתָמָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן׃
verses.english: This is the work of the families of the children of the Gershonites in the Tent of Meeting. And their charge is in the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron, the priest.

tex.original: \hP{זֹאת עֲבֹדַת מִשְׁפְּחֹת בְּנֵי הַגֵּרְשֻׁנִּי בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וּמִשְׁמַרְתָּם בְּיַד אִיתָמָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן׃}

verses.original: בְּנֵי מְרָרִי לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם תִּפְקֹד אֹתָם׃
verses.english: “The children of Merari by their families, by their fathers’ house: you shall count them.

tex.original: \hP{בְּנֵי מְרָרִי לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם תִּפְקֹד אֹתָם׃}

verses.original: מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה וְעַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה תִּפְקְדֵם כּל הַבָּא לַצָּבָא לַעֲבֹד אֶת עֲבֹדַת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: You shall count them from thirty years old and up to fifty years old, everyone who would come to the army, to do the work of the Tent of Meeting.

tex.original: \hP{מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה וְעַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה תִּפְקְדֵם כּל הַבָּא לַצָּבָא לַעֲבֹד אֶת עֲבֹדַת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וְזֹאת מִשְׁמֶרֶת מַשָּׂאָם לְכל עֲבֹדָתָם בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד קַרְשֵׁי הַמִּשְׁכָּן וּבְרִיחָיו וְעַמּוּדָיו וַאֲדָנָיו׃
verses.english: And this is their carrying task, for all their work in the Tent of Meeting: the Tabernacle’s frames and its bars and its columns and its bases

tex.original: \hP{וְזֹאת מִשְׁמֶרֶת מַשָּׂאָם לְכל עֲבֹדָתָם בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד קַרְשֵׁי הַמִּשְׁכָּן וּבְרִיחָיו וְעַמּוּדָיו וַאֲדָנָיו׃}

verses.original: וְעַמּוּדֵי הֶחָצֵר סָבִיב וְאַדְנֵיהֶם וִיתֵדֹתָם וּמֵיתְרֵיהֶם לְכל כְּלֵיהֶם וּלְכֹל עֲבֹדָתָם וּבְשֵׁמֹת תִּפְקְדוּ אֶת כְּלֵי מִשְׁמֶרֶת מַשָּׂאָם׃
verses.english: and the courtyard’s columns all around and their bases and their pegs and their cords, for all their equipment and all their service. And you shall take account of the equipment for their carrying task by name.

tex.original: \hP{וְעַמּוּדֵי הֶחָצֵר סָבִיב וְאַדְנֵיהֶם וִיתֵדֹתָם וּמֵיתְרֵיהֶם לְכל כְּלֵיהֶם וּלְכֹל עֲבֹדָתָם וּבְשֵׁמֹת תִּפְקְדוּ אֶת כְּלֵי מִשְׁמֶרֶת מַשָּׂאָם׃}

verses.original: זֹאת עֲבֹדַת מִשְׁפְּחֹת בְּנֵי מְרָרִי לְכל עֲבֹדָתָם בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד בְּיַד אִיתָמָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן׃
verses.english: This is the work of the families of the children of Merari, for all their work in the Tent of Meeting in the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron, the priest.”

tex.original: \hP{זֹאת עֲבֹדַת מִשְׁפְּחֹת בְּנֵי מְרָרִי לְכל עֲבֹדָתָם בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד בְּיַד אִיתָמָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן׃}

verses.original: וַיִּפְקֹד מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וּנְשִׂיאֵי הָעֵדָה אֶת בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִי לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם וּלְבֵית אֲבֹתָם׃
verses.english: And Moses and Aaron and the congregation’s chieftains counted the Kohathite children by their families and by their fathers’ house

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּפְקֹד מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וּנְשִׂיאֵי הָעֵדָה אֶת בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִי לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם וּלְבֵית אֲבֹתָם׃}

verses.original: מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה וְעַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה כּל הַבָּא לַצָּבָא לַעֲבֹדָה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: from thirty years old and up to fifty years old, everyone who would come to the army for the work of the Tent of Meeting.

tex.original: \hP{מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה וְעַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה כּל הַבָּא לַצָּבָא לַעֲבֹדָה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וַיִּהְיוּ פְקֻדֵיהֶם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם אַלְפַּיִם שְׁבַע מֵאוֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁים׃
verses.english: And their counts by their families were two thousand seven hundred fifty.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּהְיוּ פְקֻדֵיהֶם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם אַלְפַּיִם שְׁבַע מֵאוֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁים׃}

verses.original: אֵלֶּה פְקוּדֵי מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַקְּהָתִי כּל הָעֹבֵד בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֲשֶׁר פָּקַד מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה׃
verses.english: These are the counts of the Kohathite families, everyone who worked in the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted by YHWH’s word through Moses’ hand.

tex.original: \hP{אֵלֶּה פְקוּדֵי מִשְׁפְּחֹת הַקְּהָתִי כּל הָעֹבֵד בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֲשֶׁר פָּקַד מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה׃}

verses.original: וּפְקוּדֵי בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן לְמִשְׁפְּחוֹתָם וּלְבֵית אֲבֹתָם׃
verses.english: And the counts of the children of Gershon by their families and by their fathers’ house

tex.original: \hP{וּפְקוּדֵי בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן לְמִשְׁפְּחוֹתָם וּלְבֵית אֲבֹתָם׃}

verses.original: מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה וְעַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה כּל הַבָּא לַצָּבָא לַעֲבֹדָה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: from thirty years old and up to fifty years old, everyone who would come to the army for work in the Tent of Meeting:

tex.original: \hP{מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה וְעַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה כּל הַבָּא לַצָּבָא לַעֲבֹדָה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וַיִּהְיוּ פְּקֻדֵיהֶם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם אַלְפַּיִם וְשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וּשְׁלֹשִׁים׃
verses.english: And their counts by their families, by their fathers’ house, were two thousand six hundred thirty.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּהְיוּ פְּקֻדֵיהֶם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם אַלְפַּיִם וְשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וּשְׁלֹשִׁים׃}

verses.original: אֵלֶּה פְקוּדֵי מִשְׁפְּחֹת בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן כּל הָעֹבֵד בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֲשֶׁר פָּקַד מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: These are the counts of the families of the children of Gershon, everyone who worked in the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted by YHWH’s word.

tex.original: \hP{אֵלֶּה פְקוּדֵי מִשְׁפְּחֹת בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן כּל הָעֹבֵד בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֲשֶׁר פָּקַד מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וּפְקוּדֵי מִשְׁפְּחֹת בְּנֵי מְרָרִי לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם׃
verses.english: And the counts of the families of the children of Merari by their families, by their fathers’ house

tex.original: \hP{וּפְקוּדֵי מִשְׁפְּחֹת בְּנֵי מְרָרִי לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם׃}

verses.original: מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה וְעַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה כּל הַבָּא לַצָּבָא לַעֲבֹדָה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: from thirty years old and up to fifty years old, everyone who would come to the army for work in the Tent of Meeting:

tex.original: \hP{מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה וְעַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה כּל הַבָּא לַצָּבָא לַעֲבֹדָה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וַיִּהְיוּ פְקֻדֵיהֶם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם שְׁלֹשֶׁת אֲלָפִים וּמָאתָיִם׃
verses.english: And their counts by their families were three thousand two hundred.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּהְיוּ פְקֻדֵיהֶם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם שְׁלֹשֶׁת אֲלָפִים וּמָאתָיִם׃}

verses.original: אֵלֶּה פְקוּדֵי מִשְׁפְּחֹת בְּנֵי מְרָרִי אֲשֶׁר פָּקַד מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה׃
verses.english: These are the counts of the families of the children of Merari whom Moses and Aaron counted by YHWH’s word through Moses’ hand.

tex.original: \hP{אֵלֶּה פְקוּדֵי מִשְׁפְּחֹת בְּנֵי מְרָרִי אֲשֶׁר פָּקַד מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה׃}

verses.original: כּל הַפְּקֻדִים אֲשֶׁר פָּקַד מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וּנְשִׂיאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַלְוִיִּם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם וּלְבֵית אֲבֹתָם׃
verses.english: All the counts that Moses and Aaron and Israel’s chieftains made of the Levites by their families and by their fathers’ house

tex.original: \hP{כּל הַפְּקֻדִים אֲשֶׁר פָּקַד מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וּנְשִׂיאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַלְוִיִּם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם וּלְבֵית אֲבֹתָם׃}

verses.original: מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה וְעַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה כּל הַבָּא לַעֲבֹד עֲבֹדַת עֲבֹדָה וַעֲבֹדַת מַשָּׂא בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: from thirty years old and up to fifty years old, everyone who was coming to do the service of work and the service of carrying in the Tent of Meeting:

tex.original: \hP{מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה וְעַד בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה כּל הַבָּא לַעֲבֹד עֲבֹדַת עֲבֹדָה וַעֲבֹדַת מַשָּׂא בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וַיִּהְיוּ פְּקֻדֵיהֶם שְׁמֹנַת אֲלָפִים וַחֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת וּשְׁמֹנִים׃
verses.english: And their counts were eight thousand five hundred eighty.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּהְיוּ פְּקֻדֵיהֶם שְׁמֹנַת אֲלָפִים וַחֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת וּשְׁמֹנִים׃}

verses.original: עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה פָּקַד אוֹתָם בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה אִישׁ אִישׁ עַל עֲבֹדָתוֹ וְעַל מַשָּׂאוֹ וּפְקֻדָיו אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶת מֹשֶׁה׃
verses.english: By YHWH’s word he counted them by Moses’ hand, each man by his work or by his carrying, and his counts were as YHWH commanded Moses.

tex.original: \hP{עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה פָּקַד אוֹתָם בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה אִישׁ אִישׁ עַל עֲבֹדָתוֹ וְעַל מַשָּׂאוֹ וּפְקֻדָיו אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶת מֹשֶׁה׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: צַו אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וִישַׁלְּחוּ מִן הַמַּחֲנֶה כּל צָרוּעַ וְכל זָב וְכֹל טָמֵא לָנָפֶשׁ׃
verses.english: “Command the children of Israel that they shall have every leper and everyone who has an emission and everyone who is impure by a person go from the camp.

tex.original: \hP{צַו אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וִישַׁלְּחוּ מִן הַמַּחֲנֶה כּל צָרוּעַ וְכל זָב וְכֹל טָמֵא לָנָפֶשׁ׃}

verses.original: מִזָּכָר עַד נְקֵבָה תְּשַׁלֵּחוּ אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה תְּשַׁלְּחוּם וְלֹא יְטַמְּאוּ אֶת מַחֲנֵיהֶם אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי שֹׁכֵן בְּתוֹכָם׃
verses.english: Male or female, you shall have them go; you shall have them go outside the camp so they will not make their camps, among which I tent, impure.”

tex.original: \hP{מִזָּכָר עַד נְקֵבָה תְּשַׁלֵּחוּ אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה תְּשַׁלְּחוּם וְלֹא יְטַמְּאוּ אֶת מַחֲנֵיהֶם אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי שֹׁכֵן בְּתוֹכָם׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיְשַׁלְּחוּ אוֹתָם אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה כֵּן עָשׂוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And the children of Israel did so, and they had them go outside the camp. As YHWH spoke to Moses, so the children of Israel did.

tex.original: \hP{וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיְשַׁלְּחוּ אוֹתָם אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה כֵּן עָשׂוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה כִּי יַעֲשׂוּ מִכּל חַטֹּאת הָאָדָם לִמְעֹל מַעַל בַּיהֹוָה וְאָשְׁמָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא׃
verses.english: “Speak to the children of Israel: A man or a woman—when they will do any of the sins of humans, to make a breach against YHWH—so that person has guilt,

tex.original: \hP{דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה כִּי יַעֲשׂוּ מִכּל חַטֹּאת הָאָדָם לִמְעֹל מַעַל בַּיהֹוָה וְאָשְׁמָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא׃}

verses.original: וְהִתְוַדּוּ אֶת חַטָּאתָם אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת אֲשָׁמוֹ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ וַחֲמִישִׁתוֹ יֹסֵף עָלָיו וְנָתַן לַאֲשֶׁר אָשַׁם לוֹ׃
verses.english: then they shall confess their sin that they have done. And he shall pay back for his guilt with its principal, and he shall add to it a fifth of it, and he shall give it to the one whom he wronged.

tex.original: \hP{וְהִתְוַדּוּ אֶת חַטָּאתָם אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת אֲשָׁמוֹ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ וַחֲמִישִׁתוֹ יֹסֵף עָלָיו וְנָתַן לַאֲשֶׁר אָשַׁם לוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם אֵין לָאִישׁ גֹּאֵל לְהָשִׁיב הָאָשָׁם אֵלָיו הָאָשָׁם הַמּוּשָׁב לַיהֹוָה לַכֹּהֵן מִלְּבַד אֵיל הַכִּפֻּרִים אֲשֶׁר יְכַפֶּר בּוֹ עָלָיו׃
verses.english: And if the man does not have a redeemer, to pay him back for the guilt, the guilt that is paid back is YHWH’s, for the priest, apart from the ram of atonement by which he will make atonement for him.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם אֵין לָאִישׁ גֹּאֵל לְהָשִׁיב הָאָשָׁם אֵלָיו הָאָשָׁם הַמּוּשָׁב לַיהֹוָה לַכֹּהֵן מִלְּבַד אֵיל הַכִּפֻּרִים אֲשֶׁר יְכַפֶּר בּוֹ עָלָיו׃}

verses.original: וְכל תְּרוּמָה לְכל קדְשֵׁי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ לַכֹּהֵן לוֹ יִהְיֶה׃
verses.english: And every donation of all the holy things of the children of Israel that they will bring forward to the priest shall be his.

tex.original: \hP{וְכל תְּרוּמָה לְכל קדְשֵׁי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ לַכֹּהֵן לוֹ יִהְיֶה׃}

verses.original: וְאִישׁ אֶת קֳדָשָׁיו לוֹ יִהְיוּ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן לַכֹּהֵן לוֹ יִהְיֶה׃
verses.english: And each man’s holy things shall be his; what each man gives to the priest shall be his.”

tex.original: \hP{וְאִישׁ אֶת קֳדָשָׁיו לוֹ יִהְיוּ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן לַכֹּהֵן לוֹ יִהְיֶה׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ אִישׁ כִּי תִשְׂטֶה אִשְׁתּוֹ וּמָעֲלָה בוֹ מָעַל׃
verses.english: “Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: Any man whose wife will go astray and will make a breach of faith with him,

tex.original: \hP{דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ אִישׁ כִּי תִשְׂטֶה אִשְׁתּוֹ וּמָעֲלָה בוֹ מָעַל׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		go astray. Hebrew root  This situation is known therefore as the
%		case of the  Footnote 5:12. go astray. This section deals with
%		the case of the suspected : a woman whose husband suspects her of
%		adultery, but who has not been proved guilty by evidence or witnesses.
%		It would not merit special notice as anything more than any other law,
%		especially since it has not been practiced for at least two millennia
%		(and, I would say, probably more than two-and-a-half millennia), but it
%		has acquired special importance because, first, it is regarded as the
%		only case of trial by ordeal in the Torah and, second, because questions
%		about the legal status of women have risen to prominence in this
%		generation. The woman is made to drink a mixture of holy water, dust
%		from the Tabernacle’s floor, and ink from a document expressing a curse
%		if she is guilty. Then, if “her womb swells and her thigh sags” she is
%		understood to be guilty. There have been many attempts to understand
%		what is going on in this strange case. The traditional Talmudic belief
%		is that a miracle is expected to occur through this procedure. Another
%		view is that the procedure is designed to scare guilty women into
%		confessing rather than face the ceremony and the curse. Another is that,
%		since drinking water with dust and ink does not produce these symptoms,
%		this is a law that is designed to find all women not guilty—and thus
%		protect suspected women from their husbands’ or town’s vengeance.
%		Another view is that this procedure can result in the condition of a
%		prolapsed uterus. All the views leave questions: Why not have some
%		procedure like this for a man who is suspected of adultery? In fact, why
%		not have a procedure like this for any other crime, by a man or a woman?
%		Also, even if the woman is shown guilty, she is not executed, which
%		elsewhere is the penalty for adultery (Lev 20:10; Deut 22:22). So, to
%		begin with: this procedure must relate specifically to something (1)
%		about women and not men, and (2) about sex and adultery. I believe that
%		all of the past explanations are mistaken, and I offer the following
%		explanation of this case: If we were told that a woman’s “womb is
%		swelling and her thigh is sagging,” nearly 100 percent of us would
%		understand this to mean: she is pregnant. So, in this case, it is
%		explicitly about a woman who has had sex with another man in place of
%		her husband. That is, she has not slept with her husband recently, and
%		that is why her pregnancy is proof of adultery. The purpose of drinking
%		the mixture is not to prove her guilt but to bring about the curse
%		through her pregnancy. (Thus it is called “the bitter cursing water”;
%		and the priest says, “Let YHWH make you a curse and an oath among your
%		people when YHWH sets your thigh sagging and your womb swelling.”) This
%		is why the law applies only to women and only to the matter of adultery:
%		it is the only offense in the Torah in which guilt can be determined by
%		this biological fact, even when there are no witnesses and no other
%		evidence. And this is why the woman cannot be executed: She has not been
%		proved guilty in front of judges in a court of law through witnesses.
%		She has been shown to have done this in front of priests at the
%		Tabernacle. Therefore, she “shall bear her crime” (see the comment on
%		5:31). This has a more general implication as well. The reason that we
%		have had such difficulty understanding this case for millennia is that
%		law is constructed on analogy: we decide cases by precedents, by
%		consistent principles that apply to cases in a variety of circumstances.
%		But pregnancy is a condition that is without analogy in human
%		experience. That is why this case reads like no other. And that is why
%		there are agonizing, passionate debates in the present age over whether
%		to save the mother or the baby in a medical crisis during labor, over
%		rights to sperm and eggs that have been preserved, over surrogate
%		mothers, and, above all, over abortion: with arguments about when the
%		developing being inside the womb is a living human in its own right, and
%		about the legal rights of the mother over her own body in balance with
%		the legal protection of the fetus. There simply is no other experience
%		in which two lives are so utterly interconnected. Why are the rabbis of
%		the Talmudic era so unclear about the actual procedure if it had been
%		practiced in recent memory? Because, I think, it had not been practiced
%		since the time of the First Temple in Jerusalem. It required dust from
%		the Tabernacle floor, and the Tabernacle was only in the First Temple,
%		not in the Second. (A report in the Mishnah that Rabbi Yohanan ben
%		Zakkai abolished this procedure makes no sense historically. By the time
%		of his authority, even the Second Temple was gone.) And so it came about
%		that the actual meaning of this ceremony was forgotten after many
%		centuries of not being practiced, and the result has been uncertainty
%		and confusion about its meaning.
%	}

verses.original: וְשָׁכַב אִישׁ אֹתָהּ שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע וְנֶעְלַם מֵעֵינֵי אִישָׁהּ וְנִסְתְּרָה וְהִיא נִטְמָאָה וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ וְהִוא לֹא נִתְפָּשָׂה׃
verses.english: and a man has lain with her—an intercourse of seed—and it has been hidden from her husband’s eyes, and she has kept concealed, and she has been made impure, and there is no witness against her, and she has not been caught,

tex.original: \hP{וְשָׁכַב אִישׁ אֹתָהּ שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע וְנֶעְלַם מֵעֵינֵי אִישָׁהּ וְנִסְתְּרָה וְהִיא נִטְמָאָה וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ וְהִוא לֹא נִתְפָּשָׂה׃}

verses.original: וְעָבַר עָלָיו רוּחַ קִנְאָה וְקִנֵּא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְהִוא נִטְמָאָה אוֹ עָבַר עָלָיו רוּחַ קִנְאָה וְקִנֵּא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְהִיא לֹא נִטְמָאָה׃
verses.english: and a spirit of jealousy has come over him, and he is jealous about his wife, and she has been made impure, or a spirit of jealousy has come over him, and he is jealous about his wife, and she has not been made impure:

tex.original: \hP{וְעָבַר עָלָיו רוּחַ קִנְאָה וְקִנֵּא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְהִוא נִטְמָאָה אוֹ עָבַר עָלָיו רוּחַ קִנְאָה וְקִנֵּא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְהִיא לֹא נִטְמָאָה׃}

verses.original: וְהֵבִיא הָאִישׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ אֶל הַכֹּהֵן וְהֵבִיא אֶת קרְבָּנָהּ עָלֶיהָ עֲשִׂירִת הָאֵיפָה קֶמַח שְׂעֹרִים לֹא יִצֹק עָלָיו שֶׁמֶן וְלֹא יִתֵּן עָלָיו לְבֹנָה כִּי מִנְחַת קְנָאֹת הוּא מִנְחַת זִכָּרוֹן מַזְכֶּרֶת עָוֺן׃
verses.english: then the man shall bring his wife to the priest and shall bring her offering along with her: a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He shall not pour oil on it and shall not put frankincense on it, because it is an offering about jealousies, an offering of bringing to mind: causing a crime to be brought to mind.

tex.original: \hP{וְהֵבִיא הָאִישׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ אֶל הַכֹּהֵן וְהֵבִיא אֶת קרְבָּנָהּ עָלֶיהָ עֲשִׂירִת הָאֵיפָה קֶמַח שְׂעֹרִים לֹא יִצֹק עָלָיו שֶׁמֶן וְלֹא יִתֵּן עָלָיו לְבֹנָה כִּי מִנְחַת קְנָאֹת הוּא מִנְחַת זִכָּרוֹן מַזְכֶּרֶת עָוֺן׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		then the man shall bring his wife to the priest and shall
		bring her offering along with her: a tenth of an ephah of
		barley flour. He shall not pour oil on it and shall not
		put frankincense on it, because it is an offering about
		jealousies, an offering of bringing to mind: causing a
		crime to be brought to mind.
	}

verses.original: וְהִקְרִיב אֹתָהּ הַכֹּהֵן וְהֶעֱמִדָהּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: “And the priest shall bring her forward and stand her in front of YHWH.

tex.original: \hP{וְהִקְרִיב אֹתָהּ הַכֹּהֵן וְהֶעֱמִדָהּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן מַיִם קְדֹשִׁים בִּכְלִי חָרֶשׂ וּמִן הֶעָפָר אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בְּקַרְקַע הַמִּשְׁכָּן יִקַּח הַכֹּהֵן וְנָתַן אֶל הַמָּיִם׃
verses.english: And the priest shall take holy water in a clay container, and the priest shall take some of the dust that will be on the Tabernacle’s floor and put it into the water.

tex.original: \hP{וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן מַיִם קְדֹשִׁים בִּכְלִי חָרֶשׂ וּמִן הֶעָפָר אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בְּקַרְקַע הַמִּשְׁכָּן יִקַּח הַכֹּהֵן וְנָתַן אֶל הַמָּיִם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		holy water. This is the only reference to holy water in the Torah. It
%		may be the water from the basin that the priests use for washing (Exod
%		30:17–21); the basin is among the things that are identified as “holy of
%		holies” (30:28–29). Footnote 5:17. dust. The woman must drink the water
%		containing this dust (5:24). Some have claimed that there is a parallel
%		between this case and the episode of the golden calf. Moses grinds the
%		golden calf thin as dust (Exod 32:20; Deut 9:21), scatters it in water,
%		and makes the people drink (Exodus 32). My reaction is that such a view
%		is tenuous at best. The people in Exodus are guilty! The  case is
%		a process designed to determine guilt. And the dust from the Tabernacle
%		is something positive, while the dust of the calf is the opposite. It is
%		true that the people of Israel’s turning to pagan gods is sometimes
%		compared to adultery in the Tanak: Israel is described as a faithless
%		wife. And the term that means “a breach of faith” (ma‘al) with a husband
%		here refers to breaches of faith with God in all its other occurrences
%		in the Torah. But the cases of the  and the golden calf have so
%		many fundamental differences that drawing a connection between them may
%		mislead more than shed light.
%	}

verses.original: וְהֶעֱמִיד הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הָאִשָּׁה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וּפָרַע אֶת רֹאשׁ הָאִשָּׁה וְנָתַן עַל כַּפֶּיהָ אֵת מִנְחַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן מִנְחַת קְנָאֹת הִוא וּבְיַד הַכֹּהֵן יִהְיוּ מֵי הַמָּרִים הַמְאָרְרִים׃
verses.english: And the priest shall stand the woman in front of YHWH and loosen the hair of the woman’s head and put the offering of bringing to mind on her hands; it is an offering of jealousies. And in the priest’s hand shall be the bitter cursing water.

tex.original: \hP{וְהֶעֱמִיד הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הָאִשָּׁה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וּפָרַע אֶת רֹאשׁ הָאִשָּׁה וְנָתַן עַל כַּפֶּיהָ אֵת מִנְחַת הַזִּכָּרוֹן מִנְחַת קְנָאֹת הִוא וּבְיַד הַכֹּהֵן יִהְיוּ מֵי הַמָּרִים הַמְאָרְרִים׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And the priest shall stand the woman in front of YHWH and
		loosen the hair of the woman’s head and put the offering
		of bringing to mind on her hands; it is an offering of
		jealousies. And in the priest’s hand shall be the bitter
		cursing water.
	}

verses.original: וְהִשְׁבִּיעַ אֹתָהּ הַכֹּהֵן וְאָמַר אֶל הָאִשָּׁה אִם לֹא שָׁכַב אִישׁ אֹתָךְ וְאִם לֹא שָׂטִית טֻמְאָה תַּחַת אִישֵׁךְ הִנָּקִי מִמֵּי הַמָּרִים הַמְאָרְרִים הָאֵלֶּה׃
verses.english: And the priest shall have her swear, and he shall say to the woman: ‘If a man has not lain with you, and if you have not gone astray in impurity with someone in place of your husband, be cleared by this bitter cursing water.

tex.original: \hP{וְהִשְׁבִּיעַ אֹתָהּ הַכֹּהֵן וְאָמַר אֶל הָאִשָּׁה אִם לֹא שָׁכַב אִישׁ אֹתָךְ וְאִם לֹא שָׂטִית טֻמְאָה תַּחַת אִישֵׁךְ הִנָּקִי מִמֵּי הַמָּרִים הַמְאָרְרִים הָאֵלֶּה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		in place of your husband. Suggesting that if she is pregnant it must be
%		by the other man, not the husband. Those who have other views of the
%		 procedure understand this phrase to mean “under your husband,”
%		and they interpret it as meaning “under his authority.” But there is no
%		reason why that had to be mentioned in the context of these
%		instructions. Moreover, the term here, Hebrew , means “in place
%		of” sixteen times in the Torah but never means “under someone’s
%		authority” (the term for that is “under the hand of,” Hebrew
%		yad; cf. Gen 41:35).
%	}

verses.original: וְאַתְּ כִּי שָׂטִית תַּחַת אִישֵׁךְ וְכִי נִטְמֵאת וַיִּתֵּן אִישׁ בָּךְ אֶת שְׁכבְתּוֹ מִבַּלְעֲדֵי אִישֵׁךְ׃
verses.english: But you, if you have gone astray with someone in place of your husband and if you have been made impure, and if a man other than your husband has had his intercourse with you,’

tex.original: \hP{וְאַתְּ כִּי שָׂטִית תַּחַת אִישֵׁךְ וְכִי נִטְמֵאת וַיִּתֵּן אִישׁ בָּךְ אֶת שְׁכבְתּוֹ מִבַּלְעֲדֵי אִישֵׁךְ׃}

verses.original: וְהִשְׁבִּיעַ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הָאִשָּׁה בִּשְׁבֻעַת הָאָלָה וְאָמַר הַכֹּהֵן לָאִשָּׁה יִתֵּן יְהֹוָה אוֹתָךְ לְאָלָה וְלִשְׁבֻעָה בְּתוֹךְ עַמֵּךְ בְּתֵת יְהֹוָה אֶת יְרֵכֵךְ נֹפֶלֶת וְאֶת בִּטְנֵךְ צָבָה׃
verses.english: then the priest shall have the woman swear a curse oath, and the priest shall say to the woman, ‘let YHWH make you a curse and an oath among your people when YHWH sets your thigh sagging and your womb swelling,

tex.original: \hP{וְהִשְׁבִּיעַ הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הָאִשָּׁה בִּשְׁבֻעַת הָאָלָה וְאָמַר הַכֹּהֵן לָאִשָּׁה יִתֵּן יְהֹוָה אוֹתָךְ לְאָלָה וְלִשְׁבֻעָה בְּתוֹךְ עַמֵּךְ בְּתֵת יְהֹוָה אֶת יְרֵכֵךְ נֹפֶלֶת וְאֶת בִּטְנֵךְ צָבָה׃}

verses.original: וּבָאוּ הַמַּיִם הַמְאָרְרִים הָאֵלֶּה בְּמֵעַיִךְ לַצְבּוֹת בֶּטֶן וְלַנְפִּל יָרֵךְ וְאָמְרָה הָאִשָּׁה אָמֵן אָמֵן׃
verses.english: and this cursing water will come in your insides, to swell the womb and make the thigh sag.’ “And the woman shall say, ‘Amen, amen.’

tex.original: \hP{וּבָאוּ הַמַּיִם הַמְאָרְרִים הָאֵלֶּה בְּמֵעַיִךְ לַצְבּוֹת בֶּטֶן וְלַנְפִּל יָרֵךְ וְאָמְרָה הָאִשָּׁה אָמֵן אָמֵן׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		to swell the womb and make the thigh sag. It is not clear whether this
%		refers to God’s making this happen (as is explicit in the preceding
%		verse) or to the water’s making it happen. It appears to me that God is
%		understood here to bring about the pregnancy—in the sense that all
%		pregnancies are understood to be enabled by God—and that the water
%		brings about the curse: “the bitter cursing water.”
%	}

verses.original: וְכָתַב אֶת הָאָלֹת הָאֵלֶּה הַכֹּהֵן בַּסֵּפֶר וּמָחָה אֶל מֵי הַמָּרִים׃
verses.english: “And the priest shall write these curses in a scroll and rub them into the bitter water.

tex.original: \hP{וְכָתַב אֶת הָאָלֹת הָאֵלֶּה הַכֹּהֵן בַּסֵּפֶר וּמָחָה אֶל מֵי הַמָּרִים׃}

verses.original: וְהִשְׁקָה אֶת הָאִשָּׁה אֶת מֵי הַמָּרִים הַמְאָרְרִים וּבָאוּ בָהּ הַמַּיִם הַמְאָרְרִים לְמָרִים׃
verses.english: And he shall have the woman drink the bitter cursing water, and the bitter cursing water will come into her.

tex.original: \hP{וְהִשְׁקָה אֶת הָאִשָּׁה אֶת מֵי הַמָּרִים הַמְאָרְרִים וּבָאוּ בָהּ הַמַּיִם הַמְאָרְרִים לְמָרִים׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the bitter cursing water. Hebrew mê hammrîm hamme’rrîm. The obvious
%		alliteration is one of several cases of wordplay in this text: Hebrew
%		 (it has been hidden) reverses the root letters of
%		(breach). Hebrew  (a tenth) reverses the root letters of
%		(barley). Hebrew  (loosen the hair) reverses  (dust). And
%		Hebrew  (cursing) has strong alliteration with  (bitter).
%		This wordplay involves much more than artistry with language. Each of
%		these puns is linked to an aspect of this ceremony that is unique in
%		some way: This is the only case in which  (to make a breach) is
%		used for an offense against a human rather than God (see the comment on
%		Lev 5:15). It is the only time that  (barley flour) is used for a
%		grain offering. It is the only use of  the It is the only time
%		that (dust) from the Tabernacle. And this strange use of water (holy
%		water, with a curse melted into it) is the most unusual of all. Puns are
%		common in the Torah’s stories, but their appearance in a law is
%		extremely unusual and unexpected. They highlight the unusual aspect of
%		this case, and they summon to mind associations with the realm of magic,
%		in which the artistry of language and poetry figure in incantations and
%		ceremonies. Likewise, the dissolving of the words of the curse into the
%		water, the dust from the Tabernacle, the water from the priests’ basin,
%		the act of drinking a mixture that produces a curse: much of this has
%		parallels in magic in other cultures, and all of this renders this
%		ceremony mysterious. And it fits with the fact that the function of this
%		procedure is not to establish legal guilt but rather to produce the
%		curse.
%	}

verses.original: וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן מִיַּד הָאִשָּׁה אֵת מִנְחַת הַקְּנָאֹת וְהֵנִיף אֶת הַמִּנְחָה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וְהִקְרִיב אֹתָהּ אֶל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ׃
verses.english: And the priest shall take the offering of jealousies from the woman’s hand and elevate the offering in front of YHWH, and he shall bring her forward to the altar.

tex.original: \hP{וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן מִיַּד הָאִשָּׁה אֵת מִנְחַת הַקְּנָאֹת וְהֵנִיף אֶת הַמִּנְחָה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וְהִקְרִיב אֹתָהּ אֶל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ׃}

verses.original: וְקָמַץ הַכֹּהֵן מִן הַמִּנְחָה אֶת אַזְכָּרָתָהּ וְהִקְטִיר הַמִּזְבֵּחָה וְאַחַר יַשְׁקֶה אֶת הָאִשָּׁה אֶת הַמָּיִם׃
verses.english: And the priest shall take a fistful from the grain offering, a representative portion of it, and burn it to smoke at the altar, and after that he shall have the woman drink the water.

tex.original: \hP{וְקָמַץ הַכֹּהֵן מִן הַמִּנְחָה אֶת אַזְכָּרָתָהּ וְהִקְטִיר הַמִּזְבֵּחָה וְאַחַר יַשְׁקֶה אֶת הָאִשָּׁה אֶת הַמָּיִם׃}

verses.original: וְהִשְׁקָהּ אֶת הַמַּיִם וְהָיְתָה אִם נִטְמְאָה וַתִּמְעֹל מַעַל בְּאִישָׁהּ וּבָאוּ בָהּ הַמַּיִם הַמְאָרְרִים לְמָרִים וְצָבְתָה בִטְנָהּ וְנָפְלָה יְרֵכָהּ וְהָיְתָה הָאִשָּׁה לְאָלָה בְּקֶרֶב עַמָּהּ׃
verses.english: When he has had her drink the water, then it will be, if she has been made impure and has made a breach of faith with her husband, when the bitter cursing water will come into her, and her womb will swell and her thigh will sag, then the woman will become a curse among her people.

tex.original: \hP{וְהִשְׁקָהּ אֶת הַמַּיִם וְהָיְתָה אִם נִטְמְאָה וַתִּמְעֹל מַעַל בְּאִישָׁהּ וּבָאוּ בָהּ הַמַּיִם הַמְאָרְרִים לְמָרִים וְצָבְתָה בִטְנָהּ וְנָפְלָה יְרֵכָהּ וְהָיְתָה הָאִשָּׁה לְאָלָה בְּקֶרֶב עַמָּהּ׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		When he has had her drink the water, then it will be, if
		she has been made impure and has made a breach of faith
		with her husband, when the bitter cursing water will come
		into her, and her womb will swell and her thigh will sag,
		then the woman will become a curse among her people.
	}

verses.original: וְאִם לֹא נִטְמְאָה הָאִשָּׁה וּטְהֹרָה הִוא וְנִקְּתָה וְנִזְרְעָה זָרַע׃
verses.english: And if the woman has not been made impure, and she is pure, then she shall be cleared and shall conceive seed.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִם לֹא נִטְמְאָה הָאִשָּׁה וּטְהֹרָה הִוא וְנִקְּתָה וְנִזְרְעָה זָרַע׃}

verses.original: זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַקְּנָאֹת אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׂטֶה אִשָּׁה תַּחַת אִישָׁהּ וְנִטְמָאָה׃
verses.english: “This is the instruction for jealousies, when a woman will go astray with someone in place of her husband and be made impure,

tex.original: \hP{זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַקְּנָאֹת אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׂטֶה אִשָּׁה תַּחַת אִישָׁהּ וְנִטְמָאָה׃}

verses.original: אוֹ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲבֹר עָלָיו רוּחַ קִנְאָה וְקִנֵּא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְהֶעֱמִיד אֶת הָאִשָּׁה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וְעָשָׂה לָהּ הַכֹּהֵן אֵת כּל הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת׃
verses.english: or when a spirit of jealousy will come over a man and he will be jealous about his wife. And the priest shall stand the woman in front of YHWH and do all of this instruction to her.

tex.original: \hP{אוֹ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲבֹר עָלָיו רוּחַ קִנְאָה וְקִנֵּא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְהֶעֱמִיד אֶת הָאִשָּׁה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וְעָשָׂה לָהּ הַכֹּהֵן אֵת כּל הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת׃}

verses.original: וְנִקָּה הָאִישׁ מֵעָוֺן וְהָאִשָּׁה הַהִוא תִּשָּׂא אֶת עֲוֺנָהּ׃
verses.english: And the man shall be clear of a crime, and that woman shall bear her crime.”

tex.original: \hP{וְנִקָּה הָאִישׁ מֵעָוֺן וְהָאִשָּׁה הַהִוא תִּשָּׂא אֶת עֲוֺנָהּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the man shall be clear of a crime. This is usually understood to mean
%		that the husband is innocent of the crime of making a false charge
%		against his wife. But this is a questionable reading since the text does
%		not say that he has made any charge against her; he has just brought her
%		to the priest to make the determination of whether his jealousy is
%		correct or not. This may rather refer to the other man, the one who had
%		intercourse with the woman. The procedure proves only that the woman has
%		had intercourse; it cannot prove who the man was. It is therefore not
%		possible to convict the man by this procedure. This also answers the
%		question of why this procedure applies only to women. A man accused of
%		adultery does not go through this. Because only women can become
%		pregnant, it is only women who can be proved to have committed adultery
%		in the absence of witnesses or any other evidence. (This brings to mind
%		the case of Bathsheba, who becomes pregnant through adultery with David.
%		Her pregnancy while her husband has been away at war is what would make
%		her adultery known; 2 Samuel 11.)
%	}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה כִּי יַפְלִא לִנְדֹּר נֶדֶר נָזִיר לְהַזִּיר לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: “Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: When a man or a woman will expressly make a Nazirite vow to make a separation for YHWH,

tex.original: \hP{דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה כִּי יַפְלִא לִנְדֹּר נֶדֶר נָזִיר לְהַזִּיר לַיהֹוָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		a man or a woman. Although the rest of the law is stated in the
%		masculine, the entire matter of choosing to be a Nazirite applies to
%		both men and women. Footnote 6:2. make a separation for YHWH. A Nazirite
%		vows to give up certain things and live in a state of holiness. There is
%		the general idea in the Torah that all the people are holy (Lev 19:1),
%		but the Nazirite vow refers to a singular state that exceeds that. The
%		Nazirite gives up three things: consuming alcohol, coming near to dead
%		persons, and cutting his or her hair. Why these three things? These
%		three things are related to priesthood—and particularly to the high
%		priest. Israel’s priests are forbidden to consume alcohol at the Tent of
%		Meeting, and this is the first command in the Torah that God gives
%		directly to Aaron, the high priest, not to Moses (Lev 10:9). Priests are
%		forbidden to come to dead persons except their closest relatives (Lev
%		21:1–3), and the high priest is commanded that “he shall not come to any
%		dead persons; he shall not become impure for his father and for his
%		mother” (21:11)—which is the wording here for the Nazirite as well: “he
%		shall not come to a dead person. For his father and for his mother, for
%		his brother and for his sister: he shall not become impure for them”
%		(Num 6:6–7). But in the matter of the hair, the high priest is commanded
%		to do the opposite of the Nazirite: The Nazirite shall “grow the hair of
%		his head loose” (Num 6:5), but the high priest “shall not let loose the
%		hair of his head” (Lev 21:10). What does it mean that a Nazirite is
%		someone who chooses to live in certain respects like a high priest but
%		that a high priest is commanded not to have the most obvious
%		characteristic of the Nazirite? The issue appears to me to relate to the
%		fact that the clergy in Israel is not open to most Israelites to choose,
%		but only to members of the tribe of Levi by heredity, and then only to
%		males; and the priesthood comes to be limited only to a certain family
%		within Levi, the family of Aaron; and the high priesthood is limited to
%		a son of the preceding high priest. Prophets can be from any tribe and
%		can be male or female; one becomes a prophet by being called by God.
%		Postbiblically, rabbis replace priests as the primary clergy of the
%		Jews, and membership in the rabbinate is open to anyone who chooses it
%		and proves capable of qualifying and carrying it out. Originally it was
%		limited to males, but in the present generation the Reform,
%		Conservative, and Reconstructionist movements have included both females
%		and males. So what option does a person in the biblical world have who
%		is drawn to the holy life of a priest but who is not a male Levite from
%		the family of Aaron? Such a person can choose to be a Nazirite. And note
%		the case of Samuel: he becomes a priest, seemingly the high priest, even
%		though he is not a Levite—and Samuel is a Nazirite! He replaces the
%		Levite high priest Eli at the Tabernacle at Shiloh, and he performs
%		sacrifices, which no nonpriest, even the king, may do (1 Samuel 1–13).
%		Historically, the law forbidding the high priest to let his hair grow
%		loose may have been composed precisely to establish that this could
%		never happen again. No one outside the Aaronid Levite clan could just
%		choose to enter the clergy and rise in the priesthood. As the law stands
%		in the Torah now, preceding the story of Samuel, it means that the case
%		of Samuel must be regarded as unique, with Samuel’s rise in the
%		priesthood being the result of a special selection by God.
%	}

verses.original: מִיַּיִן וְשֵׁכָר יַזִּיר חֹמֶץ יַיִן וְחֹמֶץ שֵׁכָר לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה וְכל מִשְׁרַת עֲנָבִים לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה וַעֲנָבִים לַחִים וִיבֵשִׁים לֹא יֹאכֵל׃
verses.english: he shall separate from wine and beer; he shall not drink any vinegar of wine or vinegar of beer, and he shall not drink any juice of grapes, and he shall not eat fresh or dried grapes.

tex.original: \hP{מִיַּיִן וְשֵׁכָר יַזִּיר חֹמֶץ יַיִן וְחֹמֶץ שֵׁכָר לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה וְכל מִשְׁרַת עֲנָבִים לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה וַעֲנָבִים לַחִים וִיבֵשִׁים לֹא יֹאכֵל׃}

verses.original: כֹּל יְמֵי נִזְרוֹ מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר יֵעָשֶׂה מִגֶּפֶן הַיַּיִן מֵחַרְצַנִּים וְעַד זָג לֹא יֹאכֵל׃
verses.english: All the days of his being a Nazirite, he shall not eat anything that is made from the grapevine, from seeds to skin.

tex.original: \hP{כֹּל יְמֵי נִזְרוֹ מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר יֵעָשֶׂה מִגֶּפֶן הַיַּיִן מֵחַרְצַנִּים וְעַד זָג לֹא יֹאכֵל׃}

verses.original: כּל יְמֵי נֶדֶר נִזְרוֹ תַּעַר לֹא יַעֲבֹר עַל רֹאשׁוֹ עַד מְלֹאת הַיָּמִם אֲשֶׁר יַזִּיר לַיהֹוָה קָדֹשׁ יִהְיֶה גַּדֵּל פֶּרַע שְׂעַר רֹאשׁוֹ׃
verses.english: All the days of his Nazirite vow, a razor shall not pass on his head; until the fulfillment of the days that he will make a separation for YHWH, he shall be holy, growing the hair of his head loose.

tex.original: \hP{כּל יְמֵי נֶדֶר נִזְרוֹ תַּעַר לֹא יַעֲבֹר עַל רֹאשׁוֹ עַד מְלֹאת הַיָּמִם אֲשֶׁר יַזִּיר לַיהֹוָה קָדֹשׁ יִהְיֶה גַּדֵּל פֶּרַע שְׂעַר רֹאשׁוֹ׃}

verses.original: כּל יְמֵי הַזִּירוֹ לַיהֹוָה עַל נֶפֶשׁ מֵת לֹא יָבֹא׃
verses.english: All the days of his making a separation for YHWH he shall not come to a dead person.

tex.original: \hP{כּל יְמֵי הַזִּירוֹ לַיהֹוָה עַל נֶפֶשׁ מֵת לֹא יָבֹא׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		come to a dead person. Meaning: touch a dead body. Interestingly, the
%		case of Samson is different. Like Samuel, he is a Nazirite from birth,
%		and he is forbidden to cut his hair—which becomes the key to his story.
%		But he is not forbidden to have contact with dead bodies—which is also
%		essential to the story, because he becomes a warrior and personally
%		makes thousands of dead bodies!
%	}

verses.original: לְאָבִיו וּלְאִמּוֹ לְאָחִיו וּלְאַחֹתוֹ לֹא יִטַּמָּא לָהֶם בְּמֹתָם כִּי נֵזֶר אֱלֹהָיו עַל רֹאשׁוֹ׃
verses.english: For his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister: he shall not become impure for them when they die, because the crown of his God is on his head.

tex.original: \hP{לְאָבִיו וּלְאִמּוֹ לְאָחִיו וּלְאַחֹתוֹ לֹא יִטַּמָּא לָהֶם בְּמֹתָם כִּי נֵזֶר אֱלֹהָיו עַל רֹאשׁוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the crown of his God is on his head. As I noted in the case of the high
%		priest, the Hebrew term nzer has the same range as the English
%		word crown, denoting either the top of the head or the headdress worn by
%		a king or priest (see my comment on Lev 21:12). Here it refers to the
%		hair on the Nazirite’s head, which may not be cut. As long as the man or
%		woman wears the uncut Nazirite hair, he or she also follows the high
%		priest’s practice of not touching a corpse.
%	}

verses.original: כֹּל יְמֵי נִזְרוֹ קָדֹשׁ הוּא לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: All the days of his being a Nazirite he is holy to YHWH.

tex.original: \hP{כֹּל יְמֵי נִזְרוֹ קָדֹשׁ הוּא לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְכִי יָמוּת מֵת עָלָיו בְּפֶתַע פִּתְאֹם וְטִמֵּא רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ וְגִלַּח רֹאשׁוֹ בְּיוֹם טהֳרָתוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי יְגַלְּחֶנּוּ׃
verses.english: And if someone will die by chance suddenly by him and will make his head’s crown impure, then he shall shave his head on the day of his purification: he shall shave it on the seventh day.

tex.original: \hP{וְכִי יָמוּת מֵת עָלָיו בְּפֶתַע פִּתְאֹם וְטִמֵּא רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ וְגִלַּח רֹאשׁוֹ בְּיוֹם טהֳרָתוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי יְגַלְּחֶנּוּ׃}

verses.original: וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי יָבִא שְׁתֵּי תֹרִים אוֹ שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי יוֹנָה אֶל הַכֹּהֵן אֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: And on the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two pigeons to the priest, to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

tex.original: \hP{וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי יָבִא שְׁתֵּי תֹרִים אוֹ שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי יוֹנָה אֶל הַכֹּהֵן אֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וְעָשָׂה הַכֹּהֵן אֶחָד לְחַטָּאת וְאֶחָד לְעֹלָה וְכִפֶּר עָלָיו מֵאֲשֶׁר חָטָא עַל הַנָּפֶשׁ וְקִדַּשׁ אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא׃
verses.english: And the priest shall do one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering and shall make atonement over him in that he has sinned over a person. And he shall make his head holy on that day.

tex.original: \hP{וְעָשָׂה הַכֹּהֵן אֶחָד לְחַטָּאת וְאֶחָד לְעֹלָה וְכִפֶּר עָלָיו מֵאֲשֶׁר חָטָא עַל הַנָּפֶשׁ וְקִדַּשׁ אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא׃}

verses.original: וְהִזִּיר לַיהֹוָה אֶת יְמֵי נִזְרוֹ וְהֵבִיא כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן שְׁנָתוֹ לְאָשָׁם וְהַיָּמִים הָרִאשֹׁנִים יִפְּלוּ כִּי טָמֵא נִזְרוֹ׃
verses.english: And he shall make a separation for YHWH for the days of his being a Nazirite, and he shall bring a lamb in its first year for a guilt offering, and the first days shall fall because his Nazirite state became impure.

tex.original: \hP{וְהִזִּיר לַיהֹוָה אֶת יְמֵי נִזְרוֹ וְהֵבִיא כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן שְׁנָתוֹ לְאָשָׁם וְהַיָּמִים הָרִאשֹׁנִים יִפְּלוּ כִּי טָמֵא נִזְרוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת הַנָּזִיר בְּיוֹם מְלֹאת יְמֵי נִזְרוֹ יָבִיא אֹתוֹ אֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: “And this is the instruction for the Nazirite: On the day of the fulfillment of the days of his being a Nazirite one shall bring him to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

tex.original: \hP{וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת הַנָּזִיר בְּיוֹם מְלֹאת יְמֵי נִזְרוֹ יָבִיא אֹתוֹ אֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וְהִקְרִיב אֶת קרְבָּנוֹ לַיהֹוָה כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן שְׁנָתוֹ תָמִים אֶחָד לְעֹלָה וְכַבְשָׂה אַחַת בַּת שְׁנָתָהּ תְּמִימָה לְחַטָּאת וְאַיִל אֶחָד תָּמִים לִשְׁלָמִים׃
verses.english: And he shall make his offering to YHWH: one unblemished lamb in its first year for a burnt offering and one unblemished ewe-lamb in its first year for a sin offering and one unblemished ram for a peace offering

tex.original: \hP{וְהִקְרִיב אֶת קרְבָּנוֹ לַיהֹוָה כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן שְׁנָתוֹ תָמִים אֶחָד לְעֹלָה וְכַבְשָׂה אַחַת בַּת שְׁנָתָהּ תְּמִימָה לְחַטָּאת וְאַיִל אֶחָד תָּמִים לִשְׁלָמִים׃}

verses.original: וְסַל מַצּוֹת סֹלֶת חַלֹּת בְּלוּלֹת בַּשֶּׁמֶן וּרְקִיקֵי מַצּוֹת מְשֻׁחִים בַּשָּׁמֶן וּמִנְחָתָם וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם׃
verses.english: and a basket of unleavened bread of fine flour, cakes mixed with oil and unleavened wafers with oil poured on them with their grain offering and their libations.

tex.original: \hP{וְסַל מַצּוֹת סֹלֶת חַלֹּת בְּלוּלֹת בַּשֶּׁמֶן וּרְקִיקֵי מַצּוֹת מְשֻׁחִים בַּשָּׁמֶן וּמִנְחָתָם וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וְהִקְרִיב הַכֹּהֵן לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וְעָשָׂה אֶת חַטָּאתוֹ וְאֶת עֹלָתוֹ׃
verses.english: And the priest shall bring it forward in front of YHWH and shall do his sin offering and his burnt offering.

tex.original: \hP{וְהִקְרִיב הַכֹּהֵן לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וְעָשָׂה אֶת חַטָּאתוֹ וְאֶת עֹלָתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְאֶת הָאַיִל יַעֲשֶׂה זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים לַיהֹוָה עַל סַל הַמַּצּוֹת וְעָשָׂה הַכֹּהֵן אֶת מִנְחָתוֹ וְאֶת נִסְכּוֹ׃
verses.english: And he shall make the ram a peace-offering sacrifice to YHWH with the basket of unleavened bread, and the priest shall do his grain offering and his libation.

tex.original: \hP{וְאֶת הָאַיִל יַעֲשֶׂה זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים לַיהֹוָה עַל סַל הַמַּצּוֹת וְעָשָׂה הַכֹּהֵן אֶת מִנְחָתוֹ וְאֶת נִסְכּוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְגִלַּח הַנָּזִיר פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֶת רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ וְלָקַח אֶת שְׂעַר רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ וְנָתַן עַל הָאֵשׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּחַת זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים׃
verses.english: And the Nazirite shall shave his head’s crown at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and shall take the hair of his head’s crown and put it on the fire that is under the peace-offering sacrifice.

tex.original: \hP{וְגִלַּח הַנָּזִיר פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֶת רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ וְלָקַח אֶת שְׂעַר רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ וְנָתַן עַל הָאֵשׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּחַת זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים׃}

verses.original: וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַזְּרֹעַ בְּשֵׁלָה מִן הָאַיִל וְחַלַּת מַצָּה אַחַת מִן הַסַּל וּרְקִיק מַצָּה אֶחָד וְנָתַן עַל כַּפֵּי הַנָּזִיר אַחַר הִתְגַּלְּחוֹ אֶת נִזְרוֹ׃
verses.english: And the priest shall take the cooked shoulder from the ram and one unleavened cake from the basket and one unleavened wafer and put them on the Nazirite’s hands after his crown is shaved.

tex.original: \hP{וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַזְּרֹעַ בְּשֵׁלָה מִן הָאַיִל וְחַלַּת מַצָּה אַחַת מִן הַסַּל וּרְקִיק מַצָּה אֶחָד וְנָתַן עַל כַּפֵּי הַנָּזִיר אַחַר הִתְגַּלְּחוֹ אֶת נִזְרוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְהֵנִיף אוֹתָם הַכֹּהֵן תְּנוּפָה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה קֹדֶשׁ הוּא לַכֹּהֵן עַל חֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה וְעַל שׁוֹק הַתְּרוּמָה וְאַחַר יִשְׁתֶּה הַנָּזִיר יָיִן׃
verses.english: And the priest shall elevate them, an elevation offering in front of YHWH. It is holy for the priest along with the breast of the elevation offering and the thigh of the donation. And after that the Nazirite may drink wine.

tex.original: \hP{וְהֵנִיף אוֹתָם הַכֹּהֵן תְּנוּפָה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה קֹדֶשׁ הוּא לַכֹּהֵן עַל חֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה וְעַל שׁוֹק הַתְּרוּמָה וְאַחַר יִשְׁתֶּה הַנָּזִיר יָיִן׃}

verses.original: זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַנָּזִיר אֲשֶׁר יִדֹּר קרְבָּנוֹ לַיהֹוָה עַל נִזְרוֹ מִלְּבַד אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יָדוֹ כְּפִי נִדְרוֹ אֲשֶׁר יִדֹּר כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה עַל תּוֹרַת נִזְרוֹ׃
verses.english: This is the instruction for the Nazirite who will vow his offering to YHWH for his being a Nazirite outside of what his hand may attain. According to his vow that he will make, so he shall do along with the instruction of his being a Nazirite.”

tex.original: \hP{זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַנָּזִיר אֲשֶׁר יִדֹּר קרְבָּנוֹ לַיהֹוָה עַל נִזְרוֹ מִלְּבַד אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יָדוֹ כְּפִי נִדְרוֹ אֲשֶׁר יִדֹּר כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה עַל תּוֹרַת נִזְרוֹ׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		This is the instruction for the Nazirite who will vow his
		offering to YHWH for his being a Nazirite outside of what
		his hand may attain. According to his vow that he will
		make, so he shall do along with the instruction of his
		being a Nazirite.”
	}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: דַּבֵּר אֶל אַהֲרֹן וְאֶל בָּנָיו לֵאמֹר כֹּה תְבָרְכוּ אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָמוֹר לָהֶם׃
verses.english: “Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, This is how you shall bless the children of Israel; say to them:

tex.original: \hP{דַּבֵּר אֶל אַהֲרֹן וְאֶל בָּנָיו לֵאמֹר כֹּה תְבָרְכוּ אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָמוֹר לָהֶם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		This is how you shall bless. A new form of expression that enters
%		biblical narrative in the book of Numbers is prayer. In earlier books
%		there have been depictions of individuals in prayer, but Numbers
%		includes a formal prayer, commanded to be said verbatim by the priests,
%		known as the priestly benediction (6:22–27). This blessing has been
%		pronounced upon the congregation by those of priestly descent presumably
%		from the biblical period until the present day (in some synagogues). It
%		has come to be of special interest recently. While staying in Jerusalem
%		in the summer of 1978, I looked out my window and watched a team of
%		archaeologists working below. They had uncovered Jewish tombs of the
%		Iron Age. I (and they) did not know it then, but inscriptions in thin
%		silver foil that they discovered were later painstakingly unrolled and
%		found to bear the words of the priestly benediction. The silver foil
%		inscriptions are the oldest known texts of a passage from the Bible.
%		(Their wording differs slightly from the biblical text and from each
%		other.)
%	}

verses.original: יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ׃
verses.english: May YHWH bless you and watch over you.

tex.original: \hPaleoM{יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ׃}
tex.english: \eP{May YHWH bless you and watch over you. }
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		you. The language of the priestly benediction, like the Decalogue, is
%		formulated in the second-person singular. Although the priests are
%		instructed to bless the entire people with it, and although it
%		historically has been pronounced as a congregational blessing, it is
%		both a personal and a communal wish. In three brief lines the priests
%		wish each individual Israelite divine blessing, protection, favor,
%		grace, attention, and peace.
%	}

verses.original: יָאֵר יְהֹוָה פָּנָיו אֵלֶיךָ וִיחֻנֶּךָּ׃
verses.english: May YHWH make His face shine to you and be gracious to you.

tex.original: \hPaleoM{יָאֵר יְהֹוָה פָּנָיו אֵלֶיךָ וִיחֻנֶּךָּ׃}

verses.original: יִשָּׂא יְהֹוָה פָּנָיו אֵלֶיךָ וְיָשֵׂם לְךָ שָׁלוֹם׃
verses.english: May YHWH raise His face to you and give you peace.

tex.original: \hPaleoM{יִשָּׂא יְהֹוָה פָּנָיו אֵלֶיךָ וְיָשֵׂם לְךָ שָׁלוֹם׃}
tex.english: \eP{May YHWH raise His face to you and give you peace. }
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		and give you peace. The culminating wish of peace in the priestly
%		benediction is particularly poignant because Numbers is the first book
%		of the Bible so far to concentrate on war. Certainly peace can mean a
%		secure condition for an individual generally rather than being limited
%		to meaning an absence of war, but the issue of war is so much a part of
%		Numbers that the reference to peace in this significant position is
%		nonetheless quite striking. It appears in the beginning section of the
%		book as part of the preparation at Mount Sinai for the journey to come.
%		The people’s journey then comes to include substantial doses of reality
%		in the form of confrontations with hostile groups. Israel’s only
%		experience of war before this is in the brief account of an attack by
%		the Amalekites shortly after the exodus as the people first approach
%		Horeb (Exod 17:8–16). Indeed, the book of Exodus reports that the reason
%		the Israelites go to the Red Sea on the way out of Egypt instead of
%		taking the more obvious route, overland through Philistine territory, is
%		that YHWH is concerned that they are not yet ready to face war (13:17).
%		When the Egyptian army pursues them, Moses instructs them, “YHWH will
%		fight for you, and you’ll keep quiet!” (14:14); and again in the Song of
%		the Sea, it is the deity who is described as a warrior (15:3). Genesis
%		recounts only one battle, in which Abraham becomes involved because of
%		the capture of his nephew Lot (Genesis 14). Leviticus includes no
%		battles, and the word “war” does not occur in it. Deuteronomy, as I
%		shall discuss, treats the subject of war through remarkable legislation
%		but not through narrative other than to refer to the war episodes of
%		Numbers. It is Numbers alone among the Five Books of Moses that
%		especially develops this worst of human conditions through narrative of
%		specific military encounters. And it is Numbers that says, “May YHWH
%		give you peace”!
%	}

verses.original: וְשָׂמוּ אֶת שְׁמִי עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַאֲנִי אֲבָרְכֵם׃
verses.english: And they shall set my name on the children of Israel, and I shall bless them.”
