%		are identified as descendants of Noah’s son Ham (Gen 10:6–7). On this
%		understanding, Moses has taken an Ethiopian wife in addition to his
%		first, Midianite wife, Zipporah. This has been confused somewhat by the
%		fact that the prophet Habakkuk refers to a place called Cushan in
%		parallel with Midian (Hab 3:7). Some scholars, therefore, have concluded
%		that the Cushite wife is Zipporah herself (so Ibn Ezra). But this latter
%		view does not explain why the text should suddenly refer to her here as
%		a Cushite. Also, the words “because he had taken a Cushite wife”
%		certainly appear to be here in the verse in order to inform us of an
%		essential new fact, but we already knew that he was married to Zipporah
%		(so Rashbam). This story, therefore, is about a second, probably
%		Ethiopian wife.
%	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ הֲרַק אַךְ בְּמֹשֶׁה דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה הֲלֹא גַּם בָּנוּ דִבֵּר וַיִּשְׁמַע יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: And they said, “Has YHWH only just spoken through Moses? Hasn’t He also spoken through us?” And YHWH heard.

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמְרוּ הֲרַק אַךְ בְּמֹשֶׁה דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה הֲלֹא גַּם בָּנוּ דִבֵּר וַיִּשְׁמַע יְהֹוָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		only just spoken. Aaron and Miriam say, “Has YHWH only just spoken
%		through Moses?” “Only just” sounds redundant. The redundant word “only,”
%		though, is Hebrew raq, and the story concludes with YHWH demanding a
%		measure of punishment of Miriam comparable to the shame she would have
%		experienced if her father “had spit in her face,” which is Hebrew
%		yrq yraq (12:14), an intensive form that doubles
%		the verb—and doubly emphasizes the pun. And the pun confirms that
%		Miriam’s punishment is meant to fit the crime: see the comment on v. 10.
%		One might regard this last pun as a relatively minor item of wordplay,
%		but it is in fact part of an elaborate chain of puns that are stitched
%		through this section of Numbers. The chain encompasses this story and
%		the one that precedes it, the story of Moses’ anguished complaint and
%		the appointment of the seventy elders to share his load. The first word
%		of that story is the extremely unusual and uncertain term ’sapsup
%		(spelled with an unvocalized aleph at the beginning because it is
%		preceded by the definite article), meaning a “gathered mass”
%		(classically translated as a “mixed multitude”) among the Israelites.
%		The root letters of this strange word (’SP) then resurface in a showcase
%		of forms through this story and the next one:  Through fourteen
%		variations on the root letters, we are brought from the crisis that is
%		generated by the “gathered mass” to resolution when Miriam is “gathered
%		back” (h’sp). Moreover, this chain of paronomasia
%		may serve to stitch these two stories more tightly together and thus
%		suggest a relationship between the seventy elders’ prophesying in
%		Numbers 11 and Aaron’s and Miriam’s complaint in Numbers 12 (“Has YHWH
%		only just spoken through Moses?”). Footnote 12:2. they said, “Has YHWH
%		only just spoken through Moses?” What does this complaint have to do
%		with Moses’ wife?! Answer: nothing. Like someone who has had a bad day
%		and comes home and complains about dinner, Aaron and Miriam do not voice
%		what is really bothering them. They redirect their annoyance at Moses
%		himself. Aaron and Miriam have been identified as prophets (Exod 7:1;
%		15:20). God has spoken to Aaron, and Aaron was part of the group that
%		had a vision of God on Sinai (Exodus 24). And so they question Moses’
%		position: is he the only one close to God? It is common for people to
%		redirect anger, but it has risks in every case, especially when it
%		occurs within a family. This episode dramatizes that danger: Miriam and
%		Aaron bring God into what was a family dispute. This is a mistake! God
%		appears, and they suffer.
%	}

verses.original: וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה עָנָו מְאֹד מִכֹּל הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה׃
verses.english: And the man Moses was very humble, more than every human who was on the face of the earth.

tex.original: \hE{וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה עָנָו מְאֹד מִכֹּל הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		humble, more than every human who was on the face of the earth. Is this
%		the humblest man on earth? But he is the man who has just said things to
%		God like “Why have you done bad to your servant?” and “If this is how
%		you treat me, kill me!” We might say that his closeness to God enables
%		him to speak this way to the deity while still being humble when dealing
%		with other human beings. But then how are we to account for the way he
%		spoke to the Pharaoh before the last plague in Egypt: “All these
%		servants of yours will come down to me, and they’ll bow to me” (Exod
%		11:8)? Perhaps it is precisely his experiences in Egypt and at Sinai
%		that have made him now the humblest of humans. Having seen the extent of
%		God’s power, he feels humble. Having seen his inability to handle the
%		people and their complaints on his own, he feels humbler still. Thus,
%		even when he speaks to God with his audacious closeness, he says, “I’m
%		not able, I, by myself, to carry this entire people, because it’s too
%		heavy for me” (11:14).
%	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה פִּתְאֹם אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן וְאֶל מִרְיָם צְאוּ שְׁלשְׁתְּכֶם אֶל אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וַיֵּצְאוּ שְׁלשְׁתָּם׃
verses.english: And YHWH said suddenly to Moses and to Aaron and to Miriam, “Go out, the three of you, to the Tent of Meeting.” And the three of them went out.

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה פִּתְאֹם אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן וְאֶל מִרְיָם צְאוּ שְׁלשְׁתְּכֶם אֶל אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וַיֵּצְאוּ שְׁלשְׁתָּם׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּרֶד יְהֹוָה בְּעַמּוּד עָנָן וַיַּעֲמֹד פֶּתַח הָאֹהֶל וַיִּקְרָא אַהֲרֹן וּמִרְיָם וַיֵּצְאוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: And YHWH came down in a column of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent. And He called, “Aaron and Miriam.” And the two of them went out.

tex.original: \hE{וַיֵּרֶד יְהֹוָה בְּעַמּוּד עָנָן וַיַּעֲמֹד פֶּתַח הָאֹהֶל וַיִּקְרָא אַהֲרֹן וּמִרְיָם וַיֵּצְאוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שִׁמְעוּ נָא דְבָרָי אִם יִהְיֶה נְבִיאֲכֶם יְהֹוָה בַּמַּרְאָה אֵלָיו אֶתְוַדָּע בַּחֲלוֹם אֲדַבֶּר בּוֹ׃
verses.english: And He said, “Hear my words: If there will be a prophet among you, I, YHWH, shall be known to him in a vision; in a dream I shall speak through him.

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמֶר שִׁמְעוּ נָא דְבָרָי אִם יִהְיֶה נְבִיאֲכֶם יְהֹוָה בַּמַּרְאָה אֵלָיו אֶתְוַדָּע בַּחֲלוֹם אֲדַבֶּר בּוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		in a vision; in a dream. All prophetic experience in the Tanak is
%		understood to be through visions and dreams—except Moses’. The fifteen
%		books of the Hebrew Bible that are named for prophets either identify
%		the prophets’ experiences as visions or else leave the form of the
%		experiences undescribed (Ezek 12:27; 40:2; Hos 12:11; Hab 2:2; Mic 3:6).
%		Many begin by identifying the book’s contents as the prophet’s vision:
%		“The vision of Isaiah” (Isa 1:1; cf. 2 Chr 32:32); “The vision of
%		Obadiah” (Oba 1); “The book of the vision of Nahum” (Nah 1:1); “The
%		words of Amos … which he envisioned” (Amos 1:1); “The word of YHWH that
%		came to Micah … which he envisioned” (Mic 1:1); “The oracle that
%		Habakkuk the prophet envisioned” (Hab 1:1).
%	}

verses.original: לֹא כֵן עַבְדִּי מֹשֶׁה בְּכל בֵּיתִי נֶאֱמָן הוּא׃
verses.english: Not so is my servant Moses; in all my house he is faithful.

tex.original: \hE{לֹא כֵן עַבְדִּי מֹשֶׁה בְּכל בֵּיתִי נֶאֱמָן הוּא׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Not so is my servant Moses. Some experiences are impressive or inspiring
%		or powerful in themselves; and some experiences change a person’s life
%		ever after. The moment at which Moses sees the form of God from the back
%		on Sinai separates him from all other prophets (Exod 33:21–23). It is
%		understood that no other prophet has a standing that is equal to that of
%		Moses.
%	}

verses.original: פֶּה אֶל פֶּה אֲדַבֶּר בּוֹ וּמַרְאֶה וְלֹא בְחִידֹת וּתְמֻנַת יְהֹוָה יַבִּיט וּמַדּוּעַ לֹא יְרֵאתֶם לְדַבֵּר בְּעַבְדִּי בְמֹשֶׁה׃
verses.english: Mouth to mouth I shall speak through him and vision and not in enigmas, and he will see the form of YHWH. And why did you not fear to speak against my servant, against Moses?”

tex.original: \hE{פֶּה אֶל פֶּה אֲדַבֶּר בּוֹ וּמַרְאֶה וְלֹא בְחִידֹת וּתְמֻנַת יְהֹוָה יַבִּיט וּמַדּוּעַ לֹא יְרֵאתֶם לְדַבֵּר בְּעַבְדִּי בְמֹשֶׁה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּחַר אַף יְהֹוָה בָּם וַיֵּלַךְ׃
verses.english: And YHWH’s anger flared against them, and He went.

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּחַר אַף יְהֹוָה בָּם וַיֵּלַךְ׃}
tex.english: \eE{And YHWH’s anger flared against them, and He went. }

verses.original: וְהֶעָנָן סָר מֵעַל הָאֹהֶל וְהִנֵּה מִרְיָם מְצֹרַעַת כַּשָּׁלֶג וַיִּפֶן אַהֲרֹן אֶל מִרְיָם וְהִנֵּה מְצֹרָעַת׃
verses.english: And the cloud turned from over the tent; and, here, Miriam was leprous, like snow. And Aaron turned to Miriam, and, here, she was leprous.

tex.original: \hE{וְהֶעָנָן סָר מֵעַל הָאֹהֶל וְהִנֵּה מִרְיָם מְצֹרַעַת כַּשָּׁלֶג וַיִּפֶן אַהֲרֹן אֶל מִרְיָם וְהִנֵּה מְצֹרָעַת׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		leprous, like snow. Miriam is left with a kind of leprosy in which her
%		flesh is devoid of pigment. If we understand correctly that the Cushite
%		wife is Ethiopian, then this is a provocative case of punishment to suit
%		the crime and a powerful biblical statement regarding racism. It is as
%		if God says to Miriam: “You don’t like a woman with dark pigmentation?
%		Then you don’t have to have any pigmentation!” Or: “You don’t like a
%		woman who is black? Try being completely white!”
%	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר אַהֲרֹן אֶל מֹשֶׁה בִּי אֲדֹנִי אַל נָא תָשֵׁת עָלֵינוּ חַטָּאת אֲשֶׁר נוֹאַלְנוּ וַאֲשֶׁר חָטָאנוּ׃
verses.english: And Aaron said to Moses, “In me, my lord. Don’t set a sin on us, which we did foolishly and which we sinned.

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמֶר אַהֲרֹן אֶל מֹשֶׁה בִּי אֲדֹנִי אַל נָא תָשֵׁת עָלֵינוּ חַטָּאת אֲשֶׁר נוֹאַלְנוּ וַאֲשֶׁר חָטָאנוּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		my lord. Aaron addressed Moses as “my lord” one other time: in the
%		golden calf episode. On each of the two occasions on which he has acted
%		inappropriately toward Moses, he has ended up having to acknowledge
%		Moses’ status humbly and politely. Footnote 12:11. Don’t set a sin on
%		us. Aaron acknowledges that both he and Miriam are guilty. He says,
%		“Don’t set a sin on us, which we did foolishly and which we sinned.” Why
%		is there no consequence here for Aaron? Why does Miriam suffer while
%		Aaron does not? As I commented in the case of Aaron’s making the golden
%		calf, the answer may be that Aaron is the high priest. In that position
%		he cannot suffer any direct punishment from God, which would both
%		disqualify him and demean the office of high priest. And so what is left
%		is for Aaron to make amends through personal atonement. What is
%		impressive here is that he frames his atonement entirely in terms of
%		Miriam. He acknowledges his own equal culpability, and he pleads with
%		Moses to intercede for his sister.
%	}

verses.original: אַל נָא תְהִי כַּמֵּת אֲשֶׁר בְּצֵאתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם אִמּוֹ וַיֵּאָכֵל חֲצִי בְשָׂרוֹ׃
verses.english: Let her not be like the dead who, when he comes out of his mother’s womb, half of his flesh is eaten up!”

tex.original: \hE{אַל נָא תְהִי כַּמֵּת אֲשֶׁר בְּצֵאתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם אִמּוֹ וַיֵּאָכֵל חֲצִי בְשָׂרוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּצְעַק מֹשֶׁה אֶל יְהֹוָה לֵאמֹר אֵל נָא רְפָא נָא לָהּ׃
verses.english: And Moses cried out to YHWH, saying, “Oh, God, heal her!”

tex.original: \hE{וַיִּצְעַק מֹשֶׁה אֶל יְהֹוָה לֵאמֹר אֵל נָא רְפָא נָא לָהּ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאָבִיהָ יָרֹק יָרַק בְּפָנֶיהָ הֲלֹא תִכָּלֵם שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תִּסָּגֵר שִׁבְעַת יָמִים מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה וְאַחַר תֵּאָסֵף׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “And if her father had spit in her face, wouldn’t she be humiliated seven days? Let her be closed up seven days outside the camp, and after that let her be gathered back.”

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאָבִיהָ יָרֹק יָרַק בְּפָנֶיהָ הֲלֹא תִכָּלֵם שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תִּסָּגֵר שִׁבְעַת יָמִים מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה וְאַחַר תֵּאָסֵף׃}

verses.original: וַתִּסָּגֵר מִרְיָם מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה שִׁבְעַת יָמִים וְהָעָם לֹא נָסַע עַד הֵאָסֵף מִרְיָם׃
verses.english: And Miriam was closed up outside the camp seven days. And the people did not travel until Miriam was gathered back, and after that the people traveled from Hazeroth. And they camped in the Paran wilderness.

tex.original: \hE{וַתִּסָּגֵר מִרְיָם מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה שִׁבְעַת יָמִים וְהָעָם לֹא נָסַע עַד הֵאָסֵף מִרְיָם׃}

verses.original: וְאַחַר נָסְעוּ הָעָם מֵחֲצֵרוֹת וַיַּחֲנוּ בְּמִדְבַּר פָּארָן׃

tex.original: \hE{וְאַחַר נָסְעוּ הָעָם מֵחֲצֵרוֹת וַיַּחֲנוּ בְּמִדְבַּר פָּארָן׃}
tex.english: \eE{}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,  }

verses.original: שְׁלַח לְךָ אֲנָשִׁים וְיָתֻרוּ אֶת אֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי נֹתֵן לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אִישׁ אֶחָד אִישׁ אֶחָד לְמַטֵּה אֲבֹתָיו תִּשְׁלָחוּ כֹּל נָשִׂיא בָהֶם׃
verses.english: “Send men and let them scout the land of Canaan that I’m giving to the children of Israel. You shall send one man for each tribe of his fathers, every one of them a chieftain.”

tex.original: \hP{שְׁלַח לְךָ אֲנָשִׁים וְיָתֻרוּ אֶת אֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי נֹתֵן לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אִישׁ אֶחָד אִישׁ אֶחָד לְמַטֵּה אֲבֹתָיו תִּשְׁלָחוּ כֹּל נָשִׂיא בָהֶם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		send one man for each tribe. One scout is named for each tribe except
%		Levi. Why is the priestly tribe not represented? Perhaps no one from
%		Levi is sent to scout the territory because Levi is the one tribe that
%		will not be assigned any territory in the land. They derive their
%		support from the sacrifices, tithes, and donations of the other tribes.
%		Footnote 13:2. every one of them a chieftain. This story is commonly
%		referred to as the episode of the spies, but the men whom Moses sends
%		are tribal leaders, not ordinary scouts. The function of their mission
%		is not espionage but observation, to bring back a description of the
%		land to their people. They are leaders. That is why their negativity
%		when they return is so devastating. It is not just a disappointing bit
%		of intelligence. It is a failure to lead and encourage.
%	}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח אֹתָם מֹשֶׁה מִמִּדְבַּר פָּארָן עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה כֻּלָּם אֲנָשִׁים רָאשֵׁי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵמָּה׃
verses.english: And Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran by YHWH’s word. They were all men who were heads of the children of Israel.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּשְׁלַח אֹתָם מֹשֶׁה מִמִּדְבַּר פָּארָן עַל פִּי יְהֹוָה כֻּלָּם אֲנָשִׁים רָאשֵׁי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵמָּה׃}

verses.original: וְאֵלֶּה שְׁמוֹתָם לְמַטֵּה רְאוּבֵן שַׁמּוּעַ בֶּן זַכּוּר׃
verses.english: And these are their names: For the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur.

tex.original: \hP{וְאֵלֶּה שְׁמוֹתָם לְמַטֵּה רְאוּבֵן שַׁמּוּעַ בֶּן זַכּוּר׃}

verses.original: לְמַטֵּה שִׁמְעוֹן שָׁפָט בֶּן חוֹרִי׃
verses.english: For the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori.

tex.original: \hP{לְמַטֵּה שִׁמְעוֹן שָׁפָט בֶּן חוֹרִי׃}
tex.english: \eP{For the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori. }

verses.original: לְמַטֵּה יְהוּדָה כָּלֵב בֶּן יְפֻנֶּה׃
verses.english: For the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh.

tex.original: \hP{לְמַטֵּה יְהוּדָה כָּלֵב בֶּן יְפֻנֶּה׃}
tex.english: \eP{For the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh. }

verses.original: לְמַטֵּה יִשָּׂשכָר יִגְאָל בֶּן יוֹסֵף׃
verses.english: For the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph.

tex.original: \hP{לְמַטֵּה יִשָּׂשכָר יִגְאָל בֶּן יוֹסֵף׃}
tex.english: \eP{For the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph. }

verses.original: לְמַטֵּה אֶפְרָיִם הוֹשֵׁעַ בִּן נוּן׃
verses.english: For the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun.

tex.original: \hP{לְמַטֵּה אֶפְרָיִם הוֹשֵׁעַ בִּן נוּן׃}
tex.english: \eP{For the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun. }

verses.original: לְמַטֵּה בִנְיָמִן פַּלְטִי בֶּן רָפוּא׃
verses.english: For the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu.

tex.original: \hP{לְמַטֵּה בִנְיָמִן פַּלְטִי בֶּן רָפוּא׃}
tex.english: \eP{For the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu. }

verses.original: לְמַטֵּה זְבוּלֻן גַּדִּיאֵל בֶּן סוֹדִי׃
verses.english: For the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi.

tex.original: \hP{לְמַטֵּה זְבוּלֻן גַּדִּיאֵל בֶּן סוֹדִי׃}
tex.english: \eP{For the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi. }

verses.original: לְמַטֵּה יוֹסֵף לְמַטֵּה מְנַשֶּׁה גַּדִּי בֶּן סוּסִי׃
verses.english: For the tribe of Joseph: of the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi.

tex.original: \hP{לְמַטֵּה יוֹסֵף לְמַטֵּה מְנַשֶּׁה גַּדִּי בֶּן סוּסִי׃}

verses.original: לְמַטֵּה דָן עַמִּיאֵל בֶּן גְּמַלִּי׃
verses.english: For the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli.

tex.original: \hP{לְמַטֵּה דָן עַמִּיאֵל בֶּן גְּמַלִּי׃}
tex.english: \eP{For the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli. }

verses.original: לְמַטֵּה אָשֵׁר סְתוּר בֶּן מִיכָאֵל׃
verses.english: For the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael.

tex.original: \hP{לְמַטֵּה אָשֵׁר סְתוּר בֶּן מִיכָאֵל׃}
tex.english: \eP{For the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael. }

verses.original: לְמַטֵּה נַפְתָּלִי נַחְבִּי בֶּן ופְסִי׃
verses.english: For the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi.

tex.original: \hP{לְמַטֵּה נַפְתָּלִי נַחְבִּי בֶּן ופְסִי׃}
tex.english: \eP{For the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi. }

verses.original: לְמַטֵּה גָד גְּאוּאֵל בֶּן מָכִי׃
verses.english: For the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.

tex.original: \hP{לְמַטֵּה גָד גְּאוּאֵל בֶּן מָכִי׃}
tex.english: \eP{For the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi. }

verses.original: אֵלֶּה שְׁמוֹת הָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַח מֹשֶׁה לָתוּר אֶת הָאָרֶץ וַיִּקְרָא מֹשֶׁה לְהוֹשֵׁעַ בִּן נוּן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ׃
verses.english: These are the names of the men whom Moses sent to scout the land. And Moses called Hoshea son of Nun Joshua.

tex.original: \hP{אֵלֶּה שְׁמוֹת הָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַח מֹשֶׁה לָתוּר אֶת הָאָרֶץ וַיִּקְרָא מֹשֶׁה לְהוֹשֵׁעַ בִּן נוּן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח אֹתָם מֹשֶׁה לָתוּר אֶת אֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵהֶם עֲלוּ זֶה בַּנֶּגֶב וַעֲלִיתֶם אֶת הָהָר׃
verses.english: And Moses sent them to scout the land of Canaan. And he said to them, “Go up there in the Negeb, and you shall go up the mountain

tex.original:
\hR{וַיִּשְׁלַח אֹתָם מֹשֶׁה לָתוּר אֶת אֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן}
	\hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵהֶם עֲלוּ זֶה בַּנֶּגֶב וַעֲלִיתֶם אֶת הָהָר׃}

verses.original: וּרְאִיתֶם אֶת הָאָרֶץ מַה הִוא וְאֶת הָעָם הַיֹּשֵׁב עָלֶיהָ הֶחָזָק הוּא הֲרָפֶה הַמְעַט הוּא אִם רָב׃
verses.english: and see the land, how it is; and the people who live on it, are they strong or weak, are they few or many;

tex.original: \hJ{וּרְאִיתֶם אֶת הָאָרֶץ מַה הִוא וְאֶת הָעָם הַיֹּשֵׁב עָלֶיהָ הֶחָזָק הוּא הֲרָפֶה הַמְעַט הוּא אִם רָב׃}

verses.original: וּמָה הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר הוּא יֹשֵׁב בָּהּ הֲטוֹבָה הִוא אִם רָעָה וּמָה הֶעָרִים אֲשֶׁר הוּא יוֹשֵׁב בָּהֵנָּה הַבְּמַחֲנִים אִם בְּמִבְצָרִים׃
verses.english: and how is the land in which they live, is it good or bad; and how are the cities in which they live, are they in camps or in fortified places;

tex.original: \hJ{וּמָה הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר הוּא יֹשֵׁב בָּהּ הֲטוֹבָה הִוא אִם רָעָה וּמָה הֶעָרִים אֲשֶׁר הוּא יוֹשֵׁב בָּהֵנָּה הַבְּמַחֲנִים אִם בְּמִבְצָרִים׃}

verses.original: וּמָה הָאָרֶץ הַשְּׁמֵנָה הִוא אִם רָזָה הֲיֵשׁ בָּהּ עֵץ אִם אַיִן וְהִתְחַזַּקְתֶּם וּלְקַחְתֶּם מִפְּרִי הָאָרֶץ וְהַיָּמִים יְמֵי בִּכּוּרֵי עֲנָבִים׃
verses.english: and how is the land, is it fat or meager; does it have trees or not; and exert strength and take some fruit of the land.” And it was the days of the first grapes.

tex.original: \hJ{וּמָה הָאָרֶץ הַשְּׁמֵנָה הִוא אִם רָזָה הֲיֵשׁ בָּהּ עֵץ אִם אַיִן וְהִתְחַזַּקְתֶּם וּלְקַחְתֶּם מִפְּרִי הָאָרֶץ וְהַיָּמִים יְמֵי בִּכּוּרֵי עֲנָבִים׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעֲלוּ וַיָּתֻרוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ מִמִּדְבַּר צִן עַד רְחֹב לְבֹא חֲמָת׃
verses.english: And they went up and scouted the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob at the entrance of Hamath.

tex.original: \hP{וַיַּעֲלוּ וַיָּתֻרוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ מִמִּדְבַּר צִן עַד רְחֹב לְבֹא חֲמָת׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעֲלוּ בַנֶּגֶב וַיָּבֹא עַד חֶבְרוֹן וְשָׁם אֲחִימַן שֵׁשַׁי וְתַלְמַי יְלִידֵי הָעֲנָק וְחֶבְרוֹן שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים נִבְנְתָה לִפְנֵי צֹעַן מִצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: And they went up in the Negeb and came to Hebron. And Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the offspring of the giants, were there. (And Hebron was built seven years before Zoan of Egypt.)

tex.original: \hP{וַיַּעֲלוּ בַנֶּגֶב וַיָּבֹא עַד חֶבְרוֹן וְשָׁם אֲחִימַן שֵׁשַׁי וְתַלְמַי יְלִידֵי הָעֲנָק וְחֶבְרוֹן שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים נִבְנְתָה לִפְנֵי צֹעַן מִצְרָיִם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		came to Hebron. They return to a place where Abraham lived (Gen 13:18),
%		where he met the three visitors and first questioned God (Genesis 18;
%		Mamre is at Hebron), and where the patriarchs and matriarchs are buried
%		(Gen 23:19). It is also the place from which Jacob sent Joseph to find
%		his brothers, which, in a sense, initiated the sequence of events that
%		led to Israel’s being in Egypt. It is therefore, meaningful in a variety
%		of ways that the scouts are especially noted to come to Hebron. It
%		particularly symbolizes that this is a return home. It might have been
%		the perfect place to begin Israel’s return to the land, but the people’s
%		resistance will change all that.
%	}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ עַד נַחַל אֶשְׁכֹּל וַיִּכְרְתוּ מִשָּׁם זְמוֹרָה וְאֶשְׁכּוֹל עֲנָבִים אֶחָד וַיִּשָּׂאֻהוּ בַמּוֹט בִּשְׁנָיִם וּמִן הָרִמֹּנִים וּמִן הַתְּאֵנִים׃
verses.english: And they came to the Wadi Eshcol, and they cut a branch and one cluster of grapes from there—and carried it on a pole by two people—and some pomegranates and some figs.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּבֹאוּ עַד נַחַל אֶשְׁכֹּל וַיִּכְרְתוּ מִשָּׁם זְמוֹרָה וְאֶשְׁכּוֹל עֲנָבִים אֶחָד וַיִּשָּׂאֻהוּ בַמּוֹט בִּשְׁנָיִם וּמִן הָרִמֹּנִים וּמִן הַתְּאֵנִים׃}

verses.original: לַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא קָרָא נַחַל אֶשְׁכּוֹל עַל אֹדוֹת הָאֶשְׁכּוֹל אֲשֶׁר כָּרְתוּ מִשָּׁם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: That place was called Wadi Eshcol on account of the cluster that the children of Israel cut from there.

tex.original: \hJ{לַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא קָרָא נַחַל אֶשְׁכּוֹל עַל אֹדוֹת הָאֶשְׁכּוֹל אֲשֶׁר כָּרְתוּ מִשָּׁם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיָּשֻׁבוּ מִתּוּר הָאָרֶץ מִקֵּץ אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם׃
verses.english: And they came back from scouting the land at the end of forty days.

tex.original: \hP{וַיָּשֻׁבוּ מִתּוּר הָאָרֶץ מִקֵּץ אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּלְכוּ וַיָּבֹאוּ אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן וְאֶל כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל מִדְבַּר פָּארָן קָדֵשָׁה וַיָּשִׁיבוּ אֹתָם דָּבָר וְאֶת כּל הָעֵדָה וַיַּרְאוּם אֶת פְּרִי הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.english: And they went and came to Moses and to Aaron and to all the congregation of the children of Israel, to the wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh; and they brought back word to them and all the congregation and showed them the land’s fruit.

tex.original: \hP{וַיֵּלְכוּ וַיָּבֹאוּ אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן וְאֶל כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל מִדְבַּר פָּארָן קָדֵשָׁה וַיָּשִׁיבוּ אֹתָם דָּבָר וְאֶת כּל הָעֵדָה וַיַּרְאוּם אֶת פְּרִי הָאָרֶץ׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And they went and came to Moses and to Aaron and to all
		the congregation of the children of Israel, to the
		wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh; and they brought back word
		to them and all the congregation and showed them the
		land’s fruit.
	}

verses.original: וַיְסַפְּרוּ לוֹ וַיֹּאמְרוּ בָּאנוּ אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר שְׁלַחְתָּנוּ וְגַם זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבַשׁ הִוא וְזֶה פִּרְיָהּ׃
verses.english: And they told him and said, “We came to the land where you sent us, and also it’s flowing with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְסַפְּרוּ לוֹ וַיֹּאמְרוּ בָּאנוּ אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר שְׁלַחְתָּנוּ וְגַם זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבַשׁ הִוא וְזֶה פִּרְיָהּ׃}

verses.original: אֶפֶס כִּי עַז הָעָם הַיֹּשֵׁב בָּאָרֶץ וְהֶעָרִים בְּצֻרוֹת גְּדֹלֹת מְאֹד וְגַם יְלִדֵי הָעֲנָק רָאִינוּ שָׁם׃
verses.english: Nonetheless: the people who live in the land are strong. And the cities are fortified, very big. And also we saw the offspring of the giants there.

tex.original: \hJ{אֶפֶס כִּי עַז הָעָם הַיֹּשֵׁב בָּאָרֶץ וְהֶעָרִים בְּצֻרוֹת גְּדֹלֹת מְאֹד וְגַם יְלִדֵי הָעֲנָק רָאִינוּ שָׁם׃}

verses.original: עֲמָלֵק יוֹשֵׁב בְּאֶרֶץ הַנֶּגֶב וְהַחִתִּי וְהַיְבוּסִי וְהָאֱמֹרִי יוֹשֵׁב בָּהָר וְהַכְּנַעֲנִי יוֹשֵׁב עַל הַיָּם וְעַל יַד הַיַּרְדֵּן׃
verses.english: Amalek lives in the land of the Negeb, and the Hittite and the Jebusite and the Amorite live in the mountains, and the Canaanite lives by the sea and along the Jordan.”

tex.original: \hJ{עֲמָלֵק יוֹשֵׁב בְּאֶרֶץ הַנֶּגֶב וְהַחִתִּי וְהַיְבוּסִי וְהָאֱמֹרִי יוֹשֵׁב בָּהָר וְהַכְּנַעֲנִי יוֹשֵׁב עַל הַיָּם וְעַל יַד הַיַּרְדֵּן׃}

verses.original: וַיַּהַס כָּלֵב אֶת הָעָם אֶל מֹשֶׁה וַיֹּאמֶר עָלֹה נַעֲלֶה וְיָרַשְׁנוּ אֹתָהּ כִּי יָכוֹל נוּכַל לָהּ׃
verses.english: And Caleb quieted the people toward Moses and said, “Let’s go up, and we’ll take possession of it, because we’ll be able to handle it.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּהַס כָּלֵב אֶת הָעָם אֶל מֹשֶׁה וַיֹּאמֶר עָלֹה נַעֲלֶה וְיָרַשְׁנוּ אֹתָהּ כִּי יָכוֹל נוּכַל לָהּ׃}

verses.original: וְהָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר עָלוּ עִמּוֹ אָמְרוּ לֹא נוּכַל לַעֲלוֹת אֶל הָעָם כִּי חָזָק הוּא מִמֶּנּוּ׃
verses.english: And the men who went up with him said, “We won’t be able to go up against the people, because they’re stronger than we are.”

tex.original: \hJ{וְהָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר עָלוּ עִמּוֹ אָמְרוּ לֹא נוּכַל לַעֲלוֹת אֶל הָעָם כִּי חָזָק הוּא מִמֶּנּוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּצִיאוּ דִּבַּת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר תָּרוּ אֹתָהּ אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר עָבַרְנוּ בָהּ לָתוּר אֹתָהּ אֶרֶץ אֹכֶלֶת יוֹשְׁבֶיהָ הִוא וְכל הָעָם אֲשֶׁר רָאִינוּ בְתוֹכָהּ אַנְשֵׁי מִדּוֹת׃
verses.english: And they brought out a report of the land that they had scouted to the children of Israel, saying, “The land through which we passed to scout it: it’s a land that eats those who live in it, and all the people whom we saw in it were people of size!

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּצִיאוּ דִּבַּת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר תָּרוּ אֹתָהּ אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר עָבַרְנוּ בָהּ לָתוּר אֹתָהּ אֶרֶץ אֹכֶלֶת יוֹשְׁבֶיהָ הִוא וְכל הָעָם אֲשֶׁר רָאִינוּ בְתוֹכָהּ אַנְשֵׁי מִדּוֹת׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And they brought out a report of the land that they had
		scouted to the children of Israel, saying, “The land
		through which we passed to scout it: it’s a land that eats
		those who live in it, and all the people whom we saw in it
		were people of size!
	}

verses.original: וְשָׁם רָאִינוּ אֶת הַנְּפִילִים בְּנֵי עֲנָק מִן הַנְּפִלִים וַנְּהִי בְעֵינֵינוּ כַּחֲגָבִים וְכֵן הָיִינוּ בְּעֵינֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: And we saw the Nephilim there, sons of giants from the Nephilim, and we were like grasshoppers in our eyes, and so were we in their eyes.”

tex.original: \hJ{וְשָׁם רָאִינוּ אֶת הַנְּפִילִים בְּנֵי עֲנָק מִן הַנְּפִלִים וַנְּהִי בְעֵינֵינוּ כַּחֲגָבִים וְכֵן הָיִינוּ בְּעֵינֵיהֶם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		sons of giants from the Nephilim. The huge creatures known as the
%		Nephilim come up in a chain of references that are spread far apart
%		through several books of the Tanak. Their origin is explained near the
%		beginning of the Torah, in the story of the “sons of God” who have
%		relations with human women who then give birth to giants (Gen 6:1–4).
%		Now in the spies episode, the Israelite spies see the descendants of
%		these giants (Numbers 13). Later, Joshua eliminates the giants from all
%		of the land except from the Philistine cities, including Gath (Josh
%		11:21–22). And later still, the Philistine giant Goliath comes from Gath
%		(1 Sam 17:4). These widespread references are among the many stitches
%		that bind the Tanak together as a continuing story. Those who see the
%		Bible as a loose collection of stories fail to take proper account of
%		the substantial number of such widely distributed binding elements.
%	}

verses.original: וַתִּשָּׂא כּל הָעֵדָה וַיִּתְּנוּ אֶת קוֹלָם וַיִּבְכּוּ הָעָם בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא׃
verses.english: And all the congregation raised and let out their voices! And the people wept that night.

tex.original:
\hP{וַתִּשָּׂא כּל הָעֵדָה וַיִּתְּנוּ אֶת קוֹלָם}
	\hJ{וַיִּבְכּוּ הָעָם בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא׃}
tex.english:
\eP{And all the congregation raised and let out their voices!}
	\eJ{And the people wept that night.}

verses.original: וַיִּלֹּנוּ עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעַל אַהֲרֹן כֹּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֲלֵהֶם כּל הָעֵדָה לוּ מַתְנוּ בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם אוֹ בַּמִּדְבָּר הַזֶּה לוּ מָתְנוּ׃
verses.english: And all the children of Israel complained at Moses and at Aaron, and all the congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Egypt! Or in this wilderness, if only we had died!

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּלֹּנוּ עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעַל אַהֲרֹן כֹּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֲלֵהֶם כּל הָעֵדָה לוּ מַתְנוּ בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם אוֹ בַּמִּדְבָּר הַזֶּה לוּ מָתְנוּ׃}

verses.original: וְלָמָה יְהֹוָה מֵבִיא אֹתָנוּ אֶל הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת לִנְפֹּל בַּחֶרֶב נָשֵׁינוּ וְטַפֵּנוּ יִהְיוּ לָבַז הֲלוֹא טוֹב לָנוּ שׁוּב מִצְרָיְמָה׃
verses.english: And why is YHWH bringing us to this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and our infants will become a spoil! Isn’t it better for us to go back to Egypt?”

tex.original: \hP{וְלָמָה יְהֹוָה מֵבִיא אֹתָנוּ אֶל הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת לִנְפֹּל בַּחֶרֶב נָשֵׁינוּ וְטַפֵּנוּ יִהְיוּ לָבַז הֲלוֹא טוֹב לָנוּ שׁוּב מִצְרָיְמָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ אִישׁ אֶל אָחִיו נִתְּנָה רֹאשׁ וְנָשׁוּבָה מִצְרָיְמָה׃
verses.english: And they said, each man to his brother, “Let’s appoint a chief and go back to Egypt.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמְרוּ אִישׁ אֶל אָחִיו נִתְּנָה רֹאשׁ וְנָשׁוּבָה מִצְרָיְמָה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּפֹּל מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן עַל פְּנֵיהֶם לִפְנֵי כּל קְהַל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And Moses and Aaron fell on their faces in front of all the community of the congregation of the children of Israel.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּפֹּל מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן עַל פְּנֵיהֶם לִפְנֵי כּל קְהַל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן וְכָלֵב בֶּן יְפֻנֶּה מִן הַתָּרִים אֶת הָאָרֶץ קָרְעוּ בִּגְדֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: And Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, from those who had scouted the land, had torn their clothes.

tex.original: \hP{וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן וְכָלֵב בֶּן יְפֻנֶּה מִן הַתָּרִים אֶת הָאָרֶץ קָרְעוּ בִּגְדֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֶל כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר עָבַרְנוּ בָהּ לָתוּר אֹתָהּ טוֹבָה הָאָרֶץ מְאֹד מְאֹד׃
verses.english: And they said to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, “The land through which we passed to scout it: the land is very, very good!

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֶל כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר עָבַרְנוּ בָהּ לָתוּר אֹתָהּ טוֹבָה הָאָרֶץ מְאֹד מְאֹד׃}

verses.original: אִם חָפֵץ בָּנוּ יְהֹוָה וְהֵבִיא אֹתָנוּ אֶל הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת וּנְתָנָהּ לָנוּ אֶרֶץ אֲשֶׁר הִוא זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ׃
verses.english: If YHWH desires us, then He’ll bring us to this land and give it to us, a land that flows with milk and honey!

tex.original: \hP{אִם חָפֵץ בָּנוּ יְהֹוָה וְהֵבִיא אֹתָנוּ אֶל הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת וּנְתָנָהּ לָנוּ אֶרֶץ אֲשֶׁר הִוא זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ׃}

verses.original: אַךְ בַּיהֹוָה אַל תִּמְרֹדוּ וְאַתֶּם אַל תִּירְאוּ אֶת עַם הָאָרֶץ כִּי לַחְמֵנוּ הֵם סָר צִלָּם מֵעֲלֵיהֶם וַיהֹוָה אִתָּנוּ אַל תִּירָאֻם׃
verses.english: Just don’t revolt against YHWH. And you, don’t fear the people of the land, because they’re our bread! Their protection has turned from them, while YHWH is with us. Don’t fear them.”

tex.original: \hP{אַךְ בַּיהֹוָה אַל תִּמְרֹדוּ וְאַתֶּם אַל תִּירְאוּ אֶת עַם הָאָרֶץ כִּי לַחְמֵנוּ הֵם סָר צִלָּם מֵעֲלֵיהֶם וַיהֹוָה אִתָּנוּ אַל תִּירָאֻם׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ כּל הָעֵדָה לִרְגּוֹם אֹתָם בָּאֲבָנִים וּכְבוֹד יְהֹוָה נִרְאָה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֶל כּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And all the congregation said to batter them with stones. And YHWH’s glory appeared at the Tent of Meeting to all the children of Israel!

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמְרוּ כּל הָעֵדָה לִרְגּוֹם אֹתָם בָּאֲבָנִים וּכְבוֹד יְהֹוָה נִרְאָה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֶל כּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה עַד אָנָה יְנַאֲצֻנִי הָעָם הַזֶּה וְעַד אָנָה לֹא יַאֲמִינוּ בִי בְּכֹל הָאֹתוֹת אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי בְּקִרְבּוֹ׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “How long will this people reject me, and how long will they not trust in me, with all the signs that I’ve done among them?

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה עַד אָנָה יְנַאֲצֻנִי הָעָם הַזֶּה וְעַד אָנָה לֹא יַאֲמִינוּ בִי בְּכֹל הָאֹתוֹת אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי בְּקִרְבּוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		how long will they not trust in me, with all the signs that I’ve done
%		among them? Why in fact do the people not trust? Why are they still
%		afraid and doubtful? They have seen their God handle Egypt, the major
%		power of the world. Why would they doubt that He can handle the
%		Canaanites? They have seen Him manipulate the whole of nature with the
%		ten plagues and the splitting of the sea. They have seen water come from
%		a mountain crag. They have heard God’s voice from the sky at Sinai. They
%		are eating miraculous manna every day. They have just miraculously been
%		provided with quail to eat. Even as they complain in this moment, there
%		is a miraculous column of cloud and fire right in front of them. Why are
%		they afraid? Recall that the reason they are directed to the Red Sea
%		when they leave Egypt, rather than through Philistine territory, is that
%		YHWH is concerned that they will be afraid of facing war with the
%		Philistines. As I commented there (Exod 13:18), the Red Sea required no
%		decisions or action on their part, but facing the Philistines would have
%		required them to take up arms. Likewise, in every case so far, from the
%		plagues to the quail, God and Moses have acted for them, and they have
%		had to do very little. Even in the battle against the Amalekites, it was
%		the Amalekites who attacked them, and then Joshua chose a select group
%		to fight on their behalf (Exod 17:8–13). But now, for the first time,
%		the people perceive that they will have to act. The scouts speak in
%		terms of the people of Israel themselves having to fight: “We won’t be
%		able to go up against the people, because they’re stronger than we are”
%		(13:31). The scouts do not even mention God. What was true when they
%		left Egypt is still true: They are still slaves in their hearts. They
%		are not yet capable of independence, responsibility, or action. And so
%		God’s decision is precisely to leave the entry into the land for their
%		children. See the comment on Num 14:29.
%	}

verses.original: אַכֶּנּוּ בַדֶּבֶר וְאוֹרִשֶׁנּוּ וְאֶעֱשֶׂה אֹתְךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל וְעָצוּם מִמֶּנּוּ׃
verses.english: I’ll strike them with an epidemic and dispossess them, and I’ll make you into a bigger and more powerful nation than they are.”

tex.original: \hJ{אַכֶּנּוּ בַדֶּבֶר וְאוֹרִשֶׁנּוּ וְאֶעֱשֶׂה אֹתְךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל וְעָצוּם מִמֶּנּוּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		I’ll make you. The Septuagint and Samaritan texts have “I’ll make you
%		and your father’s house.” The extra words appear to have been lost by
%		haplography. (That is, in the Hebrew, the word for “make you” and the
%		phrase for “your father’s house” both end in the same letter, kaf, so a
%		scribe’s eye skipped from one kap to the next and left out the words in
%		between.) The addition of the reference to Moses’ father’s house may
%		suggest that Aaron’s family is to be spared as well, or it may mean more
%		broadly that the Levites as a whole are to survive. Alternatively, it
%		may still mean that only Moses is to survive to start over a new people,
%		but it is still described as the survival of his father’s house because
%		God’s relationship with Moses has focused on that link from the
%		beginning—God’s self-introduction to Moses at the bush is: “I am your
%		father’s God” (Exod 3:6).
%	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל יְהֹוָה וְשָׁמְעוּ מִצְרַיִם כִּי הֶעֱלִיתָ בְכֹחֲךָ אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה מִקִּרְבּוֹ׃
verses.english: And Moses said to YHWH, “And Egypt will hear it, for you brought this people up from among them with your power,

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל יְהֹוָה וְשָׁמְעוּ מִצְרַיִם כִּי הֶעֱלִיתָ בְכֹחֲךָ אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה מִקִּרְבּוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְאָמְרוּ אֶל יוֹשֵׁב הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת שָׁמְעוּ כִּי אַתָּה יְהֹוָה בְּקֶרֶב הָעָם הַזֶּה אֲשֶׁר עַיִן בְּעַיִן נִרְאָה אַתָּה יְהֹוָה וַעֲנָנְךָ עֹמֵד עֲלֵהֶם וּבְעַמֻּד עָנָן אַתָּה הֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵיהֶם יוֹמָם וּבְעַמּוּד אֵשׁ לָיְלָה׃
verses.english: and they’ll say it to those who live in this land. They’ve heard that you, YHWH, are among this people; that you, YHWH, have appeared eye-to-eye; and your cloud stands over them; and you go in front of them in a column of cloud by day and in a column of fire by night.

tex.original: \hJ{וְאָמְרוּ אֶל יוֹשֵׁב הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת שָׁמְעוּ כִּי אַתָּה יְהֹוָה בְּקֶרֶב הָעָם הַזֶּה אֲשֶׁר עַיִן בְּעַיִן נִרְאָה אַתָּה יְהֹוָה וַעֲנָנְךָ עֹמֵד עֲלֵהֶם וּבְעַמֻּד עָנָן אַתָּה הֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵיהֶם יוֹמָם וּבְעַמּוּד אֵשׁ לָיְלָה׃}
tex.english:
\eJ{
		and they’ll say it to those who live in this land. They’ve
		heard that you, YHWH, are among this people; that you,
		YHWH, have appeared eye-to-eye; and your cloud stands over
		them; and you go in front of them in a column of cloud by
		day and in a column of fire by night.
	}

verses.original: וְהֵמַתָּה אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד וְאָמְרוּ הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר שָׁמְעוּ אֶת שִׁמְעֲךָ לֵאמֹר׃
verses.english: And if you kill this people as one man, then the nations that have heard about you will say it, saying,

tex.original: \hJ{וְהֵמַתָּה אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד וְאָמְרוּ הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר שָׁמְעוּ אֶת שִׁמְעֲךָ לֵאמֹר׃}

verses.original: מִבִּלְתִּי יְכֹלֶת יְהֹוָה לְהָבִיא אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע לָהֶם וַיִּשְׁחָטֵם בַּמִּדְבָּר׃
verses.english: ‘Because YHWH wasn’t able to bring this people to the land that He swore to them, He slaughtered them in the wilderness.’

tex.original: \hJ{מִבִּלְתִּי יְכֹלֶת יְהֹוָה לְהָבִיא אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע לָהֶם וַיִּשְׁחָטֵם בַּמִּדְבָּר׃}

verses.original: וְעַתָּה יִגְדַּל נָא כֹּחַ אֲדֹנָי כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתָּ לֵאמֹר׃
verses.english: And now, let my Lord’s power be big, as you spoke, saying,

tex.original: \hJ{וְעַתָּה יִגְדַּל נָא כֹּחַ אֲדֹנָי כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתָּ לֵאמֹר׃}

verses.original: יְהֹוָה אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וְרַב חֶסֶד נֹשֵׂא עָוֺן וָפָשַׁע וְנַקֵּה לֹא יְנַקֶּה פֹּקֵד עֲוֺן אָבוֹת עַל בָּנִים עַל שִׁלֵּשִׁים וְעַל רִבֵּעִים׃
verses.english: ‘YHWH is slow to anger and abounding in kindness, bearing crime and offense; though not making one innocent: reckoning fathers’ crime on children, on third generations and on fourth generations.’

tex.original: \hJ{יְהֹוָה אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וְרַב חֶסֶד נֹשֵׂא עָוֺן וָפָשַׁע וְנַקֵּה לֹא יְנַקֶּה פֹּקֵד עֲוֺן אָבוֹת עַל בָּנִים עַל שִׁלֵּשִׁים וְעַל רִבֵּעִים׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		slow to anger … Moses quotes God’s own words from the moment of the
%		great revelation, when Moses saw God at Sinai (Exod 34:6–7). So he is
%		not only appealing to God’s mercy; he is citing God’s own description of
%		Himself as if to say that God must be true to Himself. Footnote 14:18.
%		on children, on third generations and on fourth generations. The passage
%		that Moses is quoting says: “on children and on children’s children, on
%		third generations and on fourth generations” (Exod 34:7). It looks like
%		“and on children’s children” has been lost, presumably by another
%		haplography: a scribe’s eye skipped from one occurrence of the word
%		“children” to the next. It is the easiest kind of scribal error to make,
%		and in fact this same omission occurs in the Ten Commandments (Exod 20:5
%		and Deut 5:9). As a less banal and more homiletical explanation of this
%		case, we might suggest that the text pictures Moses as shortening the
%		long formula so as to keep focused on the larger point. Or perhaps, by
%		leaving it out, he subtly presses God to make the correction and thus to
%		be reminded of the extent of His compassion according to His own words.
%		Deliberately misquoting someone may actually be an effective tool of
%		persuasion.
%	}

verses.original: סְלַח נָא לַעֲוֺן הָעָם הַזֶּה כְּגֹדֶל חַסְדֶּךָ וְכַאֲשֶׁר נָשָׂאתָה לָעָם הַזֶּה מִמִּצְרַיִם וְעַד הֵנָּה׃
verses.english: Forgive this people’s crime in proportion to the magnitude of your kindness and as you’ve borne this people from Egypt to here.”

tex.original: \hJ{סְלַח נָא לַעֲוֺן הָעָם הַזֶּה כְּגֹדֶל חַסְדֶּךָ וְכַאֲשֶׁר נָשָׂאתָה לָעָם הַזֶּה מִמִּצְרַיִם וְעַד הֵנָּה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה סָלַחְתִּי כִּדְבָרֶךָ׃
verses.english: And YHWH said, “I’ve forgiven according to your word.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה סָלַחְתִּי כִּדְבָרֶךָ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		I’ve forgiven according to your word. Abraham questioned God regarding
%		Sodom and Gomorrah, but his conversation did not change anything. Ten
%		virtuous persons were not found, and the cities were destroyed. But
%		Moses is pictured as actually making a difference in a divine decision
%		and in the fate of the people. This is another case in which there is
%		growth in the human stance relative to God.
%	}

verses.original: וְאוּלָם חַי אָנִי וְיִמָּלֵא כְבוֹד יְהֹוָה אֶת כּל הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.english: But indeed, as I live, and as YHWH’s glory has filled all the earth,

tex.original: \hJ{וְאוּלָם חַי אָנִי וְיִמָּלֵא כְבוֹד יְהֹוָה אֶת כּל הָאָרֶץ׃}

verses.original: כִּי כל הָאֲנָשִׁים הָרֹאִים אֶת כְּבֹדִי וְאֶת אֹתֹתַי אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי בְמִצְרַיִם וּבַמִּדְבָּר וַיְנַסּוּ אֹתִי זֶה עֶשֶׂר פְּעָמִים וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ בְּקוֹלִי׃
verses.english: I swear that all of these people, who have seen my glory and my signs that I did in Egypt and in the wilderness and who have tested me ten times now and haven’t listened to my voice,

tex.original: \hJ{כִּי כל הָאֲנָשִׁים הָרֹאִים אֶת כְּבֹדִי וְאֶת אֹתֹתַי אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי בְמִצְרַיִם וּבַמִּדְבָּר וַיְנַסּוּ אֹתִי זֶה עֶשֶׂר פְּעָמִים וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ בְּקוֹלִי׃}

verses.original: אִם יִרְאוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי לַאֲבֹתָם וְכל מְנַאֲצַי לֹא יִרְאוּהָ׃
verses.english: won’t see the land that I swore to their fathers, and all those who rejected me won’t see it.

tex.original: \hJ{אִם יִרְאוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי לַאֲבֹתָם וְכל מְנַאֲצַי לֹא יִרְאוּהָ׃}

verses.original: וְעַבְדִּי כָלֵב עֵקֶב הָיְתָה רוּחַ אַחֶרֶת עִמּוֹ וַיְמַלֵּא אַחֲרָי וַהֲבִיאֹתִיו אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר בָּא שָׁמָּה וְזַרְעוֹ יוֹרִשֶׁנָּה׃
verses.english: And my servant Caleb, because a different spirit was with him, and he went after me completely, I’ll bring him to the land where he went, and his seed will possess it.

tex.original: \hJ{וְעַבְדִּי כָלֵב עֵקֶב הָיְתָה רוּחַ אַחֶרֶת עִמּוֹ וַיְמַלֵּא אַחֲרָי וַהֲבִיאֹתִיו אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר בָּא שָׁמָּה וְזַרְעוֹ יוֹרִשֶׁנָּה׃}

verses.original: וְהָעֲמָלֵקִי וְהַכְּנַעֲנִי יוֹשֵׁב בָּעֵמֶק מָחָר פְּנוּ וּסְעוּ לָכֶם הַמִּדְבָּר דֶּרֶךְ יַם סוּף׃
verses.english: And the Amalekite and the Canaanite live in the valley. Turn and travel tomorrow to the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.”

tex.original: \hJ{וְהָעֲמָלֵקִי וְהַכְּנַעֲנִי יוֹשֵׁב בָּעֵמֶק מָחָר פְּנוּ וּסְעוּ לָכֶם הַמִּדְבָּר דֶּרֶךְ יַם סוּף׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן לֵאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן לֵאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,}

verses.original: עַד מָתַי לָעֵדָה הָרָעָה הַזֹּאת אֲשֶׁר הֵמָּה מַלִּינִים עָלָי אֶת תְּלֻנּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר הֵמָּה מַלִּינִים עָלַי שָׁמָעְתִּי׃
verses.english: “How much further for this bad congregation, that they’re complaining against me? I’ve heard the complaints of the children of Israel that they’re making against me.

tex.original: \hP{עַד מָתַי לָעֵדָה הָרָעָה הַזֹּאת אֲשֶׁר הֵמָּה מַלִּינִים עָלָי אֶת תְּלֻנּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר הֵמָּה מַלִּינִים עָלַי שָׁמָעְתִּי׃}

verses.original: אֱמֹר אֲלֵהֶם חַי אָנִי נְאֻם יְהֹוָה אִם לֹא כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתֶּם בְּאזְנָי כֵּן אֶעֱשֶׂה לָכֶם׃
verses.english: Say to them: As I live—word of YHWH—what you have spoken in my ears, that is what I’ll do to you!

tex.original: \hP{אֱמֹר אֲלֵהֶם חַי אָנִי נְאֻם יְהֹוָה אִם לֹא כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתֶּם בְּאזְנָי כֵּן אֶעֱשֶׂה לָכֶם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		what you have spoken in my ears, that is what I’ll do to you! Another
%		case of ironic divine punishment to suit the crime: They could have had
%		the land and lived, but they were afraid and said that they would die
%		and their children would be made captives. So now they will in fact die,
%		but their children will live and one day be free in the land. This is
%		the most dramatic demonstration yet of the people’s persistent slave
%		mentality. God says that He has forgiven them, and they are not stricken
%		with an epidemic as God had originally said; but they are also not ready
%		for the life of free people in a land of their own. And so this is left
%		for their children, who grow up not knowing the experience of having
%		been slaves. An entire generation’s experience is not easily reversed.
%		In our own age we see the impact on the lives of survivors of the
%		holocaust. Some become more religious, some reject religion. Some cannot
%		speak of it, and some speak of it constantly. Some return to the sites
%		where they suffered, and some will never go back. It affects their
%		medical decisions, their ways of raising their children, their trust of
%		other human beings, their work, their thoughts, their opinions, and
%		their memories. Their children carry tremendous loads of guilt and
%		obligation, but they have a chance of knowing a kind of freedom that
%		their parents cannot know.
%	}

verses.original: בַּמִּדְבָּר הַזֶּה יִפְּלוּ פִגְרֵיכֶם וְכל פְּקֻדֵיכֶם לְכל מִסְפַּרְכֶם מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וָמָעְלָה אֲשֶׁר הֲלִינֹתֶם עָלָי׃
verses.english: In this wilderness your carcasses will fall; and all of you who were counted, for all your number, from twenty years old and up, who complained against me,

tex.original: \hP{בַּמִּדְבָּר הַזֶּה יִפְּלוּ פִגְרֵיכֶם וְכל פְּקֻדֵיכֶם לְכל מִסְפַּרְכֶם מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וָמָעְלָה אֲשֶׁר הֲלִינֹתֶם עָלָי׃}

verses.original: אִם אַתֶּם תָּבֹאוּ אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נָשָׂאתִי אֶת יָדִי לְשַׁכֵּן אֶתְכֶם בָּהּ כִּי אִם כָּלֵב בֶּן יְפֻנֶּה וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן׃
verses.english: I swear that you won’t come to the land that I raised my hand to have you reside there—except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

tex.original: \hP{אִם אַתֶּם תָּבֹאוּ אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נָשָׂאתִי אֶת יָדִי לְשַׁכֵּן אֶתְכֶם בָּהּ כִּי אִם כָּלֵב בֶּן יְפֻנֶּה וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן׃}

verses.original: וְטַפְּכֶם אֲשֶׁר אֲמַרְתֶּם לָבַז יִהְיֶה וְהֵבֵיאתִי אֹתָם וְיָדְעוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר מְאַסְתֶּם בָּהּ׃
verses.english: And your infants, whom you said would become a spoil: I’ll bring them, and they will know the land that you rejected!

tex.original: \hP{וְטַפְּכֶם אֲשֶׁר אֲמַרְתֶּם לָבַז יִהְיֶה וְהֵבֵיאתִי אֹתָם וְיָדְעוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר מְאַסְתֶּם בָּהּ׃}

verses.original: וּפִגְרֵיכֶם אַתֶּם יִפְּלוּ בַּמִּדְבָּר הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: And you: your carcasses will fall in this wilderness.

tex.original: \hP{וּפִגְרֵיכֶם אַתֶּם יִפְּלוּ בַּמִּדְבָּר הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: וּבְנֵיכֶם יִהְיוּ רֹעִים בַּמִּדְבָּר אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה וְנָשְׂאוּ אֶת זְנוּתֵיכֶם עַד תֹּם פִּגְרֵיכֶם בַּמִּדְבָּר׃
verses.english: And your children will be roving in the wilderness forty years, and they’ll bear your whoring until the end of your carcasses in the wilderness.

tex.original: \hP{וּבְנֵיכֶם יִהְיוּ רֹעִים בַּמִּדְבָּר אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה וְנָשְׂאוּ אֶת זְנוּתֵיכֶם עַד תֹּם פִּגְרֵיכֶם בַּמִּדְבָּר׃}

verses.original: בְּמִסְפַּר הַיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר תַּרְתֶּם אֶת הָאָרֶץ אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם יוֹם לַשָּׁנָה יוֹם לַשָּׁנָה תִּשְׂאוּ אֶת עֲוֺנֹתֵיכֶם אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה וִידַעְתֶּם אֶת תְּנוּאָתִי׃
verses.english: For the number of days that you scouted the land, forty days, you shall bear your crimes a day for each year, forty years, and you shall know my frustration!

tex.original: \hP{בְּמִסְפַּר הַיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר תַּרְתֶּם אֶת הָאָרֶץ אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם יוֹם לַשָּׁנָה יוֹם לַשָּׁנָה תִּשְׂאוּ אֶת עֲוֺנֹתֵיכֶם אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה וִידַעְתֶּם אֶת תְּנוּאָתִי׃}

verses.original: אֲנִי יְהֹוָה דִּבַּרְתִּי אִם לֹא זֹאת אֶעֱשֶׂה לְכל הָעֵדָה הָרָעָה הַזֹּאת הַנּוֹעָדִים עָלָי בַּמִּדְבָּר הַזֶּה יִתַּמּוּ וְשָׁם יָמֻתוּ׃
verses.english: I, YHWH, have spoken: If I shall not do this to all this bad congregation who are gathered against me: in this wilderness they shall end, and they shall die there!”

tex.original: \hP{אֲנִי יְהֹוָה דִּבַּרְתִּי אִם לֹא זֹאת אֶעֱשֶׂה לְכל הָעֵדָה הָרָעָה הַזֹּאת הַנּוֹעָדִים עָלָי בַּמִּדְבָּר הַזֶּה יִתַּמּוּ וְשָׁם יָמֻתוּ׃}

verses.original: וְהָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַח מֹשֶׁה לָתוּר אֶת הָאָרֶץ וַיָּשֻׁבוּ (וילונו) [וַיַּלִּינוּ] עָלָיו אֶת כּל הָעֵדָה לְהוֹצִיא דִבָּה עַל הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.english: And the men whom Moses sent to scout the land and came back and caused all the congregation to complain against him, bringing out a report about the land:
verses.commentary: Qere Ketiv.

tex.original: \hP{וְהָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַח מֹשֶׁה לָתוּר אֶת הָאָרֶץ וַיָּשֻׁבוּ (וילונו) [וַיַּלִּינוּ] עָלָיו אֶת כּל הָעֵדָה לְהוֹצִיא דִבָּה עַל הָאָרֶץ׃}

verses.original: וַיָּמֻתוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים מוֹצִאֵי דִבַּת הָאָרֶץ רָעָה בַּמַּגֵּפָה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: the men who brought out the bad report of the land died in a plague in front of YHWH.

tex.original: \hP{וַיָּמֻתוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים מוֹצִאֵי דִבַּת הָאָרֶץ רָעָה בַּמַּגֵּפָה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן וְכָלֵב בֶּן יְפֻנֶּה חָיוּ מִן הָאֲנָשִׁים הָהֵם הַהֹלְכִים לָתוּר אֶת הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.english: But, out of those men who went to scout the land, Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh lived. And Moses spoke these things to all the children of Israel, and the people mourned very much.

tex.original: \hP{וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן וְכָלֵב בֶּן יְפֻנֶּה חָיוּ מִן הָאֲנָשִׁים הָהֵם הַהֹלְכִים לָתוּר אֶת הָאָרֶץ׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה אֶל כּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּתְאַבְּלוּ הָעָם מְאֹד׃
verses.english: When Moses told these words to all the Israelites, the people mourned greatly.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְדַבֵּר מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה אֶל כּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּתְאַבְּלוּ הָעָם מְאֹד׃}
tex.english: \eJ{When Moses told these words to all the Israelites, the people mourned greatly.}

verses.original: וַיַּשְׁכִּמוּ בַבֹּקֶר וַיַּעֲלוּ אֶל רֹאשׁ הָהָר לֵאמֹר הִנֶּנּוּ וְעָלִינוּ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אָמַר יְהֹוָה כִּי חָטָאנוּ׃
verses.english: And they got up in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying, “Here we are, and we’ll go up to the place that YHWH said, because we’ve sinned.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּשְׁכִּמוּ בַבֹּקֶר וַיַּעֲלוּ אֶל רֹאשׁ הָהָר לֵאמֹר הִנֶּנּוּ וְעָלִינוּ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אָמַר יְהֹוָה כִּי חָטָאנוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה לָמָּה זֶּה אַתֶּם עֹבְרִים אֶת פִּי יְהֹוָה וְהִוא לֹא תִצְלָח׃
verses.english: And Moses said, “Why are you violating YHWH’s word? And it won’t succeed.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה לָמָּה זֶּה אַתֶּם עֹבְרִים אֶת פִּי יְהֹוָה וְהִוא לֹא תִצְלָח׃}

verses.original: אַל תַּעֲלוּ כִּי אֵין יְהֹוָה בְּקִרְבְּכֶם וְלֹא תִּנָּגְפוּ לִפְנֵי אֹיְבֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: Don’t go up, so you won’t be stricken in front of your enemies, because YHWH isn’t among you.

tex.original: \hJ{אַל תַּעֲלוּ כִּי אֵין יְהֹוָה בְּקִרְבְּכֶם וְלֹא תִּנָּגְפוּ לִפְנֵי אֹיְבֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: כִּי הָעֲמָלֵקִי וְהַכְּנַעֲנִי שָׁם לִפְנֵיכֶם וּנְפַלְתֶּם בֶּחָרֶב כִּי עַל כֵּן שַׁבְתֶּם מֵאַחֲרֵי יְהֹוָה וְלֹא יִהְיֶה יְהֹוָה עִמָּכֶם׃
verses.english: Because the Amalekite and the Canaanite are there in front of you, and you’ll fall by the sword because of the fact that you’ve gone back from following YHWH, and YHWH won’t be with you.”

tex.original: \hJ{כִּי הָעֲמָלֵקִי וְהַכְּנַעֲנִי שָׁם לִפְנֵיכֶם וּנְפַלְתֶּם בֶּחָרֶב כִּי עַל כֵּן שַׁבְתֶּם מֵאַחֲרֵי יְהֹוָה וְלֹא יִהְיֶה יְהֹוָה עִמָּכֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעְפִּלוּ לַעֲלוֹת אֶל רֹאשׁ הָהָר וַאֲרוֹן בְּרִית יְהֹוָה וּמֹשֶׁה לֹא מָשׁוּ מִקֶּרֶב הַמַּחֲנֶה׃
verses.english: And they acted heedlessly, going up to the top of the mountain. And the ark of the covenant of YHWH and Moses did not draw away from the camp.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּעְפִּלוּ לַעֲלוֹת אֶל רֹאשׁ הָהָר וַאֲרוֹן בְּרִית יְהֹוָה וּמֹשֶׁה לֹא מָשׁוּ מִקֶּרֶב הַמַּחֲנֶה׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּרֶד הָעֲמָלֵקִי וְהַכְּנַעֲנִי הַיֹּשֵׁב בָּהָר הַהוּא וַיַּכּוּם וַיַּכְּתוּם עַד הַחרְמָה׃
verses.english: And the Amalekite and the Canaanite who lived in that mountain came down, and they struck them and crushed them as far as Hormah.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֵּרֶד הָעֲמָלֵקִי וְהַכְּנַעֲנִי הַיֹּשֵׁב בָּהָר הַהוּא וַיַּכּוּם וַיַּכְּתוּם עַד הַחרְמָה׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hR{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eR{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם כִּי תָבֹאוּ אֶל אֶרֶץ מוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי נֹתֵן לָכֶם׃
verses.english: “Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: When you will come to the land of your homes that I am giving to you,

tex.original: \hR{דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם כִּי תָבֹאוּ אֶל אֶרֶץ מוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי נֹתֵן לָכֶם׃}

verses.original: וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אִשֶּׁה לַיהֹוָה עֹלָה אוֹ זֶבַח לְפַלֵּא נֶדֶר אוֹ בִנְדָבָה אוֹ בְּמֹעֲדֵיכֶם לַעֲשׂוֹת רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה מִן הַבָּקָר אוֹ מִן הַצֹּאן׃
verses.english: and you will make a fire offering to YHWH, a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to express a vow or as a contribution or at your appointed times, to make a pleasant smell to YHWH from the cattle or from the flock,

tex.original: \hR{וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אִשֶּׁה לַיהֹוָה עֹלָה אוֹ זֶבַח לְפַלֵּא נֶדֶר אוֹ בִנְדָבָה אוֹ בְּמֹעֲדֵיכֶם לַעֲשׂוֹת רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה מִן הַבָּקָר אוֹ מִן הַצֹּאן׃}

verses.original: וְהִקְרִיב הַמַּקְרִיב קרְבָּנוֹ לַיהֹוָה מִנְחָה סֹלֶת עִשָּׂרוֹן בָּלוּל בִּרְבִעִית הַהִין שָׁמֶן׃
verses.english: then the one bringing his offering to YHWH shall bring forward a grain offering, fine flour, one-tenth of a measure, mixed with a fourth of a hin of oil.

tex.original: \hR{וְהִקְרִיב הַמַּקְרִיב קרְבָּנוֹ לַיהֹוָה מִנְחָה סֹלֶת עִשָּׂרוֹן בָּלוּל בִּרְבִעִית הַהִין שָׁמֶן׃}

verses.original: וְיַיִן לַנֶּסֶךְ רְבִיעִית הַהִין תַּעֲשֶׂה עַל הָעֹלָה אוֹ לַזָּבַח לַכֶּבֶשׂ הָאֶחָד׃
verses.english: And you shall make wine for a libation with the burnt offering or the sacrifice, a fourth of a hin for one lamb.

tex.original: \hR{וְיַיִן לַנֶּסֶךְ רְבִיעִית הַהִין תַּעֲשֶׂה עַל הָעֹלָה אוֹ לַזָּבַח לַכֶּבֶשׂ הָאֶחָד׃}

verses.original: אוֹ לָאַיִל תַּעֲשֶׂה מִנְחָה סֹלֶת שְׁנֵי עֶשְׂרֹנִים בְּלוּלָה בַשֶּׁמֶן שְׁלִשִׁית הַהִין׃
verses.english: Or for a ram, you shall make a grain offering, fine flour, two tenths, mixed with oil, a third of a hin,

tex.original: \hR{אוֹ לָאַיִל תַּעֲשֶׂה מִנְחָה סֹלֶת שְׁנֵי עֶשְׂרֹנִים בְּלוּלָה בַשֶּׁמֶן שְׁלִשִׁית הַהִין׃}

verses.original: וְיַיִן לַנֶּסֶךְ שְׁלִשִׁית הַהִין תַּקְרִיב רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: and you shall bring forward wine for a libation, a third of a hin, a pleasant smell to YHWH.

tex.original: \hR{וְיַיִן לַנֶּסֶךְ שְׁלִשִׁית הַהִין תַּקְרִיב רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְכִי תַעֲשֶׂה בֶן בָּקָר עֹלָה אוֹ זָבַח לְפַלֵּא נֶדֶר אוֹ שְׁלָמִים לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: And if you will make a bull a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to express a vow, or a peace offering to YHWH,

tex.original: \hR{וְכִי תַעֲשֶׂה בֶן בָּקָר עֹלָה אוֹ זָבַח לְפַלֵּא נֶדֶר אוֹ שְׁלָמִים לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְהִקְרִיב עַל בֶּן הַבָּקָר מִנְחָה סֹלֶת שְׁלֹשָׁה עֶשְׂרֹנִים בָּלוּל בַּשֶּׁמֶן חֲצִי הַהִין׃
verses.english: then he shall bring forward with the bull a grain offering, fine flour, three tenths, mixed with oil, half of a hin,

tex.original: \hR{וְהִקְרִיב עַל בֶּן הַבָּקָר מִנְחָה סֹלֶת שְׁלֹשָׁה עֶשְׂרֹנִים בָּלוּל בַּשֶּׁמֶן חֲצִי הַהִין׃}

verses.original: וְיַיִן תַּקְרִיב לַנֶּסֶךְ חֲצִי הַהִין אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: and you shall bring forward wine for a libation, half of a hin, an offering by fire of a pleasant smell to YHWH.

tex.original: \hR{וְיַיִן תַּקְרִיב לַנֶּסֶךְ חֲצִי הַהִין אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: כָּכָה יֵעָשֶׂה לַשּׁוֹר הָאֶחָד אוֹ לָאַיִל הָאֶחָד אוֹ לַשֶּׂה בַכְּבָשִׂים אוֹ בָעִזִּים׃
verses.english: It shall be done this way for one ox or for one ram or for a lamb of the sheep or of the goats.

tex.original: \hR{כָּכָה יֵעָשֶׂה לַשּׁוֹר הָאֶחָד אוֹ לָאַיִל הָאֶחָד אוֹ לַשֶּׂה בַכְּבָשִׂים אוֹ בָעִזִּים׃}

verses.original: כַּמִּסְפָּר אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשׂוּ כָּכָה תַּעֲשׂוּ לָאֶחָד כְּמִסְפָּרָם׃
verses.english: By the number that you will do, you shall do each one of their number this way.

tex.original: \hR{כַּמִּסְפָּר אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשׂוּ כָּכָה תַּעֲשׂוּ לָאֶחָד כְּמִסְפָּרָם׃}

verses.original: כּל הָאֶזְרָח יַעֲשֶׂה כָּכָה אֶת אֵלֶּה לְהַקְרִיב אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Every citizen shall do these this way when bringing forward an offering by fire of a pleasant smell to YHWH.

tex.original: \hR{כּל הָאֶזְרָח יַעֲשֶׂה כָּכָה אֶת אֵלֶּה לְהַקְרִיב אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְכִי יָגוּר אִתְּכֶם גֵּר אוֹ אֲשֶׁר בְּתוֹכְכֶם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם וְעָשָׂה אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשׂוּ כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה׃
verses.english: And when an alien will reside with you—or someone who is among you—through your generations and will make an offering by fire of a pleasant smell to YHWH, as you will do so he shall do.

tex.original: \hR{וְכִי יָגוּר אִתְּכֶם גֵּר אוֹ אֲשֶׁר בְּתוֹכְכֶם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם וְעָשָׂה אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשׂוּ כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה׃}

verses.original: הַקָּהָל חֻקָּה אַחַת לָכֶם וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם כָּכֶם כַּגֵּר יִהְיֶה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: You, congregation, and the resident alien have one law, an eternal law through your generations: it will be the same for you and for the alien in front of YHWH.

tex.original: \hR{הַקָּהָל חֻקָּה אַחַת לָכֶם וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם כָּכֶם כַּגֵּר יִהְיֶה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: תּוֹרָה אַחַת וּמִשְׁפָּט אֶחָד יִהְיֶה לָכֶם וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר אִתְּכֶם׃
verses.english: You and the alien who resides with you shall have one instruction and one judgment.”

tex.original: \hR{תּוֹרָה אַחַת וּמִשְׁפָּט אֶחָד יִהְיֶה לָכֶם וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר אִתְּכֶם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		You and the alien. In these verses (14–16) the text says in four
%		different ways that the law is the same for a citizen and a resident
%		alien. Thus it again emphasizes that this is an essential principle of
%		the Torah: Israelites are not privileged over anyone else. A country
%		must treat everyone who lives in it fairly, with equality under the law.
%	}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hR{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eR{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם בְּבֹאֲכֶם אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי מֵבִיא אֶתְכֶם שָׁמָּה׃
verses.english: “Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: When you come to the land where I’m bringing you,

tex.original: \hR{דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם בְּבֹאֲכֶם אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי מֵבִיא אֶתְכֶם שָׁמָּה׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה בַּאֲכלְכֶם מִלֶּחֶם הָאָרֶץ תָּרִימוּ תְרוּמָה לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: then it will be that when you eat some of the land’s bread you shall make a donation to YHWH.

tex.original: \hR{וְהָיָה בַּאֲכלְכֶם מִלֶּחֶם הָאָרֶץ תָּרִימוּ תְרוּמָה לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: רֵאשִׁית עֲרִסֹתֵכֶם חַלָּה תָּרִימוּ תְרוּמָה כִּתְרוּמַת גֹּרֶן כֵּן תָּרִימוּ אֹתָהּ׃
verses.english: The first of your dough: you shall make a loaf as a donation. Like a donation from the threshing floor, so you shall donate it.

tex.original: \hR{רֵאשִׁית עֲרִסֹתֵכֶם חַלָּה תָּרִימוּ תְרוּמָה כִּתְרוּמַת גֹּרֶן כֵּן תָּרִימוּ אֹתָהּ׃}

verses.original: מֵרֵאשִׁית עֲרִסֹתֵיכֶם תִּתְּנוּ לַיהֹוָה תְּרוּמָה לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: From the first of your dough you shall give a donation to YHWH through your generations.

tex.original: \hR{מֵרֵאשִׁית עֲרִסֹתֵיכֶם תִּתְּנוּ לַיהֹוָה תְּרוּמָה לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְכִי תִשְׁגּוּ וְלֹא תַעֲשׂוּ אֵת כּל הַמִּצְוֺת הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה׃
verses.english: “And when you will make a mistake and not do all of these commandments that YHWH has spoken to Moses,

tex.original: \hR{וְכִי תִשְׁגּוּ וְלֹא תַעֲשׂוּ אֵת כּל הַמִּצְוֺת הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה׃}

verses.original: אֵת כּל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֲלֵיכֶם בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה מִן הַיּוֹם אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה וָהָלְאָה לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: everything that YHWH has commanded you by Moses’ hand, from the day that YHWH commanded and on through your generations,

tex.original: \hR{אֵת כּל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֲלֵיכֶם בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה מִן הַיּוֹם אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה וָהָלְאָה לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה אִם מֵעֵינֵי הָעֵדָה נֶעֶשְׂתָה לִשְׁגָגָה וְעָשׂוּ כל הָעֵדָה פַּר בֶּן בָּקָר אֶחָד לְעֹלָה לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה וּמִנְחָתוֹ וְנִסְכּוֹ כַּמִּשְׁפָּט וּשְׂעִיר עִזִּים אֶחָד לְחַטָּת׃
verses.english: then it will be that, if it was done by mistake, out of the congregation’s sight, then all the congregation shall do one bull of the cattle as a burnt offering for a pleasant smell to YHWH and its grain offering and its libation according to the required manner and one goat for a sin offering.

tex.original: \hR{וְהָיָה אִם מֵעֵינֵי הָעֵדָה נֶעֶשְׂתָה לִשְׁגָגָה וְעָשׂוּ כל הָעֵדָה פַּר בֶּן בָּקָר אֶחָד לְעֹלָה לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה וּמִנְחָתוֹ וְנִסְכּוֹ כַּמִּשְׁפָּט וּשְׂעִיר עִזִּים אֶחָד לְחַטָּת׃}
tex.english:
\eR{
		then it will be that, if it was done by mistake, out of
		the congregation’s sight, then all the congregation shall
		do one bull of the cattle as a burnt offering for a
		pleasant smell to YHWH and its grain offering and its
		libation according to the required manner and one goat for
		a sin offering.%
	}

verses.original: וְכִפֶּר הַכֹּהֵן עַל כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִסְלַח לָהֶם כִּי שְׁגָגָה הִוא וְהֵם הֵבִיאוּ אֶת קרְבָּנָם אִשֶּׁה לַיהֹוָה וְחַטָּאתָם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה עַל שִׁגְגָתָם׃
verses.english: And the priest shall make atonement for all the congregation of the children of Israel, and it will be forgiven for them, because it was a mistake, and they brought their offering, an offering by fire to YHWH, and their sin offering in front of YHWH for their mistake.

tex.original: \hR{וְכִפֶּר הַכֹּהֵן עַל כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִסְלַח לָהֶם כִּי שְׁגָגָה הִוא וְהֵם הֵבִיאוּ אֶת קרְבָּנָם אִשֶּׁה לַיהֹוָה וְחַטָּאתָם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה עַל שִׁגְגָתָם׃}
tex.english:
\eR{
		And the priest shall make atonement for all the
		congregation of the children of Israel, and it will be
		forgiven for them, because it was a mistake, and they
		brought their offering, an offering by fire to YHWH, and
		their sin offering in front of YHWH for their mistake.%
	}

verses.original: וְנִסְלַח לְכל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר בְּתוֹכָם כִּי לְכל הָעָם בִּשְׁגָגָה׃
verses.english: And it will be forgiven for all the congregation of the children of Israel and the alien who resides among them, because it was by mistake for all the people.

tex.original: \hR{וְנִסְלַח לְכל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר בְּתוֹכָם כִּי לְכל הָעָם בִּשְׁגָגָה׃}

verses.original: וְאִם נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת תֶּחֱטָא בִשְׁגָגָה וְהִקְרִיבָה עֵז בַּת שְׁנָתָהּ לְחַטָּאת׃
verses.english: “And if one person will sin by mistake, then he shall bring a she-goat in its first year for a sin offering.

tex.original: \hR{וְאִם נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת תֶּחֱטָא בִשְׁגָגָה וְהִקְרִיבָה עֵז בַּת שְׁנָתָהּ לְחַטָּאת׃}

verses.original: וְכִפֶּר הַכֹּהֵן עַל הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַשֹּׁגֶגֶת בְּחֶטְאָה בִשְׁגָגָה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לְכַפֵּר עָלָיו וְנִסְלַח לוֹ׃
verses.english: And the priest shall make atonement for the person who made the mistake, sinning by mistake, in front of YHWH to make atonement for him, and it will be forgiven for him.

tex.original: \hR{וְכִפֶּר הַכֹּהֵן עַל הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַשֹּׁגֶגֶת בְּחֶטְאָה בִשְׁגָגָה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לְכַפֵּר עָלָיו וְנִסְלַח לוֹ׃}

verses.original: הָאֶזְרָח בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר בְּתוֹכָם תּוֹרָה אַחַת יִהְיֶה לָכֶם לָעֹשֶׂה בִּשְׁגָגָה׃
verses.english: The citizen among the children of Israel and for the alien who resides among them: you shall have one instruction for one who acts by mistake.

tex.original: \hR{הָאֶזְרָח בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר בְּתוֹכָם תּוֹרָה אַחַת יִהְיֶה לָכֶם לָעֹשֶׂה בִּשְׁגָגָה׃}

verses.original: וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה בְּיָד רָמָה מִן הָאֶזְרָח וּמִן הַגֵּר אֶת יְהֹוָה הוּא מְגַדֵּף וְנִכְרְתָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא מִקֶּרֶב עַמָּהּ׃
verses.english: “But the person who will act with a high hand, a citizen or an alien, he is blaspheming YHWH, and that person will be cut off from among his people,

tex.original: \hR{וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה בְּיָד רָמָה מִן הָאֶזְרָח וּמִן הַגֵּר אֶת יְהֹוָה הוּא מְגַדֵּף וְנִכְרְתָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא מִקֶּרֶב עַמָּהּ׃}

verses.original: כִּי דְבַר יְהֹוָה בָּזָה וְאֶת מִצְוָתוֹ הֵפַר הִכָּרֵת תִּכָּרֵת הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא עֲוֺנָה בָהּ׃
verses.english: because he disdained YHWH’s word and broke His commandment. That person will be cut off. His crime is in him.”

tex.original: \hR{כִּי דְבַר יְהֹוָה בָּזָה וְאֶת מִצְוָתוֹ הֵפַר הִכָּרֵת תִּכָּרֵת הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא עֲוֺנָה בָהּ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּהְיוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּדְבָּר וַיִּמְצְאוּ אִישׁ מְקֹשֵׁשׁ עֵצִים בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת׃
verses.english: And the children of Israel were in the wilderness, and they found a man collecting wood on the Sabbath day.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּהְיוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּדְבָּר וַיִּמְצְאוּ אִישׁ מְקֹשֵׁשׁ עֵצִים בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת׃}

verses.original: וַיַּקְרִיבוּ אֹתוֹ הַמֹּצְאִים אֹתוֹ מְקֹשֵׁשׁ עֵצִים אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן וְאֶל כּל הָעֵדָה׃
verses.english: And those who found him collecting wood brought him forward to Moses and to Aaron and to all the congregation.

tex.original: \hP{וַיַּקְרִיבוּ אֹתוֹ הַמֹּצְאִים אֹתוֹ מְקֹשֵׁשׁ עֵצִים אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן וְאֶל כּל הָעֵדָה׃}

verses.original: וַיַּנִּיחוּ אֹתוֹ בַּמִּשְׁמָר כִּי לֹא פֹרַשׁ מַה יֵּעָשֶׂה לוֹ׃
verses.english: And they left him under watch because it had not been determined what should be done to him.

tex.original: \hP{וַיַּנִּיחוּ אֹתוֹ בַּמִּשְׁמָר כִּי לֹא פֹרַשׁ מַה יֵּעָשֶׂה לוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		it had not been determined. There had already been commandments to
%		observe the Sabbath, not to work on that day, and not to make a fire on
%		that day; and it had already been stated that one who violates the
%		Sabbath is to be executed and cut off. But it was yet to be determined
%		whether this particular case of collecting wood constituted work or
%		whether (if the collection of wood was for building a fire) the
%		collection itself constituted a violation. This account thus not only
%		teaches a law about the Sabbath but also demonstrates the relationship
%		between a legal principle and the application of that principle to each
%		individual case. No case is to be prejudged. Every case deserves an
%		inquiry and a decision.
%	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה מוֹת יוּמַת הָאִישׁ רָגוֹם אֹתוֹ בָאֲבָנִים כּל הָעֵדָה מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “The man shall be put to death! All the congregation is to batter him with stones outside the camp.”

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה מוֹת יוּמַת הָאִישׁ רָגוֹם אֹתוֹ בָאֲבָנִים כּל הָעֵדָה מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּצִיאוּ אֹתוֹ כּל הָעֵדָה אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה וַיִּרְגְּמוּ אֹתוֹ בָּאֲבָנִים וַיָּמֹת כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶת מֹשֶׁה׃
verses.english: And all the congregation brought him outside the camp and battered him with stones, and he died, as YHWH commanded Moses.

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּצִיאוּ אֹתוֹ כּל הָעֵדָה אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה וַיִּרְגְּמוּ אֹתוֹ בָּאֲבָנִים וַיָּמֹת כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶת מֹשֶׁה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH said to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם וְעָשׂוּ לָהֶם צִיצִת עַל כַּנְפֵי בִגְדֵיהֶם לְדֹרֹתָם וְנָתְנוּ עַל צִיצִת הַכָּנָף פְּתִיל תְּכֵלֶת׃
verses.english: “Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them that they shall make fringe on the corners of their clothes through their generations. And they shall put a blue string on the fringe of the corner.

tex.original: \hP{דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם וְעָשׂוּ לָהֶם צִיצִת עַל כַּנְפֵי בִגְדֵיהֶם לְדֹרֹתָם וְנָתְנוּ עַל צִיצִת הַכָּנָף פְּתִיל תְּכֵלֶת׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		blue string. Blue string is used in the garments of the high priest
%		(Exod 28:28,37). The blue string in the fringe of every Israelite’s
%		clothing is an element of the holy in every one’s daily life. The fringe
%		in general is a reminder to keep all the commandments; the blue string
%		is a reminder of holiness. (See the next comment.)
%	}

verses.original: וְהָיָה לָכֶם לְצִיצִת וּרְאִיתֶם אֹתוֹ וּזְכַרְתֶּם אֶת כּל מִצְוֺת יְהֹוָה וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֹתָם וְלֹא תָתוּרוּ אַחֲרֵי לְבַבְכֶם וְאַחֲרֵי עֵינֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם זֹנִים אַחֲרֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: And you shall have the fringe so you will see it and bring to mind all of YHWH’s commandments and will do them, and you will not go around after your heart and after your eyes, because you whore after them.

tex.original: \hP{וְהָיָה לָכֶם לְצִיצִת וּרְאִיתֶם אֹתוֹ וּזְכַרְתֶּם אֶת כּל מִצְוֺת יְהֹוָה וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֹתָם וְלֹא תָתוּרוּ אַחֲרֵי לְבַבְכֶם וְאַחֲרֵי עֵינֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם זֹנִים אַחֲרֵיהֶם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		see it and bring to mind. Most of the commandments in the Torah are
%		given without any reason being stated. We are not told why we are not
%		allowed to eat a pig or to steal, or why the Tabernacle must have twenty
%		frames on each side. If we want to know the reasons, we have to ponder
%		and try to determine them ourselves. For some commandments the reason is
%		obvious, and for some it is extremely difficult to know. The commandment
%		to wear fringes stands out, therefore, as being one for which the reason
%		is stated explicitly: the fringe is a reminder; it is always present on
%		one’s clothing so that one will see it and be reminded of the existence
%		of all the commandments, so one will do them, and so the people will be
%		holy. Footnote 15:39. go around. Hebrew tûr. This is the same word that
%		is used for the scouting of the land by the spies in the preceding
%		chapters. This both helps us understand the word—meaning to go looking
%		all over, here with the sense of looking for trouble—and helps to
%		connect the laws of this chapter with the story of the spies that just
%		precedes it. This chapter of law is often seen as intrusive between a
%		series of stories, but the language used in the laws bring the stories
%		to mind, and vice versa.
%	}

verses.original: לְמַעַן תִּזְכְּרוּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֶת כּל מִצְוֺתָי וִהְיִיתֶם קְדֹשִׁים לֵאלֹהֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: So you will bring to mind and do all my commandments, and you will be holy to your God.

tex.original: \hP{לְמַעַן תִּזְכְּרוּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֶת כּל מִצְוֺתָי וִהְיִיתֶם קְדֹשִׁים לֵאלֹהֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי אֶתְכֶם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם לִהְיוֹת לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: I am YHWH, your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt to be God to you. I am YHWH, your God.”

tex.original: \hP{אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתִי אֶתְכֶם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם לִהְיוֹת לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח קֹרַח בֶּן יִצְהָר בֶּן קְהָת בֶּן לֵוִי וְדָתָן וַאֲבִירָם בְּנֵי אֱלִיאָב וְאוֹן בֶּן פֶּלֶת בְּנֵי רְאוּבֵן׃
verses.english: And Korah son of Izhar son of Kohath son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On, son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, took

tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Korah. He is a first cousin of Moses and Aaron (Exod 6:18–21). Footnote
%		16:1. Korah … took. He assembles a group with him, and he frames his
%		argument in terms of the people (“all of them are holy”). He is the
%		prototype of some politicians, religious leaders, and others, who act as
%		though they represent a group and are working for the people—when their
%		motives are suspect.
%	}

verses.original: וַיָּקֻמוּ לִפְנֵי מֹשֶׁה וַאֲנָשִׁים מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל חֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתָיִם נְשִׂיאֵי עֵדָה קְרִאֵי מוֹעֵד אַנְשֵׁי שֵׁם׃
verses.english: and got up in front of Moses— and two hundred fifty people from the children of Israel, chieftains of the congregation, prominent ones of the assembly, people of repute.
verses.commentary: REF: The two occurrences of the extraneous word “and” in this verse are partly a product of the Redactor’s arrangement of the combined text and partly a product of the English translation, in which a different word order from the Hebrew is necessary. Separated, the P text would read: “And Korah son of Izhar son of Kohath son of Levi took two hundred fifty people . . . ,” and the J text would read: “And Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On, son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, got up in front of Moses.”

tex.original:
\hJ{וַיָּקֻמוּ לִפְנֵי מֹשֶׁה}
	\hP{וַאֲנָשִׁים מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל חֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתָיִם נְשִׂיאֵי עֵדָה קְרִאֵי מוֹעֵד אַנְשֵׁי שֵׁם׃}
tex.commentary:
\fC{REF: The two occurrences of the extraneous word “and” in this verse are partly a product of the Redactor’s arrangement of the combined text and partly a product of the English translation, in which a different word order from the Hebrew is necessary. Separated, the P text would read: “And Korah son of Izhar son of Kohath son of Levi took two hundred fifty people . . . ,” and the J text would read: “And Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On, son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, got up in front of Moses.”}
	% TODO Num 16:2: Add the supplied REF footnote about the two extraneous occurrences of “and.”

verses.original: וַיִּקָּהֲלוּ עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעַל אַהֲרֹן וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֲלֵהֶם רַב לָכֶם כִּי כל הָעֵדָה כֻּלָּם קְדֹשִׁים וּבְתוֹכָם יְהֹוָה וּמַדּוּעַ תִּתְנַשְּׂאוּ עַל קְהַל יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: And they assembled against Moses and against Aaron and said to them, “You have much! Because all of the congregation, all of them, are holy, and YHWH is among them. And why do you raise yourselves up over YHWH’s community?”

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּקָּהֲלוּ עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעַל אַהֲרֹן וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֲלֵהֶם רַב לָכֶם כִּי כל הָעֵדָה כֻּלָּם קְדֹשִׁים וּבְתוֹכָם יְהֹוָה וּמַדּוּעַ תִּתְנַשְּׂאוּ עַל קְהַל יְהֹוָה׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And they assembled against Moses and against Aaron and
		said to them, “You have much! Because all of the
		congregation, all of them, are holy, and YHWH is among
		them. And why do you raise yourselves up over YHWH’s
		community?”
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		all of the congregation, all of them, are holy. It is true that all the
%		people have been described as a holy nation. Korah uses this now to
%		enhance his claim that he has as much right to the priesthood as Aaron.
%		But it is a deception, mixing two different meanings and degrees of
%		holiness. It is like telling a child that he or she is now “big” or
%		“grown up”—and then the child demands all the rights and privileges of
%		grownups.
%	}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁמַע מֹשֶׁה וַיִּפֹּל עַל פָּנָיו׃
verses.english: And Moses listened, and he fell on his face.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּשְׁמַע מֹשֶׁה וַיִּפֹּל עַל פָּנָיו׃}
tex.english: \eP{And Moses listened, and he fell on his face. }

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר אֶל קֹרַח וְאֶל כּל עֲדָתוֹ לֵאמֹר בֹּקֶר וְיֹדַע יְהֹוָה אֶת אֲשֶׁר לוֹ וְאֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ וְהִקְרִיב אֵלָיו וְאֵת אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר בּוֹ יַקְרִיב אֵלָיו׃
verses.english: And he spoke to Korah and to all of his congregation, saying, “In the morning YHWH will make known who is His and who is holy, and He will bring him close to Him. And He will bring the one He chooses close to Him.

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר אֶל קֹרַח וְאֶל כּל עֲדָתוֹ לֵאמֹר בֹּקֶר וְיֹדַע יְהֹוָה אֶת אֲשֶׁר לוֹ וְאֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ וְהִקְרִיב אֵלָיו וְאֵת אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר בּוֹ יַקְרִיב אֵלָיו׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		who is holy. Moses sets up a test of who is holy, to establish what it
%		means to be holy in the priestly sense, as opposed to the general
%		concept that the people should strive to be holy. The test will be the
%		use of incense, because only the holy—namely, priests—are permitted to
%		burn incense. The test will establish this, and it will be declared
%		formally following this episode (Num 17:5). And Korah and his company
%		cannot be unaware of the significance of the correct burning of incense,
%		because it was precisely a misuse of incense that led to the death of
%		Aaron’s sons, Nadab and Abihu (Lev 10:1–2).
%	}

verses.original: זֹאת עֲשׂוּ קְחוּ לָכֶם מַחְתּוֹת קֹרַח וְכל עֲדָתוֹ׃
verses.english: Do this: Take incense burners, Korah and all his congregation,

tex.original: \hP{זֹאת עֲשׂוּ קְחוּ לָכֶם מַחְתּוֹת קֹרַח וְכל עֲדָתוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Do this. Why does Korah go along with the test? Do he and his followers
%		really believe that God would support them? Answer: they have no choice.
%		Moses does not propose a test. He commands Korah and his group. His
%		verbs are four imperatives in a row: do, take, put, set! And Korah
%		cannot refuse. The whole point, after all, is that Korah is seeking
%		priesthood (Num 16:10). What Moses challenges him to do is to perform
%		one of the acts that he would commonly have to do if he were to become a
%		priest: burn incense. Korah’s claim on the priesthood would evaporate if
%		he were to decline the opportunity he has been offered to do a priestly
%		task.
%	}

verses.original: וּתְנוּ בָהֵן אֵשׁ וְשִׂימוּ עֲלֵיהֶן קְטֹרֶת לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה מָחָר וְהָיָה הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה הוּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ רַב לָכֶם בְּנֵי לֵוִי׃
verses.english: and put fire in them and set incense on them in front of YHWH tomorrow. And it will be that the man whom YHWH will choose, he will be the holy one. You have much, sons of Levi!”

tex.original: \hP{וּתְנוּ בָהֵן אֵשׁ וְשִׂימוּ עֲלֵיהֶן קְטֹרֶת לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה מָחָר וְהָיָה הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה הוּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ רַב לָכֶם בְּנֵי לֵוִי׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל קֹרַח שִׁמְעוּ נָא בְּנֵי לֵוִי׃
verses.english: And Moses said to Korah, “Listen, sons of Levi,

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל קֹרַח שִׁמְעוּ נָא בְּנֵי לֵוִי׃}
tex.english: \eP{And Moses said to Korah, “Listen, sons of Levi,}

verses.original: הַמְעַט מִכֶּם כִּי הִבְדִּיל אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶתְכֶם מֵעֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַקְרִיב אֶתְכֶם אֵלָיו לַעֲבֹד אֶת עֲבֹדַת מִשְׁכַּן יְהֹוָה וְלַעֲמֹד לִפְנֵי הָעֵדָה לְשָׁרְתָם׃
