verses.english: is it too small a thing for you that Israel’s God has distinguished you from the congregation of Israel to bring you close to him, to do the work of YHWH’s Tabernacle and to stand in front of the congregation to minister for them,

tex.original: \hP{הַמְעַט מִכֶּם כִּי הִבְדִּיל אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶתְכֶם מֵעֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַקְרִיב אֶתְכֶם אֵלָיו לַעֲבֹד אֶת עֲבֹדַת מִשְׁכַּן יְהֹוָה וְלַעֲמֹד לִפְנֵי הָעֵדָה לְשָׁרְתָם׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		is it too small a thing for you that Israel’s God has
		distinguished you from the congregation of Israel to bring
		you close to him, to do the work of YHWH’s Tabernacle and
		to stand in front of the congregation to minister for
		them,
	}

verses.original: וַיַּקְרֵב אֹתְךָ וְאֶת כּל אַחֶיךָ בְנֵי לֵוִי אִתָּךְ וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם גַּם כְּהֻנָּה׃
verses.english: and that He has brought you and all your brothers, the sons of Levi, with you close to Him? And you seek priesthood as well?!

tex.original: \hP{וַיַּקְרֵב אֹתְךָ וְאֶת כּל אַחֶיךָ בְנֵי לֵוִי אִתָּךְ וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם גַּם כְּהֻנָּה׃}

verses.original: לָכֵן אַתָּה וְכל עֲדָתְךָ הַנֹּעָדִים עַל יְהֹוָה וְאַהֲרֹן מַה הוּא כִּי (תלונו) [תַלִּינוּ] עָלָיו׃
verses.english: Therefore you and all your congregation who are gathering are against YHWH! And Aaron, what is he that you complain against him?”
verses.commentary: Qere Ketiv.

tex.original: \hP{לָכֵן אַתָּה וְכל עֲדָתְךָ הַנֹּעָדִים עַל יְהֹוָה וְאַהֲרֹן מַה הוּא כִּי (תלונו) [תַלִּינוּ] עָלָיו׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח מֹשֶׁה לִקְרֹא לְדָתָן וְלַאֲבִירָם בְּנֵי אֱלִיאָב וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֹא נַעֲלֶה׃
verses.english: And Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and they said, “We won’t come up.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשְׁלַח מֹשֶׁה לִקְרֹא לְדָתָן וְלַאֲבִירָם בְּנֵי אֱלִיאָב וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֹא נַעֲלֶה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram. Two groups with two different
%		complaints have joined together to challenge Moses. Korah’s company
%		challenge Aaron’s hold on the priesthood; Dathan and Abiram challenge
%		Moses’ hold on the leadership of Israel. This political union of two
%		agendas is presumably arranged to strengthen the positions of both.
%		Moses, however, keeps them separate. He has responded first to Korah and
%		his company who are challenging the priestly prerogatives of Moses and
%		Aaron. Now he turns to Dathan and Abiram and summons them. By separating
%		them, he weakens their position.
%	}

verses.original: הַמְעַט כִּי הֶעֱלִיתָנוּ מֵאֶרֶץ זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבַשׁ לַהֲמִיתֵנוּ בַּמִּדְבָּר כִּי תִשְׂתָּרֵר עָלֵינוּ גַּם הִשְׂתָּרֵר׃
verses.english: Is it a small thing that you brought us up from a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness, that you lord it over us as well?

tex.original: \hJ{הַמְעַט כִּי הֶעֱלִיתָנוּ מֵאֶרֶץ זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבַשׁ לַהֲמִיתֵנוּ בַּמִּדְבָּר כִּי תִשְׂתָּרֵר עָלֵינוּ גַּם הִשְׂתָּרֵר׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		you brought us up from a land flowing with milk and honey. They are
%		referring to Egypt! They use the rhetorical device of reversing their
%		opponent’s position: they say that Moses has taken them out of a land
%		flowing with milk and honey. It is a clever device (common in political
%		debate). And it is outrageous: accusing the liberator of being the
%		source of their problems, picturing the land of slavery as the land of
%		milk and honey, and, as usual, focusing on Moses rather than on God. And
%		then they say, “Will you put out those people’s eyes?”—accusing Moses of
%		being the one who is deceiving the people, when it is they who are the
%		deceivers. This is a battle for leadership, which is to say it is a
%		political battle, which is to say it is a battle for power; and it
%		dramatizes the danger of the power-seeking politician who is a skillful
%		speaker. Moses defeats his opponents because God intervenes with a
%		miracle. We who cannot count on earthquakes to identify the corrupt ones
%		among us must be thoughtful, sensitive, and diligent when we listen to
%		political argument.
%	}

verses.original: אַף לֹא אֶל אֶרֶץ זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבַשׁ הֲבִיאֹתָנוּ וַתִּתֶּן לָנוּ נַחֲלַת שָׂדֶה וָכָרֶם הַעֵינֵי הָאֲנָשִׁים הָהֵם תְּנַקֵּר לֹא נַעֲלֶה׃
verses.english: Besides, you haven’t brought us to a land flowing with milk and honey or given us possession of field or vineyard. Will you put out those people’s eyes? We won’t come up.”

tex.original: \hJ{אַף לֹא אֶל אֶרֶץ זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבַשׁ הֲבִיאֹתָנוּ וַתִּתֶּן לָנוּ נַחֲלַת שָׂדֶה וָכָרֶם הַעֵינֵי הָאֲנָשִׁים הָהֵם תְּנַקֵּר לֹא נַעֲלֶה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּחַר לְמֹשֶׁה מְאֹד וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל יְהֹוָה אַל תֵּפֶן אֶל מִנְחָתָם לֹא חֲמוֹר אֶחָד מֵהֶם נָשָׂאתִי וְלֹא הֲרֵעֹתִי אֶת אַחַד מֵהֶם׃
verses.english: And Moses was very angry, and he said to YHWH, “Don’t turn to their offering. Not one ass of theirs have I taken away, and I haven’t wronged one of them.”

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּחַר לְמֹשֶׁה מְאֹד וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל יְהֹוָה אַל תֵּפֶן אֶל מִנְחָתָם לֹא חֲמוֹר אֶחָד מֵהֶם נָשָׂאתִי וְלֹא הֲרֵעֹתִי אֶת אַחַד מֵהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל קֹרַח אַתָּה וְכל עֲדָתְךָ הֱיוּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אַתָּה וָהֵם וְאַהֲרֹן מָחָר׃
verses.english: And Moses said to Korah, “You and all your congregation, be in front of YHWH—you and they and Aaron—tomorrow.

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל קֹרַח אַתָּה וְכל עֲדָתְךָ הֱיוּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אַתָּה וָהֵם וְאַהֲרֹן מָחָר׃}

verses.original: וּקְחוּ אִישׁ מַחְתָּתוֹ וּנְתַתֶּם עֲלֵיהֶם קְטֹרֶת וְהִקְרַבְתֶּם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אִישׁ מַחְתָּתוֹ חֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתַיִם מַחְתֹּת וְאַתָּה וְאַהֲרֹן אִישׁ מַחְתָּתוֹ׃
verses.english: And each man take his fire-holder, and put incense on them, and each man bring his fire-holder forward in front of YHWH, two hundred fifty fire-holders, and you and Aaron, each man his fire-holder.”

tex.original: \hP{וּקְחוּ אִישׁ מַחְתָּתוֹ וּנְתַתֶּם עֲלֵיהֶם קְטֹרֶת וְהִקְרַבְתֶּם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אִישׁ מַחְתָּתוֹ חֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתַיִם מַחְתֹּת וְאַתָּה וְאַהֲרֹן אִישׁ מַחְתָּתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקְחוּ אִישׁ מַחְתָּתוֹ וַיִּתְּנוּ עֲלֵיהֶם אֵשׁ וַיָּשִׂימוּ עֲלֵיהֶם קְטֹרֶת וַיַּעַמְדוּ פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן׃
verses.english: And each man took his fire-holder, and they put fire on them and set incense on them, and they stood at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and Moses and Aaron.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּקְחוּ אִישׁ מַחְתָּתוֹ וַיִּתְּנוּ עֲלֵיהֶם אֵשׁ וַיָּשִׂימוּ עֲלֵיהֶם קְטֹרֶת וַיַּעַמְדוּ פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן׃}

verses.original: וַיַּקְהֵל עֲלֵיהֶם קֹרַח אֶת כּל הָעֵדָה אֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וַיֵּרָא כְבוֹד יְהֹוָה אֶל כּל הָעֵדָה׃
verses.english: And Korah assembled all the congregation against them, to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. And YHWH’s glory appeared to all the congregation.

tex.original: \hP{וַיַּקְהֵל עֲלֵיהֶם קֹרַח אֶת כּל הָעֵדָה אֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וַיֵּרָא כְבוֹד יְהֹוָה אֶל כּל הָעֵדָה׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן לֵאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן לֵאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,}

verses.original: הִבָּדְלוּ מִתּוֹךְ הָעֵדָה הַזֹּאת וַאֲכַלֶּה אֹתָם כְּרָגַע׃
verses.english: “Separate from among this congregation, and I’ll finish them in an instant!”

tex.original: \hP{הִבָּדְלוּ מִתּוֹךְ הָעֵדָה הַזֹּאת וַאֲכַלֶּה אֹתָם כְּרָגַע׃}

verses.original: וַיִּפְּלוּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶם וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵל אֱלֹהֵי הָרוּחֹת לְכל בָּשָׂר הָאִישׁ אֶחָד יֶחֱטָא וְעַל כּל הָעֵדָה תִּקְצֹף׃
verses.english: And they fell on their faces and said, “God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, will one man sin and you be angry at all the congregation?”

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּפְּלוּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶם וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵל אֱלֹהֵי הָרוּחֹת לְכל בָּשָׂר הָאִישׁ אֶחָד יֶחֱטָא וְעַל כּל הָעֵדָה תִּקְצֹף׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		will one man sin and you be angry at all the congregation. Korah has
%		brought the whole congregation of Israel along (16:19), and God has
%		threatened to destroy all of them (16:21), and so Moses and Aaron plead
%		that only those who have done something wrong should suffer. “One man”
%		here cannot mean literally only a single person; it must refer to every
%		individual in Korah’s congregation, as opposed to the entire
%		congregation of Israel. It is reminiscent of Abraham’s plea in the case
%		of Sodom and Gomorrah (“Will you also annihilate the virtuous with the
%		wicked?” Gen 18:23). The connection to the case of Sodom is highlighted
%		by the fact that Moses then tells the people to get away “or else you’ll
%		be annihilated,” which are the words that the angels say at Sodom—and
%		these words occur nowhere else in the Torah (see Gen 18:23,24;
%		19:15,17).
%	}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: דַּבֵּר אֶל הָעֵדָה לֵאמֹר הֵעָלוּ מִסָּבִיב לְמִשְׁכַּן קֹרַח דָּתָן וַאֲבִירָם ׃
verses.english: “Speak to the congregation, saying, ‘Get up from around the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan and Abiram .’”

verses.original: וַיָּקם מֹשֶׁה וַיֵּלֶךְ אֶל דָּתָן וַאֲבִירָם וַיֵּלְכוּ אַחֲרָיו זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and Israel’s elders went after him.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּקם מֹשֶׁה וַיֵּלֶךְ אֶל דָּתָן וַאֲבִירָם וַיֵּלְכוּ אַחֲרָיו זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר אֶל הָעֵדָה לֵאמֹר סוּרוּ נָא מֵעַל אהֳלֵי הָאֲנָשִׁים הָרְשָׁעִים הָאֵלֶּה וְאַל תִּגְּעוּ בְּכל אֲשֶׁר לָהֶם פֶּן תִּסָּפוּ בְּכל חַטֹּאתָם׃
verses.english: And he spoke to the congregation, saying, “Turn away from the tents of these wicked men and don’t touch anything that is theirs, or else you’ll be annihilated through all their sins.”

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר אֶל הָעֵדָה לֵאמֹר סוּרוּ נָא מֵעַל אהֳלֵי הָאֲנָשִׁים הָרְשָׁעִים הָאֵלֶּה וְאַל תִּגְּעוּ בְּכל אֲשֶׁר לָהֶם פֶּן תִּסָּפוּ בְּכל חַטֹּאתָם׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּעָלוּ מֵעַל מִשְׁכַּן קֹרַח דָּתָן וַאֲבִירָם מִסָּבִיב וְדָתָן וַאֲבִירָם יָצְאוּ נִצָּבִים פֶּתַח אהֳלֵיהֶם וּנְשֵׁיהֶם וּבְנֵיהֶם וְטַפָּם׃
verses.english: And they got up from around the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan and Abiram, And Dathan and Abiram came out, standing at the entrance of their tents, and their wives and their children and their infants.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה בְּזֹאת תֵּדְעוּן כִּי יְהֹוָה שְׁלָחַנִי לַעֲשׂוֹת אֵת כּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים הָאֵלֶּה כִּי לֹא מִלִּבִּי׃
verses.english: And Moses said, “By this you’ll know that YHWH sent me to do all these things, because it’s not from my own heart.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה בְּזֹאת תֵּדְעוּן כִּי יְהֹוָה שְׁלָחַנִי לַעֲשׂוֹת אֵת כּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים הָאֵלֶּה כִּי לֹא מִלִּבִּי׃}

verses.original: אִם כְּמוֹת כּל הָאָדָם יְמֻתוּן אֵלֶּה וּפְקֻדַּת כּל הָאָדָם יִפָּקֵד עֲלֵיהֶם לֹא יְהֹוָה שְׁלָחָנִי׃
verses.english: If these die like the death of every human, and the event of every human happens to them, then YHWH hasn’t sent me.

tex.original: \hJ{אִם כְּמוֹת כּל הָאָדָם יְמֻתוּן אֵלֶּה וּפְקֻדַּת כּל הָאָדָם יִפָּקֵד עֲלֵיהֶם לֹא יְהֹוָה שְׁלָחָנִי׃}

verses.original: וְאִם בְּרִיאָה יִבְרָא יְהֹוָה וּפָצְתָה הָאֲדָמָה אֶת פִּיהָ וּבָלְעָה אֹתָם וְאֶת כּל אֲשֶׁר לָהֶם וְיָרְדוּ חַיִּים שְׁאֹלָה וִידַעְתֶּם כִּי נִאֲצוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים הָאֵלֶּה אֶת יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: But if YHWH will create something, and the ground will open its mouth and swallow them and all that they have, and they’ll go down alive to Sheol, then you’ll know that these people have rejected YHWH.”

tex.original: \hJ{וְאִם בְּרִיאָה יִבְרָא יְהֹוָה וּפָצְתָה הָאֲדָמָה אֶת פִּיהָ וּבָלְעָה אֹתָם וְאֶת כּל אֲשֶׁר לָהֶם וְיָרְדוּ חַיִּים שְׁאֹלָה וִידַעְתֶּם כִּי נִאֲצוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים הָאֵלֶּה אֶת יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי כְּכַלֹּתוֹ לְדַבֵּר אֵת כּל הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וַתִּבָּקַע הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר תַּחְתֵּיהֶם׃
verses.english: And it was as he was finishing speaking all these things, and the ground that was under them was broken up,

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְהִי כְּכַלֹּתוֹ לְדַבֵּר אֵת כּל הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וַתִּבָּקַע הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר תַּחְתֵּיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַתִּפְתַּח הָאָרֶץ אֶת פִּיהָ וַתִּבְלַע אֹתָם וְאֶת בָּתֵּיהֶם וְאֵת כּל הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר לְקֹרַח וְאֵת כּל הָרְכוּשׁ׃
verses.english: and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households and all the people who were with Korah and all the property,

tex.original:
\hJ{וַתִּפְתַּח הָאָרֶץ אֶת פִּיהָ וַתִּבְלַע אֹתָם}
	\hP{וְאֶת בָּתֵּיהֶם וְאֵת כּל הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר לְקֹרַח וְאֵת כּל הָרְכוּשׁ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		them and their households. Meaning: their entire families die with them.
%		Why does the entire household suffer? Elsewhere in the law we are told
%		that each person is responsible for his or her own crimes. Children are
%		not to suffer for their parents’ acts (Deut 24:16). But that principle
%		applies only to ethical law: crimes between one human and another. In
%		ritual law—violations against God, such as blasphemy or, in this case,
%		openly opposing an instruction from God (“these people have rejected
%		YHWH”)—anyone who comes in contact with the source of the offense is
%		tainted by it, regardless of that person’s own intent. Thus, for
%		example, in the book of Joshua, Achan keeps some of the forbidden spoils
%		of Jericho, which are designated for complete destruction (erem).
%		He conceals them in his tent. When his offense is revealed he and the
%		spoils “and his sons and his daughters and his ox and his ass and his
%		flock and his tent and everything he had” are stoned and burned (Josh
%		7:24). It is difficult to understand in the postbiblical age, but the
%		concepts of ritual, sacred realms, purity and impurity, and violation of
%		sacred zones are fundamental to Israel’s life as pictured in the Bible’s
%		early books. It may be that the advance in psychology and especially of
%		psychoanalysis in this century can help us to appreciate the mind-set of
%		those who conceived of this notion of guilt by contact. We can recognize
%		that people feel guilt even about things that are not their fault
%		morally. Victims of childhood incest frequently feel guilt through their
%		adult lives. As a closer example: as a child I observed another boy tear
%		a Torah scroll, and I recall how upsetting this was to him and others
%		even though he did not necessarily do it out of lack of care. I also
%		recall, from my student days, knocking a pious rabbi’s black hat from a
%		hook onto the floor and feeling terrible even though it was an accident.
%		(He was wise; he just said lightly, “Praise God that my head wasn’t in
%		it at the time.”) The point is that we do have feelings of guilt in
%		connection with things that we hold in awe. And this is multiplied a
%		thousandfold in the narrative of the age of the Torah: when the divine
%		is believed to be close at hand.
%	}

verses.original: וַיֵּרְדוּ הֵם וְכל אֲשֶׁר לָהֶם חַיִּים שְׁאֹלָה וַתְּכַס עֲלֵיהֶם הָאָרֶץ וַיֹּאבְדוּ מִתּוֹךְ הַקָּהָל׃
verses.english: and they went down, they and all that they had, alive to Sheol. And the earth covered them over, and they perished from among the community.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֵּרְדוּ הֵם וְכל אֲשֶׁר לָהֶם חַיִּים שְׁאֹלָה וַתְּכַס עֲלֵיהֶם הָאָרֶץ וַיֹּאבְדוּ מִתּוֹךְ הַקָּהָל׃}

verses.original: וְכל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר סְבִיבֹתֵיהֶם נָסוּ לְקֹלָם כִּי אָמְרוּ פֶּן תִּבְלָעֵנוּ הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.english: And all Israel that was around them fled at the sound of them, for they said, “Or else the earth will swallow us.”

tex.original: \hJ{וְכל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר סְבִיבֹתֵיהֶם נָסוּ לְקֹלָם כִּי אָמְרוּ פֶּן תִּבְלָעֵנוּ הָאָרֶץ׃}

verses.original: וְאֵשׁ יָצְאָה מֵאֵת יְהֹוָה וַתֹּאכַל אֵת הַחֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתַיִם אִישׁ מַקְרִיבֵי הַקְּטֹרֶת׃
verses.english: And fire had gone out from YHWH and consumed the two hundred fifty people offering the incense.
verses.commentary: REF: The original text probably read “And fire went out” (wattēṣē’ ’ēš) in the perfect tense, and the Redactor changed it to the past perfect tense, “And fire had gone out” (wĕ’ēš yāṣĕ’āh). This was necessary because in the combined text Korah and his company were now being pictured as going down in the earthquake with Dathan and Abiram, but they were also pictured as being burned in the fire, and so R had to clarify that they had already been burned in the fire and now were swallowed along with the live rebels in the earthquake as well.

tex.original: \hP{וְאֵשׁ יָצְאָה מֵאֵת יְהֹוָה וַתֹּאכַל אֵת הַחֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתַיִם אִישׁ מַקְרִיבֵי הַקְּטֹרֶת׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: אֱמֹר אֶל אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן וְיָרֵם אֶת הַמַּחְתֹּת מִבֵּין הַשְּׂרֵפָה וְאֶת הָאֵשׁ זְרֵה הָלְאָה כִּי קָדֵשׁוּ׃
verses.english: “Say to Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest, that he should pick up the fire-holders from the burning and disperse the fire, because they have become holy.

tex.original: \hP{אֱמֹר אֶל אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן וְיָרֵם אֶת הַמַּחְתֹּת מִבֵּין הַשְּׂרֵפָה וְאֶת הָאֵשׁ זְרֵה הָלְאָה כִּי קָדֵשׁוּ׃}

verses.original: אֵת מַחְתּוֹת הַחַטָּאִים הָאֵלֶּה בְּנַפְשֹׁתָם וְעָשׂוּ אֹתָם רִקֻּעֵי פַחִים צִפּוּי לַמִּזְבֵּחַ כִּי הִקְרִיבֻם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וַיִּקְדָּשׁוּ וְיִהְיוּ לְאוֹת לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And the fire-holders of these who sinned at the cost of their lives: let them make them into hammered plates as plating for the altar, because they brought them forward in front of YHWH, and they became holy, and let them become a sign to the children of Israel.”

tex.original: \hP{אֵת מַחְתּוֹת הַחַטָּאִים הָאֵלֶּה בְּנַפְשֹׁתָם וְעָשׂוּ אֹתָם רִקֻּעֵי פַחִים צִפּוּי לַמִּזְבֵּחַ כִּי הִקְרִיבֻם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וַיִּקְדָּשׁוּ וְיִהְיוּ לְאוֹת לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And the fire-holders of these who sinned at the cost of
		their lives: let them make them into hammered plates as
		plating for the altar, because they brought them forward
		in front of YHWH, and they became holy, and let them
		become a sign to the children of Israel.”
	}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח אֶלְעָזָר הַכֹּהֵן אֵת מַחְתּוֹת הַנְּחֹשֶׁת אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיבוּ הַשְּׂרֻפִים וַיְרַקְּעוּם צִפּוּי לַמִּזְבֵּחַ׃
verses.english: And Eleazar, the priest, took the fire-holders of bronze that those who were burned had brought forward, and they hammered them into a plating for the altar,

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּקַּח אֶלְעָזָר הַכֹּהֵן אֵת מַחְתּוֹת הַנְּחֹשֶׁת אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיבוּ הַשְּׂרֻפִים וַיְרַקְּעוּם צִפּוּי לַמִּזְבֵּחַ׃}

verses.original: זִכָּרוֹן לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַעַן אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִקְרַב אִישׁ זָר אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִזֶּרַע אַהֲרֹן הוּא לְהַקְטִיר קְטֹרֶת לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וְלֹא יִהְיֶה כְקֹרַח וְכַעֲדָתוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה לוֹ׃
verses.english: a commemoration for the children of Israel so that no outsider, one who is not from Aaron’s seed, will come forward to burn incense in front of YHWH, so he will not be like Korah and like his congregation, as YHWH spoke to him by Moses’ hand.

tex.original: \hP{זִכָּרוֹן לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַעַן אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִקְרַב אִישׁ זָר אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִזֶּרַע אַהֲרֹן הוּא לְהַקְטִיר קְטֹרֶת לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וְלֹא יִהְיֶה כְקֹרַח וְכַעֲדָתוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה בְּיַד מֹשֶׁה לוֹ׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		a commemoration for the children of Israel so that no
		outsider, one who is not from Aaron’s seed, will come
		forward to burn incense in front of YHWH, so he will not
		be like Korah and like his congregation, as YHWH spoke to
		him by Moses’ hand.
	}

verses.original: וַיִּלֹּנוּ כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמּחֳרָת עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעַל אַהֲרֹן לֵאמֹר אַתֶּם הֲמִתֶּם אֶת עַם יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: And all the congregation of the children of Israel complained the next day against Moses and against Aaron, saying, “You killed YHWH’s people!”

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּלֹּנוּ כּל עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמּחֳרָת עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעַל אַהֲרֹן לֵאמֹר אַתֶּם הֲמִתֶּם אֶת עַם יְהֹוָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		all the congregation of the children of Israel complained the next day.
%		Sometimes a solution may give rise to worse conditions than the original
%		problem. Korah, Dathan, and Abiram had 250 persons in their congregation
%		challenging Moses and Aaron. They are all killed, but now the entire
%		congregation of Israel challenges them. Footnote 17:6. You killed YHWH’s
%		people! Not only do they focus, once again, on Moses and Aaron instead
%		of on their God, they say that Moses and Aaron caused the deaths of
%		Korah and his group. And they turn the truth around even further by
%		saying, “You killed YHWH’s people!”—seemingly placing Moses and Aaron on
%		the opposite side from God. Their attack turns the truth on its head,
%		and so God’s response is ironic: they have said that Moses and Aaron
%		have killed God’s people, so God now threatens to kill His people
%		Himself for their attack on Moses and Aaron! And the irony is extended
%		because Moses and Aaron are the ones who save the people from the rage
%		and plague that come. One might look at a summary of these episodes of
%		challenges to Moses and be inclined to think that the book of Numbers
%		ultimately has only one story to tell and simply keeps repeating it with
%		slight changes of detail. However, that is not likely to be the sense
%		one gets while reading through the stories themselves. The stories act
%		more like variations on a theme. They are each attractive and
%		instructive in themselves, while the recurring elements of theme and
%		language provide sufficient commonality to relate them sensibly to one
%		another and thus give shape to Numbers as a book. When one reads that
%		the people make the same error again and again, directing their
%		complaints toward their human leaders rather than toward the deity who
%		is in fact responsible for their fortunes, one errs to see in this mere
%		repetition. More fruitful would be a consideration of what is to be
%		learned from this picture of a human community who will not learn from
%		experience on this point—or who apparently refuse to accept the reality
%		of it. As in Exodus, closeness to the divine, witnessing the
%		intervention of the cosmic into the mundane, is pictured more as
%		frightening than as uplifting. Despite all that they have seen, they
%		resist coming to terms with the invisible God who has gotten them their
%		freedom and made a covenant with them. And so each new episode of
%		conflict and divine response does not resolve the problem but only leads
%		to another stage of it. But they will finally begin to recognize that
%		their conflicts are also with their God in one of their last rebellions
%		(see Num 21:4–9 and the comments on 21:5).
%	}

verses.original: וַיְהִי בְּהִקָּהֵל הָעֵדָה עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעַל אַהֲרֹן וַיִּפְנוּ אֶל אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וְהִנֵּה כִסָּהוּ הֶעָנָן וַיֵּרָא כְּבוֹד יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: And it was when the congregation was assembled against Moses and against Aaron, and they turned to the Tent of Meeting; and, here, the cloud had covered it, and YHWH’s glory appeared.

tex.original: \hP{וַיְהִי בְּהִקָּהֵל הָעֵדָה עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעַל אַהֲרֹן וַיִּפְנוּ אֶל אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וְהִנֵּה כִסָּהוּ הֶעָנָן וַיֵּרָא כְּבוֹד יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן אֶל פְּנֵי אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: And Moses and Aaron came to the front of the Tent of Meeting.

tex.original: \hP{וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן אֶל פְּנֵי אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: הֵרֹמּוּ מִתּוֹךְ הָעֵדָה הַזֹּאת וַאֲכַלֶּה אֹתָם כְּרָגַע וַיִּפְּלוּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: “Move away from among this congregation, and I’ll finish them in an instant!” And they fell on their faces.

tex.original: \hP{הֵרֹמּוּ מִתּוֹךְ הָעֵדָה הַזֹּאת וַאֲכַלֶּה אֹתָם כְּרָגַע וַיִּפְּלוּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל אַהֲרֹן קַח אֶת הַמַּחְתָּה וְתֶן עָלֶיהָ אֵשׁ מֵעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְשִׂים קְטֹרֶת וְהוֹלֵךְ מְהֵרָה אֶל הָעֵדָה וְכַפֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם כִּי יָצָא הַקֶּצֶף מִלִּפְנֵי יְהֹוָה הֵחֵל הַנָּגֶף׃
verses.english: And Moses said to Aaron, “Take a fire-holder and put fire from the altar on it and set incense and carry it quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them, because a rage has come out from in front of YHWH! The plague has begun!”

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל אַהֲרֹן קַח אֶת הַמַּחְתָּה וְתֶן עָלֶיהָ אֵשׁ מֵעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְשִׂים קְטֹרֶת וְהוֹלֵךְ מְהֵרָה אֶל הָעֵדָה וְכַפֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם כִּי יָצָא הַקֶּצֶף מִלִּפְנֵי יְהֹוָה הֵחֵל הַנָּגֶף׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And Moses said to Aaron, “Take a fire-holder and put fire
		from the altar on it and set incense and carry it quickly
		to the congregation and make atonement for them, because a
		rage has come out from in front of YHWH! The plague has
		begun!”
	}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח אַהֲרֹן כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר מֹשֶׁה וַיָּרץ אֶל תּוֹךְ הַקָּהָל וְהִנֵּה הֵחֵל הַנֶּגֶף בָּעָם וַיִּתֵּן אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת וַיְכַפֵּר עַל הָעָם׃
verses.english: And Aaron took it as Moses had spoken, and he ran among the community. And, here, the plague had begun among the people. And he put in incense and made atonement for the people.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּקַּח אַהֲרֹן כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר מֹשֶׁה וַיָּרץ אֶל תּוֹךְ הַקָּהָל וְהִנֵּה הֵחֵל הַנֶּגֶף בָּעָם וַיִּתֵּן אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת וַיְכַפֵּר עַל הָעָם׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעֲמֹד בֵּין הַמֵּתִים וּבֵין הַחַיִּים וַתֵּעָצַר הַמַּגֵּפָה׃
verses.english: And he stood between the dead and the living. And the plague was halted.

tex.original: \hP{וַיַּעֲמֹד בֵּין הַמֵּתִים וּבֵין הַחַיִּים וַתֵּעָצַר הַמַּגֵּפָה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּהְיוּ הַמֵּתִים בַּמַּגֵּפָה אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר אֶלֶף וּשְׁבַע מֵאוֹת מִלְּבַד הַמֵּתִים עַל דְּבַר קֹרַח׃
verses.english: And the dead in the plague were fourteen thousand seven hundred, apart from the dead over the matter of Korah.

tex.original: \hOther{וַיִּהְיוּ הַמֵּתִים בַּמַּגֵּפָה אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר אֶלֶף וּשְׁבַע מֵאוֹת מִלְּבַד הַמֵּתִים עַל דְּבַר קֹרַח׃}

verses.original: וַיָּשׁב אַהֲרֹן אֶל מֹשֶׁה אֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וְהַמַּגֵּפָה נֶעֱצָרָה׃
verses.english: And Aaron went back to Moses, to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, when the plague had been halted.

tex.original: \hOther{וַיָּשׁב אַהֲרֹן אֶל מֹשֶׁה אֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וְהַמַּגֵּפָה נֶעֱצָרָה׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hOther{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eOther{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְקַח מֵאִתָּם מַטֶּה מַטֶּה לְבֵית אָב מֵאֵת כּל נְשִׂיאֵהֶם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מַטּוֹת אִישׁ אֶת שְׁמוֹ תִּכְתֹּב עַל מַטֵּהוּ׃
verses.english: “Speak to the children of Israel and take from them a staff for each father’s house, from all their chieftains by their fathers’ house, twelve staffs. You shall write each man’s name on his staff,

tex.original: \hOther{דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְקַח מֵאִתָּם מַטֶּה מַטֶּה לְבֵית אָב מֵאֵת כּל נְשִׂיאֵהֶם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מַטּוֹת אִישׁ אֶת שְׁמוֹ תִּכְתֹּב עַל מַטֵּהוּ׃}

verses.original: וְאֵת שֵׁם אַהֲרֹן תִּכְתֹּב עַל מַטֵּה לֵוִי כִּי מַטֶּה אֶחָד לְרֹאשׁ בֵּית אֲבוֹתָם׃
verses.english: and you shall write Aaron’s name on the staff of Levi, because there shall be one staff for the head of their fathers’ house.

tex.original: \hOther{וְאֵת שֵׁם אַהֲרֹן תִּכְתֹּב עַל מַטֵּה לֵוִי כִּי מַטֶּה אֶחָד לְרֹאשׁ בֵּית אֲבוֹתָם׃}

verses.original: וְהִנַּחְתָּם בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד לִפְנֵי הָעֵדוּת אֲשֶׁר אִוָּעֵד לָכֶם שָׁמָּה׃
verses.english: And you shall leave them in the Tent of Meeting in front of the Testimony where I shall meet with you.

tex.original: \hOther{וְהִנַּחְתָּם בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד לִפְנֵי הָעֵדוּת אֲשֶׁר אִוָּעֵד לָכֶם שָׁמָּה׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אֶבְחַר בּוֹ מַטֵּהוּ יִפְרָח וַהֲשִׁכֹּתִי מֵעָלַי אֶת תְּלֻנּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר הֵם מַלִּינִם עֲלֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: And it will be that the man I shall choose: his staff will bloom. And I’ll decrease from me the complaints of the children of Israel that they’re making against you.”

tex.original: \hOther{וְהָיָה הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אֶבְחַר בּוֹ מַטֵּהוּ יִפְרָח וַהֲשִׁכֹּתִי מֵעָלַי אֶת תְּלֻנּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר הֵם מַלִּינִם עֲלֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר מֹשֶׁה אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּתְּנוּ אֵלָיו כּל נְשִׂיאֵיהֶם מַטֶּה לְנָשִׂיא אֶחָד מַטֶּה לְנָשִׂיא אֶחָד לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מַטּוֹת וּמַטֵּה אַהֲרֹן בְּתוֹךְ מַטּוֹתָם׃
verses.english: And Moses spoke to the children of Israel, and all their chieftains gave him a staff for each chieftain by their fathers’ house, twelve staffs, and Aaron’s staff was among their staffs.

tex.original: \hOther{וַיְדַבֵּר מֹשֶׁה אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּתְּנוּ אֵלָיו כּל נְשִׂיאֵיהֶם מַטֶּה לְנָשִׂיא אֶחָד מַטֶּה לְנָשִׂיא אֶחָד לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מַטּוֹת וּמַטֵּה אַהֲרֹן בְּתוֹךְ מַטּוֹתָם׃}

verses.original: וַיַּנַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַמַּטֹּת לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה בְּאֹהֶל הָעֵדֻת׃
verses.english: And Moses left the staffs in front of YHWH in the Tent of the Testimony.

tex.original: \hOther{וַיַּנַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַמַּטֹּת לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה בְּאֹהֶל הָעֵדֻת׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי מִמּחֳרָת וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה אֶל אֹהֶל הָעֵדוּת וְהִנֵּה פָּרַח מַטֵּה אַהֲרֹן לְבֵית לֵוִי וַיֹּצֵא פֶרַח וַיָּצֵץ צִיץ וַיִּגְמֹל שְׁקֵדִים׃
verses.english: And it was the next day, and Moses came to the Tent of the Testimony; and, here, Aaron’s staff, of the house of Levi, had bloomed; and it brought out a bloom, and it made a blossom, and it produced almonds!

tex.original: \hOther{וַיְהִי מִמּחֳרָת וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה אֶל אֹהֶל הָעֵדוּת וְהִנֵּה פָּרַח מַטֵּה אַהֲרֹן לְבֵית לֵוִי וַיֹּצֵא פֶרַח וַיָּצֵץ צִיץ וַיִּגְמֹל שְׁקֵדִים׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּצֵא מֹשֶׁה אֶת כּל הַמַּטֹּת מִלִּפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֶל כּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּרְאוּ וַיִּקְחוּ אִישׁ מַטֵּהוּ׃
verses.english: And Moses brought out all the staffs from in front of YHWH to the children of Israel. And they saw, and each took his staff.

tex.original: \hOther{וַיֹּצֵא מֹשֶׁה אֶת כּל הַמַּטֹּת מִלִּפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֶל כּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּרְאוּ וַיִּקְחוּ אִישׁ מַטֵּהוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה הָשֵׁב אֶת מַטֵּה אַהֲרֹן לִפְנֵי הָעֵדוּת לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת לְאוֹת לִבְנֵי מֶרִי וּתְכַל תְּלוּנֹּתָם מֵעָלַי וְלֹא יָמֻתוּ׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “Put back Aaron’s staff in front of the Testimony for watching over, for a sign to rebels, and you’ll end their complaints against me so they won’t die!”

tex.original: \hOther{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה הָשֵׁב אֶת מַטֵּה אַהֲרֹן לִפְנֵי הָעֵדוּת לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת לְאוֹת לִבְנֵי מֶרִי וּתְכַל תְּלוּנֹּתָם מֵעָלַי וְלֹא יָמֻתוּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Put back Aaron’s staff in front of the Testimony for watching over, for
%		a sign to rebels. Aaron’s staff that miraculously blossomed is now saved
%		by the ark as a reminder when people will rebel in the future. This will
%		be crucial to the event that will determine Aaron’s fate later, when the
%		people will rebel at Meribah. See the comment on Num Footnote 20:8.
%	}

verses.original: וַיַּעַשׂ מֹשֶׁה כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֹתוֹ כֵּן עָשָׂה׃
verses.english: And Moses did it. As YHWH had commanded him, he did so.

tex.original: \hOther{וַיַּעַשׂ מֹשֶׁה כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֹתוֹ כֵּן עָשָׂה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵאמֹר הֵן גָּוַעְנוּ אָבַדְנוּ כֻּלָּנוּ אָבָדְנוּ׃
verses.english: And the children of Israel said to Moses, saying, “Here, we’re expiring, we’re perishing, we’re all perishing!

tex.original: \hOther{וַיֹּאמְרוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵאמֹר הֵן גָּוַעְנוּ אָבַדְנוּ כֻּלָּנוּ אָבָדְנוּ׃}

verses.original: כֹּל הַקָּרֵב הַקָּרֵב אֶל מִשְׁכַּן יְהֹוָה יָמוּת הַאִם תַּמְנוּ לִגְוֺעַ׃
verses.english: Everyone who comes close—who comes close to YHWH’s Tabernacle—will die. Have we come to the end of expiring?!”

tex.original: \hOther{כֹּל הַקָּרֵב הַקָּרֵב אֶל מִשְׁכַּן יְהֹוָה יָמוּת הַאִם תַּמְנוּ לִגְוֺעַ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל אַהֲרֹן אַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ וּבֵית אָבִיךָ אִתָּךְ תִּשְׂאוּ אֶת עֲוֺן הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְאַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ אִתָּךְ תִּשְׂאוּ אֶת עֲוֺן כְּהֻנַּתְכֶם׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Aaron, “You and your sons and your father’s house with you shall bear any crime of the holy place, and you and your sons with you shall bear any crime of your priesthood.

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל אַהֲרֹן אַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ וּבֵית אָבִיךָ אִתָּךְ תִּשְׂאוּ אֶת עֲוֺן הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְאַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ אִתָּךְ תִּשְׂאוּ אֶת עֲוֺן כְּהֻנַּתְכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְגַם אֶת אַחֶיךָ מַטֵּה לֵוִי שֵׁבֶט אָבִיךָ הַקְרֵב אִתָּךְ וְיִלָּווּ עָלֶיךָ וִישָׁרְתוּךָ וְאַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ אִתָּךְ לִפְנֵי אֹהֶל הָעֵדֻת׃
verses.english: And bring forward your brothers, the tribe of Levi, your father’s tribe, with you as well, and they shall be connected to you and shall minister to you, and you and your sons with you shall be in front of the Tent of the Testimony.

tex.original: \hP{וְגַם אֶת אַחֶיךָ מַטֵּה לֵוִי שֵׁבֶט אָבִיךָ הַקְרֵב אִתָּךְ וְיִלָּווּ עָלֶיךָ וִישָׁרְתוּךָ וְאַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ אִתָּךְ לִפְנֵי אֹהֶל הָעֵדֻת׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And bring forward your brothers, the tribe of Levi, your
		father’s tribe, with you as well, and they shall be
		connected to you and shall minister to you, and you and
		your sons with you shall be in front of the Tent of the
		Testimony.
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		connected. The word is the verbal form of the word “Levite.” Some would
%		say that it might shed light on the original meaning of the term Levite
%		as being someone who is joined or attached to the sacred in order to
%		perform service; in other words, a priest. In this verse, it is used to
%		mean that these persons are rather attached to the priests, in order to
%		perform service to the priests; in other words, Levites are designated
%		as secondary clergy, whose task is to assist the priests.
%	}

verses.original: וְשָׁמְרוּ מִשְׁמַרְתְּךָ וּמִשְׁמֶרֶת כּל הָאֹהֶל אַךְ אֶל כְּלֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְאֶל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ לֹא יִקְרָבוּ וְלֹא יָמֻתוּ גַם הֵם גַּם אַתֶּם׃
verses.english: And they shall keep your charge, the charge of all of the tent, but they shall not come close to the equipment of the holy and to the altar, so they will not die, both they and you.

tex.original: \hP{וְשָׁמְרוּ מִשְׁמַרְתְּךָ וּמִשְׁמֶרֶת כּל הָאֹהֶל אַךְ אֶל כְּלֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְאֶל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ לֹא יִקְרָבוּ וְלֹא יָמֻתוּ גַם הֵם גַּם אַתֶּם׃}

verses.original: וְנִלְווּ עָלֶיךָ וְשָׁמְרוּ אֶת מִשְׁמֶרֶת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד לְכֹל עֲבֹדַת הָאֹהֶל וְזָר לֹא יִקְרַב אֲלֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: And they shall be connected to you and shall keep the charge of the Tent of Meeting, for all the work of the tent, but an outsider shall not come close to you.

tex.original: \hP{וְנִלְווּ עָלֶיךָ וְשָׁמְרוּ אֶת מִשְׁמֶרֶת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד לְכֹל עֲבֹדַת הָאֹהֶל וְזָר לֹא יִקְרַב אֲלֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֵת מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְאֵת מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְלֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד קֶצֶף עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And you shall keep the charge of the holy and the charge of the altar, so there will not be any more rage at the children of Israel.

tex.original: \hP{וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֵת מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְאֵת מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְלֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד קֶצֶף עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַאֲנִי הִנֵּה לָקַחְתִּי אֶת אֲחֵיכֶם הַלְוִיִּם מִתּוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לָכֶם מַתָּנָה נְתֻנִים לַיהֹוָה לַעֲבֹד אֶת עֲבֹדַת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: And I, here, I have taken your brothers, the Levites from among the children of Israel as a gift to you, given for YHWH, to do the work of the Tent of Meeting.

tex.original: \hP{וַאֲנִי הִנֵּה לָקַחְתִּי אֶת אֲחֵיכֶם הַלְוִיִּם מִתּוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לָכֶם מַתָּנָה נְתֻנִים לַיהֹוָה לַעֲבֹד אֶת עֲבֹדַת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וְאַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ אִתְּךָ תִּשְׁמְרוּ אֶת כְּהֻנַּתְכֶם לְכל דְּבַר הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּלְמִבֵּית לַפָּרֹכֶת וַעֲבַדְתֶּם עֲבֹדַת מַתָּנָה אֶתֵּן אֶת כְּהֻנַּתְכֶם וְהַזָּר הַקָּרֵב יוּמָת׃
verses.english: And you and your sons with you shall watch over your priesthood for everything of the altar’s and for inside the pavilion, and you shall serve. I give your priesthood as a gift of service. And the outsider who comes close shall be put to death.”

tex.original: \hP{וְאַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ אִתְּךָ תִּשְׁמְרוּ אֶת כְּהֻנַּתְכֶם לְכל דְּבַר הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּלְמִבֵּית לַפָּרֹכֶת וַעֲבַדְתֶּם עֲבֹדַת מַתָּנָה אֶתֵּן אֶת כְּהֻנַּתְכֶם וְהַזָּר הַקָּרֵב יוּמָת׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And you and your sons with you shall watch over your
		priesthood for everything of the altar’s and for inside
		the pavilion, and you shall serve. I give your priesthood
		as a gift of service. And the outsider who comes close
		shall be put to death.”
	}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל אַהֲרֹן וַאֲנִי הִנֵּה נָתַתִּי לְךָ אֶת מִשְׁמֶרֶת תְּרוּמֹתָי לְכל קדְשֵׁי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְךָ נְתַתִּים לְמשְׁחָה וּלְבָנֶיךָ לְחק עוֹלָם׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Aaron, “And I, here, I have given charge of my donations to you for all the holy things of the children of Israel. I have given them to you as an anointing and to your sons as an eternal law.

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל אַהֲרֹן וַאֲנִי הִנֵּה נָתַתִּי לְךָ אֶת מִשְׁמֶרֶת תְּרוּמֹתָי לְכל קדְשֵׁי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְךָ נְתַתִּים לְמשְׁחָה וּלְבָנֶיךָ לְחק עוֹלָם׃}

verses.original: זֶה יִהְיֶה לְךָ מִקֹּדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים מִן הָאֵשׁ כּל קרְבָּנָם לְכל מִנְחָתָם וּלְכל חַטָּאתָם וּלְכל אֲשָׁמָם אֲשֶׁר יָשִׁיבוּ לִי קֹדֶשׁ קדָשִׁים לְךָ הוּא וּלְבָנֶיךָ׃
verses.english: This shall be yours from the holy of holies, from the fire: every offering of theirs, every grain offering of theirs and every sin offering of theirs and every guilt offering of theirs that they will pay back to me. It is holy of holies for you and for your sons.

tex.original: \hP{זֶה יִהְיֶה לְךָ מִקֹּדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים מִן הָאֵשׁ כּל קרְבָּנָם לְכל מִנְחָתָם וּלְכל חַטָּאתָם וּלְכל אֲשָׁמָם אֲשֶׁר יָשִׁיבוּ לִי קֹדֶשׁ קדָשִׁים לְךָ הוּא וּלְבָנֶיךָ׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		This shall be yours from the holy of holies, from the
		fire: every offering of theirs, every grain offering of
		theirs and every sin offering of theirs and every guilt
		offering of theirs that they will pay back to me. It is
		holy of holies for you and for your sons.
	}

verses.original: בְּקֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ כּל זָכָר יֹאכַל אֹתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ יִהְיֶה לָּךְ׃
verses.english: You shall eat it in the holy of holies. Every male shall eat it. It shall be holy to you.

tex.original: \hP{בְּקֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ כּל זָכָר יֹאכַל אֹתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ יִהְיֶה לָּךְ׃}

verses.original: וְזֶה לְּךָ תְּרוּמַת מַתָּנָם לְכל תְּנוּפֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְךָ נְתַתִּים וּלְבָנֶיךָ וְלִבְנֹתֶיךָ אִתְּךָ לְחק עוֹלָם כּל טָהוֹר בְּבֵיתְךָ יֹאכַל אֹתוֹ׃
verses.english: “And this is yours: their gift donation, all the elevation offerings of the children of Israel. I have given them to you and to your sons and to your daughters with you as an eternal law. Everyone who is pure in your house shall eat it.

tex.original: \hP{וְזֶה לְּךָ תְּרוּמַת מַתָּנָם לְכל תְּנוּפֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְךָ נְתַתִּים וּלְבָנֶיךָ וְלִבְנֹתֶיךָ אִתְּךָ לְחק עוֹלָם כּל טָהוֹר בְּבֵיתְךָ יֹאכַל אֹתוֹ׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		“And this is yours: their gift donation, all the elevation
		offerings of the children of Israel. I have given them to
		you and to your sons and to your daughters with you as an
		eternal law. Everyone who is pure in your house shall eat
		it.
	}

verses.original: כֹּל חֵלֶב יִצְהָר וְכל חֵלֶב תִּירוֹשׁ וְדָגָן רֵאשִׁיתָם אֲשֶׁר יִתְּנוּ לַיהֹוָה לְךָ נְתַתִּים׃
verses.english: “All the best of the oil and all the best of the wine and grain, the first of them that they will give to YHWH: I have given them to you.

tex.original: \hP{כֹּל חֵלֶב יִצְהָר וְכל חֵלֶב תִּירוֹשׁ וְדָגָן רֵאשִׁיתָם אֲשֶׁר יִתְּנוּ לַיהֹוָה לְךָ נְתַתִּים׃}

verses.original: בִּכּוּרֵי כּל אֲשֶׁר בְּאַרְצָם אֲשֶׁר יָבִיאוּ לַיהֹוָה לְךָ יִהְיֶה כּל טָהוֹר בְּבֵיתְךָ יֹאכְלֶנּוּ׃
verses.english: The firstfruits of everything that is in their land that they will bring to YHWH shall be yours. Everyone who is pure in your house shall eat it.

tex.original: \hP{בִּכּוּרֵי כּל אֲשֶׁר בְּאַרְצָם אֲשֶׁר יָבִיאוּ לַיהֹוָה לְךָ יִהְיֶה כּל טָהוֹר בְּבֵיתְךָ יֹאכְלֶנּוּ׃}

verses.original: כּל חֵרֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְךָ יִהְיֶה׃
verses.english: Every devoted thing in Israel shall be yours.

tex.original: \hP{כּל חֵרֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְךָ יִהְיֶה׃}
tex.english: \eP{Every devoted thing in Israel shall be yours. }

verses.original: כּל פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם לְכל בָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ לַיהֹוָה בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה יִהְיֶה לָּךְ אַךְ פָּדֹה תִפְדֶּה אֵת בְּכוֹר הָאָדָם וְאֵת בְּכוֹר הַבְּהֵמָה הַטְּמֵאָה תִּפְדֶּה׃
verses.english: Every first birth of a womb of all flesh that they will bring forward to YHWH, human and animal, shall be yours. Just: you shall redeem the human firstborn, and you shall redeem the firstborn of an impure animal.

tex.original: \hP{כּל פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם לְכל בָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ לַיהֹוָה בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה יִהְיֶה לָּךְ אַךְ פָּדֹה תִפְדֶּה אֵת בְּכוֹר הָאָדָם וְאֵת בְּכוֹר הַבְּהֵמָה הַטְּמֵאָה תִּפְדֶּה׃}

verses.original: וּפְדוּיָו מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ תִּפְדֶּה בְּעֶרְכְּךָ כֶּסֶף חֲמֵשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה הוּא׃
verses.english: And their redemption price: from one month old you shall redeem it at your appraisal, five shekels of silver by the shekel of the Holy. It is twenty gerah.

tex.original: \hP{וּפְדוּיָו מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ תִּפְדֶּה בְּעֶרְכְּךָ כֶּסֶף חֲמֵשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה הוּא׃}

verses.original: אַךְ בְּכוֹר שׁוֹר אוֹ בְכוֹר כֶּשֶׂב אוֹ בְכוֹר עֵז לֹא תִפְדֶּה קֹדֶשׁ הֵם אֶת דָּמָם תִּזְרֹק עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְאֶת חֶלְבָּם תַּקְטִיר אִשֶּׁה לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Just: you shall not redeem a firstborn of an ox or firstborn of a sheep or firstborn of a goat. They are holy. You shall fling their blood on the altar and burn their fat to smoke, a fire offering for a pleasant smell to YHWH.

tex.original: \hP{אַךְ בְּכוֹר שׁוֹר אוֹ בְכוֹר כֶּשֶׂב אוֹ בְכוֹר עֵז לֹא תִפְדֶּה קֹדֶשׁ הֵם אֶת דָּמָם תִּזְרֹק עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְאֶת חֶלְבָּם תַּקְטִיר אִשֶּׁה לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		Just: you shall not redeem a firstborn of an ox or
		firstborn of a sheep or firstborn of a goat. They are
		holy. You shall fling their blood on the altar and burn
		their fat to smoke, a fire offering for a pleasant smell
		to YHWH.
	}

verses.original: וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָּךְ כַּחֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה וּכְשׁוֹק הַיָּמִין לְךָ יִהְיֶה׃
verses.english: And their meat shall be yours; like the breast of the elevation offering and the right thigh it shall be yours.

tex.original: \hP{וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָּךְ כַּחֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה וּכְשׁוֹק הַיָּמִין לְךָ יִהְיֶה׃}

verses.original: כֹּל תְּרוּמֹת הַקֳּדָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר יָרִימוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לַיהֹוָה נָתַתִּי לְךָ וּלְבָנֶיךָ וְלִבְנֹתֶיךָ אִתְּךָ לְחק עוֹלָם בְּרִית מֶלַח עוֹלָם הִוא לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לְךָ וּלְזַרְעֲךָ אִתָּךְ׃
verses.english: All the donations of the holy things that the children of Israel will donate to YHWH I have given to you and to your sons and to your daughters with you as an eternal law. It is an eternal covenant of salt in front of YHWH for you and for your seed with you.”

tex.original: \hP{כֹּל תְּרוּמֹת הַקֳּדָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר יָרִימוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לַיהֹוָה נָתַתִּי לְךָ וּלְבָנֶיךָ וְלִבְנֹתֶיךָ אִתְּךָ לְחק עוֹלָם בְּרִית מֶלַח עוֹלָם הִוא לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לְךָ וּלְזַרְעֲךָ אִתָּךְ׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		All the donations of the holy things that the children of
		Israel will donate to YHWH I have given to you and to your
		sons and to your daughters with you as an eternal law. It
		is an eternal covenant of salt in front of YHWH for you
		and for your seed with you.”
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		covenant of salt. Salt is associated with the offerings that are given
%		to the priests. Lev 2:13 emphasizes, “You shall sprinkle every offering
%		of a grain offering with salt. And you shall not let the salt of your
%		God’s covenant cease from on your grain offering; you shall bring salt
%		on all your offerings.” (Some take the fact that salt is a preservative
%		to imply that “covenant of salt” means a long-lasting covenant.) It is a
%		custom to this day to sprinkle some salt on the bread at the Sabbath
%		meal as a memorial of this practice.
%	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל אַהֲרֹן בְּאַרְצָם לֹא תִנְחָל וְחֵלֶק לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ בְּתוֹכָם אֲנִי חֶלְקְךָ וְנַחֲלָתְךָ בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Aaron, “You shall not have a legacy in their land, and you shall not have a portion among them. I am your portion and your legacy among the children of Israel.

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל אַהֲרֹן בְּאַרְצָם לֹא תִנְחָל וְחֵלֶק לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ בְּתוֹכָם אֲנִי חֶלְקְךָ וְנַחֲלָתְךָ בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וְלִבְנֵי לֵוִי הִנֵּה נָתַתִּי כּל מַעֲשֵׂר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְנַחֲלָה חֵלֶף עֲבֹדָתָם אֲשֶׁר הֵם עֹבְדִים אֶת עֲבֹדַת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: And to the children of Levi, here, I’ve given every tithe in Israel as a legacy in exchange for their work that they’re doing, the service of the Tent of Meeting.

tex.original: \hP{וְלִבְנֵי לֵוִי הִנֵּה נָתַתִּי כּל מַעֲשֵׂר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְנַחֲלָה חֵלֶף עֲבֹדָתָם אֲשֶׁר הֵם עֹבְדִים אֶת עֲבֹדַת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא יִקְרְבוּ עוֹד בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד לָשֵׂאת חֵטְא לָמוּת׃
verses.english: And the children of Israel shall not come near to the Tent of Meeting anymore so as to bear sin and die.

tex.original: \hP{וְלֹא יִקְרְבוּ עוֹד בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד לָשֵׂאת חֵטְא לָמוּת׃}

verses.original: וְעָבַד הַלֵּוִי הוּא אֶת עֲבֹדַת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וְהֵם יִשְׂאוּ עֲוֺנָם חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם וּבְתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יִנְחֲלוּ נַחֲלָה׃
verses.english: But he, the Levite, shall do the service of the Tent of Meeting, and they shall bear their crime. It is an eternal law through your generations. And they shall not have a legacy among the children of Israel,

tex.original: \hP{וְעָבַד הַלֵּוִי הוּא אֶת עֲבֹדַת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וְהֵם יִשְׂאוּ עֲוֺנָם חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם וּבְתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יִנְחֲלוּ נַחֲלָה׃}

verses.original: כִּי אֶת מַעְשַׂר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר יָרִימוּ לַיהֹוָה תְּרוּמָה נָתַתִּי לַלְוִיִּם לְנַחֲלָה עַל כֵּן אָמַרְתִּי לָהֶם בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יִנְחֲלוּ נַחֲלָה׃
verses.english: because I’ve given to the Levites as a legacy the tithe of the children of Israel that they will give to YHWH as a donation. On account of this I’ve said to them: they shall not have a legacy among the children of Israel.”

tex.original: \hP{כִּי אֶת מַעְשַׂר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר יָרִימוּ לַיהֹוָה תְּרוּמָה נָתַתִּי לַלְוִיִּם לְנַחֲלָה עַל כֵּן אָמַרְתִּי לָהֶם בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יִנְחֲלוּ נַחֲלָה׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: וְאֶל הַלְוִיִּם תְּדַבֵּר וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם כִּי תִקְחוּ מֵאֵת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַמַּעֲשֵׂר אֲשֶׁר נָתַתִּי לָכֶם מֵאִתָּם בְּנַחֲלַתְכֶם וַהֲרֵמֹתֶם מִמֶּנּוּ תְּרוּמַת יְהֹוָה מַעֲשֵׂר מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר׃
verses.english: “And you shall speak to the Levites and say to them: ‘When you will take the tithe from the children of Israel that I have given you from them as your legacy, then you shall make a donation for YHWH from it, a tithe of the tithe.

tex.original: \hP{וְאֶל הַלְוִיִּם תְּדַבֵּר וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם כִּי תִקְחוּ מֵאֵת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַמַּעֲשֵׂר אֲשֶׁר נָתַתִּי לָכֶם מֵאִתָּם בְּנַחֲלַתְכֶם וַהֲרֵמֹתֶם מִמֶּנּוּ תְּרוּמַת יְהֹוָה מַעֲשֵׂר מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר׃}

verses.original: וְנֶחְשַׁב לָכֶם תְּרוּמַתְכֶם כַּדָּגָן מִן הַגֹּרֶן וְכַמְלֵאָה מִן הַיָּקֶב׃
verses.english: And it will be counted for you as your donation, like grain from the threshing floor and like the fill of the winepress.

tex.original: \hP{וְנֶחְשַׁב לָכֶם תְּרוּמַתְכֶם כַּדָּגָן מִן הַגֹּרֶן וְכַמְלֵאָה מִן הַיָּקֶב׃}

verses.original: כֵּן תָּרִימוּ גַם אַתֶּם תְּרוּמַת יְהֹוָה מִכֹּל מַעְשְׂרֹתֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר תִּקְחוּ מֵאֵת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּנְתַתֶּם מִמֶּנּוּ אֶת תְּרוּמַת יְהֹוָה לְאַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן׃
verses.english: So you shall donate, you too, a donation for YHWH from all your tithes that you will take from the children of Israel, and you shall give a donation for YHWH to Aaron, the priest, from them.

tex.original: \hP{כֵּן תָּרִימוּ גַם אַתֶּם תְּרוּמַת יְהֹוָה מִכֹּל מַעְשְׂרֹתֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר תִּקְחוּ מֵאֵת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּנְתַתֶּם מִמֶּנּוּ אֶת תְּרוּמַת יְהֹוָה לְאַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן׃}

verses.original: מִכֹּל מַתְּנֹתֵיכֶם תָּרִימוּ אֵת כּל תְּרוּמַת יְהֹוָה מִכּל חֶלְבּוֹ אֶת מִקְדְּשׁוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ׃
verses.english: From all your gifts you shall make every donation for YHWH, from all the best of it, its holy part from it.’

tex.original: \hP{מִכֹּל מַתְּנֹתֵיכֶם תָּרִימוּ אֵת כּל תְּרוּמַת יְהֹוָה מִכּל חֶלְבּוֹ אֶת מִקְדְּשׁוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ׃}

verses.original: וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם בַּהֲרִימְכֶם אֶת חֶלְבּוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ וְנֶחְשַׁב לַלְוִיִּם כִּתְבוּאַת גֹּרֶן וְכִתְבוּאַת יָקֶב׃
verses.english: And you shall say to them: ‘When you donate the best of it from it, then it shall be counted to the Levites like the produce of the threshing floor and like the produce of the winepress.

tex.original: \hP{וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם בַּהֲרִימְכֶם אֶת חֶלְבּוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ וְנֶחְשַׁב לַלְוִיִּם כִּתְבוּאַת גֹּרֶן וְכִתְבוּאַת יָקֶב׃}

verses.original: וַאֲכַלְתֶּם אֹתוֹ בְּכל מָקוֹם אַתֶּם וּבֵיתְכֶם כִּי שָׂכָר הוּא לָכֶם חֵלֶף עֲבֹדַתְכֶם בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: And you shall eat it in every place, you and your house, because it is compensation for you in exchange for your work in the Tent of Meeting.

tex.original: \hP{וַאֲכַלְתֶּם אֹתוֹ בְּכל מָקוֹם אַתֶּם וּבֵיתְכֶם כִּי שָׂכָר הוּא לָכֶם חֵלֶף עֲבֹדַתְכֶם בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא תִשְׂאוּ עָלָיו חֵטְא בַּהֲרִימְכֶם אֶת חֶלְבּוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ וְאֶת קדְשֵׁי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תְחַלְּלוּ וְלֹא תָמוּתוּ׃
verses.english: And you will not bear sin over it, when you have donated its best from it, so you will not desecrate the holy things of the children of Israel, and you will not die.’”

tex.original: \hP{וְלֹא תִשְׂאוּ עָלָיו חֵטְא בַּהֲרִימְכֶם אֶת חֶלְבּוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ וְאֶת קדְשֵׁי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא תְחַלְּלוּ וְלֹא תָמוּתוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן לֵאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן לֵאמֹר׃}

verses.original: זֹאת חֻקַּת הַתּוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה לֵאמֹר דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיִקְחוּ אֵלֶיךָ פָרָה אֲדֻמָּה תְּמִימָה אֲשֶׁר אֵין בָּהּ מוּם אֲשֶׁר לֹא עָלָה עָלֶיהָ עֹל׃
verses.english: “This is the law of the instruction that YHWH commanded, saying: Speak to the children of Israel that they should take to you an unblemished red cow that has no injury, on which a yoke has not gone.

tex.original: \hP{זֹאת חֻקַּת הַתּוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה לֵאמֹר דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיִקְחוּ אֵלֶיךָ פָרָה אֲדֻמָּה תְּמִימָה אֲשֶׁר אֵין בָּהּ מוּם אֲשֶׁר לֹא עָלָה עָלֶיהָ עֹל׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		law. Legal texts are worked in at various points of the wilderness
%		narrative, thus conveying that not all of the law has been revealed at
%		Sinai, but that the law rather continues to be elaborated upon and added
%		to as the people move closer to the land. Also through this construction
%		the revelation of the law comes to be pictured as an ongoing part of the
%		people’s life, and it is understood to be part of the new, post–exodus
%		generation’s experience—and thus the possession of the people who will
%		carry it into the promised land.
%	}

verses.original: וּנְתַתֶּם אֹתָהּ אֶל אֶלְעָזָר הַכֹּהֵן וְהוֹצִיא אֹתָהּ אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה וְשָׁחַט אֹתָהּ לְפָנָיו׃
verses.english: And you shall give it to Eleazar, the priest, and one shall bring it outside the camp and slaughter it in front of him.

tex.original: \hP{וּנְתַתֶּם אֹתָהּ אֶל אֶלְעָזָר הַכֹּהֵן וְהוֹצִיא אֹתָהּ אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה וְשָׁחַט אֹתָהּ לְפָנָיו׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Eleazar. Here and in the matter of the fire-holders after the Korah
%		rebellion (17:2), Eleazar, Aaron’s oldest surviving son, is directly
%		commanded for the first time. It is as if the text is anticipating the
%		events of the next chapter (20), in which Aaron will suffer the same
%		fate as Moses: to die before reaching the promised land. The conclusion
%		of that story recounts the succession of Eleazar to Aaron’s place as
%		high priest (20:23–28). These first commands to Eleazar thus appear to
%		be a preparation for the moment of succession. Part of the task of a
%		wise leader is to prepare a successor.
%	}

verses.original: וְלָקַח אֶלְעָזָר הַכֹּהֵן מִדָּמָהּ בְּאֶצְבָּעוֹ וְהִזָּה אֶל נֹכַח פְּנֵי אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד מִדָּמָהּ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים׃
verses.english: And Eleazar, the priest, shall take some of its blood with his finger and sprinkle some of its blood toward the front of the Tent of Meeting seven times.

tex.original: \hP{וְלָקַח אֶלְעָזָר הַכֹּהֵן מִדָּמָהּ בְּאֶצְבָּעוֹ וְהִזָּה אֶל נֹכַח פְּנֵי אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד מִדָּמָהּ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים׃}

verses.original: וְשָׂרַף אֶת הַפָּרָה לְעֵינָיו אֶת עֹרָהּ וְאֶת בְּשָׂרָהּ וְאֶת דָּמָהּ עַל פִּרְשָׁהּ יִשְׂרֹף׃
verses.english: And one shall burn the cow before his eyes. He shall burn its skin and its meat and its blood and its dung.

tex.original: \hP{וְשָׂרַף אֶת הַפָּרָה לְעֵינָיו אֶת עֹרָהּ וְאֶת בְּשָׂרָהּ וְאֶת דָּמָהּ עַל פִּרְשָׁהּ יִשְׂרֹף׃}

verses.original: וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן עֵץ אֶרֶז וְאֵזוֹב וּשְׁנִי תוֹלָעַת וְהִשְׁלִיךְ אֶל תּוֹךְ שְׂרֵפַת הַפָּרָה׃
verses.english: And the priest shall take cedarwood and hyssop and scarlet and throw them into the fire of the cow.

tex.original: \hP{וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן עֵץ אֶרֶז וְאֵזוֹב וּשְׁנִי תוֹלָעַת וְהִשְׁלִיךְ אֶל תּוֹךְ שְׂרֵפַת הַפָּרָה׃}

verses.original: וְכִבֶּס בְּגָדָיו הַכֹּהֵן וְרָחַץ בְּשָׂרוֹ בַּמַּיִם וְאַחַר יָבֹא אֶל הַמַּחֲנֶה וְטָמֵא הַכֹּהֵן עַד הָעָרֶב׃
verses.english: And the priest shall wash his clothes and wash his flesh with water, and after that he shall come to the camp, and the priest shall be impure until evening.

tex.original: \hP{וְכִבֶּס בְּגָדָיו הַכֹּהֵן וְרָחַץ בְּשָׂרוֹ בַּמַּיִם וְאַחַר יָבֹא אֶל הַמַּחֲנֶה וְטָמֵא הַכֹּהֵן עַד הָעָרֶב׃}

verses.original: וְהַשֹּׂרֵף אֹתָהּ יְכַבֵּס בְּגָדָיו בַּמַּיִם וְרָחַץ בְּשָׂרוֹ בַּמָּיִם וְטָמֵא עַד הָעָרֶב׃
verses.english: And the one who burns it shall wash his clothes with water and wash his flesh with water and be impure until evening.

tex.original: \hP{וְהַשֹּׂרֵף אֹתָהּ יְכַבֵּס בְּגָדָיו בַּמַּיִם וְרָחַץ בְּשָׂרוֹ בַּמָּיִם וְטָמֵא עַד הָעָרֶב׃}

verses.original: וְאָסַף אִישׁ טָהוֹר אֵת אֵפֶר הַפָּרָה וְהִנִּיחַ מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה בְּמָקוֹם טָהוֹר וְהָיְתָה לַעֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת לְמֵי נִדָּה חַטָּאת הִוא׃
verses.english: And a man who is pure shall gather the cow’s ashes and leave them outside the camp in a pure place, and it shall be for the congregation of the children of Israel to be kept for water of impurity, for sin expiation.

tex.original: \hP{וְאָסַף אִישׁ טָהוֹר אֵת אֵפֶר הַפָּרָה וְהִנִּיחַ מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה בְּמָקוֹם טָהוֹר וְהָיְתָה לַעֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת לְמֵי נִדָּה חַטָּאת הִוא׃}

verses.original: וְכִבֶּס הָאֹסֵף אֶת אֵפֶר הַפָּרָה אֶת בְּגָדָיו וְטָמֵא עַד הָעָרֶב וְהָיְתָה לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר בְּתוֹכָם לְחֻקַּת עוֹלָם׃
verses.english: And the one who gathers the cow’s ashes shall wash his clothes and be impure until evening. And it will be for the children of Israel and for the alien who resides among them as an eternal law.

tex.original: \hP{וְכִבֶּס הָאֹסֵף אֶת אֵפֶר הַפָּרָה אֶת בְּגָדָיו וְטָמֵא עַד הָעָרֶב וְהָיְתָה לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלַגֵּר הַגָּר בְּתוֹכָם לְחֻקַּת עוֹלָם׃}

verses.original: הַנֹּגֵעַ בְּמֵת לְכל נֶפֶשׁ אָדָם וְטָמֵא שִׁבְעַת יָמִים׃
verses.english: “One who touches a dead body of any human being will be impure seven days.

tex.original: \hP{הַנֹּגֵעַ בְּמֵת לְכל נֶפֶשׁ אָדָם וְטָמֵא שִׁבְעַת יָמִים׃}

verses.original: הוּא יִתְחַטָּא בוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי יִטְהָר וְאִם לֹא יִתְחַטָּא בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי לֹא יִטְהָר׃
verses.english: He shall do sin expiation with it on the third day, and on the seventh day he will be pure. And if he will not do sin expiation on the third day, then on the seventh day he will not be pure.

tex.original: \hP{הוּא יִתְחַטָּא בוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי יִטְהָר וְאִם לֹא יִתְחַטָּא בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי לֹא יִטְהָר׃}

verses.original: כּל הַנֹּגֵעַ בְּמֵת בְּנֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר יָמוּת וְלֹא יִתְחַטָּא אֶת מִשְׁכַּן יְהֹוָה טִמֵּא וְנִכְרְתָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל כִּי מֵי נִדָּה לֹא זֹרַק עָלָיו טָמֵא יִהְיֶה עוֹד טֻמְאָתוֹ בוֹ׃
verses.english: Anyone who touches a dead body of a human being who has died and does not do sin expiation has made YHWH’s Tabernacle impure, and that person will be cut off from Israel. Because the water of impurity was not flung on him, he shall be impure. His impurity is still in him.

tex.original: \hP{כּל הַנֹּגֵעַ בְּמֵת בְּנֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר יָמוּת וְלֹא יִתְחַטָּא אֶת מִשְׁכַּן יְהֹוָה טִמֵּא וְנִכְרְתָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל כִּי מֵי נִדָּה לֹא זֹרַק עָלָיו טָמֵא יִהְיֶה עוֹד טֻמְאָתוֹ בוֹ׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		Anyone who touches a dead body of a human being who has
		died and does not do sin expiation has made YHWH’s
		Tabernacle impure, and that person will be cut off from
		Israel. Because the water of impurity was not flung on
		him, he shall be impure. His impurity is still in him.
	}

verses.original: זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה אָדָם כִּי יָמוּת בְּאֹהֶל כּל הַבָּא אֶל הָאֹהֶל וְכל אֲשֶׁר בָּאֹהֶל יִטְמָא שִׁבְעַת יָמִים׃
verses.english: “This is the instruction: When a human will die in a tent, anyone who comes into the tent and everything that is in the tent will be impure seven days.

tex.original: \hP{זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה אָדָם כִּי יָמוּת בְּאֹהֶל כּל הַבָּא אֶל הָאֹהֶל וְכל אֲשֶׁר בָּאֹהֶל יִטְמָא שִׁבְעַת יָמִים׃}

verses.original: וְכֹל כְּלִי פָתוּחַ אֲשֶׁר אֵין צָמִיד פָּתִיל עָלָיו טָמֵא הוּא׃
verses.english: And any open container, on which there is not a fastened cover: it is impure.

tex.original: \hP{וְכֹל כְּלִי פָתוּחַ אֲשֶׁר אֵין צָמִיד פָּתִיל עָלָיו טָמֵא הוּא׃}

verses.original: וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע עַל פְּנֵי הַשָּׂדֶה בַּחֲלַל חֶרֶב אוֹ בְמֵת אוֹ בְעֶצֶם אָדָם אוֹ בְקָבֶר יִטְמָא שִׁבְעַת יָמִים׃
verses.english: And anyone who, at an open field, will touch a corpse slain by the sword or a dead body or a human bone or a grave will be impure seven days.

tex.original: \hP{וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע עַל פְּנֵי הַשָּׂדֶה בַּחֲלַל חֶרֶב אוֹ בְמֵת אוֹ בְעֶצֶם אָדָם אוֹ בְקָבֶר יִטְמָא שִׁבְעַת יָמִים׃}

verses.original: וְלָקְחוּ לַטָּמֵא מֵעֲפַר שְׂרֵפַת הַחַטָּאת וְנָתַן עָלָיו מַיִם חַיִּים אֶל כֶּלִי׃
verses.english: And they shall take for the one who is impure some of the ashes of the fire of sin expiation, and one shall put living water on it in a container.

tex.original: \hP{וְלָקְחוּ לַטָּמֵא מֵעֲפַר שְׂרֵפַת הַחַטָּאת וְנָתַן עָלָיו מַיִם חַיִּים אֶל כֶּלִי׃}

verses.original: וְלָקַח אֵזוֹב וְטָבַל בַּמַּיִם אִישׁ טָהוֹר וְהִזָּה עַל הָאֹהֶל וְעַל כּל הַכֵּלִים וְעַל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת אֲשֶׁר הָיוּ שָׁם וְעַל הַנֹּגֵעַ בַּעֶצֶם אוֹ בֶחָלָל אוֹ בַמֵּת אוֹ בַקָּבֶר׃
verses.english: And a man who is pure shall take hyssop and dip it in the water and sprinkle it on the tent and on all the items and on the persons who were there and on the one who touched the bone or the slain corpse or the dead body or the grave.

tex.original: \hP{וְלָקַח אֵזוֹב וְטָבַל בַּמַּיִם אִישׁ טָהוֹר וְהִזָּה עַל הָאֹהֶל וְעַל כּל הַכֵּלִים וְעַל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת אֲשֶׁר הָיוּ שָׁם וְעַל הַנֹּגֵעַ בַּעֶצֶם אוֹ בֶחָלָל אוֹ בַמֵּת אוֹ בַקָּבֶר׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		And a man who is pure shall take hyssop and dip it in the
		water and sprinkle it on the tent and on all the items and
		on the persons who were there and on the one who touched
		the bone or the slain corpse or the dead body or the
		grave.
	}

verses.original: וְהִזָּה הַטָּהֹר עַל הַטָּמֵא בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי וְחִטְּאוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי וְכִבֶּס בְּגָדָיו וְרָחַץ בַּמַּיִם וְטָהֵר בָּעָרֶב׃
verses.english: And the one who is pure shall sprinkle it on the impure on the third day and on the seventh day, so he shall expiate sin from him on the seventh day, and he shall wash his clothes and wash in water and be pure in the evening.

tex.original: \hP{וְהִזָּה הַטָּהֹר עַל הַטָּמֵא בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי וְחִטְּאוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי וְכִבֶּס בְּגָדָיו וְרָחַץ בַּמַּיִם וְטָהֵר בָּעָרֶב׃}

verses.original: וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִטְמָא וְלֹא יִתְחַטָּא וְנִכְרְתָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא מִתּוֹךְ הַקָּהָל כִּי אֶת מִקְדַּשׁ יְהֹוָה טִמֵּא מֵי נִדָּה לֹא זֹרַק עָלָיו טָמֵא הוּא׃
verses.english: And if a man will be impure and will not do sin expiation, then that person will be cut off from among the community, because he has made YHWH’s holy place impure. The water of impurity has not been flung on him: he is impure.

tex.original: \hP{וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִטְמָא וְלֹא יִתְחַטָּא וְנִכְרְתָה הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא מִתּוֹךְ הַקָּהָל כִּי אֶת מִקְדַּשׁ יְהֹוָה טִמֵּא מֵי נִדָּה לֹא זֹרַק עָלָיו טָמֵא הוּא׃}

verses.original: וְהָיְתָה לָהֶם לְחֻקַּת עוֹלָם וּמַזֵּה מֵי הַנִּדָּה יְכַבֵּס בְּגָדָיו וְהַנֹּגֵעַ בְּמֵי הַנִּדָּה יִטְמָא עַד הָעָרֶב׃
verses.english: And it will become an eternal law for them. And one who sprinkles the water of impurity shall wash his clothes, and one who touches the water of impurity will be impure until evening.

tex.original: \hP{וְהָיְתָה לָהֶם לְחֻקַּת עוֹלָם וּמַזֵּה מֵי הַנִּדָּה יְכַבֵּס בְּגָדָיו וְהַנֹּגֵעַ בְּמֵי הַנִּדָּה יִטְמָא עַד הָעָרֶב׃}

verses.original: וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בּוֹ הַטָּמֵא יִטְמָא וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ הַנֹּגַעַת תִּטְמָא עַד הָעָרֶב׃
verses.english: And whatever the impure one will touch will be impure, and the person who touches it will be impure until evening.”

tex.original: \hP{וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בּוֹ הַטָּמֵא יִטְמָא וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ הַנֹּגַעַת תִּטְמָא עַד הָעָרֶב׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כּל הָעֵדָה מִדְבַּר צִן בַּחֹדֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן וַיֵּשֶׁב הָעָם בְּקָדֵשׁ וַתָּמת שָׁם מִרְיָם וַתִּקָּבֵר שָׁם׃
verses.english: And the children of Israel, all the congregation, came to the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people stayed in Kadesh. And Miriam died there and was buried there.

tex.original:
\hR{וַיָּבֹאוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כּל הָעֵדָה}
	\hP{מִדְבַּר צִן בַּחֹדֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן וַיֵּשֶׁב הָעָם בְּקָדֵשׁ וַתָּמת שָׁם מִרְיָם וַתִּקָּבֵר שָׁם׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא הָיָה מַיִם לָעֵדָה וַיִּקָּהֲלוּ עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעַל אַהֲרֹן׃
verses.english: And there was no water for the congregation, and they assembled against Moses and against Aaron.

tex.original: \hP{וְלֹא הָיָה מַיִם לָעֵדָה וַיִּקָּהֲלוּ עַל מֹשֶׁה וְעַל אַהֲרֹן׃}

verses.original: וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם מֹשֶׁה וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֵאמֹר וְלוּ גָוַעְנוּ בִּגְוַע אַחֵינוּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: And the people quarreled with Moses, and they said, saying, “If only we had expired when our brothers expired in front of YHWH!
verses.commentary: REF: This is a doublet of the E story of the water from the crag at Meribah (Exodus 17). This version of the story shows signs of P. It uses the terms “expire,” “congregation,” and “community,” and refers to the Tent of Meeting. It deals with the question of who is holy, specifically in terms of a challenge to Aaron’s exclusive right to the priesthood by his cousin Korah. Also, it continues from the preceding P story (see the next note).

tex.original: \hP{וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם מֹשֶׁה וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֵאמֹר וְלוּ גָוַעְנוּ בִּגְוַע אַחֵינוּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃}
tex.commentary: \fC{REF: This is a doublet of the E story of the water from the crag at Meribah (Exodus 17). This version of the story shows signs of P. It uses the terms “expire,” “congregation,” and “community,” and refers to the Tent of Meeting. It deals with the question of who is holy, specifically in terms of a challenge to Aaron’s exclusive right to the priesthood by his cousin Korah. Also, it continues from the preceding P story (see the next note).}

verses.original: וְלָמָה הֲבֵאתֶם אֶת קְהַל יְהֹוָה אֶל הַמִּדְבָּר הַזֶּה לָמוּת שָׁם אֲנַחְנוּ וּבְעִירֵנוּ׃
verses.english: And why have you brought YHWH’s community to this wilderness to die there, we and our cattle?

tex.original: \hP{וְלָמָה הֲבֵאתֶם אֶת קְהַל יְהֹוָה אֶל הַמִּדְבָּר הַזֶּה לָמוּת שָׁם אֲנַחְנוּ וּבְעִירֵנוּ׃}

verses.original: וְלָמָה הֶעֱלִיתֻנוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם לְהָבִיא אֹתָנוּ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם הָרָע הַזֶּה לֹא מְקוֹם זֶרַע וּתְאֵנָה וְגֶפֶן וְרִמּוֹן וּמַיִם אַיִן לִשְׁתּוֹת׃
verses.english: And why did you bring us up from Egypt to bring us to this bad place? It’s not a place of seed and fig and vine and pomegranate, and there’s no water to drink!”

tex.original: \hP{וְלָמָה הֶעֱלִיתֻנוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם לְהָבִיא אֹתָנוּ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם הָרָע הַזֶּה לֹא מְקוֹם זֶרַע וּתְאֵנָה וְגֶפֶן וְרִמּוֹן וּמַיִם אַיִן לִשְׁתּוֹת׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן מִפְּנֵי הַקָּהָל אֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וַיִּפְּלוּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶם וַיֵּרָא כְבוֹד יְהֹוָה אֲלֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: And Moses and Aaron came from in front of the community to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and they fell on their faces. And YHWH’s glory appeared to them.

tex.original: \hP{וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן מִפְּנֵי הַקָּהָל אֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וַיִּפְּלוּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶם וַיֵּרָא כְבוֹד יְהֹוָה אֲלֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃
verses.english: And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

tex.original: \hP{וַיְדַבֵּר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eP{And YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,}

verses.original: קַח אֶת הַמַּטֶּה וְהַקְהֵל אֶת הָעֵדָה אַתָּה וְאַהֲרֹן אָחִיךָ וְדִבַּרְתֶּם אֶל הַסֶּלַע לְעֵינֵיהֶם וְנָתַן מֵימָיו וְהוֹצֵאתָ לָהֶם מַיִם מִן הַסֶּלַע וְהִשְׁקִיתָ אֶת הָעֵדָה וְאֶת בְּעִירָם׃
verses.english: “Take the staff and assemble the congregation, you and Aaron, your brother. And you shall speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will give its water. So you shall bring water out of the rock for them and give a drink to the congregation and their cattle.”

tex.original: \hP{קַח אֶת הַמַּטֶּה וְהַקְהֵל אֶת הָעֵדָה אַתָּה וְאַהֲרֹן אָחִיךָ וְדִבַּרְתֶּם אֶל הַסֶּלַע לְעֵינֵיהֶם וְנָתַן מֵימָיו וְהוֹצֵאתָ לָהֶם מַיִם מִן הַסֶּלַע וְהִשְׁקִיתָ אֶת הָעֵדָה וְאֶת בְּעִירָם׃}
tex.english:
\eP{
		“Take the staff and assemble the congregation, you and
		Aaron, your brother. And you shall speak to the rock
		before their eyes, and it will give its water. So you
		shall bring water out of the rock for them and give a
		drink to the congregation and their cattle.”
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Take the staff and … speak to the rock. Why does he need the staff if he
%		is only supposed to speak to the rock?! Some might say that God is
%		testing Moses. But the reason for taking the staff is already given in
%		the story of Aaron’s blossoming staff. Moses is told there to “put back
%		Aaron’s staff in front of the Testimony … for a sign to rebels” (Num
%		17:25). The text now says that Moses “took the staff from in front of
%		YHWH” (20:9). This expression would normally be expected to mean that he
%		took a staff that was located at the ark in the Tent of Meeting, “in
%		front of YHWH.” William Propp has pointed out that this connects back to
%		the staff of Aaron that miraculously blossomed and was placed before the
%		ark in the preceding episode. As quoted above, its purpose, explicitly,
%		was to be “a sign to rebels.” That is why Moses is supposed to carry it
%		in his hand in the people’s sight while dealing with their rebellion. As
%		he holds it, his first words to the people are in fact “Listen, rebels”
%		(19:10). And that is why Aaron is implicated by its misuse even though
%		Aaron does not say or do anything at the rock. It is his staff, with his
%		name on it, to be kept in a holy place and used in specific
%		circumstances. As we have seen in Leviticus, intent is not the issue in
%		the realm of ritual. Rather, actions relating to sacred objects and
%		boundaries bring necessary consequences of themselves. Whether or not
%		Aaron has thought or done anything improper, he is tied to what has
%		happened. Footnote 20:8. you shall speak. It is a plural: both Moses and
%		Aaron are supposed to speak to the rock. Footnote 20:8. rock. This is a
%		different word from the one in the other story of Moses striking a rock
%		to get water (Exod 17:1–7). There it is a crag (ûr) of Mount
%		Horeb (Sinai). Here it is a rock (sela‘) in the wilderness. In Moses’
%		last blessings to the people before he dies, he will speak of God as
%		Israel’s ûr (Deut 32:4,15,18,30,31,37); i.e., he uses the word
%		that recalls the water-from-the-rock episode that came out well, not the
%		present episode, which comes out disastrously for himself and Aaron.
%	}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַמַּטֶּה מִלִּפְנֵי יְהֹוָה כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּהוּ׃
verses.english: And Moses took the staff from in front of YHWH as He commanded him.

tex.original: \hP{וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַמַּטֶּה מִלִּפְנֵי יְהֹוָה כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּהוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיַּקְהִלוּ מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן אֶת הַקָּהָל אֶל פְּנֵי הַסָּלַע וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם שִׁמְעוּ נָא הַמֹּרִים הֲמִן הַסֶּלַע הַזֶּה נוֹצִיא לָכֶם מָיִם׃
verses.english: And Moses and Aaron assembled the community opposite the rock. And he said to them, “Listen, rebels, shall we bring water out of this rock for you?”

tex.original: \hP{וַיַּקְהִלוּ מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן אֶת הַקָּהָל אֶל פְּנֵי הַסָּלַע וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם שִׁמְעוּ נָא הַמֹּרִים הֲמִן הַסֶּלַע הַזֶּה נוֹצִיא לָכֶם מָיִם׃}

verses.original: וַיָּרֶם מֹשֶׁה אֶת יָדוֹ וַיַּךְ אֶת הַסֶּלַע בְּמַטֵּהוּ פַּעֲמָיִם וַיֵּצְאוּ מַיִם רַבִּים וַתֵּשְׁתְּ הָעֵדָה וּבְעִירָם׃
verses.english: And Moses lifted his hand and struck the rock with his staff twice. And much water came out! And the congregation and their cattle drank.

tex.original: \hP{וַיָּרֶם מֹשֶׁה אֶת יָדוֹ וַיַּךְ אֶת הַסֶּלַע בְּמַטֵּהוּ פַּעֲמָיִם וַיֵּצְאוּ מַיִם רַבִּים וַתֵּשְׁתְּ הָעֵדָה וּבְעִירָם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		water came out! Moses is supposed to speak to the rock, but he hits it.
%		So why does the miracle still work?! We might surmise that it means that
%		God makes it happen so as not to humiliate Moses. Or the explanation may
%		be that the miraculous power is in the staff, which is the one that
%		miraculously blossomed. Whatever the reason, though, the fact remains:
%		for the first time in the Bible, a human has changed a miracle. This is
%		an all-important step in a gradual shift in the balance of control of
%		miraculous phenomena in the Tanak. Adam, Noah, Abraham, and Isaac
%		perform no miracles. But Jacob manipulates the coloring of Laban’s
%		flock. Then Joseph interprets dreams. Then Moses and Aaron perform God’s
%		miracles. And now Moses changes a miracle. This shift will continue in
%		the biblical books that follow the Torah, and it is one of the central
%		developments of the Bible: Joshua will call for the sun to stand still
%		in the skies. By calling for a miracle on his own, without direction
%		from God, he goes even further than Moses. Later, Samson has powers
%		implanted in him at birth, so that he is free to use them as he wishes
%		all his life. Later still, Elijah and Elisha use miracles for a variety
%		of personal purposes. It appears that, starting with Moses, God is
%		entrusting humans with ever more responsibility and control of their
%		destiny. By the end of the Tanak, miracles cease. There are no visible
%		miracles in the late books of Ezra, Nehemiah, and Esther. Humans rather
%		must direct their destiny with their own natural human powers, not with
%		endowments of miraculous powers from God. Through the course of the
%		Tanak, humans are forced to grow up and become more self-reliant.
%	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן יַעַן לֹא הֶאֱמַנְתֶּם בִּי לְהַקְדִּישֵׁנִי לְעֵינֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לָכֵן לֹא תָבִיאוּ אֶת הַקָּהָל הַזֶּה אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נָתַתִּי לָהֶם׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses and to Aaron, “Because you did not trust in me, to make me holy before the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore you shall not bring this community to the land that I have given them!”

tex.original: \hP{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל אַהֲרֹן יַעַן לֹא הֶאֱמַנְתֶּם בִּי לְהַקְדִּישֵׁנִי לְעֵינֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לָכֵן לֹא תָבִיאוּ אֶת הַקָּהָל הַזֶּה אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נָתַתִּי לָהֶם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		you did not trust in me, to make me holy. What is Moses’ offense? What
%		has he done that is so horrible as to deserve what is probably the worst
%		possible thing that could have been done to him: that he will not live
%		to enter the land? Many answers have been proposed to the question of
%		what the sin of Moses is. He calls the people rebels. He says, “Shall we
%		bring water out of this rock” instead of “Shall God … ” He strikes the
%		rock instead of speaking to it. The answer may lie in the wording of
%		YHWH’s reprimand: “You did not trust in me, to make me holy.” By hitting
%		the rock Moses makes it appear more as if it is his own agency that is
%		producing the water than if he had just spoken to the rock and watched
%		the water flow out. His saying “we” has the same effect verbally that
%		his physical action has visually. True, YHWH had said to him in his
%		instructions, “So you shall bring water out,” but Moses’ saying it to
%		the people before hitting the rock still makes those words appear to
%		mean something quite different from their meaning in the original
%		instructions. By word and act Moses is thus appropriating to himself an
%		act of God. In doing this he is undoing the message that God and Moses
%		himself have been conveying to the people up to this point. The people
%		have continuously directed their attention to Moses instead of to God.
%		In this story, as in the others so far, they say to Moses and Aaron,
%		“Why have you brought YHWH’s community to this wilderness … ? Why did
%		you bring us up from Egypt?” Until this episode Moses has repeatedly
%		told the people, “It is not from my own heart” and “You are congregating
%		against YHWH,” but now his words and actions confirm the people’s own
%		perception. He has come a considerable way from his timid attempts to
%		avoid the assignment at the burning bush. At Meribah Moses oversteps a
%		divine limit, and he pays a maximal price. The severity of the
%		punishment demonstrates the seriousness of the offense. Footnote 20:12.
%		you shall not bring this community to the land. In a way, the sin of
%		Moses is like the sin of Adam and Eve: stepping over the line, taking a
%		power from the divine realm. His punishment is not death. He lives to be
%		120 years old, the maximum (as decreed in Gen 6:3); his punishment is
%		exile—he is not permitted to enter the land—which is also like the
%		punishment of Adam and Eve, who are prevented from reentering Eden.
%	}

verses.original: הֵמָּה מֵי מְרִיבָה אֲשֶׁר רָבוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת יְהֹוָה וַיִּקָּדֵשׁ בָּם׃
verses.english: They are the waters of Meribah, over which the children of Israel quarreled with YHWH, and He was made holy among them.

tex.original: \hP{הֵמָּה מֵי מְרִיבָה אֲשֶׁר רָבוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת יְהֹוָה וַיִּקָּדֵשׁ בָּם׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח מֹשֶׁה מַלְאָכִים מִקָּדֵשׁ אֶל מֶלֶךְ אֱדוֹם כֹּה אָמַר אָחִיךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל אַתָּה יָדַעְתָּ אֵת כּל הַתְּלָאָה אֲשֶׁר מְצָאָתְנוּ׃
verses.english: And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom. “Your brother, Israel, says this: You know all the hardship that has found us:

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשְׁלַח מֹשֶׁה מַלְאָכִים מִקָּדֵשׁ אֶל מֶלֶךְ אֱדוֹם כֹּה אָמַר אָחִיךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל אַתָּה יָדַעְתָּ אֵת כּל הַתְּלָאָה אֲשֶׁר מְצָאָתְנוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּרְדוּ אֲבֹתֵינוּ מִצְרַיְמָה וַנֵּשֶׁב בְּמִצְרַיִם יָמִים רַבִּים וַיָּרֵעוּ לָנוּ מִצְרַיִם וְלַאֲבֹתֵינוּ׃
verses.english: And our fathers went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt many days. And Egypt was bad to us and to our fathers,

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֵּרְדוּ אֲבֹתֵינוּ מִצְרַיְמָה וַנֵּשֶׁב בְּמִצְרַיִם יָמִים רַבִּים וַיָּרֵעוּ לָנוּ מִצְרַיִם וְלַאֲבֹתֵינוּ׃}

verses.original: וַנִּצְעַק אֶל יְהֹוָה וַיִּשְׁמַע קֹלֵנוּ וַיִּשְׁלַח מַלְאָךְ וַיֹּצִאֵנוּ מִמִּצְרָיִם וְהִנֵּה אֲנַחְנוּ בְקָדֵשׁ עִיר קְצֵה גְבוּלֶךָ׃
verses.english: and we cried to YHWH, and He heard our voice and sent an angel and brought us from Egypt. And here we are in Kadesh, a city at the edge of your border.

tex.original: \hJ{וַנִּצְעַק אֶל יְהֹוָה וַיִּשְׁמַע קֹלֵנוּ וַיִּשְׁלַח מַלְאָךְ וַיֹּצִאֵנוּ מִמִּצְרָיִם וְהִנֵּה אֲנַחְנוּ בְקָדֵשׁ עִיר קְצֵה גְבוּלֶךָ׃}

verses.original: נַעְבְּרָה נָּא בְאַרְצֶךָ לֹא נַעֲבֹר בְּשָׂדֶה וּבְכֶרֶם וְלֹא נִשְׁתֶּה מֵי בְאֵר דֶּרֶךְ הַמֶּלֶךְ נֵלֵךְ לֹא נִטֶּה יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאול עַד אֲשֶׁר נַעֲבֹר גְּבֻלֶךָ׃
verses.english: Let us pass through your land. We won’t pass through a field or through a vineyard, and we won’t drink the water of a well. We’ll go by the king’s road, we won’t turn right or left, until we pass your border.”

tex.original: \hJ{נַעְבְּרָה נָּא בְאַרְצֶךָ לֹא נַעֲבֹר בְּשָׂדֶה וּבְכֶרֶם וְלֹא נִשְׁתֶּה מֵי בְאֵר דֶּרֶךְ הַמֶּלֶךְ נֵלֵךְ לֹא נִטֶּה יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאול עַד אֲשֶׁר נַעֲבֹר גְּבֻלֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו אֱדוֹם לֹא תַעֲבֹר בִּי פֶּן בַּחֶרֶב אֵצֵא לִקְרָאתֶךָ׃
verses.english: And Edom said to him, “You won’t pass through me, or else I’ll go out to you with the sword.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו אֱדוֹם לֹא תַעֲבֹר בִּי פֶּן בַּחֶרֶב אֵצֵא לִקְרָאתֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלָיו בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמְסִלָּה נַעֲלֶה וְאִם מֵימֶיךָ נִשְׁתֶּה אֲנִי וּמִקְנַי וְנָתַתִּי מִכְרָם רַק אֵין דָּבָר בְּרַגְלַי אֶעֱבֹרָה׃
verses.english: And the children of Israel said to him, “We’ll go up by the highway, and if we drink your water, I and my cattle, then I’ll pay its price. Only, it’s nothing: let me pass through by foot.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלָיו בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמְסִלָּה נַעֲלֶה וְאִם מֵימֶיךָ נִשְׁתֶּה אֲנִי וּמִקְנַי וְנָתַתִּי מִכְרָם רַק אֵין דָּבָר בְּרַגְלַי אֶעֱבֹרָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר לֹא תַעֲבֹר וַיֵּצֵא אֱדוֹם לִקְרָאתוֹ בְּעַם כָּבֵד וּבְיָד חֲזָקָה׃
verses.english: And he said, “You won’t pass.” And Edom went out to him with a heavy mass of people and a strong hand,

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר לֹא תַעֲבֹר וַיֵּצֵא אֱדוֹם לִקְרָאתוֹ בְּעַם כָּבֵד וּבְיָד חֲזָקָה׃}

verses.original: וַיְמָאֵן אֱדוֹם נְתֹן אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבֹר בִּגְבֻלוֹ וַיֵּט יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעָלָיו׃
verses.english: and Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through his border. And Israel turned away from him.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְמָאֵן אֱדוֹם נְתֹן אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבֹר בִּגְבֻלוֹ וַיֵּט יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעָלָיו׃}

verses.original: וַיִּסְעוּ מִקָּדֵשׁ וַיָּבֹאוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כּל הָעֵדָה הֹר הָהָר׃
verses.english: And they traveled from Kadesh, and the children of Israel, all the congregation, came to Mount Hor.

tex.original: \hR{וַיִּסְעוּ מִקָּדֵשׁ וַיָּבֹאוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כּל הָעֵדָה הֹר הָהָר׃}
