	}

verses.original: אַל תֹּאמַר בִּלְבָבְךָ בַּהֲדֹף יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֹתָם מִלְּפָנֶיךָ לֵאמֹר בְּצִדְקָתִי הֱבִיאַנִי יְהֹוָה לָרֶשֶׁת אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת וּבְרִשְׁעַת הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה יְהֹוָה מוֹרִישָׁם מִפָּנֶיךָ׃
verses.english: “Don’t say in your heart when YHWH pushes them from in front of you, saying, ‘Because of my virtue YHWH has brought me to take possession of this land,’ when it is because of these nations’ wickedness that YHWH dispossesses them from before you.

tex.original: \hDtrA{אַל תֹּאמַר בִּלְבָבְךָ בַּהֲדֹף יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֹתָם מִלְּפָנֶיךָ לֵאמֹר בְּצִדְקָתִי הֱבִיאַנִי יְהֹוָה לָרֶשֶׁת אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת וּבְרִשְׁעַת הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה יְהֹוָה מוֹרִישָׁם מִפָּנֶיךָ׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrA{
		“Don’t say in your heart when YHWH pushes them from in
		front of you, saying, ‘Because of my virtue YHWH has
		brought me to take possession of this land,’ when it is
		because of these nations’ wickedness that YHWH
		dispossesses them from before you.
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		take possession. Forms of this term occur more than sixty times in
%		Deuteronomy. Here it is linked specifically to the promise to the
%		patriarchs. This brings back to mind Abraham’s exchange with YHWH just
%		before their covenant, where this word occurs three times. Abraham says
%		that he is childless, so someone else will “take possession” of what is
%		his, but God assures him that his own offspring will “take possession”
%		from him (Gen 15:3–4). The numerous repetitions of the term convey the
%		central importance of the link and continuity between the episodes of
%		the patriarchs’ lives and the fate of their descendants.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא בְצִדְקָתְךָ וּבְיֹשֶׁר לְבָבְךָ אַתָּה בָא לָרֶשֶׁת אֶת אַרְצָם כִּי בְּרִשְׁעַת הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מוֹרִישָׁם מִפָּנֶיךָ וּלְמַעַן הָקִים אֶת הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע יְהֹוָה לַאֲבֹתֶיךָ לְאַבְרָהָם לְיִצְחָק וּלְיַעֲקֹב׃
verses.english: It’s not because of your virtue and your heart’s integrity that you’re coming to take possession of their land, but it is because of these nations’ wickedness that YHWH, your God, dispossesses them from before you, and in order to uphold the thing that YHWH swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

tex.original: \hDtrA{לֹא בְצִדְקָתְךָ וּבְיֹשֶׁר לְבָבְךָ אַתָּה בָא לָרֶשֶׁת אֶת אַרְצָם כִּי בְּרִשְׁעַת הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מוֹרִישָׁם מִפָּנֶיךָ וּלְמַעַן הָקִים אֶת הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע יְהֹוָה לַאֲבֹתֶיךָ לְאַבְרָהָם לְיִצְחָק וּלְיַעֲקֹב׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrA{
		It’s not because of your virtue and your heart’s integrity
		that you’re coming to take possession of their land, but
		it is because of these nations’ wickedness that YHWH, your
		God, dispossesses them from before you, and in order to
		uphold the thing that YHWH swore to your fathers, to
		Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		not because of your virtue. The point is made three times, in three
%		verses in a row (9:4–6): it is not because of your virtue but rather
%		because of these nations’ wickedness. Some think that the repetition is
%		just a scribe’s error, repeating a line by mistake. (Such errors are
%		known as dittography.) That is possible, but the repetition itself is
%		not sufficient reason to make that conclusion. On the contrary, the text
%		seems to me precisely to be making the point as emphatically as
%		possible. Moses notes the people’s own lack of virtue even more strongly
%		in the next verse (7) and he begins with the words “Remember—don’t
%		forget!” which is redundant as well but is certainly done on purpose for
%		emphasis. And he then goes on for the rest of the chapter listing the
%		people’s record of rebellions. Moses thus gives a powerful warning
%		against chauvinism and self-congratulation. And this also provides a
%		profound balance to the declaration that Israel was chosen to become a
%		treasured people, which came just two chapters earlier (7:6). Possession
%		of the land is the result of a promise to Israel’s ancestors. Status as
%		a treasured people depends on actions: faithfulness to the covenant.
%		Israel is not intrinsically better than anyone. What is special about
%		Israel is rather that it has been given a singular opportunity to follow
%		a path that will ultimately bring blessing to all the families of the
%		earth. Footnote 9:5. take possession. Forms of this term occur more than
%		sixty times in Deuteronomy. Here it is linked specifically to the
%		promise to the patriarchs. This brings back to mind Abraham’s exchange
%		with YHWH just before their covenant, where this word occurs three
%		times. Abraham says that he is childless, so someone else will “take
%		possession” of what is his, but God assures him that his own offspring
%		will “take possession” from him (Gen 15:3–4). The numerous repetitions
%		of the term convey the central importance of the link and continuity
%		between the episodes of the patriarchs’ lives and the fate of their
%		descendants.
%	}

verses.original: וְיָדַעְתָּ כִּי לֹא בְצִדְקָתְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַטּוֹבָה הַזֹּאת לְרִשְׁתָּהּ כִּי עַם קְשֵׁה עֹרֶף אָתָּה׃
verses.english: So you shall know that it is not because of your virtue that YHWH, your God, gives you this good land to take possession of it, because you’re a hardnecked people.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְיָדַעְתָּ כִּי לֹא בְצִדְקָתְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַטּוֹבָה הַזֹּאת לְרִשְׁתָּהּ כִּי עַם קְשֵׁה עֹרֶף אָתָּה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		take possession. Forms of this term occur more than sixty times in
%		Deuteronomy. Here it is linked specifically to the promise to the
%		patriarchs. This brings back to mind Abraham’s exchange with YHWH just
%		before their covenant, where this word occurs three times. Abraham says
%		that he is childless, so someone else will “take possession” of what is
%		his, but God assures him that his own offspring will “take possession”
%		from him (Gen 15:3–4). The numerous repetitions of the term convey the
%		central importance of the link and continuity between the episodes of
%		the patriarchs’ lives and the fate of their descendants.
%	}

verses.original: זְכֹר אַל תִּשְׁכַּח אֵת אֲשֶׁר הִקְצַפְתָּ אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמִּדְבָּר לְמִן הַיּוֹם אֲשֶׁר יָצָאתָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם עַד בֹּאֲכֶם עַד הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה מַמְרִים הֱיִיתֶם עִם יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Remember—don’t forget!—that you made YHWH, your God, angry in the wilderness. From the day that you went out from the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you’ve been rebellious toward YHWH.

tex.original: \hDtrA{זְכֹר אַל תִּשְׁכַּח אֵת אֲשֶׁר הִקְצַפְתָּ אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמִּדְבָּר לְמִן הַיּוֹם אֲשֶׁר יָצָאתָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם עַד בֹּאֲכֶם עַד הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה מַמְרִים הֱיִיתֶם עִם יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וּבְחֹרֵב הִקְצַפְתֶּם אֶת יְהֹוָה וַיִּתְאַנַּף יְהֹוָה בָּכֶם לְהַשְׁמִיד אֶתְכֶם׃
verses.english: And you made YHWH angry at Horeb, and YHWH was so incensed at you as to destroy you.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וּבְחֹרֵב הִקְצַפְתֶּם אֶת יְהֹוָה וַיִּתְאַנַּף יְהֹוָה בָּכֶם לְהַשְׁמִיד אֶתְכֶם׃}

verses.original: בַּעֲלֹתִי הָהָרָה לָקַחַת לוּחֹת הָאֲבָנִים לוּחֹת הַבְּרִית אֲשֶׁר כָּרַת יְהֹוָה עִמָּכֶם וָאֵשֵׁב בָּהָר אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לַיְלָה לֶחֶם לֹא אָכַלְתִּי וּמַיִם לֹא שָׁתִיתִי׃
verses.english: When I went up to the mountain to get the tablets of stones, the tablets of the covenant that YHWH made with you, and I stayed in the mountain forty days and forty nights, I didn’t eat bread and didn’t drink water.

tex.original: \hDtrA{בַּעֲלֹתִי הָהָרָה לָקַחַת לוּחֹת הָאֲבָנִים לוּחֹת הַבְּרִית אֲשֶׁר כָּרַת יְהֹוָה עִמָּכֶם וָאֵשֵׁב בָּהָר אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לַיְלָה לֶחֶם לֹא אָכַלְתִּי וּמַיִם לֹא שָׁתִיתִי׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		didn’t eat bread and didn’t drink water. This is the first mention of
%		this miracle that Moses personally experiences at Horeb. It is not
%		reported in Exodus. Moses tells the people about it now, in his list of
%		their rebellions, seemingly to convey to them that they rebelled in the
%		golden calf episode precisely while something awesome was going on.
%		While they were saying, “This man Moses, we don’t know what’s become of
%		him,” Moses was in fact experiencing a kind of physical transformation.
%		Another explanation: The people’s rebellions up to that point (and
%		frequently thereafter) were about food and water: the bitter water at
%		Marah (Exod 22–26), the manna (16:2–36), and the water from the rock
%		(17:1–7). And so Moses conveys to them that their worries and complaints
%		were utterly unnecessary: in God’s hands a man could even live without
%		food or water for forty days. Indeed, this follows Moses’ admonition in
%		the preceding chapter that “a human doesn’t live by bread alone” (Deut
%		8:3).
%	}

verses.original: וַיִּתֵּן יְהֹוָה אֵלַי אֶת שְׁנֵי לוּחֹת הָאֲבָנִים כְּתֻבִים בְּאֶצְבַּע אֱלֹהִים וַעֲלֵיהֶם כְּכל הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה עִמָּכֶם בָּהָר מִתּוֹךְ הָאֵשׁ בְּיוֹם הַקָּהָל׃
verses.english: And YHWH gave me the two tablets of stones, written with God’s finger, and on them were all the words that YHWH had spoken with you at the mountain from inside the fire in the day of the assembly.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיִּתֵּן יְהֹוָה אֵלַי אֶת שְׁנֵי לוּחֹת הָאֲבָנִים כְּתֻבִים בְּאֶצְבַּע אֱלֹהִים וַעֲלֵיהֶם כְּכל הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה עִמָּכֶם בָּהָר מִתּוֹךְ הָאֵשׁ בְּיוֹם הַקָּהָל׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לָיְלָה נָתַן יְהֹוָה אֵלַי אֶת שְׁנֵי לֻחֹת הָאֲבָנִים לֻחוֹת הַבְּרִית׃
verses.english: And it was: at the end of forty days and forty nights YHWH gave me the two tablets of stones, the tablets of the covenant.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לָיְלָה נָתַן יְהֹוָה אֵלַי אֶת שְׁנֵי לֻחֹת הָאֲבָנִים לֻחוֹת הַבְּרִית׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֵלַי קוּם רֵד מַהֵר מִזֶּה כִּי שִׁחֵת עַמְּךָ אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתָ מִמִּצְרָיִם סָרוּ מַהֵר מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ אֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִם עָשׂוּ לָהֶם מַסֵּכָה׃
verses.english: “And YHWH said to me, ‘Get up. Go down quickly from here, because your people whom you brought out from Egypt has become corrupt. They’ve turned quickly from the way that I commanded them. They’ve made themselves a molten thing.’

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֵלַי קוּם רֵד מַהֵר מִזֶּה כִּי שִׁחֵת עַמְּךָ אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתָ מִמִּצְרָיִם סָרוּ מַהֵר מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ אֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִם עָשׂוּ לָהֶם מַסֵּכָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֵלַי לֵאמֹר רָאִיתִי אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה וְהִנֵּה עַם קְשֵׁה עֹרֶף הוּא׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to me, saying, ‘I’ve seen this people; and, here, it’s a hardnecked people.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֵלַי לֵאמֹר רָאִיתִי אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה וְהִנֵּה עַם קְשֵׁה עֹרֶף הוּא׃}

verses.original: הֶרֶף מִמֶּנִּי וְאַשְׁמִידֵם וְאֶמְחֶה אֶת שְׁמָם מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמָיִם וְאֶעֱשֶׂה אוֹתְךָ לְגוֹי עָצוּם וָרָב מִמֶּנּוּ׃
verses.english: Hold back from me, and I’ll destroy them and wipe out their name from under the skies, and I’ll make you into a more powerful and numerous people than they.’

tex.original: \hDtrA{הֶרֶף מִמֶּנִּי וְאַשְׁמִידֵם וְאֶמְחֶה אֶת שְׁמָם מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמָיִם וְאֶעֱשֶׂה אוֹתְךָ לְגוֹי עָצוּם וָרָב מִמֶּנּוּ׃}

verses.original: וָאֵפֶן וָאֵרֵד מִן הָהָר וְהָהָר בֹּעֵר בָּאֵשׁ וּשְׁנֵי לוּחֹת הַבְּרִית עַל שְׁתֵּי יָדָי׃
verses.english: “And I turned and went down from the mountain—and the mountain was burning in fire—and the two tablets of the covenant were on my two hands.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וָאֵפֶן וָאֵרֵד מִן הָהָר וְהָהָר בֹּעֵר בָּאֵשׁ וּשְׁנֵי לוּחֹת הַבְּרִית עַל שְׁתֵּי יָדָי׃}

verses.original: וָאֵרֶא וְהִנֵּה חֲטָאתֶם לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם עֲשִׂיתֶם לָכֶם עֵגֶל מַסֵּכָה סַרְתֶּם מַהֵר מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶתְכֶם׃
verses.english: And I saw! And, here, you’d sinned against YHWH, your God. You’d made yourselves a molten calf. You’d turned quickly from the way that YHWH had commanded you.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וָאֵרֶא וְהִנֵּה חֲטָאתֶם לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם עֲשִׂיתֶם לָכֶם עֵגֶל מַסֵּכָה סַרְתֶּם מַהֵר מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶתְכֶם׃}

verses.original: וָאֶתְפֹּשׂ בִּשְׁנֵי הַלֻּחֹת וָאַשְׁלִכֵם מֵעַל שְׁתֵּי יָדָי וָאֲשַׁבְּרֵם לְעֵינֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: And I grasped the two tablets and threw them from on my two hands and shattered them before your eyes.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וָאֶתְפֹּשׂ בִּשְׁנֵי הַלֻּחֹת וָאַשְׁלִכֵם מֵעַל שְׁתֵּי יָדָי וָאֲשַׁבְּרֵם לְעֵינֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וָאֶתְנַפַּל לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה כָּרִאשֹׁנָה אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לַיְלָה לֶחֶם לֹא אָכַלְתִּי וּמַיִם לֹא שָׁתִיתִי עַל כּל חַטַּאתְכֶם אֲשֶׁר חֲטָאתֶם לַעֲשׂוֹת הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה לְהַכְעִיסוֹ׃
verses.english: “And I prostrated myself in front of YHWH like the first time, forty days and forty nights—I didn’t eat bread and didn’t drink water—over all your sin that you did, to do what was bad in YHWH’s eyes, to provoke Him,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וָאֶתְנַפַּל לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה כָּרִאשֹׁנָה אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לַיְלָה לֶחֶם לֹא אָכַלְתִּי וּמַיִם לֹא שָׁתִיתִי עַל כּל חַטַּאתְכֶם אֲשֶׁר חֲטָאתֶם לַעֲשׂוֹת הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה לְהַכְעִיסוֹ׃}

verses.original: כִּי יָגֹרְתִּי מִפְּנֵי הָאַף וְהַחֵמָה אֲשֶׁר קָצַף יְהֹוָה עֲלֵיכֶם לְהַשְׁמִיד אֶתְכֶם וַיִּשְׁמַע יְהֹוָה אֵלַי גַּם בַּפַּעַם הַהִוא׃
verses.english: because I was dreading on account of the anger and the fury, that YHWH was so angry at you as to destroy you. But YHWH listened to me that time as well.

tex.original: \hDtrA{כִּי יָגֹרְתִּי מִפְּנֵי הָאַף וְהַחֵמָה אֲשֶׁר קָצַף יְהֹוָה עֲלֵיכֶם לְהַשְׁמִיד אֶתְכֶם וַיִּשְׁמַע יְהֹוָה אֵלַי גַּם בַּפַּעַם הַהִוא׃}

verses.original: וּבְאַהֲרֹן הִתְאַנַּף יְהֹוָה מְאֹד לְהַשְׁמִידוֹ וָאֶתְפַּלֵּל גַּם בְּעַד אַהֲרֹן בָּעֵת הַהִוא׃
verses.english: And YHWH was very incensed at Aaron so as to destroy him, and I prayed for Aaron at that time as well.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וּבְאַהֲרֹן הִתְאַנַּף יְהֹוָה מְאֹד לְהַשְׁמִידוֹ וָאֶתְפַּלֵּל גַּם בְּעַד אַהֲרֹן בָּעֵת הַהִוא׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		incensed at Aaron. The text of the golden calf event (Exodus 32) never
%		says that God was specifically angry at Aaron. We might understand the
%		fact that Moses only makes it known now for the first time as indicating
%		that he would not mention it until after Aaron’s death. Thus he spares
%		Aaron the humiliation. And he has thus deferred any doubts that this
%		might have raised about the status of the high priest until now, when
%		they can be considered in the light of the man’s entire life and career
%		as high priest.
%	}

verses.original: וְאֶת חַטַּאתְכֶם אֲשֶׁר עֲשִׂיתֶם אֶת הָעֵגֶל לָקַחְתִּי וָאֶשְׂרֹף אֹתוֹ בָּאֵשׁ וָאֶכֹּת אֹתוֹ טָחוֹן הֵיטֵב עַד אֲשֶׁר דַּק לְעָפָר וָאַשְׁלִךְ אֶת עֲפָרוֹ אֶל הַנַּחַל הַיֹּרֵד מִן הָהָר׃
verses.english: And your sin that you made, the calf: I took it and burned it in fire and crushed it, grinding it well until it was thin as dust, and I threw its dust into the wadi that comes down from the mountain.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְאֶת חַטַּאתְכֶם אֲשֶׁר עֲשִׂיתֶם אֶת הָעֵגֶל לָקַחְתִּי וָאֶשְׂרֹף אֹתוֹ בָּאֵשׁ וָאֶכֹּת אֹתוֹ טָחוֹן הֵיטֵב עַד אֲשֶׁר דַּק לְעָפָר וָאַשְׁלִךְ אֶת עֲפָרוֹ אֶל הַנַּחַל הַיֹּרֵד מִן הָהָר׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		burned it … thin as dust. The parallels between Aaron’s golden calf and
%		those of Jeroboam I, king of Israel, are unmistakable. Jeroboam erects
%		golden calves at Dan and Beth-El (1 Kings 12:26–30). On that occasion he
%		says, “Here are your gods, Israel, which brought you out from the land
%		of Egypt”—which are the same words that the people say at the golden
%		calf in Exodus. Jeroboam’s sons are Nadab and Abiyah; Aaron’s sons are
%		Nadab and Abihu. And King Josiah destroys the high place where
%		Jeroboam’s golden calf stood at Beth-El, and, like Moses, “he burned it
%		thin as dust” (2 Kings 23:15). Also like Moses, Josiah casts the dust of
%		pagan altars into a wadi (23:6,12). A literary-historical analysis of
%		this parallel appears in my Who Wrote the Bible? (pp. 111–116). In the
%		terms of the full Tanak as it now stands, the parallel would suggest
%		that history repeats itself. This is also one of many parallels between
%		Josiah and Moses that serve to single out Josiah as the best of the
%		kings of Israel, the one who comes closest to the standards that Moses
%		taught by commandment and example. Thus the Torah says at the end of
%		Moses’ life: “And a prophet did not rise again in Israel like Moses”
%		(Deut 34:10); and the Tanak says at the end of Josiah’s life: “And after
%		him one did not rise like him” (2 Kings 23:25)—and these are the only
%		two occurrences of the expression “did not rise like him” in the Bible.
%		Again the embroidery of connections through the Tanak is apparent.
%	}

verses.original: וּבְתַבְעֵרָה וּבְמַסָּה וּבְקִבְרֹת הַתַּאֲוָה מַקְצִפִים הֱיִיתֶם אֶת יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: “And at Taberah and at Massah and at Kibroth Hattaavah you were making YHWH angry.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וּבְתַבְעֵרָה וּבְמַסָּה וּבְקִבְרֹת הַתַּאֲוָה מַקְצִפִים הֱיִיתֶם אֶת יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וּבִשְׁלֹחַ יְהֹוָה אֶתְכֶם מִקָּדֵשׁ בַּרְנֵעַ לֵאמֹר עֲלוּ וּרְשׁוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נָתַתִּי לָכֶם וַתַּמְרוּ אֶת פִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וְלֹא הֶאֱמַנְתֶּם לוֹ וְלֹא שְׁמַעְתֶּם בְּקֹלוֹ׃
verses.english: And when YHWH sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying, ‘Go up and take possession of the land that I’ve given you,’ then you rebelled at the word of YHWH, your God, and you didn’t trust Him and didn’t listen to His voice.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וּבִשְׁלֹחַ יְהֹוָה אֶתְכֶם מִקָּדֵשׁ בַּרְנֵעַ לֵאמֹר עֲלוּ וּרְשׁוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נָתַתִּי לָכֶם וַתַּמְרוּ אֶת פִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וְלֹא הֶאֱמַנְתֶּם לוֹ וְלֹא שְׁמַעְתֶּם בְּקֹלוֹ׃}

verses.original: מַמְרִים הֱיִיתֶם עִם יְהֹוָה מִיּוֹם דַּעְתִּי אֶתְכֶם׃
verses.english: You’ve been rebelling toward YHWH from the day I knew you.

tex.original: \hDtrA{מַמְרִים הֱיִיתֶם עִם יְהֹוָה מִיּוֹם דַּעְתִּי אֶתְכֶם׃}
tex.english: \eDtrA{You’ve been rebelling toward YHWH from the day I knew you.}

verses.original: וָאֶתְנַפַּל לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֵת אַרְבָּעִים הַיּוֹם וְאֶת אַרְבָּעִים הַלַּיְלָה אֲשֶׁר הִתְנַפָּלְתִּי כִּי אָמַר יְהֹוָה לְהַשְׁמִיד אֶתְכֶם׃
verses.english: “So I prostrated myself in front of YHWH for the forty days and forty nights that I had fallen down because YHWH had said He would destroy you,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וָאֶתְנַפַּל לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֵת אַרְבָּעִים הַיּוֹם וְאֶת אַרְבָּעִים הַלַּיְלָה אֲשֶׁר הִתְנַפָּלְתִּי כִּי אָמַר יְהֹוָה לְהַשְׁמִיד אֶתְכֶם׃}

verses.original: וָאֶתְפַּלֵּל אֶל יְהֹוָה וָאֹמַר אֲדֹנָי יֱהֹוִה אַל תַּשְׁחֵת עַמְּךָ וְנַחֲלָתְךָ אֲשֶׁר פָּדִיתָ בְּגדְלֶךָ אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתָ מִמִּצְרַיִם בְּיָד חֲזָקָה׃
verses.english: and I prayed to YHWH and said, ‘My Lord YHWH, don’t destroy your people and your legacy whom you redeemed by your greatness, whom you brought out from Egypt with a strong hand.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וָאֶתְפַּלֵּל אֶל יְהֹוָה וָאֹמַר אֲדֹנָי יֱהֹוִה אַל תַּשְׁחֵת עַמְּךָ וְנַחֲלָתְךָ אֲשֶׁר פָּדִיתָ בְּגדְלֶךָ אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתָ מִמִּצְרַיִם בְּיָד חֲזָקָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		destroy. The word in Hebrew, tat, has the same root
%		meaning as the word for what the people have done: become corrupt,
%		hiît (9:12). The same play on this root is used in the
%		flood story (Gen 6:12–13). There and here it is not just wordplay for
%		its own sake. It conveys the principle that punishment is meant to be in
%		proportion to the crime. The repetition of the pun here in Deuteronomy
%		conveys that what was true for all humankind in the early generations of
%		creation is still true in relations between God and humans in the
%		Torah’s final book.
%	}

verses.original: זְכֹר לַעֲבָדֶיךָ לְאַבְרָהָם לְיִצְחָק וּלְיַעֲקֹב אַל תֵּפֶן אֶל קְשִׁי הָעָם הַזֶּה וְאֶל רִשְׁעוֹ וְאֶל חַטָּאתוֹ׃
verses.english: Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Don’t look to this people’s hardness and to its wickedness and to its sin,

tex.original: \hDtrA{זְכֹר לַעֲבָדֶיךָ לְאַבְרָהָם לְיִצְחָק וּלְיַעֲקֹב אַל תֵּפֶן אֶל קְשִׁי הָעָם הַזֶּה וְאֶל רִשְׁעוֹ וְאֶל חַטָּאתוֹ׃}

verses.original: פֶּן יֹאמְרוּ הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתָנוּ מִשָּׁם מִבְּלִי יְכֹלֶת יְהֹוָה לַהֲבִיאָם אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָהֶם וּמִשִּׂנְאָתוֹ אוֹתָם הוֹצִיאָם לַהֲמִתָם בַּמִּדְבָּר׃
verses.english: or else the land from which you brought us out will say: Because YHWH wasn’t able to bring them to the land of which He spoke to them, and because He hated them, He brought them out to kill them in the wilderness!

tex.original: \hDtrA{פֶּן יֹאמְרוּ הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתָנוּ מִשָּׁם מִבְּלִי יְכֹלֶת יְהֹוָה לַהֲבִיאָם אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָהֶם וּמִשִּׂנְאָתוֹ אוֹתָם הוֹצִיאָם לַהֲמִתָם בַּמִּדְבָּר׃}

verses.original: וְהֵם עַמְּךָ וְנַחֲלָתֶךָ אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתָ בְּכֹחֲךָ הַגָּדֹל וּבִזְרֹעֲךָ הַנְּטוּיָה׃
verses.english: And they’re your people and your legacy, whom you brought out by your great power and by your outstretched arm.’

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְהֵם עַמְּךָ וְנַחֲלָתֶךָ אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתָ בְּכֹחֲךָ הַגָּדֹל וּבִזְרֹעֲךָ הַנְּטוּיָה׃}

verses.original: בָּעֵת הַהִוא אָמַר יְהֹוָה אֵלַי פְּסל לְךָ שְׁנֵי לוּחֹת אֲבָנִים כָּרִאשֹׁנִים וַעֲלֵה אֵלַי הָהָרָה וְעָשִׂיתָ לְּךָ אֲרוֹן עֵץ׃
verses.english: “At that time YHWH said to me, ‘Carve two tablets of stones like the first ones, and come up to me at the mountain. And you shall make an ark of wood.

tex.original: \hDtrA{בָּעֵת הַהִוא אָמַר יְהֹוָה אֵלַי פְּסל לְךָ שְׁנֵי לוּחֹת אֲבָנִים כָּרִאשֹׁנִים וַעֲלֵה אֵלַי הָהָרָה וְעָשִׂיתָ לְּךָ אֲרוֹן עֵץ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		you shall make an ark of wood. It says “you shall make,” but in Exodus
%		it was Bezalel, not Moses, who made the ark. Rashi and Ramban and others
%		therefore say that there must have been two arks. In current critical
%		scholarship, the apparent contradiction would generally be taken to be a
%		result of the fact that this text in Deuteronomy and the text in Exodus
%		were written by two different authors. But, even without raising such
%		solutions that are arrived at through critical approaches, we can
%		understand Moses’ words in Deuteronomy to be a brief account of what
%		happened at Sinai, and so he speaks of himself as making the ark when he
%		means that he directed Bezalel to do it. Likewise, he speaks of the ark
%		as if it were finished and ready when he came down from the mountain
%		when he knows that actually some time passed before the ark was made. J.
%		H. Hertz proposed such an understanding as an alternative to Rashi’s and
%		Ramban’s view even though Hertz harshly rejected literary-critical
%		scholarship. This is important because an almost fundamentalist view of
%		Rashi is growing at present in some communities, wherein it is
%		practically heresy to question Rashi. This gives Rashi a status that I
%		do not think he would have wanted for himself. And certainly the
%		commentators of the generations that followed him, including his own
%		grandson Rashbam, were prepared to question his comments. We respect and
%		admire the great commentators of past generations, but we should never
%		forget to distinguish between Torah and commentary. The goal of refining
%		our knowledge of the Torah and shedding new light from it in each new
%		age is never-ending; and our commentaries—including my own—are always
%		subject to criticism and improvement.
%	}

verses.original: וְאֶכְתֹּב עַל הַלֻּחֹת אֶת הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר הָיוּ עַל הַלֻּחֹת הָרִאשֹׁנִים אֲשֶׁר שִׁבַּרְתָּ וְשַׂמְתָּם בָּאָרוֹן׃
verses.english: And I’ll write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you shattered, and you shall set them in the ark.’

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְאֶכְתֹּב עַל הַלֻּחֹת אֶת הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר הָיוּ עַל הַלֻּחֹת הָרִאשֹׁנִים אֲשֶׁר שִׁבַּרְתָּ וְשַׂמְתָּם בָּאָרוֹן׃}

verses.original: וָאַעַשׂ אֲרוֹן עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים וָאֶפְסֹל שְׁנֵי לֻחֹת אֲבָנִים כָּרִאשֹׁנִים וָאַעַל הָהָרָה וּשְׁנֵי הַלֻּחֹת בְּיָדִי׃
verses.english: “And I made an ark of acacia wood, and I carved two tablets of stones like the first ones, and I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hands.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וָאַעַשׂ אֲרוֹן עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים וָאֶפְסֹל שְׁנֵי לֻחֹת אֲבָנִים כָּרִאשֹׁנִים וָאַעַל הָהָרָה וּשְׁנֵי הַלֻּחֹת בְּיָדִי׃}

verses.original: וַיִּכְתֹּב עַל הַלֻּחֹת כַּמִּכְתָּב הָרִאשׁוֹן אֵת עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה אֲלֵיכֶם בָּהָר מִתּוֹךְ הָאֵשׁ בְּיוֹם הַקָּהָל וַיִּתְּנֵם יְהֹוָה אֵלָי׃
verses.english: And He wrote on the tablets like the first writing: the Ten Commandments that YHWH spoke to you at the mountain from inside the fire in the day of the assembly, and YHWH gave them to me.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיִּכְתֹּב עַל הַלֻּחֹת כַּמִּכְתָּב הָרִאשׁוֹן אֵת עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה אֲלֵיכֶם בָּהָר מִתּוֹךְ הָאֵשׁ בְּיוֹם הַקָּהָל וַיִּתְּנֵם יְהֹוָה אֵלָי׃}

verses.original: וָאֵפֶן וָאֵרֵד מִן הָהָר וָאָשִׂם אֶת הַלֻּחֹת בָּאָרוֹן אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי וַיִּהְיוּ שָׁם כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוַּנִי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: And I turned and went down from the mountain, and I set the tablets in the ark that I had made, and they have been there, as YHWH commanded me.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וָאֵפֶן וָאֵרֵד מִן הָהָר וָאָשִׂם אֶת הַלֻּחֹת בָּאָרוֹן אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי וַיִּהְיוּ שָׁם כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוַּנִי יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נָסְעוּ מִבְּאֵרֹת בְּנֵי יַעֲקָן מוֹסֵרָה שָׁם מֵת אַהֲרֹן וַיִּקָּבֵר שָׁם וַיְכַהֵן אֶלְעָזָר בְּנוֹ תַּחְתָּיו׃
verses.english: “And the children of Israel had traveled from Beeroth-bene-Jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died, and he was buried there; and Eleazar, his son, functioned as priest in his place.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נָסְעוּ מִבְּאֵרֹת בְּנֵי יַעֲקָן מוֹסֵרָה שָׁם מֵת אַהֲרֹן וַיִּקָּבֵר שָׁם וַיְכַהֵן אֶלְעָזָר בְּנוֹ תַּחְתָּיו׃}

verses.original: מִשָּׁם נָסְעוּ הַגֻּדְגֹּדָה וּמִן הַגֻּדְגֹּדָה יטְבָתָה אֶרֶץ נַחֲלֵי מָיִם׃
verses.english: From there they traveled to Gudgod, and from Gudgod to Jotbah, a land of wadis of water.

tex.original: \hDtrA{מִשָּׁם נָסְעוּ הַגֻּדְגֹּדָה וּמִן הַגֻּדְגֹּדָה יטְבָתָה אֶרֶץ נַחֲלֵי מָיִם׃}

verses.original: בָּעֵת הַהִוא הִבְדִּיל יְהֹוָה אֶת שֵׁבֶט הַלֵּוִי לָשֵׂאת אֶת אֲרוֹן בְּרִית יְהֹוָה לַעֲמֹד לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לְשָׁרְתוֹ וּלְבָרֵךְ בִּשְׁמוֹ עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: At that time YHWH distinguished the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of YHWH’s covenant, to stand in front of YHWH to serve Him, and to bless in His name to this day.

tex.original: \hDtrA{בָּעֵת הַהִוא הִבְדִּיל יְהֹוָה אֶת שֵׁבֶט הַלֵּוִי לָשֵׂאת אֶת אֲרוֹן בְּרִית יְהֹוָה לַעֲמֹד לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לְשָׁרְתוֹ וּלְבָרֵךְ בִּשְׁמוֹ עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: עַל כֵּן לֹא הָיָה לְלֵוִי חֵלֶק וְנַחֲלָה עִם אֶחָיו יְהֹוָה הוּא נַחֲלָתוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לוֹ׃
verses.english: Therefore Levi has not had a portion and a legacy with its brothers. YHWH: He is its legacy, as YHWH, your God, spoke to it.

tex.original: \hDtrA{עַל כֵּן לֹא הָיָה לְלֵוִי חֵלֶק וְנַחֲלָה עִם אֶחָיו יְהֹוָה הוּא נַחֲלָתוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְאָנֹכִי עָמַדְתִּי בָהָר כַּיָּמִים הָרִאשֹׁנִים אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לָיְלָה וַיִּשְׁמַע יְהֹוָה אֵלַי גַּם בַּפַּעַם הַהִוא לֹא אָבָה יְהֹוָה הַשְׁחִיתֶךָ׃
verses.english: “And I: I stood in the mountain as in the first days: forty days and forty nights. And YHWH listened to me that time as well. YHWH was not willing to destroy you.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְאָנֹכִי עָמַדְתִּי בָהָר כַּיָּמִים הָרִאשֹׁנִים אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לָיְלָה וַיִּשְׁמַע יְהֹוָה אֵלַי גַּם בַּפַּעַם הַהִוא לֹא אָבָה יְהֹוָה הַשְׁחִיתֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֵלַי קוּם לֵךְ לְמַסַּע לִפְנֵי הָעָם וְיָבֹאוּ וְיִירְשׁוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי לַאֲבֹתָם לָתֵת לָהֶם׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to me, ‘Get up. Set out on the journey in front of the people, and they’ll come and take possession of the land that I swore to their fathers to give to them.’

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֵלַי קוּם לֵךְ לְמַסַּע לִפְנֵי הָעָם וְיָבֹאוּ וְיִירְשׁוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי לַאֲבֹתָם לָתֵת לָהֶם׃}

verses.original: וְעַתָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל מָה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ שֹׁאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לָלֶכֶת בְּכל דְּרָכָיו וּלְאַהֲבָה אֹתוֹ וְלַעֲבֹד אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכל נַפְשֶׁךָ׃
verses.english: “And now, Israel, what is YHWH, your God, asking from you except to fear YHWH, your God, to go in all His ways, and to love Him and to serve YHWH, your God, with all your heart and all your soul,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְעַתָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל מָה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ שֹׁאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לָלֶכֶת בְּכל דְּרָכָיו וּלְאַהֲבָה אֹתוֹ וְלַעֲבֹד אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכל נַפְשֶׁךָ׃}

verses.original: לִשְׁמֹר אֶת מִצְוֺת יְהֹוָה וְאֶת חֻקֹּתָיו אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לְטוֹב לָךְ׃
verses.english: to observe YHWH’s commandments and His laws that I command you today to be good for you.

tex.original: \hDtrA{לִשְׁמֹר אֶת מִצְוֺת יְהֹוָה וְאֶת חֻקֹּתָיו אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לְטוֹב לָךְ׃}

verses.original: הֵן לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ הַשָּׁמַיִם וּשְׁמֵי הַשָּׁמָיִם הָאָרֶץ וְכל אֲשֶׁר בָּהּ׃
verses.english: Here, YHWH, your God, has the skies—and the skies of the skies!—the earth and everything that’s in it.

tex.original: \hDtrA{הֵן לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ הַשָּׁמַיִם וּשְׁמֵי הַשָּׁמָיִם הָאָרֶץ וְכל אֲשֶׁר בָּהּ׃}

verses.original: רַק בַּאֲבֹתֶיךָ חָשַׁק יְהֹוָה לְאַהֲבָה אוֹתָם וַיִּבְחַר בְּזַרְעָם אַחֲרֵיהֶם בָּכֶם מִכּל הָעַמִּים כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: Only, YHWH was attracted to your fathers, to love them, and He chose their seed after them: you, out of all the peoples, as it is this day.

tex.original: \hDtrA{רַק בַּאֲבֹתֶיךָ חָשַׁק יְהֹוָה לְאַהֲבָה אוֹתָם וַיִּבְחַר בְּזַרְעָם אַחֲרֵיהֶם בָּכֶם מִכּל הָעַמִּים כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: וּמַלְתֶּם אֵת ערְלַת לְבַבְכֶם וְערְפְּכֶם לֹא תַקְשׁוּ עוֹד׃
verses.english: So you shall circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and you shall not harden your necks anymore.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וּמַלְתֶּם אֵת ערְלַת לְבַבְכֶם וְערְפְּכֶם לֹא תַקְשׁוּ עוֹד׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the foreskin of your heart. This concept occurs in two books of the
%		Torah (Deut 10:16; 30:6; Lev 26:41) and in two of the prophets (Jer 4:4;
%		Ezek 44:7,9). The sign of the Abrahamic covenant, and probably the most
%		commonly observed of the commandments by Jewish families for centuries,
%		is circumcision. But the Torah commands the circumcision of one’s heart
%		as well. It establishes that outward fulfillment of practices without
%		also feeling it in one’s heart is insufficient. The concept of
%		circumcising one’s heart, moreover, unlike physical circumcision,
%		applies to both women and men.
%	}

verses.original: כִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם הוּא אֱלֹהֵי הָאֱלֹהִים וַאֲדֹנֵי הָאֲדֹנִים הָאֵל הַגָּדֹל הַגִּבֹּר וְהַנּוֹרָא אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִשָּׂא פָנִים וְלֹא יִקַּח שֹׁחַד׃
verses.english: Because YHWH, your God: He is the God of gods and the Lord of lords, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God, who won’t be partial and won’t take a bribe,

tex.original: \hDtrA{כִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם הוּא אֱלֹהֵי הָאֱלֹהִים וַאֲדֹנֵי הָאֲדֹנִים הָאֵל הַגָּדֹל הַגִּבֹּר וְהַנּוֹרָא אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִשָּׂא פָנִים וְלֹא יִקַּח שֹׁחַד׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the God of gods and the Lord of lords. Admittedly, this sounds
%		unmonotheistic, seemingly acknowledging the existence of other gods.
%		But, earlier, Moses has said, “YHWH: He is God. There is no other
%		outside of Him” (4:35) and “YHWH is one” (6:4). And, later, YHWH says,
%		“There is no god with me” (32:39). How are we to reconcile the many
%		monotheistic passages in Deuteronomy with “God of gods and Lord of
%		lords”? As in the case of not having “other gods before my face,” this
%		is a linguistic matter. “God of gods” is an expression for conveying
%		that YHWH is something that all other gods in whom people believe are
%		not. It need not presume that such other gods exist. Footnote 10:17.
%		won’t take a bribe. What could it mean to bribe God?! A sacrifice, a
%		donation, a kindness, charity, prayer: one might do any of these to win
%		the deity’s favor, rather than doing them as fulfillment of the
%		commandments or as free acts. Moses informs the people that this will
%		not work.
%	}

verses.original: עֹשֶׂה מִשְׁפַּט יָתוֹם וְאַלְמָנָה וְאֹהֵב גֵּר לָתֶת לוֹ לֶחֶם וְשִׂמְלָה׃
verses.english: doing judgment for an orphan and a widow and loving an alien, to give him bread and a garment.

tex.original: \hDtrA{עֹשֶׂה מִשְׁפַּט יָתוֹם וְאַלְמָנָה וְאֹהֵב גֵּר לָתֶת לוֹ לֶחֶם וְשִׂמְלָה׃}

verses.original: וַאֲהַבְתֶּם אֶת הַגֵּר כִּי גֵרִים הֱיִיתֶם בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: So you shall love the alien, because you were aliens in the land of Egypt.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַאֲהַבְתֶּם אֶת הַגֵּר כִּי גֵרִים הֱיִיתֶם בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃}

verses.original: אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ תִּירָא אֹתוֹ תַעֲבֹד וּבוֹ תִדְבָּק וּבִשְׁמוֹ תִּשָּׁבֵעַ׃
verses.english: You shall fear YHWH, your God, you shall serve Him, and you shall cling to Him, and you shall swear by His name.

tex.original: \hDtrA{אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ תִּירָא אֹתוֹ תַעֲבֹד וּבוֹ תִדְבָּק וּבִשְׁמוֹ תִּשָּׁבֵעַ׃}

verses.original: הוּא תְהִלָּתְךָ וְהוּא אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה אִתְּךָ אֶת הַגְּדֹלֹת וְאֶת הַנּוֹרָאֹת הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר רָאוּ עֵינֶיךָ׃
verses.english: He is your splendor, and He is your God, who did these great and awesome things for you that your eyes have seen. Your fathers went down to Egypt with seventy persons, and now YHWH, your God, has made you like the stars of the skies for multitude.

tex.original: \hDtrA{הוּא תְהִלָּתְךָ וְהוּא אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה אִתְּךָ אֶת הַגְּדֹלֹת וְאֶת הַנּוֹרָאֹת הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר רָאוּ עֵינֶיךָ׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrA{
		He is your splendor, and He is your God, who did these
		great and awesome things for you that your eyes have seen.
		Your fathers went down to Egypt with seventy persons, and
		now YHWH, your God, has made you like the stars of the
		skies for multitude.
	}

verses.original: בְּשִׁבְעִים נֶפֶשׁ יָרְדוּ אֲבֹתֶיךָ מִצְרָיְמָה וְעַתָּה שָׂמְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כְּכוֹכְבֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם לָרֹב׃

tex.original: \hDtrA{בְּשִׁבְעִים נֶפֶשׁ יָרְדוּ אֲבֹתֶיךָ מִצְרָיְמָה וְעַתָּה שָׂמְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כְּכוֹכְבֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם לָרֹב׃}
tex.english: \eDtrA{}

verses.original: וְאָהַבְתָּ אֵת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְשָׁמַרְתָּ מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ וְחֻקֹּתָיו וּמִשְׁפָּטָיו וּמִצְוֺתָיו כּל הַיָּמִים׃
verses.english: “And you shall love YHWH, your God, and keep His charge and His laws and His judgments and His commandments every day.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְאָהַבְתָּ אֵת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְשָׁמַרְתָּ מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ וְחֻקֹּתָיו וּמִשְׁפָּטָיו וּמִצְוֺתָיו כּל הַיָּמִים׃}

verses.original: וִידַעְתֶּם הַיּוֹם כִּי לֹא אֶת בְּנֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָדְעוּ וַאֲשֶׁר לֹא רָאוּ אֶת מוּסַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֶת גּדְלוֹ אֶת יָדוֹ הַחֲזָקָה וּזְרֹעוֹ הַנְּטוּיָה׃
verses.english: And you shall know today that it’s not with your children, who didn’t know and who didn’t see the discipline of YHWH, your God, His greatness and His strong hand and His outstretched arm

tex.original: \hDtrA{וִידַעְתֶּם הַיּוֹם כִּי לֹא אֶת בְּנֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָדְעוּ וַאֲשֶׁר לֹא רָאוּ אֶת מוּסַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֶת גּדְלוֹ אֶת יָדוֹ הַחֲזָקָה וּזְרֹעוֹ הַנְּטוּיָה׃}

verses.original: וְאֶת אֹתֹתָיו וְאֶת מַעֲשָׂיו אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה בְּתוֹךְ מִצְרָיִם לְפַרְעֹה מֶלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם וּלְכל אַרְצוֹ׃
verses.english: and His signs and His deeds that He did in Egypt to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and to all his land,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְאֶת אֹתֹתָיו וְאֶת מַעֲשָׂיו אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה בְּתוֹךְ מִצְרָיִם לְפַרְעֹה מֶלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם וּלְכל אַרְצוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לְחֵיל מִצְרַיִם לְסוּסָיו וּלְרִכְבּוֹ אֲשֶׁר הֵצִיף אֶת מֵי יַם סוּף עַל פְּנֵיהֶם בְּרדְפָם אַחֲרֵיכֶם וַיְאַבְּדֵם יְהֹוָה עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: and what He did to Egypt’s army and to his horses and his chariots, that He flowed the waters of the Red Sea over their faces when they pursued you so YHWH destroyed them to this day,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לְחֵיל מִצְרַיִם לְסוּסָיו וּלְרִכְבּוֹ אֲשֶׁר הֵצִיף אֶת מֵי יַם סוּף עַל פְּנֵיהֶם בְּרדְפָם אַחֲרֵיכֶם וַיְאַבְּדֵם יְהֹוָה עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: וַאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לָכֶם בַּמִּדְבָּר עַד בֹּאֲכֶם עַד הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: and what He did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לָכֶם בַּמִּדְבָּר עַד בֹּאֲכֶם עַד הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: וַאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לְדָתָן וְלַאֲבִירָם בְּנֵי אֱלִיאָב בֶּן רְאוּבֵן אֲשֶׁר פָּצְתָה הָאָרֶץ אֶת פִּיהָ וַתִּבְלָעֵם וְאֶת בָּתֵּיהֶם וְאֶת אהֳלֵיהֶם וְאֵת כּל הַיְקוּם אֲשֶׁר בְּרַגְלֵיהֶם בְּקֶרֶב כּל יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: and what He did to Dathan and to Abiram, sons of Eliab son of Reuben, that the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households and their tents and all the substance that was at their feet among the children of Israel—

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לְדָתָן וְלַאֲבִירָם בְּנֵי אֱלִיאָב בֶּן רְאוּבֵן אֲשֶׁר פָּצְתָה הָאָרֶץ אֶת פִּיהָ וַתִּבְלָעֵם וְאֶת בָּתֵּיהֶם וְאֶת אהֳלֵיהֶם וְאֵת כּל הַיְקוּם אֲשֶׁר בְּרַגְלֵיהֶם בְּקֶרֶב כּל יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrA{
		and what He did to Dathan and to Abiram, sons of Eliab son
		of Reuben, that the earth opened its mouth and swallowed
		them and their households and their tents and all the
		substance that was at their feet among the children of
		Israel—
	}

verses.original: כִּי עֵינֵיכֶם הָרֹאֹת אֶת כּל מַעֲשֵׂה יְהֹוָה הַגָּדֹל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה׃
verses.english: but it’s your eyes, that saw every great deed of YHWH’s that He did.

tex.original: \hDtrA{כִּי עֵינֵיכֶם הָרֹאֹת אֶת כּל מַעֲשֵׂה יְהֹוָה הַגָּדֹל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה׃}

verses.original: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת כּל הַמִּצְוָה אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לְמַעַן תֶּחֶזְקוּ וּבָאתֶם וִירִשְׁתֶּם אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם עֹבְרִים שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃
verses.english: And you shall observe all of the commandment that I command you today so that you’ll be strong and you’ll come and take possession of the land that you’re crossing there to take possession of it,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם אֶת כּל הַמִּצְוָה אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לְמַעַן תֶּחֶזְקוּ וּבָאתֶם וִירִשְׁתֶּם אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם עֹבְרִים שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃}

verses.original: וּלְמַעַן תַּאֲרִיכוּ יָמִים עַל הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע יְהֹוָה לַאֲבֹתֵיכֶם לָתֵת לָהֶם וּלְזַרְעָם אֶרֶץ זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ׃
verses.english: and so that you’ll extend days on the land that YHWH swore to your fathers to give to them and to their seed, a land flowing with milk and honey.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וּלְמַעַן תַּאֲרִיכוּ יָמִים עַל הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע יְהֹוָה לַאֲבֹתֵיכֶם לָתֵת לָהֶם וּלְזַרְעָם אֶרֶץ זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ׃}

verses.original: כִּי הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה בָא שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ לֹא כְאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם הִוא אֲשֶׁר יְצָאתֶם מִשָּׁם אֲשֶׁר תִּזְרַע אֶת זַרְעֲךָ וְהִשְׁקִיתָ בְרַגְלְךָ כְּגַן הַיָּרָק׃
verses.english: “Because the land to which you’re coming to take possession of it: it’s not like the land of Egypt from which you’ve come out, where you plant your seed and water it at your feet like a garden of plants.

tex.original: \hDtrA{כִּי הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה בָא שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ לֹא כְאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם הִוא אֲשֶׁר יְצָאתֶם מִשָּׁם אֲשֶׁר תִּזְרַע אֶת זַרְעֲךָ וְהִשְׁקִיתָ בְרַגְלְךָ כְּגַן הַיָּרָק׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		water it at your feet like a garden. Because the Nile’s water is
%		commonly present, the human’s role is simply to get it to the plants, by
%		conveying or irrigation. But in Israel much of the land is dependent on
%		rain as its source of water; it “drinks water by the skies’ showers”
%		(11:11). And so one feels more dependent on God. But, Moses assures the
%		people, God “cares about” the land, and God’s “eyes are always on it”
%		(11:12).
%	}

verses.original: וְהָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם עֹבְרִים שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ אֶרֶץ הָרִים וּבְקָעֹת לִמְטַר הַשָּׁמַיִם תִּשְׁתֶּה מָּיִם׃
verses.english: But the land to which you’re crossing to take possession of it is a land of hills and valleys. It drinks water by the skies’ showers.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְהָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם עֹבְרִים שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ אֶרֶץ הָרִים וּבְקָעֹת לִמְטַר הַשָּׁמַיִם תִּשְׁתֶּה מָּיִם׃}

verses.original: אֶרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ דֹּרֵשׁ אֹתָהּ תָּמִיד עֵינֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בָּהּ מֵרֵשִׁית הַשָּׁנָה וְעַד אַחֲרִית שָׁנָה׃
verses.english: A land that YHWH, your God, cares about; YHWH’s eyes are always on it, from the year’s beginning to year’s end.

tex.original: \hDtrA{אֶרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ דֹּרֵשׁ אֹתָהּ תָּמִיד עֵינֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בָּהּ מֵרֵשִׁית הַשָּׁנָה וְעַד אַחֲרִית שָׁנָה׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ תִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶל מִצְוֺתַי אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּה אֶתְכֶם הַיּוֹם לְאַהֲבָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וּלְעבְדוֹ בְּכל לְבַבְכֶם וּבְכל נַפְשְׁכֶם׃
verses.english: So it will be, if you’ll listen to my commandments that I command you today, to love YHWH, your God, and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ תִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶל מִצְוֺתַי אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּה אֶתְכֶם הַיּוֹם לְאַהֲבָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וּלְעבְדוֹ בְּכל לְבַבְכֶם וּבְכל נַפְשְׁכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְנָתַתִּי מְטַר אַרְצְכֶם בְּעִתּוֹ יוֹרֶה וּמַלְקוֹשׁ וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ וְתִירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ׃
verses.english: then I’ll give your land’s showers at their time, early rain and late rain, and you’ll gather your grain and your wine and your oil.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְנָתַתִּי מְטַר אַרְצְכֶם בְּעִתּוֹ יוֹרֶה וּמַלְקוֹשׁ וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ וְתִירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		I’ll give. The subject of “I’ll give” must be God, and so Moses has
%		apparently shifted in the middle of his discussion and is now quoting
%		God when until now he has been speaking in his own name and referring to
%		God in third person. It may convey a kind of intimacy in which Moses is
%		now so close to the deity and so used to speaking in God’s name and
%		declaring the commandments that he moves into the divine first-person
%		mode with ease.
%	}

verses.original: וְנָתַתִּי עֵשֶׂב בְּשָׂדְךָ לִבְהֶמְתֶּךָ וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ׃
verses.english: And I’ll give vegetation in your field for your animals, and you’ll eat and be full.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְנָתַתִּי עֵשֶׂב בְּשָׂדְךָ לִבְהֶמְתֶּךָ וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		I’ll give. The subject of “I’ll give” must be God, and so Moses has
%		apparently shifted in the middle of his discussion and is now quoting
%		God when until now he has been speaking in his own name and referring
%		to God in third person. It may convey a kind of intimacy in which
%		Moses is now so close to the deity and so used to speaking in God’s
%		name and declaring the commandments that he moves into the divine
%		first-person mode with ease.
%	}

verses.original: הִשָּׁמְרוּ לָכֶם פֶּן יִפְתֶּה לְבַבְכֶם וְסַרְתֶּם וַעֲבַדְתֶּם אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶם לָהֶם׃
verses.english: “Watch yourselves in case your heart will be deceived so you’ll turn and serve other gods and bow to them,

tex.original: \hDtrA{הִשָּׁמְרוּ לָכֶם פֶּן יִפְתֶּה לְבַבְכֶם וְסַרְתֶּם וַעֲבַדְתֶּם אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶם לָהֶם׃}

verses.original: וְחָרָה אַף יְהֹוָה בָּכֶם וְעָצַר אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְלֹא יִהְיֶה מָטָר וְהָאֲדָמָה לֹא תִתֵּן אֶת יְבוּלָהּ וַאֲבַדְתֶּם מְהֵרָה מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ הַטֹּבָה אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה נֹתֵן לָכֶם׃
verses.english: and YHWH’s anger will flare at you, and He’ll hold back the skies, and there won’t be showers, and the earth won’t give its crop, and you’ll perish quickly from the good land that YHWH is giving you.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְחָרָה אַף יְהֹוָה בָּכֶם וְעָצַר אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְלֹא יִהְיֶה מָטָר וְהָאֲדָמָה לֹא תִתֵּן אֶת יְבוּלָהּ וַאֲבַדְתֶּם מְהֵרָה מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ הַטֹּבָה אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה נֹתֵן לָכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְשַׂמְתֶּם אֶת דְּבָרַי אֵלֶּה עַל לְבַבְכֶם וְעַל נַפְשְׁכֶם וּקְשַׁרְתֶּם אֹתָם לְאוֹת עַל יֶדְכֶם וְהָיוּ לְטוֹטָפֹת בֵּין עֵינֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: So you shall set these words of mine on your heart and on your soul, and you shall bind them for a sign on your hand, and they shall become bands between your eyes,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְשַׂמְתֶּם אֶת דְּבָרַי אֵלֶּה עַל לְבַבְכֶם וְעַל נַפְשְׁכֶם וּקְשַׁרְתֶּם אֹתָם לְאוֹת עַל יֶדְכֶם וְהָיוּ לְטוֹטָפֹת בֵּין עֵינֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְלִמַּדְתֶּם אֹתָם אֶת בְּנֵיכֶם לְדַבֵּר בָּם בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵיתֶךָ וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ וּבְשׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ׃
verses.english: and you shall teach them to your children, to speak about them when you sit in your house and when you go in the road and when you lie down and when you get up,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְלִמַּדְתֶּם אֹתָם אֶת בְּנֵיכֶם לְדַבֵּר בָּם בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵיתֶךָ וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ וּבְשׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וּכְתַבְתָּם עַל מְזוּזוֹת בֵּיתֶךָ וּבִשְׁעָרֶיךָ׃
verses.english: and you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and in your gates,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וּכְתַבְתָּם עַל מְזוּזוֹת בֵּיתֶךָ וּבִשְׁעָרֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: לְמַעַן יִרְבּוּ יְמֵיכֶם וִימֵי בְנֵיכֶם עַל הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע יְהֹוָה לַאֲבֹתֵיכֶם לָתֵת לָהֶם כִּימֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם עַל הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.english: so that your days and your children’s days will be many on the land that YHWH swore to your fathers to give them, like the days of the skies over the earth.

tex.original: \hDtrA{לְמַעַן יִרְבּוּ יְמֵיכֶם וִימֵי בְנֵיכֶם עַל הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע יְהֹוָה לַאֲבֹתֵיכֶם לָתֵת לָהֶם כִּימֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם עַל הָאָרֶץ׃}

verses.original: כִּי אִם שָׁמֹר תִּשְׁמְרוּן אֶת כּל הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּה אֶתְכֶם לַעֲשֹׂתָהּ לְאַהֲבָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם לָלֶכֶת בְּכל דְּרָכָיו וּלְדבְקָה בוֹ׃
verses.english: Because, if you will observe all of this commandment that I command you, to do it, to love YHWH, your God, to go in all His ways and to cling to Him,

tex.original: \hDtrA{כִּי אִם שָׁמֹר תִּשְׁמְרוּן אֶת כּל הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּה אֶתְכֶם לַעֲשֹׂתָהּ לְאַהֲבָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם לָלֶכֶת בְּכל דְּרָכָיו וּלְדבְקָה בוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְהוֹרִישׁ יְהֹוָה אֶת כּל הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה מִלִּפְנֵיכֶם וִירִשְׁתֶּם גּוֹיִם גְּדֹלִים וַעֲצֻמִים מִכֶּם׃
verses.english: then YHWH will dispossess all these nations in front of you, and you’ll dispossess bigger and more powerful nations than you.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְהוֹרִישׁ יְהֹוָה אֶת כּל הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה מִלִּפְנֵיכֶם וִירִשְׁתֶּם גּוֹיִם גְּדֹלִים וַעֲצֻמִים מִכֶּם׃}

verses.original: כּל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר תִּדְרֹךְ כַּף רַגְלְכֶם בּוֹ לָכֶם יִהְיֶה מִן הַמִּדְבָּר וְהַלְּבָנוֹן מִן הַנָּהָר נְהַר פְּרָת וְעַד הַיָּם הָאַחֲרוֹן יִהְיֶה גְּבֻלְכֶם׃
verses.english: Every place in which your foot will step shall be yours, from the wilderness and Lebanon, from the river, the Euphrates River, to the far sea shall be your border.

tex.original: \hDtrA{כּל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר תִּדְרֹךְ כַּף רַגְלְכֶם בּוֹ לָכֶם יִהְיֶה מִן הַמִּדְבָּר וְהַלְּבָנוֹן מִן הַנָּהָר נְהַר פְּרָת וְעַד הַיָּם הָאַחֲרוֹן יִהְיֶה גְּבֻלְכֶם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		foot. Hebrew kap regel is often taken to mean “the sole of the foot,”
%		but that is not correct. regel refers to the leg in hebrew (although we
%		often translate it as “foot” in English because of the conventions of
%		usage of the two words “leg” and “foot” in English), and kap regel
%		refers to the portion of the leg from the ankle down, i.e., the foot.
%		See Ezek 1:7, which says: “Their kap regel was like the kap regel of a
%		calf”—which must mean the appearance of a foot and not of the sole of a
%		foot. The same goes for kap yd, which is often taken to mean “the
%		palm of the hand,” but which means the portion of the yd
%		(“forearm,” although, again, we often translate it as “hand” because of
%		English usage) from the wrist down, i.e., the hand. See 2 Kings 9:35,
%		where dogs have eaten Jezebel’s body, and nothing can be found but her
%		skull, legs, and kappôt hayydyîm—which must mean “hands”
%		and not “palms.” (See also the comment on Deut 4:34.) Footnote 11:24.
%		the far sea. The Mediterranean Sea.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא יִתְיַצֵּב אִישׁ בִּפְנֵיכֶם פַּחְדְּכֶם וּמוֹרַאֲכֶם יִתֵּן יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם עַל פְּנֵי כל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר תִּדְרְכוּ בָהּ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָכֶם׃
verses.english: Not a man will stand up in front of you. YHWH, your God, will put awe of you and fear of you on the face of all the land on which you’ll step, as He spoke to you.

tex.original: \hDtrA{לֹא יִתְיַצֵּב אִישׁ בִּפְנֵיכֶם פַּחְדְּכֶם וּמוֹרַאֲכֶם יִתֵּן יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם עַל פְּנֵי כל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר תִּדְרְכוּ בָהּ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָכֶם׃}

verses.original: רְאֵה אָנֹכִי נֹתֵן לִפְנֵיכֶם הַיּוֹם בְּרָכָה וּקְלָלָה׃
verses.english: SEE “See: I’m putting in front of you today a blessing and a curse:

tex.original: \hDtrA{רְאֵה אָנֹכִי נֹתֵן לִפְנֵיכֶם הַיּוֹם בְּרָכָה וּקְלָלָה׃}

verses.original: אֶת הַבְּרָכָה אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶל מִצְוֺת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּה אֶתְכֶם הַיּוֹם׃
verses.english: the blessing when you’ll listen to the commandments of YHWH, your God, that I command you today,

tex.original: \hDtrA{אֶת הַבְּרָכָה אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶל מִצְוֺת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּה אֶתְכֶם הַיּוֹם׃}

verses.original: וְהַקְּלָלָה אִם לֹא תִשְׁמְעוּ אֶל מִצְוֺת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וְסַרְתֶּם מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּה אֶתְכֶם הַיּוֹם לָלֶכֶת אַחֲרֵי אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים אֲשֶׁר לֹא יְדַעְתֶּם׃
verses.english: and the curse if you won’t listen to the commandments of YHWH, your God, and you’ll turn from the way that I command you today, to go after other gods, whom you haven’t known.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְהַקְּלָלָה אִם לֹא תִשְׁמְעוּ אֶל מִצְוֺת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וְסַרְתֶּם מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּה אֶתְכֶם הַיּוֹם לָלֶכֶת אַחֲרֵי אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים אֲשֶׁר לֹא יְדַעְתֶּם׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה בָא שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ וְנָתַתָּה אֶת הַבְּרָכָה עַל הַר גְּרִזִים וְאֶת הַקְּלָלָה עַל הַר עֵיבָל׃
verses.english: And it shall be, when YHWH, your God, will bring you to the land to which you’re coming to take possession of it, that you shall put the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְהָיָה כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה בָא שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ וְנָתַתָּה אֶת הַבְּרָכָה עַל הַר גְּרִזִים וְאֶת הַקְּלָלָה עַל הַר עֵיבָל׃}

verses.original: הֲלֹא הֵמָּה בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן אַחֲרֵי דֶּרֶךְ מְבוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ בְּאֶרֶץ הַכְּנַעֲנִי הַיֹּשֵׁב בָּעֲרָבָה מוּל הַגִּלְגָּל אֵצֶל אֵלוֹנֵי מֹרֶה׃
verses.english: Aren’t they across the Jordan, beyond the way of the sun’s setting, in the land of the Canaanite who lives in the plain, opposite Gilgal, near the oaks of Moreh?

tex.original: \hDtrA{הֲלֹא הֵמָּה בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן אַחֲרֵי דֶּרֶךְ מְבוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ בְּאֶרֶץ הַכְּנַעֲנִי הַיֹּשֵׁב בָּעֲרָבָה מוּל הַגִּלְגָּל אֵצֶל אֵלוֹנֵי מֹרֶה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		oaks of Moreh. The first place to which Abraham comes when he moves to
%		Canaan is the oak of Moreh (Gen 12:6). There YHWH is said to appear to
%		him for the first time (which is also the first time that God is said to
%		have appeared to anyone in the Bible). There YHWH says for the first
%		time that He will give the land to Abraham’s descendants. And there
%		Abraham builds the first altar to YHWH in Canaan. Now the oaks (or oak;
%		the Septuagint has the singular) of Moreh are mentioned just before a
%		statement that those descendants are now about “to come to take
%		possession of the land.” It is thus another signal that the merit of the
%		ancestors is a source of protection and well-being for Israel many
%		generations later. In this case, because Abraham listened to God’s first
%		command and left his home for a new land, his descendants now come to
%		the land.
%	}

verses.original: כִּי אַתֶּם עֹבְרִים אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן לָבֹא לָרֶשֶׁת אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם נֹתֵן לָכֶם וִירִשְׁתֶּם אֹתָהּ וִישַׁבְתֶּם בָּהּ׃
verses.english: Because you’re crossing the Jordan to come to take possession of the land that YHWH, your God, is giving you; and you shall take possession of it and live in it

tex.original: \hDtrA{כִּי אַתֶּם עֹבְרִים אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן לָבֹא לָרֶשֶׁת אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם נֹתֵן לָכֶם וִירִשְׁתֶּם אֹתָהּ וִישַׁבְתֶּם בָּהּ׃}

verses.original: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם לַעֲשׂוֹת אֵת כּל הַחֻקִּים וְאֶת הַמִּשְׁפָּטִים אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי נֹתֵן לִפְנֵיכֶם הַיּוֹם׃
verses.english: and be watchful to do all the laws and the judgments that I’m putting in front of you today.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם לַעֲשׂוֹת אֵת כּל הַחֻקִּים וְאֶת הַמִּשְׁפָּטִים אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי נֹתֵן לִפְנֵיכֶם הַיּוֹם׃}

verses.original: אֵלֶּה הַחֻקִּים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִים אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׁמְרוּן לַעֲשׂוֹת בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵי אֲבֹתֶיךָ לְךָ לְרִשְׁתָּהּ כּל הַיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם חַיִּים עַל הָאֲדָמָה׃
verses.english: “These are the laws and the judgments that you shall be watchful to do in the land that YHWH, your fathers’ God, has given you to take possession of it, every day that you’re living on the land:
verses.commentary:
The book now becomes a law code.

This part is a few hundred years older than all the Deuteronomy we've gone through so far.

Ok so here's the things you have to do once you're in the land.

verses.original: אַבֵּד תְּאַבְּדוּן אֶת כּל הַמְּקֹמוֹת אֲשֶׁר עָבְדוּ שָׁם הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם יֹרְשִׁים אֹתָם אֶת אֱלֹהֵיהֶם עַל הֶהָרִים הָרָמִים וְעַל הַגְּבָעוֹת וְתַחַת כּל עֵץ רַעֲנָן׃

verses.original: וְנִתַּצְתֶּם אֶת מִזְבְּחֹתָם וְשִׁבַּרְתֶּם אֶת מַצֵּבֹתָם וַאֲשֵׁרֵיהֶם תִּשְׂרְפוּן בָּאֵשׁ וּפְסִילֵי אֱלֹהֵיהֶם תְּגַדֵּעוּן וְאִבַּדְתֶּם אֶת שְׁמָם מִן הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא׃
verses.english: And you shall demolish their altars and shatter their pillars and burn their Asherahs in fire and cut down the statues of their gods in fire and destroy their name from that place.
verses.commentary: Destroy their altars and their goddesses and wipe their name from their land.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְנִתַּצְתֶּם אֶת מִזְבְּחֹתָם וְשִׁבַּרְתֶּם אֶת מַצֵּבֹתָם וַאֲשֵׁרֵיהֶם תִּשְׂרְפוּן בָּאֵשׁ וּפְסִילֵי אֱלֹהֵיהֶם תְּגַדֵּעוּן וְאִבַּדְתֶּם אֶת שְׁמָם מִן הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא׃}
tex.commentary: Destroy their altars and their goddesses and wipe their name from their land.

verses.original: לֹא תַעֲשׂוּן כֵּן לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: “You shall not do that for YHWH, your God.
verses.commentary: Don't just worship wherever you want like they do.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תַעֲשׂוּן כֵּן לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃}
tex.english: \eDtn{“You shall not do that for YHWH, your God.}
tex.commentary:
Don't just worship wherever you want like they do.

%	\footnote{
%		You shall not do that. Meaning: you shall not worship your God in many
%		places. Moses has just told the people that the nations worshiped their
%		gods all over the land—on hills, in valleys, and under every tree—and
%		that the Israelites are to destroy “all the places.” In the next verse
%		Moses will tell them that they are to worship their God in only one
%		place.
%	}

verses.original: כִּי אִם אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם מִכּל שִׁבְטֵיכֶם לָשׂוּם אֶת שְׁמוֹ שָׁם לְשִׁכְנוֹ תִדְרְשׁוּ וּבָאתָ שָּׁמָּה׃
verses.english: But, rather, you shall inquire at the place that YHWH, your God, will choose from all your tribes to set His name there, to tent it. And you shall come there,
verses.commentary:
You have to worship at one specific place.

We haven't decided what it is yet, but there's one of them.

It'll be wherever YHWH chooses to put his name in a tent.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי אִם אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם מִכּל שִׁבְטֵיכֶם לָשׂוּם אֶת שְׁמוֹ שָׁם לְשִׁכְנוֹ תִדְרְשׁוּ וּבָאתָ שָּׁמָּה׃}
tex.commentary:
You have to worship at one specific place.

	We haven't decided what it is yet, but there's one of them.

	It'll be wherever YHWH chooses to put his name in a tent.

%	\footnote{
%		the place that YHWH, your God, will choose. This is the central point:
%		There are not to be Temples of YHWH all over the world, or even all over
%		Israel. There is to be only one place. I understand this to be a
%		physical, visible expression of the principle of monotheism: one God,
%		one place of worship. (This does not preclude the postbiblical Jewish
%		practice of having synagogues, nor the Christian practice of having
%		churches, as places of prayer, study, and gathering. It just means that
%		worship involving sacrifices can be done only in the one sanctioned
%		place.) Footnote 12:5. to set His name there. This is known as the
%		Deuteronomistic Name Theology. The concept is that God cannot be
%		contained in all of the universe, so how can a structure built on earth
%		by humans possibly house God? Answer: God causes His name to be
%		contained in the structure. The divine name becomes almost a tangible
%		entity, and it is connected to the structure; that is, to the Tent of
%		Meeting. The visible symbol of the presence of the divine name is the
%		ark. And so every occurrence of this expression in Deuteronomy refers to
%		the place where the ark is. Later the ark and the Tent of Meeting will
%		be moved to the Temple that Solomon builds in Jerusalem (1 Kings 8:4),
%		and on that occasion Solomon will use some of these same terms to convey
%		that the Name is now housed in the Temple (8:12–30). For prayer and
%		sacrifice, Israelites are to focus their attention in the direction of
%		the place where the name of YHWH is housed. Footnote 12:5. to tent it. I
%		follow Frank Moore Cross in the understanding of this word (Hebrew root
%		kn) as denominative from the word mikn, a tent or
%		tabernacle, so that it means that YHWH tents His name there. That is,
%		the Tent of Meeting houses the ark and the divine name. One can pray
%		anywhere, but a great many of the commandments can be fulfilled only at
%		that one place. Most notably, all sacrifices must be made there, and
%		nowhere else on earth.
%	}

verses.original: וַהֲבֵאתֶם שָׁמָּה עֹלֹתֵיכֶם וְזִבְחֵיכֶם וְאֵת מַעְשְׂרֹתֵיכֶם וְאֵת תְּרוּמַת יֶדְכֶם וְנִדְרֵיכֶם וְנִדְבֹתֵיכֶם וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקַרְכֶם וְצֹאנְכֶם׃
verses.english: and bring there your burnt offerings and your sacrifices and your tithes and your hand’s donation and your vows and your contributions and the firstborn of your herd and your flock.
verses.commentary: Bring your sacrifices and your first borns there.

tex.original: \hDtn{וַהֲבֵאתֶם שָׁמָּה עֹלֹתֵיכֶם וְזִבְחֵיכֶם וְאֵת מַעְשְׂרֹתֵיכֶם וְאֵת תְּרוּמַת יֶדְכֶם וְנִדְרֵיכֶם וְנִדְבֹתֵיכֶם וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקַרְכֶם וְצֹאנְכֶם׃}
tex.commentary: Bring your sacrifices and your first borns there.

verses.original: וַאֲכַלְתֶּם שָׁם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וּשְׂמַחְתֶּם בְּכֹל מִשְׁלַח יֶדְכֶם אַתֶּם וּבָתֵּיכֶם אֲשֶׁר בֵּרַכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And you shall eat there in front of YHWH, your God. And you shall rejoice about everything your hand has taken on, you and your households, in that YHWH, your God, has blessed you.
verses.commentary:
You have to eat there in front of Yahweh.

That's where Yahweh is.

Be there and be happy, Yahweh's your God.

tex.original: \hDtn{וַאֲכַלְתֶּם שָׁם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וּשְׂמַחְתֶּם בְּכֹל מִשְׁלַח יֶדְכֶם אַתֶּם וּבָתֵּיכֶם אֲשֶׁר בֵּרַכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃}
tex.commentary:
You have to eat there in front of Yahweh.

	That's where Yahweh is.

	Be there and be happy, Yahweh's your God.

%	\footnote{
%		you shall eat there in front of YHWH. A sacrifice is a sacred meal eaten
%		in the presence of God. The commandments of Leviticus 17 are conveyed
%		again here. The language is different, but the principle is the same:
%		Animals’ lives cannot be taken in a thoughtless way. If one wishes to
%		eat meat, the animal must be killed at the one central place of worship,
%		called the Tabernacle in Leviticus and “the place where YHWH sets His
%		name” in Deuteronomy. Then, instead of slaughter, one participates in
%		holiness when one eats the meal. The meal then includes a component of
%		reverence for the animal’s life and affirms a belief in the unity of
%		God.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא תַעֲשׂוּן כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר אֲנַחְנוּ עֹשִׂים פֹּה הַיּוֹם אִישׁ כּל הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו׃
verses.english: You shall not do it like everything that we’re doing here today, each one, everything that’s right in his own eyes,
verses.commentary: Do as we say, not as we do.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תַעֲשׂוּן כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר אֲנַחְנוּ עֹשִׂים פֹּה הַיּוֹם אִישׁ כּל הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו׃}
tex.commentary: Do as we say, not as we do.

verses.original: כִּי לֹא בָאתֶם עַד עָתָּה אֶל הַמְּנוּחָה וְאֶל הַנַּחֲלָה אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ׃
verses.english: because up to now you haven’t come to the resting place and to the legacy that YHWH, your God, is giving you.
verses.commentary: We'll start doing all the rules once we're in the land.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי לֹא בָאתֶם עַד עָתָּה אֶל הַמְּנוּחָה וְאֶל הַנַּחֲלָה אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ׃}
tex.commentary: We'll start doing all the rules once we're in the land.

verses.original: וַעֲבַרְתֶּם אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן וִישַׁבְתֶּם בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם מַנְחִיל אֶתְכֶם וְהֵנִיחַ לָכֶם מִכּל אֹיְבֵיכֶם מִסָּבִיב וִישַׁבְתֶּם בֶּטַח׃
verses.english: But when you’ll cross the Jordan and live in the land that YHWH, your God, is giving you as a legacy, and He’ll give you rest from all your enemies all around, and you’ll live securely,
verses.commentary: When you're in the land,

tex.original: \hDtn{וַעֲבַרְתֶּם אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן וִישַׁבְתֶּם בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם מַנְחִיל אֶתְכֶם וְהֵנִיחַ לָכֶם מִכּל אֹיְבֵיכֶם מִסָּבִיב וִישַׁבְתֶּם בֶּטַח׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם בּוֹ לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם שָׁמָּה תָבִיאוּ אֵת כּל אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּה אֶתְכֶם עוֹלֹתֵיכֶם וְזִבְחֵיכֶם מַעְשְׂרֹתֵיכֶם וּתְרֻמַת יֶדְכֶם וְכֹל מִבְחַר נִדְרֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר תִּדְּרוּ לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: then it shall be, the place that YHWH, your God, will choose to tent His name there: there you shall bring everything that I command you, your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and your hand’s donation and every choice one of your vows that you’ll make to YHWH.
verses.commentary:
then you go to the place where Yahweh's name is camping,

and you do all the stuff from five lines ago.

I'll say it here again to make sure you don't forget.

verses.original: וּשְׂמַחְתֶּם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אַתֶּם וּבְנֵיכֶם וּבְנֹתֵיכֶם וְעַבְדֵיכֶם וְאַמְהֹתֵיכֶם וְהַלֵּוִי אֲשֶׁר בְּשַׁעֲרֵיכֶם כִּי אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק וְנַחֲלָה אִתְּכֶם׃
verses.english: And you shall rejoice in front of YHWH, your God: you and your sons and your daughters and your servants and your maids and the Levite who is in your gates because he doesn’t have a portion or a legacy with you.
verses.commentary:
And you'll be happy.

You and your family and also the Levites who are different for some reason and they don't have any land in the land except some but don't worry about why.

tex.original: \hDtn{וּשְׂמַחְתֶּם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אַתֶּם וּבְנֵיכֶם וּבְנֹתֵיכֶם וְעַבְדֵיכֶם וְאַמְהֹתֵיכֶם וְהַלֵּוִי אֲשֶׁר בְּשַׁעֲרֵיכֶם כִּי אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק וְנַחֲלָה אִתְּכֶם׃}

	why.

verses.original: הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ פֶּן תַּעֲלֶה עֹלֹתֶיךָ בְּכל מָקוֹם אֲשֶׁר תִּרְאֶה׃
verses.english: “Watch yourself in case you would make your burnt offerings in any place that you’ll see.
verses.commentary: Don't go doing this religion just wherever you want.

tex.original: \hDtn{הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ פֶּן תַּעֲלֶה עֹלֹתֶיךָ בְּכל מָקוֹם אֲשֶׁר תִּרְאֶה׃}
tex.commentary: Don't go doing this religion just wherever you want.

verses.original: כִּי אִם בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה בְּאַחַד שְׁבָטֶיךָ שָׁם תַּעֲלֶה עֹלֹתֶיךָ וְשָׁם תַּעֲשֶׂה כֹּל אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּךָּ׃
verses.english: But, rather, in the place that YHWH will choose in one of your tribes: there you shall make your burnt offerings, and there you shall do everything that I command you.
verses.commentary:
Only do it in the one specific place we haven't decided on yet.

That's where to burn the animals and do everything else I say.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי אִם בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה בְּאַחַד שְׁבָטֶיךָ שָׁם תַּעֲלֶה עֹלֹתֶיךָ וְשָׁם תַּעֲשֶׂה כֹּל אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּךָּ׃}
tex.commentary:
Only do it in the one specific place we haven't decided on yet.

	That's where to burn the animals and do everything else I say.

verses.original: רַק בְּכל אַוַּת נַפְשְׁךָ תִּזְבַּח וְאָכַלְתָּ בָשָׂר כְּבִרְכַּת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לְךָ בְּכל שְׁעָרֶיךָ הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יֹאכְלֶנּוּ כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל׃
verses.english: Only, as much as your soul desires you may slaughter and may eat meat according to the blessing of YHWH, your God, that He has given you in all your gates. The impure and the pure may eat it: like a gazelle, like a deer.
verses.commentary:
Ok we've gotten some complaints about the rules, specifically as regards hunting.

Some very nice men with real scary weapons who like to hunt said they're not bringing their deer or gazelles to some altar several days walk from their house before they kill it.

The guys up in Dan specifically said something about how it's a 50 hour walk, and that's an unreasonable distance to carry a deer while it's alive before you're allowed to kill it.

We've decided to make an exception for these fine gentlemen with the weapons.

Kill the deer wherever.

Please don't come to the tent.

tex.original: \hDtn{רַק בְּכל אַוַּת נַפְשְׁךָ תִּזְבַּח וְאָכַלְתָּ בָשָׂר כְּבִרְכַּת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לְךָ בְּכל שְׁעָרֶיךָ הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יֹאכְלֶנּוּ כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל׃}
tex.commentary:
Ok we've gotten some complaints about the rules, specifically as regards
	hunting.

	Some very nice men with real scary weapons who like to hunt said they're not
	bringing their deer or gazelles to some altar several days walk from their
	house before they kill it.

	The guys up in Dan specifically said something about how it's a 50 hour walk,
	and that's an unreasonable distance to carry a deer while it's alive before
	you're allowed to kill it.

	We've decided to make an exception for these fine gentlemen with the weapons.

	Kill the deer wherever.

	Please don't come to the tent.

%	\footnote{
%		like a gazelle, like a deer. Israelites may kill an animal as a
%		sacrifice only at the one place that will be chosen (which will
%		ultimately be the Temple). But they may slaughter an animal in a
%		nonsacrificial way (that is, secular rather than ritual slaughter) at
%		any other place. Then the same laws apply to this slaughter as would
%		apply to animals that are killed by hunting, such as gazelles and deer:
%		(1) the blood must be spilled off and not eaten; (2) only people who are
%		in a condition of ritual purity may eat sacrificed meat, but this
%		secularly slaughtered meat may be eaten by anyone, pure or impure.
%	}

verses.original: רַק הַדָּם לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ עַל הָאָרֶץ תִּשְׁפְּכֶנּוּ כַּמָּיִם׃
verses.english: Only, you shall not eat the blood. You shall spill it like water on the earth.
verses.commentary:
Just don't eat the blood.

Spill it on the earth.

If that's too confusing for some of you, just imagine it's water.

You can spill water right?

Right, same thing.

tex.original: \hDtn{רַק הַדָּם לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ עַל הָאָרֶץ תִּשְׁפְּכֶנּוּ כַּמָּיִם׃}
tex.commentary:
Just don't eat the blood.

	Spill it on the earth.

	If that's too confusing for some of you, just imagine it's water.

	You can spill water right?

	Right, same thing.

verses.original: לֹא תוּכַל לֶאֱכֹל בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ וְתִירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנֶךָ וְכל נְדָרֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּדֹּר וְנִדְבֹתֶיךָ וּתְרוּמַת יָדֶךָ׃
verses.english: You may not eat within your gates the tithe of your grain or your wine or your oil or the firstborn of your herd or your flock or all your vows that you’ll make or your contributions or your hand’s donation.
verses.commentary:
Things you can't eat at home include your tithe (10%) of the following:

• Grain
• Wine
• Oil
• Firstborn cows
• Firstborn sheep
• Vows
• Donations

Don't eat any of those at home.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תוּכַל לֶאֱכֹל בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ וְתִירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנֶךָ וְכל נְדָרֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּדֹּר וְנִדְבֹתֶיךָ וּתְרוּמַת יָדֶךָ׃}
tex.commentary:
Things you can't eat at home include your tithe (10\%) of the following:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item Grain
		\item Wine
		\item Oil
		\item Firstborn cows
		\item Firstborn sheep
		\item Vows
		\item Donations
	\end{itemize}

	Don't eat any of those at home.

verses.original: כִּי אִם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בּוֹ אַתָּה וּבִנְךָ וּבִתֶּךָ וְעַבְדְּךָ וַאֲמָתֶךָ וְהַלֵּוִי אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ וְשָׂמַחְתָּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכֹל מִשְׁלַח יָדֶךָ׃
verses.english: But, rather, you shall eat them in front of YHWH, your God, in the place that YHWH, your God, will choose: you and your son and your daughter and your servant and your maid and the Levite who is in your gates. And you shall rejoice in front of YHWH, your God, about everything your hand has taken on.
verses.commentary:
Eat them in front of Yahweh.

He's your god, remember?

So eat it in front of him, wherever he is.

Monotheism isn't about some magic god that lives everywhere.

Monotheism is about going to where god is.

He hasn't decided where he's going to be yet.

He'll let you know when he gets there.

These are the rules for you and your sons and your daughters and your servants in your maids and the Levites who are different for some reason don't worry about why.

You'll do all of that and you'll be happy.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי אִם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בּוֹ אַתָּה וּבִנְךָ וּבִתֶּךָ וְעַבְדְּךָ וַאֲמָתֶךָ וְהַלֵּוִי אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ וְשָׂמַחְתָּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכֹל מִשְׁלַח יָדֶךָ׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		But, rather, you shall eat them in front of YHWH, your
		God, in the place that YHWH, your God, will choose: you
		and your son and your daughter and your servant and your
		maid and the Levite who is in your gates. And you shall
		rejoice in front of YHWH, your God, about everything your
		hand has taken on.
	}
tex.commentary:
Eat them in front of Yahweh.

	He's your god, remember?

	So eat it in front of him, wherever he is.

	Monotheism isn't about some magic god that lives everywhere.

	Monotheism is about going to where god is.

	He hasn't decided where he's going to be yet.

	He'll let you know when he gets there.

	These are the rules for you and your sons and your daughters and your servants
	in your maids and the Levites who are different for some reason don't worry
	about why.

	You'll do all of that and you'll be happy.

verses.original: הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ פֶּן תַּעֲזֹב אֶת הַלֵּוִי כּל יָמֶיךָ עַל אַדְמָתֶךָ׃
verses.english: Watch yourself in case you would leave the Levite, all your days in your land.
verses.commentary: Watch yourself, don't forget about the Levites.

tex.original: \hDtn{הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ פֶּן תַּעֲזֹב אֶת הַלֵּוִי כּל יָמֶיךָ עַל אַדְמָתֶךָ׃}
tex.commentary: Watch yourself, don't forget about the Levites.

verses.original: כִּי יַרְחִיב יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת גְּבֻלְךָ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ אֹכְלָה בָשָׂר כִּי תְאַוֶּה נַפְשְׁךָ לֶאֱכֹל בָּשָׂר בְּכל אַוַּת נַפְשְׁךָ תֹּאכַל בָּשָׂר׃
verses.english: “When YHWH, your God, will widen your border as He spoke to you, and you’ll say, ‘Let me eat meat,’ because your soul will desire to eat meat, you may eat meat as much as your soul desires.
verses.commentary: When Yahweh makes the country bigger and you say “Let me have meat” because naturally, you want meat, you can eat as much as you want.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יַרְחִיב יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת גְּבֻלְךָ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ אֹכְלָה בָשָׂר כִּי תְאַוֶּה נַפְשְׁךָ לֶאֱכֹל בָּשָׂר בְּכל אַוַּת נַפְשְׁךָ תֹּאכַל בָּשָׂר׃}
tex.commentary:
When Yahweh makes the country bigger and you say ``Let me have meat'' because
	naturally, you want meat, you can eat as much as you want.

verses.original: כִּי יִרְחַק מִמְּךָ הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לָשׂוּם שְׁמוֹ שָׁם וְזָבַחְתָּ מִבְּקָרְךָ וּמִצֹּאנְךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן יְהֹוָה לְךָ כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִךָ וְאָכַלְתָּ בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ בְּכֹל אַוַּת נַפְשֶׁךָ׃
verses.english: When the place that YHWH, your God, will choose to put His name there will be far from you, then you shall slaughter from your herd and from your flock that YHWH has given you as I’ve commanded you, and you may eat within your gates as much as your soul desires.
verses.commentary:
Look we've gotten more complaints about the rules.

So whenever you live too far from wherever Yahweh's name is camping, just have as much meat as you want.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִרְחַק מִמְּךָ הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לָשׂוּם שְׁמוֹ שָׁם וְזָבַחְתָּ מִבְּקָרְךָ וּמִצֹּאנְךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן יְהֹוָה לְךָ כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִךָ וְאָכַלְתָּ בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ בְּכֹל אַוַּת נַפְשֶׁךָ׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		When the place that YHWH, your God, will choose to put His
		name there will be far from you, then you shall slaughter
		from your herd and from your flock that YHWH has given you
		as I’ve commanded you, and you may eat within your gates
		as much as your soul desires.
	}
tex.commentary:
Look we've gotten more complaints about the rules.

	So whenever you live too far from wherever Yahweh's name is camping, just have
	as much meat as you want.

verses.original: אַךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵאָכֵל אֶת הַצְּבִי וְאֶת הָאַיָּל כֵּן תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יַחְדָּו יֹאכְלֶנּוּ׃
verses.english: Just: as a gazelle and a deer are eaten, so you shall eat it. The impure and the pure may eat it together.
verses.commentary: Same rules as for the hunters from earlier.

tex.original: \hDtn{אַךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר יֵאָכֵל אֶת הַצְּבִי וְאֶת הָאַיָּל כֵּן תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יַחְדָּו יֹאכְלֶנּוּ׃}
tex.commentary: Same rules as for the hunters from earlier.

verses.original: רַק חֲזַק לְבִלְתִּי אֲכֹל הַדָּם כִּי הַדָּם הוּא הַנָּפֶשׁ וְלֹא תֹאכַל הַנֶּפֶשׁ עִם הַבָּשָׂר׃
verses.english: Only, be strong not to eat the blood, because the blood: it’s the life; and you shall not eat the life with the meat.
verses.commentary:
Just don't eat the blood.

The blood is the life.

What kind of a sick disgusting murderer eats the life?

... so just kill the animal but don't eat it's life with the meat.

tex.original: \hDtn{רַק חֲזַק לְבִלְתִּי אֲכֹל הַדָּם כִּי הַדָּם הוּא הַנָּפֶשׁ וְלֹא תֹאכַל הַנֶּפֶשׁ עִם הַבָּשָׂר׃}
tex.commentary:
Just don't eat the blood.

	The blood is the life.

	What kind of a sick disgusting murderer eats the life?

	... so just kill the animal but don't eat it's life with the meat.

verses.original: לֹא תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ עַל הָאָרֶץ תִּשְׁפְּכֶנּוּ כַּמָּיִם׃
verses.english: You shall not eat it. You shall spill it like water on the earth.
verses.commentary: Don't eat it. Spill it on the ground. Do I need to explain how it's like water again?

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ עַל הָאָרֶץ תִּשְׁפְּכֶנּוּ כַּמָּיִם׃}
tex.commentary:
Don't eat it. Spill it on the ground. Do I need to explain how it's like water
	again?

verses.original: לֹא תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ לְמַעַן יִיטַב לְךָ וּלְבָנֶיךָ אַחֲרֶיךָ כִּי תַעֲשֶׂה הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: You shall not eat it, so it will be good for you and for your children after you when you do what is right in YHWH’s eyes.
verses.commentary: Don't eat it, so it'll be good for you and your descendants when you do what Yahweh says.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ לְמַעַן יִיטַב לְךָ וּלְבָנֶיךָ אַחֲרֶיךָ כִּי תַעֲשֶׂה הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה׃}
tex.commentary:
Don't eat it, so it'll be good for you and your descendants when you do what
	Yahweh says.

verses.original: רַק קדָשֶׁיךָ אֲשֶׁר יִהְיוּ לְךָ וּנְדָרֶיךָ תִּשָּׂא וּבָאתָ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: “Only, you shall carry your holy things that you’ll have and your vows and shall come to the place that YHWH will choose.
verses.commentary:
Things to carry when you come to the place we haven't decided yet that Yahweh will decide on later:

• Holy things
• Vows

tex.original: \hDtn{רַק קדָשֶׁיךָ אֲשֶׁר יִהְיוּ לְךָ וּנְדָרֶיךָ תִּשָּׂא וּבָאתָ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ עֹלֹתֶיךָ הַבָּשָׂר וְהַדָּם עַל מִזְבַּח יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ עַל מִזְבַּח יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְהַבָּשָׂר תֹּאכֵל׃
verses.english: And you shall do your burnt offerings, the meat and the blood, on the altar of YHWH, your God. And the blood of your sacrifices shall be spilled on the altar of YHWH, your God, and you shall eat the meat.
verses.commentary:
Do the thing with the burning and the meat and the blood on the altar of Yahweh, he's your God.

And you take the animal's blood and you spill it on the altar of Yahweh, he's your God.

Then you can eat the meat.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְעָשִׂיתָ עֹלֹתֶיךָ הַבָּשָׂר וְהַדָּם עַל מִזְבַּח יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְדַם זְבָחֶיךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ עַל מִזְבַּח יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְהַבָּשָׂר תֹּאכֵל׃}
tex.commentary:
Do the thing with the burning and the meat and the blood on the altar of
	Yahweh, he's your God.

	And you take the animal's blood and you spill it on the altar of Yahweh, he's
	your God.

	Then you can eat the meat.

%	\footnote{
%		sacrifices. This refers to sacrifices that are for food (as opposed to
%		burnt offerings, which the donor does not eat). The blood is to be
%		poured off at the altar, and then one may eat the meat of the sacrifice.
%	}

verses.original: שְׁמֹר וְשָׁמַעְתָּ אֵת כּל הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּךָּ לְמַעַן יִיטַב לְךָ וּלְבָנֶיךָ אַחֲרֶיךָ עַד עוֹלָם כִּי תַעֲשֶׂה הַטּוֹב וְהַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: Be watchful that you listen to all these things that I command you so that it will be good for you and for your children after you forever when you’ll do what is good and right in the eyes of YHWH, your God.
verses.commentary:
Everybody listen. It's good for you.
