verses.english: You shall not do this for YHWH, your God, because they did every offensive thing of YHWH that He hates for their gods, because they would also burn their sons and their daughters in fire to their gods!
verses.commentary: Don't do that for you always, he's your god, it's offensive to YHWH, he hates that, don't do the things he hates for their gods, because they would also do human sacrifice and burn their sons and daughters to their gods! The bible often accuses the Canaanites of human sacrifice, but there is no evidence in the archaeological record of this practice ever occuring among the native Canaanites—even at the more well excavated sites such as Ugarit. The one people in the ancient Near East whom our sources explicitly report practicing human sacrifice are, ironically, Israel themselves. The well documented evidence of human sacrifice to the god Baal Hammon comes much later from outside the ancient near east, at Punic sites in North Africa, particularly Carthage. Kings explicitly attributes child sacrifice to two kings of Judah: Ahaz (2 Kgs 16:3) and Manasseh (21:6); it also says Israelites generally sacrificed their sons and daughters (17:17) and records Josiah suppressing the practice at Topheth (23:10). Mesha, king of Moab, sacrifices a royal son during a war (3:27); the text calls him Mesha’s own heir, though this is likely a mistake of Mesha's own son for an Edomite prince from the opposing army, as Mesha had just attacked the king of Edom and Amos 2:1 independently accuses Moab of burning the bones of an Edomite king. End of chapter!

verses.original: כִּי הָרֹג תַּהַרְגֶנּוּ יָדְךָ תִּהְיֶה בּוֹ בָרִאשׁוֹנָה לַהֲמִיתוֹ וְיַד כּל הָעָם בָּאַחֲרֹנָה׃

verses.commentary:
KILL HIM.

Yes you specifically.

Kill your friend or whoever it was.

You start killing him and then everyone else in town joins in.

verses.original: וְדָרַשְׁתָּ וְחָקַרְתָּ וְשָׁאַלְתָּ הֵיטֵב וְהִנֵּה אֱמֶת נָכוֹן הַדָּבָר נֶעֶשְׂתָה הַתּוֹעֵבָה הַזֹּאת בְּקִרְבֶּךָ׃
verses.english: and you’ll inquire and investigate and ask well, and, here, the thing is true—this offensive thing was done among you—
verses.commentary: and you'll look into it and realize it's true—this offensive thing happened right here among you—

verses.original: הַכֵּה תַכֶּה אֶת יֹשְׁבֵי הָעִיר הַהִוא לְפִי חָרֶב הַחֲרֵם אֹתָהּ וְאֶת כּל אֲשֶׁר בָּהּ וְאֶת בְּהֶמְתָּהּ לְפִי חָרֶב׃
verses.english: you shall strike that city’s residents by the sword, completely destroying it and everything in it and its animals with the sword.
verses.commentary: cut 'em all up into little pieces and kill all the people in the city and all the animals too with the sword.

tex.original: \hDtn{הַכֵּה תַכֶּה אֶת יֹשְׁבֵי הָעִיר הַהִוא לְפִי חָרֶב הַחֲרֵם אֹתָהּ וְאֶת כּל אֲשֶׁר בָּהּ וְאֶת בְּהֶמְתָּהּ לְפִי חָרֶב׃}
tex.commentary:
cut 'em all up into little pieces and kill all the people in the city and all
	the animals too with the sword.

%	\footnote{
%		completely destroying it and everything in it. On the extreme violence
%		that is commanded in destroying those (Israelites) who would lead one to
%		worship other gods, or in destroying an entire Israelite town that
%		worships other gods (including any righteous; cf. Sodom): again the
%		Torah distinguishes between ethical sins and ritual sins. Ethical sins
%		(those that occur between a human and one’s fellow humans; theft, for
%		example) are judged in terms of each individual person’s actions, and
%		the person’s intent is taken into account. Ritual sins (those that are
%		between a human and God; blasphemy, for example) are judged in terms of
%		groups and zones, and intent is not an issue. Thus, when Achan violates
%		the law of erem in Joshua 7, the text says that “the children of
%		Israel” violated the erem (7:1)—and all of Israel suffers a
%		defeat. Achan takes items that were forbidden to the Israelites, and he
%		hides them in his tent; and the result is that not only is Achan stoned
%		and burned, but his family, his animals, everything that was in the
%		tent, and also the tent itself are stoned and burned. Questions about
%		the harsh response to Israelites who turn to (or seduce others to) pagan
%		worship must be addressed in this light. Worship of other gods is the
%		ultimate ritual sin in Deuteronomy. As with all ritual infringements,
%		the perpetrators must be utterly eliminated from Israel. If it is an
%		entire city, then that city must be eliminated from Israel—including any
%		righteous members of the community and even the animals. All of this may
%		seem foreign and barbaric in our time. That is because (1) Israel has
%		not been a religious state for 2000 years; and (2) after the destruction
%		of the Second Temple, ritual became less central in Judaism, and
%		emphasis on ethics rose. Also, (3) monotheism has defeated pagan
%		religion in Western civilization, so we no longer feel the degree of
%		threat that authors of the Bible felt toward it.
%	}

verses.original: וְאֶת כּל שְׁלָלָהּ תִּקְבֹּץ אֶל תּוֹךְ רְחֹבָהּ וְשָׂרַפְתָּ בָאֵשׁ אֶת הָעִיר וְאֶת כּל שְׁלָלָהּ כָּלִיל לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְהָיְתָה תֵּל עוֹלָם לֹא תִבָּנֶה עוֹד׃
verses.english: And you shall gather all its spoil into the middle of its square, and you shall burn the city and all its spoil in fire entirely to YHWH, your God, and it shall be a tell eternally. It shall not be rebuilt again.
verses.commentary: Then you gather all their stuff up into a big pile, and burn the city and all its stuff in fire to Yahweh, your God, and it'll be a big pile forever so everyone knows never to rebuild the city again!

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאֶת כּל שְׁלָלָהּ תִּקְבֹּץ אֶל תּוֹךְ רְחֹבָהּ וְשָׂרַפְתָּ בָאֵשׁ אֶת הָעִיר וְאֶת כּל שְׁלָלָהּ כָּלִיל לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְהָיְתָה תֵּל עוֹלָם לֹא תִבָּנֶה עוֹד׃}
tex.commentary:
Then you gather all their stuff up into a big pile, and burn the city and all
	its stuff in fire to Yahweh, \emph{your} God, and it'll be a big pile forever
	so everyone knows never to rebuild the city again!

%	\footnote{
%		a tell. A tell is a hill that came to exist as a result of successive
%		layers of cities being built on top of one another. Because a tell is
%		composed of sand and rock and debris rather than soil, very little grass
%		or vegetation grows on it. Such a mound is a treasure to an
%		archaeologist, but it is a curse here in the text: not only is an
%		apostate city to be destroyed, but it is to become a tell permanently,
%		never to be rebuilt.
%	}

verses.original: וְלֹא יִדְבַּק בְּיָדְךָ מְאוּמָה מִן הַחֵרֶם לְמַעַן יָשׁוּב יְהֹוָה מֵחֲרוֹן אַפּוֹ וְנָתַן לְךָ רַחֲמִים וְרִחַמְךָ וְהִרְבֶּךָ כַּאֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע לַאֲבֹתֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And let nothing from the complete destruction cling in your hand, so that YHWH will turn back from His flaring anger and will give you mercy. And He’ll be merciful to you and multiply you as He swore to your fathers
verses.commentary:
Don't keep anything. Burn it all.

That way Yahweh won't hit you with that burning anger of his and he'll give you mercy instead.

And he'll multiply your seed like the stars in the sky and give you more paternity than you can possibly father in a lifetime!

verses.original: כִּי תִשְׁמַע בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לִשְׁמֹר אֶת כּל מִצְוֺתָיו אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לַעֲשׂוֹת הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: when you’ll listen to the voice of YHWH, your God, to observe all His commandments that I command you today, to do what is right in the eyes of YHWH, your God.
verses.commentary:
Do it.

You know it's right.

End of chapter!

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תִשְׁמַע בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לִשְׁמֹר אֶת כּל מִצְוֺתָיו אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לַעֲשׂוֹת הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: בָּנִים אַתֶּם לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם לֹא תִתְגֹּדְדוּ וְלֹא תָשִׂימוּ קרְחָה בֵּין עֵינֵיכֶם לָמֵת׃
verses.english: “You are children of YHWH, your God. You shall not cut yourselves and shall not make a bald place between your eyes for the dead.

tex.original: \hDtn{בָּנִים אַתֶּם לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם לֹא תִתְגֹּדְדוּ וְלֹא תָשִׂימוּ קרְחָה בֵּין עֵינֵיכֶם לָמֵת׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		cut yourselves. This commandment is already given, in different
%		language, in Lev 19:28. Now the commandment not to “make a bald place”
%		is added to it. In Leviticus this latter commandment refers only to
%		priests (21:5). In some matters, such as entry into the Tabernacle,
%		priests are different from the rest of the people. But in certain other
%		matters, all Israelites are to behave like priests, reflecting the idea
%		that “you are a holy people to YHWH,” which is stated in the next verse

%		reminder of what Israel was told at the beginning of the covenant at
%		Sinai: if they will listen and observe the covenant, they will be a
%		“kingdom of priests” (Exod 19:6).
%	}

verses.original: כִּי עַם קָדוֹשׁ אַתָּה לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וּבְךָ בָּחַר יְהֹוָה לִהְיוֹת לוֹ לְעַם סְגֻלָּה מִכֹּל הָעַמִּים אֲשֶׁר עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה׃
verses.english: Because you are a holy people to YHWH, your God, and YHWH has chosen you to become a treasured people to Him out of all the peoples who are on the face of the earth.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי עַם קָדוֹשׁ אַתָּה לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וּבְךָ בָּחַר יְהֹוָה לִהְיוֹת לוֹ לְעַם סְגֻלָּה מִכֹּל הָעַמִּים אֲשֶׁר עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה׃}

verses.english: “You shall not eat any offensive thing.

verses.english: This is the animal that you shall eat: ox, lamb of sheep, and lamb of goats,

verses.english: deer and gazelle and roebuck and wild goat and bison and antelope and mountain sheep

tex.original: \hDtn{אַיָּל וּצְבִי וְיַחְמוּר וְאַקּוֹ וְדִישֹׁן וּתְאוֹ וָזָמֶר׃}

verses.original: וְכל בְּהֵמָה מַפְרֶסֶת פַּרְסָה וְשֹׁסַעַת שֶׁסַע שְׁתֵּי פְרָסוֹת מַעֲלַת גֵּרָה בַּבְּהֵמָה אֹתָהּ תֹּאכֵלוּ׃
verses.english: and every animal that has a hoof and that has a split of hooves in two, that regurgitates cud, among animals, you shall eat it.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכל בְּהֵמָה מַפְרֶסֶת פַּרְסָה וְשֹׁסַעַת שֶׁסַע שְׁתֵּי פְרָסוֹת מַעֲלַת גֵּרָה בַּבְּהֵמָה אֹתָהּ תֹּאכֵלוּ׃}

verses.original: אַךְ אֶת זֶה לֹא תֹאכְלוּ מִמַּעֲלֵי הַגֵּרָה וּמִמַּפְרִיסֵי הַפַּרְסָה הַשְּׁסוּעָה אֶת הַגָּמָל וְאֶת הָאַרְנֶבֶת וְאֶת הַשָּׁפָן כִּי מַעֲלֵה גֵרָה הֵמָּה וּפַרְסָה לֹא הִפְרִיסוּ טְמֵאִים הֵם לָכֶם׃
verses.english: Except you shall not eat this out of those that regurgitate the cud and out of those that have a hoof: the camel and the rock-badger and the hare, because they regurgitate cud and do not have a hoof; they are impure to you.

tex.original: \hDtn{אַךְ אֶת זֶה לֹא תֹאכְלוּ מִמַּעֲלֵי הַגֵּרָה וּמִמַּפְרִיסֵי הַפַּרְסָה הַשְּׁסוּעָה אֶת הַגָּמָל וְאֶת הָאַרְנֶבֶת וְאֶת הַשָּׁפָן כִּי מַעֲלֵה גֵרָה הֵמָּה וּפַרְסָה לֹא הִפְרִיסוּ טְמֵאִים הֵם לָכֶם׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		Except you shall not eat this out of those that
		regurgitate the cud and out of those that have a hoof: the
		camel and the rock-badger and the hare, because they
		regurgitate cud and do not have a hoof; they are impure to
		you.
	}

verses.original: וְאֶת הַחֲזִיר כִּי מַפְרִיס פַּרְסָה הוּא וְלֹא גֵרָה טָמֵא הוּא לָכֶם מִבְּשָׂרָם לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ וּבְנִבְלָתָם לֹא תִגָּעוּ׃
verses.english: And the pig, because it has a hoof but no cud; it is impure to you. You shall not eat from their meat, and you shall not touch their carcass.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאֶת הַחֲזִיר כִּי מַפְרִיס פַּרְסָה הוּא וְלֹא גֵרָה טָמֵא הוּא לָכֶם מִבְּשָׂרָם לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ וּבְנִבְלָתָם לֹא תִגָּעוּ׃}

verses.original: אֶת זֶה תֹּאכְלוּ מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר בַּמָּיִם כֹּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ סְנַפִּיר וְקַשְׂקֶשֶׂת תֹּאכֵלוּ׃
verses.english: “You shall eat this out of all that are in the water: you shall eat every one that has fins and scales.

tex.original: \hDtn{אֶת זֶה תֹּאכְלוּ מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר בַּמָּיִם כֹּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ סְנַפִּיר וְקַשְׂקֶשֶׂת תֹּאכֵלוּ׃}

verses.original: וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר אֵין לוֹ סְנַפִּיר וְקַשְׂקֶשֶׂת לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ טָמֵא הוּא לָכֶם׃
verses.english: And you shall not eat any one that does not have fins and scales; it is impure to you.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר אֵין לוֹ סְנַפִּיר וְקַשְׂקֶשֶׂת לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ טָמֵא הוּא לָכֶם׃}

verses.original: כּל צִפּוֹר טְהֹרָה תֹּאכֵלוּ׃
verses.english: “And you shall eat any pure bird.

tex.original: \hDtn{כּל צִפּוֹר טְהֹרָה תֹּאכֵלוּ׃}
tex.english: \eDtn{“And you shall eat any pure bird.}

verses.original: וְזֶה אֲשֶׁר לֹא תֹאכְלוּ מֵהֶם הַנֶּשֶׁר וְהַפֶּרֶס וְהָעזְנִיָּה׃
verses.english: And this is what you shall not eat from them: the eagle and the vulture and the black vulture

tex.original: \hDtn{וְזֶה אֲשֶׁר לֹא תֹאכְלוּ מֵהֶם הַנֶּשֶׁר וְהַפֶּרֶס וְהָעזְנִיָּה׃}

verses.original: וְהָרָאָה וְאֶת הָאַיָּה וְהַדַּיָּה לְמִינָהּ׃
verses.english: and the kite and the falcon by its kind

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהָרָאָה וְאֶת הָאַיָּה וְהַדַּיָּה לְמִינָהּ׃}
tex.english: \eDtn{and the kite and the falcon by its kind}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		kite and the falcon. There are problems, apparently scribal, in this
%		verse. The first word, r’h, is an apparent resh/dalet
%		scribal error for d’h, as it appears in Lev 11:14. The
%		third word, dayyh, may be a further confusion of
%		d’h. It does not appear in the Septuagint.
%	}

verses.original: וְאֵת כּל עֹרֵב לְמִינוֹ׃
verses.english: and every raven by its kind

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאֵת כּל עֹרֵב לְמִינוֹ׃}
tex.english: \eDtn{and every raven by its kind}

verses.original: וְאֵת בַּת הַיַּעֲנָה וְאֶת הַתַּחְמָס וְאֶת הַשָּׁחַף וְאֶת הַנֵּץ לְמִינֵהוּ׃
verses.english: and the eagle owl and the nighthawk and the seagull and the hawk by its kind,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאֵת בַּת הַיַּעֲנָה וְאֶת הַתַּחְמָס וְאֶת הַשָּׁחַף וְאֶת הַנֵּץ לְמִינֵהוּ׃}

verses.original: אֶת הַכּוֹס וְאֶת הַיַּנְשׁוּף וְהַתִּנְשָׁמֶת׃
verses.english: the little owl and the great owl and the white owl

tex.original: \hDtn{אֶת הַכּוֹס וְאֶת הַיַּנְשׁוּף וְהַתִּנְשָׁמֶת׃}
tex.english: \eDtn{the little owl and the great owl and the white owl}

verses.original: וְהַקָּאָת וְאֶת הָרָחָמָה וְאֶת הַשָּׁלָךְ׃
verses.english: and the pelican and the fish hawk and the cormorant

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהַקָּאָת וְאֶת הָרָחָמָה וְאֶת הַשָּׁלָךְ׃}
tex.english: \eDtn{and the pelican and the fish hawk and the cormorant}

verses.original: וְהַחֲסִידָה וְהָאֲנָפָה לְמִינָהּ וְהַדּוּכִיפַת וְהָעֲטַלֵּף׃
verses.english: and the stork and the heron by its kind and the hoopoe and the bat.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהַחֲסִידָה וְהָאֲנָפָה לְמִינָהּ וְהַדּוּכִיפַת וְהָעֲטַלֵּף׃}

verses.original: וְכֹל שֶׁרֶץ הָעוֹף טָמֵא הוּא לָכֶם לֹא יֵאָכֵלוּ׃
verses.english: “And every swarming thing of flying creatures; it is impure to you. It shall not be eaten.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכֹל שֶׁרֶץ הָעוֹף טָמֵא הוּא לָכֶם לֹא יֵאָכֵלוּ׃}

verses.original: כּל עוֹף טָהוֹר תֹּאכֵלוּ׃
verses.english: You shall eat every pure bird.

tex.original: \hDtn{כּל עוֹף טָהוֹר תֹּאכֵלוּ׃}
tex.english: \eDtn{You shall eat every pure bird.}

verses.original: לֹא תֹאכְלוּ כל נְבֵלָה לַגֵּר אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ תִּתְּנֶנָּה וַאֲכָלָהּ אוֹ מָכֹר לְנכְרִי כִּי עַם קָדוֹשׁ אַתָּה לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תְבַשֵּׁל גְּדִי בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ׃
verses.english: “You shall not eat any carcass. You shall give it to the alien who is in your gates, and he will eat it, or sell to a foreigner. Because you are a holy people to YHWH, your God. “You shall not cook a kid in its mother’s milk.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תֹאכְלוּ כל נְבֵלָה לַגֵּר אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ תִּתְּנֶנָּה וַאֲכָלָהּ אוֹ מָכֹר לְנכְרִי כִּי עַם קָדוֹשׁ אַתָּה לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תְבַשֵּׁל גְּדִי בַּחֲלֵב אִמּוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		a kid in its mother’s milk. This is the third occurrence of this command
%		(Exod 23:19; 34:26), and it is the first time that it is grouped with
%		the laws of forbidden animals. It does not appear in the corresponding
%		list in Leviticus 11. Its origin and purpose are thus different from the
%		other dietary laws. Its original meaning may have been ritual or moral
%		(see the comment on Exod 23:19), but it belongs to a different category
%		of law from the prohibitions of eating pigs and other animals.
%	}

verses.original: עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר אֵת כּל תְּבוּאַת זַרְעֶךָ הַיֹּצֵא הַשָּׂדֶה שָׁנָה שָׁנָה׃
verses.english: “You shall tithe all of your seed’s produce that comes out of the field year by year.

tex.original: \hDtn{עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר אֵת כּל תְּבוּאַת זַרְעֶךָ הַיֹּצֵא הַשָּׂדֶה שָׁנָה שָׁנָה׃}

verses.original: וְאָכַלְתָּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ תִּירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנֶךָ לְמַעַן תִּלְמַד לְיִרְאָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כּל הַיָּמִים׃
verses.english: And you shall eat the tithe of your grain, your wine, and your oil and the firstborn of your herd and your flock in front of YHWH, your God, in the place that He will choose to tent His name there, so that you’ll learn to fear YHWH, your God, all the days.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאָכַלְתָּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ תִּירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנֶךָ לְמַעַן תִּלְמַד לְיִרְאָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כּל הַיָּמִים׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		And you shall eat the tithe of your grain, your wine, and
		your oil and the firstborn of your herd and your flock in
		front of YHWH, your God, in the place that He will choose
		to tent His name there, so that you’ll learn to fear YHWH,
		your God, all the days.
	}

verses.original: וְכִי יִרְבֶּה מִמְּךָ הַדֶּרֶךְ כִּי לֹא תוּכַל שְׂאֵתוֹ כִּי יִרְחַק מִמְּךָ הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לָשׂוּם שְׁמוֹ שָׁם כִּי יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And if the way will be too long for you because you won’t be able to carry it because the place that YHWH, your God, will choose to set His name there will be far from you, because YHWH, your God, will bless you,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכִי יִרְבֶּה מִמְּךָ הַדֶּרֶךְ כִּי לֹא תוּכַל שְׂאֵתוֹ כִּי יִרְחַק מִמְּךָ הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לָשׂוּם שְׁמוֹ שָׁם כִּי יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: וְנָתַתָּה בַּכָּסֶף וְצַרְתָּ הַכֶּסֶף בְּיָדְךָ וְהָלַכְתָּ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בּוֹ׃
verses.english: then you shall give it by money. And you shall enclose the money in your hand and go to the place that YHWH, your God, will choose.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְנָתַתָּה בַּכָּסֶף וְצַרְתָּ הַכֶּסֶף בְּיָדְךָ וְהָלַכְתָּ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בּוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְנָתַתָּה הַכֶּסֶף בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תְּאַוֶּה נַפְשְׁךָ בַּבָּקָר וּבַצֹּאן וּבַיַּיִן וּבַשֵּׁכָר וּבְכֹל אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׁאָלְךָ נַפְשֶׁךָ וְאָכַלְתָּ שָּׁם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְשָׂמַחְתָּ אַתָּה וּבֵיתֶךָ׃
verses.english: And you shall spend the money for anything that your soul will desire: for herd and for flock and for wine and for beer and for anything that your soul will ask of you. And you shall eat there in front of YHWH, your God, and you shall rejoice, you and your household.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְנָתַתָּה הַכֶּסֶף בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תְּאַוֶּה נַפְשְׁךָ בַּבָּקָר וּבַצֹּאן וּבַיַּיִן וּבַשֵּׁכָר וּבְכֹל אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׁאָלְךָ נַפְשֶׁךָ וְאָכַלְתָּ שָּׁם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְשָׂמַחְתָּ אַתָּה וּבֵיתֶךָ׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		And you shall spend the money for anything that your soul
		will desire: for herd and for flock and for wine and for
		beer and for anything that your soul will ask of you. And
		you shall eat there in front of YHWH, your God, and you
		shall rejoice, you and your household.
	}

verses.original: וְהַלֵּוִי אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ לֹא תַעַזְבֶנּוּ כִּי אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק וְנַחֲלָה עִמָּךְ׃
verses.english: And the Levite who is in your gates: you shall not leave him, because he doesn’t have a portion and legacy with you.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהַלֵּוִי אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ לֹא תַעַזְבֶנּוּ כִּי אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק וְנַחֲלָה עִמָּךְ׃}

verses.original: מִקְצֵה שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים תּוֹצִיא אֶת כּל מַעְשַׂר תְּבוּאָתְךָ בַּשָּׁנָה הַהִוא וְהִנַּחְתָּ בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ׃
verses.english: “At the end of three years you shall bring out all the tithe of your produce in that year and leave it within your gates,

tex.original: \hDtn{מִקְצֵה שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים תּוֹצִיא אֶת כּל מַעְשַׂר תְּבוּאָתְךָ בַּשָּׁנָה הַהִוא וְהִנַּחְתָּ בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: וּבָא הַלֵּוִי כִּי אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק וְנַחֲלָה עִמָּךְ וְהַגֵּר וְהַיָּתוֹם וְהָאַלְמָנָה אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ וְאָכְלוּ וְשָׂבֵעוּ לְמַעַן יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכל מַעֲשֵׂה יָדְךָ אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה׃
verses.english: and the Levite will come, because he doesn’t have a portion and legacy with you, and the alien and the orphan and the widow who are in your gates, and they shall eat and be full, so that YHWH, your God, will bless you in all your hand’s work that you’ll do.

tex.original: \hDtn{וּבָא הַלֵּוִי כִּי אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק וְנַחֲלָה עִמָּךְ וְהַגֵּר וְהַיָּתוֹם וְהָאַלְמָנָה אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ וְאָכְלוּ וְשָׂבֵעוּ לְמַעַן יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכל מַעֲשֵׂה יָדְךָ אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		and the Levite will come, because he doesn’t have a
		portion and legacy with you, and the alien and the orphan
		and the widow who are in your gates, and they shall eat
		and be full, so that YHWH, your God, will bless you in all
		your hand’s work that you’ll do.
	}

verses.original: מִקֵּץ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים תַּעֲשֶׂה שְׁמִטָּה׃
verses.english: “At the end of seven years you shall make a remission.

tex.original: \hDtn{מִקֵּץ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים תַּעֲשֶׂה שְׁמִטָּה׃}
tex.english: \eDtn{“At the end of seven years you shall make a remission.}

verses.original: וְזֶה דְּבַר הַשְּׁמִטָּה שָׁמוֹט כּל בַּעַל מַשֵּׁה יָדוֹ אֲשֶׁר יַשֶּׁה בְּרֵעֵהוּ לֹא יִגֹּשׂ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ וְאֶת אָחִיו כִּי קָרָא שְׁמִטָּה לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: And this is the matter of the remission: every holder of a loan is to remit what he has lent his neighbor. He shall not demand it of his neighbor and his brother, because a remission for YHWH has been called.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְזֶה דְּבַר הַשְּׁמִטָּה שָׁמוֹט כּל בַּעַל מַשֵּׁה יָדוֹ אֲשֶׁר יַשֶּׁה בְּרֵעֵהוּ לֹא יִגֹּשׂ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ וְאֶת אָחִיו כִּי קָרָא שְׁמִטָּה לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: אֶת הַנּכְרִי תִּגֹּשׂ וַאֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לְךָ אֶת אָחִיךָ תַּשְׁמֵט יָדֶךָ׃
verses.english: You may demand it of a foreigner, but your hand shall remit whatever of yours is with your brother.

tex.original: \hDtn{אֶת הַנּכְרִי תִּגֹּשׂ וַאֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לְךָ אֶת אָחִיךָ תַּשְׁמֵט יָדֶךָ׃}

verses.original: אֶפֶס כִּי לֹא יִהְיֶה בְּךָ אֶבְיוֹן כִּי בָרֵךְ יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ נַחֲלָה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃
verses.english: Nonetheless, there won’t be an indigent one among you, because YHWH will bless you in the land that YHWH, your God, is giving you as a legacy, to take possession of it—

tex.original: \hDtn{אֶפֶס כִּי לֹא יִהְיֶה בְּךָ אֶבְיוֹן כִּי בָרֵךְ יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ נַחֲלָה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃}

verses.original: רַק אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לִשְׁמֹר לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת כּל הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם׃
verses.english: only if you’ll listen to the voice of YHWH, your God, to be watchful to do all of this commandment that I command you today.

tex.original: \hDtn{רַק אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לִשְׁמֹר לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת כּל הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם׃}

verses.original: כִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בֵּרַכְךָ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָךְ וְהַעֲבַטְתָּ גּוֹיִם רַבִּים וְאַתָּה לֹא תַעֲבֹט וּמָשַׁלְתָּ בְּגוֹיִם רַבִּים וּבְךָ לֹא יִמְשֹׁלוּ׃
verses.english: When YHWH, your God, will have blessed you as He spoke to you, then you’ll lend to many nations, but you won’t borrow; and you’ll dominate many nations, but they won’t dominate you.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בֵּרַכְךָ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָךְ וְהַעֲבַטְתָּ גּוֹיִם רַבִּים וְאַתָּה לֹא תַעֲבֹט וּמָשַׁלְתָּ בְּגוֹיִם רַבִּים וּבְךָ לֹא יִמְשֹׁלוּ׃}

verses.original: כִּי יִהְיֶה בְךָ אֶבְיוֹן מֵאַחַד אַחֶיךָ בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ בְּאַרְצְךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ לֹא תְאַמֵּץ אֶת לְבָבְךָ וְלֹא תִקְפֹּץ אֶת יָדְךָ מֵאָחִיךָ הָאֶבְיוֹן׃
verses.english: “When there will be an indigent one among you from one of your brothers within one of your gates in your land that YHWH, your God, is giving you, you shall not fortify your heart and shall not shut your hand from your brother who is indigent.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִהְיֶה בְךָ אֶבְיוֹן מֵאַחַד אַחֶיךָ בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ בְּאַרְצְךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ לֹא תְאַמֵּץ אֶת לְבָבְךָ וְלֹא תִקְפֹּץ אֶת יָדְךָ מֵאָחִיךָ הָאֶבְיוֹן׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		“When there will be an indigent one among you from one of
		your brothers within one of your gates in your land that
		YHWH, your God, is giving you, you shall not fortify your
		heart and shall not shut your hand from your brother who
		is indigent.
	}

verses.original: כִּי פָתֹחַ תִּפְתַּח אֶת יָדְךָ לוֹ וְהַעֲבֵט תַּעֲבִיטֶנּוּ דֵּי מַחְסֹרוֹ אֲשֶׁר יֶחְסַר לוֹ׃
verses.english: But you shall open your hand to him and shall lend to him, enough for his shortage that he has.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי פָתֹחַ תִּפְתַּח אֶת יָדְךָ לוֹ וְהַעֲבֵט תַּעֲבִיטֶנּוּ דֵּי מַחְסֹרוֹ אֲשֶׁר יֶחְסַר לוֹ׃}

verses.original: הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ פֶּן יִהְיֶה דָבָר עִם לְבָבְךָ בְלִיַּעַל לֵאמֹר קָרְבָה שְׁנַת הַשֶּׁבַע שְׁנַת הַשְּׁמִטָּה וְרָעָה עֵינְךָ בְּאָחִיךָ הָאֶבְיוֹן וְלֹא תִתֵּן לוֹ וְקָרָא עָלֶיךָ אֶל יְהֹוָה וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא׃
verses.english: Watch yourself in case there will be something good-for-nothing in your heart, saying, ‘The seventh year, the remission year, is getting close,’ and your eye will be bad toward your brother who is indigent, and you won’t give to him; and he’ll call to YHWH about you, and it will be a sin in you.

tex.original: \hDtn{הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ פֶּן יִהְיֶה דָבָר עִם לְבָבְךָ בְלִיַּעַל לֵאמֹר קָרְבָה שְׁנַת הַשֶּׁבַע שְׁנַת הַשְּׁמִטָּה וְרָעָה עֵינְךָ בְּאָחִיךָ הָאֶבְיוֹן וְלֹא תִתֵּן לוֹ וְקָרָא עָלֶיךָ אֶל יְהֹוָה וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		Watch yourself in case there will be something
		good-for-nothing in your heart, saying, ‘The seventh year,
		the remission year, is getting close,’ and your eye will
		be bad toward your brother who is indigent, and you won’t
		give to him; and he’ll call to YHWH about you, and it will
		be a sin in you.
	}

verses.original: נָתוֹן תִּתֵּן לוֹ וְלֹא יֵרַע לְבָבְךָ בְּתִתְּךָ לוֹ כִּי בִּגְלַל הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכל מַעֲשֶׂךָ וּבְכֹל מִשְׁלַח יָדֶךָ׃
verses.english: You shall give to him, and your heart shall not be bad when you’re giving to him, because on account of this thing YHWH, your God, will bless you in everything you do and in everything your hand has taken on.

tex.original: \hDtn{נָתוֹן תִּתֵּן לוֹ וְלֹא יֵרַע לְבָבְךָ בְּתִתְּךָ לוֹ כִּי בִּגְלַל הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכל מַעֲשֶׂךָ וּבְכֹל מִשְׁלַח יָדֶךָ׃}

verses.original: כִּי לֹא יֶחְדַּל אֶבְיוֹן מִקֶּרֶב הָאָרֶץ עַל כֵּן אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ לֵאמֹר פָּתֹחַ תִּפְתַּח אֶת יָדְךָ לְאָחִיךָ לַעֲנִיֶּךָ וּלְאֶבְיֹנְךָ בְּאַרְצֶךָ׃
verses.english: Because there won’t stop being an indigent in the land. On account of this I command you, saying: you shall open your hand to your brother, to your poor, and to your indigent in your land.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי לֹא יֶחְדַּל אֶבְיוֹן מִקֶּרֶב הָאָרֶץ עַל כֵּן אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ לֵאמֹר פָּתֹחַ תִּפְתַּח אֶת יָדְךָ לְאָחִיךָ לַעֲנִיֶּךָ וּלְאֶבְיֹנְךָ בְּאַרְצֶךָ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		there won’t stop being an indigent in the land. This is generally
%		understood to mean that there will never cease to be poor people. And
%		the problem is that just a few verses earlier the text says the
%		opposite: “there won’t be an indigent one among you” (15:4). Ibn Ezra
%		and others have explained this apparent contradiction by noting that the
%		statement that “there won’t be an indigent one among you” goes on to say
%		“only if you’ll listen.... ” Since Israel will not, in fact, listen in
%		the future, therefore “there won’t stop being an indigent in the land.”
%		Ramban criticizes this view, saying that it is unimaginable that the
%		Torah would say that the Jewish people will never come to listen to the
%		Torah’s commandments. It seems to me that the problem arises because
%		everyone takes this verse to mean that there will never stop being
%		indigent people. But it simply says “there won’t stop.” I take that to
%		mean that poverty will not just come to a stop on its own one
%		day—without any action by humans. That is one of the ways in which this
%		word is used elsewhere in the Torah. Sarah’s menopause is described as
%		“Sarah had stopped having the way of women” (Gen 18:11). The end of the
%		plague of hail in Egypt is described as “the shower and the hail
%		stopped” (Exod 9:34). So here, too, the full verse says that poverty
%		will not simply stop—the poor will not just disappear—and “On account of
%		this I command you, saying: you shall open your hand to your brother, to
%		your poor, and to your indigent in your land.” The statements here and
%		in v. 4 are consistent: there will be no poverty only if people act to
%		end it.
%	}

verses.original: כִּי יִמָּכֵר לְךָ אָחִיךָ הָעִבְרִי אוֹ הָעִבְרִיָּה וַעֲבָדְךָ שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים וּבַשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁבִיעִת תְּשַׁלְּחֶנּוּ חפְשִׁי מֵעִמָּךְ׃
verses.english: “When your Hebrew brother or sister will be sold to you, then he shall work for you six years, and in the seventh year you shall let him go liberated from you.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִמָּכֵר לְךָ אָחִיךָ הָעִבְרִי אוֹ הָעִבְרִיָּה וַעֲבָדְךָ שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים וּבַשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁבִיעִת תְּשַׁלְּחֶנּוּ חפְשִׁי מֵעִמָּךְ׃}

verses.original: וְכִי תְשַׁלְּחֶנּוּ חפְשִׁי מֵעִמָּךְ לֹא תְשַׁלְּחֶנּוּ רֵיקָם׃
verses.english: And when you let him go liberated from you, you shall not let him go empty-handed.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכִי תְשַׁלְּחֶנּוּ חפְשִׁי מֵעִמָּךְ לֹא תְשַׁלְּחֶנּוּ רֵיקָם׃}

verses.original: הַעֲנֵיק תַּעֲנִיק לוֹ מִצֹּאנְךָ וּמִגּרְנְךָ וּמִיִּקְבֶךָ אֲשֶׁר בֵּרַכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ תִּתֶּן לוֹ׃
verses.english: You shall provide him from your flock and from your threshing floor and from your winepress; as YHWH, your God, has blessed you, you shall give to him.

tex.original: \hDtn{הַעֲנֵיק תַּעֲנִיק לוֹ מִצֹּאנְךָ וּמִגּרְנְךָ וּמִיִּקְבֶךָ אֲשֶׁר בֵּרַכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ תִּתֶּן לוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְזָכַרְתָּ כִּי עֶבֶד הָיִיתָ בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם וַיִּפְדְּךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ עַל כֵּן אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ אֶת הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה הַיּוֹם׃
verses.english: And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and YHWH, your God, redeemed you. On account of this, I command you this thing today.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְזָכַרְתָּ כִּי עֶבֶד הָיִיתָ בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם וַיִּפְדְּךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ עַל כֵּן אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ אֶת הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה הַיּוֹם׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה כִּי יֹאמַר אֵלֶיךָ לֹא אֵצֵא מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אֲהֵבְךָ וְאֶת בֵּיתֶךָ כִּי טוֹב לוֹ עִמָּךְ׃
verses.english: “And it will be, if he’ll say to you, ‘I won’t go out from you’ because he loves you and your house, because it is good for him with you,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהָיָה כִּי יֹאמַר אֵלֶיךָ לֹא אֵצֵא מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אֲהֵבְךָ וְאֶת בֵּיתֶךָ כִּי טוֹב לוֹ עִמָּךְ׃}

verses.original: וְלָקַחְתָּ אֶת הַמַּרְצֵעַ וְנָתַתָּה בְאזְנוֹ וּבַדֶּלֶת וְהָיָה לְךָ עֶבֶד עוֹלָם וְאַף לַאֲמָתְךָ תַּעֲשֶׂה כֵּן׃
verses.english: then you shall take an awl and put it in his ear and in the door, and he shall be a slave forever to you. And you shall also do this to your maid.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְלָקַחְתָּ אֶת הַמַּרְצֵעַ וְנָתַתָּה בְאזְנוֹ וּבַדֶּלֶת וְהָיָה לְךָ עֶבֶד עוֹלָם וְאַף לַאֲמָתְךָ תַּעֲשֶׂה כֵּן׃}

verses.original: לֹא יִקְשֶׁה בְעֵינֶךָ בְּשַׁלֵּחֲךָ אֹתוֹ חפְשִׁי מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי מִשְׁנֶה שְׂכַר שָׂכִיר עֲבָדְךָ שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים וּבֵרַכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה׃
verses.english: It shall not be hard in your eyes when you let him go liberated from you, because he served you six years at twice the value of an employee, and YHWH, your God, will bless you in everything that you’ll do.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא יִקְשֶׁה בְעֵינֶךָ בְּשַׁלֵּחֲךָ אֹתוֹ חפְשִׁי מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי מִשְׁנֶה שְׂכַר שָׂכִיר עֲבָדְךָ שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים וּבֵרַכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה׃}

verses.original: כּל הַבְּכוֹר אֲשֶׁר יִוָּלֵד בִּבְקָרְךָ וּבְצֹאנְךָ הַזָּכָר תַּקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תַעֲבֹד בִּבְכֹר שׁוֹרֶךָ וְלֹא תָגֹז בְּכוֹר צֹאנֶךָ׃
verses.english: “Every male firstborn that will be born in your herd and in your flock you shall consecrate to YHWH, your God. You shall not work with your ox’s firstborn, and you shall not shear your sheep’s firstborn.

tex.original: \hDtn{כּל הַבְּכוֹר אֲשֶׁר יִוָּלֵד בִּבְקָרְךָ וּבְצֹאנְךָ הַזָּכָר תַּקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תַעֲבֹד בִּבְכֹר שׁוֹרֶךָ וְלֹא תָגֹז בְּכוֹר צֹאנֶךָ׃}

verses.original: לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אַתָּה וּבֵיתֶךָ׃
verses.english: You shall eat it in front of YHWH, your God, year by year in the place that YHWH will choose—you and your household.

tex.original: \hDtn{לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ תֹאכְלֶנּוּ שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אַתָּה וּבֵיתֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וְכִי יִהְיֶה בוֹ מוּם פִּסֵּחַ אוֹ עִוֵּר כֹּל מוּם רָע לֹא תִזְבָּחֶנּוּ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And if there will be an injury in it—crippled or blind, any bad injury—you shall not sacrifice it to YHWH, your God.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכִי יִהְיֶה בוֹ מוּם פִּסֵּחַ אוֹ עִוֵּר כֹּל מוּם רָע לֹא תִזְבָּחֶנּוּ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יַחְדָּו כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל׃
verses.english: You shall eat it within your gates—the impure and the pure together, like a gazelle and like a deer.

tex.original: \hDtn{בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ תֹּאכְלֶנּוּ הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יַחְדָּו כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל׃}

verses.original: רַק אֶת דָּמוֹ לֹא תֹאכֵל עַל הָאָרֶץ תִּשְׁפְּכֶנּוּ כַּמָּיִם׃
verses.english: Only: you shall not eat its blood. You shall spill it like water on the ground.

tex.original: \hDtn{רַק אֶת דָּמוֹ לֹא תֹאכֵל עַל הָאָרֶץ תִּשְׁפְּכֶנּוּ כַּמָּיִם׃}

verses.original: שָׁמוֹר אֶת חֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב וְעָשִׂיתָ פֶּסַח לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כִּי בְּחֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב הוֹצִיאֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מִמִּצְרַיִם לָיְלָה׃
verses.english: “Observe the month of Abib, and you shall make Passover for YHWH, your God, because in the month of Abib YHWH, your God, brought you out from Egypt at night.

tex.original: \hDtn{שָׁמוֹר אֶת חֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב וְעָשִׂיתָ פֶּסַח לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כִּי בְּחֹדֶשׁ הָאָבִיב הוֹצִיאֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מִמִּצְרַיִם לָיְלָה׃}

verses.original: וְזָבַחְתָּ פֶּסַח לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ צֹאן וּבָקָר בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם׃
verses.english: And you shall make a Passover sacrifice to YHWH, your God, of the flock and herd, in the place that YHWH will choose to tent His name there.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְזָבַחְתָּ פֶּסַח לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ צֹאן וּבָקָר בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם׃}

verses.original: לֹא תֹאכַל עָלָיו חָמֵץ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת לֶחֶם עֹנִי כִּי בְחִפָּזוֹן יָצָאתָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם לְמַעַן תִּזְכֹּר אֶת יוֹם צֵאתְךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם כֹּל יְמֵי חַיֶּיךָ׃
verses.english: You shall not eat leavened bread with it. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, the bread of degradation, with it, because you went out from the land of Egypt in haste—so that you will remember the day you went out from the land of Egypt all the days of your life.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תֹאכַל עָלָיו חָמֵץ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת לֶחֶם עֹנִי כִּי בְחִפָּזוֹן יָצָאתָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם לְמַעַן תִּזְכֹּר אֶת יוֹם צֵאתְךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם כֹּל יְמֵי חַיֶּיךָ׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		You shall not eat leavened bread with it. Seven days you
		shall eat unleavened bread, the bread of degradation, with
		it, because you went out from the land of Egypt in
		haste—so that you will remember the day you went out from
		the land of Egypt all the days of your life.
	}

verses.original: וְלֹא יֵרָאֶה לְךָ שְׂאֹר בְּכל גְּבֻלְךָ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים וְלֹא יָלִין מִן הַבָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר תִּזְבַּח בָּעֶרֶב בַּיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן לַבֹּקֶר׃
verses.english: And you shall not have leaven appear within all your borders for seven days, and none of the meat that you will sacrifice in the evening on the first day shall remain until the morning.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְלֹא יֵרָאֶה לְךָ שְׂאֹר בְּכל גְּבֻלְךָ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים וְלֹא יָלִין מִן הַבָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר תִּזְבַּח בָּעֶרֶב בַּיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן לַבֹּקֶר׃}

verses.original: לֹא תוּכַל לִזְבֹּחַ אֶת הַפָּסַח בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ׃
verses.english: You may not make the Passover sacrifice within one of your gates that YHWH, your God, is giving you.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תוּכַל לִזְבֹּחַ אֶת הַפָּסַח בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ׃}

verses.original: כִּי אִם אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם תִּזְבַּח אֶת הַפֶּסַח בָּעָרֶב כְּבוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ מוֹעֵד צֵאתְךָ מִמִּצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: But, rather, to the place that YHWH, your God, will choose to tent His name: there you shall make the Passover sacrifice in the evening at sunset, the time when you went out from Egypt.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי אִם אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם תִּזְבַּח אֶת הַפֶּסַח בָּעָרֶב כְּבוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ מוֹעֵד צֵאתְךָ מִמִּצְרָיִם׃}

verses.original: וּבִשַּׁלְתָּ וְאָכַלְתָּ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בּוֹ וּפָנִיתָ בַבֹּקֶר וְהָלַכְתָּ לְאֹהָלֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And you shall cook and eat it in the place that YHWH, your God, will choose; and you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents.

tex.original: \hDtn{וּבִשַּׁלְתָּ וְאָכַלְתָּ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בּוֹ וּפָנִיתָ בַבֹּקֶר וְהָלַכְתָּ לְאֹהָלֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצּוֹת וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי עֲצֶרֶת לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה מְלָאכָה׃
verses.english: Six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day shall be a convocation to YHWH, your God. You shall not do work.

tex.original: \hDtn{שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצּוֹת וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי עֲצֶרֶת לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה מְלָאכָה׃}

verses.original: שִׁבְעָה שָׁבֻעֹת תִּסְפּר לָךְ מֵהָחֵל חֶרְמֵשׁ בַּקָּמָה תָּחֵל לִסְפֹּר שִׁבְעָה שָׁבֻעוֹת׃
verses.english: “You shall count seven weeks. From when the sickle begins to be in the standing grain you shall begin to count seven weeks.

tex.original: \hDtn{שִׁבְעָה שָׁבֻעֹת תִּסְפּר לָךְ מֵהָחֵל חֶרְמֵשׁ בַּקָּמָה תָּחֵל לִסְפֹּר שִׁבְעָה שָׁבֻעוֹת׃}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ חַג שָׁבֻעוֹת לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מִסַּת נִדְבַת יָדְךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּתֵּן כַּאֲשֶׁר יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And you shall make a Festival of Weeks for YHWH, your God, the full amount of your hand’s contribution that you can give insofar as YHWH, your God, will bless you.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְעָשִׂיתָ חַג שָׁבֻעוֹת לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מִסַּת נִדְבַת יָדְךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּתֵּן כַּאֲשֶׁר יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: וְשָׂמַחְתָּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אַתָּה וּבִנְךָ וּבִתֶּךָ וְעַבְדְּךָ וַאֲמָתֶךָ וְהַלֵּוִי אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ וְהַגֵּר וְהַיָּתוֹם וְהָאַלְמָנָה אֲשֶׁר בְּקִרְבֶּךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם׃
verses.english: And you shall rejoice in front of YHWH, your God—you and your son and your daughter and your servant and your maid and the Levite who is within your gates and the alien and the orphan and the widow who are among you—in the place that YHWH, your God, will choose to tent His name there.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְשָׂמַחְתָּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אַתָּה וּבִנְךָ וּבִתֶּךָ וְעַבְדְּךָ וַאֲמָתֶךָ וְהַלֵּוִי אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ וְהַגֵּר וְהַיָּתוֹם וְהָאַלְמָנָה אֲשֶׁר בְּקִרְבֶּךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		And you shall rejoice in front of YHWH, your God—you and
		your son and your daughter and your servant and your maid
		and the Levite who is within your gates and the alien and
		the orphan and the widow who are among you—in the place
		that YHWH, your God, will choose to tent His name there.
	}

verses.original: וְזָכַרְתָּ כִּי עֶבֶד הָיִיתָ בְּמִצְרָיִם וְשָׁמַרְתָּ וְעָשִׂיתָ אֶת הַחֻקִּים הָאֵלֶּה׃
verses.english: And you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and you shall be watchful and do these laws.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְזָכַרְתָּ כִּי עֶבֶד הָיִיתָ בְּמִצְרָיִם וְשָׁמַרְתָּ וְעָשִׂיתָ אֶת הַחֻקִּים הָאֵלֶּה׃}

verses.original: חַג הַסֻּכֹּת תַּעֲשֶׂה לְךָ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים בְּאסְפְּךָ מִגּרְנְךָ וּמִיִּקְבֶךָ׃
verses.english: “You shall make a Festival of Booths seven days, when you gather from your threshing floor and from your winepress.

tex.original: \hDtn{חַג הַסֻּכֹּת תַּעֲשֶׂה לְךָ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים בְּאסְפְּךָ מִגּרְנְךָ וּמִיִּקְבֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וְשָׂמַחְתָּ בְּחַגֶּךָ אַתָּה וּבִנְךָ וּבִתֶּךָ וְעַבְדְּךָ וַאֲמָתֶךָ וְהַלֵּוִי וְהַגֵּר וְהַיָּתוֹם וְהָאַלְמָנָה אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And you shall rejoice on your festival—you and your son and your daughter and your servant and your maid and the Levite and the alien and the orphan and the widow who are within your gates.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְשָׂמַחְתָּ בְּחַגֶּךָ אַתָּה וּבִנְךָ וּבִתֶּךָ וְעַבְדְּךָ וַאֲמָתֶךָ וְהַלֵּוִי וְהַגֵּר וְהַיָּתוֹם וְהָאַלְמָנָה אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תָּחֹג לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה כִּי יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכֹל תְּבוּאָתְךָ וּבְכֹל מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיךָ וְהָיִיתָ אַךְ שָׂמֵחַ׃
verses.english: Seven days you shall celebrate for YHWH, your God, in the place that YHWH will choose, because YHWH, your God, will bless you in all your produce and all your hands’ work, and you shall just be happy.

tex.original: \hDtn{שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תָּחֹג לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה כִּי יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכֹל תְּבוּאָתְךָ וּבְכֹל מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיךָ וְהָיִיתָ אַךְ שָׂמֵחַ׃}

verses.original: שָׁלוֹשׁ פְּעָמִים בַּשָּׁנָה יֵרָאֶה כל זְכוּרְךָ אֶת פְּנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחָר בְּחַג הַמַּצּוֹת וּבְחַג הַשָּׁבֻעוֹת וּבְחַג הַסֻּכּוֹת וְלֹא יֵרָאֶה אֶת פְּנֵי יְהֹוָה רֵיקָם׃
verses.english: “Three times in the year every male of yours shall appear in front of YHWH, your God, in the place that He will choose: on the Festival of Unleavened Bread and on the Festival of Weeks and on the Festival of Booths. And he shall not appear in front of YHWH empty-handed:

tex.original: \hDtn{שָׁלוֹשׁ פְּעָמִים בַּשָּׁנָה יֵרָאֶה כל זְכוּרְךָ אֶת פְּנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחָר בְּחַג הַמַּצּוֹת וּבְחַג הַשָּׁבֻעוֹת וּבְחַג הַסֻּכּוֹת וְלֹא יֵרָאֶה אֶת פְּנֵי יְהֹוָה רֵיקָם׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		“Three times in the year every male of yours shall appear
		in front of YHWH, your God, in the place that He will
		choose: on the Festival of Unleavened Bread and on the
		Festival of Weeks and on the Festival of Booths. And he
		shall not appear in front of YHWH empty-handed:
	}

verses.original: אִישׁ כְּמַתְּנַת יָדוֹ כְּבִרְכַּת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לָךְ׃
verses.english: each according to what his hand can give, according to the blessing of YHWH, your God, that He has given you.

tex.original: \hDtn{אִישׁ כְּמַתְּנַת יָדוֹ כְּבִרְכַּת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן לָךְ׃}

verses.original: שֹׁפְטִים וְשֹׁטְרִים תִּתֶּן לְךָ בְּכל שְׁעָרֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ לִשְׁבָטֶיךָ וְשָׁפְטוּ אֶת הָעָם מִשְׁפַּט צֶדֶק׃
verses.english: JUDGES “You shall put judges and officers in all your gates that YHWH, your God, is giving you, for your tribes, and they shall judge the people: judgment with justice.

tex.original: \hDtn{שֹׁפְטִים וְשֹׁטְרִים תִּתֶּן לְךָ בְּכל שְׁעָרֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ לִשְׁבָטֶיךָ וְשָׁפְטוּ אֶת הָעָם מִשְׁפַּט צֶדֶק׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		judgment with justice. It should be obvious, but, regrettably, it needs
%		to be said: judgment and justice are not the same thing. Judges and
%		lawyers can be part of one of the noblest endeavors of humankind: the
%		law. When they fail to pursue justice in their performance of judgment,
%		they pervert and degrade the law, and thus they demean humankind—nothing
%		less. The same goes for clerks, bailiffs, law enforcement officers, and
%		everyone else involved in the execution of justice. They elevate or
%		lower themselves—and all of us—by the degree of their commitment to
%		justice.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא תַטֶּה מִשְׁפָּט לֹא תַכִּיר פָּנִים וְלֹא תִקַּח שֹׁחַד כִּי הַשֹּׁחַד יְעַוֵּר עֵינֵי חֲכָמִים וִיסַלֵּף דִּבְרֵי צַדִּיקִם׃
verses.english: You shall not bend judgment, you shall not recognize a face, and you shall not take a bribe, because bribery will blind the eyes of the wise and undermine the words of the virtuous.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תַטֶּה מִשְׁפָּט לֹא תַכִּיר פָּנִים וְלֹא תִקַּח שֹׁחַד כִּי הַשֹּׁחַד יְעַוֵּר עֵינֵי חֲכָמִים וִיסַלֵּף דִּבְרֵי צַדִּיקִם׃}

verses.original: צֶדֶק צֶדֶק תִּרְדֹּף לְמַעַן תִּחְיֶה וְיָרַשְׁתָּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ׃
verses.english: Justice, justice you shall pursue, so that you’ll live, and you’ll take possession of the land that YHWH, your God, is giving you.

tex.original: \hDtn{צֶדֶק צֶדֶק תִּרְדֹּף לְמַעַן תִּחְיֶה וְיָרַשְׁתָּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Justice, justice. Many interpretations have been given for the
%		repetition of the word justice in this famous verse, from taking it to
%		mean that one should go to a good court (Siphre; Rashi) to midrashic and
%		Kabbalistic meanings (Ramban), as well as the most basic explanation:
%		that it is repeated for emphasis. It has also been taken to mean
%		“justice alone” (Jeffrey Tigay). And it is often said to mean that one
%		must pursue justice in a just way: one cannot use improper means to
%		achieve it. For example, police and prosecutors must not bend the law in
%		order to get a conviction. The repetition might also be taken to mean
%		that one must pursue justice for both sides: both the plaintiff and the
%		defense in a civil matter, and both the defendant and the prosecution
%		(“the people”) in a criminal matter. Most probably, though, we should
%		understand it with those who take it to be a matter of emphasis. Lacking
%		italics or exclamation points, Biblical Hebrew has few ways other than
%		repetition to express emphasis. That is the function of placing an
%		infinitive before a cognate verb (see the comment on Exod 19:12), and
%		here it is achieved by repeating the noun.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא תִטַּע לְךָ אֲשֵׁרָה כּל עֵץ אֵצֶל מִזְבַּח יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה לָּךְ׃
verses.english: “You shall not plant an Asherah of any wood near the altar of YHWH, your God, that you will make.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תִטַּע לְךָ אֲשֵׁרָה כּל עֵץ אֵצֶל מִזְבַּח יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה לָּךְ׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא תָקִים לְךָ מַצֵּבָה אֲשֶׁר שָׂנֵא יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And you shall not set up a pillar, which YHWH, your God, hates.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְלֹא תָקִים לְךָ מַצֵּבָה אֲשֶׁר שָׂנֵא יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		you shall not set up a pillar. Moses set up pillars himself (Exod 24:4).
%		So did Jacob (Gen 28:18; 32:45; 35:14,20). So why does Moses forbid it
%		now? Rashi and some modern commentators have thought that pillars were
%		originally acceptable but came to be associated with pagan worship and
%		so were abandoned. That may or may not be the actual historical
%		development behind these changes, but that does not seem to be what is
%		presented here in the text, because Moses moves from making them to
%		saying that God hates them, all within the forty years in the
%		wilderness. Perhaps we should understand it to mean that Moses is
%		prohibiting the people from making pillars after the formal altar and
%		Temple are built in the land, because then an altar might be taken as an
%		alternative locus of God. Here in Deuteronomy Moses repeatedly
%		emphasizes that there can be only one place of worship, one structure in
%		which God’s name is housed. Thus, even Joshua sets up a large stone,
%		which seems like a pillar (although the word is not used there; Josh
%		24:26), but this may be before the establishment of an official central
%		place of worship.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא תִזְבַּח לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ שׁוֹר וָשֶׂה אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בוֹ מוּם כֹּל דָּבָר רָע כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ הוּא׃
verses.english: “You shall not sacrifice to YHWH, your God, a bull or a sheep in which will be any injury, any bad thing, because that is an offensive thing of YHWH, your God.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תִזְבַּח לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ שׁוֹר וָשֶׂה אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בוֹ מוּם כֹּל דָּבָר רָע כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ הוּא׃}

verses.original: כִּי יִמָּצֵא בְקִרְבְּךָ בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה אֶת הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לַעֲבֹר בְּרִיתוֹ׃
verses.english: “If there will be found among you, in one of your gates that YHWH, your God, is giving you, a man or woman who will do what is bad in the eyes of YHWH, your God, to violate His covenant,

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִמָּצֵא בְקִרְבְּךָ בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה אֶת הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לַעֲבֹר בְּרִיתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּלֶךְ וַיַּעֲבֹד אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ לָהֶם וְלַשֶּׁמֶשׁ אוֹ לַיָּרֵחַ אוֹ לְכל צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם אֲשֶׁר לֹא צִוִּיתִי׃
verses.english: and will go and serve other gods and bow to them and to the sun or to the moon or to any of the array of the skies, which I did not command,

tex.original: \hDtn{וַיֵּלֶךְ וַיַּעֲבֹד אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ לָהֶם וְלַשֶּׁמֶשׁ אוֹ לַיָּרֵחַ אוֹ לְכל צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם אֲשֶׁר לֹא צִוִּיתִי׃}

verses.original: וְהֻגַּד לְךָ וְשָׁמָעְתָּ וְדָרַשְׁתָּ הֵיטֵב וְהִנֵּה אֱמֶת נָכוֹן הַדָּבָר נֶעֶשְׂתָה הַתּוֹעֵבָה הַזֹּאת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: and it will be told to you and you will hear it, and you will inquire well, and, here, it is true, the thing is right, this offensive thing has been done in Israel,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהֻגַּד לְךָ וְשָׁמָעְתָּ וְדָרַשְׁתָּ הֵיטֵב וְהִנֵּה אֱמֶת נָכוֹן הַדָּבָר נֶעֶשְׂתָה הַתּוֹעֵבָה הַזֹּאת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וְהוֹצֵאתָ אֶת הָאִישׁ הַהוּא אוֹ אֶת הָאִשָּׁה הַהִוא אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ אֶת הַדָּבָר הָרָע הַזֶּה אֶל שְׁעָרֶיךָ אֶת הָאִישׁ אוֹ אֶת הָאִשָּׁה וּסְקַלְתָּם בָּאֲבָנִים וָמֵתוּ׃
verses.english: then you shall bring that man or that woman who did this bad thing out to your gates, the man or the woman, and you shall stone them with stones so they die.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהוֹצֵאתָ אֶת הָאִישׁ הַהוּא אוֹ אֶת הָאִשָּׁה הַהִוא אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ אֶת הַדָּבָר הָרָע הַזֶּה אֶל שְׁעָרֶיךָ אֶת הָאִישׁ אוֹ אֶת הָאִשָּׁה וּסְקַלְתָּם בָּאֲבָנִים וָמֵתוּ׃}

verses.original: עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם עֵדִים אוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה עֵדִים יוּמַת הַמֵּת לֹא יוּמַת עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד׃
verses.english: “On the word of two witnesses or three witnesses shall the one who is to die be put to death. One shall not be put to death on the word of one witness.

tex.original: \hDtn{עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם עֵדִים אוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה עֵדִים יוּמַת הַמֵּת לֹא יוּמַת עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד׃}

verses.original: יַד הָעֵדִים תִּהְיֶה בּוֹ בָרִאשֹׁנָה לַהֲמִיתוֹ וְיַד כּל הָעָם בָּאַחֲרֹנָה וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ׃
verses.english: The witnesses’ hand shall be on him first to put him to death, and all the people’s hand after that. So you shall burn away what is bad from among you.

tex.original: \hDtn{יַד הָעֵדִים תִּהְיֶה בּוֹ בָרִאשֹׁנָה לַהֲמִיתוֹ וְיַד כּל הָעָם בָּאַחֲרֹנָה וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		witnesses first … all the people after. Numerous commentators discuss
%		the first half of this verse but not the second. It is of course
%		significant that witnesses must know that, if they testify against
%		someone in a capital case, they will have to strike the first blows
%		against the defendant themselves. That conveys vividly how serious their
%		testimony is. But it is at least as significant that all the people
%		participate in the execution as well. Capital punishment is the act of a
%		community—in ancient Israel and even more so in democracies. In biblical
%		law, the community must know that if they are going to have capital
%		punishment they must understand that this means that the community as a
%		whole is taking lives. So that there can be no mistaking this point, the
%		entire community must participate in the execution. In postbiblical
%		societies where the entire people does not participate personally, this
%		point may easily be forgotten, but it is true all the same: a community
%		that has capital punishment is responsible as a community for the lives
%		it takes. It is not just the executioner or just the witnesses or just
%		the courts. Perhaps this fact—that in ancient Israel all the people had
%		to carry out the execution—was one of the forces that led Israel to make
%		capital punishment almost impossible in rabbinic law.
%	}

verses.original: כִּי יִפָּלֵא מִמְּךָ דָבָר לַמִּשְׁפָּט בֵּין דָּם לְדָם בֵּין דִּין לְדִין וּבֵין נֶגַע לָנֶגַע דִּבְרֵי רִיבֹת בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ וְקַמְתָּ וְעָלִיתָ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בּוֹ׃
verses.english: “If a matter for judgment will be too daunting for you, between blood and blood, between law and law, and between injury and injury, matters of disputes in your gates, then you shall get up and go up to the place that YHWH, your God, will choose.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִפָּלֵא מִמְּךָ דָבָר לַמִּשְׁפָּט בֵּין דָּם לְדָם בֵּין דִּין לְדִין וּבֵין נֶגַע לָנֶגַע דִּבְרֵי רִיבֹת בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ וְקַמְתָּ וְעָלִיתָ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בּוֹ׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		“If a matter for judgment will be too daunting for you,
		between blood and blood, between law and law, and between
		injury and injury, matters of disputes in your gates, then
		you shall get up and go up to the place that YHWH, your
		God, will choose.
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		If a matter for judgment will be too daunting for you. In every law code
%		there must be a mechanism for change and for application to new and
%		difficult situations. Even if the law is divine law, there must be such
%		a mechanism, and the Torah recognizes this and provides for it. It
%		directs that in such difficult questions, the authorities (judges and
%		priests; i.e., authorities in law and religion) in each age shall
%		determine what to do. This has always been done in Judaism. The most
%		obvious distinction among the movements in Judaism has been their
%		different views of how the law changes. The primary consideration when
%		authorities, including scholars and rabbis, determine that a law is
%		changed is that they do so with wisdom and reverence, and not with
%		arrogance. Footnote 17:8. blood and blood. Cases involving the taking of
%		life. Footnote 17:8. between law and law. Cases that are complex because
%		more than one law applies. Footnote 17:8. between injury and injury.
%		Cases involving physical hurt. Footnote 17:8. disputes. The term (Hebrew
%		rîb) meant a quarrel, as in the quarreling at the rock that leads to the
%		name Meribah (Exodus 17; Numbers 20), and it came to refer to a lawsuit,
%		a legal dispute. Israel’s prophets use it to describe God’s judgment of
%		Israel in legal terms (Hos 12:3; Mic 6:2). This is known in biblical
%		scholarship as a “covenant lawsuit.” The covenant between God and Israel
%		is a legal relationship, formulated in the legal terminology of the
%		ancient Near East (see the comment on Exod 20:1). In a rîb oracle, the
%		prophet describes God as bringing a case against His people for
%		violating the covenant, which can end in judgment and punishment.
%	}

verses.original: וּבָאתָ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם וְאֶל הַשֹּׁפֵט אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם וְדָרַשְׁתָּ וְהִגִּידוּ לְךָ אֵת דְּבַר הַמִּשְׁפָּט׃
verses.english: And you shall come to the Levite priests and to the judge who will be in those days, and you shall inquire, and they will tell you the matter of judgment.

tex.original: \hDtn{וּבָאתָ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם וְאֶל הַשֹּׁפֵט אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם וְדָרַשְׁתָּ וְהִגִּידוּ לְךָ אֵת דְּבַר הַמִּשְׁפָּט׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the Levite priests. Historically, originally all Levites were priests.
%		Later the Levite group that identified itself as descendants of Aaron
%		took exclusive hold of the priesthood and limited all the other Levites
%		to a secondary role. Thereafter a distinction was made between priests
%		and Levites. Deuteronomy reflects the original status of all Levites and
%		does not make this distinction between priests and Levites. (I have
%		discussed this history of priesthood in Who Wrote the Bible?)
%	}

verses.original: וְעָשִׂיתָ עַל פִּי הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר יַגִּידוּ לְךָ מִן הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה וְשָׁמַרְתָּ לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יוֹרוּךָ׃
verses.english: And you shall do according to the word on the matter that they will tell you from that place that YHWH will choose, and you shall be watchful to do according to everything that they will instruct you.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְעָשִׂיתָ עַל פִּי הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר יַגִּידוּ לְךָ מִן הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה וְשָׁמַרְתָּ לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יוֹרוּךָ׃}

verses.original: עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר יוֹרוּךָ וְעַל הַמִּשְׁפָּט אֲשֶׁר יֹאמְרוּ לְךָ תַּעֲשֶׂה לֹא תָסוּר מִן הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר יַגִּידוּ לְךָ יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל׃
verses.english: You shall do it according to the word of the instruction that they will give you and according to the judgment that they will say to you. You shall not turn from the thing that they will tell you, right or left.

tex.original: \hDtn{עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר יוֹרוּךָ וְעַל הַמִּשְׁפָּט אֲשֶׁר יֹאמְרוּ לְךָ תַּעֲשֶׂה לֹא תָסוּר מִן הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר יַגִּידוּ לְךָ יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל׃}

verses.original: וְהָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה בְזָדוֹן לְבִלְתִּי שְׁמֹעַ אֶל הַכֹּהֵן הָעֹמֵד לְשָׁרֶת שָׁם אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אוֹ אֶל הַשֹּׁפֵט וּמֵת הָאִישׁ הַהוּא וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And the man who will act presumptuously, not listening to the priest who is standing to serve YHWH, your God, there, or to the judge: that man shall die. So you shall burn away what is bad from Israel.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה בְזָדוֹן לְבִלְתִּי שְׁמֹעַ אֶל הַכֹּהֵן הָעֹמֵד לְשָׁרֶת שָׁם אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אוֹ אֶל הַשֹּׁפֵט וּמֵת הָאִישׁ הַהוּא וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וְכל הָעָם יִשְׁמְעוּ וְיִרָאוּ וְלֹא יְזִידוּן עוֹד׃
verses.english: And all the people will listen and fear and won’t act presumptuously anymore.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכל הָעָם יִשְׁמְעוּ וְיִרָאוּ וְלֹא יְזִידוּן עוֹד׃}

verses.original: כִּי תָבֹא אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ וִירִשְׁתָּהּ וְיָשַׁבְתָּה בָּהּ וְאָמַרְתָּ אָשִׂימָה עָלַי מֶלֶךְ כְּכל הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר סְבִיבֹתָי׃
verses.english: “When you’ll come to the land that YHWH, your God, is giving you, and you’ll take possession of it and live in it, and you’ll say, ‘Let me set a king over me like all the nations that are around me,’

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תָבֹא אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ וִירִשְׁתָּהּ וְיָשַׁבְתָּה בָּהּ וְאָמַרְתָּ אָשִׂימָה עָלַי מֶלֶךְ כְּכל הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר סְבִיבֹתָי׃}

verses.original: שׂוֹם תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ מֶלֶךְ אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בּוֹ מִקֶּרֶב אַחֶיךָ תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ מֶלֶךְ לֹא תוּכַל לָתֵת עָלֶיךָ אִישׁ נכְרִי אֲשֶׁר לֹא אָחִיךָ הוּא׃
verses.english: you shall set a king over you whom YHWH, your God, will choose! You shall set a king from among your brothers over you. You may not put a foreign man, who is not your brother, over you.

tex.original: \hDtn{שׂוֹם תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ מֶלֶךְ אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בּוֹ מִקֶּרֶב אַחֶיךָ תָּשִׂים עָלֶיךָ מֶלֶךְ לֹא תוּכַל לָתֵת עָלֶיךָ אִישׁ נכְרִי אֲשֶׁר לֹא אָחִיךָ הוּא׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		you shall set a king over you. The Torah permits Israel to have a king
%		if they wish. It is placed in their hands to decide if they want one:
%		“When … you’ll say, ‘Let me set a king over me … ,’ you shall set a king
%		over you.” But the king must be chosen by God (see the next comment).
%		Later, Gideon and Samuel will question whether it is right for Israel to
%		have a king, saying that God should be Israel’s king (Judg 8:23; 1 Sam
%		8:6). But they do not base their opposition to monarchy on the Torah.
%		Both Gideon and Samuel are judges and also priests (Judg 8:24–27), and
%		they naturally think of God’s will as being properly expressed through
%		priests, and so they see kings as a threat to the order that they know.
%		But the Torah permits the people to have kings if they wish. And so God
%		tells Samuel to give the people a king, even though their wish for a
%		king, in that particular case, involves a rejection of God (1 Sam
%		8:7,22). Footnote 17:15. whom God will choose. This means that a prophet
%		must designate the king as chosen by God. Thus Samuel designates Saul
%		and David, Nathan designates Solomon, and Ahijah designates Jeroboam.
%		The stories of the kings of Israel and Judah in the books of Samuel,
%		Kings, and Chronicles convey that kings are acceptable if the people
%		want them, but their power is limited and balanced by the power of
%		prophets. And kings who do not listen to prophets, or who imprison or
%		execute them, do so at their peril.
%	}

verses.original: רַק לֹא יַרְבֶּה לּוֹ סוּסִים וְלֹא יָשִׁיב אֶת הָעָם מִצְרַיְמָה לְמַעַן הַרְבּוֹת סוּס וַיהֹוָה אָמַר לָכֶם לֹא תֹסִפוּן לָשׁוּב בַּדֶּרֶךְ הַזֶּה עוֹד׃
verses.english: Only, he shall not get himself many horses, and he shall not bring the people back to Egypt in order to get many horses, when YHWH has said to you, ‘You shall not go back this way ever again.’

tex.original: \hDtn{רַק לֹא יַרְבֶּה לּוֹ סוּסִים וְלֹא יָשִׁיב אֶת הָעָם מִצְרַיְמָה לְמַעַן הַרְבּוֹת סוּס וַיהֹוָה אָמַר לָכֶם לֹא תֹסִפוּן לָשׁוּב בַּדֶּרֶךְ הַזֶּה עוֹד׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		not get himself many horses. Maintaining forces with a great many horses
%		means the development of a small upper class plus a large class of serfs
%		or servants to support and serve them. This is one of several laws in
%		the Torah that work to counter the development of such a two-tiered
%		feudal system. And so, when King David defeats Hadadezer and captures
%		1,700 chariots and horsemen, he hamstrings all but a small number of the
%		horses (2 Sam 8:4). Why would he deliberately give up a prize of such
%		tremendous value? Because he is obeying this Law of the King. Footnote
%		17:16. YHWH has said to you, ‘You shall not go back.’ No such words from
%		God are reported prior to this. This may appear to be a problem, but it
%		may simply be that this is Moses’ report of God’s words on this matter.
%	}

verses.original: וְלֹא יַרְבֶּה לּוֹ נָשִׁים וְלֹא יָסוּר לְבָבוֹ וְכֶסֶף וְזָהָב לֹא יַרְבֶּה לּוֹ מְאֹד׃
verses.english: And he shall not get himself many wives, so his heart will not turn away. And he shall not get himself very much silver and gold.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְלֹא יַרְבֶּה לּוֹ נָשִׁים וְלֹא יָסוּר לְבָבוֹ וְכֶסֶף וְזָהָב לֹא יַרְבֶּה לּוֹ מְאֹד׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה כְשִׁבְתּוֹ עַל כִּסֵּא מַמְלַכְתּוֹ וְכָתַב לוֹ אֶת מִשְׁנֵה הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת עַל סֵפֶר מִלִּפְנֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם׃
verses.english: And it will be, when he sits on his kingdom’s throne, that he shall write himself a copy of this instruction on a scroll from in front of the Levite priests.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהָיָה כְשִׁבְתּוֹ עַל כִּסֵּא מַמְלַכְתּוֹ וְכָתַב לוֹ אֶת מִשְׁנֵה הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת עַל סֵפֶר מִלִּפְנֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		a copy of this instruction. It is unclear whether this means a copy of
%		this Law of the King or a copy of the full law code of Deuteronomy in
%		which it is now contained. In either case, this means that Israel has a
%		constitutional monarchy. Baruch Halpern has shown substantial evidence
%		that Israel’s kings were bound by this Law of the King from the time of
%		the first king, Saul (Halpern, The Constitution of the Monarchy in
%		Israel). That means that Israel was historically a constitutional
%		monarchy, with a written constitution, more than a thousand years B.C.E.
%		Footnote 17:18. a copy … from in front of the Levite priests. That is,
%		the Levites have the text of the law, and the king makes himself a copy
%		from the text that they have before them.
%	}

verses.original: וְהָיְתָה עִמּוֹ וְקָרָא בוֹ כּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו לְמַעַן יִלְמַד לְיִרְאָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהָיו לִשְׁמֹר אֶת כּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת וְאֶת הַחֻקִּים הָאֵלֶּה לַעֲשֹׂתָם׃
verses.english: And it shall be with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life, so that he will learn to fear YHWH, his God, to observe all the words of this instruction and these laws, to do them,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהָיְתָה עִמּוֹ וְקָרָא בוֹ כּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו לְמַעַן יִלְמַד לְיִרְאָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהָיו לִשְׁמֹר אֶת כּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת וְאֶת הַחֻקִּים הָאֵלֶּה לַעֲשֹׂתָם׃}

verses.original: לְבִלְתִּי רוּם לְבָבוֹ מֵאֶחָיו וּלְבִלְתִּי סוּר מִן הַמִּצְוָה יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאול לְמַעַן יַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים עַל מַמְלַכְתּוֹ הוּא וּבָנָיו בְּקֶרֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: so his heart will not be elevated above his brothers, and so he will not turn from the commandment, right or left, and so he will extend days over his kingdom, he and his sons, within Israel.

tex.original: \hDtn{לְבִלְתִּי רוּם לְבָבוֹ מֵאֶחָיו וּלְבִלְתִּי סוּר מִן הַמִּצְוָה יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאול לְמַעַן יַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים עַל מַמְלַכְתּוֹ הוּא וּבָנָיו בְּקֶרֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: לֹא יִהְיֶה לַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם כּל שֵׁבֶט לֵוִי חֵלֶק וְנַחֲלָה עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל אִשֵּׁי יְהֹוָה וְנַחֲלָתוֹ יֹאכֵלוּן׃
verses.english: “The Levite priests, all the tribe of Levi, shall not have a portion and legacy with Israel. They shall eat YHWH’s offerings by fire and His legacy.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא יִהְיֶה לַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם כּל שֵׁבֶט לֵוִי חֵלֶק וְנַחֲלָה עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל אִשֵּׁי יְהֹוָה וְנַחֲלָתוֹ יֹאכֵלוּן׃}

verses.original: וְנַחֲלָה לֹא יִהְיֶה לּוֹ בְּקֶרֶב אֶחָיו יְהֹוָה הוּא נַחֲלָתוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לוֹ׃
verses.english: But he shall not have a legacy among his brothers. YHWH: He is his legacy, as He spoke to him.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְנַחֲלָה לֹא יִהְיֶה לּוֹ בְּקֶרֶב אֶחָיו יְהֹוָה הוּא נַחֲלָתוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְזֶה יִהְיֶה מִשְׁפַּט הַכֹּהֲנִים מֵאֵת הָעָם מֵאֵת זֹבְחֵי הַזֶּבַח אִם שׁוֹר אִם שֶׂה וְנָתַן לַכֹּהֵן הַזְּרֹעַ וְהַלְּחָיַיִם וְהַקֵּבָה׃
verses.english: And this shall be the rule for the priests from the people, from those who make a sacrifice, whether an ox or a sheep: he shall give the shoulder, the cheeks, and the stomach.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְזֶה יִהְיֶה מִשְׁפַּט הַכֹּהֲנִים מֵאֵת הָעָם מֵאֵת זֹבְחֵי הַזֶּבַח אִם שׁוֹר אִם שֶׂה וְנָתַן לַכֹּהֵן הַזְּרֹעַ וְהַלְּחָיַיִם וְהַקֵּבָה׃}

verses.original: רֵאשִׁית דְּגָנְךָ תִּירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וְרֵאשִׁית גֵּז צֹאנְךָ תִּתֶּן לוֹ׃
verses.english: You shall give him the first of your grain, your wine, and your oil, and the first shearing of your sheep.

tex.original: \hDtn{רֵאשִׁית דְּגָנְךָ תִּירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וְרֵאשִׁית גֵּז צֹאנְךָ תִּתֶּן לוֹ׃}

verses.original: כִּי בוֹ בָּחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מִכּל שְׁבָטֶיךָ לַעֲמֹד לְשָׁרֵת בְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה הוּא וּבָנָיו כּל הַיָּמִים׃
verses.english: Because YHWH, your God, has chosen him from all your tribes to stand to serve in YHWH’s name, he and his sons, for all time.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי בוֹ בָּחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מִכּל שְׁבָטֶיךָ לַעֲמֹד לְשָׁרֵת בְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה הוּא וּבָנָיו כּל הַיָּמִים׃}

verses.original: וְכִי יָבֹא הַלֵּוִי מֵאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ מִכּל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר הוּא גָּר שָׁם וּבָא בְּכל אַוַּת נַפְשׁוֹ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: “And when a Levite will come from one of your gates, from all of Israel, where he lives, then he shall come as much as his soul desires to the place that YHWH will choose

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכִי יָבֹא הַלֵּוִי מֵאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ מִכּל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר הוּא גָּר שָׁם וּבָא בְּכל אַוַּת נַפְשׁוֹ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְשֵׁרֵת בְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהָיו כְּכל אֶחָיו הַלְוִיִּם הָעֹמְדִים שָׁם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: and serve in the name of YHWH, his God, like all of his Levite brothers who are standing there in front of YHWH.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְשֵׁרֵת בְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהָיו כְּכל אֶחָיו הַלְוִיִּם הָעֹמְדִים שָׁם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: חֵלֶק כְּחֵלֶק יֹאכֵלוּ לְבַד מִמְכָּרָיו עַל הָאָבוֹת׃
verses.english: They shall eat, portion for portion, aside from his sales of patrimony.

tex.original: \hDtn{חֵלֶק כְּחֵלֶק יֹאכֵלוּ לְבַד מִמְכָּרָיו עַל הָאָבוֹת׃}

verses.original: כִּי אַתָּה בָּא אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ לֹא תִלְמַד לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּתוֹעֲבֹת הַגּוֹיִם הָהֵם׃
verses.english: “When you come to the land that YHWH, your God, is giving you, you shall not learn to do like the offensive things of those nations.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי אַתָּה בָּא אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ לֹא תִלְמַד לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּתוֹעֲבֹת הַגּוֹיִם הָהֵם׃}

verses.original: לֹא יִמָּצֵא בְךָ מַעֲבִיר בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ בָּאֵשׁ קֹסֵם קְסָמִים מְעוֹנֵן וּמְנַחֵשׁ וּמְכַשֵּׁף׃
verses.english: There shall not be found among you someone who passes his son or his daughter through fire, one who practices enchantment, a soothsayer or a diviner or a sorcerer

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא יִמָּצֵא בְךָ מַעֲבִיר בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ בָּאֵשׁ קֹסֵם קְסָמִים מְעוֹנֵן וּמְנַחֵשׁ וּמְכַשֵּׁף׃}

verses.original: וְחֹבֵר חָבֶר וְשֹׁאֵל אוֹב וְיִדְּעֹנִי וְדֹרֵשׁ אֶל הַמֵּתִים׃
verses.english: or one who casts spells or who asks of a ghost or of a spirit of an acquaintance or inquires of the dead,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְחֹבֵר חָבֶר וְשֹׁאֵל אוֹב וְיִדְּעֹנִי וְדֹרֵשׁ אֶל הַמֵּתִים׃}

verses.original: כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה כּל עֹשֵׂה אֵלֶּה וּבִגְלַל הַתּוֹעֵבֹת הָאֵלֶּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מוֹרִישׁ אוֹתָם מִפָּנֶיךָ׃
verses.english: because everyone who does these is an offensive thing of YHWH, and because of these offensive things YHWH, your God, is dispossessing them from in front of you.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה כּל עֹשֵׂה אֵלֶּה וּבִגְלַל הַתּוֹעֵבֹת הָאֵלֶּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מוֹרִישׁ אוֹתָם מִפָּנֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: תָּמִים תִּהְיֶה עִם יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: You shall be unblemished with YHWH, your God,

tex.original: \hDtn{תָּמִים תִּהְיֶה עִם יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃}
tex.english: \eDtn{You shall be unblemished with YHWH, your God,}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		unblemished. This word is the mark of the recipients of the first two
%		covenants with God. It is the word that is used to describe the merit of
%		Noah; and God tells Abraham to be unblemished as well in the opening
%		words of the covenant (Gen 6:9; 17:1). (The only other person in the
%		Tanak to be described by these words is Job.) Now all the people of
%		Israel are recipients of the third covenant, and so all of them are
%		instructed to be like Noah and Abraham. They may receive the covenant
%		initially on the merit of Abraham, but they must maintain it on their
%		own integrity.
%	}

verses.original: כִּי הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה יוֹרֵשׁ אוֹתָם אֶל מְעֹנְנִים וְאֶל קֹסְמִים יִשְׁמָעוּ וְאַתָּה לֹא כֵן נָתַן לְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: because these nations whom you are dispossessing listen to soothsayers and enchanters, but you: YHWH, your God, has not permitted such for you.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה יוֹרֵשׁ אוֹתָם אֶל מְעֹנְנִים וְאֶל קֹסְמִים יִשְׁמָעוּ וְאַתָּה לֹא כֵן נָתַן לְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: נָבִיא מִקִּרְבְּךָ מֵאַחֶיךָ כָּמֹנִי יָקִים לְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֵלָיו תִּשְׁמָעוּן׃
verses.english: YHWH, your God, will raise up for you a prophet from among you, from your brothers, like me. You shall listen to him—

tex.original: \hDtn{נָבִיא מִקִּרְבְּךָ מֵאַחֶיךָ כָּמֹנִי יָקִים לְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֵלָיו תִּשְׁמָעוּן׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		God will raise up a prophet like me. But the end of the Torah says: “A
%		prophet did not rise again in Israel like Moses” (Deut 34:10)! Still,
%		this need not be a contradiction. The context of the passage here in
%		Deuteronomy 18 is that Israel should not listen to soothsayers and
%		enchanters, but only to a prophet from God, a “prophet like me.” Moses
%		reminds the people that this is what they asked for at Sinai: that they
%		not hear God’s voice directly anymore, but that they hear from God only
%		through prophets. The passage at the end of the Torah visibly means that
%		no other prophet was as great as Moses. It is simply a linguistic
%		matter: the range of the expression “to be like someone” is wide enough
%		to have these two meanings (and several more).
%	}

verses.original: כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר שָׁאַלְתָּ מֵעִם יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּחֹרֵב בְּיוֹם הַקָּהָל לֵאמֹר לֹא אֹסֵף לִשְׁמֹעַ אֶת קוֹל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהָי וְאֶת הָאֵשׁ הַגְּדֹלָה הַזֹּאת לֹא אֶרְאֶה עוֹד וְלֹא אָמוּת׃
verses.english: in accordance with everything that you asked from YHWH, your God, at Horeb in the day of the assembly, saying, ‘Let me not continue to hear the voice of YHWH, my God, and let me not see this big fire anymore, so I won’t die!’

tex.original: \hDtn{כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר שָׁאַלְתָּ מֵעִם יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּחֹרֵב בְּיוֹם הַקָּהָל לֵאמֹר לֹא אֹסֵף לִשְׁמֹעַ אֶת קוֹל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהָי וְאֶת הָאֵשׁ הַגְּדֹלָה הַזֹּאת לֹא אֶרְאֶה עוֹד וְלֹא אָמוּת׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֵלָי הֵיטִיבוּ אֲשֶׁר דִּבֵּרוּ׃
verses.english: “And YHWH said to me, ‘They’ve been good in what they’ve spoken.

tex.original: \hDtn{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֵלָי הֵיטִיבוּ אֲשֶׁר דִּבֵּרוּ׃}

verses.original: נָבִיא אָקִים לָהֶם מִקֶּרֶב אֲחֵיהֶם כָּמוֹךָ וְנָתַתִּי דְבָרַי בְּפִיו וְדִבֶּר אֲלֵיהֶם אֵת כּל אֲשֶׁר אֲצַוֶּנּוּ׃
verses.english: I’ll raise up a prophet for them from among their brothers, like you, and I’ll put my words in his mouth, and he’ll speak to them everything that I’ll command him.

tex.original: \hDtn{נָבִיא אָקִים לָהֶם מִקֶּרֶב אֲחֵיהֶם כָּמוֹךָ וְנָתַתִּי דְבָרַי בְּפִיו וְדִבֶּר אֲלֵיהֶם אֵת כּל אֲשֶׁר אֲצַוֶּנּוּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		God will raise up a prophet like me. But the end of the Torah says: “A
%		prophet did not rise again in Israel like Moses” (Deut 34:10)! Still,
%		this need not be a contradiction. The context of the passage here in
%		Deuteronomy 18 is that Israel should not listen to soothsayers and
%		enchanters, but only to a prophet from God, a “prophet like me.” Moses
%		reminds the people that this is what they asked for at Sinai: that they
%		not hear God’s voice directly anymore, but that they hear from God only
%		through prophets. The passage at the end of the Torah visibly means that
%		no other prophet was as great as Moses. It is simply a linguistic
%		matter: the range of the expression “to be like someone” is wide enough
%		to have these two meanings (and several more).
%	}

verses.original: וְהָיָה הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִשְׁמַע אֶל דְּבָרַי אֲשֶׁר יְדַבֵּר בִּשְׁמִי אָנֹכִי אֶדְרֹשׁ מֵעִמּוֹ׃
verses.english: And it will be: the man who won’t listen to my words that he’ll speak in my name, I shall require it from him!

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהָיָה הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִשְׁמַע אֶל דְּבָרַי אֲשֶׁר יְדַבֵּר בִּשְׁמִי אָנֹכִי אֶדְרֹשׁ מֵעִמּוֹ׃}

verses.original: אַךְ הַנָּבִיא אֲשֶׁר יָזִיד לְדַבֵּר דָּבָר בִּשְׁמִי אֵת אֲשֶׁר לֹא צִוִּיתִיו לְדַבֵּר וַאֲשֶׁר יְדַבֵּר בְּשֵׁם אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וּמֵת הַנָּבִיא הַהוּא׃
verses.english: Just: the prophet who will presume to speak a thing in my name that I didn’t command him to speak, and who will speak in the name of other gods—that prophet shall die.’

tex.original: \hDtn{אַךְ הַנָּבִיא אֲשֶׁר יָזִיד לְדַבֵּר דָּבָר בִּשְׁמִי אֵת אֲשֶׁר לֹא צִוִּיתִיו לְדַבֵּר וַאֲשֶׁר יְדַבֵּר בְּשֵׁם אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וּמֵת הַנָּבִיא הַהוּא׃}

verses.original: וְכִי תֹאמַר בִּלְבָבֶךָ אֵיכָה נֵדַע אֶת הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר לֹא דִבְּרוֹ יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: “And if you’ll say in your heart, ‘How shall we know the thing, that YHWH didn’t speak it?!’—

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכִי תֹאמַר בִּלְבָבֶךָ אֵיכָה נֵדַע אֶת הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר לֹא דִבְּרוֹ יְהֹוָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		How shall we know. It is one of the Bible’s central and most difficult
%		questions: How does one tell a true prophet from a false one? Moses
%		tells the people that the way to tell a false prophet is by seeing
%		whether his prophecy comes true or not. But that is a little late, is it
%		not? The question was how to know at the time of the prophecy whether it
%		is from God. Moses’ instruction appears to mean that one should go by
%		the prophet’s past record. Even then, people’s inclination seems to be
%		to disbelieve the true prophets. Even after Jeremiah’s prophecies of
%		Jerusalem’s fall come to pass (and the prophecies of those who oppose
%		him fail), as soon as he gives a prophecy that the people do not like
%		they say, “You’re speaking a lie. YHWH hasn’t sent you” (Jer 43:2)! So
%		Moses’ criterion for identifying false prophets may seem simple and
%		obvious, but the psychological point is that people miss the obvious and
%		turn instead to the comfortable.
%	}

verses.original: אֲשֶׁר יְדַבֵּר הַנָּבִיא בְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה וְלֹא יִהְיֶה הַדָּבָר וְלֹא יָבֹא הוּא הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר לֹא דִבְּרוֹ יְהֹוָה בְּזָדוֹן דִּבְּרוֹ הַנָּבִיא לֹא תָגוּר מִמֶּנּוּ׃
verses.english: when the prophet will speak in YHWH’s name, and the thing won’t be and won’t come to pass: that is the thing that YHWH did not say. The prophet spoke it presumptuously. You shall not be fearful of him.

tex.original: \hDtn{אֲשֶׁר יְדַבֵּר הַנָּבִיא בְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה וְלֹא יִהְיֶה הַדָּבָר וְלֹא יָבֹא הוּא הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר לֹא דִבְּרוֹ יְהֹוָה בְּזָדוֹן דִּבְּרוֹ הַנָּבִיא לֹא תָגוּר מִמֶּנּוּ׃}

verses.original: כִּי יַכְרִית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ אֶת אַרְצָם וִירִשְׁתָּם וְיָשַׁבְתָּ בְעָרֵיהֶם וּבְבָתֵּיהֶם׃
verses.english: “When YHWH, your God, will cut off the nations whose land YHWH, your God, is giving you, and you’ll dispossess them and live in their cities and in their houses,

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יַכְרִית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ אֶת אַרְצָם וִירִשְׁתָּם וְיָשַׁבְתָּ בְעָרֵיהֶם וּבְבָתֵּיהֶם׃}

verses.original: שָׁלוֹשׁ עָרִים תַּבְדִּיל לָךְ בְּתוֹךְ אַרְצְךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃
verses.english: you shall distinguish three cities within your land that YHWH, your God, is giving you to take possession of it.

tex.original: \hDtn{שָׁלוֹשׁ עָרִים תַּבְדִּיל לָךְ בְּתוֹךְ אַרְצְךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃}

verses.original: תָּכִין לְךָ הַדֶּרֶךְ וְשִׁלַּשְׁתָּ אֶת גְּבוּל אַרְצְךָ אֲשֶׁר יַנְחִילְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְהָיָה לָנוּס שָׁמָּה כּל רֹצֵחַ׃
verses.english: You shall prepare the way and divide the border of your land that YHWH, your God, will give you as a legacy into three sections, and it will be for any murderer to flee there.

tex.original: \hDtn{תָּכִין לְךָ הַדֶּרֶךְ וְשִׁלַּשְׁתָּ אֶת גְּבוּל אַרְצְךָ אֲשֶׁר יַנְחִילְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְהָיָה לָנוּס שָׁמָּה כּל רֹצֵחַ׃}

verses.original: וְזֶה דְּבַר הָרֹצֵחַ אֲשֶׁר יָנוּס שָׁמָּה וָחָי אֲשֶׁר יַכֶּה אֶת רֵעֵהוּ בִּבְלִי דַעַת וְהוּא לֹא שֹׂנֵא לוֹ מִתְּמֹל שִׁלְשֹׁם׃
