verses.english: And this is the case of the manslayer who will flee there and live: one who will strike his neighbor without knowing, when he did not hate him from the day before yesterday;

tex.original: \hDtn{וְזֶה דְּבַר הָרֹצֵחַ אֲשֶׁר יָנוּס שָׁמָּה וָחָי אֲשֶׁר יַכֶּה אֶת רֵעֵהוּ בִּבְלִי דַעַת וְהוּא לֹא שֹׂנֵא לוֹ מִתְּמֹל שִׁלְשֹׁם׃}

verses.original: וַאֲשֶׁר יָבֹא אֶת רֵעֵהוּ בַיַּעַר לַחְטֹב עֵצִים וְנִדְּחָה יָדוֹ בַגַּרְזֶן לִכְרֹת הָעֵץ וְנָשַׁל הַבַּרְזֶל מִן הָעֵץ וּמָצָא אֶת רֵעֵהוּ וָמֵת הוּא יָנוּס אֶל אַחַת הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וָחָי׃
verses.english: and one who will come with his neighbor into the forest to cut down trees, and his hand will be moved with the axe to cut down the tree, and the axe head will come off the wood and find his neighbor, and he dies. He shall flee to one of these cities and live.

tex.original: \hDtn{וַאֲשֶׁר יָבֹא אֶת רֵעֵהוּ בַיַּעַר לַחְטֹב עֵצִים וְנִדְּחָה יָדוֹ בַגַּרְזֶן לִכְרֹת הָעֵץ וְנָשַׁל הַבַּרְזֶל מִן הָעֵץ וּמָצָא אֶת רֵעֵהוּ וָמֵת הוּא יָנוּס אֶל אַחַת הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וָחָי׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		and one who will come with his neighbor into the forest to
		cut down trees, and his hand will be moved with the axe to
		cut down the tree, and the axe head will come off the wood
		and find his neighbor, and he dies. He shall flee to one
		of these cities and live.
	}

verses.original: פֶּן יִרְדֹּף גֹּאֵל הַדָּם אַחֲרֵי הָרֹצֵחַ כִּי יֵחַם לְבָבוֹ וְהִשִּׂיגוֹ כִּי יִרְבֶּה הַדֶּרֶךְ וְהִכָּהוּ נָפֶשׁ וְלוֹ אֵין מִשְׁפַּט מָוֶת כִּי לֹא שֹׂנֵא הוּא לוֹ מִתְּמוֹל שִׁלְשׁוֹם׃
verses.english: In case an avenger of blood will pursue the manslayer when his heart will be hot and will catch up to him because the way will be long, and he’ll strike him mortally though he does not have a sentence of death, because he did not hate him from the day before yesterday,

tex.original: \hDtn{פֶּן יִרְדֹּף גֹּאֵל הַדָּם אַחֲרֵי הָרֹצֵחַ כִּי יֵחַם לְבָבוֹ וְהִשִּׂיגוֹ כִּי יִרְבֶּה הַדֶּרֶךְ וְהִכָּהוּ נָפֶשׁ וְלוֹ אֵין מִשְׁפַּט מָוֶת כִּי לֹא שֹׂנֵא הוּא לוֹ מִתְּמוֹל שִׁלְשׁוֹם׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		In case an avenger of blood will pursue the manslayer when
		his heart will be hot and will catch up to him because the
		way will be long, and he’ll strike him mortally though he
		does not have a sentence of death, because he did not hate
		him from the day before yesterday,
	}

verses.original: עַל כֵּן אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ לֵאמֹר שָׁלֹשׁ עָרִים תַּבְדִּיל לָךְ׃
verses.english: on account of this I command you, saying, ‘You shall distinguish three cities.’

tex.original: \hDtn{עַל כֵּן אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ לֵאמֹר שָׁלֹשׁ עָרִים תַּבְדִּיל לָךְ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם יַרְחִיב יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת גְּבֻלְךָ כַּאֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע לַאֲבֹתֶיךָ וְנָתַן לְךָ אֶת כּל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָתֵת לַאֲבֹתֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And if YHWH, your God, will widen your border as He swore to your fathers and will give you all the land that He spoke to give to your fathers,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאִם יַרְחִיב יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת גְּבֻלְךָ כַּאֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע לַאֲבֹתֶיךָ וְנָתַן לְךָ אֶת כּל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָתֵת לַאֲבֹתֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: כִּי תִשְׁמֹר אֶת כּל הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת לַעֲשֹׂתָהּ אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לְאַהֲבָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְלָלֶכֶת בִּדְרָכָיו כּל הַיָּמִים וְיָסַפְתָּ לְךָ עוֹד שָׁלֹשׁ עָרִים עַל הַשָּׁלֹשׁ הָאֵלֶּה׃
verses.english: when you’ll observe all of this commandment to do it, that which I command you today, to love YHWH, your God, and to go in His ways every day, then you shall add three more cities to these three.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תִשְׁמֹר אֶת כּל הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת לַעֲשֹׂתָהּ אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לְאַהֲבָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְלָלֶכֶת בִּדְרָכָיו כּל הַיָּמִים וְיָסַפְתָּ לְךָ עוֹד שָׁלֹשׁ עָרִים עַל הַשָּׁלֹשׁ הָאֵלֶּה׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא יִשָּׁפֵךְ דָּם נָקִי בְּקֶרֶב אַרְצְךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ נַחֲלָה וְהָיָה עָלֶיךָ דָּמִים׃
verses.english: So innocent blood will not be spilled within your land that YHWH, your God, is giving you as a legacy, and blood would be on you.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְלֹא יִשָּׁפֵךְ דָּם נָקִי בְּקֶרֶב אַרְצְךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ נַחֲלָה וְהָיָה עָלֶיךָ דָּמִים׃}

verses.original: וְכִי יִהְיֶה אִישׁ שֹׂנֵא לְרֵעֵהוּ וְאָרַב לוֹ וְקָם עָלָיו וְהִכָּהוּ נֶפֶשׁ וָמֵת וְנָס אֶל אַחַת הֶעָרִים הָאֵל׃
verses.english: “But if there will be a man who hates his neighbor and will lie in wait for him and get up against him and strike him mortally, and he dies, and he will flee to one of these cities,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכִי יִהְיֶה אִישׁ שֹׂנֵא לְרֵעֵהוּ וְאָרַב לוֹ וְקָם עָלָיו וְהִכָּהוּ נֶפֶשׁ וָמֵת וְנָס אֶל אַחַת הֶעָרִים הָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וְשָׁלְחוּ זִקְנֵי עִירוֹ וְלָקְחוּ אֹתוֹ מִשָּׁם וְנָתְנוּ אֹתוֹ בְּיַד גֹּאֵל הַדָּם וָמֵת׃
verses.english: then his city’s elders shall send and take him from there and put him in the hand of the avenger of blood, so he will die.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְשָׁלְחוּ זִקְנֵי עִירוֹ וְלָקְחוּ אֹתוֹ מִשָּׁם וְנָתְנוּ אֹתוֹ בְּיַד גֹּאֵל הַדָּם וָמֵת׃}

verses.original: לֹא תָחוֹס עֵינְךָ עָלָיו וּבִעַרְתָּ דַם הַנָּקִי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל וְטוֹב לָךְ׃
verses.english: Your eye shall not pity him. And you shall burn away the innocent blood from Israel, and it will be well with you.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תָחוֹס עֵינְךָ עָלָיו וּבִעַרְתָּ דַם הַנָּקִי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל וְטוֹב לָךְ׃}

verses.original: לֹא תַסִּיג גְּבוּל רֵעֲךָ אֲשֶׁר גָּבְלוּ רִאשֹׁנִים בְּנַחֲלָתְךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּנְחַל בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃
verses.english: “You shall not move your neighbor’s landmark that the first ones set, in your legacy that you will have in the land that YHWH, your God, is giving you to take possession of it.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תַסִּיג גְּבוּל רֵעֲךָ אֲשֶׁר גָּבְלוּ רִאשֹׁנִים בְּנַחֲלָתְךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּנְחַל בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		your legacy that you will have in the land. This chapter gives laws
%		protecting lives and property, which will apply once the people arrive
%		in the land. Most of the Torah thus looks toward the well-being of the
%		land from outside it. Only about 29 of the Torah’s 187 chapters take
%		place in the promised land. Moses never sets foot in the land. And the
%		phrase “Land of Israel” never occurs in the Torah. (The land acquires
%		this name only after the people of Israel have settled there. It first
%		occurs in 1 Sam 13:19.) Yet the Torah’s story is focused on and directed
%		toward Israel constantly. It is the promise of the covenant with
%		Abraham. The promise is renewed to Isaac and Jacob. Jacob’s body is
%		returned from Egypt to be buried there. Joseph asks to be taken back for
%		burial there someday as well. And almost the entire content of Exodus
%		through Numbers is the story of the people’s liberation and journey
%		home. The Torah thus already relates to the experience of the Jewish
%		people in the postbiblical world: For the last two millennia most of the
%		Jews have lived outside the promised land. They have lived all over the
%		world and have been good citizens of the countries where they settled
%		while having affection for the land of Israel, a consciousness of their
%		origin there, and a desire to contribute to it, travel there, and seek
%		its well-being.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא יָקוּם עֵד אֶחָד בְּאִישׁ לְכל עָוֺן וּלְכל חַטָּאת בְּכל חֵטְא אֲשֶׁר יֶחֱטָא עַל פִּי שְׁנֵי עֵדִים אוֹ עַל פִּי שְׁלֹשָׁה עֵדִים יָקוּם דָּבָר׃
verses.english: “One witness shall not get up against a man for any crime or for any sin, in any sin that one will commit. On the word of two witnesses or on the word of three witnesses a case shall stand up.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא יָקוּם עֵד אֶחָד בְּאִישׁ לְכל עָוֺן וּלְכל חַטָּאת בְּכל חֵטְא אֲשֶׁר יֶחֱטָא עַל פִּי שְׁנֵי עֵדִים אוֹ עַל פִּי שְׁלֹשָׁה עֵדִים יָקוּם דָּבָר׃}

verses.original: כִּי יָקוּם עֵד חָמָס בְּאִישׁ לַעֲנוֹת בּוֹ סָרָה׃
verses.english: If a malicious witness will get up against a man to testify a misrepresentation against him,

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יָקוּם עֵד חָמָס בְּאִישׁ לַעֲנוֹת בּוֹ סָרָה׃}

verses.original: וְעָמְדוּ שְׁנֵי הָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר לָהֶם הָרִיב לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַשֹּׁפְטִים אֲשֶׁר יִהְיוּ בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם׃
verses.english: and the two people who have the dispute shall stand in front of YHWH, in front of the priests and the judges who will be in those days,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְעָמְדוּ שְׁנֵי הָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר לָהֶם הָרִיב לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַשֹּׁפְטִים אֲשֶׁר יִהְיוּ בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם׃}

verses.original: וְדָרְשׁוּ הַשֹּׁפְטִים הֵיטֵב וְהִנֵּה עֵד שֶׁקֶר הָעֵד שֶׁקֶר עָנָה בְאָחִיו׃
verses.english: and the judges will inquire well, and, here, the witness is a lying witness, he testified a lie against his brother,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְדָרְשׁוּ הַשֹּׁפְטִים הֵיטֵב וְהִנֵּה עֵד שֶׁקֶר הָעֵד שֶׁקֶר עָנָה בְאָחִיו׃}

verses.original: וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר זָמַם לַעֲשׂוֹת לְאָחִיו וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ׃
verses.english: then you shall do to him as he schemed to do to his brother. So you shall burn away what is bad from among you.

tex.original: \hDtn{וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר זָמַם לַעֲשׂוֹת לְאָחִיו וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ׃}

verses.original: וְהַנִּשְׁאָרִים יִשְׁמְעוּ וְיִרָאוּ וְלֹא יֹסִפוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת עוֹד כַּדָּבָר הָרָע הַזֶּה בְּקִרְבֶּךָ׃
verses.english: And those who remain will listen and fear and won’t continue to do anything like this bad thing anymore among you.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהַנִּשְׁאָרִים יִשְׁמְעוּ וְיִרָאוּ וְלֹא יֹסִפוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת עוֹד כַּדָּבָר הָרָע הַזֶּה בְּקִרְבֶּךָ׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא תָחוֹס עֵינֶךָ נֶפֶשׁ בְּנֶפֶשׁ עַיִן בְּעַיִן שֵׁן בְּשֵׁן יָד בְּיָד רֶגֶל בְּרָגֶל׃
verses.english: And your eye shall not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְלֹא תָחוֹס עֵינֶךָ נֶפֶשׁ בְּנֶפֶשׁ עַיִן בְּעַיִן שֵׁן בְּשֵׁן יָד בְּיָד רֶגֶל בְּרָגֶל׃}

verses.original: כִּי תֵצֵא לַמִּלְחָמָה עַל אֹיְבֶךָ וְרָאִיתָ סוּס וָרֶכֶב עַם רַב מִמְּךָ לֹא תִירָא מֵהֶם כִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ עִמָּךְ הַמַּעַלְךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: “When you’ll go out to war against your enemies, and you’ll see horses and chariots, a people more numerous than you, you shall not fear them, because YHWH, your God, is with you, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תֵצֵא לַמִּלְחָמָה עַל אֹיְבֶךָ וְרָאִיתָ סוּס וָרֶכֶב עַם רַב מִמְּךָ לֹא תִירָא מֵהֶם כִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ עִמָּךְ הַמַּעַלְךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה כְּקָרבְכֶם אֶל הַמִּלְחָמָה וְנִגַּשׁ הַכֹּהֵן וְדִבֶּר אֶל הָעָם׃
verses.english: And it will be, when you approach the war, that the priest shall go over and speak to the people.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהָיָה כְּקָרבְכֶם אֶל הַמִּלְחָמָה וְנִגַּשׁ הַכֹּהֵן וְדִבֶּר אֶל הָעָם׃}

verses.original: וְאָמַר אֲלֵהֶם שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל אַתֶּם קְרֵבִים הַיּוֹם לַמִּלְחָמָה עַל אֹיְבֵיכֶם אַל יֵרַךְ לְבַבְכֶם אַל תִּירְאוּ וְאַל תַּחְפְּזוּ וְאַל תַּעַרְצוּ מִפְּנֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: And he shall say to them, ‘Listen, Israel, you’re approaching war against your enemies today. Let your heart not be weak. Don’t be afraid and don’t panic and don’t be scared in front of them,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאָמַר אֲלֵהֶם שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל אַתֶּם קְרֵבִים הַיּוֹם לַמִּלְחָמָה עַל אֹיְבֵיכֶם אַל יֵרַךְ לְבַבְכֶם אַל תִּירְאוּ וְאַל תַּחְפְּזוּ וְאַל תַּעַרְצוּ מִפְּנֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: כִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם הַהֹלֵךְ עִמָּכֶם לְהִלָּחֵם לָכֶם עִם אֹיְבֵיכֶם לְהוֹשִׁיעַ אֶתְכֶם׃
verses.english: because YHWH, your God, is the one going with you to fight for you with your enemies, to save you.’

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם הַהֹלֵךְ עִמָּכֶם לְהִלָּחֵם לָכֶם עִם אֹיְבֵיכֶם לְהוֹשִׁיעַ אֶתְכֶם׃}

verses.original: וְדִבְּרוּ הַשֹּׁטְרִים אֶל הָעָם לֵאמֹר מִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה בַיִת חָדָשׁ וְלֹא חֲנָכוֹ יֵלֵךְ וְיָשֹׁב לְבֵיתוֹ פֶּן יָמוּת בַּמִּלְחָמָה וְאִישׁ אַחֵר יַחְנְכֶנּוּ׃
verses.english: “And the officers shall speak to the people, saying, ‘Who is a man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go, and let him go back to his house, in case he would die in the war and another man would dedicate it.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְדִבְּרוּ הַשֹּׁטְרִים אֶל הָעָם לֵאמֹר מִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה בַיִת חָדָשׁ וְלֹא חֲנָכוֹ יֵלֵךְ וְיָשֹׁב לְבֵיתוֹ פֶּן יָמוּת בַּמִּלְחָמָה וְאִישׁ אַחֵר יַחְנְכֶנּוּ׃}

verses.original: וּמִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר נָטַע כֶּרֶם וְלֹא חִלְּלוֹ יֵלֵךְ וְיָשֹׁב לְבֵיתוֹ פֶּן יָמוּת בַּמִּלְחָמָה וְאִישׁ אַחֵר יְחַלְּלֶנּוּ׃
verses.english: And who is a man who has planted a vineyard and has not desanctified it? Let him go, and let him go back to his house, in case he would die in the war and another man would desanctify it.

tex.original: \hDtn{וּמִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר נָטַע כֶּרֶם וְלֹא חִלְּלוֹ יֵלֵךְ וְיָשֹׁב לְבֵיתוֹ פֶּן יָמוּת בַּמִּלְחָמָה וְאִישׁ אַחֵר יְחַלְּלֶנּוּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		desanctified. This may relate to a law such as that in Lev 19:23–25,
%		whereby a newly planted tree goes through a period during which its
%		fruit may not be eaten, followed by a period of being holy (“all of its
%		fruit shall be holy”), and then a third period in which its period of
%		sanctification ends and one may eat it. In the present context, then, it
%		would refer to a man who has planted a vineyard but has not yet eaten
%		any of its fruit.
%	}

verses.original: וּמִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אֵרַשׂ אִשָּׁה וְלֹא לְקָחָהּ יֵלֵךְ וְיָשֹׁב לְבֵיתוֹ פֶּן יָמוּת בַּמִּלְחָמָה וְאִישׁ אַחֵר יִקָּחֶנָּה׃
verses.english: And who is a man who has betrothed a woman and has not taken her? Let him go, and let him go back to his house, in case he would die in the war and another man would take her.’

tex.original: \hDtn{וּמִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אֵרַשׂ אִשָּׁה וְלֹא לְקָחָהּ יֵלֵךְ וְיָשֹׁב לְבֵיתוֹ פֶּן יָמוּת בַּמִּלְחָמָה וְאִישׁ אַחֵר יִקָּחֶנָּה׃}

verses.original: וְיָסְפוּ הַשֹּׁטְרִים לְדַבֵּר אֶל הָעָם וְאָמְרוּ מִי הָאִישׁ הַיָּרֵא וְרַךְ הַלֵּבָב יֵלֵךְ וְיָשֹׁב לְבֵיתוֹ וְלֹא יִמַּס אֶת לְבַב אֶחָיו כִּלְבָבוֹ׃
verses.english: And the officers shall continue to speak to the people and shall say, ‘Who is a man who is afraid and weakhearted? Let him go, and go back to his house, so he won’t melt his brothers’ heart like his heart.’

tex.original: \hDtn{וְיָסְפוּ הַשֹּׁטְרִים לְדַבֵּר אֶל הָעָם וְאָמְרוּ מִי הָאִישׁ הַיָּרֵא וְרַךְ הַלֵּבָב יֵלֵךְ וְיָשֹׁב לְבֵיתוֹ וְלֹא יִמַּס אֶת לְבַב אֶחָיו כִּלְבָבוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה כְּכַלֹּת הַשֹּׁטְרִים לְדַבֵּר אֶל הָעָם וּפָקְדוּ שָׂרֵי צְבָאוֹת בְּרֹאשׁ הָעָם׃
verses.english: And it will be, when the officers finish speaking to the people, that they shall appoint officers of the armies at the head of the people.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהָיָה כְּכַלֹּת הַשֹּׁטְרִים לְדַבֵּר אֶל הָעָם וּפָקְדוּ שָׂרֵי צְבָאוֹת בְּרֹאשׁ הָעָם׃}

verses.original: כִּי תִקְרַב אֶל עִיר לְהִלָּחֵם עָלֶיהָ וְקָרָאתָ אֵלֶיהָ לְשָׁלוֹם׃
verses.english: “When you’ll approach a city to fight against it, then you shall call to it for peace.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תִקְרַב אֶל עִיר לְהִלָּחֵם עָלֶיהָ וְקָרָאתָ אֵלֶיהָ לְשָׁלוֹם׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה אִם שָׁלוֹם תַּעַנְךָ וּפָתְחָה לָךְ וְהָיָה כּל הָעָם הַנִּמְצָא בָהּ יִהְיוּ לְךָ לָמַס וַעֲבָדוּךָ׃
verses.english: And it will be, if it will answer you with peace and open up to you, then it will be that all the people who are found in it shall become yours for a work-company and shall serve you.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהָיָה אִם שָׁלוֹם תַּעַנְךָ וּפָתְחָה לָךְ וְהָיָה כּל הָעָם הַנִּמְצָא בָהּ יִהְיוּ לְךָ לָמַס וַעֲבָדוּךָ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם לֹא תַשְׁלִים עִמָּךְ וְעָשְׂתָה עִמְּךָ מִלְחָמָה וְצַרְתָּ עָלֶיהָ׃
verses.english: And if it will not make peace with you, but it will make war with you, then you shall besiege it.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאִם לֹא תַשְׁלִים עִמָּךְ וְעָשְׂתָה עִמְּךָ מִלְחָמָה וְצַרְתָּ עָלֶיהָ׃}

verses.original: וּנְתָנָהּ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּיָדֶךָ וְהִכִּיתָ אֶת כּל זְכוּרָהּ לְפִי חָרֶב׃
verses.english: And YHWH, your God, will put it in your hand, and you shall strike all its males by the sword.

tex.original: \hDtn{וּנְתָנָהּ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּיָדֶךָ וְהִכִּיתָ אֶת כּל זְכוּרָהּ לְפִי חָרֶב׃}

verses.original: רַק הַנָּשִׁים וְהַטַּף וְהַבְּהֵמָה וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בָעִיר כּל שְׁלָלָהּ תָּבֹז לָךְ וְאָכַלְתָּ אֶת שְׁלַל אֹיְבֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לָךְ׃
verses.english: Only, you shall take as spoil the women and the infants and the animals and everything that will be in the city, all its spoil, and you shall eat your enemies’ spoil that YHWH, your God, has given you.

tex.original: \hDtn{רַק הַנָּשִׁים וְהַטַּף וְהַבְּהֵמָה וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בָעִיר כּל שְׁלָלָהּ תָּבֹז לָךְ וְאָכַלְתָּ אֶת שְׁלַל אֹיְבֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לָךְ׃}

verses.original: כֵּן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְכל הֶעָרִים הָרְחֹקֹת מִמְּךָ מְאֹד אֲשֶׁר לֹא מֵעָרֵי הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה הֵנָּה׃
verses.english: That is what you shall do to all the cities that are very distant from you, those that are not from these nations’ cities.

tex.original: \hDtn{כֵּן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְכל הֶעָרִים הָרְחֹקֹת מִמְּךָ מְאֹד אֲשֶׁר לֹא מֵעָרֵי הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה הֵנָּה׃}

verses.original: רַק מֵעָרֵי הָעַמִּים הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ נַחֲלָה לֹא תְחַיֶּה כּל נְשָׁמָה׃
verses.english: Only from these peoples’ cities that YHWH, your God, is giving you as a legacy shall you not let any soul live.

tex.original: \hDtn{רַק מֵעָרֵי הָעַמִּים הָאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ נַחֲלָה לֹא תְחַיֶּה כּל נְשָׁמָה׃}

verses.original: כִּי הַחֲרֵם תַּחֲרִימֵם הַחִתִּי וְהָאֱמֹרִי הַכְּנַעֲנִי וְהַפְּרִזִּי הַחִוִּי וְהַיְבוּסִי כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוְּךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: But you shall completely destroy them—the Hittite and the Amorite, the Canaanite and the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite—as YHWH, your God, has commanded you,

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי הַחֲרֵם תַּחֲרִימֵם הַחִתִּי וְהָאֱמֹרִי הַכְּנַעֲנִי וְהַפְּרִזִּי הַחִוִּי וְהַיְבוּסִי כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוְּךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: לְמַעַן אֲשֶׁר לֹא יְלַמְּדוּ אֶתְכֶם לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּכֹל תּוֹעֲבֹתָם אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ לֵאלֹהֵיהֶם וַחֲטָאתֶם לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: so they won’t teach you to do things like all their offensive things that they did for their gods, and you’ll sin to YHWH, your God.

tex.original: \hDtn{לְמַעַן אֲשֶׁר לֹא יְלַמְּדוּ אֶתְכֶם לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּכֹל תּוֹעֲבֹתָם אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ לֵאלֹהֵיהֶם וַחֲטָאתֶם לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: כִּי תָצוּר אֶל עִיר יָמִים רַבִּים לְהִלָּחֵם עָלֶיהָ לְתפְשָׂהּ לֹא תַשְׁחִית אֶת עֵצָהּ לִנְדֹּחַ עָלָיו גַּרְזֶן כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ תֹאכֵל וְאֹתוֹ לֹא תִכְרֹת כִּי הָאָדָם עֵץ הַשָּׂדֶה לָבֹא מִפָּנֶיךָ בַּמָּצוֹר׃
verses.english: “When you’ll besiege a city many days, fighting against it to capture it, you shall not destroy a tree of it, moving an axe at it, because you’ll eat from it, so you shall not cut it down; because is a tree of the field a human, to go from in front of you in a siege?!

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תָצוּר אֶל עִיר יָמִים רַבִּים לְהִלָּחֵם עָלֶיהָ לְתפְשָׂהּ לֹא תַשְׁחִית אֶת עֵצָהּ לִנְדֹּחַ עָלָיו גַּרְזֶן כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ תֹאכֵל וְאֹתוֹ לֹא תִכְרֹת כִּי הָאָדָם עֵץ הַשָּׂדֶה לָבֹא מִפָּנֶיךָ בַּמָּצוֹר׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		“When you’ll besiege a city many days, fighting against it
		to capture it, you shall not destroy a tree of it, moving
		an axe at it, because you’ll eat from it, so you shall not
		cut it down; because is a tree of the field a human, to go
		from in front of you in a siege?!
	}

verses.original: רַק עֵץ אֲשֶׁר תֵּדַע כִּי לֹא עֵץ מַאֲכָל הוּא אֹתוֹ תַשְׁחִית וְכָרָתָּ וּבָנִיתָ מָצוֹר עַל הָעִיר אֲשֶׁר הִוא עֹשָׂה עִמְּךָ מִלְחָמָה עַד רִדְתָּהּ׃
verses.english: Only a tree that you’ll know that it isn’t a tree for eating: that one you may destroy and cut down so you may build a siege-work against the city that is making war with you until its fall.

tex.original: \hDtn{רַק עֵץ אֲשֶׁר תֵּדַע כִּי לֹא עֵץ מַאֲכָל הוּא אֹתוֹ תַשְׁחִית וְכָרָתָּ וּבָנִיתָ מָצוֹר עַל הָעִיר אֲשֶׁר הִוא עֹשָׂה עִמְּךָ מִלְחָמָה עַד רִדְתָּהּ׃}

verses.original: כִּי יִמָּצֵא חָלָל בָּאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ לְרִשְׁתָּהּ נֹפֵל בַּשָּׂדֶה לֹא נוֹדַע מִי הִכָּהוּ׃
verses.english: “If a corpse will be found in the land that YHWH, your God, is giving you to take possession of it, fallen in the field, unknown who struck him,

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִמָּצֵא חָלָל בָּאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ לְרִשְׁתָּהּ נֹפֵל בַּשָּׂדֶה לֹא נוֹדַע מִי הִכָּהוּ׃}

verses.original: וְיָצְאוּ זְקֵנֶיךָ וְשֹׁפְטֶיךָ וּמָדְדוּ אֶל הֶעָרִים אֲשֶׁר סְבִיבֹת הֶחָלָל׃
verses.english: then your elders and your judges shall go out and measure to the cities that are around the corpse.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְיָצְאוּ זְקֵנֶיךָ וְשֹׁפְטֶיךָ וּמָדְדוּ אֶל הֶעָרִים אֲשֶׁר סְבִיבֹת הֶחָלָל׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה הָעִיר הַקְּרֹבָה אֶל הֶחָלָל וְלָקְחוּ זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִוא עֶגְלַת בָּקָר אֲשֶׁר לֹא עֻבַּד בָּהּ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מָשְׁכָה בְּעֹל׃
verses.english: And it will be, the closest city to the corpse: that city’s elders shall take a heifer that has not been worked with, that has not pulled in a yoke.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהָיָה הָעִיר הַקְּרֹבָה אֶל הֶחָלָל וְלָקְחוּ זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִוא עֶגְלַת בָּקָר אֲשֶׁר לֹא עֻבַּד בָּהּ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מָשְׁכָה בְּעֹל׃}

verses.original: וְהוֹרִדוּ זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִוא אֶת הָעֶגְלָה אֶל נַחַל אֵיתָן אֲשֶׁר לֹא יֵעָבֵד בּוֹ וְלֹא יִזָּרֵעַ וְעָרְפוּ שָׁם אֶת הָעֶגְלָה בַּנָּחַל׃
verses.english: And that city’s elders shall take the heifer down to a strongly flowing wadi that would not be worked with and would not be seeded, and they shall break the heifer’s neck there in the wadi.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהוֹרִדוּ זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִוא אֶת הָעֶגְלָה אֶל נַחַל אֵיתָן אֲשֶׁר לֹא יֵעָבֵד בּוֹ וְלֹא יִזָּרֵעַ וְעָרְפוּ שָׁם אֶת הָעֶגְלָה בַּנָּחַל׃}

verses.original: וְנִגְּשׁוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים בְּנֵי לֵוִי כִּי בָם בָּחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְשָׁרְתוֹ וּלְבָרֵךְ בְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה וְעַל פִּיהֶם יִהְיֶה כּל רִיב וְכל נָגַע׃
verses.english: And the priests, sons of Levi, shall go over, because YHWH, your God, chose them to serve Him and to bless in YHWH’s name, and every dispute and every injury shall be by their word.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְנִגְּשׁוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים בְּנֵי לֵוִי כִּי בָם בָּחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְשָׁרְתוֹ וּלְבָרֵךְ בְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה וְעַל פִּיהֶם יִהְיֶה כּל רִיב וְכל נָגַע׃}

verses.original: וְכֹל זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִוא הַקְּרֹבִים אֶל הֶחָלָל יִרְחֲצוּ אֶת יְדֵיהֶם עַל הָעֶגְלָה הָעֲרוּפָה בַנָּחַל׃
verses.english: And all of that city’s elders, who are close to the corpse, shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the wadi.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכֹל זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִוא הַקְּרֹבִים אֶל הֶחָלָל יִרְחֲצוּ אֶת יְדֵיהֶם עַל הָעֶגְלָה הָעֲרוּפָה בַנָּחַל׃}

verses.original: וְעָנוּ וְאָמְרוּ יָדֵינוּ לֹא (שפכה) [שָׁפְכוּ] אֶת הַדָּם הַזֶּה וְעֵינֵינוּ לֹא רָאוּ׃
verses.english: And they shall testify, and they shall say, ‘Our hands did not spill this blood, and our eyes did not see it.
verses.commentary: Qere Ketiv.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְעָנוּ וְאָמְרוּ יָדֵינוּ לֹא (שפכה) [שָׁפְכוּ] אֶת הַדָּם הַזֶּה וְעֵינֵינוּ לֹא רָאוּ׃}

verses.original: כַּפֵּר לְעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר פָּדִיתָ יְהֹוָה וְאַל תִּתֵּן דָּם נָקִי בְּקֶרֶב עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִכַּפֵּר לָהֶם הַדָּם׃
verses.english: Grant atonement for your people Israel, whom you redeemed, YHWH, and don’t impute innocent blood among your people Israel.’ And for them the blood will be atoned for.

tex.original: \hDtn{כַּפֵּר לְעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר פָּדִיתָ יְהֹוָה וְאַל תִּתֵּן דָּם נָקִי בְּקֶרֶב עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִכַּפֵּר לָהֶם הַדָּם׃}

verses.original: וְאַתָּה תְּבַעֵר הַדָּם הַנָּקִי מִקִּרְבֶּךָ כִּי תַעֲשֶׂה הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: So you shall burn away the innocent blood from among you when you will do what is right in YHWH’s eyes.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאַתָּה תְּבַעֵר הַדָּם הַנָּקִי מִקִּרְבֶּךָ כִּי תַעֲשֶׂה הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: כִּי תֵצֵא לַמִּלְחָמָה עַל אֹיְבֶיךָ וּנְתָנוֹ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּיָדֶךָ וְשָׁבִיתָ שִׁבְיוֹ׃
verses.english: “When you’ll go out to war against your enemies, and YHWH, your God, will put him in your hand, and you’ll take prisoners from him,

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תֵצֵא לַמִּלְחָמָה עַל אֹיְבֶיךָ וּנְתָנוֹ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּיָדֶךָ וְשָׁבִיתָ שִׁבְיוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְרָאִיתָ בַּשִּׁבְיָה אֵשֶׁת יְפַת תֹּאַר וְחָשַׁקְתָּ בָהּ וְלָקַחְתָּ לְךָ לְאִשָּׁה׃
verses.english: and you’ll see among the prisoners a woman with a beautiful figure, and you’ll be attracted to her and take her for yourself as a wife,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְרָאִיתָ בַּשִּׁבְיָה אֵשֶׁת יְפַת תֹּאַר וְחָשַׁקְתָּ בָהּ וְלָקַחְתָּ לְךָ לְאִשָּׁה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		a woman among the prisoners. A number of this law’s details have never
%		been explained definitively. Some would say she cuts her hair and nails
%		so as to be less attractive, so that the man who is attracted to her
%		will become less infatuated. Some would say it is part of her mourning.
%		But what pervades the elements of the law is an extraordinary
%		sensitivity to the humanity of a captured woman. Contrary to one of the
%		most common practices of war, the Israelite soldier is not permitted to
%		rape her. He may take her as a wife. But even then he must give her time
%		to mourn the loss of her family. And if he takes her as a wife but then
%		rejects her, he must let her go completely free. The text uses the same
%		verb as in the law of divorce (Deut 24:1). And the text recognizes that
%		he has degraded her, and so he cannot treat her like a slave to be sold;
%		he cannot receive money for her from anyone else. Notably, the words for
%		degrading her and for letting her go are the same words that are used to
%		describe the Egyptians’ degrading of Israel and then letting Israel go
%		(Exod 1:11–12; 5:1). Again Israel learns from its experience of
%		enslavement. Israel not only celebrates its own release, but it learns
%		to have compassion for others as well.
%	}

verses.original: וַהֲבֵאתָהּ אֶל תּוֹךְ בֵּיתֶךָ וְגִלְּחָה אֶת רֹאשָׁהּ וְעָשְׂתָה אֶת צִפּרְנֶיהָ׃
verses.english: then you shall bring her into your house, and she shall shave her head and do her nails

tex.original: \hDtn{וַהֲבֵאתָהּ אֶל תּוֹךְ בֵּיתֶךָ וְגִלְּחָה אֶת רֹאשָׁהּ וְעָשְׂתָה אֶת צִפּרְנֶיהָ׃}

verses.original: וְהֵסִירָה אֶת שִׂמְלַת שִׁבְיָהּ מֵעָלֶיהָ וְיָשְׁבָה בְּבֵיתֶךָ וּבָכְתָה אֶת אָבִיהָ וְאֶת אִמָּהּ יֶרַח יָמִים וְאַחַר כֵּן תָּבוֹא אֵלֶיהָ וּבְעַלְתָּהּ וְהָיְתָה לְךָ לְאִשָּׁה׃
verses.english: and take away her prisoner’s garment from on her. And she shall live in your house and shall mourn her father and her mother a month of days. And after that you may come to her and marry her, and she shall become your wife.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהֵסִירָה אֶת שִׂמְלַת שִׁבְיָהּ מֵעָלֶיהָ וְיָשְׁבָה בְּבֵיתֶךָ וּבָכְתָה אֶת אָבִיהָ וְאֶת אִמָּהּ יֶרַח יָמִים וְאַחַר כֵּן תָּבוֹא אֵלֶיהָ וּבְעַלְתָּהּ וְהָיְתָה לְךָ לְאִשָּׁה׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה אִם לֹא חָפַצְתָּ בָּהּ וְשִׁלַּחְתָּהּ לְנַפְשָׁהּ וּמָכֹר לֹא תִמְכְּרֶנָּה בַּכָּסֶף לֹא תִתְעַמֵּר בָּהּ תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר עִנִּיתָהּ׃
verses.english: And it will be, if you don’t desire her then you shall let her go on her own, and you shall not sell her for money. You shall not get profit through her, because you degraded her.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהָיָה אִם לֹא חָפַצְתָּ בָּהּ וְשִׁלַּחְתָּהּ לְנַפְשָׁהּ וּמָכֹר לֹא תִמְכְּרֶנָּה בַּכָּסֶף לֹא תִתְעַמֵּר בָּהּ תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר עִנִּיתָהּ׃}

verses.original: כִּי תִהְיֶיןָ לְאִישׁ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים הָאַחַת אֲהוּבָה וְהָאַחַת שְׂנוּאָה וְיָלְדוּ לוֹ בָנִים הָאֲהוּבָה וְהַשְּׂנוּאָה וְהָיָה הַבֵּן הַבְּכֹר לַשְּׂנִיאָה׃
verses.english: “When a man will have two wives, one loved and one hated, and they’ll give birth to children for him, the loved and the hated, and the hated will have the firstborn son,

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תִהְיֶיןָ לְאִישׁ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים הָאַחַת אֲהוּבָה וְהָאַחַת שְׂנוּאָה וְיָלְדוּ לוֹ בָנִים הָאֲהוּבָה וְהַשְּׂנוּאָה וְהָיָה הַבֵּן הַבְּכֹר לַשְּׂנִיאָה׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ אֶת בָּנָיו אֵת אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לוֹ לֹא יוּכַל לְבַכֵּר אֶת בֶּן הָאֲהוּבָה עַל פְּנֵי בֶן הַשְּׂנוּאָה הַבְּכֹר׃
verses.english: then it will be, on the day that he gives what he has as a legacy to his children, he shall not be able to give a son of the loved one the birthright before the firstborn son of the hated one.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהָיָה בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ אֶת בָּנָיו אֵת אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לוֹ לֹא יוּכַל לְבַכֵּר אֶת בֶּן הָאֲהוּבָה עַל פְּנֵי בֶן הַשְּׂנוּאָה הַבְּכֹר׃}

verses.original: כִּי אֶת הַבְּכֹר בֶּן הַשְּׂנוּאָה יַכִּיר לָתֶת לוֹ פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִמָּצֵא לוֹ כִּי הוּא רֵאשִׁית אֹנוֹ לוֹ מִשְׁפַּט הַבְּכֹרָה׃
verses.english: But he shall recognize the firstborn son of the hated one, to give him a double portion of all that he has, because he is the beginning of his might. The legal due of the firstborn is his.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי אֶת הַבְּכֹר בֶּן הַשְּׂנוּאָה יַכִּיר לָתֶת לוֹ פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִמָּצֵא לוֹ כִּי הוּא רֵאשִׁית אֹנוֹ לוֹ מִשְׁפַּט הַבְּכֹרָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		beginning of his might. Moses uses the same phrase that Jacob uses to
%		describe Reuben, his firstborn, when he speaks of his sons’ legacies
%		(Gen 49:3). Perhaps this was a known expression for firstborn sons, or
%		perhaps we should picture Moses as deliberately bringing Jacob’s words
%		to mind. It is ironic because Jacob does in fact take away the double
%		portion from Reuben, who is the son of the less-loved wife, Leah; and he
%		gives it to Joseph, who is the son of the more-loved wife, Rachel (Gen
%		29:30). It may be that Moses is teaching that the Israelites may not do
%		what Jacob did. Or it may be that Jacob’s case demonstrates the point of
%		the law that Moses is giving, since Jacob does not take the birthright
%		away from Reuben because of Reuben’s mother, Leah, being less loved. He
%		takes it away because Reuben himself committed an offense, sleeping with
%		his father’s concubine (Gen 35:22; 49:4).
%	}

verses.original: כִּי יִהְיֶה לְאִישׁ בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה אֵינֶנּוּ שֹׁמֵעַ בְּקוֹל אָבִיו וּבְקוֹל אִמּוֹ וְיִסְּרוּ אֹתוֹ וְלֹא יִשְׁמַע אֲלֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: “When a man will have a stubborn and rebellious son, not listening to his father’s voice and his mother’s voice, and they will discipline him, but he will not listen to them,

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִהְיֶה לְאִישׁ בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה אֵינֶנּוּ שֹׁמֵעַ בְּקוֹל אָבִיו וּבְקוֹל אִמּוֹ וְיִסְּרוּ אֹתוֹ וְלֹא יִשְׁמַע אֲלֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וְתָפְשׂוּ בוֹ אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֹתוֹ אֶל זִקְנֵי עִירוֹ וְאֶל שַׁעַר מְקֹמוֹ׃
verses.english: then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to his city’s elders and to the gate of his place.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְתָפְשׂוּ בוֹ אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֹתוֹ אֶל זִקְנֵי עִירוֹ וְאֶל שַׁעַר מְקֹמוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְאָמְרוּ אֶל זִקְנֵי עִירוֹ בְּנֵנוּ זֶה סוֹרֵר וּמֹרֶה אֵינֶנּוּ שֹׁמֵעַ בְּקֹלֵנוּ זוֹלֵל וְסֹבֵא׃
verses.english: And they shall say to his city’s elders, ‘This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious, he doesn’t listen to our voice, a glutton, and a drunk.’

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאָמְרוּ אֶל זִקְנֵי עִירוֹ בְּנֵנוּ זֶה סוֹרֵר וּמֹרֶה אֵינֶנּוּ שֹׁמֵעַ בְּקֹלֵנוּ זוֹלֵל וְסֹבֵא׃}

verses.original: וּרְגָמֻהוּ כּל אַנְשֵׁי עִירוֹ בָאֲבָנִים וָמֵת וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ וְכל יִשְׂרָאֵל יִשְׁמְעוּ וְיִרָאוּ׃
verses.english: And all his city’s people shall batter him with stones so he dies. So you shall burn away what is bad from among you. And all Israel will listen and fear.

tex.original: \hDtn{וּרְגָמֻהוּ כּל אַנְשֵׁי עִירוֹ בָאֲבָנִים וָמֵת וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ וְכל יִשְׂרָאֵל יִשְׁמְעוּ וְיִרָאוּ׃}

verses.original: וְכִי יִהְיֶה בְאִישׁ חֵטְא מִשְׁפַּט מָוֶת וְהוּמָת וְתָלִיתָ אֹתוֹ עַל עֵץ׃
verses.english: “And if there will be a sin bringing a sentence of death on a man, and he will be put to death, and you will hang him on a tree,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכִי יִהְיֶה בְאִישׁ חֵטְא מִשְׁפַּט מָוֶת וְהוּמָת וְתָלִיתָ אֹתוֹ עַל עֵץ׃}

verses.original: לֹא תָלִין נִבְלָתוֹ עַל הָעֵץ כִּי קָבוֹר תִּקְבְּרֶנּוּ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא כִּי קִלְלַת אֱלֹהִים תָּלוּי וְלֹא תְטַמֵּא אֶת אַדְמָתְךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ נַחֲלָה׃
verses.english: you shall not leave his corpse on the tree, but you shall bury him on that day, because a hanged person is an offense to God, and you shall not make impure your land that YHWH, your God, is giving you as a legacy.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תָלִין נִבְלָתוֹ עַל הָעֵץ כִּי קָבוֹר תִּקְבְּרֶנּוּ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא כִּי קִלְלַת אֱלֹהִים תָּלוּי וְלֹא תְטַמֵּא אֶת אַדְמָתְךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ נַחֲלָה׃}

verses.original: לֹא תִרְאֶה אֶת שׁוֹר אָחִיךָ אוֹ אֶת שֵׂיוֹ נִדָּחִים וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ מֵהֶם הָשֵׁב תְּשִׁיבֵם לְאָחִיךָ׃
verses.english: “You shall not see your brother’s ox or his sheep driven off, and you hide yourself from them. You shall bring them back to your brother.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תִרְאֶה אֶת שׁוֹר אָחִיךָ אוֹ אֶת שֵׂיוֹ נִדָּחִים וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ מֵהֶם הָשֵׁב תְּשִׁיבֵם לְאָחִיךָ׃}

verses.original: וְאִם לֹא קָרוֹב אָחִיךָ אֵלֶיךָ וְלֹא יְדַעְתּוֹ וַאֲסַפְתּוֹ אֶל תּוֹךְ בֵּיתֶךָ וְהָיָה עִמְּךָ עַד דְּרֹשׁ אָחִיךָ אֹתוֹ וַהֲשֵׁבֹתוֹ לוֹ׃
verses.english: And if your brother is not close to you, and you don’t know him, then you shall gather it into your house, and it shall be with you until your brother inquires about it, and you shall give it back to him.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאִם לֹא קָרוֹב אָחִיךָ אֵלֶיךָ וְלֹא יְדַעְתּוֹ וַאֲסַפְתּוֹ אֶל תּוֹךְ בֵּיתֶךָ וְהָיָה עִמְּךָ עַד דְּרֹשׁ אָחִיךָ אֹתוֹ וַהֲשֵׁבֹתוֹ לוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְכֵן תַּעֲשֶׂה לַחֲמֹרוֹ וְכֵן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְשִׂמְלָתוֹ וְכֵן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְכל אֲבֵדַת אָחִיךָ אֲשֶׁר תֹּאבַד מִמֶּנּוּ וּמְצָאתָהּ לֹא תוּכַל לְהִתְעַלֵּם׃
verses.english: And you shall do that with his ass, and you shall do that with his garment, and you shall do that with any lost thing of your brother’s that will be lost by him and you find it. You may not hide yourself.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכֵן תַּעֲשֶׂה לַחֲמֹרוֹ וְכֵן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְשִׂמְלָתוֹ וְכֵן תַּעֲשֶׂה לְכל אֲבֵדַת אָחִיךָ אֲשֶׁר תֹּאבַד מִמֶּנּוּ וּמְצָאתָהּ לֹא תוּכַל לְהִתְעַלֵּם׃}

verses.original: לֹא תִרְאֶה אֶת חֲמוֹר אָחִיךָ אוֹ שׁוֹרוֹ נֹפְלִים בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ מֵהֶם הָקֵם תָּקִים עִמּוֹ׃
verses.english: You shall not see your brother’s ass or his ox falling in the road, and you hide yourself from them. You shall lift it up with him.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תִרְאֶה אֶת חֲמוֹר אָחִיךָ אוֹ שׁוֹרוֹ נֹפְלִים בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ מֵהֶם הָקֵם תָּקִים עִמּוֹ׃}

verses.original: לֹא יִהְיֶה כְלִי גֶבֶר עַל אִשָּׁה וְלֹא יִלְבַּשׁ גֶּבֶר שִׂמְלַת אִשָּׁה כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כּל עֹשֵׂה אֵלֶּה׃
verses.english: “There shall not be a man’s item on a woman, and a man shall not wear a woman’s garment, because everyone who does these is an offensive thing of YHWH, your God.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא יִהְיֶה כְלִי גֶבֶר עַל אִשָּׁה וְלֹא יִלְבַּשׁ גֶּבֶר שִׂמְלַת אִשָּׁה כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כּל עֹשֵׂה אֵלֶּה׃}

verses.original: כִּי יִקָּרֵא קַן צִפּוֹר לְפָנֶיךָ בַּדֶּרֶךְ בְּכל עֵץ אוֹ עַל הָאָרֶץ אֶפְרֹחִים אוֹ בֵיצִים וְהָאֵם רֹבֶצֶת עַל הָאֶפְרֹחִים אוֹ עַל הַבֵּיצִים לֹא תִקַּח הָאֵם עַל הַבָּנִים׃
verses.english: “When a bird’s nest will happen to be in front of you on the road in any tree or on the ground—chicks or eggs—and the mother is sitting over the chicks or over the eggs, you shall not take the mother along with the children.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִקָּרֵא קַן צִפּוֹר לְפָנֶיךָ בַּדֶּרֶךְ בְּכל עֵץ אוֹ עַל הָאָרֶץ אֶפְרֹחִים אוֹ בֵיצִים וְהָאֵם רֹבֶצֶת עַל הָאֶפְרֹחִים אוֹ עַל הַבֵּיצִים לֹא תִקַּח הָאֵם עַל הַבָּנִים׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the mother along with the children. The purpose of this law, like the
%		law against cooking a kid in its mother’s milk, is uncertain. Both laws
%		may have to do with caring about animals, prohibiting unfeeling
%		treatment of them. But both may also have purposes of a different sort.
%		Both cases may have been regarded as unnatural combinations, offensive
%		in themselves. In the case of the mother bird along with the eggs or
%		chicks, that would explain why this law is grouped here with laws
%		against forbidden mixtures of seeds, fabrics, and work animals, as well
%		as the law against males wearing female clothing and females wearing
%		male items. (For another explanation of the kid cooked in milk, see the
%		comment on 22:9 below.)
%	}

verses.original: שַׁלֵּחַ תְּשַׁלַּח אֶת הָאֵם וְאֶת הַבָּנִים תִּקַּח לָךְ לְמַעַן יִיטַב לָךְ וְהַאֲרַכְתָּ יָמִים׃
verses.english: You shall let the mother go, and you may take the children for you, so that it will be good for you, and you will extend days.

tex.original: \hDtn{שַׁלֵּחַ תְּשַׁלַּח אֶת הָאֵם וְאֶת הַבָּנִים תִּקַּח לָךְ לְמַעַן יִיטַב לָךְ וְהַאֲרַכְתָּ יָמִים׃}

verses.original: כִּי תִבְנֶה בַּיִת חָדָשׁ וְעָשִׂיתָ מַעֲקֶה לְגַגֶּךָ וְלֹא תָשִׂים דָּמִים בְּבֵיתֶךָ כִּי יִפֹּל הַנֹּפֵל מִמֶּנּוּ׃
verses.english: “When you’ll build a new house, you shall make a railing for your roof, so you won’t set blood in your house when someone will fall from it.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תִבְנֶה בַּיִת חָדָשׁ וְעָשִׂיתָ מַעֲקֶה לְגַגֶּךָ וְלֹא תָשִׂים דָּמִים בְּבֵיתֶךָ כִּי יִפֹּל הַנֹּפֵל מִמֶּנּוּ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		a railing for your roof. This law seems to be out of place, in the
%		middle of laws concerning mixtures. But there is apparently more than
%		one principle of orproduce will beganization operating here. The first
%		laws of this chapter concern caring about one’s neighbor, but
%		specifically expressed in terms of the neighbor’s animals. Then it adds
%		the neighbor’s garment. These laws are followed by the law prohibiting
%		men and women to mix each other’s garments, followed by a return to laws
%		regarding animals, followed by another law of caring about one’s
%		neighbor: this law of putting a railing on one’s roof. This is followed
%		by more laws of prohibited mixtures, including mixing certain animals.
%		The full group is a complex mixture of moral and ritual laws, but as a
%		group it also shows how the Torah’s different kinds of laws are
%		interconnected. Footnote 22:8. set blood in your house. Meaning: you
%		won’t bring the responsibility on your home for a loss of life.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא תִזְרַע כַּרְמְךָ כִּלְאָיִם פֶּן תִּקְדַּשׁ הַמְלֵאָה הַזֶּרַע אֲשֶׁר תִּזְרָע וּתְבוּאַת הַכָּרֶם׃
verses.english: “You shall not seed your vineyard with two kinds, or else the whole of the seed that you’ll sow and the vineyard’s produce will become holy.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תִזְרַע כַּרְמְךָ כִּלְאָיִם פֶּן תִּקְדַּשׁ הַמְלֵאָה הַזֶּרַע אֲשֶׁר תִּזְרָע וּתְבוּאַת הַכָּרֶם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		will become holy. Why does mixing different seeds in a vineyard make the
%		resulting crop holy? Several of the laws regarding mixtures have
%		possible explanations having to do with the realm of the holy. The law
%		against cooking a kid in its mother’s milk may be because that was
%		regarded as a food for a deity, since a Ugaritic text pictures the chief
%		god, El, having kid cooked in milk (see the comment on Exod 23:19). The
%		law against wearing wool and linen together may be because they were
%		both used in the Tabernacle (see the comment on Deut 22:11 below). (Even
%		the law against men wearing clothes of the opposite sex may have to do
%		with pagan myths in which the gods and goddesses do that.) And so it may
%		be in the case of mixed seeds, as well: the prohibition of mixing them
%		may not be because the mixing is bad in some way but rather because some
%		mixtures are regarded as divine. This is only a speculation, since the
%		meaning of this law (and of the other laws concerning mixtures) has
%		stymied scholars for centuries. But this speculation at least has the
%		advantage of coming to terms with the word “holy” in this law. Other
%		commentaries and translations have commonly ascribed some other meaning
%		to the word because of the difficulty of making sense of it in this
%		context.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא תַחֲרֹשׁ בְּשׁוֹר וּבַחֲמֹר יַחְדָּו׃
verses.english: You shall not plow with an ox and an ass together.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תַחֲרֹשׁ בְּשׁוֹר וּבַחֲמֹר יַחְדָּו׃}
tex.english: \eDtn{You shall not plow with an ox and an ass together.}

verses.original: לֹא תִלְבַּשׁ שַׁעַטְנֵז צֶמֶר וּפִשְׁתִּים יַחְדָּו׃
verses.english: You shall not wear sha‘atnez: wool and linen together.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תִלְבַּשׁ שַׁעַטְנֵז צֶמֶר וּפִשְׁתִּים יַחְדָּו׃}
tex.english: \eDtn{You shall not wear sha‘atnez: wool and linen together.}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		sha‘atnez: wool and linen together. The former comes from an animal, a
%		sheep; and the latter comes from a plant, flax. Some think that such
%		fabric is prohibited because it was thought to be an unnatural mixture.
%		Others think that it is because the priests have both linen and wool in
%		their clothing, and that therefore laypersons must not wear what belongs
%		to the realm of the sacred. The problem with the latter view is that the
%		only description of priestly garments in the Torah mentions linen but
%		does not mention wool explicitly. Still, it is likely that the priests
%		have wool and linen, because some of their clothing is said to be dyed
%		(Exod 28:4–6), and it is extremely difficult to dye linen (I learned
%		this from Avigail Sheffer, a specialist in ancient textiles). Fabric
%		excavated at Kuntillat ‘Ajrud, which may have been a cultic site,
%		contained linen and wool. Alternatively, the Tabernacle is made of an
%		inside layer of linen fabric and a second layer of wool (goats’ hair)
%		fabric over it. The sha‘atnez prohibition may therefore relate to the
%		sacred state of the Tabernacle rather than of the priesthood.
%	}

verses.original: גְּדִלִים תַּעֲשֶׂה לָּךְ עַל אַרְבַּע כַּנְפוֹת כְּסוּתְךָ אֲשֶׁר תְּכַסֶּה בָּהּ׃
verses.english: “You shall make braided threads on the four corners of your apparel with which you cover yourself.

tex.original: \hDtn{גְּדִלִים תַּעֲשֶׂה לָּךְ עַל אַרְבַּע כַּנְפוֹת כְּסוּתְךָ אֲשֶׁר תְּכַסֶּה בָּהּ׃}

verses.original: כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה וּבָא אֵלֶיהָ וּשְׂנֵאָהּ׃
verses.english: “When a man will take a wife and come to her and then hate her,

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה וּבָא אֵלֶיהָ וּשְׂנֵאָהּ׃}

verses.original: וְשָׂם לָהּ עֲלִילֹת דְּבָרִים וְהוֹצִא עָלֶיהָ שֵׁם רָע וְאָמַר אֶת הָאִשָּׁה הַזֹּאת לָקַחְתִּי וָאֶקְרַב אֵלֶיהָ וְלֹא מָצָאתִי לָהּ בְּתוּלִים׃
verses.english: and he’ll assert words of abuse toward her and bring out a bad name on her and say, ‘I took this woman, and I came close to her, and I didn’t find signs of virginity for her,’

tex.original: \hDtn{וְשָׂם לָהּ עֲלִילֹת דְּבָרִים וְהוֹצִא עָלֶיהָ שֵׁם רָע וְאָמַר אֶת הָאִשָּׁה הַזֹּאת לָקַחְתִּי וָאֶקְרַב אֵלֶיהָ וְלֹא מָצָאתִי לָהּ בְּתוּלִים׃}

verses.original: וְלָקַח אֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָ וְאִמָּהּ וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת בְּתוּלֵי הַנַּעֲרָ אֶל זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַשָּׁעְרָה׃
verses.english: then the young woman’s father and her mother shall take and bring out the signs of the young woman’s virginity to the city’s elders at the gate.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְלָקַח אֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָ וְאִמָּהּ וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת בְּתוּלֵי הַנַּעֲרָ אֶל זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַשָּׁעְרָה׃}

verses.original: וְאָמַר אֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָ אֶל הַזְּקֵנִים אֶת בִּתִּי נָתַתִּי לָאִישׁ הַזֶּה לְאִשָּׁה וַיִּשְׂנָאֶהָ׃
verses.english: “And the young woman’s father shall say to the elders, ‘I gave my daughter to this man for a wife, and he hated her.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאָמַר אֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָ אֶל הַזְּקֵנִים אֶת בִּתִּי נָתַתִּי לָאִישׁ הַזֶּה לְאִשָּׁה וַיִּשְׂנָאֶהָ׃}

verses.original: וְהִנֵּה הוּא שָׂם עֲלִילֹת דְּבָרִים לֵאמֹר לֹא מָצָאתִי לְבִתְּךָ בְּתוּלִים וְאֵלֶּה בְּתוּלֵי בִתִּי וּפָרְשׂוּ הַשִּׂמְלָה לִפְנֵי זִקְנֵי הָעִיר׃
verses.english: And, here, he has asserted words of abuse, saying: “I didn’t find signs of virginity for your daughter.” But these are the signs of my daughter’s virginity!’ And they shall spread out the garment in front of the city’s elders.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהִנֵּה הוּא שָׂם עֲלִילֹת דְּבָרִים לֵאמֹר לֹא מָצָאתִי לְבִתְּךָ בְּתוּלִים וְאֵלֶּה בְּתוּלֵי בִתִּי וּפָרְשׂוּ הַשִּׂמְלָה לִפְנֵי זִקְנֵי הָעִיר׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		And, here, he has asserted words of abuse, saying: “I
		didn’t find signs of virginity for your daughter.” But
		these are the signs of my daughter’s virginity!’ And they
		shall spread out the garment in front of the city’s
		elders.
	}

verses.original: וְלָקְחוּ זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִוא אֶת הָאִישׁ וְיִסְּרוּ אֹתוֹ׃
verses.english: “And that city’s elders shall take the man and discipline him.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְלָקְחוּ זִקְנֵי הָעִיר הַהִוא אֶת הָאִישׁ וְיִסְּרוּ אֹתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְעָנְשׁוּ אֹתוֹ מֵאָה כֶסֶף וְנָתְנוּ לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָה כִּי הוֹצִיא שֵׁם רָע עַל בְּתוּלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִשָּׁה לֹא יוּכַל לְשַׁלְּחָהּ כּל יָמָיו׃
verses.english: And they shall fine him a hundred weights of silver and give it to the young woman’s father because he brought out a bad name on a virgin of Israel. And she shall be his for a wife: he shall not be able to let her go, all his days.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְעָנְשׁוּ אֹתוֹ מֵאָה כֶסֶף וְנָתְנוּ לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָה כִּי הוֹצִיא שֵׁם רָע עַל בְּתוּלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִשָּׁה לֹא יוּכַל לְשַׁלְּחָהּ כּל יָמָיו׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		a bad name on a virgin of Israel. Premarital sex is not forbidden
%		elsewhere in the Torah, and men marry women who are not virgins. Only
%		the high priest is absolutely required to marry a virgin (Lev 21:13–14).
%		The issue in this case must therefore be that the woman was represented
%		to be a virgin at the time she was married, and now her husband claims
%		that she was not. Footnote 22:19. to let her go. Meaning: to divorce
%		her. Footnote 22:19. the young woman’s father. Both the woman herself
%		and her father receive some form of compensation. The woman can never be
%		divorced. The father receives monetary compensation.
%	}

verses.original: וְאִם אֱמֶת הָיָה הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה לֹא נִמְצְאוּ בְתוּלִים לַנַּעֲרָ׃
verses.english: “But if this thing was true—signs of virginity for the young woman were not found—

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאִם אֱמֶת הָיָה הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה לֹא נִמְצְאוּ בְתוּלִים לַנַּעֲרָ׃}

verses.original: וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת הַנַּעֲרָ אֶל פֶּתַח בֵּית אָבִיהָ וּסְקָלוּהָ אַנְשֵׁי עִירָהּ בָּאֲבָנִים וָמֵתָה כִּי עָשְׂתָה נְבָלָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לִזְנוֹת בֵּית אָבִיהָ וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ׃
verses.english: then they shall take the young woman out to the entrance of her father’s house, and the people of her city shall stone her with stones so she dies, because she did a foolhardy thing in Israel, to whore at her father’s house. So you shall burn away what is bad from among you.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת הַנַּעֲרָ אֶל פֶּתַח בֵּית אָבִיהָ וּסְקָלוּהָ אַנְשֵׁי עִירָהּ בָּאֲבָנִים וָמֵתָה כִּי עָשְׂתָה נְבָלָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לִזְנוֹת בֵּית אָבִיהָ וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		then they shall take the young woman out to the entrance
		of her father’s house, and the people of her city shall
		stone her with stones so she dies, because she did a
		foolhardy thing in Israel, to whore at her father’s house.
		So you shall burn away what is bad from among you.
	}

verses.original: כִּי יִמָּצֵא אִישׁ שֹׁכֵב עִם אִשָּׁה בְעֻלַת בַּעַל וּמֵתוּ גַּם שְׁנֵיהֶם הָאִישׁ הַשֹּׁכֵב עִם הָאִשָּׁה וְהָאִשָּׁה וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: “If a man will be found lying with a woman who is a husband’s wife, then the two of them shall die: the man who lay with the woman, and the woman. So you shall burn away what is bad from Israel.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִמָּצֵא אִישׁ שֹׁכֵב עִם אִשָּׁה בְעֻלַת בַּעַל וּמֵתוּ גַּם שְׁנֵיהֶם הָאִישׁ הַשֹּׁכֵב עִם הָאִשָּׁה וְהָאִשָּׁה וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: כִּי יִהְיֶה נַעֲרָ בְתוּלָה מְאֹרָשָׂה לְאִישׁ וּמְצָאָהּ אִישׁ בָּעִיר וְשָׁכַב עִמָּהּ׃
verses.english: “If it will be that a virgin young woman will be betrothed to a man, and a man will find her in the city and lie with her,

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִהְיֶה נַעֲרָ בְתוּלָה מְאֹרָשָׂה לְאִישׁ וּמְצָאָהּ אִישׁ בָּעִיר וְשָׁכַב עִמָּהּ׃}

verses.original: וְהוֹצֵאתֶם אֶת שְׁנֵיהֶם אֶל שַׁעַר הָעִיר הַהִוא וּסְקַלְתֶּם אֹתָם בָּאֲבָנִים וָמֵתוּ אֶת הַנַּעֲרָ עַל דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר לֹא צָעֲקָה בָעִיר וְאֶת הָאִישׁ עַל דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר עִנָּה אֶת אֵשֶׁת רֵעֵהוּ וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ׃
verses.english: then you shall take the two of them to that city’s gate and stone them with stones so they die: the young woman on account of the fact that she did not cry out in the city, and the man on account of the fact that he degraded his neighbor’s wife. So you shall burn away what is bad from among you.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהוֹצֵאתֶם אֶת שְׁנֵיהֶם אֶל שַׁעַר הָעִיר הַהִוא וּסְקַלְתֶּם אֹתָם בָּאֲבָנִים וָמֵתוּ אֶת הַנַּעֲרָ עַל דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר לֹא צָעֲקָה בָעִיר וְאֶת הָאִישׁ עַל דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר עִנָּה אֶת אֵשֶׁת רֵעֵהוּ וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		then you shall take the two of them to that city’s gate
		and stone them with stones so they die: the young woman on
		account of the fact that she did not cry out in the city,
		and the man on account of the fact that he degraded his
		neighbor’s wife. So you shall burn away what is bad from
		among you.
	}

verses.original: וְאִם בַּשָּׂדֶה יִמְצָא הָאִישׁ אֶת הַנַּעֲרָ הַמְאֹרָשָׂה וְהֶחֱזִיק בָּהּ הָאִישׁ וְשָׁכַב עִמָּהּ וּמֵת הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר שָׁכַב עִמָּהּ לְבַדּוֹ׃
verses.english: But if the man will find the betrothed young woman in the field, and the man will take hold of her and lie with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאִם בַּשָּׂדֶה יִמְצָא הָאִישׁ אֶת הַנַּעֲרָ הַמְאֹרָשָׂה וְהֶחֱזִיק בָּהּ הָאִישׁ וְשָׁכַב עִמָּהּ וּמֵת הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר שָׁכַב עִמָּהּ לְבַדּוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְלַנַּעֲרָ לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה דָבָר אֵין לַנַּעֲרָ חֵטְא מָוֶת כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר יָקוּם אִישׁ עַל רֵעֵהוּ וּרְצָחוֹ נֶפֶשׁ כֵּן הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: but you shall not do a thing to the young woman. The young woman does not have a sin deserving death, because, just as a man would get up against his neighbor and murder him: this case is like that;

tex.original: \hDtn{וְלַנַּעֲרָ לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה דָבָר אֵין לַנַּעֲרָ חֵטְא מָוֶת כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר יָקוּם אִישׁ עַל רֵעֵהוּ וּרְצָחוֹ נֶפֶשׁ כֵּן הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: כִּי בַשָּׂדֶה מְצָאָהּ צָעֲקָה הַנַּעֲרָ הַמְאֹרָשָׂה וְאֵין מוֹשִׁיעַ לָהּ׃
verses.english: because he found her in the field, the betrothed young woman cried out, and there was no one to save her.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי בַשָּׂדֶה מְצָאָהּ צָעֲקָה הַנַּעֲרָ הַמְאֹרָשָׂה וְאֵין מוֹשִׁיעַ לָהּ׃}

verses.original: כִּי יִמְצָא אִישׁ נַעֲרָ בְתוּלָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא אֹרָשָׂה וּתְפָשָׂהּ וְשָׁכַב עִמָּהּ וְנִמְצָאוּ׃
verses.english: “If a man will find a virgin young woman who is not betrothed, and he’ll grasp her and lie with her, and they’ll be found,

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִמְצָא אִישׁ נַעֲרָ בְתוּלָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא אֹרָשָׂה וּתְפָשָׂהּ וְשָׁכַב עִמָּהּ וְנִמְצָאוּ׃}

verses.original: וְנָתַן הָאִישׁ הַשֹּׁכֵב עִמָּהּ לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָ חֲמִשִּׁים כָּסֶף וְלוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִשָּׁה תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר עִנָּהּ לֹא יוּכַל שַׁלְּחָהּ כּל יָמָיו׃
verses.english: then the man who lay with her shall give the young woman’s father fifty weights of silver, and she shall be his for a wife. Because he degraded her, he shall not be able to let her go, all his days.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְנָתַן הָאִישׁ הַשֹּׁכֵב עִמָּהּ לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָ חֲמִשִּׁים כָּסֶף וְלוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִשָּׁה תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר עִנָּהּ לֹא יוּכַל שַׁלְּחָהּ כּל יָמָיו׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the young woman’s father. Both the woman herself and her father receive
%		some form of compensation. The woman can never be divorced. The father
%		receives monetary compensation. Footnote 22:29. she shall be his for a
%		wife. Married to the man who raped her?! Presumably, hopefully, this
%		means that the choice was hers as well as her father’s.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא יִקַּח אִישׁ אֶת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו וְלֹא יְגַלֶּה כְּנַף אָבִיו׃
verses.english: “A man shall not take his father’s wife, so he will not expose his father’s hem.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא יִקַּח אִישׁ אֶת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו וְלֹא יְגַלֶּה כְּנַף אָבִיו׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		take his father’s wife. Before or after his father’s death. This law
%		appears as part of the list of prohibited sexual mates in Leviticus
%		(18:8; 20:11), but here it stands alone. Its apparent special
%		significance is that this issue comes up several times in Israel’s royal
%		family. When David becomes king he takes Saul’s wives, but Saul was not
%		his father. But David is succeeded by his own sons, so the matter is
%		relevant. When his son Absalom rebels, he takes ten of David’s
%		concubines (2 Sam 16:22). After David’s death, his son Adonijah asks for
%		David’s concubine Abishag, a request that David’s successor Solomon
%		regards as a claim on the throne (1 Kings 2:22–25). This law also
%		recalls Reuben’s taking of his father Jacob’s concubine Bilhah (Gen
%		35:22). Jacob takes away the birthright from Reuben because of this (Gen
%		49:3–4). The law against taking one’s father’s wife thus guards against
%		dangerous situations (that a man would marry his half-brother’s mother,
%		or that a son might kill his father to get his wife) and especially
%		guards the security of the royal succession. Footnote 23:1. expose his
%		father’s hem. Meaning: the son would have contact with the woman to whom
%		the father has been exposed. “Exposing nudity” is the euphemism for
%		prohibited sexual unions (see Leviticus 18).
%	}

verses.original: לֹא יָבֹא פְצוּעַ דַּכָּא וּכְרוּת שׁפְכָה בִּקְהַל יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: One who is wounded by crushing or whose organ is cut off shall not come into YHWH’s community.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא יָבֹא פְצוּעַ דַּכָּא וּכְרוּת שׁפְכָה בִּקְהַל יְהֹוָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		wounded by crushing. The testicles. Footnote 23:2. whose organ is cut
%		off. The penis. Footnote 23:2. come into YHWH’s community. Meaning: may
%		not marry an Israelite woman. It is also possible that there was some
%		sort of conversion by which a non-Israelite might become an Israelite
%		and that this was denied to those persons mentioned here in vv. 2–9. But
%		this is uncertain because conversion is never mentioned in the Torah.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא יָבֹא מַמְזֵר בִּקְהַל יְהֹוָה גַּם דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי לֹא יָבֹא לוֹ בִּקְהַל יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: A bastard shall not come into YHWH’s community; even in the tenth generation one shall not come into YHWH’s community.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא יָבֹא מַמְזֵר בִּקְהַל יְהֹוָה גַּם דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי לֹא יָבֹא לוֹ בִּקְהַל יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: לֹא יָבֹא עַמּוֹנִי וּמוֹאָבִי בִּקְהַל יְהֹוָה גַּם דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי לֹא יָבֹא לָהֶם בִּקְהַל יְהֹוָה עַד עוֹלָם׃
verses.english: An Ammonite and a Moabite shall not come into YHWH’s community; even in the tenth generation they shall not come into YHWH’s community, forever,

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא יָבֹא עַמּוֹנִי וּמוֹאָבִי בִּקְהַל יְהֹוָה גַּם דּוֹר עֲשִׂירִי לֹא יָבֹא לָהֶם בִּקְהַל יְהֹוָה עַד עוֹלָם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		a Moabite. Yet Ruth, a Moabite woman, marries an Israelite, and their
%		descendant is King David—and all the royal line of Judah! Elsewhere,
%		however, we have seen that biblically a woman automatically takes on her
%		husband’s religion. Therefore, it is only a Moabite or Ammonite man who
%		is prohibited from marrying an Israelite woman. A Moabite or Ammonite
%		woman may marry an Israelite man. (This is also the rabbinic
%		understanding of this law.)
%	}

verses.original: עַל דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר לֹא קִדְּמוּ אֶתְכֶם בַּלֶּחֶם וּבַמַּיִם בַּדֶּרֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶם מִמִּצְרָיִם וַאֲשֶׁר שָׂכַר עָלֶיךָ אֶת בִּלְעָם בֶּן בְּעוֹר מִפְּתוֹר אֲרַם נַהֲרַיִם לְקַלְלֶךָּ׃
verses.english: on account of the fact that they did not meet you with bread and with water on the way when you came out from Egypt, and the fact that it hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor of Aram Naharaim against you to curse you.

tex.original: \hDtn{עַל דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר לֹא קִדְּמוּ אֶתְכֶם בַּלֶּחֶם וּבַמַּיִם בַּדֶּרֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶם מִמִּצְרָיִם וַאֲשֶׁר שָׂכַר עָלֶיךָ אֶת בִּלְעָם בֶּן בְּעוֹר מִפְּתוֹר אֲרַם נַהֲרַיִם לְקַלְלֶךָּ׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא אָבָה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לִשְׁמֹעַ אֶל בִּלְעָם וַיַּהֲפֹךְ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְּךָ אֶת הַקְּלָלָה לִבְרָכָה כִּי אֲהֵבְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: But YHWH, your God, was not willing to listen to Balaam, and YHWH, your God, turned the curse into a blessing for you because YHWH, your God, loved you.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְלֹא אָבָה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לִשְׁמֹעַ אֶל בִּלְעָם וַיַּהֲפֹךְ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְּךָ אֶת הַקְּלָלָה לִבְרָכָה כִּי אֲהֵבְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: לֹא תִדְרֹשׁ שְׁלֹמָם וְטֹבָתָם כּל יָמֶיךָ לְעוֹלָם׃
verses.english: You shall not seek their well-being or their good, all your days, forever.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תִדְרֹשׁ שְׁלֹמָם וְטֹבָתָם כּל יָמֶיךָ לְעוֹלָם׃}

verses.original: לֹא תְתַעֵב אֲדֹמִי כִּי אָחִיךָ הוּא לֹא תְתַעֵב מִצְרִי כִּי גֵר הָיִיתָ בְאַרְצוֹ׃
verses.english: “You shall not abhor an Edomite, because he is your brother. You shall not abhor an Egyptian, because you were an alien in his land.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תְתַעֵב אֲדֹמִי כִּי אָחִיךָ הוּא לֹא תְתַעֵב מִצְרִי כִּי גֵר הָיִיתָ בְאַרְצוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		an Edomite … he is your brother. Edomites are the descendants of Esau.
%		As in Genesis, Esau is not regarded as an enemy. As earlier in
%		Deuteronomy, Israelites are not to enter into conflict with Edom
%		(2:4–8). Later in the biblical era and in postbiblical times, Israel and
%		Edom became bitterly hostile (see, for example, Ps 137:7). But the
%		benevolence toward Esau and Edom in the Torah is clear and a marked
%		contrast to the later feelings and midrashim concerning Esau. Footnote
%		23:8. not abhor an Egyptian. Even more remarkable is this command not to
%		disdain an Egyptian—despite everything that happened in Egypt. We have
%		seen repeated laws requiring Israelites to give aliens the same
%		protections as citizens. And apparently this is the ultimate expression
%		of that principle (and possibly the reason for it): Israelites
%		themselves were aliens in Egypt, and they were abhorred (Gen 46:34; the
%		word translated “abomination” there is cognate to the word “abhor” here)
%		and mistreated, and so they must now never abhor an Egyptian or mistreat
%		any alien. It is the prime demonstration of the principle in Judaism:
%		“What is hateful to you, don’t do to your neighbor.”
%	}

verses.original: בָּנִים אֲשֶׁר יִוָּלְדוּ לָהֶם דּוֹר שְׁלִישִׁי יָבֹא לָהֶם בִּקְהַל יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Third-generation children who will be born to them may come into YHWH’s community.

tex.original: \hDtn{בָּנִים אֲשֶׁר יִוָּלְדוּ לָהֶם דּוֹר שְׁלִישִׁי יָבֹא לָהֶם בִּקְהַל יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: כִּי תֵצֵא מַחֲנֶה עַל אֹיְבֶיךָ וְנִשְׁמַרְתָּ מִכֹּל דָּבָר רָע׃
verses.english: “When you’ll go out encamped against your enemies, you shall be watchful against any bad thing.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תֵצֵא מַחֲנֶה עַל אֹיְבֶיךָ וְנִשְׁמַרְתָּ מִכֹּל דָּבָר רָע׃}

verses.original: כִּי יִהְיֶה בְךָ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִהְיֶה טָהוֹר מִקְּרֵה לָיְלָה וְיָצָא אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה לֹא יָבֹא אֶל תּוֹךְ הַמַּחֲנֶה׃
verses.english: If there will be among you a man who will not be pure by a night occurrence, then he shall go outside the camp. He shall not come inside the camp.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִהְיֶה בְךָ אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִהְיֶה טָהוֹר מִקְּרֵה לָיְלָה וְיָצָא אֶל מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה לֹא יָבֹא אֶל תּוֹךְ הַמַּחֲנֶה׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה לִפְנוֹת עֶרֶב יִרְחַץ בַּמָּיִם וּכְבֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ יָבֹא אֶל תּוֹךְ הַמַּחֲנֶה׃
verses.english: And it shall be: toward evening he shall wash in water, and when the sun sets he shall come inside the camp.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְהָיָה לִפְנוֹת עֶרֶב יִרְחַץ בַּמָּיִם וּכְבֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ יָבֹא אֶל תּוֹךְ הַמַּחֲנֶה׃}

verses.original: וְיָד תִּהְיֶה לְךָ מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה וְיָצָאתָ שָּׁמָּה חוּץ׃
verses.english: And you shall have a location outside the camp, and you shall go out there, outside;

tex.original: \hDtn{וְיָד תִּהְיֶה לְךָ מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה וְיָצָאתָ שָּׁמָּה חוּץ׃}

verses.original: וְיָתֵד תִּהְיֶה לְךָ עַל אֲזֵנֶךָ וְהָיָה בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ חוּץ וְחָפַרְתָּה בָהּ וְשַׁבְתָּ וְכִסִּיתָ אֶת צֵאָתֶךָ׃
verses.english: and you shall have a spade among your equipment, and it shall be, when you sit outside, that you shall dig with it, and you shall go back and cover what comes out of you.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְיָתֵד תִּהְיֶה לְךָ עַל אֲזֵנֶךָ וְהָיָה בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ חוּץ וְחָפַרְתָּה בָהּ וְשַׁבְתָּ וְכִסִּיתָ אֶת צֵאָתֶךָ׃}

verses.original: כִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מִתְהַלֵּךְ בְּקֶרֶב מַחֲנֶךָ לְהַצִּילְךָ וְלָתֵת אֹיְבֶיךָ לְפָנֶיךָ וְהָיָה מַחֲנֶיךָ קָדוֹשׁ וְלֹא יִרְאֶה בְךָ עֶרְוַת דָּבָר וְשָׁב מֵאַחֲרֶיךָ׃
verses.english: Because YHWH, your God, is going within your camp, to rescue you and to put your enemies in front of you, so your camp shall be holy, so He won’t see an exposure of something in you and turn back from you.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מִתְהַלֵּךְ בְּקֶרֶב מַחֲנֶךָ לְהַצִּילְךָ וְלָתֵת אֹיְבֶיךָ לְפָנֶיךָ וְהָיָה מַחֲנֶיךָ קָדוֹשׁ וְלֹא יִרְאֶה בְךָ עֶרְוַת דָּבָר וְשָׁב מֵאַחֲרֶיךָ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		an exposure of something. Meaning: something improper. The term for
%		“exposure” (Hebrew ‘erwãh) elsewhere relates to nudity. It frequently
%		involves sexual matters. Here it involves human excretion. The phrase
%		here thus refers to something from the sexual or excremental realms that
%		offends.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא תַסְגִּיר עֶבֶד אֶל אֲדֹנָיו אֲשֶׁר יִנָּצֵל אֵלֶיךָ מֵעִם אֲדֹנָיו׃
verses.english: “You shall not turn over to his master a slave who will seek deliverance with you from his master.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תַסְגִּיר עֶבֶד אֶל אֲדֹנָיו אֲשֶׁר יִנָּצֵל אֵלֶיךָ מֵעִם אֲדֹנָיו׃}

verses.original: עִמְּךָ יֵשֵׁב בְּקִרְבְּךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ בַּטּוֹב לוֹ לֹא תּוֹנֶנּוּ׃
verses.english: He shall live with you, among you, in the place that he will choose in one of your gates, where it is good for him. You shall not persecute him.

tex.original: \hDtn{עִמְּךָ יֵשֵׁב בְּקִרְבְּךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר בְּאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ בַּטּוֹב לוֹ לֹא תּוֹנֶנּוּ׃}

verses.original: לֹא תִהְיֶה קְדֵשָׁה מִבְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא יִהְיֶה קָדֵשׁ מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: “There shall not be a sacred prostitute from the daughters of Israel, and there shall not be a sacred prostitute from the sons of Israel.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תִהְיֶה קְדֵשָׁה מִבְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא יִהְיֶה קָדֵשׁ מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		sacred prostitute. I realize that there is little evidence that there
%		was such a thing as cultic prostitution in the ancient Near East, and I
%		know that we should not derive the meaning of words solely from their
%		roots (the etymological fallacy), so we cannot assume that this word
%		(Hebrew qdh) means “sacred” prostitute just
%		because it has the same root as qd, meaning “holy.”
%		Still, I think that “sacred prostitute” is probably correct here
%		because: (1) The female and male prostitutes in this verse are in
%		parallel with bringing the price of female and male prostitutes to the
%		Temple in the next verse, so the common issue seems to be the
%		association of prostitution with the realm of the holy. (2) The story of
%		Tamar (Genesis 38) plays upon the distinction between Hebrew
%		znh, meaning “prostitute,” and Hebrew
%		qdh, meaning something higher than a regular
%		prostitute. Judah is described as thinking that Tamar is a
%		znh (38:15), but Judah’s friend uses the word
%		qdh when he discreetly inquires about her
%		later (38:21). It is possible that the distinction there is between
%		levels of prostitutes or between more and less pejorative terms
%		(comparable to English “whore” versus “prostitute”). But, since this is
%		uncertain, the combination of this point with the etymological factor
%		and the parallel verse still weighs in favor of the meaning of “sacred
%		prostitute.” Regular prostitution is not necessarily prohibited by law
%		in the Tanak, but it is disdained. The symbolism of the prophet Hosea’s
%		marriage to a prostitute indicates this (Hosea 1–3).
%	}

verses.original: לֹא תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב בֵּית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְכל נֶדֶר כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ גַּם שְׁנֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: You shall not bring the price of a prostitute or the cost of a dog to the house of YHWH, your God, for any vow, because the two of them are both an offensive thing of YHWH.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב בֵּית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְכל נֶדֶר כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ גַּם שְׁנֵיהֶם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		the price of a prostitute. It is offensive to vow an amount for the
%		Temple that is known to be the going rate for a prostitute. Footnote
%		23:19. the cost of a dog. “Dog” is widely understood to refer
%		pejoratively to a male prostitute. There is little evidence for or
%		against this understanding. It is based on the context, which is
%		concerned with prostitutes.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא תַשִּׁיךְ לְאָחִיךָ נֶשֶׁךְ כֶּסֶף נֶשֶׁךְ אֹכֶל נֶשֶׁךְ כּל דָּבָר אֲשֶׁר יִשָּׁךְ׃
verses.english: “You shall not require interest for your brother: interest of money, interest of food, interest of anything that one might charge.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תַשִּׁיךְ לְאָחִיךָ נֶשֶׁךְ כֶּסֶף נֶשֶׁךְ אֹכֶל נֶשֶׁךְ כּל דָּבָר אֲשֶׁר יִשָּׁךְ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		require interest. This law is consistent with other laws that contribute
%		to preventing the development of a small, wealthy upper class and a
%		large poor class. Like the jubilee law and the law prohibiting the king
%		from having many horses and the law against keeping an Israelite slave
%		more than six years, this law aims to protect an Israelite in financial
%		straits from entering a cycle that will keep him or her from ever
%		recovering, and thus permanently locked into a dependent position. This
%		is part of an economic system for the country, and so it applies only to
%		“your brother,” i.e., a fellow Israelite. Israelites may still require
%		interest on loans to foreign borrowers.
%	}

verses.original: לַנּכְרִי תַשִּׁיךְ וּלְאָחִיךָ לֹא תַשִּׁיךְ לְמַעַן יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכֹל מִשְׁלַח יָדֶךָ עַל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה בָא שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃
verses.english: For a foreigner you may require it, but for your brother you shall not require it, so that YHWH, your God, will bless you in everything your hand has taken on, on the land to which you’re coming to take possession of it.

tex.original: \hDtn{לַנּכְרִי תַשִּׁיךְ וּלְאָחִיךָ לֹא תַשִּׁיךְ לְמַעַן יְבָרֶכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכֹל מִשְׁלַח יָדֶךָ עַל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה בָא שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃}

verses.original: כִּי תִדֹּר נֶדֶר לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תְאַחֵר לְשַׁלְּמוֹ כִּי דָרֹשׁ יִדְרְשֶׁנּוּ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מֵעִמָּךְ וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא׃
verses.english: “When you’ll make a vow to YHWH, your God, you shall not delay to fulfill it, because YHWH, your God, will require it from you, and it will be a sin in you.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תִדֹּר נֶדֶר לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תְאַחֵר לְשַׁלְּמוֹ כִּי דָרֹשׁ יִדְרְשֶׁנּוּ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מֵעִמָּךְ וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא׃}

verses.original: וְכִי תֶחְדַּל לִנְדֹּר לֹא יִהְיֶה בְךָ חֵטְא׃
verses.english: But if you desist from vowing, that will not be a sin in you.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְכִי תֶחְדַּל לִנְדֹּר לֹא יִהְיֶה בְךָ חֵטְא׃}

verses.original: מוֹצָא שְׂפָתֶיךָ תִּשְׁמֹר וְעָשִׂיתָ כַּאֲשֶׁר נָדַרְתָּ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נְדָבָה אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתָּ בְּפִיךָ׃
verses.english: You shall watch what comes out of your lips and do as you vowed to YHWH, your God, the contribution that you spoke with your mouth.

tex.original: \hDtn{מוֹצָא שְׂפָתֶיךָ תִּשְׁמֹר וְעָשִׂיתָ כַּאֲשֶׁר נָדַרְתָּ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נְדָבָה אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתָּ בְּפִיךָ׃}

verses.original: כִּי תָבֹא בְּכֶרֶם רֵעֶךָ וְאָכַלְתָּ עֲנָבִים כְּנַפְשְׁךָ שׂבְעֶךָ וְאֶל כֶּלְיְךָ לֹא תִתֵּן׃
verses.english: “When you’ll come into your neighbor’s vineyard, then you may eat grapes as you wish, your fill; but you shall not put any into your container.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תָבֹא בְּכֶרֶם רֵעֶךָ וְאָכַלְתָּ עֲנָבִים כְּנַפְשְׁךָ שׂבְעֶךָ וְאֶל כֶּלְיְךָ לֹא תִתֵּן׃}

verses.original: כִּי תָבֹא בְּקָמַת רֵעֶךָ וְקָטַפְתָּ מְלִילֹת בְּיָדֶךָ וְחֶרְמֵשׁ לֹא תָנִיף עַל קָמַת רֵעֶךָ׃
verses.english: When you’ll come into your neighbor’s standing grain, then you may pluck ears with your hand; but you shall not lift a sickle at your neighbor’s grain.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תָבֹא בְּקָמַת רֵעֶךָ וְקָטַפְתָּ מְלִילֹת בְּיָדֶךָ וְחֶרְמֵשׁ לֹא תָנִיף עַל קָמַת רֵעֶךָ׃}

verses.original: כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה וּבְעָלָהּ וְהָיָה אִם לֹא תִמְצָא חֵן בְּעֵינָיו כִּי מָצָא בָהּ עֶרְוַת דָּבָר וְכָתַב לָהּ סֵפֶר כְּרִיתֻת וְנָתַן בְּיָדָהּ וְשִׁלְּחָהּ מִבֵּיתוֹ׃
verses.english: “When a man will take a woman and marry her, and it will be that, if she does not find favor in his eyes because he has found an exposure of something in her, and he will write a document of cutting-off for her and put it in her hand and let her go from his house,

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה וּבְעָלָהּ וְהָיָה אִם לֹא תִמְצָא חֵן בְּעֵינָיו כִּי מָצָא בָהּ עֶרְוַת דָּבָר וְכָתַב לָהּ סֵפֶר כְּרִיתֻת וְנָתַן בְּיָדָהּ וְשִׁלְּחָהּ מִבֵּיתוֹ׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		“When a man will take a woman and marry her, and it
		will be that, if she does not find favor in his eyes
		because he has found an exposure of something in her, and
		he will write a document of cutting-off for her and put it
		in her hand and let her go from his house,
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		When a man will take a woman. This law (vv. 1–4) has been taken as the
%		biblical law of divorce, but it is not. It is the law governing a
%		specific instance in which a couple might want to return to each other
%		after they were divorced and she was remarried and then was divorced
%		again or widowed. Divorce law in general has been derived in part from
%		this case because of the curious fact that there is no law in the Torah
%		telling how to get married and no law telling how to get divorced. Here,
%		the divorce procedure appears to be assumed, as a known practice. The
%		absence of marriage and divorce procedures has been used as a proof of
%		the existence of oral law that was given along with the law that is
%		written in the Torah. But the case may be rather that these ceremonies
%		were not regarded as having been given in detail by God—as few
%		ceremonies outside of the sacrifices at the Tabernacle are so given. The
%		divine interest is in the marriage relationship rather than in the
%		ceremony: the husband’s treatment of the wife, the prohibition of
%		adultery, their relationship with their children, inheritance, making
%		one’s spouse happy (see 24:5). The same goes for funerals and bar
%		mitzvah. Even such well-known Jewish practices as saying kaddish and
%		sitting shivah are not mentioned in the Torah. And bar and bat mitzvah
%		are not treated (or even mentioned): the concern is with doing the
%		commandments. The details of the ceremony of arriving at the age of
%		doing them are left for humans to choose. All of these ceremonies were
%		detailed in rabbinic law and practice later. Ceremonial procedures are
%		given in the Torah for less common cases, such as the slave who declines
%		to leave a master (Deut 15:16–17), or the brother-in-law who declines to
%		perform levirate marriage (25:7–10), or the present case of return
%		marriage. Footnote 24:1. an exposure of something. See the comment on
%		23:15 above. Footnote 24:1. a document of cutting-off. A divorce.
%	}

verses.original: וְיָצְאָה מִבֵּיתוֹ וְהָלְכָה וְהָיְתָה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר׃
verses.english: and she will go out from his house and go and become another man’s,

tex.original: \hDtn{וְיָצְאָה מִבֵּיתוֹ וְהָלְכָה וְהָיְתָה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר׃}

verses.original: וּשְׂנֵאָהּ הָאִישׁ הָאַחֲרוֹן וְכָתַב לָהּ סֵפֶר כְּרִיתֻת וְנָתַן בְּיָדָהּ וְשִׁלְּחָהּ מִבֵּיתוֹ אוֹ כִי יָמוּת הָאִישׁ הָאַחֲרוֹן אֲשֶׁר לְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה׃
verses.english: and the latter man will hate her and write a document of cutting-off for her and put it in her hand and let her go from his house, or if the latter man who took her to him for a wife will die:

tex.original: \hDtn{וּשְׂנֵאָהּ הָאִישׁ הָאַחֲרוֹן וְכָתַב לָהּ סֵפֶר כְּרִיתֻת וְנָתַן בְּיָדָהּ וְשִׁלְּחָהּ מִבֵּיתוֹ אוֹ כִי יָמוּת הָאִישׁ הָאַחֲרוֹן אֲשֶׁר לְקָחָהּ לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה׃}

verses.original: לֹא יוּכַל בַּעְלָהּ הָרִאשׁוֹן אֲשֶׁר שִׁלְּחָהּ לָשׁוּב לְקַחְתָּהּ לִהְיוֹת לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה אַחֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר הֻטַּמָּאָה כִּי תוֹעֵבָה הִוא לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וְלֹא תַחֲטִיא אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ נַחֲלָה׃
verses.english: her first husband who let her go shall not be able to come back to take her to be his for a wife since she has been made impure, because that is an offensive thing in front of YHWH, and you shall not bring sin on the land that YHWH, your God, is giving you as a legacy.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא יוּכַל בַּעְלָהּ הָרִאשׁוֹן אֲשֶׁר שִׁלְּחָהּ לָשׁוּב לְקַחְתָּהּ לִהְיוֹת לוֹ לְאִשָּׁה אַחֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר הֻטַּמָּאָה כִּי תוֹעֵבָה הִוא לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וְלֹא תַחֲטִיא אֶת הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לְךָ נַחֲלָה׃}
tex.english:
\eDtn{
		her first husband who let her go shall not be able to come
		back to take her to be his for a wife since she has been
		made impure, because that is an offensive thing in front
		of YHWH, and you shall not bring sin on the land that
		YHWH, your God, is giving you as a legacy.
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		her first husband shall not be able to come back. Jeremiah transforms
%		this into a metaphor in which God has cut off Israel the way the husband
%		in this law cuts off his wife (Jer 3:1), yet God would still take Israel
%		back, seemingly against God’s own law concerning human marriages
%		(3:12,14,22)!
%	}

verses.original: כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה חֲדָשָׁה לֹא יֵצֵא בַּצָּבָא וְלֹא יַעֲבֹר עָלָיו לְכל דָּבָר נָקִי יִהְיֶה לְבֵיתוֹ שָׁנָה אֶחָת וְשִׂמַּח אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר לָקָח׃
verses.english: “When a man will take a new wife, he shall not go out in the army and not go along with it for any matter. He shall be free at his house for one year and shall make his wife whom he has taken happy.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה חֲדָשָׁה לֹא יֵצֵא בַּצָּבָא וְלֹא יַעֲבֹר עָלָיו לְכל דָּבָר נָקִי יִהְיֶה לְבֵיתוֹ שָׁנָה אֶחָת וְשִׂמַּח אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר לָקָח׃}

verses.original: לֹא יַחֲבֹל רֵחַיִם וָרָכֶב כִּי נֶפֶשׁ הוּא חֹבֵל׃
verses.english: One shall not take a mill or an upper millstone as security, because he is taking one’s life as security.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא יַחֲבֹל רֵחַיִם וָרָכֶב כִּי נֶפֶשׁ הוּא חֹבֵל׃}

verses.original: כִּי יִמָּצֵא אִישׁ גֹּנֵב נֶפֶשׁ מֵאֶחָיו מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהִתְעַמֶּר בּוֹ וּמְכָרוֹ וּמֵת הַגַּנָּב הַהוּא וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ׃
verses.english: “When a man will be found stealing a person from among his brothers, from the children of Israel, so he will get profit through him and sell him, then that thief shall die. So you shall burn away what is bad from among you.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי יִמָּצֵא אִישׁ גֹּנֵב נֶפֶשׁ מֵאֶחָיו מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהִתְעַמֶּר בּוֹ וּמְכָרוֹ וּמֵת הַגַּנָּב הַהוּא וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ׃}

verses.original: הִשָּׁמֶר בְּנֶגַע הַצָּרַעַת לִשְׁמֹר מְאֹד וְלַעֲשׂוֹת כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יוֹרוּ אֶתְכֶם הַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִם תִּשְׁמְרוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת׃
verses.english: “Be watchful with the plague of leprosy, to be very watchful and to do according to everything that the Levite priests will instruct you. You shall be watchful to do according to what I commanded them.

tex.original: \hDtn{הִשָּׁמֶר בְּנֶגַע הַצָּרַעַת לִשְׁמֹר מְאֹד וְלַעֲשׂוֹת כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יוֹרוּ אֶתְכֶם הַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִם תִּשְׁמְרוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת׃}

verses.original: זָכוֹר אֵת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְמִרְיָם בַּדֶּרֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶם מִמִּצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: Remember what YHWH, your God, did to Miriam on the way when you were coming out from Egypt.

tex.original: \hDtn{זָכוֹר אֵת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְמִרְיָם בַּדֶּרֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶם מִמִּצְרָיִם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Remember what God did to Miriam. Why is this brought up here in the
%		context of a general law about leprosy? Because the law here is not
%		concerned only with the correct treatment for leprosy after one has
%		contracted it (which is the concern of Leviticus 13–14). It also warns
%		to be watchful (the term occurs three times) against behavior that would
%		bring about leprosy as a consequence (see 24:8). Miriam does something
%		that causes her to be stricken with leprosy. Rashi understands her
%		offense to be slanderous gossip (lôn hr‘),
%		but leprosy is more likely to be tied to a ritual offense. Miriam’s
%		words are not gossip; she is stricken with leprosy for having challenged
%		Moses’ status as a prophet compared with her own (Num 12:9–15; see the
%		comment on 12:2). And later, King Uzziah is stricken with it for burning
%		incense in the Temple, which only priests can do (2 Chr 26:16–21).
%	}

verses.original: כִּי תַשֶּׁה בְרֵעֲךָ מַשַּׁאת מְאוּמָה לֹא תָבֹא אֶל בֵּיתוֹ לַעֲבֹט עֲבֹטוֹ׃
verses.english: “When you’ll make a loan of anything to your neighbor, you shall not come into his house to get his pledge.

tex.original: \hDtn{כִּי תַשֶּׁה בְרֵעֲךָ מַשַּׁאת מְאוּמָה לֹא תָבֹא אֶל בֵּיתוֹ לַעֲבֹט עֲבֹטוֹ׃}

verses.original: בַּחוּץ תַּעֲמֹד וְהָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה נֹשֶׁה בוֹ יוֹצִיא אֵלֶיךָ אֶת הַעֲבוֹט הַחוּצָה׃
verses.english: You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you’re lending shall bring the pledge outside to you.

tex.original: \hDtn{בַּחוּץ תַּעֲמֹד וְהָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה נֹשֶׁה בוֹ יוֹצִיא אֵלֶיךָ אֶת הַעֲבוֹט הַחוּצָה׃}

verses.original: וְאִם אִישׁ עָנִי הוּא לֹא תִשְׁכַּב בַּעֲבֹטוֹ׃
verses.english: And if he is a poor man, you shall not lie down with his pledge.

tex.original: \hDtn{וְאִם אִישׁ עָנִי הוּא לֹא תִשְׁכַּב בַּעֲבֹטוֹ׃}

verses.original: הָשֵׁב תָּשִׁיב לוֹ אֶת הַעֲבוֹט כְּבוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְשָׁכַב בְּשַׂלְמָתוֹ וּבֵרְכֶךָּ וּלְךָ תִּהְיֶה צְדָקָה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: You shall give back the pledge to him as the sun sets, and he’ll lie down with his clothing, and he’ll bless you, and you’ll have virtue in front of YHWH, your God.

tex.original: \hDtn{הָשֵׁב תָּשִׁיב לוֹ אֶת הַעֲבוֹט כְּבוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְשָׁכַב בְּשַׂלְמָתוֹ וּבֵרְכֶךָּ וּלְךָ תִּהְיֶה צְדָקָה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: לֹא תַעֲשֹׁק שָׂכִיר עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן מֵאַחֶיךָ אוֹ מִגֵּרְךָ אֲשֶׁר בְּאַרְצְךָ בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ׃
verses.english: “You shall not exploit a poor or an indigent employee, from your brothers or from your aliens who are in your land, in your gates.

tex.original: \hDtn{לֹא תַעֲשֹׁק שָׂכִיר עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן מֵאַחֶיךָ אוֹ מִגֵּרְךָ אֲשֶׁר בְּאַרְצְךָ בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: בְּיוֹמוֹ תִתֵּן שְׂכָרוֹ וְלֹא תָבוֹא עָלָיו הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ כִּי עָנִי הוּא וְאֵלָיו הוּא נֹשֵׂא אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ וְלֹא יִקְרָא עָלֶיךָ אֶל יְהֹוָה וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא׃
