tex.original: \hDtrA{טַפְּכֶם נְשֵׁיכֶם וְגֵרְךָ אֲשֶׁר בְּקֶרֶב מַחֲנֶיךָ מֵחֹטֵב עֵצֶיךָ עַד שֹׁאֵב מֵימֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: לְעבְרְךָ בִּבְרִית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וּבְאָלָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כֹּרֵת עִמְּךָ הַיּוֹם׃
verses.english: for you to enter into the covenant of YHWH, your God, and into His oath, which YHWH, your God, is making with you today,

tex.original: \hDtrA{לְעבְרְךָ בִּבְרִית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וּבְאָלָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ כֹּרֵת עִמְּךָ הַיּוֹם׃}

verses.original: לְמַעַן הָקִים אֹתְךָ הַיּוֹם לוֹ לְעָם וְהוּא יִהְיֶה לְּךָ לֵאלֹהִים כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָךְ וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע לַאֲבֹתֶיךָ לְאַבְרָהָם לְיִצְחָק וּלְיַעֲקֹב׃
verses.english: in order to establish you today for Him as a people, and He will be a God to you, as He spoke to you and as He swore to your fathers: to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

tex.original: \hDtrA{לְמַעַן הָקִים אֹתְךָ הַיּוֹם לוֹ לְעָם וְהוּא יִהְיֶה לְּךָ לֵאלֹהִים כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָךְ וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע לַאֲבֹתֶיךָ לְאַבְרָהָם לְיִצְחָק וּלְיַעֲקֹב׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא אִתְּכֶם לְבַדְּכֶם אָנֹכִי כֹּרֵת אֶת הַבְּרִית הַזֹּאת וְאֶת הָאָלָה הַזֹּאת׃
verses.english: And I am not making this covenant and this oath with you alone,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְלֹא אִתְּכֶם לְבַדְּכֶם אָנֹכִי כֹּרֵת אֶת הַבְּרִית הַזֹּאת וְאֶת הָאָלָה הַזֹּאת׃}

verses.original: כִּי אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶשְׁנוֹ פֹּה עִמָּנוּ עֹמֵד הַיּוֹם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְאֵת אֲשֶׁר אֵינֶנּוּ פֹּה עִמָּנוּ הַיּוֹם׃
verses.english: but with the one who is here standing with us today in front of YHWH, our God, and with the one who isn’t here with us today.

tex.original: \hDtrA{כִּי אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶשְׁנוֹ פֹּה עִמָּנוּ עֹמֵד הַיּוֹם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְאֵת אֲשֶׁר אֵינֶנּוּ פֹּה עִמָּנוּ הַיּוֹם׃}

verses.original: כִּי אַתֶּם יְדַעְתֶּם אֵת אֲשֶׁר יָשַׁבְנוּ בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם וְאֵת אֲשֶׁר עָבַרְנוּ בְּקֶרֶב הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר עֲבַרְתֶּם׃
verses.english: Because you know that we lived in the land of Egypt and that we passed among the nations that you passed.

tex.original: \hDtrA{כִּי אַתֶּם יְדַעְתֶּם אֵת אֲשֶׁר יָשַׁבְנוּ בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם וְאֵת אֲשֶׁר עָבַרְנוּ בְּקֶרֶב הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר עֲבַרְתֶּם׃}

verses.original: וַתִּרְאוּ אֶת שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶם וְאֵת גִּלֻּלֵיהֶם עֵץ וָאֶבֶן כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב אֲשֶׁר עִמָּהֶם׃
verses.english: And you’ve seen their disgraces and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, that were with them.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַתִּרְאוּ אֶת שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶם וְאֵת גִּלֻּלֵיהֶם עֵץ וָאֶבֶן כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב אֲשֶׁר עִמָּהֶם׃}

verses.original: פֶּן יֵשׁ בָּכֶם אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה אוֹ מִשְׁפָּחָה אוֹ שֵׁבֶט אֲשֶׁר לְבָבוֹ פֹנֶה הַיּוֹם מֵעִם יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ לָלֶכֶת לַעֲבֹד אֶת אֱלֹהֵי הַגּוֹיִם הָהֵם פֶּן יֵשׁ בָּכֶם שֹׁרֶשׁ פֹּרֶה רֹאשׁ וְלַעֲנָה׃
verses.english: In case there will be among you a man or woman or family or tribe whose heart is turning today from YHWH, our God, to go to serve those nations’ gods; in case there is among you a root bearing poison and wormwood,

tex.original: \hDtrA{פֶּן יֵשׁ בָּכֶם אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה אוֹ מִשְׁפָּחָה אוֹ שֵׁבֶט אֲשֶׁר לְבָבוֹ פֹנֶה הַיּוֹם מֵעִם יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ לָלֶכֶת לַעֲבֹד אֶת אֱלֹהֵי הַגּוֹיִם הָהֵם פֶּן יֵשׁ בָּכֶם שֹׁרֶשׁ פֹּרֶה רֹאשׁ וְלַעֲנָה׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה בְּשׁמְעוֹ אֶת דִּבְרֵי הָאָלָה הַזֹּאת וְהִתְבָּרֵךְ בִּלְבָבוֹ לֵאמֹר שָׁלוֹם יִהְיֶה לִּי כִּי בִּשְׁרִרוּת לִבִּי אֵלֵךְ לְמַעַן סְפוֹת הָרָוָה אֶת הַצְּמֵאָה׃
verses.english: and it will be when he hears the words of this oath that he’ll feel himself blessed in his heart, saying, ‘I’ll have peace, though I’ll go on in my heart’s obstinacy,’ so as to annihilate the wet with the dry:

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְהָיָה בְּשׁמְעוֹ אֶת דִּבְרֵי הָאָלָה הַזֹּאת וְהִתְבָּרֵךְ בִּלְבָבוֹ לֵאמֹר שָׁלוֹם יִהְיֶה לִּי כִּי בִּשְׁרִרוּת לִבִּי אֵלֵךְ לְמַעַן סְפוֹת הָרָוָה אֶת הַצְּמֵאָה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		oath. The word can mean either “oath” or “curse.” Here it can refer to
%		the covenant oath mentioned in v. 11 or to the covenant curses; or it
%		can mean the two together, since the covenant oath implicitly invokes
%		the curses on the one who takes it. Footnote 29:18. annihilate the wet
%		with the dry. Commentators and translators struggle with this phrase,
%		which may have been an idiomatic expression whose context is no longer
%		known. The answer may lie in the phenomenon that we have seen a number
%		of times whereby expressions from Genesis recur here in Deuteronomy. The
%		verb here (“annihilate” or “sweep away”) occurs four times in the matter
%		of Sodom and Gomorrah (Gen 18:23,24; 19:15,17) and in one other place in
%		the Torah, the destruction of Korah and his group (Num 16:26). In all
%		five occurrences there is an issue of whether good people will be
%		annihilated along with the bad. And they all involve fire coming from
%		God and destroying the offenders. The meaning of this expression here,
%		therefore, may be that as a strong fire burns up what is dry and
%		evaporates what is wet (or as a forest fire destroys both the dry and
%		fresh trees), so the obstinate person, or group in this case, may bring
%		down the community with them. This understanding is reinforced by the
%		fact that Sodom and Gomorrah are referred to just four verses later
%		(29:22).
%	}

verses.original: לֹא יֹאבֶה יְהֹוָה סְלֹחַ לוֹ כִּי אָז יֶעְשַׁן אַף יְהֹוָה וְקִנְאָתוֹ בָּאִישׁ הַהוּא וְרָבְצָה בּוֹ כּל הָאָלָה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּסֵּפֶר הַזֶּה וּמָחָה יְהֹוָה אֶת שְׁמוֹ מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמָיִם׃
verses.english: YHWH will not be willing to forgive him, because YHWH’s anger and His jealousy will then smoke against that man, and every curse that is written in this scroll will weigh on him, and YHWH will wipe out his name from under the skies.

tex.original: \hDtrA{לֹא יֹאבֶה יְהֹוָה סְלֹחַ לוֹ כִּי אָז יֶעְשַׁן אַף יְהֹוָה וְקִנְאָתוֹ בָּאִישׁ הַהוּא וְרָבְצָה בּוֹ כּל הָאָלָה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּסֵּפֶר הַזֶּה וּמָחָה יְהֹוָה אֶת שְׁמוֹ מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמָיִם׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrA{
		YHWH will not be willing to forgive him, because YHWH’s
		anger and His jealousy will then smoke against that man,
		and every curse that is written in this scroll will weigh
		on him, and YHWH will wipe out his name from under the
		skies.
	}

verses.original: וְהִבְדִּילוֹ יְהֹוָה לְרָעָה מִכֹּל שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּכֹל אָלוֹת הַבְּרִית הַכְּתוּבָה בְּסֵפֶר הַתּוֹרָה הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: And YHWH will separate him from all of Israel’s tribes for bad, according to all the curses of the covenant that is written in this scroll of instruction.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְהִבְדִּילוֹ יְהֹוָה לְרָעָה מִכֹּל שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּכֹל אָלוֹת הַבְּרִית הַכְּתוּבָה בְּסֵפֶר הַתּוֹרָה הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: וְאָמַר הַדּוֹר הָאַחֲרוֹן בְּנֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר יָקוּמוּ מֵאַחֲרֵיכֶם וְהַנּכְרִי אֲשֶׁר יָבֹא מֵאֶרֶץ רְחוֹקָה וְרָאוּ אֶת מַכּוֹת הָאָרֶץ הַהִוא וְאֶת תַּחֲלֻאֶיהָ אֲשֶׁר חִלָּה יְהֹוָה בָּהּ׃
verses.english: “And a later generation will say—your children who will come up after you, and the foreigner who will come from a far land, when they’ll see that land’s plagues and its illnesses that YHWH put in it,

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְאָמַר הַדּוֹר הָאַחֲרוֹן בְּנֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר יָקוּמוּ מֵאַחֲרֵיכֶם וְהַנּכְרִי אֲשֶׁר יָבֹא מֵאֶרֶץ רְחוֹקָה וְרָאוּ אֶת מַכּוֹת הָאָרֶץ הַהִוא וְאֶת תַּחֲלֻאֶיהָ אֲשֶׁר חִלָּה יְהֹוָה בָּהּ׃}

verses.original: גּפְרִית וָמֶלַח שְׂרֵפָה כל אַרְצָהּ לֹא תִזָּרַע וְלֹא תַצְמִחַ וְלֹא יַעֲלֶה בָהּ כּל עֵשֶׂב כְּמַהְפֵּכַת סְדֹם וַעֲמֹרָה אַדְמָה (וצביים) [וּצְבוֹיִם] אֲשֶׁר הָפַךְ יְהֹוָה בְּאַפּוֹ וּבַחֲמָתוֹ׃
verses.english: brimstone and salt, all the land a burning, it won’t be seeded and won’t grow, and not any vegetation will come up in it, like the overturning of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which YHWH overturned in His anger and His fury—
verses.commentary: Qere Ketiv.

tex.original: \hDtrB{גּפְרִית וָמֶלַח שְׂרֵפָה כל אַרְצָהּ לֹא תִזָּרַע וְלֹא תַצְמִחַ וְלֹא יַעֲלֶה בָהּ כּל עֵשֶׂב כְּמַהְפֵּכַת סְדֹם וַעֲמֹרָה אַדְמָה (וצביים) [וּצְבוֹיִם] אֲשֶׁר הָפַךְ יְהֹוָה בְּאַפּוֹ וּבַחֲמָתוֹ׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrB{
		brimstone and salt, all the land a burning, it won’t be
		seeded and won’t grow, and not any vegetation will come up
		in it, like the overturning of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah
		and Zeboiim, which YHWH overturned in His anger and His
		fury—
	}

verses.original: וְאָמְרוּ כּל הַגּוֹיִם עַל מֶה עָשָׂה יְהֹוָה כָּכָה לָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת מֶה חֳרִי הָאַף הַגָּדוֹל הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: and all the nations will say, ‘For what did YHWH do something like this to this land? What is this big flaring of anger?’

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְאָמְרוּ כּל הַגּוֹיִם עַל מֶה עָשָׂה יְהֹוָה כָּכָה לָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת מֶה חֳרִי הָאַף הַגָּדוֹל הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: וְאָמְרוּ עַל אֲשֶׁר עָזְבוּ אֶת בְּרִית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵי אֲבֹתָם אֲשֶׁר כָּרַת עִמָּם בְּהוֹצִיאוֹ אֹתָם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃
verses.english: “And they’ll say, ‘For the fact that they left the covenant of YHWH, their fathers’ God, which He made with them when He brought them out from the land of Egypt.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְאָמְרוּ עַל אֲשֶׁר עָזְבוּ אֶת בְּרִית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵי אֲבֹתָם אֲשֶׁר כָּרַת עִמָּם בְּהוֹצִיאוֹ אֹתָם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּלְכוּ וַיַּעַבְדוּ אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ לָהֶם אֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר לֹא יְדָעוּם וְלֹא חָלַק לָהֶם׃
verses.english: And they went and served other gods and bowed to them, gods whom they hadn’t known and He hadn’t allocated to them.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וַיֵּלְכוּ וַיַּעַבְדוּ אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ לָהֶם אֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר לֹא יְדָעוּם וְלֹא חָלַק לָהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיִּחַר אַף יְהֹוָה בָּאָרֶץ הַהִוא לְהָבִיא עָלֶיהָ אֶת כּל הַקְּלָלָה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּסֵּפֶר הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: And YHWH’s anger flared at that land, to bring over it every curse that was written in this scroll.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וַיִּחַר אַף יְהֹוָה בָּאָרֶץ הַהִוא לְהָבִיא עָלֶיהָ אֶת כּל הַקְּלָלָה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּסֵּפֶר הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּתְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה מֵעַל אַדְמָתָם בְּאַף וּבְחֵמָה וּבְקֶצֶף גָּדוֹל וַיַּשְׁלִכֵם אֶל אֶרֶץ אַחֶרֶת כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: And YHWH plucked them from their land in anger and in fury and in great rage, and He threw them into another land, as it is this day.’

tex.original: \hDtrB{וַיִּתְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה מֵעַל אַדְמָתָם בְּאַף וּבְחֵמָה וּבְקֶצֶף גָּדוֹל וַיַּשְׁלִכֵם אֶל אֶרֶץ אַחֶרֶת כַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: הַנִּסְתָּרֹת לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְהַנִּגְלֹת לָנוּ וּלְבָנֵינוּ עַד עוֹלָם לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת כּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת׃
verses.english: “The hidden things belong to YHWH, our God, and the revealed things belong to us and to our children forever, to do all the words of this instruction.

tex.original: \hDtrA{הַנִּסְתָּרֹת לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְהַנִּגְלֹת לָנוּ וּלְבָנֵינוּ עַד עוֹלָם לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת כּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		The hidden things belong to YHWH. Moses tells the people that there are
%		things that are solely in the divine realm, hidden from humans. Humans’
%		task is here in this world: to live a certain kind of life. He breaks
%		off from this matter and turns to a discussion of future exile and
%		return to God (30:1–10). Then he returns to this picture of what humans
%		must do, and how it is not something enigmatic, in v. 11.
%	}

verses.original: וְהָיָה כִי יָבֹאוּ עָלֶיךָ כּל הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה הַבְּרָכָה וְהַקְּלָלָה אֲשֶׁר נָתַתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ וַהֲשֵׁבֹתָ אֶל לְבָבֶךָ בְּכל הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר הִדִּיחֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ שָׁמָּה׃
verses.english: And it will be, when all these things, the blessing and the curse that I’ve put in front of you, will come upon you, and you’ll store it in your heart among the nations to which YHWH, your God, has driven you,

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְהָיָה כִי יָבֹאוּ עָלֶיךָ כּל הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה הַבְּרָכָה וְהַקְּלָלָה אֲשֶׁר נָתַתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ וַהֲשֵׁבֹתָ אֶל לְבָבֶךָ בְּכל הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר הִדִּיחֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ שָׁמָּה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		your God has driven you. The word “driven” is ironic here. It has been
%		used three times until now, always referring to persons who would drive
%		Israelites away from their God (Deut 13:6,11,14). But now it describes
%		how YHWH drives Israel away to other lands because of Israel’s apostasy.
%		The term is thus another allusion to the fact of divine punishment to
%		fit the crime, which is to say: there is justice.
%	}

verses.original: וְשַׁבְתָּ עַד יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְשָׁמַעְתָּ בְקֹלוֹ כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם אַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ בְּכל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכל נַפְשֶׁךָ׃
verses.english: and you’ll come back to YHWH, your God, and listen to His voice, according to everything that I command you today, you and your children, with all your heart and with all your soul,

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְשַׁבְתָּ עַד יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְשָׁמַעְתָּ בְקֹלוֹ כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם אַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ בְּכל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכל נַפְשֶׁךָ׃}

verses.original: וְשָׁב יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת שְׁבוּתְךָ וְרִחֲמֶךָ וְשָׁב וְקִבֶּצְךָ מִכּל הָעַמִּים אֲשֶׁר הֱפִיצְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ שָׁמָּה׃
verses.english: that YHWH, your God, will bring back your captivity and be merciful to you. And He’ll come back and gather you from all the peoples to which YHWH, your God, has scattered you.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְשָׁב יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת שְׁבוּתְךָ וְרִחֲמֶךָ וְשָׁב וְקִבֶּצְךָ מִכּל הָעַמִּים אֲשֶׁר הֱפִיצְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ שָׁמָּה׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		bring back your captivity. This expression occurs about twenty-five
%		times in the Tanak. It is grammatically unclear. The verb
%		(b) would normally be in the Hiphil, but here (and
%		usually) it is in the intransitive Qal. The noun may reflect the root
%		wb, “bring back” (making it a cognate accusative with the verb),
%		or it may reflect the root bh, “captive.” On the former root, the
%		phrase would mean “to produce a coming back.” On the latter root, it
%		would mean “to bring back a captivity.” These two meanings are very
%		close to each other in any case. Those who take this phrase to mean
%		figuratively “to restore your fortunes” have a good parallel in Job
%		42:10; but all the occurrences in Jeremiah, which is linked closely with
%		Deuteronomy, fit the meaning of “coming back” or “captivity” far better.
%		Note especially Jer 30:16–23 and 48:46–47, in which this expression
%		occurs in proximity to the related word for captivity: ebî.
%	}

verses.original: אִם יִהְיֶה נִדַּחֲךָ בִּקְצֵה הַשָּׁמָיִם מִשָּׁם יְקַבֶּצְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וּמִשָּׁם יִקָּחֶךָ׃
verses.english: If you’ll be driven to the end of the skies, YHWH, your God, will gather you from there, and He’ll take you from there.

tex.original: \hDtrB{אִם יִהְיֶה נִדַּחֲךָ בִּקְצֵה הַשָּׁמָיִם מִשָּׁם יְקַבֶּצְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וּמִשָּׁם יִקָּחֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וֶהֱבִיאֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יָרְשׁוּ אֲבֹתֶיךָ וִירִשְׁתָּהּ וְהֵיטִבְךָ וְהִרְבְּךָ מֵאֲבֹתֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And YHWH, your God, will bring you to the land that your fathers possessed, and you’ll take possession of it, and He’ll be good to you and multiply you more than your fathers.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וֶהֱבִיאֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יָרְשׁוּ אֲבֹתֶיךָ וִירִשְׁתָּהּ וְהֵיטִבְךָ וְהִרְבְּךָ מֵאֲבֹתֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: וּמָל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת לְבָבְךָ וְאֶת לְבַב זַרְעֶךָ לְאַהֲבָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכל נַפְשְׁךָ לְמַעַן חַיֶּיךָ׃
verses.english: And YHWH, your God, will circumcise your heart and your seed’s heart so as to love YHWH, your God, with all your heart and with all your soul so that you’ll live.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וּמָל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת לְבָבְךָ וְאֶת לְבַב זַרְעֶךָ לְאַהֲבָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכל נַפְשְׁךָ לְמַעַן חַיֶּיךָ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		God will circumcise your heart. Earlier, Moses directs the people to
%		circumcise their hearts themselves (see Deut 10:16 and the comment
%		there), but now he speaks of God circumcising their hearts for them. The
%		difference is that now he is speaking of a future condition: the people
%		will have violated the covenant, suffered the curses, and turned back to
%		their God; and God, in response, will bring them back and then will
%		circumcise their hearts. This in turn will enable them to love the deity
%		with all their hearts and souls—which Moses had commanded them to do
%		earlier as well. The divine-human relationship is pictured as mutual.
%		Humans require the experience of being away from their God, on their
%		own. And then, more experienced, more understanding, having suffered and
%		grown, humans look to God anew. And then the new encounter with the
%		divine transforms them. Footnote 30:6. your seed’s heart. Meaning: the
%		hearts of your progeny.
%	}

verses.original: וְנָתַן יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֵת כּל הָאָלוֹת הָאֵלֶּה עַל אֹיְבֶיךָ וְעַל שֹׂנְאֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר רְדָפוּךָ׃
verses.english: And YHWH, your God, will put all these curses on your enemies and on those who hate you who have pursued you.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְנָתַן יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֵת כּל הָאָלוֹת הָאֵלֶּה עַל אֹיְבֶיךָ וְעַל שֹׂנְאֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר רְדָפוּךָ׃}

verses.original: וְאַתָּה תָשׁוּב וְשָׁמַעְתָּ בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה וְעָשִׂיתָ אֶת כּל מִצְוֺתָיו אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם׃
verses.english: And you’ll come back and listen to YHWH’s voice and do all His commandments that I command you today.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְאַתָּה תָשׁוּב וְשָׁמַעְתָּ בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה וְעָשִׂיתָ אֶת כּל מִצְוֺתָיו אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם׃}

verses.original: וְהוֹתִירְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכֹל מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶךָ בִּפְרִי בִטְנְךָ וּבִפְרִי בְהֶמְתְּךָ וּבִפְרִי אַדְמָתְךָ לְטֹבָה כִּי יָשׁוּב יְהֹוָה לָשׂוּשׂ עָלֶיךָ לְטוֹב כַּאֲשֶׁר שָׂשׂ עַל אֲבֹתֶיךָ׃
verses.english: And YHWH, your God, will give you extra of all your hand’s work, of the fruit of your womb and of the fruit of your animals and the fruit of your land for good. Because YHWH will come back to have satisfaction over you for good as He had satisfaction over your fathers,

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְהוֹתִירְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכֹל מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶךָ בִּפְרִי בִטְנְךָ וּבִפְרִי בְהֶמְתְּךָ וּבִפְרִי אַדְמָתְךָ לְטֹבָה כִּי יָשׁוּב יְהֹוָה לָשׂוּשׂ עָלֶיךָ לְטוֹב כַּאֲשֶׁר שָׂשׂ עַל אֲבֹתֶיךָ׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrB{
		And YHWH, your God, will give you extra of all your hand’s
		work, of the fruit of your womb and of the fruit of your
		animals and the fruit of your land for good. Because YHWH
		will come back to have satisfaction over you for good as
		He had satisfaction over your fathers,
	}

verses.original: כִּי תִשְׁמַע בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לִשְׁמֹר מִצְוֺתָיו וְחֻקֹּתָיו הַכְּתוּבָה בְּסֵפֶר הַתּוֹרָה הַזֶּה כִּי תָשׁוּב אֶל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכל נַפְשֶׁךָ׃
verses.english: when you’ll listen to the voice of YHWH, your God, to observe His commandments and His laws, written in this scroll of instruction, when you’ll come back to YHWH, your God, with all your heart and with all your soul.

tex.original: \hDtrB{כִּי תִשְׁמַע בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לִשְׁמֹר מִצְוֺתָיו וְחֻקֹּתָיו הַכְּתוּבָה בְּסֵפֶר הַתּוֹרָה הַזֶּה כִּי תָשׁוּב אֶל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכל נַפְשֶׁךָ׃}

verses.original: כִּי הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לֹא נִפְלֵאת הִוא מִמְּךָ וְלֹא רְחֹקָה הִוא׃
verses.english: “Because this commandment that I command you today: it’s not too wondrous for you, and it’s not too far.

tex.original: \hDtrA{כִּי הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לֹא נִפְלֵאת הִוא מִמְּךָ וְלֹא רְחֹקָה הִוא׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		it’s not too wondrous for you. Now Moses finishes what he started to say
%		ten verses earlier about the hidden things belonging to God and the
%		revealed things belonging to humans (29:28). In one of the most
%		beautiful passages in the Torah (vv. 11–14), he explains what this
%		meant: The commandments are not enigmatic, they do not reside in a
%		distant realm, and they do not require an intermediary. They are already
%		made known. And they are within a human’s ability to do.
%	}

verses.original: לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא לֵאמֹר מִי יַעֲלֶה לָּנוּ הַשָּׁמַיְמָה וְיִקָּחֶהָ לָּנוּ וְיַשְׁמִעֵנוּ אֹתָהּ וְנַעֲשֶׂנָּה׃
verses.english: It’s not in the skies, that one would say, ‘Who will go up for us to the skies and get it for us and enable us to hear it so we’ll do it?’

tex.original: \hDtrA{לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא לֵאמֹר מִי יַעֲלֶה לָּנוּ הַשָּׁמַיְמָה וְיִקָּחֶהָ לָּנוּ וְיַשְׁמִעֵנוּ אֹתָהּ וְנַעֲשֶׂנָּה׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא מֵעֵבֶר לַיָּם הִוא לֵאמֹר מִי יַעֲבר לָנוּ אֶל עֵבֶר הַיָּם וְיִקָּחֶהָ לָּנוּ וְיַשְׁמִעֵנוּ אֹתָהּ וְנַעֲשֶׂנָּה׃
verses.english: And it’s not across the sea, that one would say, ‘Who will cross for us, across the sea, and get it for us and enable us to hear it so we’ll do it?’

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְלֹא מֵעֵבֶר לַיָּם הִוא לֵאמֹר מִי יַעֲבר לָנוּ אֶל עֵבֶר הַיָּם וְיִקָּחֶהָ לָּנוּ וְיַשְׁמִעֵנוּ אֹתָהּ וְנַעֲשֶׂנָּה׃}

verses.original: כִּי קָרוֹב אֵלֶיךָ הַדָּבָר מְאֹד בְּפִיךָ וּבִלְבָבְךָ לַעֲשֹׂתוֹ׃
verses.english: But the thing is very close to you, in your mouth, and in your heart, to do it.

tex.original: \hDtrA{כִּי קָרוֹב אֵלֶיךָ הַדָּבָר מְאֹד בְּפִיךָ וּבִלְבָבְךָ לַעֲשֹׂתוֹ׃}

verses.original: רְאֵה נָתַתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ הַיּוֹם אֶת הַחַיִּים וְאֶת הַטּוֹב וְאֶת הַמָּוֶת וְאֶת הָרָע׃
verses.english: “See: I’ve put in front of you today life and good, and death and bad,

tex.original: \hDtrB{רְאֵה נָתַתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ הַיּוֹם אֶת הַחַיִּים וְאֶת הַטּוֹב וְאֶת הַמָּוֶת וְאֶת הָרָע׃}

verses.original: אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לְאַהֲבָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לָלֶכֶת בִּדְרָכָיו וְלִשְׁמֹר מִצְוֺתָיו וְחֻקֹּתָיו וּמִשְׁפָּטָיו וְחָיִיתָ וְרָבִיתָ וּבֵרַכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה בָא שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃
verses.english: in that I command you today to love YHWH, your God, to go in His ways and to observe His commandments and His laws and His judgments so you’ll live and multiply and bless YHWH, your God, in the land to which you’re coming to take possession of it.

tex.original: \hDtrB{אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם לְאַהֲבָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לָלֶכֶת בִּדְרָכָיו וְלִשְׁמֹר מִצְוֺתָיו וְחֻקֹּתָיו וּמִשְׁפָּטָיו וְחָיִיתָ וְרָבִיתָ וּבֵרַכְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בָּאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה בָא שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrB{
		in that I command you today to love YHWH, your God, to go
		in His ways and to observe His commandments and His laws
		and His judgments so you’ll live and multiply and bless
		YHWH, your God, in the land to which you’re coming to take
		possession of it.
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		so you’ll live and multiply. This is a change of wording from the
%		beginning of the Torah, where the command is to “be fruitful and
%		multiply” (Gen 1:28). The command to grow in numbers is for the purpose
%		of life. As the human population grows to the point that its number is a
%		threat to life, humankind and its leaders need enormous wisdom to
%		determine what to do. The wording there in Genesis is: “And God blessed
%		them, and God said to them, ‘Be fruitful and multiply … ’” (Gen 1:28).
%		That first commandment of the Torah is thus presented not as a strict
%		order, but as a blessing. And here at the end of the Torah as well, the
%		text is: “so you’ll live and multiply and bless YHWH.” In the Torah, the
%		creator blesses humans with the opportunity to grow, and humans will
%		bless their creator for it once it is fulfilled. The Bible’s first
%		commandment is now becoming humankind’s greatest challenge.
%	}

verses.original: וְאִם יִפְנֶה לְבָבְךָ וְלֹא תִשְׁמָע וְנִדַּחְתָּ וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתָ לֵאלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וַעֲבַדְתָּם׃
verses.english: But if your heart will turn away, and you won’t listen, and you’ll be driven so that you’ll bow to other gods and serve them,

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְאִם יִפְנֶה לְבָבְךָ וְלֹא תִשְׁמָע וְנִדַּחְתָּ וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתָ לֵאלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וַעֲבַדְתָּם׃}

verses.original: הִגַּדְתִּי לָכֶם הַיּוֹם כִּי אָבֹד תֹּאבֵדוּן לֹא תַאֲרִיכֻן יָמִים עַל הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה עֹבֵר אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן לָבוֹא שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃
verses.english: I’ve told you today that you’ll perish. You won’t extend days on the land to which you’re crossing the Jordan to come to take possession of it.

tex.original: \hDtrB{הִגַּדְתִּי לָכֶם הַיּוֹם כִּי אָבֹד תֹּאבֵדוּן לֹא תַאֲרִיכֻן יָמִים עַל הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה עֹבֵר אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן לָבוֹא שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃}

verses.original: הַעִדֹתִי בָכֶם הַיּוֹם אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת הָאָרֶץ הַחַיִּים וְהַמָּוֶת נָתַתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ הַבְּרָכָה וְהַקְּלָלָה וּבָחַרְתָּ בַּחַיִּים לְמַעַן תִּחְיֶה אַתָּה וְזַרְעֶךָ׃
verses.english: I call the skies and the earth to witness regarding you today: I’ve put life and death in front of you, blessing and curse. And you shall choose life, so you’ll live, you and your seed,

tex.original: \hDtrB{הַעִדֹתִי בָכֶם הַיּוֹם אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת הָאָרֶץ הַחַיִּים וְהַמָּוֶת נָתַתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ הַבְּרָכָה וְהַקְּלָלָה וּבָחַרְתָּ בַּחַיִּים לְמַעַן תִּחְיֶה אַתָּה וְזַרְעֶךָ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		choose life. The theme of the path to life began early in Moses’ speech
%		(Deut 4:1) and culminates here in the last words of the speech. This
%		focus at the conclusion of the Torah returns us to the Torah’s opening:
%		the loss of the tree of life. Humans lose access to the tree of life as
%		the price of having gained access to the tree of knowledge of good and
%		bad. Now the people are told, “I’ve put in front of you life and good,
%		blessing and curse.” Using the knowledge of good and bad, and choosing
%		to do good, is the path back to life—not necessarily eternal life
%		(though who knows?), but meaningful life, fulfilling life. As the book
%		of Proverbs says about knowledge and wisdom: “It is a tree of life.” And
%		Jews sing this verse from Proverbs each Sabbath after reading the Torah
%		and returning it to the ark.
%	}

verses.original: לְאַהֲבָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לִשְׁמֹעַ בְּקֹלוֹ וּלְדבְקָה בוֹ כִּי הוּא חַיֶּיךָ וְאֹרֶךְ יָמֶיךָ לָשֶׁבֶת עַל הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע יְהֹוָה לַאֲבֹתֶיךָ לְאַבְרָהָם לְיִצְחָק וּלְיַעֲקֹב לָתֵת לָהֶם׃
verses.english: to love YHWH, your God, to listen to His voice and to cling to Him, because He is your life and the extension of your days to reside on the land that YHWH swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give to them.”

tex.original: \hDtrB{לְאַהֲבָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לִשְׁמֹעַ בְּקֹלוֹ וּלְדבְקָה בוֹ כִּי הוּא חַיֶּיךָ וְאֹרֶךְ יָמֶיךָ לָשֶׁבֶת עַל הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע יְהֹוָה לַאֲבֹתֶיךָ לְאַבְרָהָם לְיִצְחָק וּלְיַעֲקֹב לָתֵת לָהֶם׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrB{
		to love YHWH, your God, to listen to His voice and to
		cling to Him, because He is your life and the extension of
		your days to reside on the land that YHWH swore to your
		fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give to
		them.”
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		to cling to Him. “Cling” is the same term that is used for man’s
%		attachment to woman at the beginning of the Torah (Gen 2:24). This is
%		part of a string of terms in this passage (vv. 15–20) that call to mind
%		the opening chapters of the Torah: life, death, good and bad, the skies
%		and earth, the ground, the day (cf. “in the day” and “in the day you eat
%		from it,” Gen 2:4,17), “your seed,” be fruitful, to give, to tell, to
%		command (cf. Gen 3:11), to watch (or observe, Hebrew mr), and to
%		listen to the voice (of God; cf. “You listened to your woman’s voice,”
%		Gen 3:17). And these are preceded by references to fruit (Deut 30:9),
%		and to the skies and the sea (30:12–13). This cluster of language here
%		in the last sentences of Moses’ address forms a great connection back to
%		the start of Genesis and a reminder of the unity of the Torah. Footnote
%		30:20. He is your life. This can also be understood to mean “It is your
%		life.” Translators are split on this. The former means that Moses is
%		saying that God is the people’s life and the source of their being in
%		their land a long time. The latter means that the people’s choice to
%		love, listen, and cling to God is their life and the source of lengthy
%		time in the land. That is, the question is whether it is God or it is
%		people’s feeling about God that brings this about. I do not know which
%		is correct.
%	}

verses.original: וַיֵּלֶךְ מֹשֶׁה וַיְדַבֵּר אֶת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה אֶל כּל יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And Moses went and spoke these things to all Israel.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיֵּלֶךְ מֹשֶׁה וַיְדַבֵּר אֶת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה אֶל כּל יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		And Moses went. Went where? The Septuagint and Qumran texts have “And
%		Moses finished speaking all these things”—reading Hebrew
%		(finished) rather than  (went), reversing the last two letters.
%		This makes better sense. It also adds a wordplay on his finishing
%		() in v. 1 and his saying “I’m not able () to go out and
%		come in anymore” in v. 2.
%	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵהֶם בֶּן מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה אָנֹכִי הַיּוֹם לֹא אוּכַל עוֹד לָצֵאת וְלָבוֹא וַיהֹוָה אָמַר אֵלַי לֹא תַעֲבֹר אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: And he said to them, “I’m a hundred twenty years old today. I’m not able to go out and come in anymore. And YHWH said to me, ‘You shall not cross this Jordan.’

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵהֶם בֶּן מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה אָנֹכִי הַיּוֹם לֹא אוּכַל עוֹד לָצֵאת וְלָבוֹא וַיהֹוָה אָמַר אֵלַי לֹא תַעֲבֹר אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ הוּא עֹבֵר לְפָנֶיךָ הוּא יַשְׁמִיד אֶת הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה מִלְּפָנֶיךָ וִירִשְׁתָּם יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הוּא עֹבֵר לְפָנֶיךָ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: YHWH, your God: He is crossing in front of you. He’ll destroy these nations in front of you, and you’ll dispossess them. Joshua: he is crossing in front of you, as YHWH has spoken.

tex.original: \hDtrA{יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ הוּא עֹבֵר לְפָנֶיךָ הוּא יַשְׁמִיד אֶת הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה מִלְּפָנֶיךָ וִירִשְׁתָּם יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הוּא עֹבֵר לְפָנֶיךָ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְעָשָׂה יְהֹוָה לָהֶם כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לְסִיחוֹן וּלְעוֹג מַלְכֵי הָאֱמֹרִי וּלְאַרְצָם אֲשֶׁר הִשְׁמִיד אֹתָם׃
verses.english: And YHWH will do to them as He did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, that He destroyed them.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וְעָשָׂה יְהֹוָה לָהֶם כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לְסִיחוֹן וּלְעוֹג מַלְכֵי הָאֱמֹרִי וּלְאַרְצָם אֲשֶׁר הִשְׁמִיד אֹתָם׃}

verses.original: וּנְתָנָם יְהֹוָה לִפְנֵיכֶם וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לָהֶם כְּכל הַמִּצְוָה אֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִי אֶתְכֶם׃
verses.english: And YHWH will put them in front of you, and you shall do to them according to all of the commandment that I’ve commanded you.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וּנְתָנָם יְהֹוָה לִפְנֵיכֶם וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לָהֶם כְּכל הַמִּצְוָה אֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִי אֶתְכֶם׃}

verses.original: חִזְקוּ וְאִמְצוּ אַל תִּירְאוּ וְאַל תַּעַרְצוּ מִפְּנֵיהֶם כִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ הוּא הַהֹלֵךְ עִמָּךְ לֹא יַרְפְּךָ וְלֹא יַעַזְבֶךָּ׃
verses.english: Be strong and be bold. Don’t be afraid and don’t be scared in front of them, because YHWH, your God: He is the one going with you. He won’t let you down and won’t leave you.”

tex.original: \hDtrA{חִזְקוּ וְאִמְצוּ אַל תִּירְאוּ וְאַל תַּעַרְצוּ מִפְּנֵיהֶם כִּי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ הוּא הַהֹלֵךְ עִמָּךְ לֹא יַרְפְּךָ וְלֹא יַעַזְבֶךָּ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקְרָא מֹשֶׁה לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו לְעֵינֵי כל יִשְׂרָאֵל חֲזַק וֶאֱמָץ כִּי אַתָּה תָּבוֹא אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע יְהֹוָה לַאֲבֹתָם לָתֵת לָהֶם וְאַתָּה תַּנְחִילֶנָּה אוֹתָם׃
verses.english: And Moses called Joshua and said to him before the eyes of all Israel, “Be strong and be bold, because you will come with this people to the land that YHWH swore to their fathers to give to them, and you will get it for them as a legacy.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיִּקְרָא מֹשֶׁה לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו לְעֵינֵי כל יִשְׂרָאֵל חֲזַק וֶאֱמָץ כִּי אַתָּה תָּבוֹא אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע יְהֹוָה לַאֲבֹתָם לָתֵת לָהֶם וְאַתָּה תַּנְחִילֶנָּה אוֹתָם׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrA{
		And Moses called Joshua and said to him before the eyes of
		all Israel, “Be strong and be bold, because you will come
		with this people to the land that YHWH swore to their
		fathers to give to them, and you will get it for them as a
		legacy.
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Be strong and be bold … you will get it for them as a legacy. This,
%		finally, is the culmination of what Moses told the people in chapter 3.
%		He had told them that God was angry at him, that he was not permitted to
%		enter the land, and that God told him to “command Joshua and strengthen
%		him and make him bold, because … he will get them the land that you’ll
%		see as a legacy” (3:28). Moses has now instructed the people in the laws
%		and exhorted them to be faithful to the covenant, and so he turns to the
%		task that he was assigned: he passes the leadership to Joshua. Note that
%		it is not just that Moses dies and Joshua replaces him. Rather, during
%		his lifetime, publicly, Moses himself identifies Joshua as his
%		successor, charges him with his task, and encourages him to be
%		successful. Although one can easily imagine Moses envying Joshua, who is
%		replacing him for the fulfillment of the promises, Moses acts in
%		Joshua’s favor: preparing him and enhancing his stature in the people’s
%		eyes. One who begrudges his successor does not understand time and
%		history.
%	}

verses.original: וַיהֹוָה הוּא הַהֹלֵךְ לְפָנֶיךָ הוּא יִהְיֶה עִמָּךְ לֹא יַרְפְּךָ וְלֹא יַעַזְבֶךָּ לֹא תִירָא וְלֹא תֵחָת׃
verses.english: And YHWH: He is the one who is going in front of you. He will be with you. He won’t let you down and won’t leave you. You shall not fear, and you shall not be dismayed.”

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיהֹוָה הוּא הַהֹלֵךְ לְפָנֶיךָ הוּא יִהְיֶה עִמָּךְ לֹא יַרְפְּךָ וְלֹא יַעַזְבֶךָּ לֹא תִירָא וְלֹא תֵחָת׃}

verses.original: וַיִּכְתֹּב מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת וַיִּתְּנָהּ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים בְּנֵי לֵוִי הַנֹּשְׂאִים אֶת אֲרוֹן בְּרִית יְהֹוָה וְאֶל כּל זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And Moses wrote this instruction and gave it to the priests, sons of Levi, who were carrying the ark of YHWH’s covenant and to all of Israel’s elders.

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיִּכְתֹּב מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת וַיִּתְּנָהּ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים בְּנֵי לֵוִי הַנֹּשְׂאִים אֶת אֲרוֹן בְּרִית יְהֹוָה וְאֶל כּל זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		And Moses wrote this instruction (and 31:24. “And it was when Moses
%		finished writing the words of this instruction on a scroll”). This
%		“instruction” (Hebrew tôrh) does not refer to the entire five
%		books, which came to be known as the Torah long after this chapter was
%		written. Those who began claiming that Moses was the author of the
%		entire Torah created much confusion and misinformation by claiming more
%		for Moses than the Torah itself ascribed to him. It became a firmly
%		established doctrine by the rabbinic period, and many great teachers,
%		including Rashi and Ramban, followed it. Ibn Ezra raised subtle doubts
%		about it, Spinoza openly challenged it, and Jewish, as well as
%		Christian, scholars came to reject it in the nineteenth and twentieth
%		centuries. Orthodox Jews still accept it. The instruction that Moses
%		writes here appears to be most of the law code that begins in
%		Deuteronomy 12 and ends at 26:15. It may also be understood to include
%		the list of blessings and curses in Deuteronomy 28. That concluding list
%		of curses especially would account for the strong reaction that is
%		ascribed to King Josiah when he hears the words of the scroll of the
%		Torah centuries later (see the comment on 31:26).
%	}

verses.original: וַיְצַו מֹשֶׁה אוֹתָם לֵאמֹר מִקֵּץ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים בְּמֹעֵד שְׁנַת הַשְּׁמִטָּה בְּחַג הַסֻּכּוֹת׃
verses.english: And Moses commanded them, saying, “At the end of seven years, at the appointed time of the year of the remission, on the Festival of Booths,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיְצַו מֹשֶׁה אוֹתָם לֵאמֹר מִקֵּץ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים בְּמֹעֵד שְׁנַת הַשְּׁמִטָּה בְּחַג הַסֻּכּוֹת׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		seven years. The biblical requirement was to read “this torah” (the law
%		code of Deuteronomy) once every seven years, on the holiday of Sukkot.
%		Later the Jewish practice became to read the entire Torah (all of the
%		Five Books of Moses), once every year or every three years, and in
%		weekly portions rather than all at once. Footnote 31:10. the remission.
%		See Deut 15:1ff.
%	}

verses.original: בְּבוֹא כל יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵרָאוֹת אֶת פְּנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחָר תִּקְרָא אֶת הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת נֶגֶד כּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאזְנֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: when all Israel comes to appear before YHWH, your God, in the place that He will choose, you shall read this instruction in front of all Israel in their ears.

tex.original: \hDtrA{בְּבוֹא כל יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵרָאוֹת אֶת פְּנֵי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחָר תִּקְרָא אֶת הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת נֶגֶד כּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאזְנֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: הַקְהֵל אֶת הָעָם הָאֲנָשִׁים וְהַנָּשִׁים וְהַטַּף וְגֵרְךָ אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ לְמַעַן יִשְׁמְעוּ וּלְמַעַן יִלְמְדוּ וְיָרְאוּ אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וְשָׁמְרוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת כּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת׃
verses.english: Assemble the people—the men and the women and the infants and your alien who is in your gates—so they will listen and so they will learn and will fear YHWH, your God, and they will be watchful to do all the words of this instruction.

tex.original: \hDtrA{הַקְהֵל אֶת הָעָם הָאֲנָשִׁים וְהַנָּשִׁים וְהַטַּף וְגֵרְךָ אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ לְמַעַן יִשְׁמְעוּ וּלְמַעַן יִלְמְדוּ וְיָרְאוּ אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וְשָׁמְרוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת כּל דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrA{
		Assemble the people—the men and the women and the infants
		and your alien who is in your gates—so they will listen
		and so they will learn and will fear YHWH, your God, and
		they will be watchful to do all the words of this
		instruction.
	}

verses.original: וּבְנֵיהֶם אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָדְעוּ יִשְׁמְעוּ וְלָמְדוּ לְיִרְאָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם כּל הַיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם חַיִּים עַל הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם עֹבְרִים אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃
verses.english: And their children who have not known will listen and learn to fear YHWH, your God, all the days that you’re living on the land to which you’re crossing the Jordan to take possession of it.”

tex.original: \hDtrA{וּבְנֵיהֶם אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָדְעוּ יִשְׁמְעוּ וְלָמְדוּ לְיִרְאָה אֶת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם כּל הַיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם חַיִּים עַל הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם עֹבְרִים אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה הֵן קָרְבוּ יָמֶיךָ לָמוּת קְרָא אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְהִתְיַצְּבוּ בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וַאֲצַוֶּנּוּ וַיֵּלֶךְ מֹשֶׁה וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ וַיִּתְיַצְּבוּ בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “Here, your days to die have come close. Call Joshua, and stand up in the Tent of Meeting, and I’ll command him.” And Moses and Joshua went and stood up in the Tent of Meeting.

tex.original: \hE{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה הֵן קָרְבוּ יָמֶיךָ לָמוּת קְרָא אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְהִתְיַצְּבוּ בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וַאֲצַוֶּנּוּ וַיֵּלֶךְ מֹשֶׁה וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ וַיִּתְיַצְּבוּ בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּרָא יְהֹוָה בָּאֹהֶל בְּעַמּוּד עָנָן וַיַּעֲמֹד עַמּוּד הֶעָנָן עַל פֶּתַח הָאֹהֶל׃
verses.english: And YHWH appeared in the tent in a column of cloud, and the column of cloud stood at the entrance of the tent.

tex.original: \hE{וַיֵּרָא יְהֹוָה בָּאֹהֶל בְּעַמּוּד עָנָן וַיַּעֲמֹד עַמּוּד הֶעָנָן עַל פֶּתַח הָאֹהֶל׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה הִנְּךָ שֹׁכֵב עִם אֲבֹתֶיךָ וְקָם הָעָם הַזֶּה וְזָנָה אַחֲרֵי אֱלֹהֵי נֵכַר הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר הוּא בָא שָׁמָּה בְּקִרְבּוֹ וַעֲזָבַנִי וְהֵפֵר אֶת בְּרִיתִי אֲשֶׁר כָּרַתִּי אִתּוֹ׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Moses, “Here, when you’re lying with your fathers, this people will get up and whore after foreign gods of the land into which it is coming, and it will leave me and break my covenant that I’ve made with it.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל מֹשֶׁה הִנְּךָ שֹׁכֵב עִם אֲבֹתֶיךָ וְקָם הָעָם הַזֶּה וְזָנָה אַחֲרֵי אֱלֹהֵי נֵכַר הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר הוּא בָא שָׁמָּה בְּקִרְבּוֹ וַעֲזָבַנִי וְהֵפֵר אֶת בְּרִיתִי אֲשֶׁר כָּרַתִּי אִתּוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		it. God repeatedly speaks of the people in the singular in this
%		passage—and quotes the people as speaking of itself in the singular as
%		well: “not present in me … these evils have found me.” The hiding of the
%		face of God, which is predicted here, is understood to be the fate of
%		the entire people, not of individuals. Divine hiddenness is not an
%		individual’s unique experience, and it is not based on an individual’s
%		behavior. It is the experience of a community and possibly of an era. At
%		the time that I am writing this, it is such an era.
%	}

verses.original: וְחָרָה אַפִּי בוֹ בַיּוֹם הַהוּא וַעֲזַבְתִּים וְהִסְתַּרְתִּי פָנַי מֵהֶם וְהָיָה לֶאֱכֹל וּמְצָאֻהוּ רָעוֹת רַבּוֹת וְצָרוֹת וְאָמַר בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא הֲלֹא עַל כִּי אֵין אֱלֹהַי בְּקִרְבִּי מְצָאוּנִי הָרָעוֹת הָאֵלֶּה׃
verses.english: And my anger will flare at it on that day, and I’ll leave them, and I’ll hide my face from them, and it will become prey, and many bad things and troubles will find it. And it will say on that day, ‘Isn’t it because my God is not present in me that these evils have found me?’

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְחָרָה אַפִּי בוֹ בַיּוֹם הַהוּא וַעֲזַבְתִּים וְהִסְתַּרְתִּי פָנַי מֵהֶם וְהָיָה לֶאֱכֹל וּמְצָאֻהוּ רָעוֹת רַבּוֹת וְצָרוֹת וְאָמַר בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא הֲלֹא עַל כִּי אֵין אֱלֹהַי בְּקִרְבִּי מְצָאוּנִי הָרָעוֹת הָאֵלֶּה׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrB{
		And my anger will flare at it on that day, and I’ll leave
		them, and I’ll hide my face from them, and it will become
		prey, and many bad things and troubles will find it. And
		it will say on that day, ‘Isn’t it because my God is not
		present in me that these evils have found me?’
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		I’ll hide my face. These words come twice in the passage that contains
%		the last words that God speaks to Moses before summoning him to die.
%		They occur in the song that God tells Moses to teach the people as a
%		witness for the future as well (32:20), and this expression occurs
%		nearly thirty times more in the Tanak after that. These words here
%		predict a time in which God will be hidden. It is more frightening than
%		divine punishment: It is one thing for a parent to punish a child; it is
%		far worse if the parent becomes hidden from the child, so the child does
%		not know if the parent is present or not. The child feels vulnerable,
%		unprotected. The child cries for the parent, but there is no answer. It
%		is terrifying.
%	}

verses.original: וְאָנֹכִי הַסְתֵּר אַסְתִּיר פָּנַי בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא עַל כּל הָרָעָה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה כִּי פָנָה אֶל אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים׃
verses.english: But I: I’ll hide my face on that day over all the bad that it has done, because it turned to other gods.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְאָנֹכִי הַסְתֵּר אַסְתִּיר פָּנַי בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא עַל כּל הָרָעָה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה כִּי פָנָה אֶל אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		it. God repeatedly speaks of the people in the singular in this
%		passage—and quotes the people as speaking of itself in the singular as
%		well: “not present in me … these evils have found me.” The hiding of the
%		face of God, which is predicted here, is understood to be the fate of
%		the entire people, not of individuals. Divine hiddenness is not an
%		individual’s unique experience, and it is not based on an individual’s
%		behavior. It is the experience of a community and possibly of an era. At
%		the time that I am writing this, it is such an era. Footnote 31:18. I’ll
%		hide my face. These words come twice in the passage that contains the
%		last words that God speaks to Moses before summoning him to die. They
%		occur in the song that God tells Moses to teach the people as a witness
%		for the future as well (32:20), and this expression occurs nearly thirty
%		times more in the Tanak after that. These words here predict a time in
%		which God will be hidden. It is more frightening than divine punishment:
%		It is one thing for a parent to punish a child; it is far worse if the
%		parent becomes hidden from the child, so the child does not know if the
%		parent is present or not. The child feels vulnerable, unprotected. The
%		child cries for the parent, but there is no answer. It is terrifying.
%		The expression hestr pnîm, the hiding of the face, became
%		a known idiom in rabbinic literature, and in theological thinking to
%		this day. I have written about how it develops through the Bible (in The
%		Hidden Face of God). The Tanak’s story moves from a time of
%		extraordinary divine involvement—creation, flood, personal contact,
%		splitting sea, hearing God’s voice at Sinai—to a time in which humans
%		are left on their own. God is not pictured as speaking or appearing in
%		the books of Ezra and Nehemiah and is never mentioned in Esther. The
%		prediction at the end of the Torah comes true at the end of the Tanak.
%		Humans are left not knowing if God exists or not. Thus the Tanak tells a
%		story of a development from a world of direct communication with God to
%		the world we have known ever since: in which the existence of God is a
%		matter of faith, or doubt, or search.
%	}

verses.original: וְעַתָּה כִּתְבוּ לָכֶם אֶת הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת וְלַמְּדָהּ אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שִׂימָהּ בְּפִיהֶם לְמַעַן תִּהְיֶה לִּי הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת לְעֵד בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: So now write this song and teach it to the children of Israel. Set it in their mouths, so this song will become a witness for me among the children of Israel.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְעַתָּה כִּתְבוּ לָכֶם אֶת הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת וְלַמְּדָהּ אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שִׂימָהּ בְּפִיהֶם לְמַעַן תִּהְיֶה לִּי הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת לְעֵד בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: כִּי אֲבִיאֶנּוּ אֶל הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי לַאֲבֹתָיו זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבַשׁ וְאָכַל וְשָׂבַע וְדָשֵׁן וּפָנָה אֶל אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וַעֲבָדוּם וְנִאֲצוּנִי וְהֵפֵר אֶת בְּרִיתִי׃
verses.english: When I’ll bring it to the land that I swore to its fathers, flowing with milk and honey, and it will eat and be full and get fat and turn to other gods, and they will serve them and reject me, and it will break my covenant,

tex.original: \hDtrB{כִּי אֲבִיאֶנּוּ אֶל הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי לַאֲבֹתָיו זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבַשׁ וְאָכַל וְשָׂבַע וְדָשֵׁן וּפָנָה אֶל אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים וַעֲבָדוּם וְנִאֲצוּנִי וְהֵפֵר אֶת בְּרִיתִי׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה כִּי תִמְצֶאןָ אֹתוֹ רָעוֹת רַבּוֹת וְצָרוֹת וְעָנְתָה הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת לְפָנָיו לְעֵד כִּי לֹא תִשָּׁכַח מִפִּי זַרְעוֹ כִּי יָדַעְתִּי אֶת יִצְרוֹ אֲשֶׁר הוּא עֹשֶׂה הַיּוֹם בְּטֶרֶם אֲבִיאֶנּוּ אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי׃
verses.english: then it will be, when many bad things and troubles will find it, that this song will testify as a witness in front of it, because it won’t be forgotten from its seed’s mouth. Because I know its inclination that it is doing today even before I bring it to the land that I swore.”

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְהָיָה כִּי תִמְצֶאןָ אֹתוֹ רָעוֹת רַבּוֹת וְצָרוֹת וְעָנְתָה הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת לְפָנָיו לְעֵד כִּי לֹא תִשָּׁכַח מִפִּי זַרְעוֹ כִּי יָדַעְתִּי אֶת יִצְרוֹ אֲשֶׁר הוּא עֹשֶׂה הַיּוֹם בְּטֶרֶם אֲבִיאֶנּוּ אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrB{
		then it will be, when many bad things and troubles will
		find it, that this song will testify as a witness in front
		of it, because it won’t be forgotten from its seed’s
		mouth. Because I know its inclination that it is doing
		today even before I bring it to the land that I swore.”
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		I know its inclination. Again an essential point from the Torah’s
%		beginning returns at its conclusion. The flood story starts and ends
%		with God’s recognition that humans’ inclination is toward doing bad: “I
%		won’t curse the ground on account of humankind again, for the
%		inclination of the human heart is bad from their youth” (Gen 6:5; 8:21).
%		The word “inclination” (yer) then does not occur again in
%		the Torah until here. God states that He knows, even before the people
%		enter the land, that this will be a problem, and so He has them learn a
%		song that refers to their rebellion and to the hiding of the face of God
%		so that they will know that they were warned.
%	}

verses.original: וַיִּכְתֹּב מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא וַיְלַמְּדָהּ אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: And Moses wrote this song on that day, and he taught it to the children of Israel.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וַיִּכְתֹּב מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא וַיְלַמְּדָהּ אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיְצַו אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן וַיֹּאמֶר חֲזַק וֶאֱמָץ כִּי אַתָּה תָּבִיא אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי לָהֶם וְאָנֹכִי אֶהְיֶה עִמָּךְ׃
verses.english: And He commanded Joshua, son of Nun, and said, “Be strong and bold, because you will bring the children of Israel to the land that I swore to them, and I shall be with you.”

tex.original: \hE{וַיְצַו אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן וַיֹּאמֶר חֲזַק וֶאֱמָץ כִּי אַתָּה תָּבִיא אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי לָהֶם וְאָנֹכִי אֶהְיֶה עִמָּךְ׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי כְּכַלּוֹת מֹשֶׁה לִכְתֹּב אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת עַל סֵפֶר עַד תֻּמָּם׃
verses.english: And it was when Moses finished writing the words of this instruction on a scroll to their end,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיְהִי כְּכַלּוֹת מֹשֶׁה לִכְתֹּב אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת עַל סֵפֶר עַד תֻּמָּם׃}

verses.original: וַיְצַו מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַלְוִיִּם נֹשְׂאֵי אֲרוֹן בְּרִית יְהֹוָה לֵאמֹר׃
verses.english: and Moses commanded the Levites, who carried the ark of the covenant of YHWH, saying,

tex.original: \hDtrA{וַיְצַו מֹשֶׁה אֶת הַלְוִיִּם נֹשְׂאֵי אֲרוֹן בְּרִית יְהֹוָה לֵאמֹר׃}

verses.original: לָקֹחַ אֵת סֵפֶר הַתּוֹרָה הַזֶּה וְשַׂמְתֶּם אֹתוֹ מִצַּד אֲרוֹן בְּרִית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וְהָיָה שָׁם בְּךָ לְעֵד׃
verses.english: “Take this scroll of instruction and set it at the side of the ark of the covenant of YHWH, your God, and it will be there for you as a witness.

tex.original: \hDtrA{לָקֹחַ אֵת סֵפֶר הַתּוֹרָה הַזֶּה וְשַׂמְתֶּם אֹתוֹ מִצַּד אֲרוֹן בְּרִית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וְהָיָה שָׁם בְּךָ לְעֵד׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		it will be there for you as a witness. The scroll that Moses has written
%		stays there beside the ark for six hundred years until the reign of King
%		Josiah. Apparently it has long been ignored by then. The priest Hilkiah
%		says there, “I’ve found the scroll of instruction (sper
%		hattrh) in the house of YHWH.” When it is read to King
%		Josiah, he tears his clothes and says, “YHWH’s fury is great that has
%		ignited at us because our fathers didn’t listen to this scroll’s words,
%		to act according to everything that’s written about us!” (2 Kings
%		22:8–13). Especially in light of the curses in Deuteronomy 28, Josiah’s
%		reaction is understandable. And so it is understood that these laws go
%		ignored for generations and then are rediscovered. Josiah has the scroll
%		read aloud to the entire people, and he institutes a renewal of the
%		covenant and a tremendous religious reform. The narrative concludes:
%		“And before him there was not a king like him, who came back to YHWH
%		with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his might,
%		according to all of Moses’ instruction, and after him none rose like
%		him” (2 Kings 23:25). All the kings in the books of 1 and 2 Kings are
%		measured by whether they fulfilled the laws of Deuteronomy, and Josiah
%		is rated the highest. Above all, Josiah institutes the practice of
%		public reading of the Torah, which prevails to the present day. And, to
%		this day, the measure of a leader among the Jews must be the degree to
%		which he or she lives by the Torah and draws others to do so as well.
%	}

verses.original: כִּי אָנֹכִי יָדַעְתִּי אֶת מֶרְיְךָ וְאֶת ערְפְּךָ הַקָּשֶׁה הֵן בְּעוֹדֶנִּי חַי עִמָּכֶם הַיּוֹם מַמְרִים הֱיִתֶם עִם יְהֹוָה וְאַף כִּי אַחֲרֵי מוֹתִי׃
verses.english: Because I know your rebellion and your hard neck. Here, while I’m still alive with you today, you’ve been rebelling at YHWH, so how much more after my death!

tex.original: \hDtrA{כִּי אָנֹכִי יָדַעְתִּי אֶת מֶרְיְךָ וְאֶת ערְפְּךָ הַקָּשֶׁה הֵן בְּעוֹדֶנִּי חַי עִמָּכֶם הַיּוֹם מַמְרִים הֱיִתֶם עִם יְהֹוָה וְאַף כִּי אַחֲרֵי מוֹתִי׃}

verses.original: הַקְהִילוּ אֵלַי אֶת כּל זִקְנֵי שִׁבְטֵיכֶם וְשֹׁטְרֵיכֶם וַאֲדַבְּרָה בְאזְנֵיהֶם אֵת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וְאָעִידָה בָּם אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.english: Assemble all the elders of your tribes and your officers to me so I may speak these things in their ears and call the skies and the earth to witness regarding them,

tex.original: \hDtrB{הַקְהִילוּ אֵלַי אֶת כּל זִקְנֵי שִׁבְטֵיכֶם וְשֹׁטְרֵיכֶם וַאֲדַבְּרָה בְאזְנֵיהֶם אֵת הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וְאָעִידָה בָּם אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת הָאָרֶץ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		call the skies and the earth to witness. Moses will do this in the
%		opening words of the song (32:1): “Listen, skies, so I may speak; and
%		let the earth hear what my mouth says.” Ancient Near Eastern treaties
%		include a summoning of witnesses, usually the gods of the parties to the
%		agreement. The biblical covenant cannot include pagan gods as witnesses,
%		but it must have eternal witnesses since the covenant is meant to last
%		forever. Therefore, the earth and sky are called on as witnesses. This
%		summoning of earth and sky rather than gods in an early poem is further
%		evidence that monotheism existed early in Israelite history.
%	}

verses.original: כִּי יָדַעְתִּי אַחֲרֵי מוֹתִי כִּי הַשְׁחֵת תַּשְׁחִתוּן וְסַרְתֶּם מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ אֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִי אֶתְכֶם וְקָרָאת אֶתְכֶם הָרָעָה בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים כִּי תַעֲשׂוּ אֶת הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה לְהַכְעִיסוֹ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: because I know, after my death, that you’ll be corrupted, and you’ll turn from the way that I’ve commanded you. And the bad thing will happen to you in the future days when you’ll do what is bad in YHWH’s eyes to provoke Him with your hands’ work.”

tex.original: \hDtrB{כִּי יָדַעְתִּי אַחֲרֵי מוֹתִי כִּי הַשְׁחֵת תַּשְׁחִתוּן וְסַרְתֶּם מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ אֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִי אֶתְכֶם וְקָרָאת אֶתְכֶם הָרָעָה בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים כִּי תַעֲשׂוּ אֶת הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה לְהַכְעִיסוֹ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵיכֶם׃}
tex.english:
\eDtrB{
		because I know, after my death, that you’ll be corrupted,
		and you’ll turn from the way that I’ve commanded you. And
		the bad thing will happen to you in the future days when
		you’ll do what is bad in YHWH’s eyes to provoke Him with
		your hands’ work.”
	}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		you’ll be corrupted. Another term from the Torah’s beginning returns at
%		its end: the Hiphil of the root t with the sense of humans
%		becoming corrupt was used to introduce the flood: “All flesh had
%		corrupted its way on the earth” (Gen 6:12). It does not occur again with
%		this meaning until Deut 4:16 and then again here, where Moses says he
%		knows that the people will someday become corrupted. That is, he
%		understands that the susceptibility to corruption has been part of human
%		nature from the beginning.
%	}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר מֹשֶׁה בְּאזְנֵי כּל קְהַל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת עַד תֻּמָּם׃
verses.english: And Moses spoke in the ears of all the community of Israel the words of this song to their end:

tex.original: \hDtrB{וַיְדַבֵּר מֹשֶׁה בְּאזְנֵי כּל קְהַל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת עַד תֻּמָּם׃}

verses.original: הַאֲזִינוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם וַאֲדַבֵּרָה וְתִשְׁמַע הָאָרֶץ אִמְרֵי פִי׃
verses.english: Listen, skies, so I may speak and let the earth hear what my mouth says.

tex.original: \hDtrB{הַאֲזִינוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם וַאֲדַבֵּרָה וְתִשְׁמַע הָאָרֶץ אִמְרֵי פִי׃}

verses.original: יַעֲרֹף כַּמָּטָר לִקְחִי תִּזַּל כַּטַּל אִמְרָתִי כִּשְׂעִירִם עֲלֵי דֶשֶׁא וְכִרְבִיבִים עֲלֵי עֵשֶׂב׃
verses.english: Let my teaching come down like showers; let my saying emerge like dew, like raindrops on plants and like rainfalls on herbs.

tex.original: \hDtrB{יַעֲרֹף כַּמָּטָר לִקְחִי תִּזַּל כַּטַּל אִמְרָתִי כִּשְׂעִירִם עֲלֵי דֶשֶׁא וְכִרְבִיבִים עֲלֵי עֵשֶׂב׃}

verses.original: כִּי שֵׁם יְהֹוָה אֶקְרָא הָבוּ גֹדֶל לֵאלֹהֵינוּ׃
verses.english: When I call YHWH’s name, avow our God’s greatness.

tex.original: \hDtrB{כִּי שֵׁם יְהֹוָה אֶקְרָא הָבוּ גֹדֶל לֵאלֹהֵינוּ׃}
tex.english: \eDtrB{When I call YHWH’s name, avow our God’s greatness.}

verses.original: הַצּוּר תָּמִים פּעֳלוֹ כִּי כל דְּרָכָיו מִשְׁפָּט אֵל אֱמוּנָה וְאֵין עָוֶל צַדִּיק וְיָשָׁר הוּא׃
verses.english: The Rock: His work is unblemished, for all His ways are judgment. A God of trust, and without injustice, He’s virtuous and right.

tex.original: \hDtrB{הַצּוּר תָּמִים פּעֳלוֹ כִּי כל דְּרָכָיו מִשְׁפָּט אֵל אֱמוּנָה וְאֵין עָוֶל צַדִּיק וְיָשָׁר הוּא׃}

verses.original: שִׁחֵת לוֹ לֹא בָּנָיו מוּמָם דּוֹר עִקֵּשׁ וּפְתַלְתֹּל׃
verses.english: It corrupted at Him—not His children, their flaw— a crooked and twisted generation.

tex.original: \hDtrB{שִׁחֵת לוֹ לֹא בָּנָיו מוּמָם דּוֹר עִקֵּשׁ וּפְתַלְתֹּל׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		It corrupted at Him—not His children, their flaw. The noun, Hebrew mûm,
%		means an injury of the sort that makes a man unacceptable for the
%		priesthood, or an animal unacceptable for sacrifice. Here I understand
%		it to be some such damage in humans’ nature, as God and Moses have just
%		said (31:21,27,29). It is not humans, “His children,” as such, but
%		rather this inherent shortcoming in their nature that brings about
%		corruption in the eyes of the deity.
%	}

verses.original: הַ לְיְהֹוָה תִּגְמְלוּ זֹאת עַם נָבָל וְלֹא חָכָם הֲלוֹא הוּא אָבִיךָ קָּנֶךָ הוּא עָשְׂךָ וַיְכֹנְנֶךָ׃
verses.english: Is it to YHWH that you repay like this?! Foolish people and unwise! Isn’t He your father, who created you, He who made you and reared you?

tex.original: \hDtrB{הַ לְיְהֹוָה תִּגְמְלוּ זֹאת עַם נָבָל וְלֹא חָכָם הֲלוֹא הוּא אָבִיךָ קָּנֶךָ הוּא עָשְׂךָ וַיְכֹנְנֶךָ׃}

verses.original: זְכֹר יְמוֹת עוֹלָם בִּינוּ שְׁנוֹת דֹּר וָדֹר שְׁאַל אָבִיךָ וְיַגֵּדְךָ זְקֵנֶיךָ וְיֹאמְרוּ לָךְ׃
verses.english: Remember the days of old. Grasp the years through generations. Ask your father, and he’ll tell you, your elders, and they’ll say to you:

tex.original: \hDtrB{זְכֹר יְמוֹת עוֹלָם בִּינוּ שְׁנוֹת דֹּר וָדֹר שְׁאַל אָבִיךָ וְיַגֵּדְךָ זְקֵנֶיךָ וְיֹאמְרוּ לָךְ׃}

verses.original: בְּהַנְחֵל עֶלְיוֹן גּוֹיִם בְּהַפְרִידוֹ בְּנֵי אָדָם יַצֵּב גְּבֻלֹת עַמִּים לְמִסְפַּר בְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים׃
verses.english: When the Highest gave nations legacies, when He dispersed humankind, He set the peoples’ borders to the number of the children of the gods.
verses.commentary: Lots to talk about on this one. See commented out footnote below.

tex.commentary:
Lots to talk about on this one.
	See commented out footnote below.

%	\footnote{
%		dispersed humankind. The term “dispersed” refers to the separation of
%		humankind into nations in Genesis (10:5,18,32; 25:23). Footnote 32:8. to
%		the number of the children of Israel. In light of the other occurrences
%		of the phrase “to the number” in the Tanak (Josh 4:5,8; Judg 21:23), it
%		means here “equal to the number of the children of Israel.” This makes
%		little sense: that the number of nations is equal to the number of the
%		children of Israel. Traditional commentators have taken this to mean
%		that there are seventy nations (as in Genesis 10), matching the seventy
%		souls of Jacob’s (Israel’s) family who go to Egypt (Exod 1:5), or that
%		there are twelve Canaanite peoples, matching Israel’s twelve sons.
%		Contemporary scholars have taken account of a Qumran (Dead Sea) scroll
%		(4QDeut\textasciicircum{}(j)) that says instead: “to the number of the
%		children of the gods” (or “children of God”—bnê
%		’lhîm). The phrase “children [or: sons] of the gods”
%		normally means: the gods. Scholars have hypothesized that this was the
%		original reading of this verse and that later scribes or editors were
%		distressed by this meaning so they changed “children of the gods” to
%		“children of Israel.” If so, then the original meaning was that God
%		allotted a nation to each of the gods—and He took Israel as His own
%		people. Thus the next verse reads: “YHWH’s portion is Israel.” One may
%		take this to mean that the author of this song believed that there were
%		in fact other gods but that YHWH was supreme. (This is known as
%		henotheism, a step between polytheism and monotheism.) Or one may
%		understand it to mean that the author’s view was that YHWH allotted the
%		peoples their gods in whom to believe, but that these gods did not
%		really exist. To complicate this picture further, the Greek text reads
%		“to the number of the angels of God.” And there are cases in which the
%		bnê ’lhîm are thought to be the angels (Gen 6:2;
%		Job 1:6). It is likely that the Greek translator had the “children of
%		the gods” reading and changed it to “angels of God” to establish that
%		these were in fact the angels and not the pagan gods. On this
%		understanding of the bnê ’lhîm, God allots a nation
%		to each of the angels but retains Israel for Himself. I believe that
%		Psalm 82 is particularly relevant to this matter. It pictures the
%		following: “God is standing in the divine council. He judges among the
%		gods” (82:1). In this extraordinary scene, God criticizes the gods for
%		failing to judge justly, and He takes away their immortality, condemning
%		them to die like humans: “I had said you are gods, children of the
%		Highest, all of you; but you shall die like a human!” (82:6). Whether
%		meant literally or figuratively, this psalm tells a myth of the death of
%		the gods. And note that it refers to God as “the Highest”
%		(‘elyn), as in our verse here in the Song of Moses (and it refers
%		to the gods as the children of the Highest); and it ends with God giving
%		legacies to the nations (82:8)—which is also what our verse here says:
%		“When the Highest gave nations legacies....” It is likely, therefore,
%		that the passage in the Song of Moses reflects the idea of Psalm 82:
%		that there once were lesser gods along with YHWH, and that each was the
%		god of a people, but they were inadequate, and they no longer exist.
%		This may have been believed literally, or it may have been conceived as
%		an answer to those who asked, “What happened to the gods we used to
%		worship?” Or it may have been conceived as a metaphor for the
%		replacement of the belief in many gods by the belief in one.
%	}

verses.original: כִּי חֵלֶק יְהֹוָה עַמּוֹ יַעֲקֹב חֶבֶל נַחֲלָתוֹ׃
verses.english: For YHWH’s portion is His people. Jacob is the share of His legacy.

tex.original: \hDtrB{כִּי חֵלֶק יְהֹוָה עַמּוֹ יַעֲקֹב חֶבֶל נַחֲלָתוֹ׃}

verses.original: יִמְצָאֵהוּ בְּאֶרֶץ מִדְבָּר וּבְתֹהוּ יְלֵל יְשִׁמֹן יְסֹבְבֶנְהוּ יְבוֹנְנֵהוּ יִצְּרֶנְהוּ כְּאִישׁוֹן עֵינוֹ׃
verses.english: He found it in a wilderness land and in a formless place, a howling desert. He surrounded it. He attended to it. He guarded it, like the pupil of his eye.

tex.original: \hDtrB{יִמְצָאֵהוּ בְּאֶרֶץ מִדְבָּר וּבְתֹהוּ יְלֵל יְשִׁמֹן יְסֹבְבֶנְהוּ יְבוֹנְנֵהוּ יִצְּרֶנְהוּ כְּאִישׁוֹן עֵינוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		a formless place. Hebrew tôhû. The word has not occurred since its
%		mention at the very beginning of the Torah: “the earth had been formless
%		and shapeless” (Gen 1:2). Now Israel’s environment in the wilderness is
%		pictured comparably to the condition of the universe prior to the acts
%		of creation: a condition of chaos.
%	}

verses.original: כְּנֶשֶׁר יָעִיר קִנּוֹ עַל גּוֹזָלָיו יְרַחֵף יִפְרֹשׂ כְּנָפָיו יִקָּחֵהוּ יִשָּׂאֵהוּ עַל אֶבְרָתוֹ׃
verses.english: As an eagle stirs its nest, hovers over its young, spreads its wings, takes it, lifts it on its pinion,

tex.original: \hDtrB{כְּנֶשֶׁר יָעִיר קִנּוֹ עַל גּוֹזָלָיו יְרַחֵף יִפְרֹשׂ כְּנָפָיו יִקָּחֵהוּ יִשָּׂאֵהוּ עַל אֶבְרָתוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		hovers. This word, too, occurred in Gen 1:2 (see the preceding comment)
%		and never again in the Torah until its appearance here. YHWH’s
%		protection of Israel in its infancy in the wilderness (like an eagle
%		hovering over its young) is pictured comparably to the divine spirit
%		hovering over the still-shapeless waters in which the earth and skies
%		will be formed.
%	}

verses.original: יְהֹוָה בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ וְאֵין עִמּוֹ אֵל נֵכָר׃
verses.english: YHWH, alone, led it, and no foreign god with Him.

tex.original: \hDtrB{יְהֹוָה בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ וְאֵין עִמּוֹ אֵל נֵכָר׃}
tex.english: \eDtrB{YHWH, alone, led it, and no foreign god with Him.}

verses.original: יַרְכִּבֵהוּ עַל [בָּמֳתֵי] (במותי) אָרֶץ וַיֹּאכַל תְּנוּבֹת שָׂדָי וַיֵּנִקֵהוּ דְבַשׁ מִסֶּלַע וְשֶׁמֶן מֵחַלְמִישׁ צוּר׃
verses.english: He had it ride over earth’s high places and fed it the field’s bounties and had it suck honey from a rock and oil from a flint rock
verses.commentary: Qere Ketiv.

tex.original: \hDtrB{יַרְכִּבֵהוּ עַל [בָּמֳתֵי] (במותי) אָרֶץ וַיֹּאכַל תְּנוּבֹת שָׂדָי וַיֵּנִקֵהוּ דְבַשׁ מִסֶּלַע וְשֶׁמֶן מֵחַלְמִישׁ צוּר׃}

verses.original: חֶמְאַת בָּקָר וַחֲלֵב צֹאן עִם חֵלֶב כָּרִים וְאֵילִים בְּנֵי בָשָׁן וְעַתּוּדִים עִם חֵלֶב כִּלְיוֹת חִטָּה וְדַם עֵנָב תִּשְׁתֶּה חָמֶר׃
verses.english: and curds of cattle and milk of the flock and fat of lambs and Bashan rams and he-goats with fat of innards of wheat —and from grape’s blood you drank wine.

tex.original: \hDtrB{חֶמְאַת בָּקָר וַחֲלֵב צֹאן עִם חֵלֶב כָּרִים וְאֵילִים בְּנֵי בָשָׁן וְעַתּוּדִים עִם חֵלֶב כִּלְיוֹת חִטָּה וְדַם עֵנָב תִּשְׁתֶּה חָמֶר׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁמַן יְשֻׁרוּן וַיִּבְעָט שָׁמַנְתָּ עָבִיתָ כָּשִׂיתָ וַיִּטֹּשׁ אֱלוֹהַּ עָשָׂהוּ וַיְנַבֵּל צוּר יְשֻׁעָתוֹ׃
verses.english: And Jeshurun got fat and kicked —you got fat, you got wide, you got stuffed!— and it left God who made it and took its saving rock for granted.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וַיִּשְׁמַן יְשֻׁרוּן וַיִּבְעָט שָׁמַנְתָּ עָבִיתָ כָּשִׂיתָ וַיִּטֹּשׁ אֱלוֹהַּ עָשָׂהוּ וַיְנַבֵּל צוּר יְשֻׁעָתוֹ׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Jeshurun. Israel. Footnote 32:15. got fat. This is a pun. The Hebrew
%		consonants ymn are the same as in the word “desert”
%		(yimn) in v. 10. But the wordplay is that the same
%		words consonantally have nearly opposite meanings: the people ironically
%		go from a desert (ymn) to getting fat (ymn).
%	}

verses.original: יַקְנִאֻהוּ בְּזָרִים בְּתוֹעֵבֹת יַכְעִיסֻהוּ׃
verses.english: They made Him jealous with outsiders. With offensive things they made him angry.

tex.original: \hDtrB{יַקְנִאֻהוּ בְּזָרִים בְּתוֹעֵבֹת יַכְעִיסֻהוּ׃}

verses.original: יִזְבְּחוּ לַשֵּׁדִים לֹא אֱלֹהַּ אֱלֹהִים לֹא יְדָעוּם חֲדָשִׁים מִקָּרֹב בָּאוּ לֹא שְׂעָרוּם אֲבֹתֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: They sacrificed to demons, a non-god, gods they hadn’t known; new ones, they came of late; your fathers hadn’t been acquainted with them.

tex.original: \hDtrB{יִזְבְּחוּ לַשֵּׁדִים לֹא אֱלֹהַּ אֱלֹהִים לֹא יְדָעוּם חֲדָשִׁים מִקָּרֹב בָּאוּ לֹא שְׂעָרוּם אֲבֹתֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: צוּר יְלָדְךָ תֶּשִׁי וַתִּשְׁכַּח אֵל מְחֹלְלֶךָ׃
verses.english: The rock that fathered you, you ignored, and you forgot God who bore you.

tex.original: \hDtrB{צוּר יְלָדְךָ תֶּשִׁי וַתִּשְׁכַּח אֵל מְחֹלְלֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וַיַּרְא יְהֹוָה וַיִּנְאָץ מִכַּעַס בָּנָיו וּבְנֹתָיו׃
verses.english: And YHWH saw and rejected from His sons’ and His daughters’ angering.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וַיַּרְא יְהֹוָה וַיִּנְאָץ מִכַּעַס בָּנָיו וּבְנֹתָיו׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר אַסְתִּירָה פָנַי מֵהֶם אֶרְאֶה מָה אַחֲרִיתָם כִּי דוֹר תַּהְפֻּכֹת הֵמָּה בָּנִים לֹא אֵמֻן בָּם׃
verses.english: And He said, “Let me hide my face from them; I’ll see what their future will be. For they’re a generation of overthrows, children with no trust in them.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וַיֹּאמֶר אַסְתִּירָה פָנַי מֵהֶם אֶרְאֶה מָה אַחֲרִיתָם כִּי דוֹר תַּהְפֻּכֹת הֵמָּה בָּנִים לֹא אֵמֻן בָּם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		Let me hide my face. See the comment on Deut 31:17. Footnote 32:20. I’ll
%		see what their future will be. Hebrew ’arît, often
%		understood as “end,” does not mean this in the sense of humankind’s
%		coming to an end. Rather, it refers to what will happen in the distant
%		future, the long run. There are two sides to the hiding of the face. It
%		is a fearful period of estrangement from their creator. It has been
%		called divine eclipse, Deus Absconditus, and “death” of God. But, after
%		living through it, humans are forced to grow up, to become more
%		responsible for their world. The words of the Song of Moses declare that
%		God is not simply hiding His face to bring His relationship with humans
%		to an end. There are rather two halves to the statement: “I’ll hide my
%		face from them; I’ll see what their future will be.” God gives humans
%		responsibility for their world. And the only way that they can be forced
%		to take that responsibility is if God is hidden. At whatever price (even
%		world wars, even the holocaust?!) and with whatever successes
%		(rebuilding Israel, conquering diseases, discovering secrets of the
%		creation of the universe), humans must grow up. And God will see what
%		their destiny will be. The Torah does not end with the natural
%		conclusions of the story: the promised land has not been reached, but it
%		is in sight. Everything lies in the future: finding a home, fulfillment
%		of the promises, bringing blessing to all the families of the earth. The
%		divine words resound: “I’ll see what their future will be.” The Torah
%		ends leaving us looking forward to what we can do and what we can be.
%	}

verses.original: הֵם קִנְאוּנִי בְלֹא אֵל כִּעֲסוּנִי בְּהַבְלֵיהֶם וַאֲנִי אַקְנִיאֵם בְּלֹא עָם בְּגוֹי נָבָל אַכְעִיסֵם׃
verses.english: They made me jealous with no-god. They made me angry with their nothings. And I: I’ll make them jealous with no-people. I’ll make them angry with a foolish nation.

tex.original: \hDtrB{הֵם קִנְאוּנִי בְלֹא אֵל כִּעֲסוּנִי בְּהַבְלֵיהֶם וַאֲנִי אַקְנִיאֵם בְּלֹא עָם בְּגוֹי נָבָל אַכְעִיסֵם׃}

verses.original: כִּי אֵשׁ קָדְחָה בְאַפִּי וַתִּיקַד עַד שְׁאוֹל תַּחְתִּית וַתֹּאכַל אֶרֶץ וִיבֻלָהּ וַתְּלַהֵט מוֹסְדֵי הָרִים׃
verses.english: For fire has ignited in my anger and burned to Sheol at bottom and consumed land and its crop and set the mountains’ foundations ablaze.

tex.original: \hDtrB{כִּי אֵשׁ קָדְחָה בְאַפִּי וַתִּיקַד עַד שְׁאוֹל תַּחְתִּית וַתֹּאכַל אֶרֶץ וִיבֻלָהּ וַתְּלַהֵט מוֹסְדֵי הָרִים׃}

verses.original: אַסְפֶּה עָלֵימוֹ רָעוֹת חִצַּי אֲכַלֶּה בָּם׃
verses.english: I’ll mass bad things over them. I’ll exhaust my arrows on them,

tex.original: \hDtrB{אַסְפֶּה עָלֵימוֹ רָעוֹת חִצַּי אֲכַלֶּה בָּם׃}

verses.original: מְזֵי רָעָב וּלְחֻמֵי רֶשֶׁף וְקֶטֶב מְרִירִי וְשֶׁן בְּהֵמֹת אֲשַׁלַּח בָּם עִם חֲמַת זֹחֲלֵי עָפָר׃
verses.english: sapped by hunger and devoured by flame. And bitter destruction and animals’ teeth I’ll let loose at them with venom of serpents of the dust.

tex.original: \hDtrB{מְזֵי רָעָב וּלְחֻמֵי רֶשֶׁף וְקֶטֶב מְרִירִי וְשֶׁן בְּהֵמֹת אֲשַׁלַּח בָּם עִם חֲמַת זֹחֲלֵי עָפָר׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		serpents of the dust. Or: things that crawl in the dust. This is
%		reminiscent of the story of Eden, in which the snake and its descendants
%		are condemned to be legless, going on their bellies and eating dust (Gen
%		3:14); and in which the descendants of the humans and the snake are
%		cursed with mutual enmity, so that the snake will bite the human’s heel
%		(3:15).
%	}

verses.original: מִחוּץ תְּשַׁכֶּל חֶרֶב וּמֵחֲדָרִים אֵימָה גַּם בָּחוּר גַּם בְּתוּלָה יוֹנֵק עִם אִישׁ שֵׂיבָה׃
verses.english: Outside: a sword will bereave, and inside: terror, both young man and virgin, suckling with aged man.

tex.original: \hDtrB{מִחוּץ תְּשַׁכֶּל חֶרֶב וּמֵחֲדָרִים אֵימָה גַּם בָּחוּר גַּם בְּתוּלָה יוֹנֵק עִם אִישׁ שֵׂיבָה׃}

verses.original: אָמַרְתִּי אַפְאֵיהֶם אַשְׁבִּיתָה מֵאֱנוֹשׁ זִכְרָם׃
verses.english: I’d say, ‘I’ll erase them. I’ll make their memory cease from mankind,’

tex.original: \hDtrB{אָמַרְתִּי אַפְאֵיהֶם אַשְׁבִּיתָה מֵאֱנוֹשׁ זִכְרָם׃}

verses.original: לוּלֵי כַּעַס אוֹיֵב אָגוּר פֶּן יְנַכְּרוּ צָרֵימוֹ פֶּן יֹאמְרוּ יָדֵנוּ רָמָה וְלֹא יְהֹוָה פָּעַל כּל זֹאת׃
verses.english: if I didn’t fear the enemy’s anger, in case their foes would misread, in case they’d say, ‘Our hand was high, and it wasn’t YHWH who did all this!’

tex.original: \hDtrB{לוּלֵי כַּעַס אוֹיֵב אָגוּר פֶּן יְנַכְּרוּ צָרֵימוֹ פֶּן יֹאמְרוּ יָדֵנוּ רָמָה וְלֹא יְהֹוָה פָּעַל כּל זֹאת׃}

verses.original: כִּי גוֹי אֹבַד עֵצוֹת הֵמָּה וְאֵין בָּהֶם תְּבוּנָה׃
verses.english: For they’re a nation void of counsel, and there’s no understanding in them.

tex.original: \hDtrB{כִּי גוֹי אֹבַד עֵצוֹת הֵמָּה וְאֵין בָּהֶם תְּבוּנָה׃}

verses.original: לוּ חָכְמוּ יַשְׂכִּילוּ זֹאת יָבִינוּ לְאַחֲרִיתָם׃
verses.english: If they were wise they’d comprehend this; they’d grasp their future.

tex.original: \hDtrB{לוּ חָכְמוּ יַשְׂכִּילוּ זֹאת יָבִינוּ לְאַחֲרִיתָם׃}

verses.original: אֵיכָה יִרְדֹּף אֶחָד אֶלֶף וּשְׁנַיִם יָנִיסוּ רְבָבָה אִם לֹא כִּי צוּרָם מְכָרָם וַיהֹוָה הִסְגִּירָם׃
verses.english: How could one pursue a thousand and two chase ten thousand if not that their rock had sold them, that YHWH had turned them over?”

tex.original: \hDtrB{אֵיכָה יִרְדֹּף אֶחָד אֶלֶף וּשְׁנַיִם יָנִיסוּ רְבָבָה אִם לֹא כִּי צוּרָם מְכָרָם וַיהֹוָה הִסְגִּירָם׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		turned them over. This is the same word that is used to refer to turning
%		an escaped slave over to his master (Deut 23:16). The preceding colon,
%		which parallels this, refers to selling the people. That is, both lines
%		convey an image of God selling Israel back into slavery, when it was God
%		who had freed them from slavery in the first place. Like the last curse
%		of the list in Deuteronomy 28, it is the ultimate horror for Israel: to
%		return to slavery.
%	}

verses.original: כִּי לֹא כְצוּרֵנוּ צוּרָם וְאֹיְבֵינוּ פְּלִילִים׃
verses.english: For their rock is not like our rock, though our enemies are the judges.

tex.original: \hDtrB{כִּי לֹא כְצוּרֵנוּ צוּרָם וְאֹיְבֵינוּ פְּלִילִים׃}

verses.original: כִּי מִגֶּפֶן סְדֹם גַּפְנָם וּמִשַּׁדְמֹת עֲמֹרָה עֲנָבֵמוֹ עִנְּבֵי רוֹשׁ אַשְׁכְּלֹת מְרֹרֹת לָמוֹ׃
verses.english: For their vine is from Sodom’s vine and from Gomorrah’s fields. Their grapes are poison grapes. They have bitter clusters.

tex.original: \hDtrB{כִּי מִגֶּפֶן סְדֹם גַּפְנָם וּמִשַּׁדְמֹת עֲמֹרָה עֲנָבֵמוֹ עִנְּבֵי רוֹשׁ אַשְׁכְּלֹת מְרֹרֹת לָמוֹ׃}

verses.original: חֲמַת תַּנִּינִם יֵינָם וְרֹאשׁ פְּתָנִים אַכְזָר׃
verses.english: Their wine is serpents’ venom and cruel poison of cobras.

tex.original: \hDtrB{חֲמַת תַּנִּינִם יֵינָם וְרֹאשׁ פְּתָנִים אַכְזָר׃}
tex.english: \eDtrB{Their wine is serpents’ venom and cruel poison of cobras.}

verses.original: הֲלֹא הוּא כָּמֻס עִמָּדִי חָתוּם בְּאוֹצְרֹתָי׃
verses.english: “Isn’t it stored with me, sealed in my treasuries?

tex.original: \hDtrB{הֲלֹא הוּא כָּמֻס עִמָּדִי חָתוּם בְּאוֹצְרֹתָי׃}
tex.english: \eDtrB{“Isn’t it stored with me, sealed in my treasuries?}

verses.original: לִי נָקָם וְשִׁלֵּם לְעֵת תָּמוּט רַגְלָם כִּי קָרוֹב יוֹם אֵידָם וְחָשׁ עֲתִדֹת לָמוֹ׃
verses.english: Vengeance and recompense are mine, for the time their foot will slip; for the day of their ordeal is close and comes fast: things prepared for them.”

tex.original: \hDtrB{לִי נָקָם וְשִׁלֵּם לְעֵת תָּמוּט רַגְלָם כִּי קָרוֹב יוֹם אֵידָם וְחָשׁ עֲתִדֹת לָמוֹ׃}

verses.original: כִּי יָדִין יְהֹוָה עַמּוֹ וְעַל עֲבָדָיו יִתְנֶחָם כִּי יִרְאֶה כִּי אָזְלַת יָד וְאֶפֶס עָצוּר וְעָזוּב׃
verses.english: For YHWH will judge His people and regret about His servants when He’ll see that their strength is gone and there’s none: held back or left alone.

tex.original: \hDtrB{כִּי יָדִין יְהֹוָה עַמּוֹ וְעַל עֲבָדָיו יִתְנֶחָם כִּי יִרְאֶה כִּי אָזְלַת יָד וְאֶפֶס עָצוּר וְעָזוּב׃}

verses.original: וְאָמַר אֵי אֱלֹהֵימוֹ צוּר חָסָיוּ בוֹ׃
verses.english: And He’ll say, “Where are their gods, the rock in whom they sought refuge,

tex.original: \hDtrB{וְאָמַר אֵי אֱלֹהֵימוֹ צוּר חָסָיוּ בוֹ׃}

verses.original: אֲשֶׁר חֵלֶב זְבָחֵימוֹ יֹאכֵלוּ יִשְׁתּוּ יֵין נְסִיכָם יָקוּמוּ וְיַעְזְרֻכֶם יְהִי עֲלֵיכֶם סִתְרָה׃
verses.english: who would eat the fat of their sacrifices, would drink the wine of their libations? Let them get up and help you! Let that be a shelter over you.

tex.original: \hDtrB{אֲשֶׁר חֵלֶב זְבָחֵימוֹ יֹאכֵלוּ יִשְׁתּוּ יֵין נְסִיכָם יָקוּמוּ וְיַעְזְרֻכֶם יְהִי עֲלֵיכֶם סִתְרָה׃}

verses.original: רְאוּ עַתָּה כִּי אֲנִי אֲנִי הוּא וְאֵין אֱלֹהִים עִמָּדִי אֲנִי אָמִית וַאֲחַיֶּה מָחַצְתִּי וַאֲנִי אֶרְפָּא וְאֵין מִיָּדִי מַצִּיל׃
verses.english: See now that I, I am He, and there is no god with me. I cause death and give life. I’ve pierced, and I’ll heal. And there’s no deliverer from my hand,

tex.original: \hDtrB{רְאוּ עַתָּה כִּי אֲנִי אֲנִי הוּא וְאֵין אֱלֹהִים עִמָּדִי אֲנִי אָמִית וַאֲחַיֶּה מָחַצְתִּי וַאֲנִי אֶרְפָּא וְאֵין מִיָּדִי מַצִּיל׃}
tex.commentary:
%	\footnote{
%		there is no god with me. It is possible that this might mean that other
%		gods exist but that they just do not happen to be present with YHWH at
%		this time, but that seems to me to be a stretch. Where would a god be
%		who is not in YHWH’s presence?! The plain sense of these words (and
%		other passages on which I have commented) is monotheistic. It comes in a
%		context of calling on gods to show themselves if they exist: “Where are
%		their gods.... Let them get up and help you!” And this poem shows
%		well-known linguistic signs of being an early composition. The
%		persistent view in biblical scholarship that monotheism is a late
%		development in biblical Israel (coming during or after the Babylonian
%		exile) is contrary to such explicit statements as this.
%	}

verses.original: כִּי אֶשָּׂא אֶל שָׁמַיִם יָדִי וְאָמַרְתִּי חַי אָנֹכִי לְעֹלָם׃
verses.english: when I raise my hand to the skies, and I say, ‘As I live forever,

tex.original: \hDtrB{כִּי אֶשָּׂא אֶל שָׁמַיִם יָדִי וְאָמַרְתִּי חַי אָנֹכִי לְעֹלָם׃}

verses.original: אִם שַׁנּוֹתִי בְּרַק חַרְבִּי וְתֹאחֵז בְּמִשְׁפָּט יָדִי אָשִׁיב נָקָם לְצָרָי וְלִמְשַׂנְאַי אֲשַׁלֵּם׃
verses.english: if I whet the lightning of my sword, and my hand takes hold of judgment, I’ll give back vengeance to my foes and pay back those who hate me.

tex.original: \hDtrB{אִם שַׁנּוֹתִי בְּרַק חַרְבִּי וְתֹאחֵז בְּמִשְׁפָּט יָדִי אָשִׁיב נָקָם לְצָרָי וְלִמְשַׂנְאַי אֲשַׁלֵּם׃}

verses.original: אַשְׁכִּיר חִצַּי מִדָּם וְחַרְבִּי תֹּאכַל בָּשָׂר מִדַּם חָלָל וְשִׁבְיָה מֵרֹאשׁ פַּרְעוֹת אוֹיֵב׃
verses.english: I’ll make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will eat flesh from the blood of the slain and captured, from the head of loose hair of the enemy.’”

tex.original: \hDtrB{אַשְׁכִּיר חִצַּי מִדָּם וְחַרְבִּי תֹּאכַל בָּשָׂר מִדַּם חָלָל וְשִׁבְיָה מֵרֹאשׁ פַּרְעוֹת אוֹיֵב׃}

verses.original: הַרְנִינוּ גוֹיִם עַמּוֹ כִּי דַם עֲבָדָיו יִקּוֹם וְנָקָם יָשִׁיב לְצָרָיו וְכִפֶּר אַדְמָתוֹ עַמּוֹ׃
verses.english: Nations: cheer His people! For He’ll requite His servants’ blood and give back vengeance to His foes and make atonement for His land, His people.

tex.original: \hDtrB{הַרְנִינוּ גוֹיִם עַמּוֹ כִּי דַם עֲבָדָיו יִקּוֹם וְנָקָם יָשִׁיב לְצָרָיו וְכִפֶּר אַדְמָתוֹ עַמּוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה וַיְדַבֵּר אֶת כּל דִּבְרֵי הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת בְּאזְנֵי הָעָם הוּא וְהוֹשֵׁעַ בִּן נוּן׃
verses.english: And Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the people’s ears, he and Hoshea son of Nun.

tex.original: \hDtrB{וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה וַיְדַבֵּר אֶת כּל דִּבְרֵי הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת בְּאזְנֵי הָעָם הוּא וְהוֹשֵׁעַ בִּן נוּן׃}
