verses.english: Why, then, do you maliciously trample upon the sacrifices and offerings that I have commanded? You have honored your sons more than Me, feeding on the first portions of every offering of My people Israel.
verses.commentary: Still not clear who he is, but he's not happy.

verses.english: Assuredly—declares YHWH, the God of Israel—I intended for you and your father’s house to remain in My service forever. But now—declares YHWH—far be it from Me! For I honor those who honor Me, but those who spurn Me shall be dishonored.
verses.commentary: So the speaker is like YHWH's H.R. or something.

verses.original: הִנֵּה יָמִים בָּאִים וְגָדַעְתִּי אֶת־זְרֹעֲךָ וְאֶת־זְרֹעַ בֵּית אָבִיךָ מִהְיוֹת זָקֵן בְּבֵיתֶךָ׃

verses.commentary: They won't be renewing Eli's contract.

verses.english: You will gaze grudgingly at all the bounty that will be bestowed on Israel, but there shall never be an elder in your house.
verses.commentary: You'll get jealous at all the awesome stuff but you won't get any.

verses.commentary: Look I'm not blaming all your kids, but you're fired. Like genetically.

Your suspiciously Egyptian named sons will both die on the same day.

These things tend to happen three times in stories.

So it happens again.

Then they're like “Oh no, god is here.”

They make a note of the fact that this is the first time that's happened.

verses.english: The Philistines fought; Israel was routed, and they all fled to their homes. The defeat was very great, thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell there.
verses.commentary:
And Israel loses anyway.

Thirty thousand of them die.

Even with the box.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּלָּחֲמוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים וַיִּנָּגֶף יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיָּנֻסוּ אִישׁ לְאֹהָלָיו וַתְּהִי הַמַּכָּה גְּדוֹלָה מְאֹד וַיִּפֹּל מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שְׁלֹשִׁים אֶלֶף רַגְלִי׃}

verses.english: The Ark of God was captured, and Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain.
verses.commentary: They steal the box, and kill the guys.

Ripped shirt, covered in dirt.

So the dirty gentleman says “I just came from war.”

Eli's like “How'd it go?”

verses.english: When he mentioned the Ark of God, [Eli] fell backward off the seat beside the gate, broke his neck and died; for he was an old man and heavy. He had been a chieftain of Israel for forty years.
verses.commentary:
So Eli falls back in his chair and breaks his neck.

Now if that sounds implausble, don't worry, we're also told

“He's old and fat.” So it works.

verses.english: His daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was with child, about to give birth. When she heard the report that the Ark of God was captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she was seized with labor pains, and she crouched down and gave birth.
verses.commentary:
Cut to pregnant girl. [Who may or may not have gotten pregnant from that thing they were doing outside the temple.]

She's Phineas's wife.

She hears her husband's dead and the box got stolen.

So naturally she goes into labor.

verses.commentary:
So while she's dying (did we mention she's dying?) the midwife is like “Look, a son.”

But she didn't care, for she was dead.

verses.commentary: Wait back up. First she names the kid a really mean name.

verses.commentary: Did she die or not?

verses.commentary: So they take the box and bring it to the beach. Ashdod is near the beach.

They bring the box into the temple of Dagon.

Dagon means “grain.”

tex.original: \hJ{וּלְקַחְתֶּם אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה וּנְתַתֶּם אֹתוֹ אֶל־הָעֲגָלָה וְאֵת כְּלֵי הַזָּהָב אֲשֶׁר הֲשֵׁבֹתֶם לוֹ אָשָׁם תָּשִׂימוּ בָאַרְגַּז מִצִּדּוֹ וְשִׁלַּחְתֶּם אֹתוֹ וְהָלָךְ׃}

verses.original: וּרְאִיתֶם אִם־דֶּרֶךְ גְּבוּלוֹ יַעֲלֶה בֵּית שֶׁמֶשׁ הוּא עָשָׂה לָנוּ אֶת־הָרָעָה הַגְּדוֹלָה הַזֹּאת וְאִם־לֹא וְיָדַעְנוּ כִּי לֹא יָדוֹ נָגְעָה בָּנוּ מִקְרֶה הוּא הָיָה לָנוּ׃
verses.english: Then watch: If it goes up the road to Beth-shemesh, to His own territory, it was He who has inflicted this great harm on us. But if not, we shall know that it was not His hand that struck us; it just happened to us by chance.”
verses.commentary:
They have some theory about which way the cows go.

If they go one way, they decide YHWH did all this.

If they go the other way, they decide it's an accident.

The theory seems to assume that YHWH can steer the cows from inside the box.

But also, that he needed the cows and the cart and all that.

Apologies to any Philistines if I've misrepresented their theology.

tex.commentary:
\aA{
		They have some theory about which way the cows go.

		If they go one way, they decide YHWH did all this.

		If they go the other way, they decide it's an accident.

		The theory seems to assume that YHWH can steer the cows
		from inside the box.

		But also, that he needed the cows and the cart and all
		that.

		Apologies to any Philistines if I've misrepresented
		their theology.
	}

verses.original: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים כֵּן וַיִּקְחוּ שְׁתֵּי פָרוֹת עָלוֹת וַיַּאַסְרוּם בָּעֲגָלָה וְאֶת־בְּנֵיהֶם כָּלוּ בַבָּיִת׃
verses.english: The men did so. They took two milch cows and harnessed them to the cart, and shut up their calves indoors.
verses.commentary:
The text now says they did all that.

It even mentions again that the other cows don't get to come.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּעֲשׂוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים כֵּן וַיִּקְחוּ שְׁתֵּי פָרוֹת עָלוֹת וַיַּאַסְרוּם בָּעֲגָלָה וְאֶת־בְּנֵיהֶם כָּלוּ בַבָּיִת׃}

verses.original: וַיָּשִׂמוּ אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה אֶל־הָעֲגָלָה וְאֵת הָאַרְגַּז וְאֵת עַכְבְּרֵי הַזָּהָב וְאֵת צַלְמֵי טְחֹרֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: They placed the Ark of YHWH on the cart together with the chest, the golden mice, and the figures of their hemorrhoids.
verses.commentary: We've sort of been over this.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּשִׂמוּ אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה אֶל־הָעֲגָלָה וְאֵת הָאַרְגַּז וְאֵת עַכְבְּרֵי הַזָּהָב וְאֵת צַלְמֵי טְחֹרֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה הַפָּרוֹת בַּדֶּרֶךְ עַל־דֶּרֶךְ בֵּית שֶׁמֶשׁ בִּמְסִלָּה אַחַת הָלְכוּ הָלֹךְ וְגָעוֹ וְלֹא־סָרוּ יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאול וְסַרְנֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים הֹלְכִים אַחֲרֵיהֶם עַד־גְּבוּל בֵּית שָׁמֶשׁ׃
verses.english: The cows went straight ahead along the road to Beth-shemesh. They went along a single highroad, lowing as they went, and turning off neither to the right nor to the left; and the lords of the Philistines walked behind them as far as the border of Beth-shemesh.
verses.commentary:
The cows walk (or YHWH drives them) straight back home.

The Philistines follow along until they reach the border.

tex.english:
\eJ{
		The cows went straight ahead along the road to Beth-shemesh. They
		went along a single highroad, lowing as they went, and turning off
		neither to the right nor to the left; and the lords of the
		Philistines walked behind them as far as the border of
		Beth-shemesh.
	}

verses.original: וּבֵית שֶׁמֶשׁ קֹצְרִים קְצִיר־חִטִּים בָּעֵמֶק וַיִּשְׂאוּ אֶת־עֵינֵיהֶם וַיִּרְאוּ אֶת־הָאָרוֹן וַיִּשְׂמְחוּ לִרְאוֹת׃
verses.english: The people of Beth-shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley. They looked up and saw the Ark, and they rejoiced when they saw [it].
verses.commentary:
The people look up and see that YHWH's back.

They're happy. They missed him.

tex.original: \hJ{וּבֵית שֶׁמֶשׁ קֹצְרִים קְצִיר־חִטִּים בָּעֵמֶק וַיִּשְׂאוּ אֶת־עֵינֵיהֶם וַיִּרְאוּ אֶת־הָאָרוֹן וַיִּשְׂמְחוּ לִרְאוֹת׃}

verses.original: וְהָעֲגָלָה בָּאָה אֶל־שְׂדֵה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֵּית־הַשִּׁמְשִׁי וַתַּעֲמֹד שָׁם וְשָׁם אֶבֶן גְּדוֹלָה וַיְבַקְּעוּ אֶת־עֲצֵי הָעֲגָלָה וְאֶת־הַפָּרוֹת הֶעֱלוּ עֹלָה לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: The cart came into the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh and it stopped there. They split up the wood of the cart and presented the cows as a burnt offering to YHWH. A large stone was there;
verses.commentary:
YHWH parks the cart.

The people are so happy they murder the cows.

There's also a big rock.

tex.original: \hJ{וְהָעֲגָלָה בָּאָה אֶל־שְׂדֵה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֵּית־הַשִּׁמְשִׁי וַתַּעֲמֹד שָׁם וְשָׁם אֶבֶן גְּדוֹלָה וַיְבַקְּעוּ אֶת־עֲצֵי הָעֲגָלָה וְאֶת־הַפָּרוֹת הֶעֱלוּ עֹלָה לַיהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְהַלְוִיִּם הוֹרִידוּ אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה וְאֶת־הָאַרְגַּז אֲשֶׁר־אִתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ כְלֵי־זָהָב וַיָּשִׂמוּ אֶל־הָאֶבֶן הַגְּדוֹלָה וְאַנְשֵׁי בֵית־שֶׁמֶשׁ הֶעֱלוּ עֹלוֹת וַיִּזְבְּחוּ זְבָחִים בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: and the Levites took down the Ark of YHWH and the chest beside it containing the gold objects and placed them on the large stone. Then the men of Beth-shemesh presented burnt offerings and other sacrifices to YHWH that day.
verses.commentary:
The Levites get the box and the golden butt souvenirs and put them on the rock.

They kept being happy, so they burned other animals too.

verses.original: וַחֲמִשָּׁה סַרְנֵי־פְלִשְׁתִּים רָאוּ וַיָּשֻׁבוּ עֶקְרוֹן בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא׃
verses.english: The five lords of the Philistines saw this and returned the same day to Ekron.
verses.commentary: The Philistines saw all this so they went back home.

tex.original: \hJ{וַחֲמִשָּׁה סַרְנֵי־פְלִשְׁתִּים רָאוּ וַיָּשֻׁבוּ עֶקְרוֹן בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא׃}

verses.original: וְאֵלֶּה טְחֹרֵי הַזָּהָב אֲשֶׁר הֵשִׁיבוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אָשָׁם לַיהֹוָהלְאַשְׁדּוֹד אֶחָדלְעַזָּה אֶחָדלְאַשְׁקְלוֹן אֶחָדלְגַת אֶחָדלְעֶקְרוֹן אֶחָד׃
verses.english: The following were the golden hemorrhoids that the Philistines paid as an indemnity to YHWH: For Ashdod, one; for Gaza, one; for Ashkelon, one; for Gath, one; for Ekron, one.
verses.commentary: Just to reiterate, one golden hemorrhoid per city.

tex.original: \hJ{וְאֵלֶּה טְחֹרֵי הַזָּהָב אֲשֶׁר הֵשִׁיבוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אָשָׁם לַיהֹוָהלְאַשְׁדּוֹד אֶחָדלְעַזָּה אֶחָדלְאַשְׁקְלוֹן אֶחָדלְגַת אֶחָדלְעֶקְרוֹן אֶחָד׃}

verses.original: וְעַכְבְּרֵי הַזָּהָב מִסְפַּר כּל־עָרֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים לַחֲמֵשֶׁת הַסְּרָנִים מֵעִיר מִבְצָר וְעַד כֹּפֶר הַפְּרָזִי וְעַד אָבֵל הַגְּדוֹלָה אֲשֶׁר הִנִּיחוּ עָלֶיהָ אֵת אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה בִּשְׂדֵה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֵּית הַשִּׁמְשִׁי׃
verses.english: As for the golden mice, their number accorded with all the Philistine towns that belonged to the five lords—both fortified towns and unwalled villages, as far as the great stone on which the Ark of YHWH was set down, to this day, in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh.
verses.commentary: Same with the mice.

tex.english:
\eJ{
		As for the golden mice, their number accorded with all the
		Philistine towns that belonged to the five lords—both fortified
		towns and unwalled villages, as far as the great stone on which
		the Ark of YHWH was set down, to this day, in the field of Joshua
		of Beth-shemesh.
	}

verses.original: וַיַּךְ בְּאַנְשֵׁי בֵית־שֶׁמֶשׁ כִּי רָאוּ בַּאֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה וַיַּךְ בָּעָם שִׁבְעִים אִישׁ חֲמִשִּׁים אֶלֶף אִישׁ וַיִּתְאַבְּלוּ הָעָם כִּי־הִכָּה יְהֹוָה בָּעָם מַכָּה גְדוֹלָה׃
verses.english: [YHWH] struck at the men of Beth-shemesh because they looked into the Ark of YHWH; He struck down seventy men among the people [and] fifty thousand men. The people mourned, for He had inflicted a great slaughter upon the population.
verses.commentary:
Back home, after the party, the home team looks in the box.

YHWH doesn't like that.

He kills seventy men.

And also fifty thousand.

tex.commentary:
\aA{
		Back home, after the party, the home team looks in the
		box.

		YHWH doesn't like that.

		He kills seventy men.

		And also fifty thousand.
	}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ אַנְשֵׁי בֵית־שֶׁמֶשׁ מִי יוּכַל לַעֲמֹד לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה הָאֱלֹהִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַזֶּה וְאֶל־מִי יַעֲלֶה מֵעָלֵינוּ׃
verses.english: And the men of Beth-shemesh asked, “Who can stand in attendance on YHWH, this holy God? And to whom shall He go up from us?”
verses.commentary:
So the people say, and I quote:

“Who can survive in the presence of YHWH, this holy God? And who can take him away from us?”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמְרוּ אַנְשֵׁי בֵית־שֶׁמֶשׁ מִי יוּכַל לַעֲמֹד לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה הָאֱלֹהִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַזֶּה וְאֶל־מִי יַעֲלֶה מֵעָלֵינוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלְחוּ מַלְאָכִים אֶל־יוֹשְׁבֵי קִרְיַת־יְעָרִים לֵאמֹר הֵשִׁבוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה רְדוּ הַעֲלוּ אֹתוֹ אֲלֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: They sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim to say, “The Philistines have sent back the Ark of YHWH. Come down and take it into your keeping.”
verses.commentary:
So the Beth-shemesh people call some neighbors from a nearby north east town.

And they say “Hey the box is back. Come get it.”

And the chapter ends on a cliffhanger.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשְׁלְחוּ מַלְאָכִים אֶל־יוֹשְׁבֵי קִרְיַת־יְעָרִים לֵאמֹר הֵשִׁבוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה רְדוּ הַעֲלוּ אֹתוֹ אֲלֵיכֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ אַנְשֵׁי קִרְיַת יְעָרִים וַיַּעֲלוּ אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה וַיָּבִאוּ אֹתוֹ אֶל־בֵּית אֲבִינָדָב בַּגִּבְעָה וְאֶת־אֶלְעָזָר בְּנוֹ קִדְּשׁוּ לִשְׁמֹר אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: The men of Kiriath-jearim came and took up the Ark of YHWH and brought it into the house of Abinadab on the hill; and they consecrated his son Eleazar to have charge of the Ark of YHWH.
verses.commentary:
So the north east folks come get the box and put it in a guy's house.

His name is Abinadab, which is like “father of generosity.”

In solemn religious language, they declare that his son is in charge of the box.

The son's name is Eleazar, which sort of means “God is helpful.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּבֹאוּ אַנְשֵׁי קִרְיַת יְעָרִים וַיַּעֲלוּ אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה וַיָּבִאוּ אֹתוֹ אֶל־בֵּית אֲבִינָדָב בַּגִּבְעָה וְאֶת־אֶלְעָזָר בְּנוֹ קִדְּשׁוּ לִשְׁמֹר אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה׃}
tex.commentary:
\aA{
		So the north east folks come get the box and put it in a
		guy's house.

		His name is Abinadab, which is like ``father of
		generosity.''

		In solemn religious language, they declare that his son
		is in charge of the box.

		The son's name is Eleazar, which sort of means ``God is
		helpful.''
	}

verses.original: וַיְהִי מִיּוֹם שֶׁבֶת הָאָרוֹן בְּקִרְיַת יְעָרִים וַיִּרְבּוּ הַיָּמִים וַיִּהְיוּ עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וַיִּנָּהוּ כּל־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחֲרֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: A long time elapsed from the day that the Ark was housed in Kiriath-jearim, twenty years in all; and all the House of Israel yearned after YHWH.
verses.commentary:
YHWH stays there for twenty years.

Israel missed him.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְהִי מִיּוֹם שֶׁבֶת הָאָרוֹן בְּקִרְיַת יְעָרִים וַיִּרְבּוּ הַיָּמִים וַיִּהְיוּ עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וַיִּנָּהוּ כּל־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל אַחֲרֵי יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־כּל־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר אִם־בְּכל־לְבַבְכֶם אַתֶּם שָׁבִים אֶל־יְהֹוָה הָסִירוּ אֶת־אֱלֹהֵי הַנֵּכָר מִתּוֹכְכֶם וְהָעַשְׁתָּרוֹת וְהָכִינוּ לְבַבְכֶם אֶל־יְהֹוָה וְעִבְדֻהוּ לְבַדּוֹ וְיַצֵּל אֶתְכֶם מִיַּד פְּלִשְׁתִּים׃
verses.english: And Samuel said to all the House of Israel, “If you mean to return to YHWH with all your heart, you must remove the alien gods and the Ashtaroth from your midst and direct your heart to YHWH and serve Him alone. Then He will deliver you from the hands of the Philistines.”
verses.commentary:
Samuel's back. I guess he hears the people saying they miss YHWH.

So he says they have to stop cheating on YHWH with other gods.

Then the war will be over. Apparently it's not over.

		the Ashtaroth from your midst and direct your heart to YHWH and
		serve Him alone. Then He will deliver you from the hands of the
		Philistines.”%
	}

verses.original: וַיָּסִירוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־הַבְּעָלִים וְאֶת־הָעַשְׁתָּרֹת וַיַּעַבְדוּ אֶת־יְהֹוָה לְבַדּוֹ׃
verses.english: And the Israelites removed the Baalim and Ashtaroth and they served YHWH alone.
verses.commentary: So they did.

tex.original: \hDtrH{וַיָּסִירוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־הַבְּעָלִים וְאֶת־הָעַשְׁתָּרֹת וַיַּעַבְדוּ אֶת־יְהֹוָה לְבַדּוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל קִבְצוּ אֶת־כּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמִּצְפָּתָה וְאֶתְפַּלֵּל בַּעַדְכֶם אֶל־יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Samuel said, “Assemble all Israel at Mizpah, and I will pray to YHWH for you.”
verses.commentary: Samuel puts everybody in one place so he can pray.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל קִבְצוּ אֶת־כּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמִּצְפָּתָה וְאֶתְפַּלֵּל בַּעַדְכֶם אֶל־יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקָּבְצוּ הַמִּצְפָּתָה וַיִּשְׁאֲבוּ־מַיִם וַיִּשְׁפְּכוּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וַיָּצוּמוּ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא וַיֹּאמְרוּ שָׁם חָטָאנוּ לַיהֹוָה וַיִּשְׁפֹּט שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּצְפָּה׃
verses.english: They assembled at Mizpah, and they drew water and poured it out before YHWH; they fasted that day, and there they confessed that they had sinned against YHWH. And Samuel acted as chieftain of the Israelites at Mizpah.
verses.commentary:
The people go where Samuel said, and they pour water on the ground.

They also don't eat, and they say they're sorry for being bad.

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים כִּי־הִתְקַבְּצוּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל הַמִּצְפָּתָה וַיַּעֲלוּ סַרְנֵי־פְלִשְׁתִּים אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּרְאוּ מִפְּנֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים׃
verses.english: When the Philistines heard that the Israelites had assembled at Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines marched out against Israel. Hearing of this, the Israelites were terrified of the Philistines
verses.commentary:
The Philistines hear that everybody's in one place, so they go out to get them.

Israel hears that this is happening and they're scared.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל אַל־תַּחֲרֵשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ מִזְּעֹק אֶל־יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְיֹשִׁעֵנוּ מִיַּד פְּלִשְׁתִּים׃
verses.english: and they implored Samuel, “Do not neglect us and do not refrain from crying out to YHWH our God to save us from the hands of the Philistines.”
verses.commentary: The people remind Samuel to also pray about helping them to not die.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמְרוּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל אַל־תַּחֲרֵשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ מִזְּעֹק אֶל־יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ וְיֹשִׁעֵנוּ מִיַּד פְּלִשְׁתִּים׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח שְׁמוּאֵל טְלֵה חָלָב אֶחָד (ויעלה) [וַיַּעֲלֵהוּ] עוֹלָה כָּלִיל לַיהֹוָה וַיִּזְעַק שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־יְהֹוָה בְּעַד יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיַּעֲנֵהוּ יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Thereupon Samuel took a suckling lamb and sacrificed it as a whole burnt offering to YHWH; and Samuel cried out to YHWH in behalf of Israel, and YHWH responded to him.
verses.commentary:
So he sets a sheep on fire and cries.

YHWH responds.

verses.original: וַיְהִי שְׁמוּאֵל מַעֲלֶה הָעוֹלָה וּפְלִשְׁתִּים נִגְּשׁוּ לַמִּלְחָמָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וַיַּרְעֵם יְהֹוָה בְּקוֹל־גָּדוֹל בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא עַל־פְּלִשְׁתִּים וַיְהֻמֵּם וַיִּנָּגְפוּ לִפְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: For as Samuel was presenting the burnt offering and the Philistines advanced to attack Israel, YHWH thundered mightily against the Philistines that day. He threw them into confusion, and they were routed by Israel.
verses.commentary: While Samuel is burning the sheep, YHWH thunders and confuses the Philistines.

verses.original: וַיֵּצְאוּ אַנְשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִן־הַמִּצְפָּה וַיִּרְדְּפוּ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּים וַיַּכּוּם עַד־מִתַּחַת לְבֵית כָּר׃
verses.english: The men of Israel sallied out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, striking them down to a point below Beth-car.
verses.commentary: Israel sees the tables have turned, and they go kill the Philistines.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֵּצְאוּ אַנְשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִן־הַמִּצְפָּה וַיִּרְדְּפוּ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּים וַיַּכּוּם עַד־מִתַּחַת לְבֵית כָּר׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח שְׁמוּאֵל אֶבֶן אַחַת וַיָּשֶׂם בֵּין־הַמִּצְפָּה וּבֵין הַשֵּׁן וַיִּקְרָא אֶת־שְׁמָהּ אֶבֶן הָעָזֶר וַיֹּאמַר עַד־הֵנָּה עֲזָרָנוּ יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen, and named it Eben-ezer: “For up to now,” he said, “YHWH has helped us.”
verses.commentary: Samuel takes a rock and names it Ebenezer, which means “helpful rock.”

verses.original: וַיִּכָּנְעוּ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּים וְלֹא־יָסְפוּ עוֹד לָבוֹא בִּגְבוּל יִשְׂרָאֵל וַתְּהִי יַד־יְהֹוָה בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּים כֹּל יְמֵי שְׁמוּאֵל׃
verses.english: The Philistines were humbled and did not invade the territory of Israel again; and the hand of YHWH was set against the Philistines as long as Samuel lived.
verses.commentary:
The Philistines decide not to invade anymore.

YHWH keeps punishing them until Samuel dies. [It's not clear why that's when. Presumably because of the prayer from earlier.]

verses.original: וַתָּשֹׁבְנָה הֶעָרִים אֲשֶׁר לָקְחוּ־פְלִשְׁתִּים מֵאֵת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעֶקְרוֹן וְעַד־גַּת וְאֶת־גְּבוּלָן הִצִּיל יִשְׂרָאֵל מִיַּד פְּלִשְׁתִּים וַיְהִי שָׁלוֹם בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל וּבֵין הָאֱמֹרִי׃
verses.english: The towns which the Philistines had taken from Israel, from Ekron to Gath, were restored to Israel; Israel recovered all her territory from the Philistines. There was also peace between Israel and the Amorites.
verses.commentary:
Israel gets its towns back.

Also there's peace between Israel and some people we haven't heard about since Judges 11.

It sounds like Samuel's about to die.

We're only 2 chapters into I Samuel.

verses.original: וּתְשֻׁבָתוֹ הָרָמָתָה כִּי־שָׁם בֵּיתוֹ וְשָׁם שָׁפָט אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּבֶן־שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Then he would return to Ramah, for his home was there, and there too he would judge Israel. He built an altar there to YHWH.

Then he would go home and keep doing the same thing.

He built an altar for YHWH.

End of chapter.

verses.english: When Samuel grew old, he appointed his sons judges over Israel.
verses.commentary: Sons of Sam.

verses.original: וַיְהִי שֶׁם־בְּנוֹ הַבְּכוֹר יוֹאֵל וְשֵׁם מִשְׁנֵהוּ אֲבִיָּה שֹׁפְטִים בִּבְאֵר שָׁבַע׃

verses.english: But his sons did not follow in his ways; they were bent on gain, they accepted bribes, and they subverted justice.
verses.commentary: Samuel follows in the tradition of Eli.

verses.english: All the elders of Israel assembled and came to Samuel at Ramah,
verses.commentary: So the old folks hold a meeting.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּתְקַבְּצוּ כֹּל זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיָּבֹאוּ אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל הָרָמָתָה׃}

verses.english: and they said to him, “You have grown old, and your sons have not followed your ways. Therefore appoint a king for us, to govern us like all other nations.”
verses.commentary: They say “We'd like a king please.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלָיו הִנֵּה אַתָּה זָקַנְתָּ וּבָנֶיךָ לֹא הָלְכוּ בִּדְרָכֶיךָ עַתָּה שִׂימָה־לָּנוּ מֶלֶךְ לְשׁפְטֵנוּ כְּכל־הַגּוֹיִם׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּרַע הַדָּבָר בְּעֵינֵי שְׁמוּאֵל כַּאֲשֶׁר אָמְרוּ תְּנָה־לָּנוּ מֶלֶךְ לְשׁפְטֵנוּ וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Samuel was displeased that they said “Give us a king to govern us.” Samuel prayed to YHWH,
verses.commentary: Samuel's not happy, so he asks YHWH for advice.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֵּרַע הַדָּבָר בְּעֵינֵי שְׁמוּאֵל כַּאֲשֶׁר אָמְרוּ תְּנָה־לָּנוּ מֶלֶךְ לְשׁפְטֵנוּ וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל שְׁמַע בְּקוֹל הָעָם לְכֹל אֲשֶׁר־יֹאמְרוּ אֵלֶיךָ כִּי לֹא אֹתְךָ מָאָסוּ כִּי־אֹתִי מָאֲסוּ מִמְּלֹךְ עֲלֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: and YHWH replied to Samuel, “Heed the demand of the people in everything they say to you. For it is not you that they have rejected; it is Me they have rejected as their king.
verses.commentary: YHWH's like “It's not you it's me.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל שְׁמַע בְּקוֹל הָעָם לְכֹל אֲשֶׁר־יֹאמְרוּ אֵלֶיךָ כִּי לֹא אֹתְךָ מָאָסוּ כִּי־אֹתִי מָאֲסוּ מִמְּלֹךְ עֲלֵיהֶם׃}

verses.english: Like everything else they have done ever since I brought them out of Egypt to this day—forsaking Me and worshiping other gods—so they are doing to you.
verses.commentary: This line feels sort of out of place.

tex.original: \hDtrH{כְּכל־הַמַּעֲשִׂים אֲשֶׁר־עָשׂוּ מִיּוֹם הַעֲלֹתִי אוֹתָם מִמִּצְרַיִם וְעַד־הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה וַיַּעַזְבֻנִי וַיַּעַבְדוּ אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים כֵּן הֵמָּה עֹשִׂים גַּם־לָךְ׃}

verses.commentary: Ok so YHWH's like “Do it, but remind them what kings do.”

verses.commentary: So Samuel does.

verses.commentary: Samuel's like “Look, kings take your sons.”

verses.original: וְלָשׂוּם לוֹ שָׂרֵי אֲלָפִים וְשָׂרֵי חֲמִשִּׁים וְלַחֲרֹשׁ חֲרִישׁוֹ וְלִקְצֹר קְצִירוֹ וְלַעֲשׂוֹת כְּלֵי־מִלְחַמְתּוֹ וּכְלֵי רִכְבּוֹ׃
verses.english: He will appoint them as his chiefs of thousands and of fifties; or they will have to plow his fields, reap his harvest, and make his weapons and the equipment for his chariots.
verses.commentary: “He makes them leaders or farmers or weapon makers or whatever he wants, he's a king.”

verses.original: וְאֶת־בְּנוֹתֵיכֶם יִקָּח לְרַקָּחוֹת וּלְטַבָּחוֹת וּלְאֹפוֹת׃
verses.english: He will take your daughters as perfumers, cooks, and bakers.
verses.commentary:
“Also he'll take your daughters...”

(The people's ears perk up, as Samuel seems like he's maybe making a good point here. Then Samuel continues.)

“...and make them smell good and cook.”

(Cut to the crowd, confused about Samuel's strategy in this argument.)

tex.original: \hJ{וְאֶת־בְּנוֹתֵיכֶם יִקָּח לְרַקָּחוֹת וּלְטַבָּחוֹת וּלְאֹפוֹת׃}

verses.original: וְאֶת־שְׂדוֹתֵיכֶם וְאֶת־כַּרְמֵיכֶם וְזֵיתֵיכֶם הַטּוֹבִים יִקָּח וְנָתַן לַעֲבָדָיו׃
verses.english: He will seize your choice fields, vineyards, and olive groves, and give them to his courtiers.
verses.commentary: Argument getting slightly more convincing.

tex.original: \hJ{וְאֶת־שְׂדוֹתֵיכֶם וְאֶת־כַּרְמֵיכֶם וְזֵיתֵיכֶם הַטּוֹבִים יִקָּח וְנָתַן לַעֲבָדָיו׃}

verses.original: וְזַרְעֵיכֶם וְכַרְמֵיכֶם יַעְשֹׂר וְנָתַן לְסָרִיסָיו וְלַעֲבָדָיו׃
verses.english: He will take a tenth part of your grain and vintage and give it to his eunuchs and courtiers.
verses.commentary:
Ten percent.

You know, the amount that the Levites have been taking from the people since Egypt.

So basically no new taxes.

Argument not going great for Samuel.

verses.english: He will take your male and female slaves, your choice young men, and your asses, and put them to work for him.
verses.commentary: No giggling from the crowd please, show some respect.

tex.original: \hJ{וְאֶת־עַבְדֵיכֶם וְאֶת־שִׁפְחוֹתֵיכֶם וְאֶת־בַּחוּרֵיכֶם הַטּוֹבִים וְאֶת־חֲמוֹרֵיכֶם יִקָּח וְעָשָׂה לִמְלַאכְתּוֹ׃}

verses.original: צֹאנְכֶם יַעְשֹׂר וְאַתֶּם תִּהְיוּ־לוֹ לַעֲבָדִים׃
verses.english: He will take a tenth part of your flocks, and you shall become his slaves.
verses.commentary: Ten percent again.

tex.original: \hJ{צֹאנְכֶם יַעְשֹׂר וְאַתֶּם תִּהְיוּ־לוֹ לַעֲבָדִים׃}

verses.original: וּזְעַקְתֶּם בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא מִלִּפְנֵי מַלְכְּכֶם אֲשֶׁר בְּחַרְתֶּם לָכֶם וְלֹא־יַעֲנֶה יְהֹוָה אֶתְכֶם בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא׃
verses.english: The day will come when you cry out because of the king whom you yourselves have chosen; and YHWH will not answer you on that day.”
verses.commentary: So in summary, says Samuel, eventually you're gonna miss me and regret asking for a king but don't go crying to YHWH, he won't answer.

verses.original: וַיְמָאֲנוּ הָעָם לִשְׁמֹעַ בְּקוֹל שְׁמוּאֵל וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֹּא כִּי אִם־מֶלֶךְ יִהְיֶה עָלֵינוּ׃
verses.english: But the people would not listen to Samuel’s warning. “No,” they said. “We must have a king over us,
verses.commentary:
The people aren't convinced.

They still want a king.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְמָאֲנוּ הָעָם לִשְׁמֹעַ בְּקוֹל שְׁמוּאֵל וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֹּא כִּי אִם־מֶלֶךְ יִהְיֶה עָלֵינוּ׃}

verses.original: וְהָיִינוּ גַם־אֲנַחְנוּ כְּכל־הַגּוֹיִם וּשְׁפָטָנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ וְיָצָא לְפָנֵינוּ וְנִלְחַם אֶת־מִלְחֲמֹתֵנוּ׃
verses.english: that we may be like all the other nations: Let our king rule over us and go out at our head and fight our battles.”
verses.commentary:
And their reasons are, and I quote:

1. Because all the other nations are doing it, and 2. So he'll go out and fight our wars for us.

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁמַע שְׁמוּאֵל אֵת כּל־דִּבְרֵי הָעָם וַיְדַבְּרֵם בְּאזְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: When Samuel heard all that the people said, he reported it to YHWH.
verses.commentary:
So Samuel goes and tells YHWH what the people said.

Presumably YHWH was doing something else at the time.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל שְׁמַע בְּקוֹלָם וְהִמְלַכְתָּ לָהֶם מֶלֶךְ וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־אַנְשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכוּ אִישׁ לְעִירוֹ׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Samuel, “Heed their demands and appoint a king for them.” Samuel then said to the men of Israel, “All of you go home.”

So YHWH's like “Well, do it.”

Then Samuel looks over at the people (apparently they're still here) and he's like “All of you go home.”

verses.original: וַיְהִי־אִישׁ (מבן ימין) [מִבִּנְיָמִין] וּשְׁמוֹ קִישׁ בֶּן־אֲבִיאֵל בֶּן־צְרוֹר בֶּן־בְּכוֹרַת בֶּן־אֲפִיחַ בֶּן־אִישׁ יְמִינִי גִּבּוֹר חָיִל׃

verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

There's this guy named Kish.

He's got substance.

Also ancestors.

verses.english: He had a son whose name was Saul, an excellent young man; no one among the Israelites was handsomer than he; he was a head taller than any of the people.
verses.commentary:
He has a son named Saul.

Saul's the tallest guy in town.

Best looking too.

verses.original: וַתֹּאבַדְנָה הָאֲתֹנוֹת לְקִישׁ אֲבִי שָׁאוּל וַיֹּאמֶר קִישׁ אֶל־שָׁאוּל בְּנוֹ קַח־נָא אִתְּךָ אֶת־אַחַד מֵהַנְּעָרִים וְקוּם לֵךְ בַּקֵּשׁ אֶת־הָאֲתֹנֹת׃
verses.english: Once the asses of Saul’s father Kish went astray, and Kish said to his son Saul, “Take along one of the servants and go out and look for the asses.”
verses.commentary:
Saul's dad has some ass retention problems.

So he asks Saul for help.

Saul's apparently better at that.

verses.original: וַיַּעֲבֹר בְּהַר־אֶפְרַיִם וַיַּעֲבֹר בְּאֶרֶץ־שָׁלִשָׁה וְלֹא מָצָאוּ וַיַּעַבְרוּ בְאֶרֶץ־שַׁעֲלִים וָאַיִן וַיַּעֲבֹר בְּאֶרֶץ־יְמִינִי וְלֹא מָצָאוּ׃
verses.english: He passed into the hill country of Ephraim. He crossed the district of Shalishah, but they did not find them. They passed through the district of Shaalim, but they were not there. They traversed the [entire] territory of Benjamin, and still they did not find them.
verses.commentary: So Saul goes around chasing ass. No success.

verses.original: הֵמָּה בָּאוּ בְּאֶרֶץ צוּף וְשָׁאוּל אָמַר לְנַעֲרוֹ אֲשֶׁר־עִמּוֹ לְכָה וְנָשׁוּבָה פֶּן־יֶחְדַּל אָבִי מִן־הָאֲתֹנוֹת וְדָאַג לָנוּ׃
verses.english: When they reached the district of Zuph, Saul said to the servant who was with him, “Let us turn back, or my father will stop worrying about the asses and begin to worry about us.”
verses.commentary: Eventually Saul's like “Dad's ass is still lost and now my ass is lost.”

tex.original: \hX{הֵמָּה בָּאוּ בְּאֶרֶץ צוּף וְשָׁאוּל אָמַר לְנַעֲרוֹ אֲשֶׁר־עִמּוֹ לְכָה וְנָשׁוּבָה פֶּן־יֶחְדַּל אָבִי מִן־הָאֲתֹנוֹת וְדָאַג לָנוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ הִנֵּה־נָא אִישׁ־אֱלֹהִים בָּעִיר הַזֹּאת וְהָאִישׁ נִכְבָּד כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יְדַבֵּר בּוֹא יָבוֹא עַתָּה נֵלְכָה שָּׁם אוּלַי יַגִּיד לָנוּ אֶת־דַּרְכֵּנוּ אֲשֶׁר־הָלַכְנוּ עָלֶיהָ׃
verses.english: But he replied, “There is a man of God in that town, and the man is highly esteemed; everything that he says comes true. Let us go there; perhaps he will tell us about the errand on which we set out.”
verses.commentary: But his assistant says “There's a guy up here who's really good at guessing. Let's go there. Maybe be can guess where the asses are.”

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל לְנַעֲרוֹ וְהִנֵּה נֵלֵךְ וּמַה־נָּבִיא לָאִישׁ כִּי הַלֶּחֶם אָזַל מִכֵּלֵינוּ וּתְשׁוּרָה אֵין־לְהָבִיא לְאִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים מָה אִתָּנוּ׃
verses.english: “But if we go,” Saul said to his servant, “what can we bring the man? For the food in our bags is all gone, and there is nothing we can bring to the man of God as a present. What have we got?”
verses.commentary:
Saul wants to bring a present.

Saul is the present, but don't tell him.

verses.english: The servant answered Saul again, “I happen to have a quarter-shekel of silver. I can give that to the man of God and he will tell us about our errand.”—
verses.commentary: The servant's like “Here, I have some money. Men of God love money.”

verses.original: לְפָנִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כֹּה־אָמַר הָאִישׁ בְּלֶכְתּוֹ לִדְרוֹשׁ אֱלֹהִים לְכוּ וְנֵלְכָה עַד־הָרֹאֶה כִּי לַנָּבִיא הַיּוֹם יִקָּרֵא לְפָנִים הָרֹאֶה׃
verses.english: Formerly in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God, he would say, “Come, let us go to the seer,” for the prophet of today was formerly called a seer.—
verses.commentary: “Side Note: Prophets used to be called seers,” says the bible. Thanks bible. That's good to know.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל לְנַעֲרוֹ טוֹב דְּבָרְךָ לְכָה נֵלֵכָה וַיֵּלְכוּ אֶל־הָעִיר אֲשֶׁר־שָׁם אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים׃
verses.english: Saul said to his servant, “A good idea; let us go.” And they went to the town where the man of God lived.
verses.commentary: Saul says “Good idea” and they go to find the guy.

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל לְנַעֲרוֹ טוֹב דְּבָרְךָ לְכָה נֵלֵכָה וַיֵּלְכוּ אֶל־הָעִיר אֲשֶׁר־שָׁם אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים׃}

verses.original: הֵמָּה עֹלִים בְּמַעֲלֵה הָעִיר וְהֵמָּה מָצְאוּ נְעָרוֹת יֹצְאוֹת לִשְׁאֹב מָיִם וַיֹּאמְרוּ לָהֶן הֲיֵשׁ בָּזֶה הָרֹאֶה׃
verses.english: As they were climbing the ascent to the town, they met some girls coming out to draw water, and they asked them, “Is the seer in town?”
verses.commentary:
Along the way, there's a well, and surprise surprise, they meet some girls.

I think this is the fourth time in the bible we've met girls at a well.

So they ask if the seer is here.

verses.original: וַתַּעֲנֶינָה אוֹתָם וַתֹּאמַרְנָה יֵּשׁ הִנֵּה לְפָנֶיךָ מַהֵר עַתָּה כִּי הַיּוֹם בָּא לָעִיר כִּי זֶבַח הַיּוֹם לָעָם בַּבָּמָה׃
verses.english: “Yes,” they replied. “He is up there ahead of you. Hurry, for he has just come to the town because the people have a sacrifice at the shrine today.
verses.commentary: The girls are like “Yeah but hurry up he's just here for a meeting.”

tex.original: \hX{וַתַּעֲנֶינָה אוֹתָם וַתֹּאמַרְנָה יֵּשׁ הִנֵּה לְפָנֶיךָ מַהֵר עַתָּה כִּי הַיּוֹם בָּא לָעִיר כִּי זֶבַח הַיּוֹם לָעָם בַּבָּמָה׃}

verses.original: כְּבֹאֲכֶם הָעִיר כֵּן תִּמְצְאוּן אֹתוֹ בְּטֶרֶם יַעֲלֶה הַבָּמָתָה לֶאֱכֹל כִּי לֹא־יֹאכַל הָעָם עַד־בֹּאוֹ כִּי־הוּא יְבָרֵךְ הַזֶּבַח אַחֲרֵי־כֵן יֹאכְלוּ הַקְּרֻאִים וְעַתָּה עֲלוּ כִּי־אֹתוֹ כְהַיּוֹם תִּמְצְאוּן אֹתוֹ׃
verses.english: As soon as you enter the town, you will find him before he goes up to the shrine to eat; the people will not eat until he comes; for he must first bless the sacrifice and only then will the guests eat. Go up at once, for you will find him right away.”
verses.commentary: “Catch him on the way to dinner,” say the girls.

verses.original: וַיַּעֲלוּ הָעִיר הֵמָּה בָּאִים בְּתוֹךְ הָעִיר וְהִנֵּה שְׁמוּאֵל יֹצֵא לִקְרָאתָם לַעֲלוֹת הַבָּמָה׃
verses.english: So they went up to the town; and as they were entering the town, Samuel came out toward them, on his way up to the shrine.
verses.commentary: So they do that. Out comes Samuel.

verses.original: כָּעֵת מָחָר אֶשְׁלַח אֵלֶיךָ אִישׁ מֵאֶרֶץ בִּנְיָמִן וּמְשַׁחְתּוֹ לְנָגִיד עַל־עַמִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהוֹשִׁיעַ אֶת־עַמִּי מִיַּד פְּלִשְׁתִּים כִּי רָאִיתִי אֶת־עַמִּי כִּי בָּאָה צַעֲקָתוֹ אֵלָי׃
verses.english: “At this time tomorrow, I will send a man to you from the territory of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him ruler of My people Israel. He will deliver My people from the hands of the Philistines; for I have taken note of My people, their outcry has come to Me.”
verses.commentary: “I'll send you the king you're looking for tomorrow. He's from the war tribe.”

tex.english:

verses.commentary: Saul's like “Pardon me sir, have you seen the seer?”

verses.english: And Samuel answered Saul, “I am the seer. Go up ahead of me to the shrine, for you shall eat with me today; and in the morning I will let you go, after telling you whatever may be on your mind.
verses.commentary: Samuel's like “That's me” and invites him to dinner.

verses.original: וְלָאֲתֹנוֹת הָאֹבְדוֹת לְךָ הַיּוֹם שְׁלֹשֶׁת הַיָּמִים אַל־תָּשֶׂם אֶת־לִבְּךָ לָהֶם כִּי נִמְצָאוּ וּלְמִי כּל־חֶמְדַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל הֲלוֹא לְךָ וּלְכֹל בֵּית אָבִיךָ׃
verses.english: As for your asses that strayed three days ago, do not concern yourself about them, for they have been found. And for whom is all Israel yearning, if not for you and all your ancestral house?”
verses.commentary: “And by the way I know about your ass problem and it's taken care of. By the way Israel is yearning for you.”

verses.original: וַיַּעַן שָׁאוּל וַיֹּאמֶר הֲלוֹא בֶן־יְמִינִי אָנֹכִי מִקְּטַנֵּי שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמִשְׁפַּחְתִּי הַצְּעִרָה מִכּל־מִשְׁפְּחוֹת שִׁבְטֵי בִנְיָמִן וְלָמָּה דִּבַּרְתָּ אֵלַי כַּדָּבָר הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: Saul replied, “But I am only a Benjaminite, from the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and my clan is the least of all the clans of the tribe of Benjamin! Why do you say such things to me?”
verses.commentary: Saul is like “You realize I'm not famous right?”

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־שָׁאוּל וְאֶת־נַעֲרוֹ וַיְבִיאֵם לִשְׁכָּתָה וַיִּתֵּן לָהֶם מָקוֹם בְּרֹאשׁ הַקְּרוּאִים וְהֵמָּה כִּשְׁלֹשִׁם אִישׁ׃
verses.english: Samuel took Saul and his servant and brought them into the hall, and gave them a place at the head of the guests, who numbered about thirty.
verses.commentary: Samuel's like “Yes yes follow me, you'll be sitting in the good seats.”

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּקַּח שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־שָׁאוּל וְאֶת־נַעֲרוֹ וַיְבִיאֵם לִשְׁכָּתָה וַיִּתֵּן לָהֶם מָקוֹם בְּרֹאשׁ הַקְּרוּאִים וְהֵמָּה כִּשְׁלֹשִׁם אִישׁ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל לַטַּבָּח תְּנָה אֶת־הַמָּנָה אֲשֶׁר נָתַתִּי לָךְ אֲשֶׁר אָמַרְתִּי אֵלֶיךָ שִׂים אֹתָהּ עִמָּךְ׃
verses.english: And Samuel said to the cook, “Bring the portion which I gave you and told you to set aside.”
verses.commentary: Then Samuel's like “Bring out that food I had you hide earlier.”

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל לַטַּבָּח תְּנָה אֶת־הַמָּנָה אֲשֶׁר נָתַתִּי לָךְ אֲשֶׁר אָמַרְתִּי אֵלֶיךָ שִׂים אֹתָהּ עִמָּךְ׃}

verses.original: וַיָּרֶם הַטַּבָּח אֶת־הַשּׁוֹק וְהֶעָלֶיהָ וַיָּשֶׂם לִפְנֵי שָׁאוּל וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֵּה הַנִּשְׁאָר שִׂים־לְפָנֶיךָ אֱכֹל כִּי לַמּוֹעֵד שָׁמוּר־לְךָ לֵאמֹר הָעָם קָרָאתִי וַיֹּאכַל שָׁאוּל עִם־שְׁמוּאֵל בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא׃
verses.english: The cook lifted up the thigh and what was on it, and set it before Saul. And [Samuel] said, “What has been reserved is set before you. Eat; it has been kept for you for this occasion, when I said I was inviting the people.” So Saul ate with Samuel that day.
verses.commentary:
The cook lifts up someone's thigh, which is either the food or the hiding place, hopefully the former.

Then they eat.

verses.original: וַיֵּרְדוּ מֵהַבָּמָה הָעִיר וַיְדַבֵּר עִם־שָׁאוּל עַל־הַגָּג׃
verses.english: They then descended from the shrine to the town, and [Samuel] talked with Saul on the roof.
verses.commentary: After dinner they have a chat on the roof.

tex.original: \hX{וַיֵּרְדוּ מֵהַבָּמָה הָעִיר וַיְדַבֵּר עִם־שָׁאוּל עַל־הַגָּג׃}

verses.original: וַיַּשְׁכִּמוּ וַיְהִי כַּעֲלוֹת הַשַּׁחַר וַיִּקְרָא שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־שָׁאוּל (הגג) [הַגָּגָה] לֵאמֹר קוּמָה וַאֲשַׁלְּחֶךָּ וַיָּקם שָׁאוּל וַיֵּצְאוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם הוּא וּשְׁמוּאֵל הַחוּצָה׃
verses.english: Early, at the break of day, Samuel called to Saul on the roof. He said, “Get up, and I will send you off.” Saul arose, and the two of them, Samuel and he, went outside.
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

Cut to morning. Apparently Saul slept on the roof and it's time to wake up and say goodbye.

verses.original: הֵמָּה יוֹרְדִים בִּקְצֵה הָעִיר וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר אֶל־שָׁאוּל אֱמֹר לַנַּעַר וְיַעֲבֹר לְפָנֵינוּ וַיַּעֲבֹר וְאַתָּה עֲמֹד כַּיּוֹם וְאַשְׁמִיעֲךָ אֶת־דְּבַר אֱלֹהִים׃
verses.english: As they were walking toward the end of the town, Samuel said to Saul, “Tell the servant to walk ahead of us”—and he walked ahead—“but you stop here a moment and I will make known to you the word of God.”
verses.commentary:
And as he's sending them off, Samuel says he needs to say something to Saul in private.

Cliffhanger.

End of chapter.

tex.original: \hX{הֵמָּה יוֹרְדִים בִּקְצֵה הָעִיר וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר אֶל־שָׁאוּל אֱמֹר לַנַּעַר וְיַעֲבֹר לְפָנֵינוּ וַיַּעֲבֹר וְאַתָּה עֲמֹד כַּיּוֹם וְאַשְׁמִיעֲךָ אֶת־דְּבַר אֱלֹהִים׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־פַּךְ הַשֶּׁמֶן וַיִּצֹק עַל־רֹאשׁוֹ וַיִּשָּׁקֵהוּ וַיֹּאמֶר הֲלוֹא כִּי־מְשָׁחֲךָ יְהֹוָה עַל־נַחֲלָתוֹ לְנָגִיד׃
verses.english: Samuel took a flask of oil and poured some on Saul’s head and kissed him, and said, “YHWH herewith anoints you ruler over His own people.
verses.commentary:
Previously, on bible: Samuel needed a private moment with Saul.

Now, safely in private, Samuel pours some oil on Saul's head and says “YHWH says you're king now.”

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּקַּח שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־פַּךְ הַשֶּׁמֶן וַיִּצֹק עַל־רֹאשׁוֹ וַיִּשָּׁקֵהוּ וַיֹּאמֶר הֲלוֹא כִּי־מְשָׁחֲךָ יְהֹוָה עַל־נַחֲלָתוֹ לְנָגִיד׃}

verses.original: בְּלֶכְתְּךָ הַיּוֹם מֵעִמָּדִי וּמָצָאתָ שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים עִם־קְבֻרַת רָחֵל בִּגְבוּל בִּנְיָמִן בְּצֶלְצַח וְאָמְרוּ אֵלֶיךָ נִמְצְאוּ הָאֲתֹנוֹת אֲשֶׁר הָלַכְתָּ לְבַקֵּשׁ וְהִנֵּה נָטַשׁ אָבִיךָ אֶת־דִּבְרֵי הָאֲתֹנוֹת וְדָאַג לָכֶם לֵאמֹר מָה אֶעֱשֶׂה לִבְנִי׃
verses.english: When you leave me today, you will meet two men near the tomb of Rachel in the territory of Benjamin, at Zelzah, and they will tell you that the asses you set out to look for have been found, and that your father has stopped being concerned about the asses and is worrying about you, saying: ‘What shall I do about my son?’
verses.commentary:
“By the way your asses are near Rachel's grave.”

“Also your dad's not worried about you.”

Samuel basically took care of everything.

tex.english:
\eX{
		When you leave me today, you will meet two men near the tomb of
		Rachel in the territory of Benjamin, at Zelzah, and they will tell
		you that the asses you set out to look for have been found, and
		that your father has stopped being concerned about the asses and
		is worrying about you, saying: ‘What shall I do about my son?’
	}

verses.original: וְחָלַפְתָּ מִשָּׁם וָהָלְאָה וּבָאתָ עַד־אֵלוֹן תָּבוֹר וּמְצָאוּךָ שָּׁם שְׁלֹשָׁה אֲנָשִׁים עֹלִים אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִים בֵּית־אֵל אֶחָד נֹשֵׂא שְׁלֹשָׁה גְדָיִים וְאֶחָד נֹשֵׂא שְׁלֹשֶׁת כִּכְּרוֹת לֶחֶם וְאֶחָד נֹשֵׂא נֵבֶל־יָיִן׃
verses.english: You shall pass on from there until you come to the terebinth of Tabor. There you will be met by three men making a pilgrimage to God at Bethel. One will be carrying three kids, another will be carrying three loaves of bread, and the third will be carrying a jar of wine.
verses.commentary:
“Then keep walking and you'll see: 1. three guys with 2. three kids and 3. three breads and 4. well... one wine.”

(Something happened to that wine.)

(We don't get to know what.)

tex.english:
\eX{
		You shall pass on from there until you come to the terebinth of
		Tabor. There you will be met by three men making a pilgrimage to
		God at Bethel. One will be carrying three kids, another will be
		carrying three loaves of bread, and the third will be carrying a
		jar of wine.
	}

verses.original: וְשָׁאֲלוּ לְךָ לְשָׁלוֹם וְנָתְנוּ לְךָ שְׁתֵּי־לֶחֶם וְלָקַחְתָּ מִיָּדָם׃
verses.english: They will greet you and offer you two loaves of bread, which you shall accept.
verses.commentary: You get two of the breads.

tex.original: \hX{וְשָׁאֲלוּ לְךָ לְשָׁלוֹם וְנָתְנוּ לְךָ שְׁתֵּי־לֶחֶם וְלָקַחְתָּ מִיָּדָם׃}

verses.original: אַחַר כֵּן תָּבוֹא גִּבְעַת הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר־שָׁם נְצִבֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים וִיהִי כְבֹאֲךָ שָׁם הָעִיר וּפָגַעְתָּ חֶבֶל נְבִאִים יֹרְדִים מֵהַבָּמָה וְלִפְנֵיהֶם נֵבֶל וְתֹף וְחָלִיל וְכִנּוֹר וְהֵמָּה מִתְנַבְּאִים׃
verses.english: After that, you are to go on to the Hill of God, where the Philistine prefects reside. There, as you enter the town, you will encounter a band of prophets coming down from the shrine, preceded by lyres, timbrels, flutes, and harps, and they will be speaking in ecstasy.
verses.commentary: After that, keep walking and you'll see some musicians and some creative types.

tex.english:
\eX{
		After that, you are to go on to the Hill of God, where the
		Philistine prefects reside. There, as you enter the town, you will
		encounter a band of prophets coming down from the shrine, preceded
		by lyres, timbrels, flutes, and harps, and they will be speaking
		in ecstasy.
	}

verses.original: וְצָלְחָה עָלֶיךָ רוּחַ יְהֹוָה וְהִתְנַבִּיתָ עִמָּם וְנֶהְפַּכְתָּ לְאִישׁ אַחֵר׃
verses.english: The spirit of YHWH will grip you, and you will speak in ecstasy along with them; you will become another man.
verses.commentary: Blend in.

tex.original: \hX{וְצָלְחָה עָלֶיךָ רוּחַ יְהֹוָה וְהִתְנַבִּיתָ עִמָּם וְנֶהְפַּכְתָּ לְאִישׁ אַחֵר׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה כִּי (תבאינה) [תָבֹאנָה] הָאֹתוֹת הָאֵלֶּה לָךְ עֲשֵׂה לְךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּמְצָא יָדֶךָ כִּי הָאֱלֹהִים עִמָּךְ׃
verses.english: And once these signs have happened to you, act when the occasion arises, for God is with you.
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

After that, just act when the occasion arises and you're done.

tex.original: \hX{וְהָיָה כִּי (תבאינה) [תָבֹאנָה] הָאֹתוֹת הָאֵלֶּה לָךְ עֲשֵׂה לְךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּמְצָא יָדֶךָ כִּי הָאֱלֹהִים עִמָּךְ׃}

verses.original: וְיָרַדְתָּ לְפָנַי הַגִּלְגָּל וְהִנֵּה אָנֹכִי יֹרֵד אֵלֶיךָ לְהַעֲלוֹת עֹלוֹת לִזְבֹּחַ זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תּוֹחֵל עַד־בּוֹאִי אֵלֶיךָ וְהוֹדַעְתִּי לְךָ אֵת אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה׃
verses.english: After that, you are to go down to Gilgal ahead of me, and I will come down to you to present burnt offerings and offer sacrifices of well-being. Wait seven days until I come to you and instruct you what you are to do next.”
verses.commentary: Then we have the ceremony where we make it all official.

verses.original: וְהָיָה כְּהַפְנֹתוֹ שִׁכְמוֹ לָלֶכֶת מֵעִם שְׁמוּאֵל וַיַּהֲפךְ־לוֹ אֱלֹהִים לֵב אַחֵר וַיָּבֹאוּ כּל־הָאֹתוֹת הָאֵלֶּה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא׃
verses.english: As [Saul] turned around to leave Samuel, God gave him another heart; and all those signs were fulfilled that same day.
verses.commentary: Ok so all the stuff above happens.

tex.original: \hX{וְהָיָה כְּהַפְנֹתוֹ שִׁכְמוֹ לָלֶכֶת מֵעִם שְׁמוּאֵל וַיַּהֲפךְ־לוֹ אֱלֹהִים לֵב אַחֵר וַיָּבֹאוּ כּל־הָאֹתוֹת הָאֵלֶּה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ שָׁם הַגִּבְעָתָה וְהִנֵּה חֶבֶל־נְבִאִים לִקְרָאתוֹ וַתִּצְלַח עָלָיו רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים וַיִּתְנַבֵּא בְּתוֹכָם׃
verses.english: And when they came there, to the Hill, he saw a band of prophets coming toward him. Thereupon the spirit of God gripped him, and he spoke in ecstasy among them.
verses.commentary: He blends in and gets creative.

tex.original: \hX{וַיָּבֹאוּ שָׁם הַגִּבְעָתָה וְהִנֵּה חֶבֶל־נְבִאִים לִקְרָאתוֹ וַתִּצְלַח עָלָיו רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים וַיִּתְנַבֵּא בְּתוֹכָם׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי כּל־יוֹדְעוֹ מֵאִתְּמוֹל שִׁלְשֹׁם וַיִּרְאוּ וְהִנֵּה עִם־נְבִאִים נִבָּאוַיֹּאמֶר הָעָם אִישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵהוּ מַה־זֶּה הָיָה לְבֶן־קִישׁ הֲגַם שָׁאוּל בַּנְּבִיאִים׃
verses.english: When all who knew him previously saw him speaking in ecstasy together with the prophets, the people said to one another, “What’s happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul too among the prophets?”
verses.commentary: His friends say this is pretty unusual behavior for Saul.

tex.original: \hX{וַיְהִי כּל־יוֹדְעוֹ מֵאִתְּמוֹל שִׁלְשֹׁם וַיִּרְאוּ וְהִנֵּה עִם־נְבִאִים נִבָּאוַיֹּאמֶר הָעָם אִישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵהוּ מַה־זֶּה הָיָה לְבֶן־קִישׁ הֲגַם שָׁאוּל בַּנְּבִיאִים׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעַן אִישׁ מִשָּׁם וַיֹּאמֶר וּמִי אֲבִיהֶם עַל־כֵּן הָיְתָה לְמָשָׁל הֲגַם שָׁאוּל בַּנְּבִאִים׃
verses.english: But another person there spoke up and said, “And who are their fathers?” Thus the proverb arose: “Is Saul too among the prophets?”
verses.commentary: And that's why we say “Is X among the prophets” when your friend X is acting strange.

tex.original: \hX{וַיַּעַן אִישׁ מִשָּׁם וַיֹּאמֶר וּמִי אֲבִיהֶם עַל־כֵּן הָיְתָה לְמָשָׁל הֲגַם שָׁאוּל בַּנְּבִאִים׃}

verses.original: וַיְכַל מֵהִתְנַבּוֹת וַיָּבֹא הַבָּמָה׃
verses.english: And when he stopped speaking in ecstasy, he entered the shrine.
verses.commentary: Ok so Saul goes back to acting normal and goes into the shrine.

tex.original: \hX{וַיְכַל מֵהִתְנַבּוֹת וַיָּבֹא הַבָּמָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר דּוֹד שָׁאוּל אֵלָיו וְאֶל־נַעֲרוֹ אָן הֲלַכְתֶּם וַיֹּאמֶר לְבַקֵּשׁ אֶת־הָאֲתֹנוֹת וַנִּרְאֶה כִי־אַיִן וַנָּבוֹא אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל׃
verses.english: Saul’s uncle asked him and his servant, “Where did you go?” “To look for the asses,” he replied. “And when we saw that they were not to be found, we went to Samuel.”
verses.commentary:
Saul's uncle asks where they've been.

They explain.

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר דּוֹד שָׁאוּל אֵלָיו וְאֶל־נַעֲרוֹ אָן הֲלַכְתֶּם וַיֹּאמֶר לְבַקֵּשׁ אֶת־הָאֲתֹנוֹת וַנִּרְאֶה כִי־אַיִן וַנָּבוֹא אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר דּוֹד שָׁאוּל הַגִּידָה־נָּא לִי מָה־אָמַר לָכֶם שְׁמוּאֵל׃
verses.english: “Tell me,” said Saul’s uncle, “what did Samuel say to you?”
verses.commentary: “What do you talk about?”

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר דּוֹד שָׁאוּל הַגִּידָה־נָּא לִי מָה־אָמַר לָכֶם שְׁמוּאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל אֶל־דּוֹדוֹ הַגֵּד הִגִּיד לָנוּ כִּי נִמְצְאוּ הָאֲתֹנוֹת וְאֶת־דְּבַר הַמְּלוּכָה לֹא־הִגִּיד לוֹ אֲשֶׁר אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל׃
verses.english: Saul answered his uncle, “He just told us that the asses had been found.” But he did not tell him anything of what Samuel had said about the kingship.
verses.commentary: “Nothing. Just ass stuff.”

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל אֶל־דּוֹדוֹ הַגֵּד הִגִּיד לָנוּ כִּי נִמְצְאוּ הָאֲתֹנוֹת וְאֶת־דְּבַר הַמְּלוּכָה לֹא־הִגִּיד לוֹ אֲשֶׁר אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיַּצְעֵק שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־הָעָם אֶל־יְהֹוָה הַמִּצְפָּה׃
verses.english: Samuel summoned the people to YHWH at Mizpah
verses.commentary:
Ok so the people have asked for a king, and Samuel's ready to give them one.

So Samuel tells the people to come to where YHWH is.

I guess it's easier to move the people than to move YHWH.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּצְעֵק שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־הָעָם אֶל־יְהֹוָה הַמִּצְפָּה׃}
tex.english: \eJ{Samuel summoned the people to YHWH at Mizpah}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵלכֹּה־אָמַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָנֹכִי הֶעֱלֵיתִי אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרָיִם וָאַצִּיל אֶתְכֶם מִיַּד מִצְרַיִם וּמִיַּד כּל־הַמַּמְלָכוֹת הַלֹּחֲצִים אֶתְכֶם׃
verses.english: and said to them, “Thus said YHWH, the God of Israel: ‘I brought Israel out of Egypt, and I delivered you from the hands of the Egyptians and of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.’
verses.commentary: To start the ceremony, Samuel says that YHWH said a thing reminding the people of who he is and what they've been through together.

verses.original: וְאַתֶּם הַיּוֹם מְאַסְתֶּם אֶת־אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲשֶׁר־הוּא מוֹשִׁיעַ לָכֶם מִכּל־רָעוֹתֵיכֶם וְצָרֹתֵיכֶם וַתֹּאמְרוּ לוֹ כִּי־מֶלֶךְ תָּשִׂים עָלֵינוּ וְעַתָּה הִתְיַצְּבוּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לְשִׁבְטֵיכֶם וּלְאַלְפֵיכֶם׃
verses.english: But today you have rejected your God who delivered you from all your troubles and calamities. For you said, ‘No, set up a king over us!’ Now station yourselves before YHWH, by your tribes and clans.”
verses.commentary:
Then Samuel says “Today you have rejected your God.”

The party's taken an awkward turn.

verses.original: וַיַּקְרֵב שְׁמוּאֵל אֵת כּל־שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּלָּכֵד שֵׁבֶט בִּנְיָמִן׃
verses.english: Samuel brought forward each of the tribes of Israel, and the lot indicated the tribe of Benjamin.
verses.commentary:
Ok so Samuel holds a lottery to decide who the king is.

First he picks one of the twelve tribes.

It's Benjamin, the war tribe.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּקְרֵב שְׁמוּאֵל אֵת כּל־שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיִּלָּכֵד שֵׁבֶט בִּנְיָמִן׃}

verses.original: וַיַּקְרֵב אֶת־שֵׁבֶט בִּנְיָמִן לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָו וַתִּלָּכֵד מִשְׁפַּחַת הַמַּטְרִי וַיִּלָּכֵד שָׁאוּל בֶּן־קִישׁ וַיְבַקְשֻׁהוּ וְלֹא נִמְצָא׃
verses.english: Then Samuel brought forward the tribe of Benjamin by its clans, and the clan of the Matrites was indicated; and then Saul son of Kish was indicated. But when they looked for him, he was not to be found.
verses.commentary:
Then he chooses a clan from Benjamin at random.

It's some clan called the Matrites.

Then he picks from all the people in that tribe, and the lottery falls to someone named Saul.

So Saul wins the lottery.

Also Saul's not here.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּקְרֵב אֶת־שֵׁבֶט בִּנְיָמִן לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָו וַתִּלָּכֵד מִשְׁפַּחַת הַמַּטְרִי וַיִּלָּכֵד שָׁאוּל בֶּן־קִישׁ וַיְבַקְשֻׁהוּ וְלֹא נִמְצָא׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁאֲלוּ־עוֹד בַּיהֹוָה הֲבָא עוֹד הֲלֹם אִישׁוַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה הִנֵּה־הוּא נֶחְבָּא אֶל־הַכֵּלִים׃
verses.english: They inquired of YHWH again, “Has anyone else come here?” And YHWH replied, “Yes; he is hiding among the baggage.”
verses.commentary:
Nevermind, they found him.

He's hiding in the baggage.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשְׁאֲלוּ־עוֹד בַּיהֹוָה הֲבָא עוֹד הֲלֹם אִישׁוַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה הִנֵּה־הוּא נֶחְבָּא אֶל־הַכֵּלִים׃}

verses.original: וַיָּרֻצוּ וַיִּקָּחֻהוּ מִשָּׁם וַיִּתְיַצֵּב בְּתוֹךְ הָעָם וַיִּגְבַּהּ מִכּל־הָעָם מִשִּׁכְמוֹ וָמָעְלָה׃
verses.english: So they ran over and brought him from there; and when he took his place among the people, he stood a head taller than all the people.
verses.commentary:
So they bring him up.

And he's tall.

Way taller than everyone else.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּרֻצוּ וַיִּקָּחֻהוּ מִשָּׁם וַיִּתְיַצֵּב בְּתוֹךְ הָעָם וַיִּגְבַּהּ מִכּל־הָעָם מִשִּׁכְמוֹ וָמָעְלָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־כּל־הָעָם הַרְּאִיתֶם אֲשֶׁר בָּחַר־בּוֹ יְהֹוָה כִּי אֵין כָּמֹהוּ בְּכל־הָעָם וַיָּרִעוּ כל־הָעָם וַיֹּאמְרוּ יְחִי הַמֶּלֶךְ׃
verses.english: And Samuel said to the people, “Do you see the one whom YHWH has chosen? There is none like him among all the people.” And all the people acclaimed him, shouting, “Long live the king!”
verses.commentary:
And Samuel's like:

“Look who YHWH chose.

Mi chamocha ba this guy am I right?“

And the people shout “Long live the king!”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־כּל־הָעָם הַרְּאִיתֶם אֲשֶׁר בָּחַר־בּוֹ יְהֹוָה כִּי אֵין כָּמֹהוּ בְּכל־הָעָם וַיָּרִעוּ כל־הָעָם וַיֹּאמְרוּ יְחִי הַמֶּלֶךְ׃}

verses.original: וַיְדַבֵּר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־הָעָם אֵת מִשְׁפַּט הַמְּלֻכָה וַיִּכְתֹּב בַּסֵּפֶר וַיַּנַּח לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וַיְשַׁלַּח שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־כּל־הָעָם אִישׁ לְבֵיתוֹ׃
verses.english: Samuel expounded to the people the rules of the monarchy, and recorded them in a document which he deposited before YHWH. Samuel then sent the people back to their homes.
verses.commentary: In this sentence the text casually notes that this is a constitutional monarchy.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְדַבֵּר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־הָעָם אֵת מִשְׁפַּט הַמְּלֻכָה וַיִּכְתֹּב בַּסֵּפֶר וַיַּנַּח לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וַיְשַׁלַּח שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־כּל־הָעָם אִישׁ לְבֵיתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְגַם־שָׁאוּל הָלַךְ לְבֵיתוֹ גִּבְעָתָה וַיֵּלְכוּ עִמּוֹ הַחַיִל אֲשֶׁר־נָגַע אֱלֹהִים בְּלִבָּם׃
verses.english: Saul also went home to Gibeah, accompanied by upstanding men whose hearts God had touched.
verses.commentary: Then Saul goes home.

tex.original: \hJ{וְגַם־שָׁאוּל הָלַךְ לְבֵיתוֹ גִּבְעָתָה וַיֵּלְכוּ עִמּוֹ הַחַיִל אֲשֶׁר־נָגַע אֱלֹהִים בְּלִבָּם׃}

verses.original: וּבְנֵי בְלִיַּעַל אָמְרוּ מַה־יֹּשִׁעֵנוּ זֶה וַיִּבְזֻהוּ וְלֹא־הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ מִנְחָה וַיְהִי כְּמַחֲרִישׁ׃
verses.english: But some scoundrels said, “How can this fellow save us?” So they scorned him and brought him no gift. But he pretended not to mind.
verses.commentary: Some people are skeptical, but Saul's ok with that.

tex.original: \hJ{וּבְנֵי בְלִיַּעַל אָמְרוּ מַה־יֹּשִׁעֵנוּ זֶה וַיִּבְזֻהוּ וְלֹא־הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ מִנְחָה וַיְהִי כְּמַחֲרִישׁ׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעַל נָחָשׁ הָעַמּוֹנִי וַיִּחַן עַל־יָבֵישׁ גִּלְעָד וַיֹּאמְרוּ כּל־אַנְשֵׁי יָבֵישׁ אֶל־נָחָשׁ כְּרת־לָנוּ בְרִית וְנַעַבְדֶךָּ׃
verses.english: Nahash the Ammonite marched up and besieged Jabesh-gilead. All the men of Jabesh-gilead said to Nahash, “Make a pact with us, and we will serve you.”
verses.commentary:
Ok so there's this king of Ammon named Nahash, which means Snake.

And the people of Jabesh (which means Dry Place) Gilead (which means Pile of Rocks of the Covenant)) are like,

“Hey Snake, let's make a treaty.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּעַל נָחָשׁ הָעַמּוֹנִי וַיִּחַן עַל־יָבֵישׁ גִּלְעָד וַיֹּאמְרוּ כּל־אַנְשֵׁי יָבֵישׁ אֶל־נָחָשׁ כְּרת־לָנוּ בְרִית וְנַעַבְדֶךָּ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם נָחָשׁ הָעַמּוֹנִי בְּזֹאת אֶכְרֹת לָכֶם בִּנְקוֹר לָכֶם כּל־עֵין יָמִין וְשַׂמְתִּיהָ חֶרְפָּה עַל־כּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: But Nahash the Ammonite answered them, “I will make a pact with you on this condition, that everyone’s right eye be gouged out; I will make this a humiliation for all Israel.”
verses.commentary:
And Snake says,

“How's this for a treaty?

I gouge out everyone's right eye!

(laughs maniacally)“

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם נָחָשׁ הָעַמּוֹנִי בְּזֹאת אֶכְרֹת לָכֶם בִּנְקוֹר לָכֶם כּל־עֵין יָמִין וְשַׂמְתִּיהָ חֶרְפָּה עַל־כּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלָיו זִקְנֵי יָבֵישׁ הֶרֶף לָנוּ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים וְנִשְׁלְחָה מַלְאָכִים בְּכֹל גְּבוּל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאִם־אֵין מוֹשִׁיעַ אֹתָנוּ וְיָצָאנוּ אֵלֶיךָ׃
verses.english: The elders of Jabesh said to him, “Give us seven days’ respite, so that we may send messengers throughout the territory of Israel; if no one comes to our aid, we will surrender to you.”
verses.commentary:
So the old people of Dry Place of Pile of Rocks of the Covenant say,

“Give us a week to think about it.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלָיו זִקְנֵי יָבֵישׁ הֶרֶף לָנוּ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים וְנִשְׁלְחָה מַלְאָכִים בְּכֹל גְּבוּל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאִם־אֵין מוֹשִׁיעַ אֹתָנוּ וְיָצָאנוּ אֵלֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ הַמַּלְאָכִים גִּבְעַת שָׁאוּל וַיְדַבְּרוּ הַדְּבָרִים בְּאזְנֵי הָעָם וַיִּשְׂאוּ כל־הָעָם אֶת־קוֹלָם וַיִּבְכּוּ׃
verses.english: When the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and gave this report in the hearing of the people, all the people broke into weeping.
verses.commentary: So during the week they go to Saul's town and tell the people, and the people are not happy about this treaty.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּבֹאוּ הַמַּלְאָכִים גִּבְעַת שָׁאוּל וַיְדַבְּרוּ הַדְּבָרִים בְּאזְנֵי הָעָם וַיִּשְׂאוּ כל־הָעָם אֶת־קוֹלָם וַיִּבְכּוּ׃}

verses.original: וְהִנֵּה שָׁאוּל בָּא אַחֲרֵי הַבָּקָר מִן־הַשָּׂדֶה וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל מַה־לָּעָם כִּי יִבְכּוּ וַיְסַפְּרוּ־לוֹ אֶת־דִּבְרֵי אַנְשֵׁי יָבֵישׁ׃
verses.english: Saul was just coming from the field driving the cattle; and Saul asked, “Why are the people crying?” And they told him about the situation of the men of Jabesh.
verses.commentary: So as Saul's coming back with the cows he's like “Why's everyone crying?” And they told him about the snake eye situation.

tex.original: \hJ{וְהִנֵּה שָׁאוּל בָּא אַחֲרֵי הַבָּקָר מִן־הַשָּׂדֶה וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל מַה־לָּעָם כִּי יִבְכּוּ וַיְסַפְּרוּ־לוֹ אֶת־דִּבְרֵי אַנְשֵׁי יָבֵישׁ׃}

verses.original: וַתִּצְלַח רוּחַ־אֱלֹהִים עַל־שָׁאוּל (בשמעו) [כְּשׁמְעוֹ] אֶת־הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וַיִּחַר אַפּוֹ מְאֹד׃
verses.english: When he heard these things, the spirit of God gripped Saul and his anger blazed up.
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

Saul gets angry.

tex.original: \hJ{וַתִּצְלַח רוּחַ־אֱלֹהִים עַל־שָׁאוּל (בשמעו) [כְּשׁמְעוֹ] אֶת־הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וַיִּחַר אַפּוֹ מְאֹד׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח צֶמֶד בָּקָר וַיְנַתְּחֵהוּ וַיְשַׁלַּח בְּכל־גְּבוּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיַד הַמַּלְאָכִים לֵאמֹר אֲשֶׁר אֵינֶנּוּ יֹצֵא אַחֲרֵי שָׁאוּל וְאַחַר שְׁמוּאֵל כֹּה יֵעָשֶׂה לִבְקָרוֹ וַיִּפֹּל פַּחַד־יְהֹוָה עַל־הָעָם וַיֵּצְאוּ כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד׃
verses.english: He took a yoke of oxen and cut them into pieces, which he sent by messengers throughout the territory of Israel, with the warning, “Thus shall be done to the cattle of anyone who does not follow Saul and Samuel into battle!” Terror from YHWH fell upon the people, and they came out as one man.
verses.commentary:
So he cuts up some cows and mails the pieces around the country with a note saying “Follow me and Samuel or you're gonna be like these cows.”

Then YHWH pours some fear onto the people and they unite.

tex.english:
\eJ{
		He took a yoke of oxen and cut them into pieces, which he sent by
		messengers throughout the territory of Israel, with the warning,
		“Thus shall be done to the cattle of anyone who does not follow
		Saul and Samuel into battle!” Terror from YHWH fell upon the

verses.original: וְאִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל רָאוּ כִּי צַר־לוֹ כִּי נִגַּשׂ הָעָם וַיִּתְחַבְּאוּ הָעָם בַּמְּעָרוֹת וּבַחֲוָחִים וּבַסְּלָעִים וּבַצְּרִחִים וּבַבֹּרוֹת׃
verses.english: When the men of Israel saw that they were in trouble—for the troops were hard pressed—the people hid in caves, among thorns, among rocks, in tunnels, and in cisterns.
verses.commentary:
However many it was, it was scary.

People hid.

tex.original: \hX{וְאִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל רָאוּ כִּי צַר־לוֹ כִּי נִגַּשׂ הָעָם וַיִּתְחַבְּאוּ הָעָם בַּמְּעָרוֹת וּבַחֲוָחִים וּבַסְּלָעִים וּבַצְּרִחִים וּבַבֹּרוֹת׃}

verses.original: וְעִבְרִים עָבְרוּ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּן אֶרֶץ גָּד וְגִלְעָד וְשָׁאוּל עוֹדֶנּוּ בַגִּלְגָּל וְכל־הָעָם חָרְדוּ אַחֲרָיו׃
verses.english: Some Hebrews crossed the Jordan, [to] the territory of Gad and Gilead. Saul was still at Gilgal, and the rest of the people rallied to him in alarm.d
verses.commentary: Saul's still at Circle.

tex.original: \hX{וְעִבְרִים עָבְרוּ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּן אֶרֶץ גָּד וְגִלְעָד וְשָׁאוּל עוֹדֶנּוּ בַגִּלְגָּל וְכל־הָעָם חָרְדוּ אַחֲרָיו׃}

verses.original: (וייחל) [וַיּוֹחֶל ] שִׁבְעַת יָמִים לַמּוֹעֵד אֲשֶׁר שְׁמוּאֵל וְלֹא־בָא שְׁמוּאֵל הַגִּלְגָּל וַיָּפֶץ הָעָם מֵעָלָיו׃
verses.english: He waited seven days, the time that Samuel [had set]. But when Samuel failed to come to Gilgal, and the people began to scatter,
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

He did what Samuel told him to do awhile back in the lost asses story.

Remember the lost asses story?

tex.original: \hX{(וייחל) [וַיּוֹחֶל ] שִׁבְעַת יָמִים לַמּוֹעֵד אֲשֶׁר שְׁמוּאֵל וְלֹא־בָא שְׁמוּאֵל הַגִּלְגָּל וַיָּפֶץ הָעָם מֵעָלָיו׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל הַגִּשׁוּ אֵלַי הָעֹלָה וְהַשְּׁלָמִים וַיַּעַל הָעֹלָה׃
verses.english: Saul said, “Bring me the burnt offering and the sacrifice of well-being”; and he presented the burnt offering.
verses.commentary: So Saul's going through the motions.

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל הַגִּשׁוּ אֵלַי הָעֹלָה וְהַשְּׁלָמִים וַיַּעַל הָעֹלָה׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי כְּכַלֹּתוֹ לְהַעֲלוֹת הָעֹלָה וְהִנֵּה שְׁמוּאֵל בָּא וַיֵּצֵא שָׁאוּל לִקְרָאתוֹ לְבָרְכוֹ׃
verses.english: He had just finished presenting the burnt offering when Samuel arrived; and Saul went out to meet him and welcome him.
verses.commentary: Trying to be good how Samuel said to.

tex.original: \hX{וַיְהִי כְּכַלֹּתוֹ לְהַעֲלוֹת הָעֹלָה וְהִנֵּה שְׁמוּאֵל בָּא וַיֵּצֵא שָׁאוּל לִקְרָאתוֹ לְבָרְכוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל מֶה עָשִׂיתָ וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל כִּי־רָאִיתִי כִי־נָפַץ הָעָם מֵעָלַי וְאַתָּה לֹא־בָאתָ לְמוֹעֵד הַיָּמִים וּפְלִשְׁתִּים נֶאֱסָפִים מִכְמָשׂ׃
verses.english: But Samuel said, “What have you done?” Saul replied, “I saw the people leaving me and scattering; you had not come at the appointed time, and the Philistines had gathered at Michmas.
verses.commentary: Samuel's mad anyway.

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל מֶה עָשִׂיתָ וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל כִּי־רָאִיתִי כִי־נָפַץ הָעָם מֵעָלַי וְאַתָּה לֹא־בָאתָ לְמוֹעֵד הַיָּמִים וּפְלִשְׁתִּים נֶאֱסָפִים מִכְמָשׂ׃}

verses.original: וָאֹמַר עַתָּה יֵרְדוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אֵלַי הַגִּלְגָּל וּפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לֹא חִלִּיתִי וָאֶתְאַפַּק וָאַעֲלֶה הָעֹלָה׃
verses.english: I thought the Philistines would march down against me at Gilgal before I had entreated YHWH, so I forced myself to present the burnt offering.”
verses.commentary: Saul has reasons.

tex.original: \hX{וָאֹמַר עַתָּה יֵרְדוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אֵלַי הַגִּלְגָּל וּפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לֹא חִלִּיתִי וָאֶתְאַפַּק וָאַעֲלֶה הָעֹלָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־שָׁאוּל נִסְכָּלְתָּ לֹא שָׁמַרְתָּ אֶת־מִצְוַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר צִוָּךְ כִּי עַתָּה הֵכִין יְהֹוָה אֶת־מַמְלַכְתְּךָ אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד־עוֹלָם׃
verses.english: Samuel answered Saul, “You acted foolishly in not keeping the commandments that YHWH your God laid upon you! Otherwise YHWH would have established your dynasty over Israel forever.
verses.commentary:
So Samuel says “You acted foolishly in not keeping the commandments that YHWH your God—”

And Saul's like: “יהוה אלהיך... Deuteronomist is that you?”

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־שָׁאוּל נִסְכָּלְתָּ לֹא שָׁמַרְתָּ אֶת־מִצְוַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר צִוָּךְ כִּי עַתָּה הֵכִין יְהֹוָה אֶת־מַמְלַכְתְּךָ אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד־עוֹלָם׃}

verses.original: וְעַתָּה מַמְלַכְתְּךָ לֹא־תָקוּם בִּקֵּשׁ יְהֹוָה לוֹ אִישׁ כִּלְבָבוֹ וַיְצַוֵּהוּ יְהֹוָה לְנָגִיד עַל־עַמּוֹ כִּי לֹא שָׁמַרְתָּ אֵת אֲשֶׁר־צִוְּךָ יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: But now your dynasty will not endure. YHWH will seek out a man after His own heart, and YHWH will appoint him ruler over His people, because you did not abide by what YHWH had commanded you.”
verses.commentary:
Then they just sort of glare at each other suspiciously.

Expression redacted.

verses.original: וַיָּקם שְׁמוּאֵל וַיַּעַל מִן־הַגִּלְגָּל גִּבְעַת בִּנְיָמִן וַיִּפְקֹד שָׁאוּל אֶת־הָעָם הַנִּמְצְאִים עִמּוֹ כְּשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת אִישׁ׃

verses.commentary:
Saul leaves Circle.

600 guys come too.

tex.original: \hX{וַיָּקם שְׁמוּאֵל וַיַּעַל מִן־הַגִּלְגָּל גִּבְעַת בִּנְיָמִן וַיִּפְקֹד שָׁאוּל אֶת־הָעָם הַנִּמְצְאִים עִמּוֹ כְּשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת אִישׁ׃}

verses.original: וְשָׁאוּל וְיוֹנָתָן בְּנוֹ וְהָעָם הַנִּמְצָא עִמָּם יֹשְׁבִים בְּגֶבַע בִּנְיָמִן וּפְלִשְׁתִּים חָנוּ בְמִכְמָשׂ׃
verses.english: Saul and his son Jonathan, and the troops who remained with them, stayed in Geba of Benjamin, while the Philistines were encamped at Michmas.
verses.commentary: They stay at The Hill of Benjamin.

tex.original: \hX{וְשָׁאוּל וְיוֹנָתָן בְּנוֹ וְהָעָם הַנִּמְצָא עִמָּם יֹשְׁבִים בְּגֶבַע בִּנְיָמִן וּפְלִשְׁתִּים חָנוּ בְמִכְמָשׂ׃}

verses.english: The raiders came out of the Philistine camp in three columns: One column headed for the Ophrah road that leads to the district of Shual,

tex.original: \hX{וַיֵּצֵא הַמַּשְׁחִית מִמַּחֲנֵה פְלִשְׁתִּים שְׁלֹשָׁה רָאשִׁים הָרֹאשׁ אֶחָד יִפְנֶה אֶל־דֶּרֶךְ עפְרָה אֶל־אֶרֶץ שׁוּעָל׃}

verses.original: וְהָרֹאשׁ אֶחָד יִפְנֶה דֶּרֶךְ בֵּית חֹרוֹן וְהָרֹאשׁ אֶחָד יִפְנֶה דֶּרֶךְ הַגְּבוּל הַנִּשְׁקָף עַל־גֵּי הַצְּבֹעִים הַמִּדְבָּרָה׃

verses.commentary:
Another group headed for House of Caves road.

The third group headed for the road by Hyena Valley.

tex.original: \hX{וְהָרֹאשׁ אֶחָד יִפְנֶה דֶּרֶךְ בֵּית חֹרוֹן וְהָרֹאשׁ אֶחָד יִפְנֶה דֶּרֶךְ הַגְּבוּל הַנִּשְׁקָף עַל־גֵּי הַצְּבֹעִים הַמִּדְבָּרָה׃}

verses.original: וְחָרָשׁ לֹא יִמָּצֵא בְּכֹל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי־[אָמְרוּ] (אמר) פְלִשְׁתִּים פֶּן יַעֲשׂוּ הָעִבְרִים חֶרֶב אוֹ חֲנִית׃
verses.english: No smith was to be found in all the land of Israel, for the Philistines were afraid that the Hebrews would make swords or spears.
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

Swords are regulated.

tex.original: \hX{וְחָרָשׁ לֹא יִמָּצֵא בְּכֹל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי־[אָמְרוּ] (אמר) פְלִשְׁתִּים פֶּן יַעֲשׂוּ הָעִבְרִים חֶרֶב אוֹ חֲנִית׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּרְדוּ כל־יִשְׂרָאֵל הַפְּלִשְׁתִּים לִלְטוֹשׁ אִישׁ אֶת־מַחֲרַשְׁתּוֹ וְאֶת־אֵתוֹ וְאֶת־קַרְדֻּמּוֹ וְאֵת מַחֲרֵשָׁתוֹ׃
verses.english: So all the Israelites had to go down to the Philistines to have their plowshares, their mattocks, axes, and colters sharpened.
verses.commentary: The Israelites have to go to a licensed Philistine to get their metal fixed.

tex.original: \hX{וַיֵּרְדוּ כל־יִשְׂרָאֵל הַפְּלִשְׁתִּים לִלְטוֹשׁ אִישׁ אֶת־מַחֲרַשְׁתּוֹ וְאֶת־אֵתוֹ וְאֶת־קַרְדֻּמּוֹ וְאֵת מַחֲרֵשָׁתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְהָיְתָה הַפְּצִירָה פִים לַמַּחֲרֵשֹׁת וְלָאֵתִים וְלִשְׁלֹשׁ קִלְּשׁוֹן וּלְהַקַּרְדֻּמִּים וּלְהַצִּיב הַדָּרְבָן׃
verses.english: The charge for sharpening was a pim for plowshares, mattocks, three-pronged forks, and axes, and for setting the goads.
verses.commentary:
The word “pim” is only used once in the bible.

Archeologists figured out what it means after digging up some stuff in Israel that said “pim” on it.

Turns out it's a unit of weight that's a bit heavier than a sheet of printer paper and a bit lighter than a AAA battery, which the internet claims weigh nearly the same.

Here it means “however much silver weighs that amount”

Price seems to have been about two days work.

But don't quote me on that.

Not an expert on pims.

tex.original: \hX{וְהָיְתָה הַפְּצִירָה פִים לַמַּחֲרֵשֹׁת וְלָאֵתִים וְלִשְׁלֹשׁ קִלְּשׁוֹן וּלְהַקַּרְדֻּמִּים וּלְהַצִּיב הַדָּרְבָן׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה בְּיוֹם מִלְחֶמֶת וְלֹא נִמְצָא חֶרֶב וַחֲנִית בְּיַד כּל־הָעָם אֲשֶׁר אֶת־שָׁאוּל וְאֶת־יוֹנָתָן וַתִּמָּצֵא לְשָׁאוּל וּלְיוֹנָתָן בְּנוֹ׃
verses.english: Thus on the day of the battle, no sword or spear was to be found in the possession of any of the troops with Saul and Jonathan; only Saul and Jonathan had them.
verses.commentary:
Anyways because of those laws, only two guys have swords.

So it's shaping up to be a pretty rough battle.

tex.original: \hX{וְהָיָה בְּיוֹם מִלְחֶמֶת וְלֹא נִמְצָא חֶרֶב וַחֲנִית בְּיַד כּל־הָעָם אֲשֶׁר אֶת־שָׁאוּל וְאֶת־יוֹנָתָן וַתִּמָּצֵא לְשָׁאוּל וּלְיוֹנָתָן בְּנוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּצֵא מַצַּב פְּלִשְׁתִּים אֶל־מַעֲבַר מִכְמָשׂ׃
verses.english: Now the Philistine garrison had marched out to the pass of Michmas.
verses.commentary: The chapter then ends here, in the middle of a thought.

tex.original: \hX{וַיֵּצֵא מַצַּב פְּלִשְׁתִּים אֶל־מַעֲבַר מִכְמָשׂ׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי הַיּוֹם וַיֹּאמֶר יוֹנָתָן בֶּן־שָׁאוּל אֶל־הַנַּעַר נֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו לְכָה וְנַעְבְּרָה אֶל־מַצַּב פְּלִשְׁתִּים אֲשֶׁר מֵעֵבֶר הַלָּז וּלְאָבִיו לֹא הִגִּיד׃
verses.english: One day, Jonathan son of Saul said to the attendant who carried his arms, “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine garrison on the other side”; but he did not tell his father.
verses.commentary: Jonathan has an idea. He doesn't tell dad.

tex.original: \hX{וַיְהִי הַיּוֹם וַיֹּאמֶר יוֹנָתָן בֶּן־שָׁאוּל אֶל־הַנַּעַר נֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו לְכָה וְנַעְבְּרָה אֶל־מַצַּב פְּלִשְׁתִּים אֲשֶׁר מֵעֵבֶר הַלָּז וּלְאָבִיו לֹא הִגִּיד׃}

verses.original: וְשָׁאוּל יוֹשֵׁב בִּקְצֵה הַגִּבְעָה תַּחַת הָרִמּוֹן אֲשֶׁר בְּמִגְרוֹן וְהָעָם אֲשֶׁר עִמּוֹ כְּשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת אִישׁ׃
verses.english: Now Saul was staying on the outskirts of Gibeah, under the pomegranate tree at Migron, and the troops with him numbered about 600.
verses.commentary: The king's staying under a pomegranate tree with 600 guys.

tex.original: \hX{וְשָׁאוּל יוֹשֵׁב בִּקְצֵה הַגִּבְעָה תַּחַת הָרִמּוֹן אֲשֶׁר בְּמִגְרוֹן וְהָעָם אֲשֶׁר עִמּוֹ כְּשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת אִישׁ׃}

verses.original: וַאֲחִיָּה בֶן־אֲחִטוּב אֲחִי אִיכָבוֹד בֶּן־פִּינְחָס בֶּן־עֵלִי כֹּהֵן יְהֹוָה בְּשִׁלוֹ נֹשֵׂא אֵפוֹד וְהָעָם לֹא יָדַע כִּי הָלַךְ יוֹנָתָן׃
verses.english: Ahijah son of Ahitub brother of Ichabod son of Phinehas son of Eli, the priest of YHWH at Shiloh, was there bearing an ephod.—The troops did not know that Jonathan had gone.
verses.commentary:
Ahijah has a genealogy and an ephod.

Jonathan left Irishly.

tex.original: \hX{וַאֲחִיָּה בֶן־אֲחִטוּב אֲחִי אִיכָבוֹד בֶּן־פִּינְחָס בֶּן־עֵלִי כֹּהֵן יְהֹוָה בְּשִׁלוֹ נֹשֵׂא אֵפוֹד וְהָעָם לֹא יָדַע כִּי הָלַךְ יוֹנָתָן׃}

verses.original: וּבֵין הַמַּעְבְּרוֹת אֲשֶׁר בִּקֵּשׁ יוֹנָתָן לַעֲבֹר עַל־מַצַּב פְּלִשְׁתִּים שֵׁן־הַסֶּלַע מֵהָעֵבֶר מִזֶּה וְשֵׁן־הַסֶּלַע מֵהָעֵבֶר מִזֶּה וְשֵׁם הָאֶחָד בּוֹצֵץ וְשֵׁם הָאֶחָד סֶנֶּה׃
verses.english: At the crossing by which Jonathan sought to reach the Philistine garrison, there was a rocky crag on one side, and another rocky crag on the other, the one called Bozez and the other Seneh.
verses.commentary: Jonathan's between a rock and a hard place.

verses.original: הַשֵּׁן הָאֶחָד מָצוּק מִצָּפוֹן מוּל מִכְמָשׂ וְהָאֶחָד מִנֶּגֶב מוּל גָּבַע׃
verses.english: One crag was located on the north, near Michmas, and the other on the south, near Geba.
verses.commentary: One was on this side, one was on the opposite side.

tex.original: \hX{הַשֵּׁן הָאֶחָד מָצוּק מִצָּפוֹן מוּל מִכְמָשׂ וְהָאֶחָד מִנֶּגֶב מוּל גָּבַע׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוֹנָתָן אֶל־הַנַּעַר נֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו לְכָה וְנַעְבְּרָה אֶל־מַצַּב הָעֲרֵלִים הָאֵלֶּה אוּלַי יַעֲשֶׂה יְהֹוָה לָנוּ כִּי אֵין לַיהֹוָה מַעְצוֹר לְהוֹשִׁיעַ בְּרַב אוֹ בִמְעָט׃
verses.english: Jonathan said to the attendant who carried his arms, “Come, let us cross over to the outpost of those uncircumcised fellows. Perhaps YHWH will act in our behalf, for nothing prevents YHWH from winning a victory by many or by few.”
verses.commentary:
So Jonathan says to the guy who's carrying his swords,

“Let's go over where those foreskin people are, if YHWH's on our side, maybe we can win as just the two of us.”

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ נֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו עֲשֵׂה כּל־אֲשֶׁר בִּלְבָבֶךָ נְטֵה לָךְ הִנְנִי עִמְּךָ כִּלְבָבֶךָ׃
verses.english: His arms-bearer answered him, “Do whatever you like. You go first, I am with you, whatever you decide.”
verses.commentary: So the guy carrying his swords says “You go first. Whatever you decide boss.”

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ נֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו עֲשֵׂה כּל־אֲשֶׁר בִּלְבָבֶךָ נְטֵה לָךְ הִנְנִי עִמְּךָ כִּלְבָבֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוֹנָתָן הִנֵּה אֲנַחְנוּ עֹבְרִים אֶל־הָאֲנָשִׁים וְנִגְלִינוּ אֲלֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: Jonathan said, “We’ll cross over to those men and let them see us.
verses.commentary: So Jonathan says let's make sure they see us.

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוֹנָתָן הִנֵּה אֲנַחְנוּ עֹבְרִים אֶל־הָאֲנָשִׁים וְנִגְלִינוּ אֲלֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: אִם־כֹּה יֹאמְרוּ אֵלֵינוּ דֹּמּוּ עַד־הַגִּיעֵנוּ אֲלֵיכֶם וְעָמַדְנוּ תַחְתֵּינוּ וְלֹא נַעֲלֶה אֲלֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: If they say to us, ‘Wait until we get to you,’ then we’ll stay where we are, and not go up to them.
verses.commentary: If they say we'll come to you, then we'll wait while they do.

tex.original: \hX{אִם־כֹּה יֹאמְרוּ אֵלֵינוּ דֹּמּוּ עַד־הַגִּיעֵנוּ אֲלֵיכֶם וְעָמַדְנוּ תַחְתֵּינוּ וְלֹא נַעֲלֶה אֲלֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וְאִם־כֹּה יֹאמְרוּ עֲלוּ עָלֵינוּ וְעָלִינוּ כִּי־נְתָנָם יְהֹוָה בְּיָדֵנוּ וְזֶה־לָּנוּ הָאוֹת׃
verses.english: But if they say, ‘Come up to us,’ then we will go up, for YHWH is delivering them into our hands. That shall be our sign.”
verses.commentary: If they say you come over here, then we'll do that.

tex.original: \hX{וְאִם־כֹּה יֹאמְרוּ עֲלוּ עָלֵינוּ וְעָלִינוּ כִּי־נְתָנָם יְהֹוָה בְּיָדֵנוּ וְזֶה־לָּנוּ הָאוֹת׃}

verses.original: וַיִּגָּלוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם אֶל־מַצַּב פְּלִשְׁתִּים וַיֹּאמְרוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים הִנֵּה עִבְרִים יֹצְאִים מִן־הַחֹרִים אֲשֶׁר הִתְחַבְּאוּ־שָׁם׃
verses.english: They both showed themselves to the Philistine outpost and the Philistines said, “Look, some Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they have been hiding.”
verses.commentary:
So they show themselves to the enemy camp.

The Philistines are like get a load of these guys.

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּגָּלוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם אֶל־מַצַּב פְּלִשְׁתִּים וַיֹּאמְרוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים הִנֵּה עִבְרִים יֹצְאִים מִן־הַחֹרִים אֲשֶׁר הִתְחַבְּאוּ־שָׁם׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעֲנוּ אַנְשֵׁי הַמַּצָּבָה אֶת־יוֹנָתָן וְאֶת־נֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו וַיֹּאמְרוּ עֲלוּ אֵלֵינוּ וְנוֹדִיעָה אֶתְכֶם דָּבָרוַיֹּאמֶר יוֹנָתָן אֶל־נֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו עֲלֵה אַחֲרַי כִּי־נְתָנָם יְהֹוָה בְּיַד יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: The men of the outpost shouted to Jonathan and his arms-bearer, “Come up to us, and we’ll teach you a lesson.” Then Jonathan said to his arms-bearer, “Follow me, for YHWH will deliver them into the hands of Israel.”
verses.commentary:
So the entire enemy camp says to the two guys “Come here.”

And they do.

verses.original: וַיַּעַל יוֹנָתָן עַל־יָדָיו וְעַל־רַגְלָיו וְנֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו אַחֲרָיו וַיִּפְּלוּ לִפְנֵי יוֹנָתָן וְנֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו מְמוֹתֵת אַחֲרָיו׃
verses.english: And Jonathan clambered up on his hands and feet, his arms-bearer behind him; [the Philistines] fell before Jonathan, and his arms-bearer finished them off behind him.
verses.commentary: And they win?

tex.original: \hX{וַיַּעַל יוֹנָתָן עַל־יָדָיו וְעַל־רַגְלָיו וְנֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו אַחֲרָיו וַיִּפְּלוּ לִפְנֵי יוֹנָתָן וְנֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו מְמוֹתֵת אַחֲרָיו׃}

verses.original: וַתְּהִי הַמַּכָּה הָרִאשֹׁנָה אֲשֶׁר הִכָּה יוֹנָתָן וְנֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו כְּעֶשְׂרִים אִישׁ כְּבַחֲצִי מַעֲנָה צֶמֶד שָׂדֶה׃
verses.english: The initial attack that Jonathan and his arms-bearer made accounted for some twenty men, within a space about half a furrow long [in] an acre of land.
verses.commentary: So the two guys kill about 20 guys. I guess.

tex.original: \hX{וַתְּהִי הַמַּכָּה הָרִאשֹׁנָה אֲשֶׁר הִכָּה יוֹנָתָן וְנֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו כְּעֶשְׂרִים אִישׁ כְּבַחֲצִי מַעֲנָה צֶמֶד שָׂדֶה׃}

verses.original: וַתְּהִי חֲרָדָה בַמַּחֲנֶה בַשָּׂדֶה וּבְכל־הָעָם הַמַּצָּב וְהַמַּשְׁחִית חָרְדוּ גַּם־הֵמָּה וַתִּרְגַּז הָאָרֶץ וַתְּהִי לְחֶרְדַּת אֱלֹהִים׃
verses.english: Terror broke out among all the troops both in the camp [and] in the field; the outposts and the raiders were also terrified. The very earth quaked, and a terror from God ensued.
verses.commentary: And so the enemies are scared, because that's quite the ratio.

tex.original: \hX{וַתְּהִי חֲרָדָה בַמַּחֲנֶה בַשָּׂדֶה וּבְכל־הָעָם הַמַּצָּב וְהַמַּשְׁחִית חָרְדוּ גַּם־הֵמָּה וַתִּרְגַּז הָאָרֶץ וַתְּהִי לְחֶרְדַּת אֱלֹהִים׃}

verses.original: וַיִּרְאוּ הַצֹּפִים לְשָׁאוּל בְּגִבְעַת בִּנְיָמִן וְהִנֵּה הֶהָמוֹן נָמוֹג וַיֵּלֶךְ וַהֲלֹם׃
verses.english: Saul’s scouts in Gibeah of Benjamin saw that the multitude was scattering in all directions.
verses.commentary: So Saul's scouts see that everybody is freaking out.

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּרְאוּ הַצֹּפִים לְשָׁאוּל בְּגִבְעַת בִּנְיָמִן וְהִנֵּה הֶהָמוֹן נָמוֹג וַיֵּלֶךְ וַהֲלֹם׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל לָעָם אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ פִּקְדוּ־נָא וּרְאוּ מִי הָלַךְ מֵעִמָּנוּ וַיִּפְקְדוּ וְהִנֵּה אֵין יוֹנָתָן וְנֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו׃
verses.english: And Saul said to the troops with him, “Take a count and see who has left us.” They took a count and found that Jonathan and his arms-bearer were missing.
verses.commentary:
Saul tells his guys to take roll.

They realize Jonathan and the caddy are gone.

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל לָעָם אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ פִּקְדוּ־נָא וּרְאוּ מִי הָלַךְ מֵעִמָּנוּ וַיִּפְקְדוּ וְהִנֵּה אֵין יוֹנָתָן וְנֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל לַאֲחִיָּה הַגִּישָׁה אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים כִּי־הָיָה אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: Thereupon Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring the Ark of God here”; for the Ark of God was at the time among the Israelites.
verses.commentary:
So Saul calls for the box of God.

Seems like a bit of a digression but let's roll with him.

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל לַאֲחִיָּה הַגִּישָׁה אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים כִּי־הָיָה אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי עַד דִּבֶּר שָׁאוּל אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן וְהֶהָמוֹן אֲשֶׁר בְּמַחֲנֵה פְלִשְׁתִּים וַיֵּלֶךְ הָלוֹךְ וָרָבוַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן אֱסֹף יָדֶךָ׃
verses.english: But while Saul was speaking to the priest, the confusion in the Philistine camp kept increasing; and Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”
verses.commentary: So while Saul's arranging for the god box to be delivered, the freaking out intensifies and he says “Hold that thought, I have to go do something.”

tex.original: \hX{וַיְהִי עַד דִּבֶּר שָׁאוּל אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן וְהֶהָמוֹן אֲשֶׁר בְּמַחֲנֵה פְלִשְׁתִּים וַיֵּלֶךְ הָלוֹךְ וָרָבוַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן אֱסֹף יָדֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּזָּעֵק שָׁאוּל וְכל־הָעָם אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ וַיָּבֹאוּ עַד־הַמִּלְחָמָה וְהִנֵּה הָיְתָה חֶרֶב אִישׁ בְּרֵעֵהוּ מְהוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה מְאֹד׃
verses.english: Saul and the troops with him assembled and rushed into battle; they found [the Philistines] in very great confusion, every man’s sword turned against his fellow.
verses.commentary: So Saul rushes into battle and the Philistines are freaking out.

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּזָּעֵק שָׁאוּל וְכל־הָעָם אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ וַיָּבֹאוּ עַד־הַמִּלְחָמָה וְהִנֵּה הָיְתָה חֶרֶב אִישׁ בְּרֵעֵהוּ מְהוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה מְאֹד׃}

verses.english: And he said to all the Israelites, “You stand on one side, and my son Jonathan and I shall stand on the other.” The troops said to Saul, “Do as you please.”
verses.commentary: So he puts everyone over there, and him and his son over here.

And Jonathan admits he licked the stick and had some honey.

verses.english: Saul broke off his pursuit of the Philistines, and the Philistines returned to their homes.
verses.commentary: Saul gives up and the Philistines go home.
