verses.english: After Saul had secured his kingship over Israel, he waged war on every side against all his enemies: against the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, the Philistines, and the kings of Zobah; and wherever he turned he worsted [them].
verses.commentary: Never mind, Saul very much doesn't give up. He fights everybody.

verses.english: He was triumphant, defeating the Amalekites and saving Israel from those who plundered it.
verses.commentary: He wins.

tex.original: \hX{וַיַּעַשׂ חַיִל וַיַּךְ אֶת־עֲמָלֵק וַיַּצֵּל אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל מִיַּד שֹׁסֵהוּ׃}

verses.english: Saul’s sons were: Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua; and the names of his two daughters were Merab, the older, and Michal, the younger.
verses.commentary: By the way, here's his kid's names.

verses.english: The name of Saul’s wife was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz; and the name of his army commander was Abiner son of Saul’s uncle Ner.
verses.commentary: And the name of his wife and mother-in-law and army commander.

tex.original: \hX{וְשֵׁם אֵשֶׁת שָׁאוּל אֲחִינֹעַם בַּת־אֲחִימָעַץ וְשֵׁם שַׂר־צְבָאוֹ אֲבִינֵר בֶּן־נֵר דּוֹד שָׁאוּל׃}

Okay so despite what we heard six sentences ago, Saul fights the Philistines the whole time.

He also hires good guys whenever he meets any.

There's two groups mixed together and Saul only wants to kill one.

So he tells one to move, and they move.

verses.commentary: He keeps the King as a souvenir.

verses.original: וַיַּחְמֹל שָׁאוּל וְהָעָם עַל־אֲגָג וְעַל־מֵיטַב הַצֹּאן וְהַבָּקָר וְהַמִּשְׁנִים וְעַל־הַכָּרִים וְעַל־כּל־הַטּוֹב וְלֹא אָבוּ הַחֲרִימָם וְכל־הַמְּלָאכָה נְמִבְזָה וְנָמֵס אֹתָהּ הֶחֱרִימוּ׃
verses.english: but Saul and the troops spared Agag and the best of the sheep, the oxen, the second-born, the lambs, and all else that was of value. They would not proscribe them; they proscribed only what was cheap and worthless.
verses.commentary: He also keeps the stuff he wants.

verses.original: וַיְהִי דְּבַר־יְהֹוָה אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל לֵאמֹר׃
verses.english: The word of YHWH then came to Samuel:
verses.commentary: So Samuel gets a call.

tex.english: \eJ{The word of YHWH then came to Samuel:}

verses.original: נִחַמְתִּי כִּי־הִמְלַכְתִּי אֶת־שָׁאוּל לְמֶלֶךְ כִּי־שָׁב מֵאַחֲרַי וְאֶת־דְּבָרַי לֹא הֵקִים וַיִּחַר לִשְׁמוּאֵל וַיִּזְעַק אֶל־יְהֹוָה כּל־הַלָּיְלָה׃
verses.english: “I regret that I made Saul king, for he has turned away from Me and has not carried out My commands.” Samuel was distressed and he entreated YHWH all night long.
verses.commentary: YHWH opens up to Samuel and says Saul was a mistake.

tex.original: \hJ{נִחַמְתִּי כִּי־הִמְלַכְתִּי אֶת־שָׁאוּל לְמֶלֶךְ כִּי־שָׁב מֵאַחֲרַי וְאֶת־דְּבָרַי לֹא הֵקִים וַיִּחַר לִשְׁמוּאֵל וַיִּזְעַק אֶל־יְהֹוָה כּל־הַלָּיְלָה׃}

verses.original: וַיַּשְׁכֵּם שְׁמוּאֵל לִקְרַאת שָׁאוּל בַּבֹּקֶר וַיֻּגַּד לִשְׁמוּאֵל לֵאמֹר בָּא־שָׁאוּל הַכַּרְמֶלָה וְהִנֵּה מַצִּיב לוֹ יָד וַיִּסֹּב וַיַּעֲבֹר וַיֵּרֶד הַגִּלְגָּל׃
verses.english: Early in the morning Samuel went to meet Saul. Samuel was told, “Saul went to Carmel, where he erected a monument for himself; then he left and went on down to Gilgal.”
verses.commentary:
Samuel wakes up early to meet Saul.

He'd gotten word that Saul was doing some rather narcissistic things.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּשְׁכֵּם שְׁמוּאֵל לִקְרַאת שָׁאוּל בַּבֹּקֶר וַיֻּגַּד לִשְׁמוּאֵל לֵאמֹר בָּא־שָׁאוּל הַכַּרְמֶלָה וְהִנֵּה מַצִּיב לוֹ יָד וַיִּסֹּב וַיַּעֲבֹר וַיֵּרֶד הַגִּלְגָּל׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־שָׁאוּל וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ שָׁאוּל בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה לַיהֹוָה הֲקִימֹתִי אֶת־דְּבַר יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: When Samuel came to Saul, Saul said to him, “Blessed are you of YHWH! I have fulfilled YHWH’s command.”
verses.commentary: Saul's happy to see Samuel and wants to show how good he's been.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּבֹא שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־שָׁאוּל וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ שָׁאוּל בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה לַיהֹוָה הֲקִימֹתִי אֶת־דְּבַר יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל וּמֶה קוֹל־הַצֹּאן הַזֶּה בְּאזְנָי וְקוֹל הַבָּקָר אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי שֹׁמֵעַ׃
verses.english: “Then what,” demanded Samuel, “is this bleating of sheep in my ears, and the lowing of oxen that I hear?”
verses.commentary: So Sam's like “What meaneth this bleating of sheep that I hear in mine ears?” in perfect King James English.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל וּמֶה קוֹל־הַצֹּאן הַזֶּה בְּאזְנָי וְקוֹל הַבָּקָר אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי שֹׁמֵעַ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל מֵעֲמָלֵקִי הֱבִיאוּם אֲשֶׁר חָמַל הָעָם עַל־מֵיטַב הַצֹּאן וְהַבָּקָר לְמַעַן זְבֹחַ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְאֶת־הַיּוֹתֵר הֶחֱרַמְנוּ׃
verses.english: Saul answered, “They were brought from the Amalekites, for the troops spared the choicest of the sheep and oxen for sacrificing to YHWH your God. And we proscribed the rest.”
verses.commentary:
Saul pauses for a moment and goes...

“Sacrifices! We saved the sheep for sacrifices.”

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־שָׁאוּל הֶרֶף וְאַגִּידָה לְּךָ אֵת אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה אֵלַי הַלָּיְלָה (ויאמרו) [וַיֹּאמֶר] לוֹ דַּבֵּר׃
verses.english: Samuel said to Saul, “Stop! Let me tell you what YHWH said to me last night!” “Speak,” he replied.
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

So Samuel's like “Stop. Look, me and YHWH had a talk about you last night.”

verses.english: And Samuel said, “You may look small to yourself, but you are the head of the tribes of Israel. YHWH anointed you king over Israel,
verses.commentary: Samuels like “I know your self esteem isn't the best, but you're the King man get your act together.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲלוֹא אִם־קָטֹן אַתָּה בְּעֵינֶיךָ רֹאשׁ שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָתָּה וַיִּמְשָׁחֲךָ יְהֹוָה לְמֶלֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלָחֲךָ יְהֹוָה בְּדָרֶךְ וַיֹּאמֶר לֵךְ וְהַחֲרַמְתָּה אֶת־הַחַטָּאִים אֶת־עֲמָלֵק וְנִלְחַמְתָּ בוֹ עַד כַּלּוֹתָם אֹתָם׃
verses.english: and YHWH sent you on a mission, saying, ‘Go and proscribe the sinful Amalekites; make war on them until you have exterminated them.’
verses.commentary: C told you to kill D, and D includes the D sheep you F head.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשְׁלָחֲךָ יְהֹוָה בְּדָרֶךְ וַיֹּאמֶר לֵךְ וְהַחֲרַמְתָּה אֶת־הַחַטָּאִים אֶת־עֲמָלֵק וְנִלְחַמְתָּ בוֹ עַד כַּלּוֹתָם אֹתָם׃}

verses.original: וְלָמָּה לֹא־שָׁמַעְתָּ בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה וַתַּעַט אֶל־הַשָּׁלָל וַתַּעַשׂ הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Why did you disobey YHWH and swoop down on the spoil in defiance of YHWH’s will?”
verses.commentary: Why did you take all the stuff?

tex.original: \hJ{וְלָמָּה לֹא־שָׁמַעְתָּ בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה וַתַּעַט אֶל־הַשָּׁלָל וַתַּעַשׂ הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה וָאֵלֵךְ בַּדֶּרֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־שְׁלָחַנִי יְהֹוָה וָאָבִיא אֶת־אֲגַג מֶלֶךְ עֲמָלֵק וְאֶת־עֲמָלֵק הֶחֱרַמְתִּי׃
verses.english: Saul said to Samuel, “But I did obey YHWH! I performed the mission on which YHWH sent me: I captured King Agag of Amalek, and I proscribed Amalek,
verses.commentary: Saul objects that the terms of the request were insufficiently specified, particularly with respect to the details of request's low level implementation vis-a-vis the subject of sheep.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה וָאֵלֵךְ בַּדֶּרֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־שְׁלָחַנִי יְהֹוָה וָאָבִיא אֶת־אֲגַג מֶלֶךְ עֲמָלֵק וְאֶת־עֲמָלֵק הֶחֱרַמְתִּי׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח הָעָם מֵהַשָּׁלָל צֹאן וּבָקָר רֵאשִׁית הַחֵרֶם לִזְבֹּחַ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּגִּלְגָּל׃
verses.english: and the troops took from the spoil some sheep and oxen—the best of what had been proscribed—to sacrifice to YHWH your God at Gilgal.”
verses.commentary: I kept the best stuff cuz I thought YHWH might want it.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּקַּח הָעָם מֵהַשָּׁלָל צֹאן וּבָקָר רֵאשִׁית הַחֵרֶם לִזְבֹּחַ לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בַּגִּלְגָּל׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל הַחֵפֶץ לַיהֹוָה בְּעֹלוֹת וּזְבָחִים כִּשְׁמֹעַ בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה הִנֵּה שְׁמֹעַ מִזֶּבַח טוֹב לְהַקְשִׁיב מֵחֵלֶב אֵילִים׃
verses.english: But Samuel said: “Does YHWH delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices As much as in obedience to YHWH’s command? Surely, obedience is better than sacrifice, Compliance than the fat of rams.
verses.commentary:
So Samuel says does Yahweh like burnt offerings as much as listening?

Then he goes into poetry for the last two lines.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל הַחֵפֶץ לַיהֹוָה בְּעֹלוֹת וּזְבָחִים כִּשְׁמֹעַ בְּקוֹל יְהֹוָה הִנֵּה שְׁמֹעַ מִזֶּבַח טוֹב לְהַקְשִׁיב מֵחֵלֶב אֵילִים׃}

verses.original: כִּי חַטַּאת־קֶסֶם מֶרִי וְאָוֶן וּתְרָפִים הַפְצַר יַעַן מָאַסְתָּ אֶת־דְּבַר יְהֹוָה וַיִּמְאָסְךָ מִמֶּלֶךְ׃
verses.english: For rebellion is like the sin of divination, Defiance, like the iniquity of teraphim. Because you rejected YHWH’s command, He has rejected you as king.”
verses.commentary: He's not done with the poetry.

tex.original: \hJ{כִּי חַטַּאת־קֶסֶם מֶרִי וְאָוֶן וּתְרָפִים הַפְצַר יַעַן מָאַסְתָּ אֶת־דְּבַר יְהֹוָה וַיִּמְאָסְךָ מִמֶּלֶךְ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל חָטָאתִי כִּי־עָבַרְתִּי אֶת־פִּי־יְהֹוָה וְאֶת־דְּבָרֶיךָ כִּי יָרֵאתִי אֶת־הָעָם וָאֶשְׁמַע בְּקוֹלָם׃

verses.commentary: Now Saul admits he broke the rules on purpose but he was scared of his subordinates, presumably because they had swords and wanted food.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל חָטָאתִי כִּי־עָבַרְתִּי אֶת־פִּי־יְהֹוָה וְאֶת־דְּבָרֶיךָ כִּי יָרֵאתִי אֶת־הָעָם וָאֶשְׁמַע בְּקוֹלָם׃}

verses.original: וְעַתָּה שָׂא נָא אֶת־חַטָּאתִי וְשׁוּב עִמִּי וְאֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶה לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Please, forgive my offense and come back with me, and I will bow low to YHWH.”
verses.commentary:
I can change.

Take me back.

No. We're done.

Goodbye Saul.

verses.commentary: Damn this book is good.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּסֹּב שְׁמוּאֵל לָלֶכֶת וַיַּחֲזֵק בִּכְנַף־מְעִילוֹ וַיִּקָּרַע׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו שְׁמוּאֵל קָרַע יְהֹוָה אֶת־מַמְלְכוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעָלֶיךָ הַיּוֹם וּנְתָנָהּ לְרֵעֲךָ הַטּוֹב מִמֶּךָּ׃
verses.english: And Samuel said to him, “YHWH has this day torn the kingship over Israel away from you and has given it to another who is worthier than you.
verses.commentary: So Samuel looks down at Saul holding that little patch of robe, and he's like “That robe is your kingdom.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו שְׁמוּאֵל קָרַע יְהֹוָה אֶת־מַמְלְכוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵעָלֶיךָ הַיּוֹם וּנְתָנָהּ לְרֵעֲךָ הַטּוֹב מִמֶּךָּ׃}

verses.original: וְגַם נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יְשַׁקֵּר וְלֹא יִנָּחֵם כִּי לֹא אָדָם הוּא לְהִנָּחֵם׃
verses.english: Moreover, the Glory of Israel does not deceive or change His mind, for He is not human that He should change His mind.”
verses.commentary: Our decision is final. Don't expect us to take you back.

tex.original: \hJ{וְגַם נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יְשַׁקֵּר וְלֹא יִנָּחֵם כִּי לֹא אָדָם הוּא לְהִנָּחֵם׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר חָטָאתִי עַתָּה כַּבְּדֵנִי נָא נֶגֶד זִקְנֵי־עַמִּי וְנֶגֶד יִשְׂרָאֵל וְשׁוּב עִמִּי וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֵיתִי לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃
verses.english: But [Saul] pleaded, “I did wrong. Please, honor me in the presence of the elders of my people and in the presence of Israel, and come back with me until I have bowed low to YHWH your God.”
verses.commentary: So Saul's like “Take me back!”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר חָטָאתִי עַתָּה כַּבְּדֵנִי נָא נֶגֶד זִקְנֵי־עַמִּי וְנֶגֶד יִשְׂרָאֵל וְשׁוּב עִמִּי וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֵיתִי לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: וַיָּשׁב שְׁמוּאֵל אַחֲרֵי שָׁאוּל וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ שָׁאוּל לַיהֹוָה׃
verses.english: So Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul bowed low to YHWH.
verses.commentary:
So he did.

Wait what?

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּשׁב שְׁמוּאֵל אַחֲרֵי שָׁאוּל וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ שָׁאוּל לַיהֹוָה׃}
tex.english: \eJ{So Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul bowed low to YHWH.}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל הַגִּישׁוּ אֵלַי אֶת־אֲגַג מֶלֶךְ עֲמָלֵק וַיֵּלֶךְ אֵלָיו אֲגַג מַעֲדַנֹּת וַיֹּאמֶר אֲגָג אָכֵן סָר מַר־הַמָּוֶת׃
verses.english: Samuel said, “Bring forward to me King Agag of Amalek.” Agag approached him with faltering steps; and Agag said, “Ah, bitter death is at hand!”
verses.commentary:
Samuel's like “Bring me that guy you were supposed to kill.”

And Agag is like “I'm already dead, boy.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל הַגִּישׁוּ אֵלַי אֶת־אֲגַג מֶלֶךְ עֲמָלֵק וַיֵּלֶךְ אֵלָיו אֲגַג מַעֲדַנֹּת וַיֹּאמֶר אֲגָג אָכֵן סָר מַר־הַמָּוֶת׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל כַּאֲשֶׁר שִׁכְּלָה נָשִׁים חַרְבֶּךָ כֵּן־תִּשְׁכַּל מִנָּשִׁים אִמֶּךָ וַיְשַׁסֵּף שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־אֲגָג לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה בַּגִּלְגָּל׃
verses.english: Samuel said: “As your sword has bereaved women, So shall your mother be bereaved among women.” And Samuel cut Agag down before YHWH at Gilgal.
verses.commentary: Samuel tells the first your mother joke and cuts Agag in pieces.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל כַּאֲשֶׁר שִׁכְּלָה נָשִׁים חַרְבֶּךָ כֵּן־תִּשְׁכַּל מִנָּשִׁים אִמֶּךָ וַיְשַׁסֵּף שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־אֲגָג לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה בַּגִּלְגָּל׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּלֶךְ שְׁמוּאֵל הָרָמָתָה וְשָׁאוּל עָלָה אֶל־בֵּיתוֹ גִּבְעַת שָׁאוּל׃
verses.english: Samuel then departed for Ramah, and Saul went up to his home at Gibeah of Saul.
verses.commentary: Then they go their separate ways.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֵּלֶךְ שְׁמוּאֵל הָרָמָתָה וְשָׁאוּל עָלָה אֶל־בֵּיתוֹ גִּבְעַת שָׁאוּל׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא־יָסַף שְׁמוּאֵל לִרְאוֹת אֶת־שָׁאוּל עַד־יוֹם מוֹתוֹ כִּי־הִתְאַבֵּל שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־שָׁאוּל וַיהֹוָה נִחָם כִּי־הִמְלִיךְ אֶת־שָׁאוּל עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: Samuel never saw Saul again to the day of his death. But Samuel grieved over Saul, because YHWH regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel.
verses.commentary: And never saw each other again.

tex.original: \hJ{וְלֹא־יָסַף שְׁמוּאֵל לִרְאוֹת אֶת־שָׁאוּל עַד־יוֹם מוֹתוֹ כִּי־הִתְאַבֵּל שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־שָׁאוּל וַיהֹוָה נִחָם כִּי־הִמְלִיךְ אֶת־שָׁאוּל עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל עַד־מָתַי אַתָּה מִתְאַבֵּל אֶל־שָׁאוּל וַאֲנִי מְאַסְתִּיו מִמְּלֹךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל מַלֵּא קַרְנְךָ שֶׁמֶן וְלֵךְ אֶשְׁלָחֲךָ אֶל־יִשַׁי בֵּית־הַלַּחְמִי כִּי־רָאִיתִי בְּבָנָיו לִי מֶלֶךְ׃
verses.english: And YHWH said to Samuel, “How long will you grieve over Saul, since I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and set out; I am sending you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have decided on one of his sons to be king.”
verses.commentary: Ok so YHWH says to Samuel, “Get over Saul, I have someone I want you to meet.”

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֵיךְ אֵלֵךְ וְשָׁמַע שָׁאוּל וַהֲרָגָנִי וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה עֶגְלַת בָּקָר תִּקַּח בְּיָדֶךָ וְאָמַרְתָּ לִזְבֹּחַ לַיהֹוָה בָּאתִי׃
verses.english: Samuel replied, “How can I go? If Saul hears of it, he will kill me.” YHWH answered, “Take a heifer with you, and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to YHWH.’
verses.commentary:
And Samuel's like “What will Saul say if he hears?”

So YHWH's like “Take a cow and pretend you're doing a religious thing.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֵיךְ אֵלֵךְ וְשָׁמַע שָׁאוּל וַהֲרָגָנִי וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה עֶגְלַת בָּקָר תִּקַּח בְּיָדֶךָ וְאָמַרְתָּ לִזְבֹּחַ לַיהֹוָה בָּאתִי׃}

verses.original: וְקָרָאתָ לְיִשַׁי בַּזָּבַח וְאָנֹכִי אוֹדִיעֲךָ אֵת אֲשֶׁר־תַּעֲשֶׂה וּמָשַׁחְתָּ לִי אֵת אֲשֶׁר־אֹמַר אֵלֶיךָ׃
verses.english: Invite Jesse to the sacrificial feast, and then I will make known to you what you shall do; you shall anoint for Me the one I point out to you.”
verses.commentary: “Invite this Jesse guy to dinner. I'll be in touch with further instructions. It's about a king.”

tex.original: \hJ{וְקָרָאתָ לְיִשַׁי בַּזָּבַח וְאָנֹכִי אוֹדִיעֲךָ אֵת אֲשֶׁר־תַּעֲשֶׂה וּמָשַׁחְתָּ לִי אֵת אֲשֶׁר־אֹמַר אֵלֶיךָ׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעַשׂ שְׁמוּאֵל אֵת אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה וַיָּבֹא בֵּית לָחֶם וַיֶּחֶרְדוּ זִקְנֵי הָעִיר לִקְרָאתוֹ וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁלֹם בּוֹאֶךָ׃
verses.english: Samuel did what YHWH commanded. When he came to Bethlehem, the elders of the city went out in alarm to meet him and said, “Do you come on a peaceful errand?”
verses.commentary:
So Samuel did.

He gets to Bethlehem and talks to customs.

They ask if he's here for violence or peace.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּעַשׂ שְׁמוּאֵל אֵת אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהֹוָה וַיָּבֹא בֵּית לָחֶם וַיֶּחֶרְדוּ זִקְנֵי הָעִיר לִקְרָאתוֹ וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁלֹם בּוֹאֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁלוֹם לִזְבֹּחַ לַיהֹוָה בָּאתִי הִתְקַדְּשׁוּ וּבָאתֶם אִתִּי בַּזָּבַח וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת־יִשַׁי וְאֶת־בָּנָיו וַיִּקְרָא לָהֶם לַזָּבַח׃
verses.english: “Yes,” he replied, “I have come to sacrifice to YHWH. Purify yourselves and join me in the sacrificial feast.” He also instructed Jesse and his sons to purify themselves and invited them to the sacrificial feast.
verses.commentary: He says “religion.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁלוֹם לִזְבֹּחַ לַיהֹוָה בָּאתִי הִתְקַדְּשׁוּ וּבָאתֶם אִתִּי בַּזָּבַח וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת־יִשַׁי וְאֶת־בָּנָיו וַיִּקְרָא לָהֶם לַזָּבַח׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי בְּבוֹאָם וַיַּרְא אֶת־אֱלִיאָב וַיֹּאמֶר אַךְ נֶגֶד יְהֹוָה מְשִׁיחוֹ׃
verses.english: When they arrived and he saw Eliab, he thought: “Surely YHWH’s anointed stands before Him.”
verses.commentary: So now he's in Bethlehem, which means house of food, and he sees a guy and thinks “That's him.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְהִי בְּבוֹאָם וַיַּרְא אֶת־אֱלִיאָב וַיֹּאמֶר אַךְ נֶגֶד יְהֹוָה מְשִׁיחוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל אַל־תַּבֵּט אֶל־מַרְאֵהוּ וְאֶל־גְּבֹהַּ קוֹמָתוֹ כִּי מְאַסְתִּיהוּ כִּי לֹא אֲשֶׁר יִרְאֶה הָאָדָם כִּי הָאָדָם יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם וַיהֹוָה יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב׃
verses.english: But YHWH said to Samuel, “Pay no attention to his appearance or his stature, for I have rejected him. For not as man sees [does YHWH see]; man sees only what is visible, but YHWH sees into the heart.”
verses.commentary: But YHWH's like “Don't focus on height, that's how we ended up with Saul. Focus on what's in his heart.”

verses.original: וַיִּקְרָא יִשַׁי אֶל־אֲבִינָדָב וַיַּעֲבִרֵהוּ לִפְנֵי שְׁמוּאֵל וַיֹּאמֶר גַּם־בָּזֶה לֹא־בָחַר יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Then Jesse called Abinadab and had him pass before Samuel; but he said, “YHWH has not chosen this one either.”
verses.commentary:
So he looks at some other guys.

He's not impressed.

Next.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּקְרָא יִשַׁי אֶל־אֲבִינָדָב וַיַּעֲבִרֵהוּ לִפְנֵי שְׁמוּאֵל וַיֹּאמֶר גַּם־בָּזֶה לֹא־בָחַר יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעֲבֵר יִשַׁי שַׁמָּה וַיֹּאמֶר גַּם־בָּזֶה לֹא־בָחַר יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Next Jesse presented Shammah; and again he said, “YHWH has not chosen this one either.”
verses.commentary: Next.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּעֲבֵר יִשַׁי שַׁמָּה וַיֹּאמֶר גַּם־בָּזֶה לֹא־בָחַר יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעֲבֵר יִשַׁי שִׁבְעַת בָּנָיו לִפְנֵי שְׁמוּאֵל וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־יִשַׁי לֹא־בָחַר יְהֹוָה בָּאֵלֶּה׃
verses.english: Thus Jesse presented seven of his sons before Samuel, and Samuel said to Jesse, “YHWH has not chosen any of these.”
verses.commentary: Next. Next. Next. Next.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּעֲבֵר יִשַׁי שִׁבְעַת בָּנָיו לִפְנֵי שְׁמוּאֵל וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־יִשַׁי לֹא־בָחַר יְהֹוָה בָּאֵלֶּה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־יִשַׁי הֲתַמּוּ הַנְּעָרִים וַיֹּאמֶר עוֹד שָׁאַר הַקָּטָן וְהִנֵּה רֹעֶה בַּצֹּאן וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל־יִשַׁי שִׁלְחָה וְקָחֶנּוּ כִּי לֹא־נָסֹב עַד־בֹּאוֹ פֹה׃
verses.english: Then Samuel asked Jesse, “Are these all the boys you have?” He replied, “There is still the youngest; he is tending the flock.” And Samuel said to Jesse, “Send someone to bring him, for we will not sit down to eat until he gets here.”
verses.commentary:
Samuel's like “Is that it?”

Jesse says there's one more, but he's off with the lambs.

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח וַיְבִיאֵהוּ וְהוּא אַדְמוֹנִי עִם־יְפֵה עֵינַיִם וְטוֹב רֹאִיוַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה קוּם מְשָׁחֵהוּ כִּי־זֶה הוּא׃
verses.english: So they sent and brought him. He was ruddy-cheeked, bright-eyed, and handsome. And YHWH said, “Rise and anoint him, for this is the one.”
verses.commentary:
When they saw him, they realized how misguided they'd been to choose the tall guy before.

This guy was different.

He was handsome.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשְׁלַח וַיְבִיאֵהוּ וְהוּא אַדְמוֹנִי עִם־יְפֵה עֵינַיִם וְטוֹב רֹאִיוַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה קוּם מְשָׁחֵהוּ כִּי־זֶה הוּא׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־קֶרֶן הַשֶּׁמֶן וַיִּמְשַׁח אֹתוֹ בְּקֶרֶב אֶחָיו וַתִּצְלַח רוּחַ־יְהֹוָה אֶל־דָּוִד מֵהַיּוֹם הַהוּא וָמָעְלָה וַיָּקם שְׁמוּאֵל וַיֵּלֶךְ הָרָמָתָה׃
verses.english: Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers; and the spirit of YHWH gripped David from that day on. Samuel then set out for Ramah.
verses.commentary:
So Samuel pours oil on his head.

And YHWH grabs hold of David and never lets go.

Then Samuel leaves.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּקַּח שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־קֶרֶן הַשֶּׁמֶן וַיִּמְשַׁח אֹתוֹ בְּקֶרֶב אֶחָיו וַתִּצְלַח רוּחַ־יְהֹוָה אֶל־דָּוִד מֵהַיּוֹם הַהוּא וָמָעְלָה וַיָּקם שְׁמוּאֵל וַיֵּלֶךְ הָרָמָתָה׃}

verses.original: וְרוּחַ יְהֹוָה סָרָה מֵעִם שָׁאוּל וּבִעֲתַתּוּ רוּחַ־רָעָה מֵאֵת יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: Now the spirit of YHWH had departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from YHWH began to terrify him.
verses.commentary: Meanwhile, Saul's gone from blessed to anti-blessed.

tex.original: \hJ{וְרוּחַ יְהֹוָה סָרָה מֵעִם שָׁאוּל וּבִעֲתַתּוּ רוּחַ־רָעָה מֵאֵת יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ עַבְדֵי־שָׁאוּל אֵלָיו הִנֵּה־נָא רוּחַ־אֱלֹהִים רָעָה מְבַעִתֶּךָ׃
verses.english: Saul’s courtiers said to him, “An evil spirit of God is terrifying you.
verses.commentary: Saul's team describes the situation to him.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמְרוּ עַבְדֵי־שָׁאוּל אֵלָיו הִנֵּה־נָא רוּחַ־אֱלֹהִים רָעָה מְבַעִתֶּךָ׃}

verses.original: יֹאמַר־נָא אֲדֹנֵנוּ עֲבָדֶיךָ לְפָנֶיךָ יְבַקְשׁוּ אִישׁ יֹדֵעַ מְנַגֵּן בַּכִּנּוֹר וְהָיָה בִּהְיוֹת עָלֶיךָ רוּחַ־אֱלֹהִים רָעָה וְנִגֵּן בְּיָדוֹ וְטוֹב לָךְ׃
verses.english: Let our lord give the order [and] the courtiers in attendance on you will look for someone who is skilled at playing the lyre; whenever the evil spirit of God comes over you, he will play it and you will feel better.”
verses.commentary:
They suggest finding a good harp guy.

To help with the ghosts.

tex.original: \hJ{יֹאמַר־נָא אֲדֹנֵנוּ עֲבָדֶיךָ לְפָנֶיךָ יְבַקְשׁוּ אִישׁ יֹדֵעַ מְנַגֵּן בַּכִּנּוֹר וְהָיָה בִּהְיוֹת עָלֶיךָ רוּחַ־אֱלֹהִים רָעָה וְנִגֵּן בְּיָדוֹ וְטוֹב לָךְ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל אֶל־עֲבָדָיו רְאוּ־נָא לִי אִישׁ מֵיטִיב לְנַגֵּן וַהֲבִיאוֹתֶם אֵלָי׃
verses.english: So Saul said to his courtiers, “Find me someone who can play well and bring him to me.”
verses.commentary: So Saul says to them “Ok. Do that.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל אֶל־עֲבָדָיו רְאוּ־נָא לִי אִישׁ מֵיטִיב לְנַגֵּן וַהֲבִיאוֹתֶם אֵלָי׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעַן אֶחָד מֵהַנְּעָרִים וַיֹּאמֶר הִנֵּה רָאִיתִי בֵּן לְיִשַׁי בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי יֹדֵעַ נַגֵּן וְגִבּוֹר חַיִל וְאִישׁ מִלְחָמָה וּנְבוֹן דָּבָר וְאִישׁ תֹּאַר וַיהֹוָה עִמּוֹ׃
verses.english: One of the attendants spoke up, “I have observed a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who is skilled in music; he is a stalwart fellow and a warrior, sensible in speech, and handsome in appearance, and YHWH is with him.”
verses.commentary:
Someone has a very specific guy in mind.

A handsome one.

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח שָׁאוּל מַלְאָכִים אֶל־יִשָׁי וַיֹּאמֶר שִׁלְחָה אֵלַי אֶת־דָּוִד בִּנְךָ אֲשֶׁר בַּצֹּאן׃
verses.english: Whereupon Saul sent messengers to Jesse to say, “Send me your son David, who is with the flock.”
verses.commentary: So Saul tells Jesse to send that son of his who's off with the lambs.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשְׁלַח שָׁאוּל מַלְאָכִים אֶל־יִשָׁי וַיֹּאמֶר שִׁלְחָה אֵלַי אֶת־דָּוִד בִּנְךָ אֲשֶׁר בַּצֹּאן׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח יִשַׁי חֲמוֹר לֶחֶם וְנֹאד יַיִן וּגְדִי עִזִּים אֶחָד וַיִּשְׁלַח בְּיַד־דָּוִד בְּנוֹ אֶל־שָׁאוּל׃
verses.english: Jesse took an ass [laden with] bread, a skin of wine, and a kid, and sent them to Saul by his son David.
verses.commentary: Jesse takes an ass, some bread, some wine, a kid, and David, and sends them from Bethlehem to help the king with his ghosts.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּקַּח יִשַׁי חֲמוֹר לֶחֶם וְנֹאד יַיִן וּגְדִי עִזִּים אֶחָד וַיִּשְׁלַח בְּיַד־דָּוִד בְּנוֹ אֶל־שָׁאוּל׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא דָוִד אֶל־שָׁאוּל וַיַּעֲמֹד לְפָנָיו וַיֶּאֱהָבֵהוּ מְאֹד וַיְהִי־לוֹ נֹשֵׂא כֵלִים׃
verses.english: So David came to Saul and entered his service; [Saul] took a strong liking to him and made him one of his arms-bearers.
verses.commentary:
So David meets Saul.

Saul like him.

He has him carry swords and stuff.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּבֹא דָוִד אֶל־שָׁאוּל וַיַּעֲמֹד לְפָנָיו וַיֶּאֱהָבֵהוּ מְאֹד וַיְהִי־לוֹ נֹשֵׂא כֵלִים׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח שָׁאוּל אֶל־יִשַׁי לֵאמֹר יַעֲמד־נָא דָוִד לְפָנַי כִּי־מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינָי׃
verses.english: Saul sent word to Jesse, “Let David remain in my service, for I am pleased with him.”
verses.commentary: Saul sends thanks to Jesse and asks if David can stay.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשְׁלַח שָׁאוּל אֶל־יִשַׁי לֵאמֹר יַעֲמד־נָא דָוִד לְפָנַי כִּי־מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינָי׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה בִּהְיוֹת רוּחַ־אֱלֹהִים אֶל־שָׁאוּל וְלָקַח דָּוִד אֶת־הַכִּנּוֹר וְנִגֵּן בְּיָדוֹ וְרָוַח לְשָׁאוּל וְטוֹב לוֹ וְסָרָה מֵעָלָיו רוּחַ הָרָעָה׃
verses.english: Whenever the [evil] spirit of God came upon Saul, David would take the lyre and play it; Saul would find relief and feel better, and the evil spirit would leave him.
verses.commentary: And David plays the harp and helps the king with his ghosts.

tex.original: \hJ{וְהָיָה בִּהְיוֹת רוּחַ־אֱלֹהִים אֶל־שָׁאוּל וְלָקַח דָּוִד אֶת־הַכִּנּוֹר וְנִגֵּן בְּיָדוֹ וְרָוַח לְשָׁאוּל וְטוֹב לוֹ וְסָרָה מֵעָלָיו רוּחַ הָרָעָה׃}

verses.original: וַיַּאַסְפוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אֶת־מַחֲנֵיהֶם לַמִּלְחָמָה וַיֵּאָסְפוּ שֹׂכֹה אֲשֶׁר לִיהוּדָה וַיַּחֲנוּ בֵּין־שׂוֹכֹה וּבֵין־עֲזֵקָה בְּאֶפֶס דַּמִּים׃
verses.english: The Philistines assembled their forces for battle; they massed at Socoh of Judah, and encamped at Ephes-dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
verses.commentary: War time.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּאַסְפוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אֶת־מַחֲנֵיהֶם לַמִּלְחָמָה וַיֵּאָסְפוּ שֹׂכֹה אֲשֶׁר לִיהוּדָה וַיַּחֲנוּ בֵּין־שׂוֹכֹה וּבֵין־עֲזֵקָה בְּאֶפֶס דַּמִּים׃}

verses.original: וְשָׁאוּל וְאִישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶאֶסְפוּ וַיַּחֲנוּ בְּעֵמֶק הָאֵלָה וַיַּעַרְכוּ מִלְחָמָה לִקְרַאת פְּלִשְׁתִּים׃
verses.english: Saul and the men of Israel massed and encamped in the valley of Elah. They drew up their line of battle against the Philistines,
verses.commentary: Israel vs Philistines.

tex.original: \hJ{וְשָׁאוּל וְאִישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶאֶסְפוּ וַיַּחֲנוּ בְּעֵמֶק הָאֵלָה וַיַּעַרְכוּ מִלְחָמָה לִקְרַאת פְּלִשְׁתִּים׃}

verses.original: וּפְלִשְׁתִּים עֹמְדִים אֶל־הָהָר מִזֶּה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל עֹמְדִים אֶל־הָהָר מִזֶּה וְהַגַּיְא בֵּינֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: with the Philistines stationed on one hill and Israel stationed on the opposite hill; the ravine was between them.
verses.commentary: The text notes that they aren't on the same side of the thing.

tex.original: \hJ{וּפְלִשְׁתִּים עֹמְדִים אֶל־הָהָר מִזֶּה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל עֹמְדִים אֶל־הָהָר מִזֶּה וְהַגַּיְא בֵּינֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּצֵא אִישׁ־הַבֵּנַיִם מִמַּחֲנוֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּים גּלְיָת שְׁמוֹ מִגַּת גּבְהוֹ שֵׁשׁ אַמּוֹת וָזָרֶת׃
verses.english: A champion of the Philistine forces stepped forward; his name was Goliath of Gath, and he was six cubits and a span tall.
verses.commentary:
A cubit's about 18 inches, a span's about 9.

Some sources say six cubits, others say four.

So Goliath is either 9'9” (Masoretic Text) or 6'9” (Dead Sea Scrolls & Septuagint).

Or maybe 6'5” if we use Hebrew cubits, which were a bit shorter than the standardized Egyptian royal ones.

Either way, he's tall.

Take your pick and let's keep moving.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֵּצֵא אִישׁ־הַבֵּנַיִם מִמַּחֲנוֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּים גּלְיָת שְׁמוֹ מִגַּת גּבְהוֹ שֵׁשׁ אַמּוֹת וָזָרֶת׃}

verses.original: וְכוֹבַע נְחֹשֶׁת עַל־רֹאשׁוֹ וְשִׁרְיוֹן קַשְׂקַשִּׂים הוּא לָבוּשׁ וּמִשְׁקַל הַשִּׁרְיוֹן חֲמֵשֶׁת־אֲלָפִים שְׁקָלִים נְחֹשֶׁת׃
verses.english: He had a bronze helmet on his head, and wore a breastplate of scale armor, a bronze breastplate weighing five thousand shekels.
verses.commentary: He has a helmet and some armor and it's heavy, as you'd expect.

tex.original: \hJ{וְכוֹבַע נְחֹשֶׁת עַל־רֹאשׁוֹ וְשִׁרְיוֹן קַשְׂקַשִּׂים הוּא לָבוּשׁ וּמִשְׁקַל הַשִּׁרְיוֹן חֲמֵשֶׁת־אֲלָפִים שְׁקָלִים נְחֹשֶׁת׃}

verses.original: וּמִצְחַת נְחֹשֶׁת עַל־רַגְלָיו וְכִידוֹן נְחֹשֶׁת בֵּין כְּתֵפָיו׃
verses.english: He had bronze greaves on his legs, and a bronze javelin [slung] from his shoulders.
verses.commentary: He's dressed to fight.

tex.original: \hJ{וּמִצְחַת נְחֹשֶׁת עַל־רַגְלָיו וְכִידוֹן נְחֹשֶׁת בֵּין כְּתֵפָיו׃}

verses.original: (וחץ) [וְעֵץ] חֲנִיתוֹ כִּמְנוֹר אֹרְגִים וְלַהֶבֶת חֲנִיתוֹ שֵׁשׁ־מֵאוֹת שְׁקָלִים בַּרְזֶל וְנֹשֵׂא הַצִּנָּה הֹלֵךְ לְפָנָיו׃
verses.english: The shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s bar, and the iron head of his spear weighed six hundred shekels; and the shield-bearer marched in front of him.
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

The thing about the weaver's bar means there's rope wrapped around it for a handle.

His spear his heavy.

And there's a guy in front of him holding his shield.

tex.original: \hJ{(וחץ) [וְעֵץ] חֲנִיתוֹ כִּמְנוֹר אֹרְגִים וְלַהֶבֶת חֲנִיתוֹ שֵׁשׁ־מֵאוֹת שְׁקָלִים בַּרְזֶל וְנֹשֵׂא הַצִּנָּה הֹלֵךְ לְפָנָיו׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעֲמֹד וַיִּקְרָא אֶל־מַעַרְכֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם לָמָּה תֵצְאוּ לַעֲרֹךְ מִלְחָמָה הֲלוֹא אָנֹכִי הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי וְאַתֶּם עֲבָדִים לְשָׁאוּל בְּרוּ־לָכֶם אִישׁ וְיֵרֵד אֵלָי׃
verses.english: He stopped and called out to the ranks of Israel and he said to them, “Why should you come out to engage in battle? I am the Philistine [champion], and you are Saul’s servants. Choose one of your men and let him come down against me.
verses.commentary: He taunts them and says they should choose someone for him to fight.

verses.original: אִם־יוּכַל לְהִלָּחֵם אִתִּי וְהִכָּנִי וְהָיִינוּ לָכֶם לַעֲבָדִים וְאִם־אֲנִי אוּכַל־לוֹ וְהִכִּיתִיו וִהְיִיתֶם לָנוּ לַעֲבָדִים וַעֲבַדְתֶּם אֹתָנוּ׃
verses.english: If he bests me in combat and kills me, we will become your slaves; but if I best him and kill him, you shall be our slaves and serve us.”
verses.commentary: “If your guy kills me, then all our guys will be your slaves, except me cuz I'll be dead. And vice versa.”

tex.original: \hJ{אִם־יוּכַל לְהִלָּחֵם אִתִּי וְהִכָּנִי וְהָיִינוּ לָכֶם לַעֲבָדִים וְאִם־אֲנִי אוּכַל־לוֹ וְהִכִּיתִיו וִהְיִיתֶם לָנוּ לַעֲבָדִים וַעֲבַדְתֶּם אֹתָנוּ׃}

verses.english: And the Philistine ended, “I herewith defy the ranks of Israel. Get me a man and let’s fight it out!”
verses.commentary: He talks shit for a bit.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי אֲנִי חֵרַפְתִּי אֶת־מַעַרְכוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה תְּנוּ־לִי אִישׁ וְנִלָּחֲמָה יָחַד׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁמַע שָׁאוּל וְכל־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־דִּבְרֵי הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי הָאֵלֶּה וַיֵּחַתּוּ וַיִּרְאוּ מְאֹד׃
verses.english: When Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, they were dismayed and terror-stricken.
verses.commentary: Israel is scared.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשְׁמַע שָׁאוּל וְכל־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־דִּבְרֵי הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי הָאֵלֶּה וַיֵּחַתּוּ וַיִּרְאוּ מְאֹד׃}

verses.original: וְדָוִד בֶּן־אִישׁ אֶפְרָתִי הַזֶּה מִבֵּית לֶחֶם יְהוּדָה וּשְׁמוֹ יִשַׁי וְלוֹ שְׁמֹנָה בָנִים וְהָאִישׁ בִּימֵי שָׁאוּל זָקֵן בָּא בַאֲנָשִׁים׃
verses.english: David was the son of a certain Ephrathite of Bethlehem in Judah whose name was Jesse. He had eight sons, and in the days of Saul the man was already old, advanced in years.
verses.commentary: Now the text introduces David for the first time.

tex.original: \hX{וְדָוִד בֶּן־אִישׁ אֶפְרָתִי הַזֶּה מִבֵּית לֶחֶם יְהוּדָה וּשְׁמוֹ יִשַׁי וְלוֹ שְׁמֹנָה בָנִים וְהָאִישׁ בִּימֵי שָׁאוּל זָקֵן בָּא בַאֲנָשִׁים׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּלְכוּ שְׁלֹשֶׁת בְּנֵי־יִשַׁי הַגְּדֹלִים הָלְכוּ אַחֲרֵי־שָׁאוּל לַמִּלְחָמָה וְשֵׁם שְׁלֹשֶׁת בָּנָיו אֲשֶׁר הָלְכוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָה אֱלִיאָב הַבְּכוֹר וּמִשְׁנֵהוּ אֲבִינָדָב וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁי שַׁמָּה׃
verses.english: The three oldest sons of Jesse had left and gone with Saul to the war. The names of his three sons who had gone to the war were Eliab the first-born, the next Abinadab, and the third Shammah;
verses.commentary: Then it lists his brothers so we know who they are.

verses.original: וְדָוִד הוּא הַקָּטָן וּשְׁלֹשָׁה הַגְּדֹלִים הָלְכוּ אַחֲרֵי שָׁאוּל׃
verses.english: and David was the youngest. The three oldest had followed Saul,
verses.commentary: And it mentions that David's the youngest, which we didn't know until now.

verses.original: וְדָוִד הֹלֵךְ וָשָׁב מֵעַל שָׁאוּל לִרְעוֹת אֶת־צֹאן אָבִיו בֵּית לָחֶם׃
verses.english: and David would go back and forth from attending on Saul to shepherd his father’s flock at Bethlehem.
verses.commentary:
So this David has two jobs.

• The sheep.
• The king.

verses.english: The Philistine stepped forward morning and evening and took his stand for forty days.
verses.commentary: Goliath may be a bit rough around the edges but you can't say he's not consistent.

verses.english: Jesse said to his son David, “Take an ephah of this parched corn and these ten loaves of bread for your brothers, and carry them quickly to your brothers in camp.
verses.commentary: Jessie tells David to take corn and bread to his brothers.

Also cheese.

verses.commentary: Cut back to David, he heads out to war.

verses.original: וַתַּעֲרֹךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּפְלִשְׁתִּים מַעֲרָכָה לִקְרַאת מַעֲרָכָה׃
verses.english: Israel and the Philistines drew up their battle lines opposite each other.
verses.commentary: Suspense scene.

verses.original: וַיִּטֹּשׁ דָּוִד אֶת־הַכֵּלִים מֵעָלָיו עַל־יַד שׁוֹמֵר הַכֵּלִים וַיָּרץ הַמַּעֲרָכָה וַיָּבֹא וַיִּשְׁאַל לְאֶחָיו לְשָׁלוֹם׃
verses.english: David left his baggage with the man in charge of the baggage and ran toward the battle line and went to greet his brothers.
verses.commentary: He leaves his bag with the bag man and runs to his brothers at the front.

verses.original: וְהוּא מְדַבֵּר עִמָּם וְהִנֵּה אִישׁ הַבֵּנַיִם עוֹלֶה גּלְיָת הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי שְׁמוֹ מִגַּת (ממערות) [מִמַּעַרְכוֹת] פְּלִשְׁתִּים וַיְדַבֵּר כַּדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וַיִּשְׁמַע דָּוִד׃
verses.english: While he was talking to them, the champion, whose name was Goliath, the Philistine of Gath, stepped forward from the Philistine ranks and spoke the same words as before and David heard him.
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

Resumptive repetition.

Picking up where we left off in 17:10.

verses.original: וְכֹל אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּרְאוֹתָם אֶת־הָאִישׁ וַיָּנֻסוּ מִפָּנָיו וַיִּירְאוּ מְאֹד׃
verses.english: When the men of Israel saw the man, they fled in terror.
verses.commentary:
In 17:16 we heard this had been going on for forty days.

You'd think the men would've acclimated a bit by now but apparently not.

verses.english: And the men of Israel were saying [among themselves], “Do you see that man coming out? He comes out to defy Israel! The man who kills him will be rewarded by the king with great riches; he will also give him his daughter in marriage and grant exemption to his father’s house in Israel.”
verses.commentary: The men do the usual banter about how the lottery has an upside and a downside.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד אֶל־הָאֲנָשִׁים הָעֹמְדִים עִמּוֹ לֵאמֹר מַה־יֵּעָשֶׂה לָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יַכֶּה אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי הַלָּז וְהֵסִיר חֶרְפָּה מֵעַל יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי מִי הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי הֶעָרֵל הַזֶּה כִּי חֵרֵף מַעַרְכוֹת אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים׃
verses.english: David asked the men standing near him, “What will be done for the man who kills that Philistine and removes the disgrace from Israel? Who is that uncircumcised Philistine that he dares defy the ranks of the living God?”
verses.commentary:
David's like “Say that again, I was watching the sheep earlier.”

Then he calls him a foreskin.

The Hebrew הערלהזה can be parsed as:

ה + ערל + הזה | “this uncircumcised one”
ה + ערלה + זה | “this foreskin”

The latter's a bit grammatically off, since it's the masculine word for “this” while foreskin is feminine.

Then again, the only grammatical sin you have to commit to make it work is to treat the word “foreskin” as masculine and not feminine, which isn't exactly a stretch for a sufficiently playful (read: awake) author, given that foreskins are, well. Nevermind. Forget I said anything.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ הָעָם כַּדָּבָר הַזֶּה לֵאמֹר כֹּה יֵעָשֶׂה לָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יַכֶּנּוּ׃

verses.commentary: So the troops update David on the payoff structure of the situation.

And David's like Jesus.

No need to get all mad.

verses.original: וַיִּסֹּב מֵאֶצְלוֹ אֶל־מוּל אַחֵר וַיֹּאמֶר כַּדָּבָר הַזֶּה וַיְשִׁבֻהוּ הָעָם דָּבָר כַּדָּבָר הָרִאשׁוֹן׃

(Narrator: The author dons his midrash hat.)

Saul: “You fight... the lions?”

David: “Correct.”

Saul: ...

David: “And the bears.”

Saul: (incredulously) “And how exactly do you fight these... bears?”

David: I grab it by the beard and I (gesturing) give him one of these.

Saul: By the beard?

David: Correct, the beard.

Saul: (turns to his men) “What word is the boy using here?”

Saul's Men: זקנו sir. ZQNW.

Saul: (to his men) And this term means... beard?

Men: Yes sir. Or rather, “His beard.” From the root ZQN. The W is a pronominal suffix, meaning “his.”

Saul: So... beard.

Men: Yes sir.

Saul: Does it perhaps also have a meaning of “mane” or “fur”?

Men: No sir.

Saul: It means beard?

Men: Yes sir.

Saul: Of a human?

Men: Yes sir.

Saul: And not fur.

Men: No sir.

Saul: It never means “mane” or “fur”?

Men: Well, there is one important text in which the usage of זקנו to mean “fur” or “mane” of an animal is attested.

Saul: What text?

Men: 1 Samuel 17:35, sir.

Saul: That's here, you imbecile.

Men: Ah, indeed it is sir. My apologies.

Saul: (to his other men) So the child is actually saying beard?

Men: I believe so sir.

Saul: The child is claiming to fight, and kill...

Men: Lions and bears, sire.

Saul: And his strategy for doing so is... to grab them by the beard.

Men: That is the claim sir. According to the text.

Saul: (turning back to David) Please continue.

(Narrator: The author's hat returns to normal.)

The tension now reaches a crescendo.

And the fight of the millennium begins!

tex.original: \hX{וְהָיָה כִּי־קָם הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי וַיֵּלֶךְ וַיִּקְרַב לִקְרַאת דָּוִד וַיְמַהֵר דָּוִד וַיָּרץ הַמַּעֲרָכָה לִקְרַאת הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח דָּוִד אֶת־יָדוֹ אֶל־הַכֶּלִי וַיִּקַּח מִשָּׁם אֶבֶן וַיְקַלַּע וַיַּךְ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי אֶל־מִצְחוֹ וַתִּטְבַּע הָאֶבֶן בְּמִצְחוֹ וַיִּפֹּל עַל־פָּנָיו אָרְצָה׃
verses.english: David put his hand into the bag; he took out a stone and slung it. It struck the Philistine in the forehead; the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell face down on the ground.
verses.commentary:
Battle's over.

David wins.

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּשְׁלַח דָּוִד אֶת־יָדוֹ אֶל־הַכֶּלִי וַיִּקַּח מִשָּׁם אֶבֶן וַיְקַלַּע וַיַּךְ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי אֶל־מִצְחוֹ וַתִּטְבַּע הָאֶבֶן בְּמִצְחוֹ וַיִּפֹּל עַל־פָּנָיו אָרְצָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֶּחֱזַק דָּוִד מִן־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי בַּקֶּלַע וּבָאֶבֶן וַיַּךְ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי וַיְמִתֵהוּ וְחֶרֶב אֵין בְּיַד־דָּוִד׃
verses.english: Thus David bested the Philistine with sling and stone; he struck him down and killed him. David had no sword;
verses.commentary:
In summary, David wins.

The text notes he had no sword.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֶּחֱזַק דָּוִד מִן־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי בַּקֶּלַע וּבָאֶבֶן וַיַּךְ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי וַיְמִתֵהוּ וְחֶרֶב אֵין בְּיַד־דָּוִד׃}

verses.original: וַיָּרץ דָּוִד וַיַּעֲמֹד אֶל־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי וַיִּקַּח אֶת־חַרְבּוֹ וַיִּשְׁלְפָהּ מִתַּעְרָהּ וַיְמֹתְתֵהוּ וַיִּכְרת־בָּהּ אֶת־רֹאשׁוֹ וַיִּרְאוּ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּים כִּי־מֵת גִּבּוֹרָם וַיָּנֻסוּ׃
verses.english: so David ran up and stood over the Philistine, grasped his sword and pulled it from its sheath; and with it he dispatched him and cut off his head. When the Philistines saw that their warrior was dead, they ran.
verses.commentary:
So he takes out his sword.

And cuts off his head.

And the other team decides to head home early today.

verses.original: וַיָּקֻמוּ אַנְשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל וִיהוּדָה וַיָּרִעוּ וַיִּרְדְּפוּ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּים עַד־בּוֹאֲךָ גַיְא וְעַד שַׁעֲרֵי עֶקְרוֹן וַיִּפְּלוּ חַלְלֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים בְּדֶרֶךְ שַׁעֲרַיִם וְעַד־גַּת וְעַד־עֶקְרוֹן׃
verses.english: The men of Israel and Judah rose up with a war cry and they pursued the Philistines all the way to Gai and up to the gates of Ekron; the Philistines fell mortally wounded along the road to Shaarim up to Gath and Ekron.
verses.commentary: The Israel Judah team (two separate countries at this point) has a different idea, and they kill a bunch of them.

verses.original: וַיָּשֻׁבוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִדְּלֹק אַחֲרֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים וַיָּשֹׁסּוּ אֶת־מַחֲנֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: Then the Israelites returned from chasing the Philistines and looted their camp.
verses.commentary: They also steal their stuff.

tex.original: \hX{וַיָּשֻׁבוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִדְּלֹק אַחֲרֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים וַיָּשֹׁסּוּ אֶת־מַחֲנֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח דָּוִד אֶת־רֹאשׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי וַיְבִאֵהוּ יְרוּשָׁלָ͏ִם וְאֶת־כֵּלָיו שָׂם בְּאהֳלוֹ׃
verses.english: David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem; and he put his weapons in his own tent.
verses.commentary:
David takes the head to Jerusalem which is sort of a minor plot hole. [Jerusalem isn't conquered until 2 Samuel 5. Judges 1:21 says the Jebusites were still living there with Benjamin. David has no meaningful connection with Jerusalem before he captures it. Rather, David is associated with Bethlehem (his birthplace), Judah and Hebron (where he reigns for 7½ years), the wilderness (Adullam, Ziph, En-gedi), and Ziklag (given to him by Achish) but Jerusalem is essentially absent from David's story until the conquest.]

And he also takes his weapons to his tent.

Ok so...

Assuming the tent is near the battle site.

Battle to Jerusalem:

• 5 hours 30 mins.
• Holding the head.
• Holding the weapons.

In Jerusalem

• Presumably he drops the head off.
• With the Jebusites.
• Who run Jerusalem then.
• Which is a weird thing to do.
• Because they seem to be Canaanites.
• Not Philistines.
• And not Israelites.
• So they're unlikely to have any interest in this head, positively or negatively.
• That said, it's a severed head.
• So probably negative.
• All else being equal.
• Back to the road.

Jerusalem to Tent:

• About 5 hours 20 mins.
• Holding the weapons.
• No longer holding the head.
• Assuming he dropped it off with the Jebusites.

Tent to Home:

• 4 hours 20 minutes.

Alternatively, to play apologetics:

• If his tent was at home in Bethlehem.

Then we shave about 8 hours off the total walk.

In addition:

• If we don't require the ordering of the trips to match the order in the text.
• If we assume he had someone to help him carry the stuff.
• If we assume he didn't walk, but drove some cows in a cart or something.
• Or any other such assumptions.

We still have to explain taking a severed head to a city that neither side of this battle was involved with.

Which is a pretty weird behavior, to say the least.

Not just being silly here. There are entire academic papers on this.

But we've had enough fun in this verse.

Moving on.

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּקַּח דָּוִד אֶת־רֹאשׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי וַיְבִאֵהוּ יְרוּשָׁלָ͏ִם וְאֶת־כֵּלָיו שָׂם בְּאהֳלוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְכִרְאוֹת שָׁאוּל אֶת־דָּוִד יֹצֵא לִקְרַאת הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי אָמַר אֶל־אַבְנֵר שַׂר הַצָּבָא בֶּן־מִי־זֶה הַנַּעַר אַבְנֵר וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְנֵר חֵי־נַפְשְׁךָ הַמֶּלֶךְ אִם־יָדָעְתִּי׃
verses.english: When Saul saw David going out to assault the Philistine, he asked his army commander Abner, “Whose son is that boy, Abner?” And Abner replied, “By your life, Your Majesty, I do not know.”
verses.commentary:
Cut back to Saul, earlier in the day, Saul turns to his commander Abner and asks who David's dad is.

Then Abner, aka “Father of Ner Son of Ner” (who has some “who's your dad” type issues of his own) says “I don't know.”

tex.original: \hX{וְכִרְאוֹת שָׁאוּל אֶת־דָּוִד יֹצֵא לִקְרַאת הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי אָמַר אֶל־אַבְנֵר שַׂר הַצָּבָא בֶּן־מִי־זֶה הַנַּעַר אַבְנֵר וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְנֵר חֵי־נַפְשְׁךָ הַמֶּלֶךְ אִם־יָדָעְתִּי׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁאַל אַתָּה בֶּן־מִי־זֶה הָעָלֶם׃
verses.english: “Then find out whose son that young fellow is,” the king ordered.
verses.commentary: So Saul says “Go find out.”

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁאַל אַתָּה בֶּן־מִי־זֶה הָעָלֶם׃}

verses.original: וּכְשׁוּב דָּוִד מֵהַכּוֹת אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי וַיִּקַּח אֹתוֹ אַבְנֵר וַיְבִאֵהוּ לִפְנֵי שָׁאוּל וְרֹאשׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי בְּיָדוֹ׃
verses.english: So when David returned after killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him to Saul, with the head of the Philistine still in his hand.
verses.commentary:
So when David's back from his 15 hour severed head marathon walk to the Jebusites and back, Abner brings him to Saul and—

Wait scratch that, he's still holding the head.

tex.original: \hX{וּכְשׁוּב דָּוִד מֵהַכּוֹת אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי וַיִּקַּח אֹתוֹ אַבְנֵר וַיְבִאֵהוּ לִפְנֵי שָׁאוּל וְרֹאשׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי בְּיָדוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו שָׁאוּל בֶּן־מִי אַתָּה הַנָּעַר וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד בֶּן־עַבְדְּךָ יִשַׁי בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי׃
verses.english: Saul said to him, “Whose son are you, my boy?” And David answered, “The son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.”
verses.commentary:
Saul asks who David's father is.

David says it's Jesse from Bethlehem.

So Saul and David finally meet for the first time.

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו שָׁאוּל בֶּן־מִי אַתָּה הַנָּעַר וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד בֶּן־עַבְדְּךָ יִשַׁי בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי כְּכַלֹּתוֹ לְדַבֵּר אֶל־שָׁאוּל וְנֶפֶשׁ יְהוֹנָתָן נִקְשְׁרָה בְּנֶפֶשׁ דָּוִד (ויאהבו) [וַיֶּאֱהָבֵהוּ] יְהוֹנָתָן כְּנַפְשׁוֹ׃
verses.english: When [David] finished speaking with Saul, Jonathan’s soul became bound up with the soul of David; Jonathan loved David as himself.
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

Ok so Jonathan (Saul's son) falls hard for David.

tex.original: \hX{וַיְהִי כְּכַלֹּתוֹ לְדַבֵּר אֶל־שָׁאוּל וְנֶפֶשׁ יְהוֹנָתָן נִקְשְׁרָה בְּנֶפֶשׁ דָּוִד (ויאהבו) [וַיֶּאֱהָבֵהוּ] יְהוֹנָתָן כְּנַפְשׁוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקָּחֵהוּ שָׁאוּל בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא וְלֹא נְתָנוֹ לָשׁוּב בֵּית אָבִיו׃
verses.english: Saul took him [into his service] that day and would not let him return to his father’s house.—
verses.commentary:
Saul hires David full-time.

Like seriously full-time.

No more going back home.

Also if you recall 17:57, three sentences ago, he's presumably still holding the head.

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּקָּחֵהוּ שָׁאוּל בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא וְלֹא נְתָנוֹ לָשׁוּב בֵּית אָבִיו׃}

verses.original: וַיִּכְרֹת יְהוֹנָתָן וְדָוִד בְּרִית בְּאַהֲבָתוֹ אֹתוֹ כְּנַפְשׁוֹ׃
verses.english: Jonathan and David made a pact, because [Jonathan] loved him as himself.
verses.commentary:
Jonathan and David make it official.

Best friends forever.

Head still in hand.

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּכְרֹת יְהוֹנָתָן וְדָוִד בְּרִית בְּאַהֲבָתוֹ אֹתוֹ כְּנַפְשׁוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּתְפַּשֵּׁט יְהוֹנָתָן אֶת־הַמְּעִיל אֲשֶׁר עָלָיו וַיִּתְּנֵהוּ לְדָוִד וּמַדָּיו וְעַד־חַרְבּוֹ וְעַד־קַשְׁתּוֹ וְעַד־חֲגֹרוֹ׃
verses.english: Jonathan took off the cloak and tunic he was wearing and gave them to David, together with his sword, bow, and belt.
verses.commentary:
Jonathan gives his clothes to David.

Like the ones he's currently wearing.

Belt included.

Things are getting serious.

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּתְפַּשֵּׁט יְהוֹנָתָן אֶת־הַמְּעִיל אֲשֶׁר עָלָיו וַיִּתְּנֵהוּ לְדָוִד וּמַדָּיו וְעַד־חַרְבּוֹ וְעַד־קַשְׁתּוֹ וְעַד־חֲגֹרוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּצֵא דָוִד בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁלָחֶנּוּ שָׁאוּל יַשְׂכִּיל וַיְשִׂמֵהוּ שָׁאוּל עַל אַנְשֵׁי הַמִּלְחָמָה וַיִּיטַב בְּעֵינֵי כל־הָעָם וְגַם בְּעֵינֵי עַבְדֵי שָׁאוּל׃
verses.english: David went out [with the troops], and he was successful in every mission on which Saul sent him, and Saul put him in command of all the soldiers; this pleased all the troops and Saul’s courtiers as well.
verses.commentary:
David keeps winning.

Everyone likes him.

tex.original: \hX{וַיֵּצֵא דָוִד בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁלָחֶנּוּ שָׁאוּל יַשְׂכִּיל וַיְשִׂמֵהוּ שָׁאוּל עַל אַנְשֵׁי הַמִּלְחָמָה וַיִּיטַב בְּעֵינֵי כל־הָעָם וְגַם בְּעֵינֵי עַבְדֵי שָׁאוּל׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי בְּבוֹאָם בְּשׁוּב דָּוִד מֵהַכּוֹת אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי וַתֵּצֶאנָה הַנָּשִׁים מִכּל־עָרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (לשור) [לָשִׁיר] וְהַמְּחֹלוֹת לִקְרַאת שָׁאוּל הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּתֻפִּים בְּשִׂמְחָה וּבְשָׁלִשִׁים׃
verses.english: When the [troops] came home [and] David returned from killing the Philistine, the women of all the towns of Israel came out singing and dancing to greet King Saul with timbrels, shouting, and sistrums.
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

David comes home after winning.

The girls are into David.

verses.original: וַתַּעֲנֶינָה הַנָּשִׁים הַמְשַׂחֲקוֹת וַתֹּאמַרְןָ הִכָּה שָׁאוּל בַּאֲלָפָו וְדָוִד בְּרִבְבֹתָיו׃
verses.english: The women sang as they danced, and they chanted: Saul has slain his thousands; David, his tens of thousands!
verses.commentary: First law of power.

tex.original: \hJ{וַתַּעֲנֶינָה הַנָּשִׁים הַמְשַׂחֲקוֹת וַתֹּאמַרְןָ הִכָּה שָׁאוּל בַּאֲלָפָו וְדָוִד בְּרִבְבֹתָיו׃}

verses.original: וַיִּחַר לְשָׁאוּל מְאֹד וַיֵּרַע בְּעֵינָיו הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה וַיֹּאמֶר נָתְנוּ לְדָוִד רְבָבוֹת וְלִי נָתְנוּ הָאֲלָפִים וְעוֹד לוֹ אַךְ הַמְּלוּכָה׃

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוֹנָתָן אֶל־דָּוִד לְכָה וְנֵצֵא הַשָּׂדֶה וַיֵּצְאוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם הַשָּׂדֶה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוֹנָתָן אֶל־דָּוִד יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי־אֶחְקֹר אֶת־אָבִי כָּעֵת מָחָר הַשְּׁלִשִׁית וְהִנֵּה־טוֹב אֶל־דָּוִד וְלֹא־אָז אֶשְׁלַח אֵלֶיךָ וְגָלִיתִי אֶת־אזְנֶךָ׃
verses.english: Then Jonathan said to David, “By YHWH, the God of Israel! I will sound out my father at this time tomorrow, [or] on the third day; and if [his response] is favorable for David, I will send a message to you at once and disclose it to you.
verses.commentary: Then Jonathan says his plan, out in the open.

verses.original: כֹּה־יַעֲשֶׂה יְהֹוָה לִיהוֹנָתָן וְכֹה יֹסִיף כִּי־יֵיטִב אֶל־אָבִי אֶת־הָרָעָה עָלֶיךָ וְגָלִיתִי אֶת־אזְנֶךָ וְשִׁלַּחְתִּיךָ וְהָלַכְתָּ לְשָׁלוֹם וִיהִי יְהֹוָה עִמָּךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר הָיָה עִם־אָבִי׃
verses.english: But if my father intends to do you harm, may YHWH do thus to Jonathan and more if I do [not] disclose it to you and send you off to escape unharmed. May YHWH be with you, as He used to be with my father.
verses.commentary: He spells out all the details for anyone who might be listening. Just in case they missed the first part of the conversation.

verses.original: וְלֹא אִם־עוֹדֶנִּי חָי וְלֹא־תַעֲשֶׂה עִמָּדִי חֶסֶד יְהֹוָה וְלֹא אָמוּת׃
verses.english: Nor shall you fail to show me YHWH’s faithfulness, while I am alive; nor, when I am dead,
verses.commentary: More plan.

tex.original: \hX{וְלֹא אִם־עוֹדֶנִּי חָי וְלֹא־תַעֲשֶׂה עִמָּדִי חֶסֶד יְהֹוָה וְלֹא אָמוּת׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא־תַכְרִית אֶת־חַסְדְּךָ מֵעִם בֵּיתִי עַד־עוֹלָם וְלֹא בְּהַכְרִת יְהֹוָה אֶת־אֹיְבֵי דָוִד אִישׁ מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה׃
verses.english: shall you ever discontinue your faithfulness to my house—not even after YHWH has wiped out every one of David’s enemies from the face of the earth.
verses.commentary: Out in the open.

tex.original: \hX{וְלֹא־תַכְרִית אֶת־חַסְדְּךָ מֵעִם בֵּיתִי עַד־עוֹלָם וְלֹא בְּהַכְרִת יְהֹוָה אֶת־אֹיְבֵי דָוִד אִישׁ מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּכְרֹת יְהוֹנָתָן עִם־בֵּית דָּוִד וּבִקֵּשׁ יְהֹוָה מִיַּד אֹיְבֵי דָוִד׃
verses.english: Thus has Jonathan covenanted with the house of David; and may YHWH requite the enemies of David!”
verses.commentary: Jonathan seems to want people to overhear this covenant.

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּכְרֹת יְהוֹנָתָן עִם־בֵּית דָּוִד וּבִקֵּשׁ יְהֹוָה מִיַּד אֹיְבֵי דָוִד׃}

verses.original: וַיּוֹסֶף יְהוֹנָתָן לְהַשְׁבִּיעַ אֶת־דָּוִד בְּאַהֲבָתוֹ אֹתוֹ כִּי־אַהֲבַת נַפְשׁוֹ אֲהֵבוֹ׃
verses.english: Jonathan, out of his love for David, adjured him again, for he loved him as himself.
verses.commentary: Then the Narrator steps in to clarify some things that may not have been clear from the previous scene.

tex.original: \hX{וַיּוֹסֶף יְהוֹנָתָן לְהַשְׁבִּיעַ אֶת־דָּוִד בְּאַהֲבָתוֹ אֹתוֹ כִּי־אַהֲבַת נַפְשׁוֹ אֲהֵבוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר־לוֹ יְהוֹנָתָן מָחָר חֹדֶשׁ וְנִפְקַדְתָּ כִּי יִפָּקֵד מוֹשָׁבֶךָ׃
verses.english: Jonathan said to him, “Tomorrow will be the new moon; and you will be missed when your seat remains vacant.
verses.commentary: So Jonathan's like “Tomorrow's moonday. I'll miss you when your seat remains vacant.”

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר־לוֹ יְהוֹנָתָן מָחָר חֹדֶשׁ וְנִפְקַדְתָּ כִּי יִפָּקֵד מוֹשָׁבֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וְשִׁלַּשְׁתָּ תֵּרֵד מְאֹד וּבָאתָ אֶל־הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־נִסְתַּרְתָּ שָּׁם בְּיוֹם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְיָשַׁבְתָּ אֵצֶל הָאֶבֶן הָאָזֶל׃
verses.english: So the day after tomorrow, go down all the way to the place where you hid the other time, and stay close to the Ezel stone.
verses.commentary: The day after that, go down to the rock. You know the one.

tex.original: \hX{וְשִׁלַּשְׁתָּ תֵּרֵד מְאֹד וּבָאתָ אֶל־הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־נִסְתַּרְתָּ שָּׁם בְּיוֹם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְיָשַׁבְתָּ אֵצֶל הָאֶבֶן הָאָזֶל׃}

verses.original: וַאֲנִי שְׁלֹשֶׁת הַחִצִּים צִדָּה אוֹרֶה לְשַׁלַּח־לִי לְמַטָּרָה׃
verses.english: Now I will shoot three arrows to one side of it, as though I were shooting at a mark,
verses.commentary: I'll shoot three arrows.

tex.original: \hX{וַאֲנִי שְׁלֹשֶׁת הַחִצִּים צִדָּה אוֹרֶה לְשַׁלַּח־לִי לְמַטָּרָה׃}

verses.original: וְהִנֵּה אֶשְׁלַח אֶת־הַנַּעַר לֵךְ מְצָא אֶת־הַחִצִּים אִם־אָמֹר אֹמַר לַנַּעַר הִנֵּה הַחִצִּים מִמְּךָ וָהֵנָּה קָחֶנּוּ וָבֹאָה כִּי־שָׁלוֹם לְךָ וְאֵין דָּבָר חַי־יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: and I will order the boy to go and find the arrows. If I call to the boy, ‘Hey! the arrows are on this side of you,’ be reassured and come, for you are safe and there is no danger—as YHWH lives!
verses.commentary: If you hear me say this, that means it's safe.

tex.original: \hX{וְהִנֵּה אֶשְׁלַח אֶת־הַנַּעַר לֵךְ מְצָא אֶת־הַחִצִּים אִם־אָמֹר אֹמַר לַנַּעַר הִנֵּה הַחִצִּים מִמְּךָ וָהֵנָּה קָחֶנּוּ וָבֹאָה כִּי־שָׁלוֹם לְךָ וְאֵין דָּבָר חַי־יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְאִם־כֹּה אֹמַר לָעֶלֶם הִנֵּה הַחִצִּים מִמְּךָ וָהָלְאָה לֵךְ כִּי שִׁלַּחֲךָ יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: But if, instead, I call to the lad, ‘Hey! the arrows are beyond you,’ then leave, for YHWH has sent you away.
verses.commentary: If you hear me say that, then run.

tex.original: \hX{וְאִם־כֹּה אֹמַר לָעֶלֶם הִנֵּה הַחִצִּים מִמְּךָ וָהָלְאָה לֵךְ כִּי שִׁלַּחֲךָ יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְהַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְנוּ אֲנִי וָאָתָּה הִנֵּה יְהֹוָה בֵּינִי וּבֵינְךָ עַד־עוֹלָם׃
verses.english: As for the promise we made to each other, may YHWH be [witness] between you and me forever.”
verses.commentary: Remember what we promised.

tex.original: \hX{וְהַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְנוּ אֲנִי וָאָתָּה הִנֵּה יְהֹוָה בֵּינִי וּבֵינְךָ עַד־עוֹלָם׃}

verses.original: וַיִּסָּתֵר דָּוִד בַּשָּׂדֶה וַיְהִי הַחֹדֶשׁ וַיֵּשֶׁב הַמֶּלֶךְ (על) [אֶל־]הַלֶּחֶם לֶאֱכוֹל׃
verses.english: David hid in the field. The new moon came, and the king sat down to partake of the meal.
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

Cut to moonday. David's by the special rock, his seat vacant. He's not at dinner.

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּסָּתֵר דָּוִד בַּשָּׂדֶה וַיְהִי הַחֹדֶשׁ וַיֵּשֶׁב הַמֶּלֶךְ (על) [אֶל־]הַלֶּחֶם לֶאֱכוֹל׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּשֶׁב הַמֶּלֶךְ עַל־מוֹשָׁבוֹ כְּפַעַם בְּפַעַם אֶל־מוֹשַׁב הַקִּיר וַיָּקם יְהוֹנָתָן וַיֵּשֶׁב אַבְנֵר מִצַּד שָׁאוּל וַיִּפָּקֵד מְקוֹם דָּוִד׃
verses.english: When the king took his usual place on the seat by the wall, Jonathan rose and Abner sat down at Saul’s side; but David’s place remained vacant.
verses.commentary: Saul sits by the wall. Dadner sits next to him. David's nowhere to be seen.

tex.original: \hX{וַיֵּשֶׁב הַמֶּלֶךְ עַל־מוֹשָׁבוֹ כְּפַעַם בְּפַעַם אֶל־מוֹשַׁב הַקִּיר וַיָּקם יְהוֹנָתָן וַיֵּשֶׁב אַבְנֵר מִצַּד שָׁאוּל וַיִּפָּקֵד מְקוֹם דָּוִד׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא־דִבֶּר שָׁאוּל מְאוּמָה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא כִּי אָמַר מִקְרֶה הוּא בִּלְתִּי טָהוֹר הוּא כִּי־לֹא טָהוֹר׃
verses.english: That day, however, Saul said nothing. “It’s accidental,” he thought. “He must be unclean and not yet cleansed.”
verses.commentary:
Saul suspects nothing much.

David's probably just dirty.

tex.original: \hX{וְלֹא־דִבֶּר שָׁאוּל מְאוּמָה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא כִּי אָמַר מִקְרֶה הוּא בִּלְתִּי טָהוֹר הוּא כִּי־לֹא טָהוֹר׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי מִמּחֳרַת הַחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי וַיִּפָּקֵד מְקוֹם דָּוִדוַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל אֶל־יְהוֹנָתָן בְּנוֹ מַדּוּעַ לֹא־בָא בֶן־יִשַׁי גַּם־תְּמוֹל גַּם־הַיּוֹם אֶל־הַלָּחֶם׃
verses.english: But on the day after the new moon, the second day, David’s place was vacant again. So Saul said to his son Jonathan, “Why didn’t the son of Jesse come to the meal yesterday or today?”
verses.commentary:
The day after moonday, Saul begins to expect something.

He asks Jonathan where David is, reluctant to say his name.

tex.original: \hX{וַיְהִי מִמּחֳרַת הַחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי וַיִּפָּקֵד מְקוֹם דָּוִדוַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל אֶל־יְהוֹנָתָן בְּנוֹ מַדּוּעַ לֹא־בָא בֶן־יִשַׁי גַּם־תְּמוֹל גַּם־הַיּוֹם אֶל־הַלָּחֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעַן יְהוֹנָתָן אֶת־שָׁאוּל נִשְׁאֹל נִשְׁאַל דָּוִד מֵעִמָּדִי עַד־בֵּית לָחֶם׃
verses.english: Jonathan answered Saul, “David begged leave of me to go to Bethlehem.
verses.commentary: Jonathan says “David's at home.”

tex.original: \hX{וַיַּעַן יְהוֹנָתָן אֶת־שָׁאוּל נִשְׁאֹל נִשְׁאַל דָּוִד מֵעִמָּדִי עַד־בֵּית לָחֶם׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שַׁלְּחֵנִי נָא כִּי זֶבַח מִשְׁפָּחָה לָנוּ בָּעִיר וְהוּא צִוָּה־לִי אָחִי וְעַתָּה אִם־מָצָאתִי חֵן בְּעֵינֶיךָ אִמָּלְטָה נָּא וְאֶרְאֶה אֶת־אֶחָי עַל־כֵּן לֹא־בָא אֶל־שֻׁלְחַן הַמֶּלֶךְ׃
verses.english: He said, ‘Please let me go, for we are going to have a family feast in our town and my brother has summoned me to it. Do me a favor, let me slip away to see my kinsmen.’ That is why he has not come to the king’s table.”
verses.commentary: “I have a family thing.”

verses.original: וַיִּחַר־אַף שָׁאוּל בִּיהוֹנָתָן וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ בֶּן־נַעֲוַת הַמַּרְדּוּת הֲלוֹא יָדַעְתִּי כִּי־בֹחֵר אַתָּה לְבֶן־יִשַׁי לְבשְׁתְּךָ וּלְבֹשֶׁת עֶרְוַת אִמֶּךָ׃
verses.english: Saul flew into a rage against Jonathan. “You son of a perverse, rebellious woman!” he shouted. “I know that you side with the son of Jesse—to your shame, and to the shame of your mother’s nakedness!
verses.commentary:
Saul explodes and insults his wife. And son.

He accuses Jonathan, correctly, of siding with David.

And of shaming his mother's nakedness.

Now we know from Leviticus (and maybe elsewhere) that “your father's nakedness” sometimes means “your mother.” So “your mother's nakedness” potentially means “your father.”

In which case he's now using euphemisms for both David and himself and sort of also for Jonathan all at once.

Either way, Saul's all over the place.

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּחַר־אַף שָׁאוּל בִּיהוֹנָתָן וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ בֶּן־נַעֲוַת הַמַּרְדּוּת הֲלוֹא יָדַעְתִּי כִּי־בֹחֵר אַתָּה לְבֶן־יִשַׁי לְבשְׁתְּךָ וּלְבֹשֶׁת עֶרְוַת אִמֶּךָ׃}

verses.original: כִּי כל־הַיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר בֶּן־יִשַׁי חַי עַל־הָאֲדָמָה לֹא תִכּוֹן אַתָּה וּמַלְכוּתֶךָ וְעַתָּה שְׁלַח וְקַח אֹתוֹ אֵלַי כִּי בֶן־מָוֶת הוּא׃
verses.english: For as long as the son of Jesse lives on earth, neither you nor your kingship will be secure. Now then, have him brought to me, for he is marked for death.”
verses.commentary: Saul tries to appeal to Jonathan's desire to be king himself.

tex.original: \hX{כִּי כל־הַיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר בֶּן־יִשַׁי חַי עַל־הָאֲדָמָה לֹא תִכּוֹן אַתָּה וּמַלְכוּתֶךָ וְעַתָּה שְׁלַח וְקַח אֹתוֹ אֵלַי כִּי בֶן־מָוֶת הוּא׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעַן יְהוֹנָתָן אֶת־שָׁאוּל אָבִיו וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו לָמָּה יוּמַת מֶה עָשָׂה׃
verses.english: But Jonathan spoke up and said to his father, “Why should he be put to death? What has he done?”
verses.commentary: Jonathan is apparently more interested in David.

So Saul does his famous spear trick that always misses.

Jonathan storms off.

He's too upset to eat.

Also dad.

The next morning, Jonathan goes out to that field with the special rock.

verses.commentary: He shoots the arrows past the boy.

verses.english: When the boy came to the place where the arrows shot by Jonathan had fallen, Jonathan called out to the boy, “Hey, the arrows are beyond you!”
verses.commentary: Jonathan gives David the emergency signal that they agreed on before in private, but in public.

verses.english: And Jonathan called after the boy, “Quick, hurry up. Don’t stop!” So Jonathan’s boy gathered the arrows and came back to his master.—
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

The boy brings the arrows back.

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּקְרָא יְהוֹנָתָן אַחֲרֵי הַנַּעַר מְהֵרָה חוּשָׁה אַל־תַּעֲמֹד וַיְלַקֵּט נַעַר יְהוֹנָתָן אֶת־[הַחִצִּים] (החצי) וַיָּבֹא אֶל־אֲדֹנָיו׃}

verses.original: וְהַנַּעַר לֹא־יָדַע מְאוּמָה אַךְ יְהוֹנָתָן וְדָוִד יָדְעוּ אֶת־הַדָּבָר׃
verses.english: The boy suspected nothing; only Jonathan and David knew the arrangement.—
verses.commentary: Their secret public plan is going exactly as planned.

tex.original: \hX{וְהַנַּעַר לֹא־יָדַע מְאוּמָה אַךְ יְהוֹנָתָן וְדָוִד יָדְעוּ אֶת־הַדָּבָר׃}

verses.original: וַיִּתֵּן יְהוֹנָתָן אֶת־כֵּלָיו אֶל־הַנַּעַר אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ לֵךְ הָבֵיא הָעִיר׃

verses.original: הַנַּעַר בָּא וְדָוִד קָם מֵאֵצֶל הַנֶּגֶב וַיִּפֹּל לְאַפָּיו אַרְצָה וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים וַיִּשְּׁקוּ אִישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵהוּ וַיִּבְכּוּ אִישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵהוּ עַד־דָּוִד הִגְדִּיל׃
verses.english: When the boy got there, David emerged from his concealment at the Negeb. He flung himself face down on the ground and bowed low three times. They kissed each other and wept together; David wept the longer.
verses.commentary:
David comes out from behind the special rock, bows low, and they kiss and cry together.

David cried longer.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוֹנָתָן לְדָוִד לֵךְ לְשָׁלוֹם אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּעְנוּ שְׁנֵינוּ אֲנַחְנוּ בְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה לֵאמֹר יְהֹוָה יִהְיֶה בֵּינִי וּבֵינֶךָ וּבֵין זַרְעִי וּבֵין זַרְעֲךָ עַד־עוֹלָם׃
verses.english: Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace! For we two have sworn to each other in the name of YHWH: ‘May YHWH be [witness] between you and me, and between your offspring and mine, forever!’”
verses.commentary:
Jonathan says “Go. Remember our promise.”

End of chapter.

verses.english: David went to the priest Ahimelech at Nob. Ahimelech came out in alarm to meet David, and he said to him, “Why are you alone, and no one with you?”
verses.commentary: David goes to meet the priest named “Brother of the King,” and he says “Why's wrong? Why are you alone?”

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד לַאֲחִימֶלֶךְ הַכֹּהֵן הַמֶּלֶךְ צִוַּנִי דָבָר וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלַי אִישׁ אַל־יֵדַע מְאוּמָה אֶת־הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר־אָנֹכִי שֹׁלֵחֲךָ וַאֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִךָ וְאֶת־הַנְּעָרִים יוֹדַעְתִּי אֶל־מְקוֹם פְּלֹנִי אַלְמוֹנִי׃
verses.english: David answered the priest Ahimelech, “The king has ordered me on a mission, and he said to me, ‘No one must know anything about the mission on which I am sending you and for which I have given you orders.’ So I have directed [my] young men to such and such a place.
verses.commentary: David says “I'm on a secret mission from the melech. No one must know. I've sent my men... somewhere.”

verses.original: וְעַתָּה מַה־יֵּשׁ תַּחַת־יָדְךָ חֲמִשָּׁה־לֶחֶם תְּנָה בְיָדִי אוֹ הַנִּמְצָא׃
verses.english: Now then, what have you got on hand? Any loaves of bread? Let me have them—or whatever is available.”
verses.commentary: Now them, what food have you got? I'll have all of it.

tex.original: \hX{וְעַתָּה מַה־יֵּשׁ תַּחַת־יָדְךָ חֲמִשָּׁה־לֶחֶם תְּנָה בְיָדִי אוֹ הַנִּמְצָא׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעַן הַכֹּהֵן אֶת־דָּוִד וַיֹּאמֶר אֵין־לֶחֶם חֹל אֶל־תַּחַת יָדִי כִּי־אִם־לֶחֶם קֹדֶשׁ יֵשׁ אִם־נִשְׁמְרוּ הַנְּעָרִים אַךְ מֵאִשָּׁה׃
verses.english: The priest answered David, “I have no ordinary bread on hand; there is only consecrated bread—provided the young men have kept away from women.”
verses.commentary: So the priest says “I only have religious bread. Have your men kept away from women?”

tex.original: \hX{וַיַּעַן הַכֹּהֵן אֶת־דָּוִד וַיֹּאמֶר אֵין־לֶחֶם חֹל אֶל־תַּחַת יָדִי כִּי־אִם־לֶחֶם קֹדֶשׁ יֵשׁ אִם־נִשְׁמְרוּ הַנְּעָרִים אַךְ מֵאִשָּׁה׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעַן דָּוִד אֶת־הַכֹּהֵן וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ כִּי אִם־אִשָּׁה עֲצֻרָה־לָנוּ כִּתְמוֹל שִׁלְשֹׁם בְּצֵאתִי וַיִּהְיוּ כְלֵי־הַנְּעָרִים קֹדֶשׁ וְהוּא דֶּרֶךְ חֹל וְאַף כִּי הַיּוֹם יִקְדַּשׁ בַּכֶּלִי׃
verses.english: In reply to the priest, David said, “I assure you that women have been kept from us, as always. Whenever I went on a mission, even if the journey was a common one, the vessels of the young men were consecrated; all the more then may consecrated food be put into their vessels today.”
verses.commentary:
David's like “I promise they haven't been with women, as always.”

“Their vessels are holy so put your vessels in their holes.”

verses.original: וַיִּתֶּן־לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן קֹדֶשׁ כִּי לֹא־הָיָה שָׁם לֶחֶם כִּי־אִם־לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים הַמּוּסָרִים מִלִּפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לָשׂוּם לֶחֶם חֹם בְּיוֹם הִלָּקְחוֹ׃
verses.english: So the priest gave him consecrated bread, because there was none there except the bread of display, which had been removed from the presence of YHWH, to be replaced by warm bread as soon as it was taken away.—
verses.commentary: So they eat the religious bread.

tex.original: \hX{וַיִּתֶּן־לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן קֹדֶשׁ כִּי לֹא־הָיָה שָׁם לֶחֶם כִּי־אִם־לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים הַמּוּסָרִים מִלִּפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לָשׂוּם לֶחֶם חֹם בְּיוֹם הִלָּקְחוֹ׃}

verses.original: וְשָׁם אִישׁ מֵעַבְדֵי שָׁאוּל בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא נֶעְצָר לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וּשְׁמוֹ דֹּאֵג הָאֲדֹמִי אַבִּיר הָרֹעִים אֲשֶׁר לְשָׁאוּל׃
verses.english: Now one of Saul’s officials was there that day, detained before YHWH; his name was Doeg the Edomite, Saul’s chief herdsman.
verses.commentary: Doeg was there. He's Saul's head cowboy.

tex.original: \hX{וְשָׁם אִישׁ מֵעַבְדֵי שָׁאוּל בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא נֶעְצָר לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וּשְׁמוֹ דֹּאֵג הָאֲדֹמִי אַבִּיר הָרֹעִים אֲשֶׁר לְשָׁאוּל׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד לַאֲחִימֶלֶךְ וְאִין יֶשׁ־פֹּה תַחַת־יָדְךָ חֲנִית אוֹ־חָרֶב כִּי גַם־חַרְבִּי וְגַם־כֵּלַי לֹא־לָקַחְתִּי בְיָדִי כִּי־הָיָה דְבַר־הַמֶּלֶךְ נָחוּץ׃
verses.english: David said to Ahimelech, “Haven’t you got a spear or sword on hand? I didn’t take my sword or any of my weapons with me, because the king’s mission was urgent.”
