		The Philistine officers asked, “Who are those Hebrews?” “Why,
		that’s David, the servant of King Saul of Israel,” Achish answered
		the Philistine officers. “He has been with me for a year or more,
		and I have found no fault in him from the day he defected until
		now.”
	}

verses.original: וַיִּקְצְפוּ עָלָיו שָׂרֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים וַיֹּאמְרוּ לוֹ שָׂרֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים הָשֵׁב אֶת־הָאִישׁ וְיָשֹׁב אֶל־מְקוֹמוֹ אֲשֶׁר הִפְקַדְתּוֹ שָׁם וְלֹא־יֵרֵד עִמָּנוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָה וְלֹא־יִהְיֶה־לָּנוּ לְשָׂטָן בַּמִּלְחָמָה וּבַמֶּה יִתְרַצֶּה זֶה אֶל־אֲדֹנָיו הֲלוֹא בְּרָאשֵׁי הָאֲנָשִׁים הָהֵם׃
verses.english: But the Philistine officers were angry with him; and the Philistine officers said to him, “Send the man back; let him go back to the place you assigned him. He shall not march down with us to the battle, or else he may become our adversary in battle. For with what could that fellow appease his master if not with the heads of these men?
verses.commentary: The officers are still suspicious.

tex.english:
\eJ{
		But the Philistine officers were angry with him; and the
		Philistine officers said to him, “Send the man back; let him go
		back to the place you assigned him. He shall not march down with
		us to the battle, or else he may become our adversary in battle.
		For with what could that fellow appease his master if not with the
		heads of these men?
	}

verses.original: הֲלוֹא־זֶה דָוִד אֲשֶׁר יַעֲנוּ־לוֹ בַּמְּחֹלוֹת לֵאמֹר הִכָּה שָׁאוּל בַּאֲלָפָיו וְדָוִד בְּרִבְבֹתָו׃
verses.english: Remember, he is the David of whom they sang as they danced: Saul has slain his thousands; David, his tens of thousands.”
verses.commentary: “My king, this is the guy from the murder song. The more murder-y one!”

tex.original: \hJ{הֲלוֹא־זֶה דָוִד אֲשֶׁר יַעֲנוּ־לוֹ בַּמְּחֹלוֹת לֵאמֹר הִכָּה שָׁאוּל בַּאֲלָפָיו וְדָוִד בְּרִבְבֹתָו׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקְרָא אָכִישׁ אֶל־דָּוִד וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו חַי־יְהֹוָה כִּי־יָשָׁר אַתָּה וְטוֹב בְּעֵינַי צֵאתְךָ וּבֹאֲךָ אִתִּי בַּמַּחֲנֶה כִּי לֹא־מָצָאתִי בְךָ רָעָה מִיּוֹם בֹּאֲךָ אֵלַי עַד־הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה וּבְעֵינֵי הַסְּרָנִים לֹא־טוֹב אָתָּה׃
verses.english: Achish summoned David and said to him, “As YHWH lives, you are an honest man, and I would like to have you serve in my forces; for I have found no fault with you from the day you joined me until now. But you are not acceptable to the other lords.
verses.commentary: So the king is like “Look David. You've done nothing wrong. I like you. But the men aren't having it.”

verses.original: וְעַתָּה שׁוּב וְלֵךְ בְּשָׁלוֹם וְלֹא־תַעֲשֶׂה רָע בְּעֵינֵי סַרְנֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים׃
verses.english: So go back in peace, and do nothing to displease the Philistine lords.”
verses.commentary: “Go home.”

tex.original: \hJ{וְעַתָּה שׁוּב וְלֵךְ בְּשָׁלוֹם וְלֹא־תַעֲשֶׂה רָע בְּעֵינֵי סַרְנֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד אֶל־אָכִישׁ כִּי מֶה עָשִׂיתִי וּמַה־מָּצָאתָ בְעַבְדְּךָ מִיּוֹם אֲשֶׁר הָיִיתִי לְפָנֶיךָ עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה כִּי לֹא אָבוֹא וְנִלְחַמְתִּי בְּאֹיְבֵי אֲדֹנִי הַמֶּלֶךְ׃
verses.english: David, however, said to Achish, “But what have I done, what fault have you found in your servant from the day I appeared before you to this day, that I should not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”
verses.commentary: David's like “What have I done?”

verses.original: וַיַּעַן אָכִישׁ וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל־דָּוִד יָדַעְתִּי כִּי טוֹב אַתָּה בְּעֵינַי כְּמַלְאַךְ אֱלֹהִים אַךְ שָׂרֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים אָמְרוּ לֹא־יַעֲלֶה עִמָּנוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָה׃
verses.english: Achish replied to David, “I know; you are as acceptable to me as an angel of God. But the Philistine officers have decided that you must not march out with us to the battle.
verses.commentary: The king's like “I sort of went over this three sentences ago in 29:6 but you're my friend so I'll say it again.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּעַן אָכִישׁ וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל־דָּוִד יָדַעְתִּי כִּי טוֹב אַתָּה בְּעֵינַי כְּמַלְאַךְ אֱלֹהִים אַךְ שָׂרֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים אָמְרוּ לֹא־יַעֲלֶה עִמָּנוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָה׃}

verses.original: וְעַתָּה הַשְׁכֵּם בַּבֹּקֶר וְעַבְדֵי אֲדֹנֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר־בָּאוּ אִתָּךְ וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּם בַּבֹּקֶר וְאוֹר לָכֶם וָלֵכוּ׃
verses.english: So rise early in the morning, you and your lord’s servants who came with you—rise early in the morning, and leave as soon as it is light.”
verses.commentary: “Anyways get up early tomorrow—get up early tomorrow and leave.”

tex.original: \hJ{וְעַתָּה הַשְׁכֵּם בַּבֹּקֶר וְעַבְדֵי אֲדֹנֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר־בָּאוּ אִתָּךְ וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּם בַּבֹּקֶר וְאוֹר לָכֶם וָלֵכוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיַּשְׁכֵּם דָּוִד הוּא וַאֲנָשָׁיו לָלֶכֶת בַּבֹּקֶר לָשׁוּב אֶל־אֶרֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּים וּפְלִשְׁתִּים עָלוּ יִזְרְעֶאל׃
verses.english: Accordingly, David and his men rose early in the morning to leave, to return to the land of the Philistines, while the Philistines marched up to Jezreel.
verses.commentary:
So they leave.

Meanwhile the Philistines march up to God Spreads His Seed.

Note: David is now no longer at the battle.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּשְׁכֵּם דָּוִד הוּא וַאֲנָשָׁיו לָלֶכֶת בַּבֹּקֶר לָשׁוּב אֶל־אֶרֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּים וּפְלִשְׁתִּים עָלוּ יִזְרְעֶאל׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי בְּבֹא דָוִד וַאֲנָשָׁיו צִקְלַג בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי וַעֲמָלֵקִי פָשְׁטוּ אֶל־נֶגֶב וְאֶל־צִקְלַג וַיַּכּוּ אֶת־צִקְלַג וַיִּשְׂרְפוּ אֹתָהּ בָּאֵשׁ׃
verses.english: By the time David and his men arrived in Ziklag, on the third day, the Amalekites had made a raid into the Negeb and against Ziklag; they had stormed Ziklag and burned it down.
verses.commentary:
David goes back home to the town that the king gave him back in 27:6.

Then three days later, someone's trying to burn it down.

No scratch that.

The noun (the Amalekites, עמלקי) comes before the verb (invaded, פשׁטו) here.

So the town had already been burned down by the time they got there.

So “on the third day” doesn't mean their third day in Ziklag.

The journey took three days.

Arrive in town.

It's already burning.

Note: David is now

• No longer at the battle.
• Busy putting out fires.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְהִי בְּבֹא דָוִד וַאֲנָשָׁיו צִקְלַג בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי וַעֲמָלֵקִי פָשְׁטוּ אֶל־נֶגֶב וְאֶל־צִקְלַג וַיַּכּוּ אֶת־צִקְלַג וַיִּשְׂרְפוּ אֹתָהּ בָּאֵשׁ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁבּוּ אֶת־הַנָּשִׁים אֲשֶׁר־בָּהּ מִקָּטֹן וְעַד־גָּדוֹל לֹא הֵמִיתוּ אִישׁ וַיִּנְהֲגוּ וַיֵּלְכוּ לְדַרְכָּם׃
verses.english: They had taken the women in it captive, low-born and high-born alike; they did not kill any, but carried them off and went their way.
verses.commentary: The Amalekites hadn't killed the women. Women are useful.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשְׁבּוּ אֶת־הַנָּשִׁים אֲשֶׁר־בָּהּ מִקָּטֹן וְעַד־גָּדוֹל לֹא הֵמִיתוּ אִישׁ וַיִּנְהֲגוּ וַיֵּלְכוּ לְדַרְכָּם׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא דָוִד וַאֲנָשָׁיו אֶל־הָעִיר וְהִנֵּה שְׂרוּפָה בָּאֵשׁ וּנְשֵׁיהֶם וּבְנֵיהֶם וּבְנֹתֵיהֶם נִשְׁבּוּ׃
verses.english: When David and his men came to the town and found it burned down, and their wives and sons and daughters taken captive,
verses.commentary:
They wouldn't necessarily know that they'd been kidnapped and not killed when they arrived in the town and saw it burning.

But give them a break, their wives and sons and daughters just got kidnapped.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּבֹא דָוִד וַאֲנָשָׁיו אֶל־הָעִיר וְהִנֵּה שְׂרוּפָה בָּאֵשׁ וּנְשֵׁיהֶם וּבְנֵיהֶם וּבְנֹתֵיהֶם נִשְׁבּוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשָּׂא דָוִד וְהָעָם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּוֹ אֶת־קוֹלָם וַיִּבְכּוּ עַד אֲשֶׁר אֵין־בָּהֶם כֹּחַ לִבְכּוֹת׃
verses.english: David and the troops with him broke into tears, until they had no strength left for weeping.
verses.commentary: They cry until they're too tired to cry.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשָּׂא דָוִד וְהָעָם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּוֹ אֶת־קוֹלָם וַיִּבְכּוּ עַד אֲשֶׁר אֵין־בָּהֶם כֹּחַ לִבְכּוֹת׃}

verses.original: וּשְׁתֵּי נְשֵׁי־דָוִד נִשְׁבּוּ אֲחִינֹעַם הַיִּזְרְעֵלִית וַאֲבִיגַיִל אֵשֶׁת נָבָל הַכַּרְמְלִי׃
verses.english: David’s two wives had been taken captive, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail wife of Nabal from Carmel.
verses.commentary: Remind the reader David's two wives have been kidnapped.

tex.original: \hJ{וּשְׁתֵּי נְשֵׁי־דָוִד נִשְׁבּוּ אֲחִינֹעַם הַיִּזְרְעֵלִית וַאֲבִיגַיִל אֵשֶׁת נָבָל הַכַּרְמְלִי׃}

verses.original: וַתֵּצֶר לְדָוִד מְאֹד כִּי־אָמְרוּ הָעָם לְסקְלוֹ כִּי־מָרָה נֶפֶשׁ כּל־הָעָם אִישׁ עַל־בָּנָו וְעַל־בְּנֹתָיו וַיִּתְחַזֵּק דָּוִד בַּיהֹוָה אֱלֹהָיו׃
verses.english: David was in great danger, for the troops threatened to stone him; for all the troops were embittered on account of their sons and daughters. But David sought strength in YHWH his God.
verses.commentary:
Now both sides hate David.

David finds strength in YHWH.

YHWH isn't yelling at him.

tex.original: \hJ{וַתֵּצֶר לְדָוִד מְאֹד כִּי־אָמְרוּ הָעָם לְסקְלוֹ כִּי־מָרָה נֶפֶשׁ כּל־הָעָם אִישׁ עַל־בָּנָו וְעַל־בְּנֹתָיו וַיִּתְחַזֵּק דָּוִד בַּיהֹוָה אֱלֹהָיו׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד אֶל־אֶבְיָתָר הַכֹּהֵן בֶּן־אֲחִימֶלֶךְ הַגִּישָׁה־נָּא לִי הָאֵפוֹד וַיַּגֵּשׁ אֶבְיָתָר אֶת־הָאֵפוֹד אֶל־דָּוִד׃
verses.english: David said to the priest Abiathar son of Ahimelech, “Bring the ephod up to me.” When Abiathar brought up the ephod to David,
verses.commentary: So David says to Abiathar (the Mushite priest who escaped the Doeg massacre) “Bring me that priest shirt.”

tex.original: \hX{וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד אֶל־אֶבְיָתָר הַכֹּהֵן בֶּן־אֲחִימֶלֶךְ הַגִּישָׁה־נָּא לִי הָאֵפוֹד וַיַּגֵּשׁ אֶבְיָתָר אֶת־הָאֵפוֹד אֶל־דָּוִד׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁאַל דָּוִד בַּיהֹוָה לֵאמֹר אֶרְדֹּף אַחֲרֵי הַגְּדוּד־הַזֶּה הַאַשִּׂגֶנּוּ וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ רְדֹף כִּי־הַשֵּׂג תַּשִּׂיג וְהַצֵּל תַּצִּיל׃
verses.english: David inquired of YHWH, “Shall I pursue those raiders? Will I overtake them?” And He answered him, “Pursue, for you shall overtake and you shall rescue.”
verses.commentary:
So David (possibly wearing ephod) asks YHWH if he should go attack the attackers.

YHWH says “Yes, you'll win.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשְׁאַל דָּוִד בַּיהֹוָה לֵאמֹר אֶרְדֹּף אַחֲרֵי הַגְּדוּד־הַזֶּה הַאַשִּׂגֶנּוּ וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ רְדֹף כִּי־הַשֵּׂג תַּשִּׂיג וְהַצֵּל תַּצִּיל׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּלֶךְ דָּוִד הוּא וְשֵׁשׁ־מֵאוֹת אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ וַיָּבֹאוּ עַד־נַחַל הַבְּשׂוֹר וְהַנּוֹתָרִים עָמָדוּ׃
verses.english: So David and the six hundred men with him set out, and they came to the Wadi Besor, where a halt was made by those who were to be left behind.
verses.commentary: So David and his 600 guys set out until they stop at Cheerful Valley.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֵּלֶךְ דָּוִד הוּא וְשֵׁשׁ־מֵאוֹת אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ וַיָּבֹאוּ עַד־נַחַל הַבְּשׂוֹר וְהַנּוֹתָרִים עָמָדוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּרְדֹּף דָּוִד הוּא וְאַרְבַּע־מֵאוֹת אִישׁ וַיַּעַמְדוּ מָאתַיִם אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר פִּגְּרוּ מֵעֲבֹר אֶת־נַחַל הַבְּשׂוֹר׃
verses.english: David continued the pursuit with four hundred men; two hundred men had halted, too faint to cross the Wadi Besor.
verses.commentary: Two hundred of the six hundred guys decide to stay here.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּרְדֹּף דָּוִד הוּא וְאַרְבַּע־מֵאוֹת אִישׁ וַיַּעַמְדוּ מָאתַיִם אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר פִּגְּרוּ מֵעֲבֹר אֶת־נַחַל הַבְּשׂוֹר׃}

verses.original: וַיִּמְצְאוּ אִישׁ־מִצְרִי בַּשָּׂדֶה וַיִּקְחוּ אֹתוֹ אֶל־דָּוִד וַיִּתְּנוּ־לוֹ לֶחֶם וַיֹּאכַל וַיַּשְׁקֻהוּ מָיִם׃
verses.english: They came upon an Egyptian in the open country and brought him to David. They gave him food to eat and water to drink;
verses.commentary:
They find an Egyptian.

They give him food and water.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּמְצְאוּ אִישׁ־מִצְרִי בַּשָּׂדֶה וַיִּקְחוּ אֹתוֹ אֶל־דָּוִד וַיִּתְּנוּ־לוֹ לֶחֶם וַיֹּאכַל וַיַּשְׁקֻהוּ מָיִם׃}

verses.original: וַיִּתְּנוּ־לוֹ פֶלַח דְּבֵלָה וּשְׁנֵי צִמֻּקִים וַיֹּאכַל וַתָּשׁב רוּחוֹ אֵלָיו כִּי לֹא־אָכַל לֶחֶם וְלֹא־שָׁתָה מַיִם שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה לֵילוֹת׃
verses.english: he was also given a piece of pressed fig cake and two cakes of raisins. He ate and regained his strength, for he had eaten no food and drunk no water for three days and three nights.
verses.commentary:
And snacks.

The Egyptian feels better now, he hadn't eaten for three days.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּתְּנוּ־לוֹ פֶלַח דְּבֵלָה וּשְׁנֵי צִמֻּקִים וַיֹּאכַל וַתָּשׁב רוּחוֹ אֵלָיו כִּי לֹא־אָכַל לֶחֶם וְלֹא־שָׁתָה מַיִם שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה לֵילוֹת׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ דָוִד לְמִי־אַתָּה וְאֵי מִזֶּה אָתָּה וַיֹּאמֶר נַעַר מִצְרִי אָנֹכִי עֶבֶד לְאִישׁ עֲמָלֵקִי וַיַּעַזְבֵנִי אֲדֹנִי כִּי חָלִיתִי הַיּוֹם שְׁלֹשָׁה׃
verses.english: Then David asked him, “To whom do you belong and where are you from?” “I am an Egyptian boy,” he answered, “the slave of an Amalekite. My master abandoned me when I fell ill three days ago.
verses.commentary:
David: “Who owns you? Where are you from?

Egyptian: “I'm Egyptian. I though we'd established that.”

David: “What about the other question?”

Egyptian: “I belong to an Amalekite. I got sick and he threw me away.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ דָוִד לְמִי־אַתָּה וְאֵי מִזֶּה אָתָּה וַיֹּאמֶר נַעַר מִצְרִי אָנֹכִי עֶבֶד לְאִישׁ עֲמָלֵקִי וַיַּעַזְבֵנִי אֲדֹנִי כִּי חָלִיתִי הַיּוֹם שְׁלֹשָׁה׃}

verses.original: אֲנַחְנוּ פָּשַׁטְנוּ נֶגֶב הַכְּרֵתִי וְעַל־אֲשֶׁר לִיהוּדָה וְעַל־נֶגֶב כָּלֵב וְאֶת־צִקְלַג שָׂרַפְנוּ בָאֵשׁ׃
verses.english: We had raided the Negeb of the Cherethites, and [the Negeb] of Judah, and the Negeb of Caleb; we also burned down Ziklag.”
verses.commentary: Egyptian: “I was on the side that did the burning.”

tex.original: \hJ{אֲנַחְנוּ פָּשַׁטְנוּ נֶגֶב הַכְּרֵתִי וְעַל־אֲשֶׁר לִיהוּדָה וְעַל־נֶגֶב כָּלֵב וְאֶת־צִקְלַג שָׂרַפְנוּ בָאֵשׁ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו דָּוִד הֲתוֹרִדֵנִי אֶל־הַגְּדוּד הַזֶּה וַיֹּאמֶר הִשָּׁבְעָה לִּי בֵאלֹהִים אִם־תְּמִיתֵנִי וְאִם־תַּסְגִּרֵנִי בְּיַד־אֲדֹנִי וְאוֹרִדְךָ אֶל־הַגְּדוּד הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: And David said to him, “Can you lead me down to that band?” He replied, “Swear to me by God that you will not kill me or deliver me into my master’s hands, and I will lead you down to that band.”
verses.commentary:
David: “Can you lead me to them?”

Egyptian: “Sure, just don't sell me or kill me.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו דָּוִד הֲתוֹרִדֵנִי אֶל־הַגְּדוּד הַזֶּה וַיֹּאמֶר הִשָּׁבְעָה לִּי בֵאלֹהִים אִם־תְּמִיתֵנִי וְאִם־תַּסְגִּרֵנִי בְּיַד־אֲדֹנִי וְאוֹרִדְךָ אֶל־הַגְּדוּד הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּרִדֵהוּ וְהִנֵּה נְטֻשִׁים עַל־פְּנֵי כל־הָאָרֶץ אֹכְלִים וְשֹׁתִים וְחֹגְגִים בְּכֹל הַשָּׁלָל הַגָּדוֹל אֲשֶׁר לָקְחוּ מֵאֶרֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּים וּמֵאֶרֶץ יְהוּדָה׃
verses.english: So he led him down, and there they were, scattered all over the ground, eating and drinking and making merry because of all the vast spoil they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
verses.commentary:
So the Egyptian leads David to the Amalekites.

They're all scattered about drunk and partying.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּרִדֵהוּ וְהִנֵּה נְטֻשִׁים עַל־פְּנֵי כל־הָאָרֶץ אֹכְלִים וְשֹׁתִים וְחֹגְגִים בְּכֹל הַשָּׁלָל הַגָּדוֹל אֲשֶׁר לָקְחוּ מֵאֶרֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּים וּמֵאֶרֶץ יְהוּדָה׃}

verses.original: וַיַּכֵּם דָּוִד מֵהַנֶּשֶׁף וְעַד־הָעֶרֶב לְמחֳרָתָם וְלֹא־נִמְלַט מֵהֶם אִישׁ כִּי אִם־אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת אִישׁ־נַעַר אֲשֶׁר־רָכְבוּ עַל־הַגְּמַלִּים וַיָּנֻסוּ׃
verses.english: David attacked them from before dawn until the evening of the next day; none of them escaped, except four hundred young men who mounted camels and got away.
verses.commentary:
David attacks them from morning today until night time tomorrow.

Not a single one escaped.

Except four hundred.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּכֵּם דָּוִד מֵהַנֶּשֶׁף וְעַד־הָעֶרֶב לְמחֳרָתָם וְלֹא־נִמְלַט מֵהֶם אִישׁ כִּי אִם־אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת אִישׁ־נַעַר אֲשֶׁר־רָכְבוּ עַל־הַגְּמַלִּים וַיָּנֻסוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיַּצֵּל דָּוִד אֵת כּל־אֲשֶׁר לָקְחוּ עֲמָלֵק וְאֶת־שְׁתֵּי נָשָׁיו הִצִּיל דָּוִד׃
verses.english: David rescued everything the Amalekites had taken; David also rescued his two wives.
verses.commentary:
David got back all his stuff, except the stuff they ate during that drunken party up above.

Also he finds his wives.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּצֵּל דָּוִד אֵת כּל־אֲשֶׁר לָקְחוּ עֲמָלֵק וְאֶת־שְׁתֵּי נָשָׁיו הִצִּיל דָּוִד׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא נֶעְדַּר־לָהֶם מִן־הַקָּטֹן וְעַד־הַגָּדוֹל וְעַד־בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת וּמִשָּׁלָל וְעַד כּל־אֲשֶׁר לָקְחוּ לָהֶם הַכֹּל הֵשִׁיב דָּוִד׃
verses.english: Nothing of theirs was missing—young or old, sons or daughters, spoil or anything else that had been carried off—David recovered everything.
verses.commentary: Scratch that. David got everything back. Every single everything.

tex.original: \hJ{וְלֹא נֶעְדַּר־לָהֶם מִן־הַקָּטֹן וְעַד־הַגָּדוֹל וְעַד־בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת וּמִשָּׁלָל וְעַד כּל־אֲשֶׁר לָקְחוּ לָהֶם הַכֹּל הֵשִׁיב דָּוִד׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח דָּוִד אֶת־כּל־הַצֹּאן וְהַבָּקָר נָהֲגוּ לִפְנֵי הַמִּקְנֶה הַהוּא וַיֹּאמְרוּ זֶה שְׁלַל דָּוִד׃
verses.english: David took all the flocks and herds, which [the troops] drove ahead of the other livestock; and they declared, “This is David’s spoil.”
verses.commentary: David's stuff goes ahead of everyone else's stuff, and they say “This is David's stuff.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּקַּח דָּוִד אֶת־כּל־הַצֹּאן וְהַבָּקָר נָהֲגוּ לִפְנֵי הַמִּקְנֶה הַהוּא וַיֹּאמְרוּ זֶה שְׁלַל דָּוִד׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא דָוִד אֶל־מָאתַיִם הָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר־פִּגְּרוּ מִלֶּכֶת אַחֲרֵי דָוִד וַיֹּשִׁיבֻם בְּנַחַל הַבְּשׂוֹר וַיֵּצְאוּ לִקְרַאת דָּוִד וְלִקְרַאת הָעָם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּוֹ וַיִּגַּשׁ דָּוִד אֶת־הָעָם וַיִּשְׁאַל לָהֶם לְשָׁלוֹם׃
verses.english: When David reached the two hundred men who were too faint to follow David and who had been left at the Wadi Besor, they came out to welcome David and the troops with him; David came forward with the troops and greeted them.
verses.commentary:
So David comes back to the 200 tired guys who stayed behind at the Valley of Cheerfulness.

David says hi.

verses.original: וַיַּעַן כּל־אִישׁ־רָע וּבְלִיַּעַל מֵהָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר הָלְכוּ עִם־דָּוִד וַיֹּאמְרוּ יַעַן אֲשֶׁר לֹא־הָלְכוּ עִמִּי לֹא־נִתֵּן לָהֶם מֵהַשָּׁלָל אֲשֶׁר הִצַּלְנוּ כִּי־אִם־אִישׁ אֶת־אִשְׁתּוֹ וְאֶת־בָּנָיו וְיִנְהֲגוּ וְיֵלֵכוּ׃
verses.english: But all the mean and churlish fellows among the men who had accompanied David spoke up, “Since they did not accompany us, we will not give them any of the spoil that we seized—except that each may take his wife and children and go.”
verses.commentary:
The 400 who fought the fight say:

“The 200 who didn't come don't get to have any stuff.

They can take their families and leave.“

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד לֹא־תַעֲשׂוּ כֵן אֶחָי אֵת אֲשֶׁר־נָתַן יְהֹוָה לָנוּ וַיִּשְׁמֹר אֹתָנוּ וַיִּתֵּן אֶת־הַגְּדוּד הַבָּא עָלֵינוּ בְּיָדֵנוּ׃
verses.english: David, however, spoke up, “You must not do that, my brothers, in view of what YHWH has granted us, guarding us and delivering into our hands the band that attacked us.
verses.commentary: David, however, wants the 200 guys back in his army.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד לֹא־תַעֲשׂוּ כֵן אֶחָי אֵת אֲשֶׁר־נָתַן יְהֹוָה לָנוּ וַיִּשְׁמֹר אֹתָנוּ וַיִּתֵּן אֶת־הַגְּדוּד הַבָּא עָלֵינוּ בְּיָדֵנוּ׃}

verses.original: וּמִי יִשְׁמַע לָכֶם לַדָּבָר הַזֶּה כִּי כְּחֵלֶק הַיֹּרֵד בַּמִּלְחָמָה וּכְחֵלֶק הַיֹּשֵׁב עַל־הַכֵּלִים יַחְדָּו יַחֲלֹקוּ׃
verses.english: How could anyone agree with you in this matter? The share of those who remain with the baggage shall be the same as the share of those who go down to battle; they shall share alike.”
verses.commentary:
So he says “Who could possibly agree with you that the guys who fight don't get stuff?”

“You get the same amount for staying with the bags as for fighting.”

tex.original: \hJ{וּמִי יִשְׁמַע לָכֶם לַדָּבָר הַזֶּה כִּי כְּחֵלֶק הַיֹּרֵד בַּמִּלְחָמָה וּכְחֵלֶק הַיֹּשֵׁב עַל־הַכֵּלִים יַחְדָּו יַחֲלֹקוּ׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי מֵהַיּוֹם הַהוּא וָמָעְלָה וַיְשִׂמֶהָ לְחֹק וּלְמִשְׁפָּט לְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: So from that day on it was made a fixed rule for Israel, continuing to the present day.
verses.commentary: So that's the rule now. Still.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְהִי מֵהַיּוֹם הַהוּא וָמָעְלָה וַיְשִׂמֶהָ לְחֹק וּלְמִשְׁפָּט לְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא דָוִד אֶל־צִקְלַג וַיְשַׁלַּח מֵהַשָּׁלָל לְזִקְנֵי יְהוּדָה לְרֵעֵהוּ לֵאמֹר הִנֵּה לָכֶם בְּרָכָה מִשְּׁלַל אֹיְבֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: When David reached Ziklag, he sent some of the spoil to the elders of Judah [and] to his friends, saying, “This is a present for you from our spoil of the enemies of YHWH.”
verses.commentary:
David gets back home to Ziklag, the free town he got as a present from the enemy king.

He mails some of the stuff to Judah, to the old people and to his friends.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּבֹא דָוִד אֶל־צִקְלַג וַיְשַׁלַּח מֵהַשָּׁלָל לְזִקְנֵי יְהוּדָה לְרֵעֵהוּ לֵאמֹר הִנֵּה לָכֶם בְּרָכָה מִשְּׁלַל אֹיְבֵי יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: לַאֲשֶׁר בְּבֵית־אֵלוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּרָמוֹת־נֶגֶבוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּיַתִּר׃
verses.english: [He sent the spoil to the elders] in Bethel, Ramoth-negeb, and Jattir;
verses.commentary: He sends the stuff to the old people in House of God, in the High and Dry Places, and in Excellent.

tex.original: \hJ{לַאֲשֶׁר בְּבֵית־אֵלוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּרָמוֹת־נֶגֶבוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּיַתִּר׃}

verses.original: וְלַאֲשֶׁר בַּעֲרֹעֵרוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּשִׂפְמוֹתוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּאֶשְׁתְּמֹעַ׃
verses.english: in Aroer, Siphmoth, and Eshtemoa;
verses.commentary: in the Ruins, the Fruitful Places, and in Obedience;

tex.original: \hJ{וְלַאֲשֶׁר בַּעֲרֹעֵרוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּשִׂפְמוֹתוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּאֶשְׁתְּמֹעַ׃}
tex.english: \eJ{in Aroer, Siphmoth, and Eshtemoa;}

verses.original: וְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּרָכָלוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּעָרֵי הַיְּרַחְמְאֵלִיוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּעָרֵי הַקֵּינִי׃
verses.english: in Racal, in the towns of the Jerahmeelites, and in the towns of the Kenites;
verses.commentary: in Trade, in the towns of God Have Mercy and in Smithtown.

tex.original: \hJ{וְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּרָכָלוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּעָרֵי הַיְּרַחְמְאֵלִיוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּעָרֵי הַקֵּינִי׃}

verses.original: וְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּחרְמָהוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּבוֹר־עָשָׁןוְלַאֲשֶׁר בַּעֲתָךְ׃
verses.english: in Hormah, Bor-ashan, and Athach;
verses.commentary: in Destruction, in Smoking Pit, and in Hotel;

tex.original: \hJ{וְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּחרְמָהוְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּבוֹר־עָשָׁןוְלַאֲשֶׁר בַּעֲתָךְ׃}
tex.english: \eJ{in Hormah, Bor-ashan, and Athach;}

verses.original: וְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּחֶבְרוֹן וּלְכל־הַמְּקֹמוֹת אֲשֶׁר־הִתְהַלֶּךְ־שָׁם דָּוִד הוּא וַאֲנָשָׁיו׃
verses.english: and to those in Hebron—all the places where David and his men had roamed.
verses.commentary: and to those in Friendship—all the places where David and his men had roamed.

tex.original: \hJ{וְלַאֲשֶׁר בְּחֶבְרוֹן וּלְכל־הַמְּקֹמוֹת אֲשֶׁר־הִתְהַלֶּךְ־שָׁם דָּוִד הוּא וַאֲנָשָׁיו׃}

verses.original: וּפְלִשְׁתִּים נִלְחָמִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וַיָּנֻסוּ אַנְשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִפְּנֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים וַיִּפְּלוּ חֲלָלִים בְּהַר הַגִּלְבֹּעַ׃
verses.english: The Philistines attacked Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and [many] fell on Mount Gilboa.
verses.commentary: The Philistines attack, and Israel runs away to the Mountain of Bubbling Fountain. [Or possibly, Swollen Heap.]

tex.original: \hJ{וּפְלִשְׁתִּים נִלְחָמִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וַיָּנֻסוּ אַנְשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִפְּנֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים וַיִּפְּלוּ חֲלָלִים בְּהַר הַגִּלְבֹּעַ׃}

verses.original: וַיַּדְבְּקוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אֶת־שָׁאוּל וְאֶת־בָּנָיו וַיַּכּוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אֶת־יְהוֹנָתָן וְאֶת־אֲבִינָדָב וְאֶת־מַלְכִּישׁוּעַ בְּנֵי שָׁאוּל׃
verses.english: The Philistines pursued Saul and his sons, and the Philistines struck down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, sons of Saul.
verses.commentary:
The Philistines kill Jonathan, the one who really loves David.

They also kill My Father Is Noble and My King Is Wealth, sons of Saul.

tex.original: \hX{וַיַּדְבְּקוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אֶת־שָׁאוּל וְאֶת־בָּנָיו וַיַּכּוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים אֶת־יְהוֹנָתָן וְאֶת־אֲבִינָדָב וְאֶת־מַלְכִּישׁוּעַ בְּנֵי שָׁאוּל׃}

verses.original: וַתִּכְבַּד הַמִּלְחָמָה אֶל־שָׁאוּל וַיִּמְצָאֻהוּ הַמּוֹרִים אֲנָשִׁים בַּקָּשֶׁת וַיָּחֶל מְאֹד מֵהַמּוֹרִים׃
verses.english: The battle raged around Saul, and some of the archers hit him, and he was severely wounded by the archers.
verses.commentary: Saul gets shot by arrows.

tex.original: \hX{וַתִּכְבַּד הַמִּלְחָמָה אֶל־שָׁאוּל וַיִּמְצָאֻהוּ הַמּוֹרִים אֲנָשִׁים בַּקָּשֶׁת וַיָּחֶל מְאֹד מֵהַמּוֹרִים׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל לְנֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו שְׁלֹף חַרְבְּךָ וְדקְרֵנִי בָהּ פֶּן־יָבוֹאוּ הָעֲרֵלִים הָאֵלֶּה וּדְקָרֻנִי וְהִתְעַלְּלוּ־בִי וְלֹא אָבָה נֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו כִּי יָרֵא מְאֹד וַיִּקַּח שָׁאוּל אֶת־הַחֶרֶב וַיִּפֹּל עָלֶיהָ׃
verses.english: Saul said to his arms-bearer, “Draw your sword and run me through, so that the uncircumcised may not run me through and make sport of me.” But his arms-bearer, in his great awe, refused; whereupon Saul grasped the sword and fell upon it.
verses.commentary:
Saul says to the guy carrying his swords, “Take one of those swords and kill me, so those foreskins don't kill me and have fun with it.”

The guy holding the swords says that's a bit much to ask.

So Saul does it himself, falling on his sword and dying.

verses.original: וַיַּרְא נֹשֵׂא־כֵלָיו כִּי מֵת שָׁאוּל וַיִּפֹּל גַּם־הוּא עַל־חַרְבּוֹ וַיָּמת עִמּוֹ׃
verses.english: When his arms-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his sword and died with him.
verses.commentary: When the guy holding the swords sees that Saul is dead, he does the same thing.

tex.original: \hX{וַיַּרְא נֹשֵׂא־כֵלָיו כִּי מֵת שָׁאוּל וַיִּפֹּל גַּם־הוּא עַל־חַרְבּוֹ וַיָּמת עִמּוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיָּמת שָׁאוּל וּשְׁלֹשֶׁת בָּנָיו וְנֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו גַּם כּל־אֲנָשָׁיו בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יַחְדָּו׃
verses.english: Thus Saul and his three sons and his arms-bearer, as well as all his men, died together on that day.
verses.commentary: So Saul, his three sons, and the sword carryer all died on that day.

tex.original: \hX{וַיָּמת שָׁאוּל וּשְׁלֹשֶׁת בָּנָיו וְנֹשֵׂא כֵלָיו גַּם כּל־אֲנָשָׁיו בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יַחְדָּו׃}

verses.original: וַיִּרְאוּ אַנְשֵׁי־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר־בְּעֵבֶר הָעֵמֶק וַאֲשֶׁר בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן כִּי־נָסוּ אַנְשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכִי־מֵתוּ שָׁאוּל וּבָנָיו וַיַּעַזְבוּ אֶת־הֶעָרִים וַיָּנֻסוּ וַיָּבֹאוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים וַיֵּשְׁבוּ בָּהֶן׃
verses.english: And when the men of Israel on the other side of the valley and on the other side of the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned the towns and fled; the Philistines then came and occupied them.
verses.commentary:
When the men of Israel see all this, they skip town and run.

Then the Philistines came and occupied them.

Them as in the towns. Not the people. The people are gone.

verses.original: וַיְהִי מִמּחֳרָת וַיָּבֹאוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים לְפַשֵּׁט אֶת־הַחֲלָלִים וַיִּמְצְאוּ אֶת־שָׁאוּל וְאֶת־שְׁלֹשֶׁת בָּנָיו נֹפְלִים בְּהַר הַגִּלְבֹּעַ׃

verses.english: Thereupon David called one of the attendants and said to him, “Come over and strike him!” He struck him down and he died.
verses.commentary: So David has the guy killed.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּקְרָא דָוִד לְאַחַד מֵהַנְּעָרִים וַיֹּאמֶר גַּשׁ פְּגַע־בּוֹ וַיַּכֵּהוּ וַיָּמֹת׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו דָּוִד (דמיך) [דָּמְךָ] עַל־רֹאשֶׁךָ כִּי פִיךָ עָנָה בְךָ לֵאמֹר אָנֹכִי מֹתַתִּי אֶת־מְשִׁיחַ יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: And David said to him, “Your blood be on your own head! Your own mouth testified against you when you said, ‘I put YHWH’s anointed to death.’”
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

Then David says to the dead body, “You're guilty. You said it yourself.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו דָּוִד (דמיך) [דָּמְךָ] עַל־רֹאשֶׁךָ כִּי פִיךָ עָנָה בְךָ לֵאמֹר אָנֹכִי מֹתַתִּי אֶת־מְשִׁיחַ יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וַיְקֹנֵן דָּוִד אֶת־הַקִּינָה הַזֹּאת עַל־שָׁאוּל וְעַל־יְהוֹנָתָן בְּנוֹ׃
verses.english: And David intoned this dirge over Saul and his son Jonathan—
verses.commentary: So David writes a song.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְקֹנֵן דָּוִד אֶת־הַקִּינָה הַזֹּאת עַל־שָׁאוּל וְעַל־יְהוֹנָתָן בְּנוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר לְלַמֵּד בְּנֵי־יְהוּדָה קָשֶׁת הִנֵּה כְתוּבָה עַל־סֵפֶר הַיָּשָׁר׃
verses.english: He ordered the Judites to be taught [The Song of the] Bow. It is recorded in the Book of Jashar.
verses.commentary:
And he made the people learn it so they know what happened.

It goes like this.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר לְלַמֵּד בְּנֵי־יְהוּדָה קָשֶׁת הִנֵּה כְתוּבָה עַל־סֵפֶר הַיָּשָׁר׃}

verses.original: הַצְּבִי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל־בָּמוֹתֶיךָ חָלָל אֵיךְ נָפְלוּ גִבּוֹרִים׃
verses.english: Your glory, O Israel, Lies slain on your heights; How have the mighty fallen!
verses.commentary:
Ever heard the phrase “How the mighty have fallen?”

That's from here.

The bible's kind of a big deal.

tex.original: \hJ{הַצְּבִי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל־בָּמוֹתֶיךָ חָלָל אֵיךְ נָפְלוּ גִבּוֹרִים׃}

verses.original: אַל־תַּגִּידוּ בְגַת אַל־תְּבַשְּׂרוּ בְּחוּצֹת אַשְׁקְלוֹן פֶּן־תִּשְׂמַחְנָה בְּנוֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּים פֶּן־תַּעֲלֹזְנָה בְּנוֹת הָעֲרֵלִים׃
verses.english: Tell it not in Gath, Do not proclaim it in the streets of Ashkelon, Lest the daughters of the Philistine rejoice, Lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
verses.commentary: Don't tell the enemy or they'll be happy.

tex.original: \hJ{אַל־תַּגִּידוּ בְגַת אַל־תְּבַשְּׂרוּ בְּחוּצֹת אַשְׁקְלוֹן פֶּן־תִּשְׂמַחְנָה בְּנוֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּים פֶּן־תַּעֲלֹזְנָה בְּנוֹת הָעֲרֵלִים׃}

verses.original: הָרֵי בַגִּלְבֹּעַ אַל־טַל וְאַל־מָטָר עֲלֵיכֶם וּשְׂדֵי תְרוּמֹת כִּי שָׁם נִגְעַל מָגֵן גִּבּוֹרִים מָגֵן שָׁאוּל בְּלִי מָשִׁיחַ בַּשָּׁמֶן׃
verses.english: O hills of Gilboa— Let there be no dew or rain on you, Or bountiful fields, For there the shield of warriors lay rejected, The shield of Saul, Polished with oil no more.
verses.commentary: Saul's shield is no longer oily.

tex.original: \hJ{הָרֵי בַגִּלְבֹּעַ אַל־טַל וְאַל־מָטָר עֲלֵיכֶם וּשְׂדֵי תְרוּמֹת כִּי שָׁם נִגְעַל מָגֵן גִּבּוֹרִים מָגֵן שָׁאוּל בְּלִי מָשִׁיחַ בַּשָּׁמֶן׃}

verses.original: מִדַּם חֲלָלִים מֵחֵלֶב גִּבּוֹרִים קֶשֶׁת יְהוֹנָתָן לֹא נָשׂוֹג אָחוֹר וְחֶרֶב שָׁאוּל לֹא תָשׁוּב רֵיקָם׃
verses.english: From the blood of slain, From the fat of warriors— The bow of Jonathan Never turned back; The sword of Saul Never withdrew empty.
verses.commentary: David says he misses them.

tex.original: \hJ{מִדַּם חֲלָלִים מֵחֵלֶב גִּבּוֹרִים קֶשֶׁת יְהוֹנָתָן לֹא נָשׂוֹג אָחוֹר וְחֶרֶב שָׁאוּל לֹא תָשׁוּב רֵיקָם׃}

verses.original: שָׁאוּל וִיהוֹנָתָן הַנֶּאֱהָבִים וְהַנְּעִימִם בְּחַיֵּיהֶם וּבְמוֹתָם לֹא נִפְרָדוּ מִנְּשָׁרִים קַלּוּ מֵאֲרָיוֹת גָּבֵרוּ׃
verses.english: Saul and Jonathan, Beloved and cherished, Never parted In life or in death! They were swifter than eagles, They were stronger than lions!
verses.commentary: He says it again.

tex.original: \hJ{שָׁאוּל וִיהוֹנָתָן הַנֶּאֱהָבִים וְהַנְּעִימִם בְּחַיֵּיהֶם וּבְמוֹתָם לֹא נִפְרָדוּ מִנְּשָׁרִים קַלּוּ מֵאֲרָיוֹת גָּבֵרוּ׃}

verses.original: בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל־שָׁאוּל בְּכֶינָה הַמַּלְבִּשְׁכֶם שָׁנִי עִם־עֲדָנִים הַמַּעֲלֶה עֲדִי זָהָב עַל לְבוּשְׁכֶן׃
verses.english: Daughters of Israel, Weep over Saul, Who clothed you in crimson and finery, Who decked your robes with jewels of gold.
verses.commentary: He gives the dead credit for the girls clothes and jewelry.

tex.original: \hJ{בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל־שָׁאוּל בְּכֶינָה הַמַּלְבִּשְׁכֶם שָׁנִי עִם־עֲדָנִים הַמַּעֲלֶה עֲדִי זָהָב עַל לְבוּשְׁכֶן׃}

verses.original: אֵיךְ נָפְלוּ גִבֹּרִים בְּתוֹךְ הַמִּלְחָמָה יְהוֹנָתָן עַל־בָּמוֹתֶיךָ חָלָל׃
verses.english: How have the mighty fallen In the thick of battle— Jonathan, slain on your heights!
verses.commentary: Refrain.

tex.original: \hJ{אֵיךְ נָפְלוּ גִבֹּרִים בְּתוֹךְ הַמִּלְחָמָה יְהוֹנָתָן עַל־בָּמוֹתֶיךָ חָלָל׃}

verses.original: צַר־לִי עָלֶיךָ אָחִי יְהוֹנָתָן נָעַמְתָּ לִּי מְאֹד נִפְלְאַתָה אַהֲבָתְךָ לִי מֵאַהֲבַת נָשִׁים׃
verses.english: I grieve for you, My brother Jonathan, You were most dear to me. Your love was wonderful to me More than the love of women.
verses.commentary:
People think this line means they're gay.

There's no other evidence for that except this line.

Moving on.

tex.original: \hJ{צַר־לִי עָלֶיךָ אָחִי יְהוֹנָתָן נָעַמְתָּ לִּי מְאֹד נִפְלְאַתָה אַהֲבָתְךָ לִי מֵאַהֲבַת נָשִׁים׃}

verses.original: אֵיךְ נָפְלוּ גִבּוֹרִים וַיֹּאבְדוּ כְּלֵי מִלְחָמָה׃
verses.english: How have the mighty fallen, The weapons of war perished!
verses.commentary: Refrain and end chapter.

tex.original: \hJ{אֵיךְ נָפְלוּ גִבּוֹרִים וַיֹּאבְדוּ כְּלֵי מִלְחָמָה׃}
tex.english: \eJ{How have the mighty fallen, The weapons of war perished!}

verses.original: וַיְהִי אַחֲרֵי־כֵן וַיִּשְׁאַל דָּוִד בַּיהֹוָה לֵאמֹר הַאֶעֱלֶה בְּאַחַת עָרֵי יְהוּדָה וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֵלָיו עֲלֵה וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד אָנָה אֶעֱלֶה וַיֹּאמֶר חֶבְרֹנָה׃
verses.english: Sometime afterward, David inquired of YHWH, “Shall I go up to one of the towns of Judah?” YHWH answered, “Yes.” David further asked, “Which one shall I go up to?” And YHWH replied, “To Hebron.”
verses.commentary:
David asks YHWH if he should go somewhere.

YHWH says yes.

YHWH always says yes to David.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְהִי אַחֲרֵי־כֵן וַיִּשְׁאַל דָּוִד בַּיהֹוָה לֵאמֹר הַאֶעֱלֶה בְּאַחַת עָרֵי יְהוּדָה וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֵלָיו עֲלֵה וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד אָנָה אֶעֱלֶה וַיֹּאמֶר חֶבְרֹנָה׃}

verses.original: וַיַּעַל שָׁם דָּוִד וְגַם שְׁתֵּי נָשָׁיו אֲחִינֹעַם הַיִּזְרְעֵלִית וַאֲבִיגַיִל אֵשֶׁת נָבָל הַכַּרְמְלִי׃
verses.english: So David went up there, along with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.commentary:
David goes up with his two wives, which, we're reminded, are:

• The former wife of Fool.
• The (possibly) former wife of Saul (or at least someone with the same name).

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּעַל שָׁם דָּוִד וְגַם שְׁתֵּי נָשָׁיו אֲחִינֹעַם הַיִּזְרְעֵלִית וַאֲבִיגַיִל אֵשֶׁת נָבָל הַכַּרְמְלִי׃}

verses.original: וַאֲנָשָׁיו אֲשֶׁר־עִמּוֹ הֶעֱלָה דָוִד אִישׁ וּבֵיתוֹ וַיֵּשְׁבוּ בְּעָרֵי חֶבְרוֹן׃
verses.english: David also took the men who were with him, each with his family, and they settled in the towns about Hebron.
verses.commentary:
David also takes his men.

And their families.

They go live in the Hebron area.

tex.original: \hJ{וַאֲנָשָׁיו אֲשֶׁר־עִמּוֹ הֶעֱלָה דָוִד אִישׁ וּבֵיתוֹ וַיֵּשְׁבוּ בְּעָרֵי חֶבְרוֹן׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ אַנְשֵׁי יְהוּדָה וַיִּמְשְׁחוּ־שָׁם אֶת־דָּוִד לְמֶלֶךְ עַל־בֵּית יְהוּדָה וַיַּגִּדוּ לְדָוִד לֵאמֹר אַנְשֵׁי יָבֵישׁ גִּלְעָד אֲשֶׁר קָבְרוּ אֶת־שָׁאוּל׃
verses.english: The men of Judah came and there they anointed David king over the House of Judah. David was told about the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul.
verses.commentary: The Judah people come and poor oil on David's head to make him king.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּבֹאוּ אַנְשֵׁי יְהוּדָה וַיִּמְשְׁחוּ־שָׁם אֶת־דָּוִד לְמֶלֶךְ עַל־בֵּית יְהוּדָה וַיַּגִּדוּ לְדָוִד לֵאמֹר אַנְשֵׁי יָבֵישׁ גִּלְעָד אֲשֶׁר קָבְרוּ אֶת־שָׁאוּל׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח דָּוִד מַלְאָכִים אֶל־אַנְשֵׁי יָבֵישׁ גִּלְעָד וַיֹּאמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם בְּרֻכִים אַתֶּם לַיהֹוָה אֲשֶׁר עֲשִׂיתֶם הַחֶסֶד הַזֶּה עִם־אֲדֹנֵיכֶם עִם־שָׁאוּל וַתִּקְבְּרוּ אֹתוֹ׃
verses.english: So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead and said to them, “May you be blessed of YHWH because you performed this act of faithfulness to your lord Saul and buried him.
verses.commentary: David says a thank you message to the guys who buried Saul.

verses.original: וְעַתָּה יַעַשׂ־יְהֹוָה עִמָּכֶם חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת וְגַם אָנֹכִי אֶעֱשֶׂה אִתְּכֶם הַטּוֹבָה הַזֹּאת אֲשֶׁר עֲשִׂיתֶם הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: May YHWH in turn show you true faithfulness; and I too will reward you generously because you performed this act.
verses.commentary: David says Yahweh and I owe you one.

tex.original: \hJ{וְעַתָּה יַעַשׂ־יְהֹוָה עִמָּכֶם חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת וְגַם אָנֹכִי אֶעֱשֶׂה אִתְּכֶם הַטּוֹבָה הַזֹּאת אֲשֶׁר עֲשִׂיתֶם הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: וְעַתָּה תֶּחֱזַקְנָה יְדֵיכֶם וִהְיוּ לִבְנֵי־חַיִל כִּי־מֵת אֲדֹנֵיכֶם שָׁאוּל וְגַם־אֹתִי מָשְׁחוּ בֵית־יְהוּדָה לְמֶלֶךְ עֲלֵיהֶם׃
verses.english: Now take courage and be brave men; for your lord Saul is dead and the House of Judah have already anointed me king over them.”
verses.commentary: Now sack up cuz I'm the king.

tex.original: \hJ{וְעַתָּה תֶּחֱזַקְנָה יְדֵיכֶם וִהְיוּ לִבְנֵי־חַיִל כִּי־מֵת אֲדֹנֵיכֶם שָׁאוּל וְגַם־אֹתִי מָשְׁחוּ בֵית־יְהוּדָה לְמֶלֶךְ עֲלֵיהֶם׃}

verses.original: וְאַבְנֵר בֶּן־נֵר שַׂר־צָבָא אֲשֶׁר לְשָׁאוּל לָקַח אֶת־אִישׁ בֹּשֶׁת בֶּן־שָׁאוּל וַיַּעֲבִרֵהוּ מַחֲנָיִם׃
verses.english: But Abner son of Ner, Saul’s army commander, had taken Ish-bosheth son of Saul and brought him across to Mahanaim
verses.commentary:
Ok so Saul has a son.

In 1 Chronicles 8:33 he's called Ish-baal.

Here he's called Ish-bosheth.

Ish-bosheth means “Man of shame.”

Somehow I doubt his mom gave him that name.

Ish-baal means “Man of baal.”

Now baal isn't a specific god, it's just a generic term that means “Lord, master, owner, or husband.”

But “Lord” is a good translation.

So he's “Man of Baal” or “Lordman” of the house of Saul.

So anyways, Saul Godman is taken by Father of Ner, Son of Ner.

Lots of wild names in this verse.

Moving on.

verses.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ הַבַּיִת וְהוּא־שֹׁכֵב עַל־מִטָּתוֹ בַּחֲדַר מִשְׁכָּבוֹ וַיַּכֻּהוּ וַיְמִתֻהוּ וַיָּסִירוּ אֶת־רֹאשׁוֹ וַיִּקְחוּ אֶת־רֹאשׁוֹ וַיֵּלְכוּ דֶּרֶךְ הָעֲרָבָה כּל־הַלָּיְלָה׃
verses.english: and entered the house while he was asleep on his bed in his bedchamber; and they stabbed him to death. They cut off his head and took his head and made their way all night through the Arabah.
verses.commentary: and into his house while he was sleeping on his bed in his bedroom and they stab him to dead and cut his head off and head back through the valley.

verses.original: וַיָּבִאוּ אֶת־רֹאשׁ אִישׁ־בֹּשֶׁת אֶל־דָּוִד חֶבְרוֹן וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֶל־הַמֶּלֶךְ הִנֵּה־רֹאשׁ אִישׁ־בֹּשֶׁת בֶּן־שָׁאוּל אֹיִבְךָ אֲשֶׁר בִּקֵּשׁ אֶת־נַפְשֶׁךָ וַיִּתֵּן יְהֹוָה לַאדֹנִי הַמֶּלֶךְ נְקָמוֹת הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה מִשָּׁאוּל וּמִזַּרְעוֹ׃
verses.english: They brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David in Hebron. “Here,” they said to the king, “is the head of your enemy, Ish-bosheth son of Saul, who sought your life. This day YHWH has avenged my lord the king upon Saul and his offspring.”
verses.commentary:
They bring Ish-bosheth's shameful head to David in Hebron and they're like “Here”

“is the head of your enemy, Man of Shame son of Saul, who wanted you dead. YHWH got revenge today on Saul and his kids.”

verses.original: וַיַּעַן דָּוִד אֶת־רֵכָב וְאֶת־בַּעֲנָה אָחִיו בְּנֵי רִמּוֹן הַבְּאֵרֹתִי וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם חַי־יְהֹוָה אֲשֶׁר־פָּדָה אֶת־נַפְשִׁי מִכּל־צָרָה׃
verses.english: But David answered Rechab and his brother Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, “As YHWH lives, who has rescued me from every trouble:
verses.commentary:
So David looks at War Wagon and Sorrow, sons of Pomegranate the Wellerman and he's like

“Praise the Lord, for saving me from all my problems...”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּעַן דָּוִד אֶת־רֵכָב וְאֶת־בַּעֲנָה אָחִיו בְּנֵי רִמּוֹן הַבְּאֵרֹתִי וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם חַי־יְהֹוָה אֲשֶׁר־פָּדָה אֶת־נַפְשִׁי מִכּל־צָרָה׃}

verses.original: כִּי הַמַּגִּיד לִי לֵאמֹר הִנֵּה־מֵת שָׁאוּל וְהוּא־הָיָה כִמְבַשֵּׂר בְּעֵינָיו וָאֹחֲזָה בוֹ וָאֶהְרְגֵהוּ בְּצִקְלָג אֲשֶׁר לְתִתִּי־לוֹ בְּשֹׂרָה׃
verses.english: The man who told me in Ziklag that Saul was dead thought he was bringing good news. But instead of rewarding him for the news, I seized and killed him.
verses.commentary: “Anyways there was this guy in Ziklag who told me he killed Saul when Saul asked him to. He thought I'd be proud of him or whatever. Instead I killed him.”

tex.original: \hJ{כִּי הַמַּגִּיד לִי לֵאמֹר הִנֵּה־מֵת שָׁאוּל וְהוּא־הָיָה כִמְבַשֵּׂר בְּעֵינָיו וָאֹחֲזָה בוֹ וָאֶהְרְגֵהוּ בְּצִקְלָג אֲשֶׁר לְתִתִּי־לוֹ בְּשֹׂרָה׃}

verses.original: אַף כִּי־אֲנָשִׁים רְשָׁעִים הָרְגוּ אֶת־אִישׁ־צַדִּיק בְּבֵיתוֹ עַל־מִשְׁכָּבוֹ וְעַתָּה הֲלוֹא אֲבַקֵּשׁ אֶת־דָּמוֹ מִיֶּדְכֶם וּבִעַרְתִּי אֶתְכֶם מִן־הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.english: How much more, then, when wicked men have killed a blameless man in bed in his own house! I will certainly avenge his blood on you, and I will rid the earth of you.”
verses.commentary: “You guys killed an innocent man in his bed. What do you think I'm gonna do to you?”

tex.original: \hJ{אַף כִּי־אֲנָשִׁים רְשָׁעִים הָרְגוּ אֶת־אִישׁ־צַדִּיק בְּבֵיתוֹ עַל־מִשְׁכָּבוֹ וְעַתָּה הֲלוֹא אֲבַקֵּשׁ אֶת־דָּמוֹ מִיֶּדְכֶם וּבִעַרְתִּי אֶתְכֶם מִן־הָאָרֶץ׃}

verses.original: וַיְצַו דָּוִד אֶת־הַנְּעָרִים וַיַּהַרְגוּם וַיְקַצְּצוּ אֶת־יְדֵיהֶם וְאֶת־רַגְלֵיהֶם וַיִּתְלוּ עַל־הַבְּרֵכָה בְּחֶבְרוֹן וְאֵת רֹאשׁ אִישׁ־בֹּשֶׁת לָקָחוּ וַיִּקְבְּרוּ בְקֶבֶר־אַבְנֵר בְּחֶבְרוֹן׃
verses.english: David gave orders to the young men, who killed them; they cut off their hands and feet and hung them up by the pool in Hebron. And they took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in the grave of Abner at Hebron.
verses.commentary:
So David has their hands and feet cut off and he hangs their dismembered bodies up by the pool in Hebron.

He buries Ish-bosheth's head in a respectful manner next to Abner, since they were friends, at least for awhile, until that episode about the lady where Abner switched sides and made friends with David.

End of chapter.

verses.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ כּל־שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל־דָּוִד חֶבְרוֹנָה וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֵאמֹר הִנְנוּ עַצְמְךָ וּבְשָׂרְךָ אֲנָחְנוּ׃
verses.english: All the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, “We are your own flesh and blood.
verses.commentary: Everyone comes to David at Hebron and says “Hey brother.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּבֹאוּ כּל־שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל־דָּוִד חֶבְרוֹנָה וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֵאמֹר הִנְנוּ עַצְמְךָ וּבְשָׂרְךָ אֲנָחְנוּ׃}

verses.original: גַּם־אֶתְמוֹל גַּם־שִׁלְשׁוֹם בִּהְיוֹת שָׁאוּל מֶלֶךְ עָלֵינוּ אַתָּה (הייתה מוציא) [הָיִיתָ הַמּוֹצִיא] וְהַמֵּבִי אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה לְךָ אַתָּה תִרְעֶה אֶת־עַמִּי אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאַתָּה תִּהְיֶה לְנָגִיד עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: Long before now, when Saul was king over us, it was you who led Israel in war; and YHWH said to you: You shall shepherd My people Israel; you shall be ruler of Israel.”
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

They remind him about everything they've been through together.

verses.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ כּל־זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל־הַמֶּלֶךְ חֶבְרוֹנָה וַיִּכְרֹת לָהֶם הַמֶּלֶךְ דָּוִד בְּרִית בְּחֶבְרוֹן לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וַיִּמְשְׁחוּ אֶת־דָּוִד לְמֶלֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: All the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a pact with them in Hebron before YHWH. And they anointed David king over Israel.
verses.commentary: The elders make a deal with David and they rub his head slick with the oils of the royals and he's King in the North now as well as the South.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּבֹאוּ כּל־זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל־הַמֶּלֶךְ חֶבְרוֹנָה וַיִּכְרֹת לָהֶם הַמֶּלֶךְ דָּוִד בְּרִית בְּחֶבְרוֹן לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וַיִּמְשְׁחוּ אֶת־דָּוִד לְמֶלֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: בֶּן־שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה דָּוִד בְּמלְכוֹ אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה מָלָךְ׃
verses.english: David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years.
verses.commentary:
He was thirty.

He would eventually be seventy.

tex.original: \hJ{בֶּן־שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה דָּוִד בְּמלְכוֹ אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה מָלָךְ׃}

verses.original: בְּחֶבְרוֹן מָלַךְ עַל־יְהוּדָה שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים וְשִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים וּבִירוּשָׁלַ͏ִם מָלַךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנָה עַל כּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל וִיהוּדָה׃
verses.english: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned over all Israel and Judah thirty-three years.
verses.commentary: First 30 years: King of sheep and rocks. Age 30 to 37.5: King of the South. Age 37.5 to 70.5: King of the United Kingdom.

tex.original: \hJ{בְּחֶבְרוֹן מָלַךְ עַל־יְהוּדָה שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים וְשִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים וּבִירוּשָׁלַ͏ִם מָלַךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנָה עַל כּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל וִיהוּדָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּלֶךְ הַמֶּלֶךְ וַאֲנָשָׁיו יְרוּשָׁלַ͏ִם אֶל־הַיְבֻסִי יוֹשֵׁב הָאָרֶץ וַיֹּאמֶר לְדָוִד לֵאמֹר לֹא־תָבוֹא הֵנָּה כִּי אִם־הֱסִירְךָ הַעִוְרִים וְהַפִּסְחִים לֵאמֹר לֹא־יָבוֹא דָוִד הֵנָּה׃
verses.english: The king and his men set out for Jerusalem against the Jebusites who inhabited the region. David was told, “You will never get in here! Even the blind and the lame will turn you back.” (They meant: David will never enter here.)
verses.commentary:
So David's like “Ok guys, remember that town I took Goliath's severed head to when I was a kid? Well when I was there I thought it would be a good town if we could get rid of all the people. So how about we go take it over and call it City of David until basically forever.”

The Jebusites overhear the plan and they're like “No.”

Thus begins the legendary battle for Jerusalem, grab some coffee and strap in.

verses.original: וַיִּלְכֹּד דָּוִד אֵת מְצֻדַת צִיּוֹן הִיא עִיר דָּוִד׃
verses.english: But David captured the stronghold of Zion; it is now the City of David.
verses.commentary:
He wins!

City of David.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּלְכֹּד דָּוִד אֵת מְצֻדַת צִיּוֹן הִיא עִיר דָּוִד׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא כּל־מַכֵּה יְבֻסִי וְיִגַּע בַּצִּנּוֹר וְאֶת־הַפִּסְחִים וְאֶת־הַעִוְרִים (שנאו) [שְׂנוּאֵי] נֶפֶשׁ דָּוִד עַל־כֵּן יֹאמְרוּ עִוֵּר וּפִסֵּחַ לֹא יָבוֹא אֶל־הַבָּיִת׃
verses.english: On that occasion David said, “Those who attack the Jebusites shall reach the water channel and [strike down] the lame and the blind, who are hateful to David.” That is why they say: “No one who is blind or lame may enter the House.”
verses.commentary:
Qere Ketiv.

Wait hold on, we're back in the battle.

Ok so he's making a plan about going in through a water channel maybe.

They're gonna kill the cripples for some reason?

Not entirely sure what's going on here.

verses.original: וַיֵּשֶׁב דָּוִד בַּמְּצֻדָה וַיִּקְרָא־לָהּ עִיר דָּוִד וַיִּבֶן דָּוִד סָבִיב מִן־הַמִּלּוֹא וָבָיְתָה׃
verses.english: David occupied the stronghold and renamed it the City of David; David also fortified the surrounding area, from the Millo inward.
verses.commentary:
Ok so he wins.

City of David.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֵּשֶׁב דָּוִד בַּמְּצֻדָה וַיִּקְרָא־לָהּ עִיר דָּוִד וַיִּבֶן דָּוִד סָבִיב מִן־הַמִּלּוֹא וָבָיְתָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּלֶךְ דָּוִד הָלוֹךְ וְגָדוֹל וַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵי צְבָאוֹת עִמּוֹ׃
verses.english: David kept growing stronger, for YHWH, the God of Hosts, was with him.
verses.commentary: David just keeps winning.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֵּלֶךְ דָּוִד הָלוֹךְ וְגָדוֹל וַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵי צְבָאוֹת עִמּוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח חִירָם מֶלֶךְ־צֹר מַלְאָכִים אֶל־דָּוִד וַעֲצֵי אֲרָזִים וְחָרָשֵׁי עֵץ וְחָרָשֵׁי אֶבֶן קִיר וַיִּבְנוּ־בַיִת לְדָוִד׃
verses.english: King Hiram of Tyre sent envoys to David with cedar logs, carpenters, and stonemasons; and they built a palace for David.
verses.commentary: David's friend sends him some building materials and some builders and they get all Tyred out and build a palace.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשְׁלַח חִירָם מֶלֶךְ־צֹר מַלְאָכִים אֶל־דָּוִד וַעֲצֵי אֲרָזִים וְחָרָשֵׁי עֵץ וְחָרָשֵׁי אֶבֶן קִיר וַיִּבְנוּ־בַיִת לְדָוִד׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּדַע דָּוִד כִּי־הֱכִינוֹ יְהֹוָה לְמֶלֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכִי נִשֵּׂא מַמְלַכְתּוֹ בַּעֲבוּר עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: Thus David knew that YHWH had established him as king over Israel and had exalted his kingship for the sake of His people Israel.
verses.commentary: David knew he was king and he knew it was YHWH's idea and had made him king for the people's own good.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֵּדַע דָּוִד כִּי־הֱכִינוֹ יְהֹוָה לְמֶלֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכִי נִשֵּׂא מַמְלַכְתּוֹ בַּעֲבוּר עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וַיִּקַּח דָּוִד עוֹד פִּלַגְשִׁים וְנָשִׁים מִירוּשָׁלַ͏ִם אַחֲרֵי בֹּאוֹ מֵחֶבְרוֹן וַיִּוָּלְדוּ עוֹד לְדָוִד בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת׃
verses.english: After he left Hebron, David took more concubines and wives in Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to David.
verses.commentary:
So naturally he gets some more wives.

Official and unofficial ones.

And he does his thing and more sons and daughters happen.

verses.original: וְאֵלֶּה שְׁמוֹת הַיִּלֹּדִים לוֹ בִּירוּשָׁלָ͏ִם שַׁמּוּעַ וְשׁוֹבָב וְנָתָן וּשְׁלֹמֹה׃

He has one kid, and the wife is like “YHWH has heard my request” and names him Shammua as a pun, cuz it means “YHWH has heard.”

Then he has another one and the wife is like “My rank has been restored” and she names him Shobab which means restored.

Then he has another kid and the wife is like “What a gift” and names him Nathan which is the verb “to give.”

Then it gets really loud and messy from all the kids so the final wife tries to escape to find some peace and he sees her bathing from the roof and thinks she's cute (long story) so long story short he gets her pregnant a couple times and kills her husband and the second time it lives (the baby not the husband (though I guess either works)) so she names it (the baby) Solomon which means peace because at last after all that chaos she finally got a peace.

Thank god.

The Philistines are back.

These guys are always predictable.

verses.original: וּפְלִשְׁתִּים בָּאוּ וַיִּנָּטְשׁוּ בְּעֵמֶק רְפָאִים׃

verses.commentary: The Philistines came and spread out over the valley of Those Really Tall Ghosts.

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁאַל דָּוִד בַּיהֹוָה לֵאמֹר הַאֶעֱלֶה אֶל־פְּלִשְׁתִּים הֲתִתְּנֵם בְּיָדִיוַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל־דָּוִד עֲלֵה כִּי־נָתֹן אֶתֵּן אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּים בְּיָדֶךָ׃
verses.english: David inquired of YHWH, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will You deliver them into my hands?” And YHWH answered David, “Go up, and I will deliver the Philistines into your hands.”
verses.commentary:
David's like “Should I fight em?”

YHWH says “Yeah.”

YHWH always says yeah to David.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשְׁאַל דָּוִד בַּיהֹוָה לֵאמֹר הַאֶעֱלֶה אֶל־פְּלִשְׁתִּים הֲתִתְּנֵם בְּיָדִיוַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל־דָּוִד עֲלֵה כִּי־נָתֹן אֶתֵּן אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּים בְּיָדֶךָ׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹא דָוִד בְּבַעַל־פְּרָצִים וַיַּכֵּם שָׁם דָּוִד וַיֹּאמֶר פָּרַץ יְהֹוָה אֶת־אֹיְבַי לְפָנַי כְּפֶרֶץ מָיִם עַל־כֵּן קָרָא שֵׁם־הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא בַּעַל פְּרָצִים׃
verses.english: Thereupon David marched to Baal-perazim, and David defeated them there. And he said, “YHWH has broken through my enemies before me as waters break through [a dam].” That is why that place was named Baal-perazim.
verses.commentary:
David marches to Lord Of The Breakthroughs and defeated the Philistines there.

And he's like “The Lord has Broken Through my enemies (get it?) as water breaks through [the stuff in parentheses is inferred but they're guessing it says a dam].

That's why the place is named that.

See how that works?

verses.original: וַיַּעַזְבוּ שָׁם אֶת־עֲצַבֵּיהֶם וַיִּשָּׂאֵם דָּוִד וַאֲנָשָׁיו׃

verses.commentary:
Where's your gods now?

The reference to 1 Chronicles 14:12 uses a form of the verb “To carry off” that means “bonfire” to suggest that David burned Philistine icons that another text says he “carried off.”

They're with David.

He took them.

verses.commentary: The Philistines spread out over the valley of Those Really Tall Ghosts again.

verses.original: וִיהִי (בשמעך) [כְּשׁמְעֲךָ] אֶת־קוֹל צְעָדָה בְּרָאשֵׁי הַבְּכָאִים אָז תֶּחֱרָץ כִּי אָז יָצָא יְהֹוָה לְפָנֶיךָ לְהַכּוֹת בְּמַחֲנֵה פְלִשְׁתִּים׃

Qere Ketiv.

When you hear marching in the tops of the weeping trees (I assume they're supposed to be hiding up there) then jump out and attack them.

YHWH says he'll lead the charge.

verses.original: וַיַּעַשׂ דָּוִד כֵּן כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּהוּ יְהֹוָה וַיַּךְ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּים מִגֶּבַע עַד־בֹּאֲךָ גָזֶר׃
verses.english: David did as YHWH had commanded him; and he routed the Philistines from Geba all the way to Gezer.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּעַשׂ דָּוִד כֵּן כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּהוּ יְהֹוָה וַיַּךְ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּים מִגֶּבַע עַד־בֹּאֲךָ גָזֶר׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּסֶף עוֹד דָּוִד אֶת־כּל־בָּחוּר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁלֹשִׁים אָלֶף׃

verses.commentary:
David picks some men so then they're picked men.

Thirty thousand.

verses.original: וַיָּקם וַיֵּלֶךְ דָּוִד וְכל־הָעָם אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ מִבַּעֲלֵי יְהוּדָה לְהַעֲלוֹת מִשָּׁם אֵת אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָא שֵׁם שֵׁם יְהֹוָה צְבָאוֹת יֹשֵׁב הַכְּרֻבִים עָלָיו׃
verses.english: Then David and all the troops that were with him set out from Baalim of Judah to bring up from there the Ark of God to which the Name was attached, the name LORD of Hosts Enthroned on the Cherubim.
verses.commentary: David and his men leave the Baals and go get the Box of God (also known as The Name), namely the name YHWH of the forces who sits invisibly enthroned beneath the wings of the golden sphinxes.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּקם וַיֵּלֶךְ דָּוִד וְכל־הָעָם אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ מִבַּעֲלֵי יְהוּדָה לְהַעֲלוֹת מִשָּׁם אֵת אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָא שֵׁם שֵׁם יְהֹוָה צְבָאוֹת יֹשֵׁב הַכְּרֻבִים עָלָיו׃}

verses.original: וַיַּרְכִּבוּ אֶת־אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים אֶל־עֲגָלָה חֲדָשָׁה וַיִּשָּׂאֻהוּ מִבֵּית אֲבִינָדָב אֲשֶׁר בַּגִּבְעָה וְעֻזָּא וְאַחְיוֹ בְּנֵי אֲבִינָדָב נֹהֲגִים אֶת־הָעֲגָלָה חֲדָשָׁה׃
verses.english: They loaded the Ark of God onto a new cart and conveyed it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill; and Abinadab’s sons, Uzza and Ahio, guided the new cart.
verses.commentary:
They put the box on a cart, and move it from the house of My Father Is Noble, aka Abinadab, on the hill.

His two sons, “Strength,” and Strength's Brother “Brother” guide the cart.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיַּרְכִּבוּ אֶת־אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים אֶל־עֲגָלָה חֲדָשָׁה וַיִּשָּׂאֻהוּ מִבֵּית אֲבִינָדָב אֲשֶׁר בַּגִּבְעָה וְעֻזָּא וְאַחְיוֹ בְּנֵי אֲבִינָדָב נֹהֲגִים אֶת־הָעֲגָלָה חֲדָשָׁה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּשָּׂאֻהוּ מִבֵּית אֲבִינָדָב אֲשֶׁר בַּגִּבְעָה עִם אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים וְאַחְיוֹ הֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵי הָאָרוֹן׃
verses.english: They conveyed it from Abinadab’s house on the hill, [Uzza walking] alongside the Ark of God and Ahio walking in front of the Ark.
verses.commentary: They move it from dad's house on the hill, while Strength walks beside and Brother walks in front.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּשָּׂאֻהוּ מִבֵּית אֲבִינָדָב אֲשֶׁר בַּגִּבְעָה עִם אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים וְאַחְיוֹ הֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵי הָאָרוֹן׃}

verses.original: וְדָוִד וְכל־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשַׂחֲקִים לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה בְּכֹל עֲצֵי בְרוֹשִׁים וּבְכִנֹּרוֹת וּבִנְבָלִים וּבְתֻפִּים וּבִמְנַעַנְעִים וּבְצֶלְצֱלִים׃
verses.english: Meanwhile, David and all the House of Israel danced before YHWH to [the sound of] all kinds of cypress wood [instruments], with lyres, harps, timbrels, sistrums, and cymbals.
verses.commentary: Meanwhile David's dancing. There's music.

tex.original: \hJ{וְדָוִד וְכל־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשַׂחֲקִים לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה בְּכֹל עֲצֵי בְרוֹשִׁים וּבְכִנֹּרוֹת וּבִנְבָלִים וּבְתֻפִּים וּבִמְנַעַנְעִים וּבְצֶלְצֱלִים׃}

verses.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ עַד־גֹּרֶן נָכוֹן וַיִּשְׁלַח עֻזָּה אֶל־אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים וַיֹּאחֶז בּוֹ כִּי שָׁמְטוּ הַבָּקָר׃
verses.english: But when they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out for the Ark of God and grasped it, for the oxen had stumbled.
verses.commentary:
Ok so as they're coming to the wheat preparation area [A big flat place on a farm where people beat wheat to get the grain out to prepare it so they can grind it into flour later.] owned by a guy named Prepared, the cows pulling the cart stumble, and the Box of God, the most sacred object in the world, is at risk of falling off!

So Strength musters his strength and grabs the box to make sure it doesn't drop to the ground.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיָּבֹאוּ עַד־גֹּרֶן נָכוֹן וַיִּשְׁלַח עֻזָּה אֶל־אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים וַיֹּאחֶז בּוֹ כִּי שָׁמְטוּ הַבָּקָר׃}

verses.original: וַיִּחַר־אַף יְהֹוָה בְּעֻזָּה וַיַּכֵּהוּ שָׁם הָאֱלֹהִים עַל־הַשַּׁל וַיָּמת שָׁם עִם אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים׃
verses.english: YHWH was incensed at Uzzah. And God struck him down on the spot for his indiscretion, and he died there beside the Ark of God.
verses.commentary: YHWH is furious, so he kills Strength for his lack of good judgement, and Strength dies right there beside the Box of God.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּחַר־אַף יְהֹוָה בְּעֻזָּה וַיַּכֵּהוּ שָׁם הָאֱלֹהִים עַל־הַשַּׁל וַיָּמת שָׁם עִם אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים׃}

verses.original: וַיִּחַר לְדָוִד עַל אֲשֶׁר פָּרַץ יְהֹוָה פֶּרֶץ בְּעֻזָּה וַיִּקְרָא לַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא פֶּרֶץ עֻזָּה עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃
verses.english: David was distressed because YHWH had inflicted a breach upon Uzzah; and that place was named Perez-uzzah, as it is still called.
verses.commentary:
So David's like “Wait what?”

Side Note: They name the place “The Violation Of Uzzah,” which is a pretty good name. It's still called that today.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּחַר לְדָוִד עַל אֲשֶׁר פָּרַץ יְהֹוָה פֶּרֶץ בְּעֻזָּה וַיִּקְרָא לַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא פֶּרֶץ עֻזָּה עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃}

verses.original: וַיִּרָא דָוִד אֶת־יְהֹוָה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא וַיֹּאמֶר אֵיךְ יָבוֹא אֵלַי אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: David was afraid of YHWH that day; he said, “How can I let the Ark of YHWH come to me?”
verses.commentary:
So David's like “What WHAT?”

“Keep that box away from me.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיִּרָא דָוִד אֶת־יְהֹוָה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא וַיֹּאמֶר אֵיךְ יָבוֹא אֵלַי אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וְלֹא־אָבָה דָוִד לְהָסִיר אֵלָיו אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה עַל־עִיר דָּוִד וַיַּטֵּהוּ דָוִד בֵּית עֹבֵד־אֱדֹם הַגִּתִּי׃
verses.english: So David would not bring the Ark of YHWH to his place in the City of David; instead, David diverted it to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
verses.commentary:
David decides he doesn't want the “You Die If You Touch It Even Just To Help” box in his city, so he sends it to the house of Worshipper Of Edom.

He's from Gath, which means Winepress.

tex.original: \hJ{וְלֹא־אָבָה דָוִד לְהָסִיר אֵלָיו אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה עַל־עִיר דָּוִד וַיַּטֵּהוּ דָוִד בֵּית עֹבֵד־אֱדֹם הַגִּתִּי׃}

verses.original: וַיֵּשֶׁב אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה בֵּית עֹבֵד אֱדֹם הַגִּתִּי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים וַיְבָרֶךְ יְהֹוָה אֶת־עֹבֵד אֱדֹם וְאֶת־כּל־בֵּיתוֹ׃
verses.english: The Ark of YHWH remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months, and YHWH blessed Obed-edom and his whole household.
verses.commentary:
The box stays there three months.

It makes Servant Of Edom and his whole family have really good luck.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֵּשֶׁב אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה בֵּית עֹבֵד אֱדֹם הַגִּתִּי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים וַיְבָרֶךְ יְהֹוָה אֶת־עֹבֵד אֱדֹם וְאֶת־כּל־בֵּיתוֹ׃}

verses.original: וַיֻּגַּד לַמֶּלֶךְ דָּוִד לֵאמֹר בֵּרַךְ יְהֹוָה אֶת־בֵּית עֹבֵד אֱדֹם וְאֶת־כּל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ בַּעֲבוּר אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים וַיֵּלֶךְ דָּוִד וַיַּעַל אֶת־אֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים מִבֵּית עֹבֵד אֱדֹם עִיר דָּוִד בְּשִׂמְחָה׃
verses.english: It was reported to King David: “YHWH has blessed Obed-edom’s house and all that belongs to him because of the Ark of God.” Thereupon David went and brought up the Ark of God from the house of Obed-edom to the City of David, amid rejoicing.
verses.commentary:
David hears that things are going great for Obed-edom because of the Box.

So David changes his mind and goes and fetches the Box.

He brings it to David City (aka, Jerusalem) and the people celebrate.

verses.original: וַיְהִי כִּי צָעֲדוּ נֹשְׂאֵי אֲרוֹן־יְהֹוָה שִׁשָּׁה צְעָדִים וַיִּזְבַּח שׁוֹר וּמְרִיא׃
verses.english: When the bearers of the Ark of YHWH had moved forward six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.
verses.commentary:
Ok, it's not clear if Obed-edom lives in Gath or if he's just from Gath, but by my calculations, Gath to Jerusalem is about a 13 hour walk.

Now we're not interested in time here, we're interested in steps.

So assuming an average stride length, that's about 80,000 steps.

On the other hand, if we assume Obed-edom's house is just a mile away from the palace, that's more like 2,000 steps.

Now, some quick background on the animals:

Ox: An adult cow. Basically a farm tractor made of meat.

Fatling: This can be a young cow, or sometimes another livestock animal. Basically a grain-fed, premium steak animal raised for a special dinner.

Now, in terms of cost, as best as I can estimate, circa 1000 BC when this is all taking place, in terms of the hours worked at the average wage:

Animal | Approximate Price | Equivalent Labor
Young calf (fatling) | 5–10 shekels | 5–10 months (900–1,800 work hours)
Ox (trained working animal) | 20–30 shekels | 20–30 months (3,600–5,400 work hours)

Let's agree that “1 ox + 1 fatling” is about 30 shekels in 1000 BC, or about 30 months work at the average wage.

As for weight, a conservative estimate is that a fatling weighs 500 lbs and the ox weighs 1000 lbs.

That's all the background we need. Now let's get down to business.

David wants the God Box, because it's lucky and he wants the luck.

But he's clearly a bit freaked out by the “Touch it and you die” thing, as noted in 2 Sam 6:8-10.

Summary: in this scene, David isn't taking any risks.

How do you make the gods happy?

Naturally, sacrifices.

So, the text notes that David kills an ox and a fatling every time the guys move six steps.

Now, in our more conservative estimate of the distance of house to palace, that's 2,000 steps, or 2000/6 = 333 adult cows and 333 young cows (or whatever animal that was) for a total of 666 dead animals weighing almost exactly half a million pounds, spread out over a mile long walk, at a cost of about 10,000 shekels total, or 10,000 months (833 years) of work at the average wage.

However, if “Obed-edom the Gath guy” does in fact live in Gath, then we're looking at 80,000/6 = 13,333 sacrifices of 1,500 lbs each for a total of 20 million pounds of meat stretching over 32.3 miles in a very much not refrigerated outdoor mid-day sun, at a cost of 400,000 shekels total, or 400,000 months (33,333 years) of work at the average wage.

Now During the Davidic era (around 1000 BC), Jerusalem was a small hilltop fortress town.

Most mainstream archaeologists and historians estimate the population of Jerusalem was roughly 1,500 to 2,000 people.

The estimated population of Israel overall during the Davidic period ranges drastically between 40,000 to 300,000 people according to archaeological estimates, compared to several million people implied by biblical texts.

Taking the geometric mean of 40k and 300k, we get an estimate of about 100,000 people, halfway between the two estimates on a logarithmic scale.

Now, the shekel is a unit of weight, with the unit of currency being the amount of silver with that weight. A shekel is about 11-14 grams of silver.

A common back-of-the-envelope estimate is that an ordinary person in the Iron Age produced goods and services worth roughly 10–20 shekels per year (most of it consumed directly rather than sold).

Using 15 shekels/person/year as a midpoint:

Region | Population | Estimated Annual GDP
Jerusalem | 2,000 | 30,000 shekels/year
Kingdom of David | 100,000 | 1.5 million shekels/year

So we're looking at a ceremony with a cost somewhere between about 1/3 of the GDP of Jerusalem on the low end, and 1/3 of the GDP of all of Israel on the high end.

In conclusion, though the numbers above are inherently uncertain, and more qualitative than quantitative, one thing we can know with certainty is that when it David is not fucking around.

We now return to the story.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְהִי כִּי צָעֲדוּ נֹשְׂאֵי אֲרוֹן־יְהֹוָה שִׁשָּׁה צְעָדִים וַיִּזְבַּח שׁוֹר וּמְרִיא׃}

verses.original: וְדָוִד מְכַרְכֵּר בְּכל־עֹז לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וְדָוִד חָגוּר אֵפוֹד בָּד׃
verses.english: David whirled with all his might before YHWH; David was girt with a linen ephod.
verses.commentary:
Ok so naturally, given a ceremony of that size, David plans to enjoy himself.

The text notes that he's wearing an ephod.

Recall that an ephod is part of the priest clothes that P kept yammering about back in Exodus. To refresh our memory:

Chapters | Source | Contents
Exodus 25 | P | Ark, table, lampstand
Exodus 26 | P | Tabernacle curtains, frames, veil
Exodus 27 | P | Bronze altar, courtyard, lamp oil
Exodus 28 | P (here) | Priestly garments (ephod, breastpiece, robe, turban)
Exodus 29 | P | Ordination of Aaron and his sons
Exodus 30 | P | Incense altar, census tax, bronze basin, anointing oil, incense
Exodus 31 | P | Bezalel, Oholiab, Sabbath
Exodus 32 | E | Golden Calf (polemic against Aaronid priesthood and Jeroboam)
Exodus 33 | E | Moses intercedes; Tent of Meeting outside the camp
Exodus 34 | J/P | Covenant renewed; new tablets; ritual laws
Exodus 35 | P | Collection of materials; craftsmen
Exodus 36 | P | Construction of the Tabernacle
Exodus 37 | P | Construction of the furnishings
Exodus 38 | P | Altar, courtyard, inventory
Exodus 39 | P | Priestly garments; completion of the work
Exodus 40 | P | Assembly of the Tabernacle; glory fills it
Leviticus | P | It's Leviticus.
Numbers 1–10 | P | Census, camp arrangement, Levites, priestly duties, offerings, Passover, silver trumpets; departure from Sinai
Numbers 11–16 | Mixed (J/E/P) | Complaints, quail, Miriam and Aaron, spies, Korah's rebellion
Numbers 17–19 | P | Aaron's staff, priestly dues, Levites, Red Heifer
Numbers 20–25 | Mixed (J/E/P) | Wilderness narratives, Balaam, Baal-Peor
Numbers 26–31 | Mostly P | Second census, inheritance laws, Joshua commissioned, offerings, Midian campaign
Numbers 32–36 | Mostly P | Transjordan settlement, itinerary, boundaries, Levitical cities, daughters of Zelophehad

As you can see, there's a lot of P in there.

Lots of cubits.

Lots of rules about how you have to make him clothes and bring him gold.

The Torah sort of falls apart after that and never quite gets back on track.

Many devoted readers never make it past the long march from Exodus 25 to Numbers 11. And a sizable fraction of those who make it through skim.

Just mentioning this to clarify: We understand if you don't remember exactly what an ephod is.

Ok so an ephod is basically a skirt.

Open at the bottom. Less privacy than pants.

Now, it's probably not correct to say that underwear didn't exist yet. But it's probably not too common, and it's certainly not a standard everyday thing like it is today.

And as we'll see pretty clearly from context in the upcoming scene, David is commando in both senses of the term.

Commando. 1. A commando is a trained soldier, a special military unit. 2. A slang term for not wearing underwear.

verses.original: וְדָוִד וְכל־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל מַעֲלִים אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה בִּתְרוּעָה וּבְקוֹל שׁוֹפָר׃
verses.english: Thus David and all the House of Israel brought up the Ark of YHWH with shouts and with blasts of the horn.
verses.commentary: So David holds a party that costs somewhere between 1/3 of the GDP of Jerusalem and 1/3 of the GDP of Israel.

tex.original: \hJ{וְדָוִד וְכל־בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל מַעֲלִים אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה בִּתְרוּעָה וּבְקוֹל שׁוֹפָר׃}

verses.original: וְהָיָה אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה בָּא עִיר דָּוִד וּמִיכַל בַּת־שָׁאוּל נִשְׁקְפָה בְּעַד הַחַלּוֹן וַתֵּרֶא אֶת־הַמֶּלֶךְ דָּוִד מְפַזֵּז וּמְכַרְכֵּר לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וַתִּבֶז לוֹ בְּלִבָּהּ׃
verses.english: As the Ark of YHWH entered the City of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked out of the window and saw King David leaping and whirling before YHWH; and she despised him for it.
verses.commentary:
He's wearing an ephod, and dancing around like mad.

One particularly brilliant and knowledgeable scholar describes the scene as “David cavorting with less circumspection than enthusiasm before the ark, perhaps doing cartwheels in an era before the invention of underwear.”

And Michal... (

Saul's daughter, and David's first wife, who he originally paid 200 Philistine foreskins for, before she was eventually married off to someone else and then finally retrieved from her new husband and brought back to David in that scene with the Village Of Young Men following a defection by Abner against Ish-bosheth that began when Ish-bosheth scolded Abner for having some sex. You've gotta love the bible. Underappreciated book, for real.

)... sees David “leaping and whirling” and for some reason hates him for it ...(

Following the text, I'm assuming she hates him for the leaping and whirling, and not for, e.g.,

• Probably killing her dad.
• Probably marrying both her and her mom.
• Probably being involved in the death of her brother.
• Definitely taking her back from a husband who she'd been building a life with for an unspecified amount of time.
• Sort of participating in the systematic extermination of everybody in her entire family line and then publicly crying about how tragic it is as he sings songs every time.

I'm assuming it's not that.

The text says she hates him for the leaping and whirling.

)... Which is more evidence of the proposition that he's wearing that ephod (i.e., skirt) with no underwear in this scene.

And perhaps doing cartwheels.

So picture all that and let's keep moving.

verses.original: וַיָּבִאוּ אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה וַיַּצִּגוּ אֹתוֹ בִּמְקוֹמוֹ בְּתוֹךְ הָאֹהֶל אֲשֶׁר נָטָה־לוֹ דָּוִד וַיַּעַל דָּוִד עֹלוֹת לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה וּשְׁלָמִים׃
verses.english: They brought in the Ark of YHWH and set it up in its place inside the tent which David had pitched for it, and David sacrificed burnt offerings and offerings of well-being before YHWH.
verses.commentary:
They put the Box of YHWH in the tabernacle tent type place.

Then they do even more sacrifices.

Apparently there's still a cow or two somewhere on earth and he wants to make sure YHWH gets them all.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד אֶל־מִיכַל לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֲשֶׁר בָּחַר־בִּי מֵאָבִיךְ וּמִכּל־בֵּיתוֹ לְצַוֺּת אֹתִי נָגִיד עַל־עַם יְהֹוָה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל וְשִׂחַקְתִּי לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verses.english: David answered Michal, “It was before YHWH who chose me instead of your father and all his family and appointed me ruler over YHWH’s people Israel! I will dance before YHWH
verses.commentary: And David goes “YHWH chose me over your dad and all the rest of your family and made me king. I can dance if I want to.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד אֶל־מִיכַל לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה אֲשֶׁר בָּחַר־בִּי מֵאָבִיךְ וּמִכּל־בֵּיתוֹ לְצַוֺּת אֹתִי נָגִיד עַל־עַם יְהֹוָה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל וְשִׂחַקְתִּי לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃}

verses.original: וּנְקַלֹּתִי עוֹד מִזֹּאת וְהָיִיתִי שָׁפָל בְּעֵינָי וְעִם־הָאֲמָהוֹת אֲשֶׁר אָמַרְתְּ עִמָּם אִכָּבֵדָה׃
verses.english: and dishonor myself even more, and be low in my own esteem; but among the slavegirls that you speak of I will be honored.”
verses.commentary: “Look babe, I get it, I may hate myself too, but the girls you're talking about: they love me.”

tex.original: \hJ{וּנְקַלֹּתִי עוֹד מִזֹּאת וְהָיִיתִי שָׁפָל בְּעֵינָי וְעִם־הָאֲמָהוֹת אֲשֶׁר אָמַרְתְּ עִמָּם אִכָּבֵדָה׃}

verses.original: וּלְמִיכַל בַּת־שָׁאוּל לֹא־הָיָה לָהּ יָלֶד עַד יוֹם מוֹתָהּ׃
verses.english: So to her dying day Michal daughter of Saul had no children.
verses.commentary:
And Michal was childless until the day of her death.

End of chapter.

verses.original: וַיְהִי כִּי־יָשַׁב הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּבֵיתוֹ וַיהֹוָה הֵנִיחַ־לוֹ מִסָּבִיב מִכּל־אֹיְבָיו׃
verses.english: When the king was settled in his palace and YHWH had granted him safety from all the enemies around him,
verses.commentary:
So David settles in to the palace.

YHWH has gotten rid of most of his enemies by now.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְהִי כִּי־יָשַׁב הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּבֵיתוֹ וַיהֹוָה הֵנִיחַ־לוֹ מִסָּבִיב מִכּל־אֹיְבָיו׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶל־נָתָן הַנָּבִיא רְאֵה נָא אָנֹכִי יוֹשֵׁב בְּבֵית אֲרָזִים וַאֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים יֹשֵׁב בְּתוֹךְ הַיְרִיעָה׃
verses.english: the king said to the prophet Nathan: “Here I am dwelling in a house of cedar, while the Ark of YHWH abides in a tent!”
verses.commentary: David says to Nathan, “Hey, I think YHWH deserves a house too.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶל־נָתָן הַנָּבִיא רְאֵה נָא אָנֹכִי יוֹשֵׁב בְּבֵית אֲרָזִים וַאֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים יֹשֵׁב בְּתוֹךְ הַיְרִיעָה׃}

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר נָתָן אֶל־הַמֶּלֶךְ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר בִּלְבָבְךָ לֵךְ עֲשֵׂה כִּי יְהֹוָה עִמָּךְ׃
verses.english: Nathan said to the king, “Go and do whatever you have in mind, for YHWH is with you.”
verses.commentary: Nathan's like “Do whatever you want.”

tex.original: \hJ{וַיֹּאמֶר נָתָן אֶל־הַמֶּלֶךְ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר בִּלְבָבְךָ לֵךְ עֲשֵׂה כִּי יְהֹוָה עִמָּךְ׃}

verses.original: וַיְהִי בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּאוַיְהִי דְּבַר־יְהֹוָה אֶל־נָתָן לֵאמֹר׃
verses.english: But that same night the word of YHWH came to Nathan:
verses.commentary: But that night, Nathan has a dream.

tex.original: \hJ{וַיְהִי בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּאוַיְהִי דְּבַר־יְהֹוָה אֶל־נָתָן לֵאמֹר׃}
tex.english: \eJ{But that same night the word of YHWH came to Nathan:}

verses.original: לֵךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ אֶל־עַבְדִּי אֶל־דָּוִדכֹּה אָמַר יְהֹוָה הַאַתָּה תִּבְנֶה־לִּי בַיִת לְשִׁבְתִּי׃
verses.english: “Go and say to My servant David: Thus said YHWH: Are you the one to build a house for Me to dwell in?
verses.commentary: And YHWH's like “Is David really the guy who builds my house?”

tex.original: \hJ{לֵךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ אֶל־עַבְדִּי אֶל־דָּוִדכֹּה אָמַר יְהֹוָה הַאַתָּה תִּבְנֶה־לִּי בַיִת לְשִׁבְתִּי׃}

verses.original: כִּי לֹא יָשַׁבְתִּי בְּבַיִת לְמִיּוֹם הַעֲלֹתִי אֶת־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרַיִם וְעַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה וָאֶהְיֶה מִתְהַלֵּךְ בְּאֹהֶל וּבְמִשְׁכָּן׃
verses.english: From the day that I brought the people of Israel out of Egypt to this day I have not dwelt in a house, but have moved about in Tent and Tabernacle.
verses.commentary: “I'm fine in a tent. I'm used to it.”

tex.original: \hJ{כִּי לֹא יָשַׁבְתִּי בְּבַיִת לְמִיּוֹם הַעֲלֹתִי אֶת־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרַיִם וְעַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה וָאֶהְיֶה מִתְהַלֵּךְ בְּאֹהֶל וּבְמִשְׁכָּן׃}

verses.original: בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר־הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי בְּכל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֲדָבָר דִּבַּרְתִּי אֶת־אַחַד שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִי לִרְעוֹת אֶת־עַמִּי אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר לָמָּה לֹא־בְנִיתֶם לִי בֵּית אֲרָזִים׃
verses.english: As I moved about wherever the Israelites went, did I ever reproach any of the tribal leaders whom I appointed to care for My people Israel: Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?
verses.commentary: “I never got mad at anyone for keeping me in the box in the back [The ark is located in the holy of holies, which is, in fact, in the back of the tent.] of the tent.”

verses.original: וְעַתָּה כֹּה־תֹאמַר לְעַבְדִּי לְדָוִד כֹּה אָמַר יְהֹוָה צְבָאוֹת אֲנִי לְקַחְתִּיךָ מִן־הַנָּוֶה מֵאַחַר הַצֹּאן לִהְיוֹת נָגִיד עַל־עַמִּי עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verses.english: “Further, say thus to My servant David: Thus said YHWH of Hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler of My people Israel,
verses.commentary: “Say this to David. 'YHWH says this. I took you from your sheep job and made you king.”'

tex.original: \hJ{וְעַתָּה כֹּה־תֹאמַר לְעַבְדִּי לְדָוִד כֹּה אָמַר יְהֹוָה צְבָאוֹת אֲנִי לְקַחְתִּיךָ מִן־הַנָּוֶה מֵאַחַר הַצֹּאן לִהְיוֹת נָגִיד עַל־עַמִּי עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל׃}

verses.original: וָאֶהְיֶה עִמְּךָ בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר הָלַכְתָּ וָאַכְרִתָה אֶת־כּל־אֹיְבֶיךָ מִפָּנֶיךָ וְעָשִׂתִי־לְךָ שֵׁם גָּדוֹל כְּשֵׁם הַגְּדֹלִים אֲשֶׁר בָּאָרֶץ׃
verses.english: and I have been with you wherever you went, and have cut down all your enemies before you. Moreover, I will give you great renown like that of the greatest men on earth.
verses.commentary: “'and I've been following you around and killing all your enemies. Moreover, I plan to make you famous. Like world famous.”'

tex.original: \hJ{וָאֶהְיֶה עִמְּךָ בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר הָלַכְתָּ וָאַכְרִתָה אֶת־כּל־אֹיְבֶיךָ מִפָּנֶיךָ וְעָשִׂתִי־לְךָ שֵׁם גָּדוֹל כְּשֵׁם הַגְּדֹלִים אֲשֶׁר בָּאָרֶץ׃}

verses.original: וְשַׂמְתִּי מָקוֹם לְעַמִּי לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וּנְטַעְתִּיו וְשָׁכַן תַּחְתָּיו וְלֹא יִרְגַּז עוֹד וְלֹא־יֹסִיפוּ בְנֵי־עַוְלָה לְעַנּוֹתוֹ כַּאֲשֶׁר בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה׃
verses.english: I will establish a home for My people Israel and will plant them firm, so that they shall dwell secure and shall tremble no more. Evil men shall not oppress them any more as in the past,

verses.english: Yet even this, O Lord GOD, has seemed too little to You; for You have spoken of Your servant’s house also for the future. May that be the law for the people, O Lord GOD.
verses.commentary:
“You've promised so much, but even that seems too little for You. I mean we're talking about the future here. May your words become the law, Lord Gᴏᴅ.”

Side Note: In a rare case of typographical theology, the “Lord” here is in normal font while “Gᴏᴅ” is in smallcaps.

From this, we can infer that:

• David actually said Adonai, the literal Hebrew word for Lord.
• David did not say Elohim after that, because Elohim doesn't render as Gᴏᴅ in smallcaps.
• Therefore, David must have said “Adonai YHWH.”
• Which, given the conventions of English bible translation, would render (on first pass) as “Lord Lᴏʀᴅ.”
• But that's just silly.
• Therefore, the translation above must have fixed the problem with a one-off decision to replace the smallcaps Lᴏʀᴅ with smallcaps Gᴏᴅ.
• The O before Lord isn't there in the original. They just put that in for like, garnish.
• You can check the Hebrew. That's what happened.

The bible is fun.

verses.english: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was commander of the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons were priests.
verses.commentary:
(Narrator: Ominous music fills the book.)

By the יד way Son of YHW Son of YHW ידע now enters the scene looking dead eyed and mean.

He's the head of the Cherethites and the Pelethites.

They're David's army of foreign mercenaries.

So David can basically dominate the country without having to muster soldiers from the twelve tribes or curry favor with the tribal elders.

Now he has an army of foreigners loyal only to him, with no particular concern for Israel or the people.

Director's Notes on the character of Beniaiah.

• Tall, gaunt, and skeletal-looking, with a corpse-like appearance.
• Deep-set, pale eyes that seem cold and empty, giving the impression that he's always watching but never showing or even experiencing emotion.
• Long, stringy gray hair and a scraggly gray beard, making him look unkempt rather than noble. Bald of head and beard.
• Face is harsh and cadaverous, with a fixed, grim expression.
• Dressed plainly in dark clothing or armor, without ornamentation, emphasizing function over status.
• Believed to be completely mute, according to legend his tongue was torn out by the Mad King which makes his silence itself unsettling.
• Moves quietly and deliberately, often appearing without warning.
• Others frequently react to him with unease or fear before he does anything at all.

The chapter ends here.

verses.english: and when Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul came to David, he flung himself on his face and prostrated himself. David said, “Mephibosheth!” and he replied, “At your service, sir.”
verses.commentary:
So Mephibosheth (Son of David's former best friend, also Grandson of Saul) comes to David (presumably with help) and he immediately falls on his face (from respect, not the legs) and David's like “Mephibosheth” and he replies (presumably still from the ground) “At your service, sir.”

Also his name means “Mephi of Shame.”

We don't know what a Mephi is.

In 1 Chronicles 8:34 and 9:40, he's called Meribaal, which means “Baal contends.”

And since one of the readings of the folk etymology of Israel from Genesis 32:28 is “El contends,” we've basically got:

Israel = The Canaanite highest god contends.

Meribaal = The Canaanite storm god contends.

Now of course El and Baal are also the generic terms for God and Lord respectively.

This isn't anything deep going on in the text probably.

But it's a thing, and it's in the text.

Just make a note of that and let's keep moving.
